Kuvio 7: Bruttokansantuotteen osatekijt EU:ssa ja USA:ssa: kumulatiivinen muutos (log.) vuodesta 1980 alkaen Toimialakohtaiset tarkastelut eivt mykn yleens kerro siit, miten kansantalous sopeutuu uuteen kilpailulliseen ympristn ja millaisia mahdollisia negatiivisia vaikutuksia kilpailun lisntymisell voisi olla. Toimialoittaiset tarkastelut ovat tyypillisesti vain osittaisen tasapainon analyysej, jolloin esimerkiksi heijastusvaikutukset jvt huomioimatta. Kilpailun kiristymisen kokonaistaloudellisten vaikutusten arviointi on vaikeaa, mutta tss yhteydess ns. dynaamiset yleisen tasapainon mallit ovat osoittautuneet hyyllisiksi. Tllaiset mallit, joista yksi on Suomen Pankissakin kehitetty Aino malli, perustuvat talousteoriaan ja taloudenpitjien rationaaliseen ja optimaaliseen kyttytymiseen vallitsevien rajoitteiden puitteissa. Dynaamiset yleisen tasapainon mallit ovat hyyllisi koska ne mahdollistavat monimutkaisten reaalitaloudellisten sopeutumismekanismien tarkastelun. Toisaalta tytyy tietenkin muistaa ett tllaisilla malleilla tehdyt laskemat ovat aina vain suuntaa antavia. Seuraavassa tarkastelen kilpailun lisntymisen kokonaistalouden vaikutuksia saatujen mallilaskelmien valossa (GEM, AINO). Ennen laskelmiin menemist, lienee kuitenkin syyt palauttaa hieman mieleen se, miten erilaisia kilpailutilanteita voidaan kuvailla ja milt reaalitalouden sopeutumisdynamiikka voisi talousteorian valossa nytt. Kuva 8: Kilpailun kiristyminen hydykemarkkinoilla Puhtaasti talousteorian nkkulmasta katsoen kilpailun puute on synonyymi eptydelliselle kilpailulle. Eptydellinen kilpailu esimerkiksi hydykemarkkinoilla merkitsee sit, ett talous on sellaisessa tasapainossa miss yritykset tuottavat vhemmn, mutta korkeammalla hinnalla suhteessa kilpailulliseen tasapainoon. Tss tilanteessa yritykset tekevt voittoa, joka puolestaan pienent ns. kuluttajien ylijm. Tydellisen kilpailun tilanteessa hinnat sopeutuvat siten, ett kysynt ja tarjonta kohtaavat ja kuluttajien ylijm on maksimissaan. Samoin eptydellinen kilpailu tymarkkinoilla merkitsee sit, ett palkka on korkeampi ja ty kysynt vastaavasti alhaisempi. Korkeampi palkkataso merkitsee yrityksille korkeampia kustannuksia suhteessa kilpailulliseen tasapainoon. Koska yritykset siirtvt korkeammat kustannukset hintoihin, merkitsee tymarkkinoiden eptydellinen kilpailu my korkeampaa talouden hintatasoa suhteessa kilpailulliseen tasapainoon. Tmn lisksi trke rahapolitiikan kannalta on ottaa huomioon se, ett tarjontajoustot hyyke- ja tyarkkinoilla ovat tyypillisesti alhaisemmat eptydellisen kilpailun tilanteessa. Tm merkitsee sit, ett hyykkeiden - ja ty tarjonta joustaa vhemmn markkinatilanteen mukaan ja tekee nin rahapolitiikan harjoittamisen vaikeammaksi. Kilpailun kiristyminen puolestaan voidaan tulkita tllaisissa tarkasteluissa hinta/palkka marginaalien pienenemiseksi: voitot pienenevt, taloudellinen toiminta tehostuu, tarjonta reagoi herkemmin markkinoiden muutoksiin ja kuluttajien ylijm lopulta kasvaa. Kilpailun kiristymisen hyyke ja tymarkkinoilla voi siis odottaa merkitsevn pitkll aikavlill talouden tuotannontason nousua ja alhaisempaa hintatasoa. Jos lisntynyt tuotanto toteutetaan kotimaassa, kysynnn lisntyminen kannustaa yritykset lopulta lismn investointeja. Tt kautta talouden pomakanta kasvaa. Mikli tyt sstvss teknisess kehityksess ei oleteta tapahtuvan muutoksia, korkeampi tuotannon taso edellytt my tyanoksen kasvattamista. Tm heijastuu yhdess hintatason laskun kanssa ennen pitk reaalipalkkojen ja kotitalouksien tulotason nousuun. Kohonnut pomakanta ja tyanoksen nousu mahdollistaa lopulta my korkeamman talouden tuotantopotentiaalin. Kuva 9. Nist viiveist syntyy todellisia taloudellisia kustannuksia. Lopuksi, kun ns. varallisuusvaikutukset huomioidaan, erityisesti hyykemarkkinakilpailun lisntymisest johtuva vliaikainen yritysten voittojen supistuminen voi alentaa yksityist kulutusta lyhyell ja keskipitkll aikavlill. Title: Speech entitled "The imbalances and challenges of the global economy - Europe, Asia, America" at a seminar of the Economic Committee
text: Director General Erkki Liikanen With reservations for change IMBALANCES IN THE GLOBAL ECONOMY AND CHALLENGES d0 EUROPE, ASIA, AMERICAS Seminar of the Economic Committee 20.4.2005, Parliament Introduction The development of the global economy over the past ten years has had a number of key features: Figure 2. Text box listing the things below. . a5 first a technology-driven global sharp rise in stock prices at the end of the last decade and a sharp appreciation of the dollar, mirroring the significant and unexpected depreciation of the newborn euro; a5 the sharp global fall in share prices that began in 2000 and the weakening of the dollar, which began in early 2002 and mirrored by the strengthening of the euro; a5 a growing current account deficit in the United States, which was later accompanied by a rapidly swelling government deficit; a5 global monetary easing and exceptionally long-term monetary easing; a5 low inflation, which has become global a5 the intensification of productivity growth in the United States: after a long catch-up, Europe began to lag behind the United States again; a5 China's emergence as a major player in the global economy I will try to form an interpretation of this development and assess what risks exist, how serious the imbalances that have been identified are and what chance we have of getting rid of them in a controlled way. Figure 1. Facts and their interpretation Exchange rates The weakening of the euro in the early years of the euro came as a surprise to many, and also a disappointment to many. Figure 3. Effective exchange rate between the dollar and the euro 1998-2005. Demonstrate the latest years, one experience/cycle. The figure below shows the effective, i.e. trade-weighted, exchange rate of the euro and the dollar. It reflects the weakening and subsequent strengthening of the euro. However, the figure shows only one experience. Trade-oriented courses have varied greatly before, bilateral rates even more so. This can be clearly seen in the second photo. The contents of the previous image are displayed in that small box. Figure 4. The effective exchange rate of the dollar and the euro 1980-2005, where the contents of the previous picture are separated by a box. From a historical point of view, neither the weakness of the dollar nor the strength of the euro today are unprecedented. Not far from long-term averages. What catches the eye in the chart is the strength of the dollar in the early 1980s, to which level it did not reach during the technology boom, even though it was exceptionally strong. How is this to be interpreted? In the early 1980s, the dollar was pushed in a strong direction by a monetary policy that was initially very tight, followed by a very light fiscal policy at the beginning of the Rea-gan era. High interest rates attracted investment in the dollar and light fiscal policies pushed up domestic demand, displacing exports. At the turn of the millennium, the technology boom and optimistic perceptions of investment returns and long-term growth attracted foreign investment. The dollar strengthened in this wave, and the appreciation was not very much even complained about in the USA. It will all come to an end in due course. In the mid-1980s, the dollar turned to a sharp decline, and the decline continued for several years. The same thing happened two or three years ago. As technology optimism evaporated, cas leaks moderated, stock prices fell, equity investments and direct investment in the United States subsided. The dollar began its long-predicted low, which would probably have been even steeper than experienced without the dollar-supporting investments by Asian central banks. These investments have also contributed to the fact that long-term interest rates have not risen as expected. Us monetary policy was driven exceptionally light, and the budget deficit was allowed to grow. This resulted in a double deficit that is of concern to many. Us dual deficit The U.S. current account deficit began to swell again at the start of the technology boom in 1998. The federal budget deficit, on the other hand, had been on a downward trajectory since 1993. In 2000, a surplus of about two percentage cents had already been reached. Figure 5. Current account deficit and budget deficit in the USA 1990-2004. The current account deficit swelled during the technology boom because resources were in full use and domestic demand grew so fast. However, the current account deficit has continued to grow even after the technology boom. As a counter-item, the indebtedness of households and, in particular, of central government, has continued. By contrast, corporate sector indebtedness is not a problem in the US, as the cash flow to capital spending has strengthened strongly in recent years. There has been debate as to whether or not the double deficit poses a threat to the stable development of the USA and thus to the global economy. This issue was strongly discussed at the Meeting of the International Monetary Fund at the weekend in Washington. Optimists point to the flexible US market, growth potential, high returns and low risk on investments there, and the unsurpassed importance of the dollar as a reserve and investment currency and as an international means of payment. Even if the deficits cannot swell indefinitely, the US economy will eventually grow out of these problems, say optimists. The need for adjustment in the USA is also facilitated by the fact that the majority of Americans' ve-lois are in their home currency, while the receivables are largely in the foreign currency. (In this way, the depreciation of the currency does not increase the value of liabilities d0 unlike, for example, in the case of Finland in the early 1990s, when the weakening of the markka significantly increased the value of debt denominated in foreign currency.) Pessimists, on the other hand, point out that investor capital flows have already begun to turn away from dollar investments, making it difficult to finance deficits. These developments show that both the current budget deficit and the current account deficit are already unsustainable. If the deficits continue at the current level or increase, us foreign debt and federal debt will cross the line at which dollar investments will cease to be of interest. We are facing a collapse in the dollar exchange rate and a fall in the exchange rates of dollar-denominated bonds. The latter is synonymous with an increase in long-term interest rates. Monetary policy By historical comparison, the easing of monetary policy between 2001 and 2003 was exceptionally high, particularly in the United States, although monetary policy had tightened more sharply in previous years than elsewhere. Figure 6. Central bank interest rates. Fed and ECB In the United States, real short-term interest rates have been slightly negative for the past couple of years, and in the euro area, too, around zero. Figure 7 3-month real interest rate in the US and the euro area 1995-2005. So far, the light monetary policy has not been reflected in inflation. It is true that inflation expectations have risen somewhat since 2003 and in the United States and in the euro area, but the increase is not very high. This does not mean that a light monetary policy has not also had an impact on prices. The light monetary policy has contributed to accelerating the rise in asset prices in the United States and also in other parts of the world. Stock prices rose quite strongly in 2004. Bond prices have remained relatively high, which is reflected in the low level of long-term interest rates. Liquid money has sought better returns on riskier claims, which is why interest rate differentials have remained low (the spread between BBB and AAA-rated corporate bonds, the risk premium for developing countries). The rise in house prices also looks like a global phenomenon. House prices have been rising fairly rapidly in almost all OECD countries except Germany and Japan. The rise in house prices in Finland looks only average in an international comparison. The rise in house prices is clearly supported by a light monetary policy. Through this channel, monetary policy has also supported domestic demand, especially in the United States, but also in some euro area countries, such as Finland. The light monetary policy has also indirectly pushed up commodity prices. The impact comes from the fact that the light monetary policy of the USA has been transferred to the Asian countries as a result of the exchange rate policy pursued by these countries. Currency interventions have kept the exchange rate stable against the dollar or the strengthening of the currency has been counteracted. The resulting liquidity has made it possible to finance rapid growth, especially in China. Rapid growth in Asia has pushed up raw material prices. There has also been a direct channel. Money has been cheaply available to take various speculative positions in the commodity market. Taken together, all these factors mean that a prolonged period of light monetary policy will have inflationary effects in the face of globalisation and rapid productivity growth. It will only take more time for them to appear at the rate of increase in the general price level than before. Part of the reason for price stability may be the improvement in the credibility of central banks and, as a result, the fact that inflation expectations remain low. The threshold for raising prices rises when central banks are believed to keep inflation low. Low inflation Price stability, i.e. low inflation, is now beginning to be expected and generally accepted in all OECD countries. Figure 8, which demonstrates the convergence of inflation to low levels. The transition to low inflation has been facilitated by increased competition with the opening up of national economies and rapid productivity growth in many sectors. The prices of many manufactured goods have been falling as production has shifted to countries with lower costs. However, the main reason for the low inflation has been the changed monetary policy. Central banks have become independent and low inflation has become their main objective. Productivity For a long time, productivity growth in Europe was faster than in the United States. There were two reasons for this. Europe is bridging the productivity gap created during the Second World War. Another reason was the rapid rise in labour costs in Europe in the 1970s and early 1980s, which prompted the replacement of labour by capital. Since the middle of the last decade, the opposite has been the case. In the United States, productivity growth accelerated and slowed down in Europe. In the United States, the retail and wholesale trade and the financial services sector, with its ancillary activities, accounted for 95% of the increase in productivity growth by a good percentage point between 1990-1995 and 1995-2001. Figure 9. Acceleration of productivity growth in the US divided into key industry contributions. In Europe, productivity growth slowed down over the same period in most countries. Of course, there are sectors in Europe, such as telecommunications, where productivity growth has been rapid. However, evidence of a spurt in productivity growth in the service sector and in the ICT-enabled industries in general is lacking. Chinese China has emerged as a major player in the global economy. China's growth has been very fast for a long time, and there is nothing to suggest that it cannot continue for another decade or two. China's rise in global economic importance is evidenced by the fact that it is currently the third most important country in the world in terms of foreign trade. China's share of world oil consumption is approaching one-tenth: between 1999 and 2003, the country accounted for about 40% of global oil consumption growth. As a user of steel, China is the largest in the world. In addition, it is expected to surpass the United States in 2005 as the world's largest consumer of aluminum. Figure 12. Aluminium consumption in 2003. The rapid growth of China and other emerging economies is good for the global economy. There is a locomotive for growth. At the same time, it means that many of the goods and services that used to be produced in developed countries are now produced in these lower-cost countries. Figure 10. China's share of world imports Figure 11. Steel consumption in 2002. The production structures of developed countries must adapt to the new division of labor. Adaptation creates more problems for some countries or regions than for others. However, there are still opportunities, as the rapid growth of China (and other countries) means that their imports are also growing rapidly. For others, this means opportunities to increase exports quickly. China's peculiarity is that, although the country is poor, it finances its own large investments mainly by itself. It has a very high saving rate and a current account surplus. Due to the rapid growth and interesting profit expectations, the country is flooded with its main own. In order to prevent the currency from strengthening, the Chinese authorities are forced to constantly buy foreign currency. The expansion of foreign exchange reserves feeds credit expansion, some of which goes to finance efficient and some of which goes to finance efficient investments. This, too, is part of the global imbalance when it is understood as a situation that cannot continue in the same way for very long. Correction of the US dual deficit Above, I have described and interpreted a number of well-known facts. I am now trying to put these pieces together by starting with the twin deficit of the United States. I consider it unbalanced in the same sense as above: the expansion of the budget deficit and the current account deficit cannot continue for very long. Even the current level is unsustainable, but it may persist for some time. Such imbalances are usually resolved in some way, uncontrollably or in a controlled manner. Unmanaged solution The uncontrolled solution for the US is accompanied by a sharp, possibly over-the-top weakening of the dollar as foreign investors exit the dollar. In such a situation, interest rates on dollar-denominated bonds rise. The situation could get even worse if the rise in long-term interest rates pushed house prices down, causing a sharp rise in the saving rate of American households. In such a situation, stock prices would also take a downward turn, pulling prices down globally. The US economy would plunge into a serious recession and drag the global economy with it. As a counterweight to the weakening of the dollar, the euro would strengthen sharply, especially if the Asian monetary authorities kept their currencies at a fixed ratio to the dolla-rii. A strengthening of the euro and a global economic downturn would drag the euro area towards deflation. Although an uncontrollable solution can be prevented, it cannot be achieved solely by economic policy in the right direction. Economic structures also need to adapt to the new global economic environment. However, the measures taken by one region or country are not sufficient, and measures and adaptations are needed in the United States, China and Europe. Managed solution What would a managed solution be like? What kind of elements are included in it? At least the following have been offered: United states a5 the gradual tightening of monetary policy will continue; a5 putting the federal budget deficit on a progressively shrinking path; a5 the household saving rate is rising China a5 overheating control, which in due course will also be accompanied by currency revaluation; Euro area a5 monetary policy will remain accommodative; a5 the strengthening of the euro area and, in particular, the productivity of its services sector; Figure 13 . A text box that lists em. Things. A year ago, the Bank of Finland made model calculations of the adjustment paths of the US current account. The starting point was a contraction of the current account by 2 percentage points relative to GDP. Such a result was achieved in two different ways. In the first option, this was achieved by reducing the permanent income of consumers and thereby increasing the household saving rate. In the second option, a similar reduction in the deficit was achieved by increasing the risk premium for dollar investments. Among the options, the latter corresponds to an uncontrollable solution. In it, the dollar weakens by more than 20% in nominal terms, inflation rises in the United States, and as a result, monetary policy tightens and interest rates rise. Consumption and investment are both shrinking. The current account deficit is decreasing as a result of export growth and contraction in imports. In the rest of the world (the euro area), domestic demand is picking up, but declining net exports are pushing real GDP growth to zero. Prices start to fall, and monetary policy collides with a zero interest rate constraint. The previous option, the rise in saving for American households, is much more favorable in response to a controlled solution. Here, too, the dollar weakens in real terms, but not nominally. Inflationary pressures will remain in place and monetary policy could be eased both in the United States and in the rest of the world (euro area). Such a solution would be supported by a reduction in the US federal budget deficit, which would also reduce the need for an increase in the household saving rate. However, it is not very easy to influence the saving rate through direct house policy measures. Similar calculations have been carried out by the OECD Secretariat. Their results were presented in a review published last summer. Also, according to these calculations, controlled adaptation is difficult if it takes place through only one channel. China's exchange rate policy Hopes have been placed on China from both Europeans and Americans to revaluate or float the currency. Europeans justify this by sharing the burden: while the underlying factors for the depreciation of the dollar originate in the United States, the euro area will suffer an unreasonably large part of the adjustment burden because of the desire of China and some other countries to follow the dollar. The Americans, on the other hand, would see the renminbi stronger because competition from China in the US market would ease a little. A 10% revaluation of the Chinese currency, the Renminbi, would weaken the US effective (trade-weight) exchange rate by only 1%. It feels awkward when there is already a 20% effective deterioration behind it. No imaginable revaluation of the renminbi will change the fact that the level of costs in China will remain low compared to the United States or other developed countries. Floating the currency would likely lead to a strengthening of the renminbi, but the question is whether china's financial system and money market mechanisms are ripe to operate under floating-rate conditions. In order to function well, capital movements should be free and domestic money markets should function well in such a way that market prices effectively reflect all available information, including monetary policy expectations. China is not at this stage of development yet. The revaluation of the Chinese currency could contribute to facilitating adjustment. The best justification for revaluation comes from the fact that the Chinese authorities themselves see it as a need to curb credit expansion or to break rising inflationary pressures. China will make its decisions within a timeframe that it has decided for itself, when the time comes. Challenges facing Europe Europeans have traditionally tended to take a stronger view of exchange rate movements than Americans. This is understandable in that, before Economic and Monetary Union, each European currency area was small compared to the United States. In small and open economies, the effects of exchange rate changes are large, while in large and closed economies these effects are small. The situation should be different now that the euro area is also a large and relatively closed currency area. Trade outside the region accounts for 17-18% of GDP. In the United States, the corresponding figure is even lower. It is precisely because the share of foreign trade is very small that a major change in the exchange rate is needed in order for it to have a significant impact on the external balance. Europeans have tended to blame others for the problems caused by the appreciation of the euro and to expect corrective measures from others. An example is the calls for a reduction in budget deficits in the United States and a revaluation of the currency in China. As noted above, there are good arguments for these wishes. But we also need to ask what europe can do to alleviate the pain of a strong euro and to promote a controlled dismantling of global imbalances. Accommodative monetary and fiscal policy Many commentators have suggested that the euro area's domestic demand should be boosted by accommodative monetary and fiscal policies. The implementation of these proposals would mean accepting higher budget deficits, regardless of the constraints of the Stability and Growth Pact, and an even lighter financial policy. It has even been suggested that the European Central Bank should counterattack and resolutely weaken the euro by lowering interest rates and using currency interventions. It is difficult to see how a significant fiscal stimulus in euro area countries would help to reduce the US current account deficit. Monetary policy stance is currently accommodative. It can remain so as long as inflation and inflation expectations remain low. This does not mean that short-term interest rates in the euro area will not rise towards a neutral level in due course. An explicit attempt to weaken the euro by easing monetary policy or by means of monetary intervention would be a path of destruction. It would be reminiscent of the so-called .... the path of competing de-powers and would take even further away from the controlled solution of global imbalances. Productivity of the services sector in the euro area American researchers Maurice Obstfeldt and Kenneth Rogoff have considered whether an increase in productivity in the euro area services sector could make the us exchange-rate adjustment process more painless for all parties involved. The real depreciation of the dollar, which is inevitably associated with the adjustment to the current situation, means that American products will become cheaper and demand for them in Europe will increase. Similarly, exports from euro area countries will contract or grow more slowly. However, if productivity were to rise in the services sector in euro area countries, it would counteract the appreciation of the currency. As the prices of services fall, the real income of citizens increases, which is reflected not only in the increase in demand for services, but also for goods. This would benefit both US exports and euro area domestic demand. The fastest way to influence productivity growth in the services sector is to increase competition. This brings us back to the same issues that have been discussed at length at European level, namely structural reforms. In this respect, for example, the adoption of the Services Directive, which is being discussed in the Council of the EU, is important. It would open up the closed sector to wider competition. This would contribute to facilitating the dismantling of global imbalances in a controlled manner. However, structural reforms are necessary even without imbalances: they play a key role in raising living standards and prosperity. Attention to this issue has recently been paid, for example, in the calculations of the IMF and the Bank of Finland. Figure 14: Intensification of competition in product markets The link between increased competition and well-being is roughly described as follows. From the point of view of purely economic theory, the lack of competition is synonymous with imperfect competition. Imperfect competition in the commodity market, for example, is reflected in the fact that companies produce less, but at a higher price. This reduces the number of consumers well Similarly, the lack of competition in the labour market means that wages are higher and employment is correspondingly lower. A higher level of wages means higher costs for companies, which they pass on to the prices of their products. Thus, a lack of competition in the labour market also means a higher price level in the economy. In turn, the intensification of competition can be interpreted in such analyses as a reduction in price/wage margins: profits are reduced, economic activity becomes more efficient and supply is more sensitive to market changes. The intensification of competition in product and labour markets can therefore be expected to mean, in the long term, an increase in the level of output of the economy and lower prices. If the increased production is carried out domestically, then the increase in demand will eventually encourage companies to increase their investments. A reduction in corporate profits due to increased competition in the commodity market may, in the initial phase, reduce the so-called 'soft market'. through wealth effects on private consumption. However, this is temporary. A higher level of production usually requires an increase in labour input. This, together with the fall in the price level, will eventually lead to an increase in real wages and household incomes, a recovery in consumption and, consequently, an increase in prosperity. How great, then, could the overall economic impact be? Figure 15. Increased competition in Europe: assessing the long-term impact using the IMF's GEM model Calculations by the International Monetary Fund show that if competition in the product and labour markets in the euro area were to increase to the same level as in the United States, the effects on the real economy would be considerable. The calculations estimate that output in the euro area could rise by more than 10%. This would significantly reduce the gap in living standards between the United States and Europe. IMF calculations also show that increased competition in the euro area would have spill-over effects on the rest of the world. Production and consumption could rise by around one per cent relative to the baseline situation. Thus, prosperity would increase both in the euro area and in the surrounding global economy. The Bank of Finland has also assessed the effects of increased competition. In the autumn of 2004, the Euro & Talous magazine used the Bank of Finland's Aino model to make initial calculations of the effects of increased competition in product markets. These calculations came to the same conclusion as those of the IMF: in the long run, increased competition in product markets would lead to an increase in consumption and investment. The March 2005 issue of Euro&Talous, on the other hand, examined, in accordance with IMF calculations, a situation in which competitiveness would increase in both product and labour markets at the same time. The main results are presented in the following table. Figure 16. Tightening competition in the commodity and labour markets in Finland d0 results of the Aino model As the economy adjusts to the new equilibrium, private production will grow, fuelled by private consumption. In the long term, this will be reflected in the rise in employment and the increase in investment. The real wage level will rise and the real exchange rate will also be devalued as a result of the fall in the domestic price level. The increase in exports in relation to imports is also notable. This is due to the increased competitiveness of the economy. Of course, such model calculations are only indicative and the uncertainty associated with them is quite high. However, they contribute to the generally accepted view that the liberalisation of product markets has a very positive impact on productivity and consumer welfare. Increased competition forces us to benefit ICT, to seek new business models and processes. As far as the labour market is concerned, the situation is more problematic. This has been well seen in the directive on the liberalisation of services. But even in this area, progress in learning from the best of European practices and applying them to national circumstances is of paramount importance. Summary A manifestation of global imbalances has been defined as the dual deficit of the USA. We can talk about imbalances in the sense that the current situation is clearly unsustainable: the budget deficit and the current account deficit cannot always remain at the current level. The contraction of both deficits will be imminent at some point. It is not even necessary to completely eliminate the current account deficit, because the USA still has a favourable demographic for the time being and, as a result of immigration, the number of employees is increasing. Federal indebtedness is not yet alarmingly high on a European scale either. There is therefore time for the adjustment to take place in a controlled manner. While the dual deficit is a U.S. problem, it is also a global concern. The growth of Asian countries and the economic policy strategy that emphasizes exports have contributed to making room for the us current account deficit to widen. Europe's supply conditions are such that it seems to be suffering more from the appreciation of the euro than the United States suffered from the appreciation of the dollar a few years ago. However, since the dual deficit is first and foremost a US problem, an orderly adjustment requires a slowdown in the growth of domestic demand in the US. It is supported by the gradual tightening of monetary policy and the gradual reduction of the budget deficit. A controlled solution should also be accompanied by a gradual increase in the household saving rate. However, it should be borne in mind all the time that all solutions, including a controlled solution, are accompanied by a real weakening of the dollar. A significant part of it has already happened. Whether this will be enough or whether the dollar will weaken further, there is no need to speculate here. The challenge for Europe is to strengthen its adaptability. At the same time, tolerance to fluctuations in the exchange rate will be strengthened. An adaptable economy is better able to respond to a changing environment. It also creates incentives to increase productivity in all sectors. The rapid increase in productivity in the service sector over the past 10 years separates the United States from Europe. Europe therefore has catching up to do. Increasing competition automatically increases the pressure to increase productivity in the service market. Such a development in this situation would also contribute to facilitating the controlled dismantling of global imbalances.

Kiinan erikoisuus on se, ett vaikka maa on kyh, se rahoittaa omat suuret in-vestointinsa posin itse. Sen sstmisaste on hyvin korkea, ja vaihtotase on ylijminen. Nopean kasvun ja kiinnostavien tuotto-odotusten vuoksi maahan virtaa p-omia. Estkseen valuutan vahvistumisen, Kiinan viranomaiset joutuvat osta-maan jatkuvasti ulkomaanvaluuttaa. Valuuttavarannon paisuminen ruokkii luottoekspansiota, mist osa menee tehokkaiden ja osa tehottomien investoin-tien rahoittamiseen. Mys tm on osa globaalista eptasapainoa, kun sill ymmrretn tilannetta, joka ei samankaltaisena voi jatkua kovin pitkn. Yhdysvaltain kaksoisvajeen korjautuminen Edell olen kuvannut ja tulkinnut joukon hyvin tunnettuja tosiasioita. Yritn nyt koota nit paloja yhteen lhtemll liikkeelle Yhdysvaltain kak-soisvajeesta. Pidn sit eptasapainoisena samassa mieless kuin yll: budjetti-vajeen ja vaihtotaseen alijmn paisuminen eivt voi jatkua kovin pitkn. Nykyinenkin taso on kestmtn, mutta se voi sily jonkin aikaa. Tllaiset eptasapainot yleens ratkeavat jollakin tavalla, hallitsemattomasti tai hallitusti. Hallitsematon ratkaisu Hallitsemattomaan ratkaisuun USA:n osalta liittyy dollarin jyrkk, mahdolli-sesti yliampuva heikkeneminen, kun ulkomaiset sijoittajat irtautuvat dollarista. Tllaisessa tilanteessa dollarimristen joukkovelkakirjojen korot nousevat. Tilanne voisi pahentua entisestn, jos pitkien korkojen nousu painaisi asunto-hinnat laskuun, jolloin amerikkalaisten kotitalouksien sstmisaste nousisi jyrksti. Mys osakkeiden hinnat kntyisivt tllaisessa tilanteessa laskuun veten kursseja alaspin maailmanlaajuisesti. Yhdysvaltain talous ajautuisi va-kavaan taantumaan ja vetisi maailmantalouden mukanaan. Dollarin heikkenemisen vastapainona euro vahvistuisi jyrksti varsinkin, jos Aasian rahaviranomaiset pitisivt valuuttansa yh kiintess suhteessa dolla-riin. Euron vahvistuminen ja maailmantalouden taantuminen vetisisivt euro-alueen kohti deflaatiota. Vaikka hallitsemattoman ratkaisun toteutuminen on estettviss, siihen ei ps-t yksinomaan oikeansuuntaisella talouspolitiikalla. Mys talouksien rakentei-den on sopeuduttava uuteen maailmantalouden ympristn. Yhden alueen tai maan toimenpiteet eivt kuitenkaan ole riittvi, vaan toimenpiteit ja sopeu-tumista tarvitaan niin Yhdysvalloissa, Kiinassa kuin Euroopassakin. Hallittu ratkaisu Millainen olisi hallittu ratkaisu? Millaisia elementtej siihen kuuluu? Ainakin seuraavia on tarjottu: Yhdysvalloissa  rahapolitiikan asteittaista kiristmist jatketaan  liittovaltion budjettialijm saatetaan asteittain supistuvalle uralle  kotitalouksien sstmisaste nousee Kiinassa  ylikuumenemisen hallinta, johon liittyy aikanaan mys valuutan reval-vointi Euroalueella  rahapolitiikka jatkuu kasvua tukevana  euroalue vahvistuu ja erityisesti sen palvelusektorin tuottavuus nousee Kuva 13 . Tekstiruutu, jossa on lueteltu em. asiat. Suomen Pankissa tehtiin vuosi sitten mallilaskelmia USA:n vaihtotaseen vaih-toehtoisista sopeutumisurista. Lhtkohtana oli vaihtotaseen supistuminen 2 prosenttiyksikll suhteessa bruttokansantuotteeseen. Tllainen tulos saatiin aikaan kahdella eri tavalla. Ensimmisess vaihtoehdos-sa thn pstiin alentamalla kuluttajien pysyvistuloa ja sit kautta nostamalla kotitalouksien sstmisastetta. Toisessa vaihtoehdossa vastaavan suuruiseen vajeen supistumiseen pstiin nostamalla dollarisijoitusten riskipreemiota. Vaihtoehdoista jlkimminen vastaa hallitsematonta ratkaisua. Siin dollari heikkenee nimellisesti yli 20 prosenttia, inflaatio kiihtyy Yhdysvalloissa, min-k seurauksena rahapolitiikka kiristyy ja korot nousevat. Kulutus ja investoin-nit molemmat supistuvat. Vaihtotaseen vaje pienenee viennin kasvun ja tuon-nin supistumisen seurauksena. Muussa maailmassa (euroalueella) kotimainen kysynt vilkastuu, mutta pienenev nettovienti pudottaa kokonaistuotannon kasvun nollille. Hinnat kntyvt laskuun, ja rahapolitiikka trm nollakorko-rajoitukseen. Edellinen vaihtoehto, amerikkalaisten kotitalouksien sstmisen nousu, on paljon suopeampi vastaten hallittua ratkaisua. Siinkin dollari heikentyy reaali-sesti, mutta ei nimellisesti. Inflaatiopaineet pysyvt poissa ja rahapolitiikkaa voidaan kevent sek Yhdysvalloissa ett muussa maailmassa (euroalueella). Tllaista ratkaisua tukisi se, ett Yhdysvaltain liittovaltion budjettialijm supistetaan, mik vhentisi mys kotitalouksien sstmisasteen nousun tar-vetta. Sstmisasteeseen ei kuitenkaan ole kovin helppo vaikuttaa suorin talo-uspoliittisin toimin. OECD:n sihteerist on tehnyt vastaavia laskelmia. Niiden tuloksia esitettiin viime kesn julkaistussa katsauksessa. Mys niden laskelmien mukaan hal-littu sopeutuminen on vaikeaa, jos se tapahtuu vain yhden kanavan kautta. Kiinan valuuttakurssipolitiikka Kiinalle on kohdistettu toivomuksia sek eurooppalaisten ett amerikkalaisten suunnalta valuutan revalvoimiseksi tai kelluttamiseksi. Eurooppalaiset peruste-levat tt taakan jaolla: kun dollarin heikkenemisen taustatekijt ovat lhtisin Yhdysvalloista, euroalue joutuu krsimn sopeutumistaakasta kohtuuttoman suuren osan sen takia, ett Kiina ja ert muut maat haluavat seurata dollaria. Amerikkalaiset puolestaan nkisivt renminbin vahvempana sen vuoksi, ett Kiinasta tuleva kilpailu Yhdysvaltain markkinoilla vhn hellittisi. Kiinan valuutan, Renminbin revalvoiminen 10 prosentilla heikentisi USA:n efektiivist (kauppapainoista) valuuttakurssia vain 1 prosentilla. Se tuntuu v-hiselt kun takana on jo 20 prosentin efektiivinen heikkeneminen. Mikn kuviteltavissa oleva renminbin revalvointi ei muuta sit tosiasiaa, ett kustan-nustaso Kiinassa pysyy alhaisena verrattuna Yhdysvaltoihin tai muihin kehit-tyneisiin maihin. Valuutan kelluttaminen todennkisesti johtaisi renminbin vahvistumiseen, mutta kysy sopii, ovatko Kiinan rahoitusjrjestelm ja rahamarkkinameka-nismit kypsi toimimaan kelluvan kurssin oloissa. Toimiakseen hyvin p-omanliikkeiden tulisi olla vapaita ja kotimaisten rahamarkkinoiden tulisi toi-mia hyvin siten, ett markkinoilla muodostuvat hinnat tehokkaasti heijastavat kaikkea saatavilla olevaa informaatiota, ml. rahapolitiikkaa koskevia odotuk-sia. Kiina ei ole tss kehitysvaiheessa viel. Kiinan valuutan revalvointi voisi osaltaan helpottaa sopeutumista. Paras perus-telu revalvaatiolle syntyy siit, ett Kiinan viranomaiset itse nkevt sen tar-peelliseksi luottoekspansion hillitsemiseksi tai nousevien inflaatiopaineiden katkaisemiseksi. Kiina tekee ratkaisunsa itse pttmssn aikataulussa, kun se aika tulee. Euroopan haasteet Eurooppalaisilla on perinteisesti ollut tapana suhtautua valuuttakurssimuutok-siin voimakkaammin kuin amerikkalaisilla. Tm on sikli ymmrrettv, ett ennen Euroopan talous- ja rahaliittoa, jokainen eurooppalainen valuutta-alue oli Yhdysvaltoihin verrattuna pieni. Pieniss ja avoimissa talouksissa valuutta-kurssimuutosten vaikutukset ovat suuria, kun taas suurissa ja suljetuissa talo-uksissa nm vaikutukset ovat pieni. Tilanteen pitisi olla toinen nyt, kun euroaluekin on suuri ja suhteellisen suljet-tu valuutta-alue. Alueen ulkopuolelle suuntautuvan kaupan osuus on 17-18 prosenttia bruttokansantuotteesta. Yhdysvalloissa vastaava luku on viel pie-nempi. Juuri siit syyst, ett ulkomaankaupan osuus on kovin pieni, tarvitaan suuri kurssimuutos, jotta sill olisi merkittv vaikutus ulkoiseen tasapainoon. Eurooppalaisilla on ollut taipumus syytt muita euron vahvistumisen aiheut-tamista ongelmista ja odottaa muilta korjaavia toimenpiteit. Esimerkkin voi mainita vaatimukset budjettialijmien supistamisesta Yhdysvalloissa ja valuu-tan revalvoimisesta Kiinassa. Kuten edell on todettu, nille toiveille lytyy hyvi perusteluja. Mutta pit kysy mys sit, mit Euroopassa voitaisiin teh-d vahvan euron aiheuttamien kipujen lievittmiseksi ja globaalisten tasapai-nottomuuksien hallitun purkamisen edistmiseksi. Elvyttv raha- ja finanssipolitiikka Monet kommentaattorit ovat ehdottaneet euroalueelle kotimaisen kysynnn li-smist elvyttvll raha- ja finanssipolitiikalla. Niden ehdotusten toteutta-minen merkitsisi nykyist suurempien budjettialijmien hyvksymist vaka-us- ja kasvusopimuksen rajoitteista riippumatta sek entistkin kevyemp ra-hapolitiikkaa. On jopa esitetty, ett Euroopan keskuspankin tulisi tehd vasta-hykkys ja mrtietoisesti heikent euroa alentamalla korkoja ja kyttml-l valuuttainterventioita. On vaikea nhd, miten merkittv finanssipoliittinen elvytys euroalueen maissa auttaisi Yhdysvaltain vaihtotaseen vajeen supistumista. Rahapolitiikka on tll hetkell kasvua tukevaa. Se voi pysy sellaisena niin kauan kun inflaatio ja inflaatio-odotukset pysyvt matalina. Tm ei merkitse, etteik lyhyet korot euroalueellakin aikanaan nousisi kohti neutraalia tasoa. Nimenomainen pyrkiminen euron heikentmiseen rahapolitiikkaa keventml-l tai valuuttainterventioilla olisi tuhon tie. Se muistuttaisi ns. kilpailevien de-valvaatioiden tiet ja veisi entist kauemmaksi globaalisten tasapainottomuu-den hallitusta ratkaisusta. Palvelusektorin tuottavuus euroalueella Amerikkalaiset tutkijat Maurice Obstfeldt ja Kenneth Rogoff ovat pohtineet sit, voisiko euroalueen palvelusektorin tuottavuuden nousu tehd USA:n vaih-totaseen sopeutumisprosessista kivuttomamman kaikille osapuolille. Vaihtota-seen sopeutumiseen vistmtt liittyv dollarin reaalinen heikkeneminen merkitsee, ett amerikkalaiset tuotteet halpenevat ja niiden kysynt Euroopassa kasvaa. Vastaavasti euroalueen maiden vienti supistuu tai kasvaa hitaammin. Jos kuitenkin tuottavuus nousisi euroalueen maiden palvelusektorissa, se muo-dostaisi vastavoiman valuutan vahvistumiselle. Palveluiden hintojen alentuessa kansalaisten reaalitulot kasvavat, mik nkyy paitsi palveluiden mys tavaroi-den kysynnn lisntymisen. Tst hytyisivt sek Yhdysvaltojen vienti ett euroalueen kotimainen kysynt. Nopein tapa vaikuttaa tuottavuuden nousuun palvelusektorissa on kilpailun li-sminen. Nin palataan samoihin kysymyksiin, joista Euroopan tasolla on keskusteltu pitkn, nimittin rakennereformeihin. Tss mieless esimerkiksi EU:n neuvostossa ksittelyss olevan palveludirektiivin hyvksyminen on tr-ke. Se avaisi suljetun sektorin nykyist laajemmin kilpailulle. Tm omalta osaltaan helpottaisi globaalien tasapainottomuuksien purkamista hallitulla ta-valla. Rakenneuudistukset ovat kuitenkin tarpeellisia ilman tasapainottomuuk-siakin: ne ovat avainasemassa, kun pyritn elintason ja hyvinvoinnin kohot-tamiseen. Thn asiaan on viime aikoina kiinnitetty huomiota mm. IMF:n ja Suomen Pankin laskelmissa. Kuva 14: Kilpailun kiristymi-nen hydykemarkkinoilla Kilpailun lisntymisen ja hyvinvoinnin vlinen yhteys on karkeasti kuvailtuna seuraavanlainen. Puhtaasti talousteorian nkkulmasta katsoen kilpailun puute on synonyymi eptydelliselle kilpailulle. Eptydellinen kilpailu esimerkiksi hydyke-markkinoilla nkyy siin, ett yritykset tuottavat vhemmn, mutta korkeammalla hinnalla. Tm vhent kuluttajien hyvin Samoin kilpailun puute tymarkkinoilla merkitsee sit, ett palkkataso on kor-keampi ja tyllisyys vastaavasti alhaisempi. Korkeampi palkkataso merkitsee yrityksille korkeampia kustannuksia, jotka ne siirtvt tuotteidensa hintoihin. Siten mys tymarkkinoiden puutteellinen kilpailu merkitsee korkeampaa hintatasoa taloudess Kilpailun kiristyminen puolestaan voidaan tulkita tllaisissa tarkasteluissa hin-ta/palkkamarginaalien pienenemiseksi: voitot pienenevt, taloudellinen toimin-ta tehostuu ja tarjonta reagoi herkemmin markkinoiden muutoksiin. Kilpailun kiristymisen hydyke- ja tymarkkinoilla voi siis odottaa merkitse-vn pitkll aikavlill talouden tuotantotason nousua ja alhaisempaa hintata-soa. Jos lisntynyt tuotanto toteutetaan kotimaassa, kysynnn lisntyminen kannustaa yritykset lopulta lismn investointejaan. Hydykemarkkinakilpailun lisntymisest johtuva yritysten voittojen supis-tuminen voi alkuvaiheessa alentaa ns. varallisuusvaikutusten kautta yksityist kulutusta. Tm on kuitenkin vliaikaista. Korkeampi tuotannon taso edellytt yleens typanoksen kasvattamista. Tm johtaa yhdess hintatason laskun kanssa ennen pitk reaalipalkkojen ja kotita-louksien reaalitulotason nousuun, kulutuksen elpymiseen ja siten hyvinvoinnin lisntymiseen. Kuinka suuria sitten kokonaistaloudelliset vaikutukset voisivat olla? Kuvio 15. Kilpailun kiristy-minen Euroopassa: pitkn ai-kavlin vaikutusten arviointia IMF:n GEM-mallilla Kansainvlisen valuuttarahaston laskelmat osoittavat, ett jos hydyke ja ty-markkinoiden kilpailu lisntyisi euroalueella samalle tasolle kuin se on Yh-dysvalloissa, olisivat reaalitaloudelliset vaikutukset huomattavat. Laskelmissa arvioidaan, ett euroalueen tuotanto voisi kohota reilut 10 prosenttia. Tm ka-ventaisi huomattavasti elintasokuilua Yhdysvaltojen ja Euroopan vlill. IMF:n laskelmat osoittavat mys, ett euroalueen kilpailun lisntymisell oli-si heijastusvaikutuksia muualle maailmaan. Tuotanto ja kulutus voisi kohota noin prosentin verran suhteessa perustilanteeseen. Hyvinvointi lisntyisi siis sek euroalueella ett ymprivss maailmantaloudessa. Mys Suomen Pankki on arvioinut kilpailun lisntymisen vaikutuksia. Euro & Talous -lehdess syksyll 2004 Suomen Pankin Aino-mallilla tehtiin alusta-via laskelmia hydykemarkkinoiden kilpailun lisntymisen vaikutuksista. Niss laskelmissa pdyttiin samansuuntaisiin tuloksiin kuin IMF:n laskel-missakin: pitkll aikavlill hydykemarkkinakilpailun lisntyminen johtaisi kulutuksen ja investointien lisntymiseen. Maaliskuussa 2005 ilmestyneess Euro& Talous -lehdess puolestaan tarkas-teltiin IMF:n laskelmien mukaisesti tilannetta, jossa kilpailullisuus lisntyisi samanaikaisesti sek hydyke- ett tymarkkinoilla. Keskeiset tulokset esite-tn seuraavassa taulukossa. Kuva 16. Hydyke- ja tymarkki-nakilpailun kiristyminen Suomes-sa  Aino-mallin tuloksia Talouden sopeuduttua uuteen tasapainoon yksityinen tuotanto kasvaa yksityi-sen kulutuksen ruokkimana. Tm heijastuu pitkll aikavlill tyllisyyden nousuun sek investointien vilkastumiseen. Reaalipalkkataso kohoaa ja mys reaalinen valuuttakurssi devalvoituu kotimaisen hintatason laskun seurauksena. Huomattavaa on mys viennin lisntyminen suhteessa tuontiin. Tm johtuu talouden kilpailukyvyn lisntymisest. Tllaiset mallilaskelmat ovat tietenkin vain suuntaa-antavia ja niihin liittyv epvarmuus on varsin suuri. Ne kuitenkin osaltaan tukevat sit yleisesti hyvk-sytty nkemyst, ett hydykemarkkinoiden kilpailun vapauttamisella on suu-ria mynteisi vaikutuksia tuottavuuteen ja kuluttajien hyvinvointiin. Kilpailun lisminen pakottaa hydyttmn tieto- ja viestinttekniikkaa, hakemaan uu-sia liiketoimintamalleja ja prosesseja. Tymarkkinoiden osalta tilanne on on-gelmallisempi. Tm on nhty hyvin palvelujen vapauttamista koskevan direk-tiivin yhteydess. Mutta tllkin alueella eteneminen siten, ett opitaan par-haista eurooppalaisista kytnnist ja sovelletaan niit kansallisiin olosuhtei-siin, on ensiarvoisen trke. Yhteenveto Globaalisen eptasapainon ilmentymksi on mritelty USA:n kaksoisvaje. Eptasapainosta voidaan puhua siin mieless, ett nykyinen tilanne on selvsti kestmtn: budjettialijm ja vaihtotaseen alijm eivt voi alati pysy ny-kyisen suuruisina. Molempien vajeiden supistuminen on jossain vaiheessa edess. Vaihtotaseen alijmst ei edes tarvitse pst kokonaan eroon, koska USA:lla on viel toistaiseksi suotuisa demografia ja maahanmuuton seurauk-sena tyvoiman mr kasvaa. Liittovaltion velkaantuminen ei sekn viel ole eurooppalaisessa mittakaavassa hlyttvn korkea. Aikaa siis on sille, ett so-peutuminen voi tapahtua hallitusti. Vaikka kaksoisvaje on Yhdysvaltain ongelma, se on mys globaalinen huolen aihe. Aasian maiden kasvu ja vienti korostava talouspoliittinen strategia ovat osaltaan olleet tekemss tilaa USA:n vaihtotaseen vajeen paisumiselle. Eu-roopan tarjontaolosuhteet ovat sellaiset, ett se tuntuu krsivn euron vahvis-tumisesta enemmn kuin Yhdysvallat krsi dollarin vahvistumisesta muutama vuosi sitten. Koska kuitenkin kaksoisvaje on ennen muuta Yhdysvaltain ongelma, hallittu sopeutuminen edellytt kotimaisen kysynnn kasvun hidastumista Yhdysval-loissa. Sit tukevat rahapolitiikan asteittainen kiristyminen ja budjettialijmn asteittainen supistaminen. Hallittuun ratkaisuun tulisi liitty mys kotitalouksi-en sstmisasteen asteittainen nousu. On kuitenkin syyt pit koko ajan mieless, ett kaikkiin ratkaisuihin, mys hallittuun ratkaisuun, liittyy dollarin reaalinen heikkeneminen. Siit merkittv osa on jo tapahtunut. Riittk tm vai heikkeneek dollari lis, ei tss kan-nata ryhty arvailemaan. Euroopan haasteena on vahvistaa sopeutumiskykyn. Samalla sietokyky va-luuttakurssivaihteluiden varalta vahvistuu. Sopeutumiskykyinen talous pystyy paremmin vastaamaan muuttuvaan ympristn. Se luo mys kannusteita tuot-tavuuden kohottamiseksi kaikilla toimialoilla. Nopea tuottavuuden nousu palvelusektorissa 10 viime vuoden aikana erottaa Yhdysvallat Euroopasta. Euroopalla on nin ollen kiinni otettavaa. Kilpailun lisminen lis automaattisesti painetta tuottavuuden nostamiseen palvelusek-torilla. Tllainen kehitys tss tilanteessa helpottaisi omalta osaltaan mys glo-baalisten tasapainottomuuksien hallittua purkamista.

Title: Speech on "Household indebtedness and housing market" at the XXVII National Housing and Community Day
text: PUBLICATION FREE 12.5.2005 at 10.30 Director-General Erkki Liikanen XXVII National Housing and Community Day 12.5.2005, Finlandia Hall Household indebtedness and the housing market Developments in the housing market are the subject of constant monitoring by monetary policymakers. A central theme in the monetary policy debate has been the impact of changes in interest rates on house prices and the position of mortgage indebted people. The Bank of Finland has a long tradition in this debate. Already in the transformation of the real estate market in the 1920s, the then Governor of the Bank of Finland, Risto Ryti, warned against over-lending to the real estate sector. The price development of dwellings in Finland has been unstable in the past decades. The problem of instability was also raised, among other things. In 2002, in the report of an international group of experts that assessed Finnish housing financing. We experienced the strongest fluctuations in house prices after the wars, but instability has also been common at other times. (Figure 1) Significant spikes in growth occurred in the early 1970s and late 1980s. The spike in house prices in the early 1970s arose in a situation where the economy was recovering after the recession. In the spring of 1972, the Bank of Finland, in a circular, urged financial institutions to favour productive investment and lending to support residential construction, while at the same time reducing the interest rate on central bank credit to commercial banks. In addition to the easing of monetary policy, the ensuing growth in aggregate demand was surprising. The housing market overheated. Interest rates were adjusted upwards in 1973. The events of 19881990 are still fresh in many people's memories. Following the liberalisation of financial markets and the deregulation of credit, the stock of mortgages and house prices rose sharply. This was followed, both historically and internationally, by an exceptionally large fall in housing prices during the recession years of the 1990s. The concept of 'two-dwelling trap', which became common at the time, is a sad reminder of the concern about the instability of the housing market. Chart 1 What is the cause of the instability of the housing market? At best, housing prices would reflect the steady flow of well-being that housing brings us. However, such a wish is usually not fulfilled, and house prices fluctuate with the economic cycle with household income, financial conditions, unemployment, and other cyclical factors. The strongest price changes in the housing market are due to changes in demand. They, on the other hand, are influenced by interest rates and income expectations. When the supply of housing is rigid in the short term, prices react sensitively to fluctuations in demand. The instability of housing prices in the past decades can be partly understood against the background of the structure of Finland's national economy. A couple of decades ago, Finnish exports were still strongly focused on the forest and metal industries. Foreign trade has been an important source of wealth, but at the same time Finns got used to the fact that international economic cycles rocked the national economy. After the transformation of the 1990s, the structure of the economy is now stronger than before to withstand fluctuations in international economic cycles. Exports have diversified with the breakthrough of high technology, and the solvency of our companies is good. Although Finland is still dependent on international economic cycles, the housing market has no longer been destabilised by the recent difficult years of the forest industry. Monetary policy also has an impact on the stability of the housing market. In some industrialised countries, the situation in the housing market has overheated even alarmingly during the low interest rate in recent years. In the United Kingdom, Spain and France, the rate of house price growth has exceeded 15% for several years in a row in the current decade (Figure 2). In Finland, as in the other Nordic countries, the development of house prices has been faster than the general price level. The rise in house prices in Finland has not been exceptionally fast, rather the European average. Chart 2 In their recent assessments, key international organisations such as the International Monetary Fund and the OECD have highlighted the impact of financial market liberalisation on the development of the housing market.1 We completed the liberalisation of financial markets in the early 1990s, and the deregulation of rents by the mid-1990s. As a result of deregulation, the rental housing market has recovered and the mortgage market has diversified. Banks have introduced new types of lending products to the market, and the length of mortgage loans has grown to the average level by European standards. Mortgage margins have narrowed by more than half a percentage point in the current decade alone. But the transition from regulated conditions to a free situation was not easy. The road passed through the crisis. Many still remember the transition of the late 1980s from regulated conditions, when first lending was heavily rationed and even foreign currency loans, heavily marketed. The temptation to become indebted was increased by the extensive right to deduct interest. A housing price bubble was created, and the price level of dwellings was detached from the fundamentals of the national economy. A self-reinforcing spiral was born: people bought because they expected the rise in prices to continue, and the price increase continued because people bought. When this cycle was then broken, prices plummeted. The sharp fall in prices created serious problems for many households. After the liberalisation of the financial markets, the Finnish economy was in the throes of intense changes, and it was difficult to find an anchor for expectations. The conditions for the creation of a price bubble were favourable. Now these extraordinary challenges are behind us. Today, many factors speak in favor of a more stable future in the housing market. The export industry has diversified. The real economy is stronger than before to withstand fluctuations in the international economy. Domestic demand no longer reacts to international economic cycles in the same way as before. Accession to the euro area has stabilised the evolution of interest rates. Although our housing market is still partly in the throes of change, many pitfalls have already passed. Deregulation initially caused the housing market to become unbalanced, but it is now possible to enjoy the fruits of deregulation and increased competition. These include the recovery of the rental housing market, the diversified mortgage market, and low-cost mortgages. 1 Esim. BIS Quarterly Review, March 2004; Gatte P., Girouard N., Price R. and Andre C. (2004), "Housing Markets, Wealth and the Business Cycle", OECD Economics Department Working Papers No. 394, 7.12.2004; Real and financial effects of bursting asset price bubbles", IMF World Economic Outlook Growth and Institutions, April 2003. In the post-liberalisation of the financial markets, the main challenges facing our housing policy are no longer focused on the problem of access to finance in the same way as before. In the new situation, the structural change in housing is a major challenge for housing policy. According to international comparative studies, Finns still live quite overcrowded compared to other industrialised countries. With short mortgages and tight repayment schedules, young families didn't have a decent chance of expanding their homes at the point in their lives when space was most needed. Traditionally, a spacious apartment could only be accessed when the children of the family were already starting to look for life outside the home. This situation is changing. As housing financing works and long-term mortgages are available, more and more families with children are hoping to get a more spacious home at an earlier stage than before. However, changes in the availability of funding alone will not be enough to make this wish a reality. Residential construction must be able to meet the challenge of demand. At the same time, care must be taken to ensure that indebtedness remains under control and that the events of the late 1980s are not repeated. The structural change in the demand for housing is visible in construction in that the size of new dwellings has increased. With new construction, the average size of apartments will increase, currently slightly less than 80 square meters. On the other hand, the volume of construction investments has been lower in the current decade than in the early 1980s, for example. One of the bottlenecks in construction has been the availability of plot land, especially in the Helsinki metropolitan area and other growth centres. Land prices have risen at an alarming rate in recent years. To make matters worse, there is a risk that the benefits of financial liberalisation and a light monetary policy will trickle down. According to a study by the Association of Finnish Local and Regional Authorities, the most important problems in plot production are related to zoning. The task of the decision-makers is to decide how to get enough plot land zoned in municipalities for the needs of new construction. The development of land prices leaves no room for doubt: supply has not been able to meet the challenge of demand. There is no shortage of buildable land in Finland. Chart 3 What, then, is the current state of our housing market more broadly? Concerns about the high cost of housing are often raised in the media. It is often asked whether we are now in the same situation as we were in 1988-1990. The concern is understandable in that house prices in Finland have risen somewhat faster than household incomes and rents in recent years. At the Bank of Finland, the situation in the housing market has been assessed by economist Risto Herrala, among others.2 Overall, supply bottlenecks, especially the high cost of plot land, have accelerated housing price inflation. However, our housing market is not in the kind of overheated state that was experienced in the late 1980s. Although house prices are now at a high level relative to household income, the calculations do not suggest that the price level has become unrealistic for households. 2 Herrala, R. (14.2.2005), "Assessment of the situation in the housing market", memorandum. The example illustrates this aspect (Figure 4). Consider a family buying a hundred-square-metre apartment with an 80% debt share.3 According to a rough calculation, about ten years ago, the resulting annual financial expenditure, the sum of interest and repayments after taxes, was about 55 percent of the median household's annual income. At the moment, the financial expenditure arising from the purchase of a dwelling of a similar size is "only" 40 per cent of the median household's annual income. Although house prices have risen, the increase in household incomes, lower interest rates, and longer loan periods have more than compensated for this change for the home buyer. Viewed in this way, the price level of dwellings does not seem unreasonable and the rise in house prices in recent years does not appear to be particularly worrying. However, it should be noted that the calculation described above describes precisely the situation of the average household, and not, for example, the situation of a household whose housing level depends on the price development of plots in greater Helsinki. Chart 44 3 The average floor area of the apartments is currently just under 80 m2. An apartment of one hundred square meters is taken as the basis for an example calculation as an equal number that is easy to remember and relate in one's mind to an apartment of the size one wants. The conclusions drawn from the calculation in the text do not change even if an apartment of another size is taken as the object of the calculation. 4 The financial expenditure is the sum of the estimated repayments and interest expenses according to the loan plan. Loan repayments have been estimated on the assumption that the purchase of a square metre of housing will be financed by an 80% debt financing share, that the loan will be evenly shortened, and that the maturity of the loan will increase steadily from 11 to 16 years between 1998 and 2004. If. the change in the maturity of the loan is in line with the report on saving and credit use published by the banking association in 2004. The interest expense has been estimated by applying to the loan amount the average interest rate on new loans presented in the Bank of Finland's financial market statistics after the interest deduction according to the withholding tax rate. Similarly, a comparison between owner-occupied housing and rental housing does not suggest that the housing market is unbalanced. The prices of owner-occupied dwellings have risen faster than the rent level in recent years, but this happens when interest rates fall. The low interest rate level contributes to reducing the opportunity cost of owner-occupied housing compared to rental housing. Recently, some large investors have been selling their properties that were rental apartments, some of which have been converted into owner-occupied apartments. However, this cannot be seen as a sign of market imbalances, but rather as a sign of the adaptability of the market. Supply adjusts to the prevailing demand situation. The availability of rental apartments is still good overall. One of the characteristics of the transformation of the housing market in recent years has been the rapid growth in housing indebtedness. In Finland, households' housing loan stock has grown by more than 10% every year during the current decade. The share of households with housing loans has not changed significantly: just over one in four households currently have a mortgage. The increase in the stock of debt shown in the statistics is due to the fact that larger and larger loans are being taken out when buying a house, and that loans are being paid off at a slower pace than before. In an international comparison, Finland's situation is not exceptional. The Bank for International Settlements (BIS), among others, has drawn attention to the fact that in many countries household indebtedness has grown much faster than income in recent years. Of the euro area countries, Germany and Portugal, which are plagued only by low growth, saw mortgage growth below the 10% level last year. In Finland, the average level5 of household indebtedness is not high internationally. There are many factors behind the increase in indebtedness seen in recent years. Finland's economic activity has been above the euro area average and household incomes have developed favourably. Monetary policy has supported low interest rates. Increased competition between banks has led to lower mortgage margins and longer maturity. The low interest rate level has significantly increased the demand for mortgages in Finland. As recently as ten years ago, the average interest rate on mortgages was over eight per cent. At the moment, you can get a mortgage at an average interest rate of just over three percent. However, it is important to understand the exceptional nature of the current situation. In terms of nominal interest rates, loans are now cheaper than at any time in Finland in the 150 years for which data on credit rates are available.6 Most of the fall in the interest rate on mortgages is due to a change in the general interest rate. The narrowing of interest rate margins has also played a role. Bank credit customers have benefited from increased competition between banks. 5 Households' debts in relation to disposable income are about 76%. A level of more than 100% is normal in industrial countries. Favourable economic developments and falling interest rates alone do not explain the increase in household debt. An important role has also been played by the extension of loan periods. According to data collected by the Finnish Banking Association, the maturity of new loans has increased from 11 to 16 years between 1998 and 2004. Until very recently, more and more long-term mortgages have appeared on the market. The extension of loan periods has made it possible to raise significantly larger mortgages than before. With an increase in the maturity of loans, the annual repayments of loans decrease. At the moment, the amount of credit losses due to housing indebtedness is small in Finland. However, we know from experience that the position of indebted households can quickly deteriorate if the financial situation suddenly changes. The burden on the stock of housing loans can be roughly assessed by relating the interest and repayments on the debt to households' income. It is estimated that the burden on households arising from servicing the stock of mortgage loans is currently, on average, at the same level relative to household income as it was ten years ago (Figure 5). 6 Autio, J. (1996) Interest rates in Finland 1862 - 1952, Bank of Finland discussion initiatives 7/96. Chart 57 However, when assessing the debt burden, it is not enough to look at the situation solely in the context of the prevailing interest rates. Especially in times of historically very low interest rates, the possibility of an increase in the interest rate must always be taken into account in the calculations. This is particularly important in Finland, as Finnish households tie their mortgages to variable interest rates more often than households in other euro area countries. In February this year, 98% of new mortgages taken out in Finland were at variable interest rates, which was the highest figure in the euro area. In Germany, only 17% of new mortgages were variable rate loans. In the USA, interest rates have already started to rise. There, the 3-month market rate has risen by about two percentage points since last summer, and the market is still expecting an increase of one percentage point over the next year. 7 The calculation describes the situation before taxes. What would a change in interest rates like the US, which has already taken place and included projected interest rate increases, mean for Finnish households? Figure (Figure 5) shows that in this case the index showing the debt burden would already reach almost the level that prevailed during the worst recession years in the early 1990s. In the conditions of a free financial market, the decisive decisions on indebtedness are made between the loan customer and the bank in the loan negotiation. The question of the fate of the mortgage market is whether banks and customers pay sufficient attention to risks when agreeing on a loan. In 2004, the Banking Association asked credit customers whether they were prepared for a possible increase in the mortgage interest rate and the consequent increase in the cost of servicing the loan. Slightly over 70 per cent of the households that responded said they had done so. That is all well and good, but the figure is too low. Every mortgage customer should have a clear plan for an increase in interest rates when making a loan decision. In the production of such calculations, banks play an important role. Fortunately, according to the survey, those credit customers with the largest mortgages were more likely than others to prepare for rising interest rates. Public authorities must ensure, for their part, that their actions do not encourage over-indebtedness. Currently, in Finland, the state influences the functioning of the loan market both through the right to tax deduction of interest and through the loan guarantee system. In the 1990s, the right to deduct interest was substantially reduced, and this change contributed to the recovery of the loan market. The State Guarantee Facility was set up in 1996 to reduce the need for personal guarantees in our housing market, which was in a severe recession at the time. The state guarantee is currently bought by about half of the households buying their first home. Both the state guarantee scheme and the tax deduction for loan interest contribute to the purchase of housing for families. It is important that they do not encourage excessive indebtedness. With banks competing fiercely in housing finance, and with mortgage debt growing sharply, there is a risk of excesses. The public sector must ensure, through financial supervision, that serious excesses are avoided. This warning is worth remembering. But still, I would like to reiterate the view that the transformation of our mortgage market in recent years is welcome and has brought real benefits to our households. We have left behind the old world, where debt, if it was available at all, was limited and paid off at the earliest opportunity. In the new situation, debt will be taken out for a longer period of time, and in general, a debt management programme can be agreed more flexibly to meet the needs of households. Our banks have developed methods of managing risks, and our last serious crisis is still well remembered. We also have effective financial supervision.

On kuitenkin trke ymmrt nykytilanteen poikkeuksellisuus. Nimelliskorolla mitattuna lainat ovat nyt halvempia kuin koskaan Suomessa sen 150 vuoden aikana, jolta tietoja luottokoroista on saatavilla.6 Asuntolainojen koron laskusta suurin osa johtuu yleisen korkotason muutoksesta. Oma merkityksens on mys ollut korkomarginaalien kapenemisella. Pankkien luottoasiakkaat ovat hytyneet pankkien vlisen kilpailun kiristymisest. 5 Kotitalouksien velat suhteessa kytettviss oleviin tuloihin ovat noin 76 %. Yli 100 %n taso on tavanomaista teollisuusmais-sa. Suotuisa talouskehitys ja korkojen lasku eivt yksin selit kotitalouksien velkamrn kasvua. Trke rooli on mys ollut laina-aikojen pidentymisell. Lainojen maturiteetin kasvun myt lainojen vuosilyhennykset vhenevt. Tll hetkell asuntovelkaantumisesta johtuvien luottotappioiden mr on Suomessa pieni. Kokemuksesta kuitenkin tiedmme, ett velkaantuneiden kotitalouksien asema voi nopeasti heiket jos taloudellinen tilanne killisesti muuttuu. Asuntovelkakannan rasittavuutta voidaan karkeasti arvioida suhteuttamalla velan korot ja lyhennykset kotitalouksien tuloihin. Varsinkin historiallisesti hyvin alhaisten korkojen aikana laskelmissa pit aina huomioida mys koron nousun mahdollisuus. Tm on erityisen trke Suomessa, koska suomalaiset kotitaloudet sitovat asuntolainansa muiden euromaiden kotitalouksia useammin vaihtuviin korkoihin. Kuluvan vuoden helmikuussa Suomessa otetuista uusista asuntolainoista 98 % oli vaihtuvakorkoisia, mik oli euroalueen korkein luku. Saksassa vain 17 % uusista asuntoluotoista oli vaihtuvakorkoisia. USA:ssa korot ovat jo kntyneet nousuun. Siell 3 kk markkinakorko on noussut noin kaksi prosenttiyksikk viime kesn jlkeen, ja markkinat odottavat viel prosenttiyksikn nousua seuraavan vuoden aikana. 7 Laskelmaa kuvaa tilannetta ennen veroja. Mit USA:n tyyppinen, jo toteutuneet ja ennustetut koronnousut sisltv korkotason muutos merkitsisi suomalaisille kotitalouksille? Kuviosta (kuvio 5) havaitaan, ett tss tapauksessa velkarasitusta osoittava indeksi saavuttaisi jo lhes sen tason, joka vallitsi pahimpina lamavuosina 1990-luvun alussa. Vapaiden rahoitusmarkkinoiden oloissa ratkaisevat ptkset velkaantumisesta tehdn laina-asiakkaan ja pankin vlill lainaneuvottelussa. Asuntolainamarkkinoiden kohtalon kysymys on, kiinnittvtk pankit ja asiakkaat riittv huomiota riskeihin lainasta sovittaessa. Pankkiyhdistys kysyi vuonna 2004 luottoasiakkailta, ovatko nm varautuneet asuntolainan koron mahdolliseen nousuun ja sen mukanaan tuomaan lainanhoitokulujen kasvuun. Hieman runsas 70 % vastanneista kotitalouksista ilmoitti nin tehneens. Hyv niin, mutta luku on liian alhainen. Onneksi kyselyn mukaan muita useammin korkojen nousuun olivat varautuneet ne luottoasiakkaat, joiden asuntolainat olivat suurimmat.
