Kahden viikon matkan p<8a><8a>tteeksi h<8a>nell<8a> oli valmiina ehdotus Hiili.ja ter<8a>syhteisty<9a>ksi. Molemmat tiesiv<8a>t, murtomaahiihto kirkasti ajatuksia. Toiseksi Jean Monnet<ab>n vaimo, Silvia oli my<9a>s paikalla Maison Carressa. Heill<8a> oli oma erityissuhteensa Neuvostoliittoon. Heid<8a>t oli nimitt<8a>in vihitty Moskovassa vuona 1934. Monnet oli rakastunut italialaiseen, katoliseen rouvaan illallisella Pariisissa. Aviomies oli paikalla. Eroa oli mahdoton saada. Ainoa keino oli paeta Moskovaan, joka ei tunnustanut katolista avioliittoa. Viranomaiset auttoivat heid<8a>t avioliiton satamaan. Ja viel<8a> kolmanneksi Alko Oy oli tuonut Monnet-konjakin hyllyille jo vuonna 1934. Se oli Suomessa tunnettu, parempi konjakkimerkki. Pekka Vilpas voi kertoa, kuinka paljon linnassa sit<8a> tarjottiin. Samana vuonna Monnet k<8a>rsi suuret tappiot pankkiirina San Franciscossa. Kuka j<8a>rjestitapaamisen Monnet<ab>n ja Kekkosen v<8a>lill<8a>?Olen kysynyt asiaa matka-seurueeseen kuuluneelta Ossi Sunellilta ja Pariisissa tuolloin avustajana palvelleelta Matti H<8a>kk<8a>selt<8a>. Molempien mukaan kutsujan t<8a>yty olla Louis Carr<8e>. T<8a>m<8a> oli yksinkertaisesti kutsunut naapurinsa Jean Monnet<ab>n paikalle. Suul<8a>hettil<8a>s Gunnar Palmroth olisi siihen tuskin ryhtynyt eik<8a> l<8a>hetyst<9a>neuvos M<8a>kinenk<8a><8a>n. Tapaamisen mielenkiintoa lis<8a><8a> todellakin se, ett<8a> Monnet ja de Gaulle edustivat vierailun aikaan t<8a>ysin vastakkaisia n<8a>kemyksi<8a> Euroopan integraation peruskysymyksist<8a>, syvent<8a>misest<8a> ja laajentumisesta. Presidentti de Gaullen mukaan kansallinen suvereniteetti oli loukkaamaton, h<8a>n ei hyv<8a>ksynyt vahvoja eurooppalaisia instituutiota ja suhtautui kielteisesti m<8a><8a>r<8a>enemmist<9a>p<8a><8a>t<9a>ksiin. Muutamaa vuotta my<9a>hemmin h<8a>n <d3> tyhj<8a>n tuolin politiikallaan<d3> j<8a><8a>dytti EEC:n koko toiminnan. Monnet taas katsoi, ett<8a> EEC:n tavoitteet ja tehokas p<8a><8a>t<9a>ksenteko voitiin turvata vain m<8a><8a>r<8a>enemmist<9a>s<8a><8a>nn<9a>ksill<8a> ja yhteisill<8a>, itsen<8a>isill<8a> instituutioilla. Ne olivat tehokkaan p<8a><8a>t<9a>ksenteon kaksi t<8a>rke<8a><8a> edellytyst<8a>. Ne ovat sit<8a> syvent<8a>mist<8a>. Ensimm<8a>iset EEC:n laajentumisneuvottelut olivat k<8a>ynniss<8a> Britannian, Irlannin, Tanskan ja Norjan kanssa Kekkosen vierailun aikoihin. Tavanomaiset ongelmat olivat p<9a>yd<8a>ll<8a>, ennen kaikkea maatalous. Konservatiivihallitus oli j<8a>senyyden puolesta, labour oli oppositiossa k<8a><8a>ntynyt vastaan. N<8a>m<8a> seikat de Gaulle k<8a>ytti hyv<8a>kseen, kun h<8a>n veto-oikeudellaan pani tammikuussa 1963 poikki laajentumisneuvottelut Britannian kanssa. Kolmaskin syy oli taustalla: <d3>Englannista on tullut USA:n satelliitti.. Skandinaavit ovat Englannin satelliitteja<d3>, kertoi de Gaulle tiedottajalleen Alain Peyrefittelle. Monnet taas oli laajentumiselle my<9a>nteinen. H<8a>n oli ollut kahden sodan aikana Englannissa ja kunnioitti maan demokraattisten instituutioiden ja sananvapauden traditiota. Monnet tuomitsi jyrk<8a>sti de Gaullen p<8a><8a>t<9a>ksen: " Sen sijaan, ett<8a> olisi luotu Iso-Britannian sis<8a>lt<8a>v<8a> Euroopan unioni (union) ja sen pohjalle kumppanuus Euroopan ja USA:n v<8a>lill<8a>, on saatu aikaan hajaannus (desunion) ja sen mukanaan tuomat vaarat". Vuosi Kekkosen vierailun j<8a>lkeen Eisenhower tapasi de Gaullen Pariisissa. H<8a>n kysyi Monnet<ab>sta. De Gaulle vastasi: <d3>H<8a>n tekee hyv<8a><8a> konjakkia. Valitettavasti se ei riit<8a> h<8a>nelle<d3>. Juhani Suomi arvioi Presidentti-kirjassaan, ett<8a> de Gaullessa <d3>voitiin n<8a>hd<8a>perustellustitakuumies sille, etteij<8a>rjest<9a>n (siis EEC:n)kehitys tulisi vaarantamaan Suomen etuja". Sen sijaan Monnet<ab>n tapaamisesta eik<8a> h<8a>nen k<8a>sityksist<8a><8a>n EEC:n kehityksest<8a> ole mainintaa. Suomi on juuri p<8a><8a>tt<8a>nyt toisen puheenjohtajakautensa EU:ssa. Yli 40 vuotta on kulunut Kekkosen vierailusta Pariisiin. Maailma on toinen. Mutta niin vaan samat asiat ovat asialistalla, syveneminen ja laajeneminen ja my<9a>s suhde Yhdysvaltoihin. Milt<8a> n<8a>ytt<8a><8a> de Gaullen ja Monnet<ab>n erimielisyys t<8a>m<8a>n p<8a>iv<8a>n valossa? Kun EU-puheenjohtajuus p<8a><8a>ttyi, p<8a><8a>ministeri Matti Vanhanensanoi, ett<8a> m<8a><8a>r<8a>enemmist<9a>p<8a><8a>t<9a>ksentekoa pit<8a><8a> vahvistaa. Helsingin Sanomat jopa kysyi, onko h<8a>n kaappifederalisti. Ratifioimalla EU:n perustuslain Suomi on asettunut tukemaan yhteisi<8a> instituutioita ja m<8a><8a>r<8a>enemmist<9a>p<8a><8a>t<9a>ksentekoa. Ranskan kansan<8a><8a>nestys valitsi toisen tien. Laajentumiseen Suomi on valinnut aktiivisen my<9a>nteisen linjan. Suomalainen komissaari Olli Rehn on viel<8a> laajentumisesta vastuussa komissiossa. Turkin j<8a>senyys taas kaivertaa Ranskassa pahasti. Viimeksi oikeiston presidenttiehdokas Sarkozy ilmoitti, ettei Turkin paikka ole Euroopan Unionissa. N<8a>ytt<8a><8a> silt<8a>, ett<8a> olemme asettumassa my<9a>s laajentumisessa ainakin jossain m<8a><8a>rin eri kannalle. Ent<8a> sitten suhteet Yhdysvaltoihin? Kun muistelee tunnelmia vaalien alla nelj<8a> vuotta sitten ja sit<8a> latausta, mill<8a> k<8a>siteltiin suhteita Yhdysvaltoihin, j<8a>t<8a>n n<8a>ilt<8a> osin de Gaullen ja Monnet<ab>n erimielisyydet keskustelun varaan. Ainakin n<8a>in vaalien alla. Vuonna 1962 elimme toisessa maailmassa. Mutta olisiko niin, ett<8a> Suomessa EU-j<8a>senyyden my<9a>t<8a> muutkin kuin kaappifederalistit ovat asettuneet Unionin syvent<8a>misess<8a> Monnet<ab>n kannalle de Gaullen kantaa vastaan? M<8a><8a>r<8a>enemmist<9a>t ja yhteiset instituutiot turvaavat sen, ettei EU:ssa kukaan saa hegemoniaa, mutta silti se voi toimia tehokkaasti. Monnet ei tiett<8a>v<8a>sti koskaan vieraillut Suomessa. Sen sijaan huhtikuussa vuonna 1953 Euroopan toinen perustaja.is<8a> Robert Schuman oli Helsingiss<8a> puhujavieraana. Kev<8a><8a>ll<8a> 1953 maailman huomio suuntautui Neuvostoliittoon. Stalin oli kuollut maalis-kuussa. Suurella mielenkiinnolla seurattiin uuden johdon valintaa. Stalinin hautajaisissa p<8a><8a>ministeri Urho Kekkonen edusti Suomea. Jussi M<8a>kinen muuten kertoi Kekkosen asuneen h<8a>nen luonaan. Palattuaan h<8a>n kertoi presidentti Paasikivelle, ett<8a> mielet Moskovassa olivat rauhoittuneet. Uusi johtaja Malenkov on Stalinin hengen mies ja tulee ajamaan samaa politiikkaa. Uusi hallitus oli tarkan suunnitelman mukaan j<8a>rjestetty ja Malenkov ja Berija olivat yht<8a> mielt<8a>. Schumanin vierailukutsun takana oli ollut Suomen Ulkomaankauppaliitto, mutta asian junailijana Pariisissa oli lehdist<9a>neuvos Heikki Brotherus. T<8a>m<8a> taas kertoi muistelmis-saan saaneensa siit<8a> syyst<8a> kansliap<8a><8a>llikk<9a> Tarjanteelta kirjeen, jossa h<8a>nt<8a> syytettiin oma-valtaisesta toiminnasta. Brotherus v<8a>itti kirjassaan ulkoministeri<9a>n menneen niin pitk<8a>lle, ett<8a> se pyysi Ranskan Suomen suurl<8a>hettil<8a>st<8a> peruuttamaan Schumanin vierailun. Vierailu kuitenkin toteutui kolme kuukautta sen j<8a>lkeen, kun Schuman oli j<8a><8a>nyt pois Ranskan hallituksesta. Ralf T<9a>rngren kertoi viikoittaisessa tapaamisessa presidentti Paasikivelle, ett<8a> ulkomaankauppaliiton johto haluaa tehd<8a> vierailusta suuren jutun, mutta hallitus ei. H<8a>n totesi Paasikiven p<8a>iv<8a>kirjojen mukaan, ett<8a> <d3>hallitus ei pid<8a> p<8a>iv<8a>llist<8a>, eik<8a> muuta huomiota<d3>. P<8a><8a>ministeri Urho Kekkonen ei siksi Schumania tavannut. Presidentti J.K. Paasikivi oli kuitenkin kuuntelemassa Robert Schumanin puhetta 9.4.1953 ja otti h<8a>net my<9a>s vastaan seuraavana p<8a>iv<8a>n<8a>. H<8a>n keskusteli tunnin Schumanin kanssa. Schuman arvioi Saksan tulevaisuutta ja uskoi Hiili-ja ter<8a>syhteis<9a>n osaltaan poistavan antagonismia Saksan ja Ranskan v<8a>lill<8a>. Paasikivi selosti Suomen asemaa. <d3>Schuman on tosiaan miellytt<8a>v<8a> ja intelligentti mies<d3>, tiivisti Paasikivi tapaamisensa p<8a>iv<8a>kirjoissa. Vaikka hallitus ei j<8a>rjest<8a>nyt ohjelmaa, Kekkosen hallituksen sosiaaliministeri V<8a>in<9a> Leskinen vei h<8a>net yksityiselle illalliselle Helsingin ty<9a>v<8a>entalolle, miss<8a> vieras tapasi ammattiyhdistysv<8a>ke<8a>. Ajan kuvaan kuului, ett<8a> Pravda kirjoitti vierailusta viikkoa my<9a>hemmin. Pravdan mukaan ei voitu kiist<8a><8a>, etteik<9a> Schumanin vierailulla ollut yhteytt<8a> Suomen ja Neuvostoliiton kauppavaihdon el<8a>v<9a>itt<8a>mist<8a> vastaan suunnattuun keskusteluun, johon oikeistososialistit ovat ryhtyneet. N<8a>in Leskinenkin sai osansa. Kirjoituksen oli laatinut Stefan Smirnov, joka my<9a>hemmin palveli NKP:n kansainv<8a>lisen osaston Suomi-yksik<9a>ss<8a> aina1980-luvulle saakka. Samoissa tiloissa, Paasitornin juhlasalissa, Suomi EU:n puheenjohtajamaana tarjosi viime syyskuussa ep<8a>virallisen Ecofinin virallisen illallisen, johon osallistuivat 27 eurooppalaisen maan valtiovarainministerit ja keskuspankkien p<8a><8a>johtajat. Ympyr<8a> oli sulkeutunut. Carr<8e>n talo avataan syksyll<8a> 2007 yleis<9a>lle. Carr<8e>n taloa tulee yll<8a>pit<8a>m<8a><8a>n Ranskan Alvar Aalto-yhdistys. Siksi olen esitt<8a>nyt, ett<8a> se olisi nyt hyv<8a> foorumi my<9a>s yhteisille keskusteluille.

Title: Europe's financial markets as a catalyst for economic growth at the House of the Estates
text: President Erkki Liikanen's speech "Europe's financial markets create the conditions for economic growth" at the House of the Estates . Speech . Friday 30March 2007, 12:00 AM Director-General Erkki Liikanen Speech at the Right Direction seminar at the House of the Estates 30.3.2007 Speech associated kalvosarja (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and. . interviews/documents/el_oikeasuunta_kalvot_20070328.pdf) (PDF) [ SLIDE 1] EUROPE'S FINANCIAL MARKETS CREATING THE CONDITIONS FOR ECONOMIC GROWTH [ SLIDE 2] In the historical milieu of the House of the Estates, opposite the main building of the Bank of Finland, it is natural to reflect on Finland's monetary history and wonder if there is some kind of plot in it, a red thread that takes us to modern times and helps us understand the solutions made On the surface, the birth of the Finnish markka in the 1860s and the introduction of the euro in 1999 seem to be opposing solutions. After all, it was less than 150 years ago that we got "our own money", things into our own hands: The New Mark foreshadowed, albeit after the initial difficulties, the prosperity of our country and the independence of the nation half a century later. The introduction of the euro, on the other hand, is seen as a renunciation of our own mark, our national symbol. However, such an examination forgets the root causes that gave rise to the Finnish markka in the 1860s. The Finns needed stable money that would strengthen the country's commercial links with Europe. This attempt at stable monetary conditions reflects very well the red thread of Finnish monetary history. In this sense, monetary units, the marks or the euro, have not in themselves been objectives, but rather means of achieving stability. *** [ SLIDE 3] The Crimean War, which broke out between Russia and Turkey in 1854, disrupted the monetary conditions in Finland. The redemption of rubles with silver stopped, the value of money began to decline, and silver coins disappeared from circulation. Exchange rates in relation to traditional trading partners in Sweden and northern Germany also began to fluctuate. This made it difficult to trade and use foreign credit. Finns' concerns about the instability of monetary conditions received a response from the emperor in 1860 when he granted Finland its own currency, the markka. However, due to the fact that the value of the mark was tied to the unstable banknote ruble, the reform did not bring the desired result, stability. Stability was finally brought about by the monetary reform of 1865, in which the Finnish markka was tied to the silver standard. The finalist and negotiator of this reform was J.V. Snellman, the finance manager, who was celebrated with many expenses last year. In the light of the markka's origins, Snellman appears above all as a builder of monetary stability. The purpose of the transition to the silver standard was not to isolate Finland from the rest of the world, but to strengthen ties with Europe above all through stability. *** The Square of the Bank of Finland is dominated by the statue of J.V. Snellman, which was erected only in 1923 due to the First World War. The same war washed away the stability that Snellman's monetary reform had achieved. At that time, a new foundation for the Finnish monetary system began to be laid in the shadow of Snellman's statue by Risto Ryti, first as Minister of Finance and from 1924 as governor of the Bank of Finland. Ryti wanted to integrate the markka into the international monetary system. In his presentation, he outlined: "It is not enough to have a good monetary system, it is also required that our monetary system be such that it is trusted abroad". Ryti managed to establish the value of the markka in relation to the U.S. gold dollar and, with the monetary law that came into force in 1926, formally entered into force with the gold standard. However, the next crisis was already knocking at the door, the Great Depression of the 1930s forced the international monetary system to its knees. *** [ SLIDE 4 ] The introduction of the euro in the 1990s was also preceded by a period of monetary instability in Finland. The liberalisation of financial markets and credit expansion led to an uncontrolled overheating of the economy and an increase in asset values in the late 1980s. At the beginning of the next decade, total output and asset values plummeted, external debt and budget deficits grew rapidly, unemployment rose sharply, and the country's banking system plunged into a serious crisis. The crisis was deepened by the collapse of Finland's eastern trade and the rise in international interest rates. Finland's economic crisis showed how vulnerable a fixed but adaptable monetary system can be in a world of free capital movements. In the early 1990s, the eu's entire monetary system was disrupted. The plan for the changeover to the single currency had already been confirmed in Maastricht in 1991, but monetary developments did not appear to be stabilising within the exchange rate mechanism ERM as expected, and the pressures piled up unsustainable. In 1992, many countries were forced to abandon the exchange rate linkage. Some thought that the crisis of the currencies at the same time dashed hopes of a single currency. In reality, the crisis in the ERM demonstrated how acute the need for a single currency, the euro, was! The patchwork of small currencies no longer ensured stability in the EU, where capital, goods and labour moved more freely from one country to another. A more robust weapon was needed for the resulting internal market, and the stability of exchange rates was best anchored by the common euro. Finland was among the ten other EU Member States to adopt the euro at the beginning of 1999, i.e. among the first. ********************************* Tasks of the Bank of Finland According to studies, Finns value the euro quite a lot. Citizens' confidence in their central bank is also good, but there is limited awareness of its activities. In particular, there is uncertainty about the Bank of Finland's relationship with the European Central Bank. [ SLIDE 5 ] In today's world, the Bank of Finland has two faces. On the one hand, the Bank of Finland is the national monetary authority, which it has been for almost 200 years. On the other hand, the introduction of the euro has introduced a new, fundamental element. The Bank of Finland is not only a national authority, it is also a member of the Eurosystem. The Bank of Finland is an integral part of the system that manages the use of the world's second largest currency d0 the euro. The euro area is home to more than 300 million people and includes 13 member states. Thus, the Bank of Finland sets targets for its operations related to both finland and the eurosystem. It is often said that Finland no longer has its own monetary policy. In reality, Finland has a monetary policy that is shared with 12 other EU countries. As part of its stability-oriented work with the Eurosystem, the Bank of Finland is working more closely with the European Central Bank and other national central banks than ever before in our country's monetary history. [ SLIDE 6] As a member of the Eurosystem, the Governor of the Bank of Finland sits on the Governing Council of the European Central Bank to decide on interest rates in the euro area and, at the same time, in Finland. Decisions are taken with the objective of price stability throughout the euro area and monetary policy is implemented in a decentralised manner through the national central banks. The Bank of Finland naturally assesses the effects of the single monetary policy on the Finnish economy and, on that basis, takes a position on domestic economic policy. For example, the Bank of Finland publishes an overall economic forecast twice a year. The Bank of Finland thus presents itself in this respect both as a decision-maker and in the role of an expert. [ SLIDE 7 ] Monetary policy is not the bank's only core task either. Other key functions include financial supervision, banking and money management. ********************************* Why is price stability important? [ SLIDE 8 ] In the picture below, you can see two kindred spirits. On the left is the Bank of Finland's inflation troll from 1995. At that time, the Bank of Finland distributed a brochure to Finns to raise public awareness of the problems that excessively high inflation can lead to. The second figure is the ECB's inflation monster. The picture is from educational material distributed by the Eurosystem, i.e. the European Central Bank and the national central banks of the euro area (in Finland, the Bank of Finland) to around 50,000 schools and educational institutions across the euro area. In the material, the inflation monster recklessly distributes money and drives the economy to ruin. The projects show that central banks are working to sharpen to the general public why price stability is Important. The school system has a key role to play in this. Maintaining price stability is a priority for the Eurosystem. This objective is not only enshrined in the EU Treaty, but can also be found in national legislation. Setting price stability as the main objective of the Eurosystem reflects the prevailing broad consensus that the central bank is best placed to support other economic policy objectives, such as growth and employment, by creating monetary stability. At the same time, the thinking that central banks must be given an independent role so that they can also make genuine efforts to achieve price stability has been reinforced. [ SLIDE 9 ] The notion created by A.W. Phillips of the inverse link between unemployment and inflation came to an end no later than the 1970s, when many countries experienced a combination of stagflation, high unemployment and rising prices. It was discovered that "money cannot be pushed", that is, an expansive monetary policy does not increase the volume of production (and employment) in the end at all. The only consequence is an increase in the price level and an increase in uncertainty related to the development of prices. Uncertainty has its costs. For example, due to uncertainty, investors demand more return on their portfolio investments (the so-called risk premium). This raises real interest rates, which in turn reduces investment in the economy. Similarly, wage earners who do not have confidence in price stability demand additional compensation for the risk of inflation. However, this has often fueled further inflation. Inflation also makes it difficult to compare prices, it is difficult for economic operators to distinguish the change in relative prices from the development of the general price level. Thus, price stability has a positive impact on the sustainable development of the economy and employment in many ways. It helps economic operators to make sound consumption and investment decisions, i.e. at the level of the national economy, to allocate the resources of the economy efficiently. Economic operators can focus on their actual productive activities and do not have to sacrifice time and effort to hedge against inflation. Price stability also prevents the arbitrary distribution of wealth and income. Changes in the price level affect different social groups in different ways, often the weakest suffer. [ SLIDE 10 ] The monetary policy of the euro area has been able to ensure price stability for euro area citizens. The anchor of the price stability is the Eurosystem. Its independent status and mandate based on price stability provide a good institutional basis for conducting a credible monetary policy. The Eurosystem has managed to achieve credibility and moderate interest rates, which before the birth of the euro were the prerogative of only a few countries d0 in particular Germany. [ SLIDE 11 ] Price stability also improves the efficiency of financial markets. Promoting the stability and efficiency of the financial system is, in fact, one of the core activities of the Bank of Finland. This function has been called "financial supervision" in the attached slide. I shall now focus above all on the functioning and efficiency of the financial and financial markets. ********************************* Why is the efficiency of financial markets important? The monetary and financial markets and their importance are justifiable to consider a little more closely, as it is difficult for anyone to escape them. They actually penetrate homes in the form of economic news via newspapers, radio, television and the Internet. I don't think everyone is following this economic news voluntarily and in the so-called "green light". for those who follow it, only frequently repeated words such as "interest rates", "stock prices", "investment funds", "acquisitions" or even "insider information" and "speculation" remain in the minds of the monetary and financial markets. [ SLIDE 12 ] These buzzwords, repeated daily by economic news, shape our perception of what is happening in the financial system and how it works. a5 Firstly, the functioning of the financial markets is often perceived as short-term. This is understandable, because financial news often only tells about current events: Yesterday, attention was focused on the fall in stock prices, today the main economic news is associated with the newly announced acquisition. a5 Secondly, producers of economic news cannot, at least not very easily, stop to consider the long-term effects of the functioning of the financial system. In a way, this is also understandable: why would anyone be interested in the question of, for example, how the intensification of the financial system 10-15 years ago affects today's economic growth? a5 Thirdly, even if the link between the functioning of the financial system and long-term economic growth is considered interesting in itself, it is not easy to write about it: This connection is, after all, difficult for contemporaries to perceive or measure. So writing concrete economic news on the subject is not simple. However, the link between the financial system and long-term economic growth is precisely why it is worth worrying about the functioning and efficiency of the financial system: According to economic research, well-functioning financial markets accelerate long-term economic growth. It is important to be aware of the existence of this growth effect: Long-term economic growth reflects changes in our standard of living and is therefore an important indicator of the change in the standard of living of citizens. A well-functioning financial system thus creates, at least indirectly, wealth and well-being for present and future generations. [ SLIDE 13] The modern financial system is a very complex network of networks in which the so-called "financial institutions" are located. the savings of households and businesses with financial surpluses pass through many channels and intermediaries to the final sources of financing. The financial system is needed because not all households and businesses want to use their income immediately for consumption or investment. These savings allow households whose expenditure (at least at that moment) exceeds income to finance their consumption and/or investment needs. In its simplest form, there is no need for intermediaries, in which case we are talking about the so-called middlemen. direct funding. Examples of such financing are loans between friends and other vips, or so-called vips. risky investments made by angel investors with their own money in early-stage companies. Indirect financing is referred to if a third party, such as a financial institution, is involved in the financial intermediation. The most typical example of such financing is the activities of deposit banks: they collect deposits from households and non-financial corporations and, using the funds thus obtained, finance, for example, the purchase of housing by other households (mortgages) or real investments by enterprises (corporate credit). The modern financial system has a wide variety of direct finance markets and is home to specialised financial institutions that channel indirect finance. In addition to channelling savings forward, they perform many other tasks, such as providing payment and cash services, various settlement services related to securities trading, and issuing insurance. [ SLIDE 14] Although the study supports the view that a well-functioning and efficient financial system contributes to economic growth, it should be stressed that the link between them has still not been fully established. Indeed, it sometimes seems that the financial sector and the economy are developing at the same time, supporting each other. For Finland, too, it is not clear which is the egg and which is the chicken. In fact, we also have a long tradition in the financial sector: in Finland, the first financial institution operated from 1663 to 1667 and was a branch of the Swedish Palmstruch Bank, the predecessor of sweden's current central bank, the Riksbank. The predecessor of the Bank of Finland, Waihetus-ja Laina and Depositioni Contori, was founded as early as 1811. The first savings bank was founded in Turku in 1823, finland's first commercial bank (SYP) in 1862 and the stock exchange in 1912. How these (and other) financial institutions have contributed to economic growth in Finland is not simple to determine or measure. This measurement problem is not helped by the fact that the link between the financial system and economic growth may have changed over the decades. Although in Finland, for example, commercial banks seem to have played an important role in launching the first industrial projects in the late 1800s, it is not clear to what extent they or the banking sector more generally have contributed to economic growth, for example, in the years of monetary regulation after the Second World War or in the context of the deregulation of the financial markets in the late 1980s. With the banking crisis of the early 1990s, the role of deposit banks may have changed again, as since those years the banks have become more efficient. On the other hand, at the same time, the Finnish financial system has diversified and has become slightly more stock market-oriented due to the development of the private equity industry, for example. [ SLIDE 15] Although the ensemble between the financial system and the real sector (industrial engineering and management) is not fully understood, something is at least known. A well-functioning and efficient financial system contributes to investment, economic growth and the well-being of citizens through at least three channels: It (i) lowers the cost of external financing, (ii) accelerates long-term economic growth, and (iii) helps to hedge against financial risks. [ SLIDE 16] First of all, a well-functioning and efficient financial system lowers the cost of capital. Lower cost of capital leads to an increase in investment, since traditional (neoclassical) investment theory predicts that companies will continue to invest until the marginal product from the investment is equal to the real cost of capital. This means that the lower the cost of capital, the more profitable investment targets companies have from their point of view d0 and that the more they are willing to invest. Investment growth, on the other hand, is often thought to support employment and accelerate economic growth, at least for a period of time. [ SLIDE 17] Secondly, well-functioning financial markets accelerate long-term economic growth. Growth will accelerate above all because an efficient financial sector is able to accelerate growth in total factor productivity. The growth in multi-factor productivity is important, for example, for maintaining the services of the welfare state: When total productivity grows, more goods and services can be produced than before without the need to increase the capital stock or labour input. [ SLIDE 18] This effect is largely due to the fact that countries whose financial markets and banking systems can be considered developed increase investment in growing industries more and make less investment in shrinking industries than countries where these financial institutions are less developed. The functioning of the financial system is therefore important because it affects the allocation of available resources to the best and most profitable areas for investment. This means that financial markets contribute to economic growth because they determine which sectors resources are channelled into and what kind of technological, organisational or other innovations companies and entrepreneurs can pursue through external funding. The quality of traditional and R&D investments through external funding affects, for example, how efficient and modern manufacturing methods and technologies companies use. So it is not necessarily so much a question of the quantity of funding as it is of quality. [ SLIDE 19] The flip side of this statement is an important but often overlooked characteristic of a well-functioning corporate finance market: Efficient financial markets also "prune projects", i.e. allocate funding only to a limited extent d0 if at all d0 for example, to projects, companies or industries with low chances of success and prospects for the future. [ SLIDE 20] A well-functioning financial system also contributes to the well-being of citizens through the third channel. Indeed, it helps both households and businesses to hedge against financial risks. As European integration progresses, we can talk, for example, of a deepening of the risk-sharing between regions: Diversifying investments across countries and regions using (international) capital markets is a way of sharing risks with other countries and/or regions. In other words, it is a means of protecting against disturbances that only affect one's own residential area (national economy). Such risk-sharing is possible because the disturbances affecting different regions and economies are only partly simultaneous or parallel, for better or for worse. [ SLIDE 21] Let's take an example from the United States: While, for example, the state of Massachusetts, which is slightly larger in population than Finland and in the northeastern Part of the United States, is hit by an economic shock, other states bear some of the costs of this disruption through the financial markets. This happens because residents of different states "cross-own" property/wealth in each other's territories. Thus, residents of states other than Massachusetts also suffer from the "bad luck" of the Massachusetts region, that is, corporate bankruptcies caused by the economic disruption of the example, or the fall in the value of real estate. Although the results vary slightly between different studies, it is often estimated that in the United States, risk sharing between states is mainly done through the financial markets, not through the federal budget. The same mechanism could be thought to work in Europe if the market had been sufficiently integrated. Concrete examples of risk-sharing through the financial markets are easy to come up with also in Finland: the rise in the value of Nokia shares in the 1990s made many Finnish small investors clearly wealthier than before. When the value of these shares fell when the technology bubble burst in the early 2000s, a large part of Nokia's owners were no longer Finnish. In this situation, foreign owners bore the risk associated with ict traffic investments made in Finland with Finns. Similar risk sharing can be thought to have occurred when foreign investors have recently bought Finnish properties. ********************************* Finally There have been many twists and turns in Finland's monetary history, but the goal of stable monetary conditions is, in my opinion, a good reflection of the red thread of Finnish monetary history. Monetary stability was achieved when Finland was among the first to adopt the euro at the beginning of 1999. Finland has a monetary policy that is shared with 12 other EU countries. As part of its stability-oriented work with the Eurosystem, the Bank of Finland is working more closely with the European Central Bank and other national central banks than ever before in our country's monetary history. The importance of financial markets for economic growth has been one of the main reasons why there has been a desire to accelerate the integration of financial markets in the EU area and why the Bank of Finland also monitors and supports the integration process. The Bank of Finland's task is to contribute to the reliability and efficiency of the financial system and to contribute to its development. It is important that, in the frenetic flood of economic news, more and more people also realise the importance of well-functioning money and financial markets for economic development.

T<8a>m<8a>kin on tavallaan ymm<8a>rrett<8a>v<8a><8a>: Miksi ket<8a><8a>n ylip<8a><8a>t<8a><8a>n kiinnostaisi kysymys esimerkiksi siit<8a>, kuinka rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a>n toiminnan tehostuminen 10-15 vuotta sitten vaikuttaa t<8a>m<8a>n hetken talouskasvuun? <a5> Kolmanneksi, vaikka rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a>n toiminnan ja pitk<8a>n aikav<8a>lin talouskasvun v<8a>linen yhteys koettaisiin sin<8a>ll<8a><8a>n kiinnostavaksi, siit<8a> ei ole helppoa kirjoittaa: T<8a>t<8a> yhteytt<8a> on nimitt<8a>in aikalaisten vaikea havaita tai mitata. Aihetta k<8a>sittelevien, konkreettisten talousuutisten kirjoittaminen ei siis ole yksinkertaista. Rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a>n ja pitk<8a>n aikav<8a>lin talouskasvun v<8a>linen yhteys on kuitenkin juuri se, miksi rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a>n toimivuudesta ja tehokkuudesta kannattaa kantaa huolta: Taloustieteellisen tutkimuksen mukaan hyvin toimivat rahoitusmarkkinat nopeuttavat pitk<8a>n aikav<8a>lin talouskasvua. T<8a>m<8a>n kasvuvaikutuksen olemassaolo on t<8a>rke<8a><8a> tiedostaa: Pitk<8a>n aikav<8a>lin talouskasvu kuvaa elintasossamme tapahtuvia muutoksia ja on siten t<8a>rke<8a> kansalaisten elintason muutosta kuvaava mittari. Hyvin toimiva rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a> luo siten v<8a>hint<8a><8a>nkin v<8a>lillisesti vaurautta ja hyvinvointia nykyisille ja tuleville sukupolville. [ KALVO 13] Nykyaikainen rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a> on hyvin monimutkainen verkostojen verkosto, jossa ns. rahoitusylij<8a><8a>m<8a>isten kotitalouksien ja yrityksien s<8a><8a>st<9a>t kulkevat monien kanavien ja v<8a>lik<8a>sien kautta lopullisille rahoituksen tarvitsijoille. Rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a><8a> tarvitaan, koska kaikki kotitaloudet ja yritykset eiv<8a>t halua k<8a>ytt<8a><8a> saamiaan tulojaan saman tien kulutukseen tai investointeihin. N<8a>iden s<8a><8a>st<9a>jen avulla sellaiset kotitaloudet, joiden menot (ainakin sill<8a> hetkell<8a>) ylitt<8a>v<8a>t tulot, voivat rahoittaa kulutus-ja/tai investointitarpeitaan. Yksinkertaisimmillaan v<8a>lik<8a>si<8a> ei tarvita, jolloin puhutaan ns. suorasta rahoituksesta. Esimerkkej<8a> t<8a>llaisesta rahoituksesta ovat yst<8a>vien v<8a>liset lainat ja muut vipit tai ns. enkelisijoittajien omilla rahoillaan tekem<8a>t riskisijoitukset alkuvaiheen yrityksiin. Ep<8a>suorasta rahoituksesta puhutaan, jos rahoituksen v<8a>litykseen osallistuu jokin kolmas osapuoli, kuten esimerkiksi rahoituslaitos. Tyypillisin esimerkki t<8a>llaisesta rahoituksesta on talletuspankkien toiminta: Ne ker<8a><8a>v<8a>t kotitalouksilta ja yrityksilt<8a> talletuksia ja rahoittavat n<8a>in saatujen varojen avulla mm. toisien kotitalouksien asuntojen hankintaa (asuntoluotot) tai yrityksien reaali-investointeja (yritysluotot). Nykyaikaisessa rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a>ss<8a> on hyvin monenlaisia suoran rahoituksen markkinoita ja siell<8a> toimii moniin eri teht<8a>viin erikoistuneita, ep<8a>suoraa rahoitusta kanavoivia rahoituslaitoksia. S<8a><8a>st<9a>jen eteenp<8a>in kanavoimisen ohella ne hoitavat monia muita teht<8a>vi<8a>, kuten tuottavat maksu-ja k<8a>teispalveluita, erilaisia arvopaperikauppaan liittyvi<8a> selvityspalveluita, ja my<9a>nt<8a>v<8a>t vakuutuksia. [ KALVO 14] Vaikka tutkimus tukee n<8a>kemyst<8a>, ett<8a> hyvin toimiva ja tehokas rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a> my<9a>t<8a>vaikuttaa talouskasvuun, on syyt<8a> korostaa, ett<8a> niiden v<8a>list<8a> yhteytt<8a> ei ole viel<8a>k<8a><8a>n kaikilta osin pystytty selvitt<8a>m<8a><8a>n. Toisinaan n<8a>ytt<8a><8a> nimitt<8a>in silt<8a>, ett<8a> rahoitussektori ja talous kehittyv<8a>t yht<8a> aikaa, toisiaan tukien. Suomenkaan osalta ei ole selv<8a><8a>, kumpi on muna ja kumpi kana. Rahoitussektorilla on nimitt<8a>in meill<8a>kin pitk<8a>t perinteet: Suomessa ensimm<8a>inen rahoituslaitos toimi vuosina 1663-1667 ja oli ruotsalaisen Palmstruchin pankin eli Ruotsin nykyisen keskuspankin Riksbankin edelt<8a>j<8a>n Suomen sivukonttori. Suomen Pankin edelt<8a>j<8a> eli Waihetus-ja Laina ja Depositioni Contori Suomen Suuren-Ruhtinanmaasa perustettiin jo vuonna 1811. Ensimm<8a>inen s<8a><8a>st<9a>pankki perustettiin puolestaan Turkuun 1823, Suomen ensimm<8a>inen liikepankki (SYP) 1862 ja p<9a>rssi 1912. Sit<8a>, kuinka n<8a>m<8a> (ja muut) rahoitusinstituutiot ovat vaikuttaneet talouskasvuun Suomessa, ei ole yksinkertaista selvitt<8a><8a> tai mitata. T<8a>t<8a> mittausongelmaa ei helpota se, ett<8a> rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a>n ja talouskasvun v<8a>linen yhteys on saattanut muuttua vuosikymmenten kuluessa. Vaikka esimerkiksi Suomessa liikepankeilla oli n<8a>ht<8a>v<8a>sti t<8a>rke<8a> merkitys ensimm<8a>isten teollisuushankkeiden k<8a>ynnist<8a>misess<8a> 1800-luvun lopulla, ei ole selv<8a><8a>, miss<8a> m<8a><8a>rin ne tai pankkisektori yleisemmin ovat vaikuttaneet talouskasvuun esimerkiksi rahatalouden s<8a><8a>ntelyn vuosina toisen maailmansodan j<8a>lkeen tai rahoitusmarkkinoiden s<8a><8a>ntelyn purkamisen yhteydess<8a> 1980-luvun lopulla. 1990-luvun alun pankkikriisin my<9a>t<8a> talletuspankkien rooli on saattanut j<8a>lleen muuttua, sill<8a> noiden vuosien j<8a>lkeen pankkien toiminta on tehostunut. Toisaalta suomalainen rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a> on samaan aikaan monipuolistunut ja tullut mm. p<8a><8a>omasijoitustoimialan kehittymisen my<9a>t<8a> hieman aikaisempaa osakemarkkinakeskeisemm<8a>ksi. [ KALVO 15] Vaikka rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a>n ja reaalisektorin (tuotantotalouden) v<8a>list<8a> yhtyett<8a> ei kaikilta osin t<8a>ysin tunneta, jotain sent<8a><8a>n tiedet<8a><8a>n. Hyvin toimiva ja tehokas rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a> my<9a>t<8a>vaikuttaa investointeihin, talouskasvuun ja kansalaisten hyvinvointiin ainakin kolmen kanavan kautta: Se (i) alentaa ulkoisen rahoituksen kustannuksia, (ii) nopeutta pitk<8a>n aikav<8a>lin talouskasvua ja (iii) auttaa suojautumaan taloudellisilta riskeilt<8a>. [ KALVO 16] Ensinn<8a>kin, hyvin toimiva ja tehokas rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a> laskee p<8a><8a>oman kustannuksia. Alhaisemmat p<8a><8a>oman kustannukset johtavat investointien kasvuun, koska perinteinen (neoklassinen) investointiteoria ennustaa, ett<8a> yritykset jatkavat investointien tekemist<8a> kunnes investoinnista saatava lis<8a>tuotto ("marginal product") on yht<8a> suuri kuin p<8a><8a>oman reaalinen kustannus. T<8a>m<8a> tarkoittaa, ett<8a> mit<8a> alhaisemmat ovat p<8a><8a>oman kustannukset, sit<8a> enemm<8a>n yrityksill<8a> on niiden n<8a>k<9a>kulmasta kannattavia investointikohteita <d0> ja ett<8a> sit<8a> enemm<8a>n ne ovat halukkaita tekem<8a><8a>n investointeja. Investointien kasvun puolestaan ajatellaan usein tukevan ty<9a>llisyytt<8a> ja nopeuttavan talouskasvua ainakin joksikin aikaa. [ KALVO 17] Toiseksi, hyvin toimivat rahoitusmarkkinat nopeuttavat pitk<8a>n aikav<8a>lin talouskasvua. Kasvu nopeutuu ennen kaikkea siksi, ett<8a> tehokkaasti toimiva rahoitussektori kykenee nopeuttamaan kokonaistuottavuuden kasvua. Kokonaistuottavuuden kasvu on t<8a>rke<8a><8a> mm. hyvinvointivaltion palveluiden yll<8a>pit<8a>misen kannalta: Kun kokonaistuottavuus kasvaa, voidaan hy<9a>dykkeit<8a> ja palveluita tuottaa aikaisempaa enemm<8a>n ilman ett<8a> p<8a><8a>omakantaa tai ty<9a>panosta tarvitsee kasvattaa. [ KALVO 18] T<8a>m<8a> vaikutus syntyy pitk<8a>lti siit<8a>, ett<8a> maat, joiden rahoitusmarkkinoita ja pankkij<8a>rjestelm<8a><8a> voidaan pit<8a><8a> kehittynein<8a>, lis<8a><8a>v<8a>t kasvaville toimialoille teht<8a>vi<8a> investointeja enemm<8a>n ja tekev<8a>t supistuville toimialoille v<8a>hemm<8a>n investointeja kuin maat, joissa n<8a>m<8a> rahoitusinstituutiot ovat v<8a>hemm<8a>n kehittyneit<8a>. Rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a>n toimivuudella on siis merkityst<8a>, koska se vaikuttaa saatavilla olevien voimavarojen kohdentumiseen parhaisiin ja tuottavimpiin investointikohteisiin. Edell<8a> sanottu tarkoittaa, ett<8a> rahoitusmarkkinat vaikuttavat talouskasvuun siksi, ett<8a> ne m<8a><8a>r<8a><8a>v<8a>t, mille aloille voimavarat kanavoituvat ja mink<8a>laisia teknologisia, organisatorisia tai muita innovaatioita yritykset ja yritt<8a>j<8a>t voivat tavoitella ulkoisen rahoituksen turvin. Ulkoisen rahoituksen turvin teht<8a>vien perinteisten ja T&K.investointien laatu vaikuttaa esimerkiksi siihen, kuinka tehokkaita ja nykyaikaisia valmistusmenetelmi<8a> ja teknologioita yritykset k<8a>ytt<8a>v<8a>t. Kyse ei siis v<8a>ltt<8a>m<8a>tt<8a> ole niink<8a><8a>n rahoituksen m<8a><8a>r<8a>st<8a> kuin laadusta. [ KALVO 19] T<8a>m<8a>n toteamuksen k<8a><8a>nt<9a>puoli on t<8a>rke<8a> mutta usein unohdettu toimivien yritysrahoitusmarkkinoiden ominaispiirre: Tehokkaat rahoitusmarkkinat my<9a>s "karsivat hankkeita" eli kohdistavat rahoitusta vain rajoitetusti <d0> jos lainkaan <d0> esimerkiksi hankkeille, yrityksille tai toimialoille, joiden menestymismahdollisuudet ja tulevaisuuden n<8a>kym<8a>t ovat heikot. [ KALVO 20] Hyvin toimiva rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a> my<9a>t<8a>vaikuttaa kansalaisten hyvinvointiin my<9a>s kolmannen kanavan kautta. Se nimitt<8a>in auttaa niin kotitalouksia kuin yrityksi<8a>kin suojautumaan taloudellisilta riskeilt<8a>. Euroopan integraation edetess<8a> voidaan puhua esimerkiksi alueiden v<8a>lisen riskien jaon syventymisest<8a>: Sijoitusten hajauttaminen yli maiden ja alueiden (kansainv<8a>lisi<8a>) p<8a><8a>omamarkkinoita k<8a>ytt<8a>en on keino jakaa riskej<8a> muiden maiden ja/tai alueiden kanssa. Se on toisin sanoen keino suojautua vain omaa asuinaluetta (kansantaloutta) kohtaavilta h<8a>iri<9a>ilt<8a>. T<8a>llainen riskien jako on mahdollista, koska eri alueita ja kansantalouksia koskevat h<8a>iri<9a>t ovat vain osin samanaikaisia tai samansuuntaisia, niin hyv<8a>ss<8a> kuin pahassa. [ KALVO 21] Otetaan esimerkki Yhdysvalloista: Kun vaikkapa v<8a>kiluvultaan hieman Suomea suurempaa, Yhdysvaltojen koillisosassa sijaitsevaa Massachusettsin osavaltiota kohtaa taloudellinen h<8a>iri<9a>, toiset osavaltiot kantavat osan t<8a>m<8a>n h<8a>iri<9a>n aiheuttamista kustannuksista rahoitusmarkkinoiden v<8a>lityksell<8a>. N<8a>in tapahtuu siksi, ett<8a> eri osavaltioiden asukkaat omistavat toistensa alueilla olevaa omaisuutta/varallisuutta "ristiin". N<8a>in ollen my<9a>s muiden osavaltioiden kuin Massachusettsin asukkaat k<8a>rsiv<8a>t Massachusettsin alueen "huonosta onnesta" eli esimerkin taloudellisen h<8a>iri<9a>n aiheuttamista yritysten konkursseista tai kiinteist<9a>jen arvon laskusta. Vaikka tulokset vaihtelevat hieman eri tutkimusten v<8a>lill<8a>, usein arvioidaan, ett<8a> Yhdysvalloissa osavaltioiden v<8a>linen riskienjako tapahtuu p<8a><8a>osin rahoitusmarkkinoiden v<8a>lityksell<8a>, ei liittovaltion budjetin kautta. Saman mekanismin voisi ajatella toimivan my<9a>s Euroopassa, jos markkinat olisivat integroituneet riitt<8a>v<8a>sti. Konkreettisia esimerkkej<8a> rahoitusmarkkinoiden v<8a>lityksell<8a> tapahtuvasta riskien jaosta on helppoa keksi<8a> my<9a>s Suomesta: Nokian osakkeiden arvonnousu 1990-luvulla teki monista suomalaisista piensijoittajistakin aikaisempaa selv<8a>sti varakkaampia. Kun n<8a>iden osakkeiden arvo laski teknologiakuplan puhjetessa 2000-luvun alussa, suuri osa Nokian omistajista ei en<8a><8a> ollut suomalaisia. T<8a>ss<8a> tilanteessa ulkomaiset omistajat kantoivat Suomessa tehtyihin tieto-ja viestint<8a>liikenneinvestointeihin liittyv<8a><8a> riski<8a> suomalaisten kanssa. Vastaavaa riskinjakoa voidaan ajatella tapahtuneen, kun ulkomaalaiset sijoittajat ovat viime aikoina ostaneet suomalaisia kiinteist<9a>j<8a>. ********************************* Lopuksi Suomen rahahistoriassa on ollut monenlaisia mutkia, mutta tavoite vakaista rahaoloista kuvastaa mielest<8a>ni hyvin Suomen rahahistorian punaista lankaa. Vakaat rahaolot saavutettiin, kun Suomi otti euron k<8a>ytt<9a><9a>n ensimm<8a>isten joukossa vuoden 1999 alusta. Suomella on rahapolitiikka, joka on yhteinen 12 muun EU-maan kanssa. Suomen Pankki tekee euroj<8a>rjestelm<8a>n osana vakauteen t<8a>ht<8a><8a>v<8a><8a> ty<9a>t<8a><8a>n Euroopan keskuspankin ja muiden kansallisten keskuspankkien kanssa tiiviimmin kuin koskaan aiemmin maamme rahahistoriassa. Rahoitusmarkkinoiden merkitys talouskasvulle on ollut yksi t<8a>rke<8a> syy sille, miksi rahoitusmarkkinoiden yhdentymist<8a> EU-alueella on haluttu nopeuttaa ja miksi my<9a>s Suomen Pankissa seurataan ja tuetaan yhdentymiskehityst<8a>. Suomen Pankin teht<8a>v<8a>n<8a> on huolehtia osaltaan rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a>n luottavuudesta ja tehokkuudesta, sek<8a> osallistua sen kehitt<8a>miseen. On t<8a>rke<8a><8a>, ett<8a> kiihke<8a>rytmisess<8a> talousuutisten tulvassa yh<8a> useammat ymm<8a>rt<8a>isiv<8a>t my<9a>s hyvin toimivien raha.ja finanssimarkkinoiden suuren merkityksen taloudellisen kehityksen kannalta.

Title: The legacy of Tokoi and Chydenius in Finland and Europe today at the 90th anniversary seminar of Finnish and Finnish parliamentarianism in Kokkola
text: Director-General Erkki Liikanen's speech "The Legacy of Tokoi and Chydenius in Today's Finland and Europe" at the seminar celebrating the 90th anniversary of Finnish and Finnish parliamentarism in Kokkola . Speech . Monday11 June 2007,12:00AM Director-General Erkki Liikanen Seminar celebrating the 90th anniversary of Finland and Finnish parliamentarism with the legacy of Tokoi and Chydenius into the future Kokkola 11.6.2007, Kokkola City Hall The legacy of Tokoi and Chydenius in today's Finland and Europe Carbon, Wyoming was the terminus of Oskari Tokoi's ticket when he boarded a train in New York city in the spring of 1891. Carbon was a coal mining town in the far midwest state of Wyoming. The train ride from New York to Carbon took a whole week. Tokoi had begun his journey to the great west from Kannus station "one cold and stormy morning" in mid-January 1891. First by train to Kokkola, then to Hanko and from Hanko to Copenhagen. From there, he boarded a train with other emigrants that took Bremerhaven. And from here, the journey finally continued by ship across the Atlantic to New York. At the end of this coming August, central bank governors from all over the world will gather in the same state of Wyoming for a symposium on the core issues of monetary policy. The symposium will be held by the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, one of the fed's regional banks. The practical organizer of this already traditional symposium is Craig Hakkio, research manager at the bank. Craig's great-grandfather left Vaasa for America around the same time as Tokoi. The central bankers gather at Jackson Hole, just off Yellowstone and three hundred miles northwest of Tokoin Carbon. Today, the journey is a little faster than in the 1800s. First we fly four hours from New York to Salt Lake City and from there another hour to Jackson Hole. Oskari Tokoi, an Ostrobothnian boy in his twenties, began his work in Wyoming, on the 19th plateau of a coal mine, deep in the depths of the earth. Almost all Finnish emigrants aspired to the mines, even though they had not seen one in their home country. Tokoi colorfully describes the stages in his book "Memoirs of an Exile". He began his social activities in 1891 as the secretary of the Temperance Society Aamurusko, and the first major event he organized was the Midsummer celebrations of Finnish emigrants that summer. Carbon's coal sales deteriorated and work stopped. Tokoi moved to new localities in search of work. When it was found, he founded a new temperance society, which was in great need. Tokoi also studied English. Tokoi also experienced the deep economic downturn of the 1890s in concrete terms. Miners roamed in hordes along the land from one mine to another. He joined the Union of Miners and thus became familiar with trade union activities. Oskari Tokoi saw a lot of America and, of course, Finnish immigrants. Finally, in the spring of 1900, after nine years in America, Tokoi returned with his family to Finland and Ostrobothnia. *** When Oskari Tokoi returned to Kannus, the local economy was on a completely different level than when he left. The effects of the railway were visible. They had accelerated the spread of the use of money. In this way, the importance of banks was emphasized, and socially active people saw the establishment of a savings bank as an important means of promoting the economic development of their own region. Besides, society was being organized into various broad popular movements, allowing the bank to be used to pursue the common goals of such a popular movement. Savings banks were divided into two groups. In the cities, savings banks were established with donations from private citizens, in the countryside, on the other hand, it happened under the leadership of municipalities, when there were no donors. This is how Oskari Tokoi also started working for a municipal savings bank in Kannus. Individual donors could not be relied on in Kannus because there were no such wealthy people. The only way out was to get the basic capital from the municipality, and for that Tokoi turned to the municipal supervisor. The meeting took place, but the reception was hostile. In the municipalities at that time, power was held by the masters in accordance with their mantle, and attitudes towards any reform were often obstructive. At the end of the chaotic meeting, the President-in-Office proposed that the matter be put on the table. The most vocal opponents demand that it be put "under the table". But that wasn't the end of it. After a long period of maturation, the Savings Bank of the Municipality of Kannus started its operations at the beginning of 1908. The scale was initially modest: the bank was open only twice a month. But the growth rate was rapid, since in 1912 the number of depositors already exceeded the limit of four hundred. In the case of Kannus, the savings bank was founded by the municipality, and thus the forces behind the establishment were mainly found in the circle of the local peasants. In the same year, in 1908, by the way, the Workers' Savings Bank was established in Helsinki and the Kymenlaakso Workers' Savings Bank in Kotka. However, Tokoi was not actively involved in these projects, so Tokoi's savings bank career was limited only to this role of initiator in Kannus. Chydenius' active activities took place in the second half of the 1700s, which was a period of social upheaval in Ostrobothnia, as was tokoi's time in the early 1900s. The use of money in Ostrobothnia was still low, except in foreign trade, and local banks were not on Chydenius' agenda. But from the point of view of a central banker, Chydenius's action in favor of the stability of the value of money at that time is of great interest. The background is as follows. As a result of the war policy of the Hat Party, the Swedish monetary system had fallen into a paper stump. The means of payment used were banknotes that had been issued to cover government expenditure and support industry to such an extent that their value had approximately halved in relation to silver, the monetary metal that prevailed internationally at the time. When the myssy party, to which Chydenius also belonged, came to power, it took steps to stabilize the monetary system. The party adopted the line that the convertibility of banknotes to metal should be restored in accordance with their original face value. This would have meant doubling the value of money. By turning inflation, which has been raging in Sweden for a couple of decades, into an even steeper deflationary effect, the injustices caused by inflation would have been undone, the leaders speculated. Chydenius considered a stable value of money to be an indispensable foundation of economic life. He therefore supported stopping inflation and returning to the metal base. But he also realised the damage that deflation, which was part of the plan, would have caused to indebted agriculture and industry, and what a sudden doubling of the value of the Swedish bucks would have meant for the country's exports. Chydenius therefore called for the pernicious plan of revaluation and deflation to be abandoned and proposed tying the value of money to silver at the level of the then current rate. This proposal, which is perfectly reasonable from the current point of view, caused a huge scandal. Chydenius had publicly questioned the decision already made by the Diet to restore the value of money. He was suspected of conspiring with the opposition Hat Party. Besides, even if Chydenius's proposal had in practice stabilized the value of money, legally it would have meant a devaluation, since the banknotes would not have been redeemed for their original value. It was feared that this would mean bankruptcy and the ruin of both the Bank and Sweden as a whole. The end result of the dispute was that Chydenius was expelled from the Diet because he had criticized the decisions of the estates. From what is known today about monetary policy, it is hardly surprising that the ferocious revaluation plan of the musketeers failed. Deflation caused a serious economic crisis and the plan eventually had to be abandoned. After seizing power, In 1776, Gustav III carried out a successful monetary reform, which finally stabilized the value of the bucks. The reform followed the principles set out by Chydenius ten years earlier, which were thus subsequently recognised as correct. Oskari Tokoi was not involved in monetary policy. In his memoirs, however, he recounts an interesting episode related to the Bank of Finland from the time of the People's Delegation. Tokoi was a food manager and the food situation was extremely difficult. The revolutionary government had discovered that the Bank of Finland's gold reserves were running out and banknote money had been depleted, with the exception of Russian banknotes. With these rubles, almost all of which were issued by the Provisional Government of Russia, the so-called "roubles". kerenkos, it was decided to buy grain. Tokoi was sent to Russia to negotiate the purchase of grain. The situation in St. Petersburg was chaotic. In the end, a representative of the Council of Labour and Soldiers called for the continuation of grain lifting in Siberia. Locomotive driver Jaakko Rahja was chosen as the technical director of the tour. Finally, the expedition, which set off in February, arrived in Helsinki on Good Friday by grain train, tokoi with it. In honor of the arrival of the grain train, a general civic celebration was held at the National Theater. Signed by E.G. Palmen and K.J. Stahlberg, the Bank of Finland's bank delegates' report on the bank's activities "during the 1918 rebellion" tells colorfully how the ruble banknotes ended up in the revolutionary government. The Chairman of the Board of Governors was Edvard Gylling. The reopening of the Bank of Finland's closed headquarters was discussed at three meetings of the Board of Governors. Gylling demanded it, the board of directors opposed. The opening of the headquarters was formally a matter for the banking delegates to decide, but the Board of Directors considered that this could not be done for security reasons. Eventually, guarded by the Guards sent by the Red Guard commander Eero Haapalainen, the vault was broken and with the keys obtained from it, safes were opened and an inventory of funds was started. There were found these rubles. *** Before his dismissal, Antti Chydenius was in the Diet for only 18 months. His activity was downright breathtaking. All the writings for which Chydenius is famous arose during its frantic year and a half, 176566, when Chydenius was in his first Diet in Stockholm. His works on economic policy, "The Refutation of Those Causes," "The Source of the Powerlessness of the Empire," "National Victory," and "Helping the Empire with a Natural Monetary System," are not cool academic treatises, but political flybooks with which Chydenius stepped into the eye of the storm of the daytime politics of his time, even so boldly that it eventually cost him his place in the Diet. His fifth landmark work from the same period, the report on freedom of writing and the press, is of an even more political nature: it is a memorandum written for distribution to the Diet. The fact that it was the political struggle that propelled Chydenius to his best performances says something about his character. Many people hardly remember his master's dissertation on the craft of American Indians, and even fewer have read it. But when Chydenius found himself in a situation where he was able to take a stand on important issues, he did so fieryly and with such a strong appeal to both morality and reason of his readers that the results were permanently consigned to history. In this sense, Chydenius was a kindred soul of Oskari Tokoi. Both were political fighters driven by moral pathos. Both were pen-men flamming with current issues  Tokoi journalist, Chydenius a pamphletist. Chydenius seems to have enjoyed himself when he managed to annoy the rulers of his time. Proudly, Chydenius recounts how the men of the Estates' Banking Committee viewed his "Natural Monetary System," for which he was then expelled from the Diet: "They curseand they read!" Most political writing loses its topicality in a muddy month. This has not happened to the works of Chydenius. The durability of his political writings lies in the fact that, although they were highly topical, their starting point was not political manoeuvring or otherwise transient incidents in the political life of the Swedish empire. He approached political issues from a principled point of view. The principled basis on which he built his argument has proved so durable that Chydenius's works are at the same time - as if a by-product - a sustainable political theory and applied social philosophy from a modern point of view. This transformation of pamphlet literature into a political classic is not entirely unique. As a point of comparison, the "Federalist writings" of Chydenius' contemporaries, the forces behind the US constitutions, Alexander Hamilton and James Madison, come to mind. They published a series of analytical but polemical writings to pass the Constitution. They have the same spirit as the writings of Chydenius. Anders Chydenius was in the Swedish Parliament on a total of three occasions, first in 17661767, the second ten years later in 17781779. These two seasons were a time of great influence. He returned briefly for the 1792 session, but it was less significant. Oskari Tokoi was elected to the first unicameral parliament in 1907 and served as a representative until the Civil War. The circumstances were very different, but their careers also had in common. Both entered their first diets at a young age, Tokoi at the age of 33 and Chydenius at the age of 35. Both Chydenius and Tokoi faced major conflicts in their political careers. As noted above, Chydenius was expelled from the Diet in 1766. Tokoi always progressed to the position of speaker of parliament and deputy chairman of the Senate, i.e. prime minister. During the Civil War, he was the Food Commissar of the People's Commissariat. Tokoi was sentenced to death twice, both by whites at the end of the Civil War and by Otto Ville Kuusinen, Kullervo Manner, Jukka Rahja and others. by signing a decision during the Murmannian Legion. Two weeks ago, the Parliament celebrated its 100th anniversary. There were 196 current and more than 300 former representatives present. The chairmen of the parliamentary groups spoke on the permanentisation of state aid to women's organisations. The 50th anniversary session of the Parliament, held in the spring of 1957, was attended by five members of the first Parliament: Vaino Tanner, Paavo Virkkunen, Hedvig Gebhard, Vaino Hakkila and Oskari Tokoi. At that time, the guests of honour were also given the floor at the formal sitting. Speaking on their behalf was Oskari Tokoi, who arrived from the United States, who stated: "Fifty years ago, the gathering of the Unicameral Parliament of Finland was a landmark event in the history of the world's parliaments. Despite our country's remote and then still non-independent position, the gathering of the new Parliament had attracted attention around the world, especially in the european parliamentary countries." *** Chydenius made an effort in the Diet to improve the position of farmworkers. He was concerned about low population growth and emigration. Chydenius considered that the poor position of farm workers was the cause of both emigration and slow population growth, and, in addition, an explanation for the low level of prosperity. Farmworkers' wages were regulated very low. In place of regulation, Chydenius demanded freedom of contract for the master and servant to agree among themselves on annual service or daily wages. He assumed that once the restrictions had been lifted, the parties would agree on wages in a free competition. Chydenius wrote, "Toil like a slave in the work of others as long as he can, to be cast aside in the old days, and to die in miserythat is the laurels that ought to tempt the working people to love their motherland." Of the working people, he said: "It is the most vulnerable group of the inhabitants of our country, scattered throughout the country, without a rule of profession, without leaders... it has no organizations." It was not until two hundred years later that the trade union movement really organised itself. The Finnish Trade Union Confederation was founded in 1907. Oskari Tokoi unexpectedly became the second chairman of the Finnish Trade Union Association in 1912. The miners had asked him to be a candidate because he had experience in the trade union movement in the United States. Another reason was that Eero Haapalainen wanted to be put aside. Tokoi operated all the time between two fires. Employers did not want to know about trade unions. There was still a long way to go before collective agreements were reached. On the other hand, in a frenzied climate of struggle, the trade unions did not always even want to try to resolve issues through the path of mediation. It was a tough time for Tokoi as a man of reconciliation. As a trade union leader, Tokoi had the opportunity to see Europe. In 1913, he visited the Assembly of the International Trade Union Movement in Zurich and became acquainted with trade union leaders from all over Europe and the United States. On the way there, he became acquainted in Berlin with the German labor movement, which lived in its heyday. The return journey passed through Austria, Poland and Russia. "Even though I had seen the Rocky Mountains of America and the snow peaks of the Sierra Nevada, the Alps were an experience after all." Tokoi's political career in Finland culminated in the position of deputy chairman of the Senate, i.e. practically prime minister. He tried to hold the broad-based Senate together by mediating between social democratic and bourgeois senators. At the same time, he was the target of fierce criticism from the left flank of the Social Democrats in his party, led by Kuusinen, Gylling and Valpas. Vaino Tanner was responsible for the management of state funds in the Senate. Tanner rated Tokoi's operations positively: "If anyone had expected uncertainty or hesitation in him, then he was fundamentally mistaken. At the very first sitting, Tokoi took over the chair as if he had never done anything else." The Tokoi Senate fell apart due to the power law dispute and also due to the social democrats sitting on two chairs. On the eve of the civil war, Tokoi and Tanner found themselves on different sides. Among those close to the trade union movement, Tokoi sided with the supporters of the revolution and served in the People's Commissariat. This famously led to exile to Russia after the Civil War and from there, after a colourful period, to British service to the Murmanni Legion, which, in Tokoi's opinion, has rarely existed in the world. *** After the dissolution of the Muurmann Legion in 1919, Oskari Tokoi's longest trek began. Five legionnaires, among them Tokoi, did not receive the right to return within the borders of Finland. After many stages, Tokoi arrived in November 1919 by ship to England, where he spent almost a year until October 1920. Tokoi lived mainly in London, where he was greatly impressed with freedom of speech. He seemed to have spent many Saturdays and Sundays in Hyde Park admiring the atmosphere of freedom of speech there. In his memoirs, he states, "When I saw these platforms and listened to the speeches made from them, the durability of the foundation of the Kingdom of England began to become clear to me." Alavetel's chaplain Antti Chydenius was not a world traveler like Tokoi. In addition to Ostrobothnia, his circle of experience extended to the universities of Turku and Uppsala, and then to the Riksdag in Stockholm. On the other hand, Johan Arckenholtz, whom Juha Manninen judged to have had a great influence on Chydenius' perceptions of freedom of the press, was a connoisseur of England and a great admirer of its freedom of speech. Chydenius later wrote in his memoirs that in his first Diet he had not worked so anything as freedom of the press. Indeed, the importance of Chydenius was absolutely crucial when the Diet in 1766 implemented a truly extensive freedom of the press. Chydenius saw freedom of the press precisely as a political matter, and realized the importance of publicity as the "fourth power." For Chydenius, "the freedom of a nation is not that almighty estates are allowed to act arbitrarily, but requires that the enlightenment of the nation binds their hands and prevents them from acting autocratically." This notion of the importance of publicity as a central element of political freedom connects Chydenius with Snellman, who in his philosophy made the national public the most important element of political freedom, even more important than formal state bodies. It also connects Chydenius with the political journalist Tokoi, who practically implemented the freedom of speech for which both Chydenius and Snellman had fought. When Oskari Tokoi finally settled in the United States at the end of his long journey, in the spring of 1922 he joined the editorial board of the Finnish social democratic newspaper Raivaajan. This became his longest posting, which continued "until the communion of life." It wasn't just a celebration for a journalist. This is how he describes it in his memoirs: "Delivering a small Finnish daily newspaper in a foreign land, especially when it has to be done with little labor, is mentally and physically deadly work. From morning to night, it is the same deadly tinkering with trifles, translating the news, correcting the scribbles of almost unwritten correspondents, proofreading, and, in addition, constant chatting with people who consider it their business and right to come to the editorial office of a newspaper to tell and talk about all things, to complain about all their ailments and to ask for advice and to ask for help with their language difficulties. If a person has had enthusiasm and desire for something, it will go out and die in just a few years in the editorial office of a small newspaper." But of course, he also told me that "I did feel formally and outwardly free. After all, nothing haunted me or frightened me. But even then, human freedom has certain limits that everyone instinctively shuns from crossing". *** The fact that Chydenius did not cross the borders of the Swedish empire did not limit the space of his views. This is what Chydenius wrote in his booklet "The Source of the Powerlessness of the Kingdom": "The simpler a nation has followed nature, the more affluent and numerous it has become" He also had his ideal state at that time  in the 1760s. And it was  "China, the richest empire in the world, is an undeniable example of that. There the cities have no privileges, and no distinctions are made between urban and rural industries; therefore the whole country is like a city and all cities the most wonderful countryside... the crafts are free there, that is why the workman is tireless in his diligence, and multifunctionality goes into exile by itself without the laws having to banish it there." Holland and England were closest to the ideal, but then so far away: no one had allowed the laws of nature to prevail as freely as the Chinese, the others are blind, except the Dutch and English, who are second-eyed. Contrary to these examples, Sweden had believed that they would be enriched by exclusive rights, restrictions and various prohibitions. With these strong arguments, Chydenius actually began his speech in favor of expanding the trade rights of ostrobothnian cities. The debate must not be detached from its own era. But China at that time was the world's great economic power, and even today it is growing strongly, although it is still far from the status of a leading power. How to regulate what is necessary and how to avoid overregulation is still a major topic of discussion, for example within the European Union. *** Finally, a few words about the essential features of the activities of Chydenius and Tokoi from a contemporary perspective: Chydenius advocated freedom of foreign trade and the freedom to conduct a business, and opposed the hat party's industrial policy based on subsidies and prohibitions. He advocated the stabilization of the value of money at the base of its prevailing value; he advocated for freedom of speech, transparency in government, and opposed censorship; and he wanted to increase the rights of wage earners and expand religious freedom. It is clear that the liberal Chydenius saw the world in many respects in very different ways than the social democrat Tokoi. In particular, their solutions to social problems were different and their attitudes to the mechanisms of the market economy were different and sometimes even opposite. But for both Chydenius and Tokoi, the justification for the political program was to reduce social justice and abolish various privileges based on power. Chydenius insisted in the "National Victory" that "all means of living without work are cut off, and no one but the hardworking can become wealthy." This requirement would also have suited Tokoi's mouth. Chydenius's concern about the vulnerable position of the wage earners and the idea that in an undemocratic state the poorest are oppressed by the laws also unites him in the Tokos. Both were convinced Democrats and had a negative attitude towards the society of estates. Both liberalism and the political labour movement have their roots in the Enlightenment, and Chydenius is a good example of the political reform efforts of the Enlightenment. *** In the light of today, the life stories of both have sensational features. As men of both cause and action, both put themselves on the line and also experienced its consequences. The farsightedness of Chydenius's ideas and the sharpness of the language are impressive. So many issues and problems have remained relevant to this day. His activities affected the economy of Ostrobothnia and is still felt today in the political life of both Sweden and Finland, for example, as a high regard for openness and freedom of speech. Tokoi's life story is more colorful, downright unique. He lived in the United States for more than forty years, saw two recessions on the one hand, and the rise of the United States on the other. He was a member of the first parliament, the first prime minister, the second chairman of the SAJ, a member of the people's delegation, a strong defender of democracy and, above all, a survivor. Anders Chydenius has been the subject of a remarkable biography. One is also needed from Oskari Tokoinen.
