Skogsindustrin verkar ha stannat p<8c> en betydligt l<8a>gre produktionsniv<8c> <8a>n var den befann sig f<9a>re krisens utbrott. Kemiindustrin har utvecklat sig gynnsamt efter krisen, men tillv<8a>xten varierar kraftigt fr<8c>n kvartal till kvartal. Utrikeshandeln har varit viktig f<9a>r <8c>terh<8a>mtningen fr<8c>n den globala finanskrisen i Finland. Fallet i exporten var kraftigt, men s<8c> var ocks<8c> uppg<8c>ngen. I b<9a>rjan av detta <8c>r har exportens tillv<8a>xt stannat av, men trots det har f<9a>retagens tilltro till framtiden f<9a>rblivit positiv. Orderb<9a>ckerna <8a>r n<8a>stan lika fulla som de <8a>r i genomsnitt och lagren har normaliserats. Skillnaderna mellan f<9a>retagen <8a>r dock stora; en fj<8a>rdedel av f<9a>retagen har fortfarande ledig kapacitet i relation till efterfr<8c>gan. Ocks<8c> hush<8c>llens f<9a>rtroende har utvecklat sig positivt under det senaste <8c>ret. Samtidigt har den relativt goda l<9a>neutvecklingen gett st<9a>d <8c>t detaljhandeln. Detfinns dock m<8c>nga aspekter g<8a>llande hush<8c>llens framtidsutsikter som inte ser s<8c> ljusa ut. Ett orosmomentiden finl<8a>ndska ekonomin just nu <8a>r hush<8c>llens <9a>kande skulds<8a>ttning. Vi har inte sett n<8c>gon "deleveraging" inom hush<8c>llssektorn efter den ekonomiska krisen. Tv<8a>rtom s<8c> <9a>kar skulds<8a>ttningen alltj<8a>mnt. J<8a>mf<9a>rt med situationen i mitten av 90-talet har hush<8c>llens skuld i f<9a>rh<8c>llande till de disponibla inkomsterna <9a>kat drastiskt. L<8c>nen <8a>r allt l<8a>ngre och st<9a>rre b<8c>de i relation till inkomsterna och i relation till s<8a>kerheterna. Den h<9a>ga och tilltagande skulds<8a>ttningsgraden <8a>r ett fenomen som kan sk<9a>njas i hela Norden. Allt fler hush<8c>ll i Finland <8a>r kraftigt skuldsatta och <8a>r s<8c>ledes extra utsatta f<9a>r f<9a>r<8a>ndringar i den ekonomiska situationen. Cirka 17 % av de skuldsatta hush<8c>llen har en skulds<8a>ttningsgrad p<8c> <9a>ver 300 % av sina disponibla inkomster, och den h<8a>r andelen har stigit kraftigt de senaste <8c>ren. N<8a>rmare 50 % av hush<8c>llens totalskuld innehas av de h<8a>r kraftigt skuldsatta hush<8c>llen. Man kan under inga omst<8a>ndigheter prata om detta som ett marginellt fenomen. Det <8a>r av yttersta vikt atthush<8c>llen och bankerna iakttar f<9a>rsiktighet i de h<8a>r fr<8c>gorna. Hush<8c>llen b<9a>r ta l<8c>n efter betalningsf<9a>rm<8c>ga och ocks<8c> t<8a>nka p<8c> att r<8a>nteutgifterna kan stiga. Bankerna b<9a>r f<9a>r sin del inte bevilja hush<8c>llen alltf<9a>r stora l<8c>n i f<9a>rh<8c>llande till uppst<8a>llda s<8a>kerheter och betalningsf<9a>rm<8c>ga. B<8c>da parterna, b<8c>de l<8c>ngivaren och l<8c>ntagaren, b<9a>r ut<9a>va en viss f<9a>rsiktighet i de h<8a>r fr<8c>gorna f<9a>r att undvika katastrofer i framtiden. Faran med kraftig skulds<8a>ttning h<8a>rr<9a>r sig ofta till <9a>kade risker. Ett hush<8c>ll med h<9a>g skulds<8a>ttning <8a>r inte s<8c> flexibelt och kan inte ta emot lika stora t<9a>rnar som ett hush<8c>ll som har l<8a>gre skulds<8a>ttning. De kraftigt skuldsatta hush<8c>llen <8a>r ofta speciellt utsatta f<9a>r risker. I Finland <8a>r n<8a>sta alla bostadsl<8c>n knutna till korta marknadsr<8a>ntor, 1 m<8c>nads, 3 m<8c>naders och 12 m<8c>naders euribor samt bankernas egna prime-r<8a>ntor. Delvis inneb<8a>r det h<8a>r att penningpolitiken f<9a>rmedlas snabbt och effektivt i Finland, vilket <8a>r en positiv sak. Men myntets andra sida <8a>r att stigande r<8a>ntor p<8c>verkar finl<8a>ndska l<8c>nekunder snabbare <8a>n l<8c>nekunder i de flesta andra l<8a>nder i euroomr<8c>det d<8a>r bostadsl<8c>n fr<8a>mst <8a>r knutna till betydligt l<8a>ngre r<8a>ntor. D<8c> marknadsr<8a>ntorna sjunker gynnas de finl<8a>ndska hush<8c>llen p<8c> motsvarande s<8a>tt, men till det fenomenen h<8a>rr<9a>r sig f<8a>rre risker. En av de st<9a>rsta riskerna f<9a>r etthush<8c>ll <8a>r alltid arbetsl<9a>shetsrisken. N<8a>r man blir arbetsl<9a>s minskar ens inkomster och s<8c>ledes ocks<8c> f<9a>rm<8c>gan att sk<9a>ta sina l<8c>nekostnader. Ju st<9a>rre l<8c>n man har desto st<9a>rre hot utg<9a>r arbetsl<9a>sheten. Via arbetsl<9a>sheten kan man m<8a>ta de m<8a>nskliga kostnaderna av en kris. F<9a>ljderna av en l<8c>gkonjunktur blir ofta utdragna och sm<8a>rtsamma f<9a>r hush<8c>llen via den h<8a>r kanalen. Speciellt ur ett centralbanksperspektiv <8a>r just risken att l<8c>nekostnaderna blir osk<9a>tta en viktig aspekt av arbetsl<9a>sheten, eftersom detta <8a>r en kanal via vilken arbetsl<9a>shetens problem kan sprida sig vidare i samh<8a>llet via finanssektorn. Arbetsl<9a>sheten steg relativt sett litet under den senaste ekonomiska krisen, men i dagsl<8a>ge ser det ut som om nedg<8c>ngen skulle bli r<8a>tt s<8c> l<8c>ngsam. Arbetsl<9a>sheten har nu en l<8a>ngre tid stampat p<8c> st<8a>llet mellan 8 och 9 %. I praktiken betyder det h<8a>r att vi i april i <8c>r hade 207 000 arbetsl<9a>sa. I april 2008 fanns det 55000 f<8a>rre arbetsl<9a>sa. I ett litet land som Finland <8a>r det h<8a>r mycket. I samband med en l<8c>gkonjunktur stiger l<8c>ngtidsarbetsl<9a>sheten vanligtvis med en viss f<9a>rdr<9a>jning eftersom man m<8c>ste ha varit arbetsl<9a>s ett <8c>r f<9a>r att r<8a>knas som l<8c>ngtidsarbetsl<9a>s. F<9a>ljaktligen b<9a>rjade Finlands l<8c>ngtidsarbetsl<9a>shet stiga senare <8a>n arbetsl<9a>sheten och ingen nedg<8c>ng har <8a>nnu kunnat sk<9a>njas. Den intressanta fr<8c>gan f<9a>r tillf<8a>llet <8a>r ocks<8c> hur l<8c>ngtidsarbetsl<9a>sheten kommer att utvecklas och hurudana strukturella problem som h<8a>rr<9a>r sig till detta. N<8a>ra relaterat till den stigande skulds<8a>ttningen <8a>r utvecklingen p<8c>bostadsmarknaden, vilken ocks<8c> <8a>r relevant f<9a>r hush<8c>llen, eftersom hush<8c>llen <8a>r aktiva akt<9a>rer p<8c>bostadsmarknaden och en stor del av hush<8c>llens f<9a>rm<9a>genhet <8a>r knuten till bostadsmarknaden. Finland har liksom v<8a>ldigt m<8c>nga andra l<8a>nder sett en mycket kraftig uppg<8c>ng i de reala bostadspriserna under 2000-talet. Under perioden 2000<d0>2008 steg de reala bostadspriserna med cirka 50 %. I en internationell j<8a>mf<9a>relse ter detta sig inte som s<8c> v<8a>ldigt mycket. Till exempel har utvecklingen i Sverige under den h<8a>r tidsperioden varit kraftigare <8a>n i Finland. J<8a>mf<9a>rt med Tyskland, som i <9a>vrigt (men inte p<8c> bostadsmarknaden) har en r<8a>tt s<8c> likadan ekonomisk struktur som Finland, <8a>r utvecklingen dock hisnande. Vad har d<8c> m<9a>jliggjort en s<8c>dan stegringi bostadspriserna? F<9a>rklaringarna <8a>r de samma i de flesta l<8a>nder som har sett en kraftig uppg<8c>ng p<8c> bostadsmarknaden; M<9a>jligheten att f<8c> st<9a>rre och l<8a>ngre l<8c>n, liksom l<8c>ga r<8a>ntor och marginaler samt faktumet att utbudet inte riktigt h<8a>ngt med efterfr<8c>gan har alla bidragit till utvecklingen. En allm<8a>n <9a>veroptimism g<8a>llande den egna ekonomiska situationen och dess framtidsutsikter har troligtvis ocks<8c> lett till att vissa hush<8c>ll har fattat vad man i efterskott uppfattar som ickeoptimala ekonomiska beslut. Riskerna har underv<8a>rderats och det egna framtida inkomstfl<9a>det <9a>verv<8a>rderats. Till stor del kan dock utvecklingen i bostadspriserna f<9a>rklaras med uppg<8c>ngen i l<9a>ntagarnas inkomstniv<8c>. Som framg<8c>r ur bilden befinner sig bostadspriserna i relation till inkomsterna inte s<8c> mycket ovanf<9a>r det historiska snittet f<9a>r tillf<8a>llet. J<8a>mf<9a>rt med hyresutvecklingen ser ni att bostadspriserna har skenat iv<8a>g betydligt mera. En del av prisstegringen kan f<9a>rklaras med f<9a>r sn<8a>vt utbud. Speciellt i huvudstadsregionen <8a>r bristen p<8c> tomtmark ett problem, vilket ocks<8c> har bidragit till prisstegringen p<8c> bost<8a>der. Som ni ser i den h<8a>r grafen s<8c> har tomtmarkspriserna stigit betydligt snabbare <8a>n bostadspriserna i hela landet. Det h<8a>r <8a>r ett l<8c>ngsiktigt strukturellt problem p<8c> bostadsmarknaden som <8a>r speciellt synligt i huvudstadsregionen, ett problem som ocks<8c> <8c>terfinns i till exempel Stockholm, och som b<9a>r <8c>tg<8a>rdas. Vi lyckades i Finland undvika de v<8a>rsta excesserna p<8c> bostadsmarknaden i samband med den ekonomiska krisen. Den kraftiga tillv<8a>xten i byggaktiviteten avtog redan i god tid f<9a>re krisens utbrytande bland annat p<8c> grund av <8c>tstramande penningpolitik och brist p<8c> arbetskraft och h<9a>ga byggkostnader. S<8c>ledes undvek vi den v<8a>rsta <9a>verhettningen p<8c> bostadsmarknaden. I retrospekt kan vi konstatera att detta var lyckosamt. Nedg<8c>ngen i bostadspriser blev dock kort. Byggaktiviteten avtog snabbt, vilket ledde till ett tilltagande gap mellan utbud och efterfr<8c>gan. Samtidigt st<9a>dde den expansiva penningpolitiken hush<8c>llens ekonomiska situation. Bostadspriserna v<8a>nde snabbt brant upp<8c>t och v<8a>xte ifjol med n<8a>stan 9 %. I och med att det tar tid att bygga hus, n<8a>rmar vi oss f<9a>rst nu en situation d<8a>r utbudet av bost<8a>der b<9a>rjar normalisera sig, vilket torde hj<8a>lpa till att lugna ner bostadsprisutvecklingen fram<9a>ver. Riskerna p<8c> bostadsmarknaden <8a>r trots detta p<8c>tagliga. Hush<8c>llens skulds<8a>ttning bara <9a>kar och bostadspriserna har stigit kraftigt de tv<8c> senaste <8c>ren. Problemen har inte l<9a>sts. Understatssekreterare Martti Hetem<8a>kis arbetsgrupp har som en <8c>tg<8a>rd f<9a>reslagit att man skulle slopa avdragsr<8a>tten av l<8c>nekostnader i beskattningen. Vi st<9a>der f<9a>rslaget men anser samtidigt att detta knappast kommer att leda till att den kraftiga skulds<8a>ttningen skulle minska m<8a>rkbart. Inflationen <8a>r ur ett centralbanksperspektiv speciellt viktig. Det europeiska centralbankssystemets prim<8a>ra mandat <8a>r att h<8c>lla inflationen n<8a>ra men litet under 2 % p<8c> medell<8c>ng sikt. I april var inflationen i euroomr<8c>det 2,8 %, det vill s<8a>ga betydligt h<9a>gre <8a>n m<8c>let p<8c> medell<8c>ng sikt och det finns ett upp<8c>ttryck p<8c> inflationen <9a>verlag. Inflationen har f<8c>tt fart fr<8a>mst p<8c> grund av att r<8c>varupriserna har skjutit i h<9a>jden liksom livsmedelspriserna. Men ocks<8c> priset p<8c> service och industriprodukter har tilltagit under de senaste m<8c>naderna. F<9a>rv<8a>ntningen <8a>r dock att inflationen kommer att sjunka tillbaka under 2 % under <8c>r 2012 som en f<9a>ljd av att marknadspriserna p<8c> r<8c>varor sjunker. Ocks<8c> marknadens inflationsf<9a>rv<8a>ntningar tyder p<8c> en tilltro till att inflationen kommer att sjunka. Inflationen i Finland har under det h<8a>r <8c>ret hela tiden befunnit sig <9a>ver 3 %. Inflationen i Finland <8a>r allts<8c> h<9a>gre <8a>n i euroomr<8c>det i snitt. I Finland har livsmedelpriserna och servicepriserna stigit snabbare <8a>n i euroomr<8c>det i snitt. De genomf<9a>rda skattef<9a>r<8a>ndringarna under <8c>r 2010 i Finland f<9a>rklarar ocks<8c> delvis inflationsskillnaderna. ECB-r<8c>det har h<9a>jt r<8a>ntan en g<8c>ng under v<8c>ren till skillnad fr<8c>n de <9a>vriga stora centralbankerna som inte har h<9a>jt sina r<8a>ntor. M<8c>nga centralbanker har varit f<9a>rsiktiga med att strama <8c>t penningpolitiken, andra har igen varit aktivare, speciellt mindre centralbanker. Till exempel har Sveriges Riksbank h<9a>jt styrr<8a>ntan i flera repriser f<9a>r att stabilisera inflationen. I och med den ekonomiska l<8c>gkonjunkturen f<9a>rsvagades Finlands offentliga ekonomi kraftigt. Fast den tillv<8a>xt vi nu kan se <9a>kar skatteint<8a>kterna och minskar p<8c> de konjunkturberoende offentliga utgifterna kommer statens underskott att f<9a>rbli stort om inte nya finanspolitiska <8c>tg<8a>rder vidtas. Samtidigt kommer hela den offentliga sektorns underskott att forts<8a>tta existera. D<8c> man till den h<8a>r ekvationen s<8a>tter <8c>ldrandets effekter och utmaningar i framtiden b<9a>rjar det redan vara br<8c>ttom f<9a>r den offentliga sektorns konsolidering, och konsolideringsbehoven <8a>r p<8c>tagbara. Enligt finansministeriets bed<9a>mning <8a>r Finlands h<8c>llbarhetsgap cirka 5 % av BNP. Finlands Banks bed<9a>mning <8a>r motsvarande. Hur den offentliga sektorns konsolidering lyckas beror mycket p<8c> hur den genomf<9a>rs. Man b<9a>r fr<8a>mst v<8a>lja s<8c>dana tillv<8a>gag<8c>ngss<8a>tt som f<9a>rs<8a>mrar den ekonomiska tillv<8a>xten och syssels<8a>ttningen s<8c> litet som m<9a>jligt. Det h<8a>r b<9a>r beaktas speciellt i l<9a>sningar som ber<9a>r beskattningen. Ut<9a>ver detta <8a>r den valda stategins trov<8a>rdighet viktig. Om planerna <8a>r trov<8a>rdiga s<8c> minskar samtidigt hoten om framtida skatte<8c>tstramningar. Det h<8a>r st<9a>der konsumtion och investeringar i nul<8a>get. Fast Finlands ekonomiska utsikter ser r<8a>tt s<8c> goda ut finns det m<8c>nga utmaningar inom den n<8a>rmaste framtiden. Den offentliga sektorns h<8c>llbarhetsgap har vuxit sig s<8c> stort att det nu beh<9a>vs strukturf<9a>r<8a>ndringar samt en omv<8a>rdering av den offentliga sektorns utgifter och inkomster. <81>ldrandetkommer att spela en central roll i Finlands n<8a>ra framtid. Befolkningens <8c>ldrande minskar ekonomins tillv<8a>xtf<9a>ruts<8a>ttningar och den arbetsf<9a>ra befolkningen kommer att minska samtidigt som allt mer personal beh<9a>vs f<9a>r h<8a>lsov<8c>rds-och <9a>vriga v<8c>rdtj<8a>nster. En viktig aspekt <8a>r den offentliga ekonomins h<8c>llbarhet n<8a>r befolkningen blir allt <8a>ldre. Hur kan vi f<9a>rbereda oss p<8c> <8c>ldrandet? Arbetets produktivitet m<8c>ste h<9a>jas inom den offentliga basservicen. Detta inneb<8a>r b<8a>ttre och effektivare utnyttjande av informations-och kommunikationsteknik samt utvecklandet av nya arbetss<8a>tt. Det andra centrala elementet i denna ekvation <8a>r f<9a>rl<8a>ngandet av yrkeskarri<8a>rerna <d0> b<8c>de i b<9a>rjan, i slutet och i mitten. Ut<9a>ver dessa utmaningar inneb<8a>r utvecklingsl<8a>ndernas uppg<8c>ng <c2><d0> <8a>ven om de inneb<8a>r stora m<9a>jligheter <d0> ocks<8c> <9a>kad konkurrens p<8c> flera marknader b<8c>de inom service och mera traditionell varumarknad. Samtidigt f<9a>rflyttas efterfr<8c>gans k<8a>rna allt l<8a>ngre bort fr<8c>n Finland. Detta medf<9a>r stora anpassningsbehov f<9a>r m<8c>nga branscher och yrkesgrupper <d0> och d<8a>rmed f<9a>r hela Finlands ekonomi. Speciellt f<9a>r industriproduktionen, som sj<9a>nk kraftigt under l<8c>gkonjunkturen, <8a>r utmaningarna stora. <80>ven i s<8c>dana h<8a>r f<9a>rh<8c>llandena kan strukturf<9a>r<8a>ndringar st<9a>da den ekonomiska tillv<8a>xten. Ekonomins mikrostruktur borde hela tiden vara i omv<8a>lvning s<8c> att f<9a>retagen fortl<9a>pande kan anpassa sig till den nya omgivningen. Dessa <8a>r ocks<8c> av vikt f<9a>r l<9a>nebildningen. D<8c> industrins andel av v<8a>rde<9a>kningen minskar, <9a>kar servicebranschens betydelse. Enligt existerande forskning <8a>r produktiviteten inom flera servicebranscher betydligt l<8a>gre i Finland <8a>n i m<8c>nga andra industrialiserade l<8a>nder. Detta kan ses som en m<9a>jlighet. Inom de h<8a>r branscherna borde det vara f<9a>rh<8c>llandevis l<8a>tt att h<9a>ja produktivitetsniv<8c>n genom att l<8a>ra sig av internationellt sett b<8a>sta praxis samt genom att avskaffa konkurrenshinder. Exempel p<8c> konkurrenshinder <8a>r regleringar betr<8a>ffande planl<8a>ggning samt regleringar som begr<8a>nsar f<9a>retagsverksamhet. Vi lever i en tid av ekonomisk brytning. Nya l<9a>sningar och strukturer h<8c>ller p<8c> att utformas. Samtidigt <8a>r arbetet l<8c>ngt ifr<8c>n klart. Den offentliga sektorn, hush<8c>llen och m<8c>nga f<9a>retag har stora utmaningar framf<9a>r sig. En av utmaningarna <8a>r den h<9a>ga skulds<8a>ttningen och vad som skall och kan g<9a>ras <8c>t den. Inga av utmaningarna har klara och l<8a>tta l<9a>sningsalternativ. P<8c> det internationella planet <8a>r den offentliga skuldkrisen <8a>nnu ytterst bekymmersam och finanssektorns utmaningar har inte f<9a>rsvunnit n<8c>gonstans. Ut<9a>ver dessa problem <8a>r f<9a>rebyggandet av systemrisker en stor, men viktig, utmaning f<9a>r myndigheterna fram<9a>ver. Det g<8a>ller att hitta redskap som lyckas f<9a>rhindra att den kris vi genomlevt upprepar sig utan att strypa den ekonomiska tillv<8a>xten. Title: Opening words at seminar "Financial integration of the Baltic Sea district"
text: Director General Erkki Liikanen: Opening words at the seminar "Integration of the Baltic Sea District" in Turku 16.8.2011 . Speech . Tuesday 16August 2011, 2:00 PM Dear Mayor Randell, dear Russian and Swedish participants, professors, ladies and gentlemen. The Bank of Finland celebrates its 200th anniversary next December. 12.12.1811 Emperor Alexander I signed a manifesto by which The bank was founded  then known as Waihetus-Laina-and Depositioni-Contori in the Great Princeland of Finland. On the occasion of the anniversary, the Bank of Finland is organising a few events aimed at promoting the Bank of Finland's operations before and now. This history seminar is one of these events. It was clear that Turku was the right place to organise this seminar on the financial history of Finland and the surrounding area. In a way, the organisation of this seminar in Turku marks the return of the Bank of Finland to its roots. The bank was opened to the public here in Turku on August 14, 1812. The first seat was in the wooden house of gustaf Gadolin, a member of the board of trustees, professor and judge, which was located between the cathedral and the Aura River. From Gadolin's house, two upstairs rooms were rented to the bank, which the professor had previously used to give lectures, as well as a downstairs chamber and two basement vaults with iron doors. The Board of Trustees considered the premises thus obtained to be "almost commensurate with their needs and purpose." In the end, the bank's operating time in Turku was rather short. When Helsinki was made the capital of the Grand Duchy of Finland, the Bank moved there with the Senate. At this stage, the Bank acted as a branch under the auspices of the ministry of finance at the time, that is to say, the economic department of the Imperial Senate. It was a kind of exchange and loan fund, which also issued some banknotes. The bank moved to Helsinki in the autumn of 1819. Even today, you can still see a coffin in the Bank of Finland's Monetary Museum on Snellmaninkatu in Helsinki, where the bank's cashier was transported by horse-drawn carriage to its new location. The modest size of the coffin shows that the Bank of Finland's activities in the early days were quite small-scale. In the words of Emil Schybergson, the author of the first history of the bank, it was characterized by a "lack of refreshment." From this humble beginning, the Bank has grown along with Finnish society and the economy. Throughout its existence, the Bank has played a key role in the development of Finnish society from an official and backward Grand Duchy to a democratic and open welfare state. I will give just one telling example of this. Regular parliamentary activities began in Finland in 1863. Already a few years after that, from the beginning of 1868, the Bank of Finland was transferred from the Imperial Senate to the "guarantee and care" of the Diet. It is noteworthy that from now on and for the next five decades, the Bank of Finland was the only parliamentaryly governed part of the Finnish state apparatus. At that time, the entire rest of the state administration was still operating on the basis of a mandate from the emperor, without parliamentary responsibility. Without in any way praising the democratic nature of the Diet of the time, it has to be said, however, that the Bank of Finland was the forerunner of the public authorities based on parliament in Finland, even with a half-century lead. By the way, the Bank of Finland returned to Turku in 1840, when a branch was opened here for exchanging money. The branch's operations continued until the end of 2007, when it had to close due to changes in the logistics of money supply. For a long time, the Turku branch was one of the most important branches of the Bank of Finland located in 12 different parts of Finland. The Bank of Finland has decided to declare the students of abo Akademi University and the University of Turku a grant to apply for a master's thesis on the history of the Bank of Finland's Turku branch. A letter to that effect has been sent to the universities just mentioned. The theme of this seminar is the history of financial integration in the Baltic Sea region. The topic is interesting for the Bank of Finland because, in a small open economy such as Finland's, the central bank carries out its task at the interface between the domestic economy and the international economy. This position at the centre of the internationalisation of the economy has always set the tone for the Bank of Finland's operations as well. This has been the case regardless of how the Finnish monetary system has joined the world economy at different times. The arrangements have varied, but the objectives have been surprisingly permanent. Finland's monetary history consists of a series of different solutions, starting with the gold standard and the introduction of the euro. They have all arisen from the desire to integrate Finland into the broad world economy on which our well-being depends in the most stable and credible way possible. Today, the world economy and Europe as part of it are still living in the crisis that escalated three years ago. Major financial crises come from time to time, and they come as a surprise. The best lesson in what happens in crises often comes from history and underestimating history is dangerous. Carmen Reinhart and Kenneth Rogoff's excellent, fairly recent book ,"This Time Is Different," goes through hundreds of years of crisis. Crises have certain common features. According to the authors, behind financial crises there is often a "ignorance or arrogance": either history is not known, or it is arrogantly thought that the world has changed right now in such a way that the laws of the past no longer apply. This is where the title of the book comes from. Unfortunately, history cannot provide mechanical instructions for action or certain signs of crisis. Nevertheless, it is good for central banks and financial supervisors, as well as other economic decision-makers, to know history and to feel a certain humility in the face of it. That is why events such as this seminar and the research that I hope they will stimulate are very valuable. In recent weeks, the international economic situation has again changed in a worrying direction. There is increasing uncertainty about economic growth and the problems of indebted developed countries have caused unrest in the financial markets. In order to safeguard the transmission of monetary policy, the European Central Bank has acted decisively. The ECB has announced long-term lending operations to safeguard bank liquidity and activated its securities purchase programme. However, monetary policy alone cannot resolve the tension in financial markets against the background of excessive government indebtedness. This requires action by governments and parliaments. The Finnish economy has grown, but the risk of a dip in economic growth has also increased here. The situation requires caution and care in balancing central government finances even in changing circumstances. In a potentially deteriorating global economy, it is also important to take care of Finland's international competitiveness. An increase in domestic production costs in such a situation would entail risks to employment, economic growth and, consequently, to the consolidation of public finances. We have had the honour of having a number of very interesting and authoritative performers at our seminar. In the morning, Professor Susanna Fellman from the University of Helsinki will give us a presentation on the history of the Baltic Sea economic area, and Dr Mika Arola from the State Treasury will talk about Finland's entry into the international capital markets under the title Foreign Capital and Finland. After the lunch break, the seminar continues with two sessions. In the first, Bank Director Seppo Honkapohja, my colleague from the Board of Directors of the Bank of Finland, talks about his comparative research on nordic financial crises, and Antti Suvanto, Doctor of Political Science, talks about the internationalisation development of the Finnish banking system. The last session of the afternoon will be international and will be presented in English. Antti Kuustera and Juha Tarkka, authors of the history of the Bank of Finland, talk about the Bank of Finland's role in Finland's participation in international economic integration. We have also brought in representatives from our neighbouring countries. The histories of both the Central Banks of Sweden and Russia are very closely related to the history of the Bank of Finland. The Central Bank of Russia celebrated its 150th anniversary last year. Representatives of the Bank of Finland also had the honour of celebrating its anniversary, and at that time we had, among other things, a small stand at a historical exhibition held in Moscow. In honor of its anniversary, the Central Bank of Russia also published a two-volume history, Istorija Banka Rossii, the authors of which are here today: professor Yuri Petrov, director of the Institute of Russian History of the Russian Academy of Sciences, and Sergey Tatarinov, director of the Central Bank of Russia. In their presentation, they have promised to compare the monetary systems of Finland and Russia during the Empire. Sweden's central bank, the Riksbanken, is the oldest central bank in the world, founded as early as 1668. It also served as the Central Bank of Finland for over 140 years, when our country belonged to the Swedish Empire. Two years ago, the Central Bank of Sweden published its own history, an interesting work called "Pengarna och makten". It was written by the well-known Swedish historian Gunnar Wetterberg. He has also written biographies of swedish statesmen Axel Oxenstjerna and Arvid Horn, the latter of whom was otherwise Finnish by birth. Wetterberg is currently the Public Affairs Director of Saco, the Swedish Confederation of Academic Trade Unions. He tells us today about the history of the Riksbank, which is also the monetary history of Finland. I would like to extend a warm welcome to you all on this occasion and now give the floor to the Mayor of Turku, Aleksi Randell. The first session of the seminar will be chaired by Seppo Honkapohja.

Title: Speech at the Ylistaro Church
text: Director General Erkki Liikanen: Speech at Ylistaro Church, 23.10.2011 . Speech . Sunday 23 October 2011,10:00AM Director-General Erkki Liikanen Newspaper Ostrobothnian Hymn Sunday, Ylistaro Church on Sunday 23.10.2011 at 3 pm In 1961, our parents had acquired the first car, a Skoda of the 1951 model. During dad's summer vacation, we went on that trip around Finland. It was on that trip that I visited ylistaro church for the first time. It became its 50th anniversary in July. The world and Finland were living in an exciting time then. John F. Kennedy, the young President of the United States, and NikolaiHrushtshhev, the leader of the Soviet Union, had held a summit in May 1961 in Vienna. The meeting failed and superpower relations were strained. Berlin was at the center of the tension. Bailiff Eino Liikanen's family's holiday plan was not affected. We returned home from Lapland via Ostrobothnia to Mikkeli. On the way back, my parents wanted to take their four children to Seinajoki. Why Seinajoki? In Seinajoki, the chaplain was Erkki Kuparinen, a friend of his parents. My parents also thought it important to visit the recently completed fine Alvar Aalto Lakeuden Risti. Before Seinajoki, we stopped here in Ylistaro. The huge and impressive church of Ylistaro was visible on the flat in the landscape from afar. I don't forget it. The Church still makes a big impression today. After that memorable childhood summer trip, the situation in Europe became extremely tense. A month later, the Berlin Wall was erected. Next Sunday, 30.10., it will be 50 years since the Soviet Union submitted a note to Finland to start military consultations due to the tense situation in Europe. On the same day, the Soviet Union detonated a huge nuclear bomb on Novoja Zemlya. The memories of the war were still close and the citizens were worried. President Urho Kekkonen travelled to Novosibirsk to meet Hrushtsev. How much has happened since then. But let's return to the chaplain of Seinajoki, Erkki Kuparinen. He completed his pastoral degree in Mikkeli In the diocese in 1946 and then served as a priest in Mikkeli. The post-war years in Mikkeli were a time of intense youth revival. My mother and father met in the ward youth. Erkki Kuparinen was an important influence there. He married my parents in 1948. As the second oldest child, Erkki Kuparinen baptized me in the autumn of 1950. The parish youth of Mikkeli also included Toivo Tirronen, my father's neighbour from the rural municipality of Mikkeli. He studied mathematics and science at the University of Helsinki. After receiving a religious revival, Toivo Tirronen decided to move to Africa as a missionary. He moved there in 1950 and first acquired the training of a secondary school teacher. After that, he became a teacher and became a well-known influencer in Ovamboland. He translated the Bible into the local Ndonga language and did the grammar of the language. Later, in 1960, Toivo Tirronen founded oshigambo middle school and high school, of which he served as director for a long time. Many of Namibia's current leaders have received their basic education at Tirrose High School. Toivo Tirronen enjoys great respect in Namibia as a man of popular education. Everyone has their own recollections of when they had their first contact with missionary work, Ovamboland, and thus Africa. My father told about Hope Tirrose often. Africa was therefore exciting and close to us at the same time. But there was another connection. In 1955, dad got a part-time job as a part-time caretaker at a summer parish home. No salary was paid for the position, but the benefits of the post included a two-room and kitchen apartment on the upper floor of the parish home. Downstairs, on the other hand, diverse church services were held. We ran in them since we were five years old. The most exciting ones were related to the sewing clubs of the Finnish Missionary Society. They knitted and talked about Ovamboland and Africa. This all happened even before going to school. The Finnish Missionary Society has been operating in Namibia for a long time. It had to think deeply about its attitude to African issues in the 1960s as the independence movement rose. The president of the FMS was Professor Mikko Juva, who later became archbishop. In 1961, the Sharpeville massacre caused a lot of confusion within the FMS. In the same year, Mikko Juva travelled there for as many as seven weeks to get to know the situation. That's where Professor Juva was told. that a new political movement, SWAPO, caused concern among missionaries. Juva was sympathetic and positive about the rise of the independence movement. Title: Responsibility in decision-making before and now
text: President and CEO Erkki Liikanen: Responsibility in decision-making before and now, presentation at the 100th anniversary of Kusti Eskola's birth, 3.12.2011 . Speech . Saturday 3 December 2011,11:00AM Director-General Erkki Liikanen Presentation at the 100th anniversary of Kusti Eskola's birth in Sievi on 3.12.2011 at 11.00 a.m. RESPONSIBILITY IN DECISION-MAKING BEFORE AND NOW Ladies and gentlemen, friends, ladies and gentlemen. The theme of the centenary of Kusti Eskola's birth is "trust and responsibility". From the point of view of the current economic and political debate, one could hardly have chosen a more topical theme. Perceptions of the content of the responsibility of economic decision-makers in particular  to whom they are accountable and for what  are once again changing as a result of the global economic crisis and there is a lively debate on the issue, both in the media and in expert forums. *** KustiEskola is an example of a man who was trusted and who received a lot of responsibility in many fields of activity. He represented both his native region and his ideology in many of the highest positions in the kingdom. Of course, from the Bank of Finland's point of view, what attracts the most attention in his career is the long stint that he served as a member of the highest decision-making body of our central bank in the parliamentary banking council, and for a long time even as its chairman. Kusti Eskola was elected a member of the Bank of Finland's Banking Board in 1951. He became chairman of the banking council as early as 1954, when the previous chairman of the council, VihtoriVesterinen, a legendary figure in the Agrarian Union, left the banking council. Eskola's membership in the banking board lasted fifteen years and he also served as chairman for more than a decade. He supervised three governors of the Bank of Finland, Sakari Tuomioomioja, Rainer von Fieandt and Klaus Waris. Although Eskola dropped out of parliament in 1962, he continued as chairman of the banking council for one more term, until the 1966 parliamentary elections. After these elections, the central banking commissioners were replaced. Eskola and Toivo Kinnunen were replaced by Nestori Kaasalainen and Eino Uusitalo. When Sakari Tuomioja moved from the position of Governor of the Bank of Finland to London in 1955, the Bank's Board of Governors voted to succeed him. By a vote of 7 to 2, it featured Klaus Warista. Chairman Kusti Eskola and party secretary Arvo Korsimo supported von Fieandt. Paasikivi appointed von Fieandt. The following year, Finance Minister Penna Tervo, who was appointed to the executive board, died in a car accident. He never had time to take up the post. In the Banking Council, VainoTanner proposed permanent secretary Toivo Takki to replace him. Kusti Eskola proposed the then Minister of Finance Aarre Simo, behind whom the Banking Council finally sided. Kekkonen appointed Simonen. In the Banking Council, Eskola opposed raising interest rates and therefore had disagreements, especially with President Klaus Waris, who would have liked to use a flexible interest rate policy as a means of combating inflation. At that time, interest rate control was practised in Finland, and as a result, the Banking Council had a tight grip on banks' loan interest rates. During the long period during which Eskola was a banking commissioner, no general increases in bank lending rates were implemented in Finland. (The Bank of Finland's own base rate was increased a couple of times, but these increases were not allowed to be passed on to bank lending rates.) In 1962, Klaus Waris tried to push through one of the raises, but was forced to retreat to the so-called "bulwark". in the interest rate war in front of the banking council headed by Eskola. *** Returning to the question of responsibility, from today's point of view, it is startling how, in the 1950s and even in the 1960s, positions of trust in society piled up in the same people. Kusti Eskolakin served as a minister in three different governments at the same time as chairman of the banking council  minister of transport in Kekkonen's IV government, minister of agriculture in sukselainen's government and minister of transport in fagerholm II government. Combining the functions of a minister and a banking commissioner would not be an option at present, as it is thought to violate the independence of the Bank of Finland in relation to the government. In the past decades, however, such a combination of tasks was common and was considered completely normal in the case of leading politicians. For example, Vaino Tanner served simultaneously as chairman of the banking council and as minister of finance in the Cajander government in the 1930s, as well as in the governments during the Continuation War. The combination of ministerial duties and the management duties of the Bank of Finland was not limited to the Board of Governors. In the old days, the members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Finland also sometimes acted as ministers without taking a leave of absence from the Bank for that purpose. It is something of an extreme case when Sakari Tuomioja served at the beginning of the 1950s simultaneously as governor of the Bank of Finland, minister of foreign trade in Kekkonen's government and, at the same time, minister of trade and industry. The time is also illustrated by the fact that Kusti Eskola was able to combine his work at the Central Bank with a position of trust in a private financial institution. Kusti Eskola had held positions of trust in the cooperative fund movement since the 1950s, and in 1962 he rose to the position of chairman of the supervisory board of OKO, the central financial institution of cooperative funds. In this case, a situation arose in which the chairman of the highest decision-making body of the Central Bank, the Banking Council, was at the same time the chairman of the board of directors of a significant monetary institution. In these roles, he found himself in a difficult middleman, especially when OKO in 1966 ran into a liquidity crisis due to, for example, the financing of Mekes Oy and had to rely on the support of the Central Bank. The situation led OKO to a change of management. I do not want to make Kusti Eskola a special case in his dual role. The situation was not as unique as it seems now, but was part of the picture of the times. For example, until the 1980s, it was the practice for the Governor of the Bank of Finland to at the same time act as chairman of the board of one Finnish bank  Postipankki. When this practice after the war began, it seemed natural. It became impossible only when Postipankki was converted into a limited liability company. It should also be remembered that ministers sat on the supervisory boards of state-owned companies. It was also considered normal. It was not until the late 1980s that the debate on the issue began. *** These examples from recent history show how much attitudes towards the position of decision-maker, including shop stewards, have changed in Finland over the years. The change has been great, but inevitable. It would be an interesting research topic to find out which underlying currents of social and economic development have contributed to this change. I believe that, if the matter were investigated, one of the main reasons would be that the attitude towards competition and competition policy has changed. The activities of the same persons in several different roles in the market would lead to conflicts of interest and jeopardise the neutrality of competition. Another reason for the change may be the growth of financial markets and the emphasis on the importance of information affecting them. This has put insider problems in the spotlight. The change is not only Finnish. Since the 1990s, the development of corporate governance has become an ideal all over the world, and the seating of managers in various decision-making bodies, their potential conflicts of interest and disqualifications are assessed accordingly. As a result of the changes that have taken place, it is now generally thought that the role of management bodies and senior management in companies is to think only about the best interests of the company and, in particular, about the development of the shareholder's wealth. The company would be primarily responsible to its owners. Of course, the owner's perspective is not necessarily at odds with looking at the interests of other stakeholders as well. In a successful company, for example, the satisfaction of customers and employees is also in the long run in the interest of the owners, as is well known. Perhaps the most essential content of the change in corporate governance that began in the 1980s was the emphasis on the interests of the owners, precisely in relation to the executive management and any specific objectives of the management. The idea of corporate governance has had some important consequences for today's debate. When executive management incentives were designed in such a way as to serve the interests of the owners, the general solution was remuneration schemes tied to the share price. The idea, of course, was to emphasize the responsibility of management to the owners, but practical applications and the results achieved have recently attracted growing criticism. In recent years, there has been an increasing emphasis on another demand on economic decision-makers: the emphasis is increasingly on the need for socially, environmental and morally responsible decision-making. As has been said, these requirements do not necessarily conflict with the long-term interests of the owners, but in practice, a social responsibility mindset leads to a rather different and more diverse picture of who the company and the decision-makers within it are responsible for. What is clear is that companies are paying more and more attention to the fact that their activities can withstand critical scrutiny from many different angles. In practice, the concept of responsible business has already expanded to include transparency and general acceptability of operations. This may sound obvious, but the changes underway are major, not least in the financial sector. *** Recently, the debate on sustainability in the financial sector has been related to executive remuneration in particular. This is linked to the broader question of the activities of banks in the years leading to the current financial crisis. One of the causes of the international debt crisis was the over-careless attitude of financial institutions to risk, more precisely, the distortion of the relationship between return and risk in the decision-making of banks and institutional investors. This has probably been contributed to by management reward schemes based on options or increases in the value of shares, which have encouraged imprudent risk-taking in areas such as investment, M&A and credit marketing. Carelessly constructed reward systems created mechanisms in which risk was distributed very asymmetrically. Management and portfolio managers received shares of potential profits, but did not suffer any losses. It is easy to see what kind of risk-taking this encourages if the reward tied to the share price does not have a predetermined upper limit. The concern is not new. In Finland, the Commercial Banking Act of 1933, which was enacted in the midst of the banking crisis of the 1930s, banned the use of remuneration based on results or business expansion in banks. Later on about that so-called. the ban on partial wages was lifted, but now the issue is once again topical. The importance of responsible remuneration was recognised and recognised early on in the current crisis. In november 2008, the G20 leaders in Washington committed themselves in a statement to reforming financial markets in accordance with commonly agreed principles. The first of these principles concerned transparency and accountability in the financial markets. It said that in the financial sector, incentives had to be "adjusted to avoid excessive risk-taking." In the autumn of 2009, the International Financial Stability Committee (FSB) responded to the challenge of G20 leaders and published the principles of good remuneration, which has since been put into practice in the regulation and supervision of various countries. They require supervisors to require significant financial institutions to demonstrate that their remuneration systems take sufficient account of risk, solvency and liquidity. If a credit institution's remuneration system does not meet these principles, it may, for example, be subject to an increased capital requirement. At European level, the directive regulating the remuneration system entered into force last year. In Finland, the new principles concerning remuneration were defined in a decree that entered into force at the beginning of this year. The Financial Supervisory Authority supplemented the provisions of the decree with its statement last spring. I will not go into detail here about the content of the new principles, but there are a couple of points worth mentioning. First of all, banks must ensure that remuneration policies take into account the bank's risks, cost of capital and liquidity. There must be a predetermined upper limit for variable remuneration. Any severance pay granted to the Director shall be determined in such a way that it does not lead to the rewarding of a failed performance. A significant change is that a large part of the variable remuneration can only be paid to the recipient 3-5 years after it has been earned. Perseverance and risk-bearing are also favoured by obliging banks to pay at least half of variable remuneration in shares or other similar financial instruments that cannot be realised except within that 3-5-year waiting period. Furthermore, the remuneration policy must include a condition that if a bank's solvency falls too low, the variable remuneration may be waived altogether. *** The new rules that have now been introduced aim, above all, to make the risk-taking rate of the senior management of credit institutions more moderate and to make incentive schemes give more weight to long-term sustainable growth. But responsibility in remuneration means more than that the reward system should not encourage unhealthy risk-taking. The other aspect of responsibility is moderation. Sometimes a word is put in quotation marks because it is so open to interpretation. But there is no way around the question. Banks and the financial sector more broadly have notoriously come under criticism. One of the reasons has been precisely the debate about the reasonableness of remuneration. Businesses  and public authorities alike  depend on acting in accordance with their audiences' sense of justice. If it turns out that there is a sharp discrepancy between one's own assessment and the public's perception, damage may arise that will be difficult to repair. The financial sector is fulfilling an important community role. It provides an opportunity for people to save for the future and spend in advance on future savings. Its task is to direct the capital accumulated by savers to productive objects. Well-functioning financing is a prerequisite for housing production and, more generally, for growth and employment. In Finland, the situation of banks is better than in many other countries. But even here, they depend on how the climate of opinion in the world develops. A necessary starting point for maintaining trust is to understand and recognise how dependent banks are on the full acceptability of their activities in society. *** Democracy and the market economy both operate on trust and responsibility. At the time of Kusti Eskola, men like him represented their stakeholders, background and ideas in the most diverse positions. In today's world, the requirements are different and the ways of working have changed with them. Policymakers are the target of increasingly fierce economic competition and increasingly stringent demands for efficiency, but also of the media's ruthless scrutiny. But perhaps a common feature of the current operating environment and Eskola's time is that people in positions of responsibility must  in addition to being able to achieve good economic results  also visibly represent certain values that society considers to be right. If there is a suspicion that this requirement is not met, the financial results of the work are unlikely to turn out to be sustainable either.

Eskolan j<8a>senyys pankkivaltuustossa kesti viisitoista vuotta ja puheenjohtajanakin h<8a>n toimi yli vuosikymmenen ajan. H<8a>n ehti valvoa kolmea Suomen Pankin p<8a><8a>johtajaa, SakariTuomiojaa, Rainer von Fieandtia ja Klaus Warista. Vaikka Eskola putosi eduskunnasta vuonna 1962, h<8a>n jatkoi pankkivaltuuston puheenjohtajana viel<8a> yhden vaalikauden ajan, vuoden 1966 eduskuntavaaleihin asti. N<8a>iden vaalien j<8a>lkeen keskustan pankkivaltuutetut vaihdettiin. Eskolan ja Toivo Kinnusen tilalle valittiin Nestori Kaasalainen ja Eino Uusitalo. Kun Sakari Tuomioja siirtyi vuonna 1955 Suomen Pankin p<8a><8a>johtajan teht<8a>v<8a>st<8a> Lontooseen, pankkivaltuusto <8a><8a>nesti h<8a>nen seuraajastaan. <80><8a>nin 7<d0>2 se esitti Klaus Warista. Puheenjohtaja Kusti Eskola ja puoluesihteeri Arvo Korsimo olivat von Fieandtin kannalla. Paasikivi nimitti von Fieandtin. Seuraavana vuonna johtokuntaan nimitetty valtiovarainministeri Penna Tervo kuoli auto-onnettomuudessa. H<8a>n ei ehtinyt koskaan ottaa virkaa vastaan. Pankkivaltuustossa V<8a>in<9a>Tanner esitti tilalle kansliap<8a><8a>llikk<9a> Toivo Takkia. Kusti Eskola esitti silloista valtiovarainministeri Aarre Simosta, jonka taakse pankkivaltuusto lopulta asettui. Kekkonen nimitti Simosen. Pankkivaltuustossa Eskola asettui korkojen korottamista vastaan ja joutui siksi erimielisyyksiin varsinkin p<8a><8a>johtaja Klaus Wariksen kanssa, joka olisi halunnut k<8a>ytt<8a><8a> joustavaa korkopolitiikkaa inflaation torjuntakeinona. Tuolloin Suomessa harjoitettiin korkos<8a><8a>nn<9a>stely<8a> ja pankkivaltuustolla oli sen johdosta tiukka ote pankkien lainakoroista. Sin<8a> pitk<8a>n<8a> aikana, jonka Eskola oli pankkivaltuutettuna, Suomessa ei toteutettu yht<8a><8a>n yleist<8a> pankkien antolainauskorkojen korotusta. (Suomen Pankin omaa peruskorkoa korotettiin pari kertaa, mutta n<8a>iden korotusten ei annettu v<8a>litty<8a> pankkien antolainauskorkoihin.) Vuonna 1962 Klaus Waris yritti ajaa yhden korotuksen l<8a>pi, mutta joutui per<8a><8a>ntym<8a><8a>n ns. korkosodassa Eskolan johtaman pankkivaltuuston edess<8a>. *** Vastuukysymykseen palataksemme, nykyajan n<8a>k<9a>kulmasta on h<8a>tk<8a>hdytt<8a>v<8a><8a>, miten 1950-luvulla ja viel<8a> 1960.luvullakin yhteiskunnalliset luottamusteht<8a>v<8a>t kasaantuivat samoille henkil<9a>ille. Kusti Eskolakin toimi ministerin<8a> kolmessa eri hallituksessa samaan aikaan kun oli pankkivaltuuston puheenjohtajana <d0> Kekkosen IV hallituksen kulkulaitosministerin<8a>, Sukselaisen hallituksen maatalousministerin<8a> ja Fagerholmin IIIhallituksen kulkulaitosministerin<8a>. Ministerin ja pankkivaltuutetun teht<8a>vien yhdist<8a>minen ei nykyisin tulisi kysymykseen, koska sen ajatellaan loukkaavan Suomen Pankin itsen<8a>isyytt<8a> suhteessa hallitukseen. Mennein<8a> vuosikymmenin<8a> t<8a>llainen teht<8a>vien yhdistely kuitenkin oli yleist<8a> ja sit<8a> pidettiin johtavien poliitikkojen tapauksessa t<8a>ysin normaalina. Esimerkiksi V<8a>in<9a> Tanner toimi yht<8a> aikaa sek<8a> pankkivaltuuston puheenjohtajana ett<8a> valtiovarainministerin<8a> Cajanderin hallituksessa 1930-luvulla ja samoin my<9a>s jatkosodan aikaisissa hallituksissa. Ministerin teht<8a>vien ja Suomen Pankin johtoteht<8a>vien yhdistely ei rajoittunut pankkivaltuustoon. My<9a>s Suomen Pankin johtokunnan j<8a>senet toimivat ennen vanhaan joskus ministerein<8a> ottamatta sit<8a> varten virkavapautta pankista. Jonkinlainen <8a><8a>ritapaus on, kun Sakari Tuomioja toimi 1950-luvun alussa yht<8a> aikaa Suomen Pankin p<8a><8a>johtajana, Kekkosen hallituksen ulkomaankauppaministerin<8a> ja samalla viel<8a> kauppa-ja teollisuusministerin<8a>kin. Aikaa kuvaa sekin, ett<8a> Kusti Eskola saattoi yhdist<8a><8a> toimintansa keskuspankissa luottamusteht<8a>v<8a><8a>n yksityisess<8a> rahalaitoksessa. Kusti Eskola oli toiminut 1950-luvulta asti osuuskassaliikkeen luottamusteht<8a>viss<8a>, ja vuonna 1962 h<8a>n nousi osuuskassojen keskusrahalaitoksen OKO:n hallintoneuvoston puheenjohtajaksi. T<8a>ll<9a>in syntyi tilanne, jossa keskuspankin korkeimman p<8a><8a>t<9a>ksentekoelimen, pankkivaltuuston puheenjohtaja oli samalla merkitt<8a>v<8a>n rahalaitoksen hallintoneuvoston puheenjohtaja. H<8a>n joutui n<8a>iss<8a> rooleissaan hankalaan v<8a>lik<8a>teen erityisesti kun OKO vuonna 1966 ajautui maksuvalmiuskriisiin mm. Mekes Oy:n rahoittamisen vuoksi ja joutui turvautumaan keskuspankin tukeen. Tilanne vei OKO:n johdon vaihtamiseen. En t<8a>ss<8a> halua nostaa Kusti Eskolaa kaksoisroolissaan mitenk<8a><8a>n erikoistapaukseksi. Tilanne ei ollut niin ainoalaatuinen kuin milt<8a> se nyt tuntuu, vaan kuului ajan kuvaan. Esimerkiksi aina 1980-luvulle asti oli k<8a>yt<8a>nt<9a>n<8a>, ett<8a> Suomen Pankin p<8a><8a>johtaja toimi samalla yhden suomalaisen pankin <d0> Postipankin <d0> hallituksen puheenjohtajana. Kun t<8a>m<8a> k<8a>yt<8a>nt<9a> sodan j<8a>lkeen alkoi, se tuntui luonnolliselta. Mahdottomaksi se muuttui vasta kun Postipankki muutettiin osakeyhti<9a>ksi. Pit<8a><8a> my<9a>s muistaa, ett<8a> ministerit istuivat valtioyhti<9a>iden hallintoneuvostoissa. Sit<8a> pidettiin my<9a>s normaalina. Asiasta alkoi keskustelu vasta 1980-luvun lopulla. *** N<8a>m<8a> esimerkit l<8a>hihistoriasta osoittavat, miten paljon suhtautuminen p<8a><8a>t<9a>ksentekij<8a>n, my<9a>s luottamushenkil<9a>n asemaan on vuosien varrella Suomessa muuttunut. Muutos on ollut suuri, mutta v<8a>ist<8a>m<8a>t<9a>n. Olisi mielenkiintoinen tutkimuskohde selvitt<8a><8a>, mitk<8a> yhteiskunnallisen ja taloudellisen kehityksen pohjavirrat ovat vaikuttaneet t<8a>h<8a>n muutokseen. Luulen, ett<8a> jos asiaa selvitett<8a>isiin, yhdeksi keskeiseksi syyksi nousisi se, ett<8a> suhtautuminen kilpailuun ja kilpailupolitiikkaan on muuttunut. Samojen henkil<9a>iden toiminta useissa eri rooleissa markkinoilla johtaisi eturistiriitoihin ja vaarantaisi kilpailun neutraalisuuden. Toinen syy muutokseen voi olla rahoitusmarkkinoiden kasvu ja niill<8a> vaikuttavan tiedon merkityksen korostuminen. T<8a>m<8a> on nostanut sis<8a>piiriongelmat valokeilaan. Muutos ei ole vain suomalainen. Corporate Governancen eli hyv<8a>n hallintotavan kehitt<8a>minen on 1990-luvulta alkaen noussut ihanteeksi kaikkialla maailmassa, ja johtohenkil<9a>iden istumista erilaisissa p<8a><8a>t<9a>ksentekoelimiss<8a>, heid<8a>n mahdollisia intressiristiriitojaan ja esteellisyyksi<8a><8a>n arvioidaan sen mukaan. Tapahtuneiden muutosten seurauksena nykyisin ajatellaan yleisesti, ett<8a> hallintoelinten ja toimivan johdon teht<8a>v<8a>n<8a> yrityksiss<8a> on ajatella vain yhti<9a>n parasta ja nimenomaan osakkeenomistajan varallisuuden kehityst<8a>. Yritys olisi ensi sijassa vastuussa omistajilleen. Omistajan<8a>k<9a>kulma ei ole tietenk<8a><8a>n ole v<8a>ltt<8a>m<8a>tt<8a> ristiriidassa sen kanssa, ett<8a> tarkastellaan my<9a>s muiden sidosryhmien etua. Menestyv<8a>ss<8a> yrityksess<8a> esimerkiksi asiakkaiden ja ty<9a>ntekij<9a>iden tyytyv<8a>isyys on pitk<8a>n p<8a><8a>lle my<9a>s omistajien etu, kuten hyvin tiedet<8a><8a>n. Ehk<8a> 1980-luvulla alkaneen hallintotapamuutoksen oleellisin sis<8a>lt<9a> oli omistajien edun korostuminen nimenomaan suhteessa toimivaan johtoon ja johdon mahdollisiin erityistavoitteisiin. Corporate Governance-aatteella on ollut er<8a>it<8a> t<8a>m<8a>n p<8a>iv<8a>n keskustelun kannalta merkitt<8a>vi<8a> seurauksia. Kun toimivan johdon kannustimet suunniteltiin siten, ett<8a> ne toteuttaisivat omistajien etua, yleinen ratkaisu olivat osakekurssiin sidotut palkitsemisj<8a>rjestelm<8a>t. Ajatuksena oli tietysti korostaa johdon vastuuta omistajille, mutta k<8a>yt<8a>nn<9a>n sovellukset ja saavutetut tulokset ovat viime aikoina her<8a>tt<8a>neet kasvavaa kritiikki<8a>. Viime vuosina on yh<8a> enemm<8a>n ollut esill<8a> toinenkin, talousel<8a>m<8a>n p<8a><8a>tt<8a>jiin kohdistuva vaatimus: yh<8a> enemm<8a>n korostetaan, ett<8a> p<8a><8a>t<9a>ksenteon on oltava vastuullista sosiaalisesti, ymp<8a>rist<9a>llisesti ja moraalisesti. Kuten sanottu, n<8a>m<8a> vaatimukset eiv<8a>t ole v<8a>ltt<8a>m<8a>tt<8a> ristiriidassa omistajien pitk<8a>n aikav<8a>lin intressien kanssa, mutta k<8a>yt<8a>nn<9a>ss<8a> yhteiskuntavastuuta painottava ajattelutapa johtaa melko lailla toisenlaiseen ja monipuolisempaan kuvaan siit<8a>, kenelle yritys ja sen piiriss<8a> toimivat p<8a><8a>tt<8a>j<8a>t ovat vastuussa. Selv<8a><8a> on, ett<8a> yritykset kiinnitt<8a>v<8a>t yh<8a> enemm<8a>n huomiota siihen, ett<8a> niiden toiminta kest<8a><8a> kriittisen tarkastelun monista eri n<8a>k<9a>kulmista. Vastuullisen liiketoiminnan k<8a>site on k<8a>yt<8a>nn<9a>ss<8a> jo laajentunut sis<8a>lt<8a>m<8a><8a>n toiminnan l<8a>pin<8a>kyvyyden ja yleisen hyv<8a>ksytt<8a>vyyden. T<8a>m<8a> saattaa kuulostaa itsest<8a><8a>n selv<8a>t<8a>, mutta k<8a>ynniss<8a> olevat muutokset ovat suuria eik<8a> v<8a>hiten rahoitusalalla. *** Viime aikoina rahoitusalaa koskeva keskustelu vastuullisuudesta on liittynyt varsinkin johdon palkitsemiseen. T<8a>m<8a> kytkeytyy laajempaan kysymykseen pankkien toiminnasta nykyiseen rahoituskriisiin johtaneina vuosina. Yksi kansainv<8a>lisen velkakriisin syist<8a> oli rahoituslaitosten liian huoleton suhtautuminen riskeihin, tarkemmin sanoen tuoton ja riskin v<8a>lisen suhteen v<8a><8a>ristyminen pankkien ja institutionaalisten sijoittajien p<8a><8a>t<9a>ksenteossa. T<8a>h<8a>n ovat luultavasti my<9a>t<8a>vaikuttaneet optioihin tai osakkeiden arvonnousuun perustuvat johdon palkintaj<8a>rjestelm<8a>t, jotka ovat kannustaneet varomattomaan riskinottoon esimerkiksi sijoitustoiminnassa, yrityskaupoissa ja luottojen markkinoinnissa. Varomattomasti rakennetut palkitsemisj<8a>rjestelm<8a>t loivat mekanismeja, joissa riski jaettiin hyvin ep<8a>symmetrisesti. Johto ja salkunhoitajat saivat osuuksia mahdollisista voitoista, mutta eiv<8a>t k<8a>rsineet mahdollisista tappioista. On helppo n<8a>hd<8a>, millaiseen riskinottoon t<8a>llainen kannustaa, jos osakekurssiin sidotulla palkkiolla ei ole ennalta m<8a><8a>r<8a>tty<8a> yl<8a>rajaa. Huolenaihe ei ole uusi. Suomessa vuoden 1933 liikepankkilaki, joka s<8a><8a>dettiin 1930-luvun pankkikriisin tunnelmissa, kielsi tulokseen tai liiketoiminnan laajentumiseen perustuvan palkitsemisen k<8a>yt<9a>n pankeissa. My<9a>hemmin tuosta ns. osapalkkakiellosta luovuttiin, mutta nyt kysymys on siis j<8a>lleen ajankohtainen. Vastuullisen palkitsemisen merkitys tunnistettiin ja tunnustettiin jo t<8a>m<8a>nkertaisen kriisin varhaisessa vaiheessa. Marraskuussa 2008 Washingtoniin kokoontuneet G20-maiden johtajat sitoutuivat julkilausumassaan uudistamaan rahoitusmarkkinoita yhteisesti sovittujen periaatteiden mukaan. Ensimm<8a>inen n<8a>ist<8a> periaatteista koski rahoitusmarkkinoiden l<8a>pin<8a>kyvyytt<8a> ja vastuullisuutta. Sen mukaan rahoitusalalla kannustimet oli <d3>mukautettava v<8a>ltt<8a>m<8a><8a>n liiallista riskinottoa.<d3> Syksyll<8a> 2009 Kansainv<8a>linen finanssimarkkinoiden vakauskomitea (FSB) vastasi G20-johtajien haasteeseen ja julkaisi hyv<8a>n palkitsemisen periaatteet, jota on sen j<8a>lkeen viety k<8a>yt<8a>nt<9a><9a>n eri maiden s<8a><8a>ntelyss<8a> ja valvonnassa. Niiden mukaan valvontaviranomaisten on vaadittava merkitt<8a>vi<8a> rahoituslaitoksia osoittamaan, ett<8a> niiden palkintaj<8a>rjestelm<8a>t ottavat riskin, vakavaraisuuden ja maksuvalmiuden riitt<8a>v<8a>sti huomioon. Mik<8a>li luottolaitoksen palkintaj<8a>rjestelm<8a> ei t<8a>yt<8a> n<8a>it<8a> periaatteita, sille voidaan esimerkiksi asettaa korotettu p<8a><8a>omavaatimus. Euroopan tasolla palkintaj<8a>rjestelm<8a><8a> s<8a><8a>telev<8a> direktiivi tuli voimaan viime vuonna. Suomessa palkitsemista koskevat uudet periaatteet m<8a><8a>riteltiin asetuksella, joka tuli voimaan t<8a>m<8a>n vuoden alusta. Finanssivalvonta t<8a>ydensi asetuksen m<8a><8a>r<8a>yksi<8a> kannanotollaan viime kev<8a><8a>n<8a>. En t<8a>ss<8a> ryhdy kertaamaan uusien periaatteiden sis<8a>lt<9a><8a> yksityiskohtaisesti, mutta pari kohtaa kannattaa mainita. Pankkien on ensinn<8a>kin huolehdittava, ett<8a> palkitsemisj<8a>rjestelm<8a>t ottavat huomioon pankin riskit, p<8a><8a>omakustannukset ja maksuvalmiuden. Muuttuville palkkioille on oltava ennalta m<8a><8a>r<8a>tty yl<8a>raja. Johtajalle my<9a>nnett<8a>v<8a>n mahdollisen erorahan on m<8a><8a>r<8a>ydytt<8a>v<8a> siten, ett<8a> se ei johda ep<8a>onnistuneen suorituksen palkitsemiseen. Merkitt<8a>v<8a> muutos on, ett<8a> suuri osa muuttuvasta palkkiosta voidaan maksaa sen saajalle vasta 3<d0>5 vuoden kuluttua siit<8a> kun se on ansaittu. Pitk<8a>j<8a>nteisyytt<8a> ja riskin kantoa suositaan sill<8a>kin, ett<8a> pankkeja velvoitetaan maksamaan v<8a>hint<8a><8a>n puolet muuttuvista palkkioista osakkeina tai muina vastaavina rahoitusinstrumentteina, joita ei voi realisoida kuin tuon 3<d0>5 vuoden odotusajan puitteissa. Palkitsemisj<8a>rjestelm<8a>ss<8a> on sit<8a> paitsi oltava ehto, ett<8a> jos pankin vakavaraisuus laskee liian huonoksi, muuttuva palkkio voidaan j<8a>tt<8a><8a> kokonaan maksamatta. *** Nyt k<8a>ytt<9a><9a>n tulleilla uusilla s<8a><8a>nn<9a>ill<8a> pyrit<8a><8a>n ennen kaikkea s<8a><8a>t<8a>m<8a><8a>n luottolaitosten toimivan johdon riskinottohalukuutta maltillisempaan suuntaan ja saamaan kannustinj<8a>rjestelm<8a>t antamaan enemm<8a>n painoa pitk<8a>n aikav<8a>lin kest<8a>v<8a>lle kasvulle. Mutta palkitsemisen vastuullisuus merkitsee muutakin kuin sit<8a>, ett<8a> palkkioj<8a>rjestelm<8a> ei saisi kannustaa ep<8a>terveeseen riskinottoon. Toinen vastuullisuuden puoli on kohtuus. Joskus sana laitetaan lainausmerkkeihin, koska se on niin tulkinnanvarainen. Mutta kysymyst<8a> ei voi kiert<8a><8a>. Pankit ja rahoitusala laajemminkin on tunnetusti joutunut kritiikin kohteeksi. Yhten<8a> syyn<8a> on ollut juuri keskustelu palkitsemisen kohtuullisuudesta. Yritykset <d0> ja yht<8a> lailla viranomaiset <d0> ovat riippuvaisia siit<8a>, ett<8a> ne toimivat yleis<9a>jens<8a> oikeudentajun mukaisesti. Jos k<8a>y niin, ett<8a> oma arvio ja kansalaisten k<8a>sitys poikkeavat rajusti toisistaan, voi synty<8a> vahinkoa, jota on vaikea korjata. Rahoitusala toteuttaa t<8a>rke<8a><8a> yhteiskuista teht<8a>v<8a><8a>. Se tarjoaa ihmisille mahdollisuuden s<8a><8a>st<8a><8a> tulevaisuutta varten ja kuluttaa etuk<8a>teen tulevaisuuden s<8a><8a>st<9a>j<8a>. Sen teht<8a>v<8a>n<8a> on suunnata s<8a><8a>st<8a>jien ker<8a><8a>m<8a>t p<8a><8a>omat tuottaviin kohteisiin. Toimiva rahoitus on asuntotuotannon ja yleisemminkin kasvun ja ty<9a>llisyyden edellytys. Suomessa pankkien tilanne on parempi kuin monessa muussa maassa. Mutta meill<8a>kin ne ovat riippuvaisia siit<8a>, miten mielipideilmasto maailmalla kehittyy. V<8a>ltt<8a>m<8a>t<9a>n l<8a>ht<9a>kohta luottamuksen yll<8a>pit<8a>miselle on, ett<8a> ymm<8a>rret<8a><8a>n ja tunnustetaan miten riippuvaisia pankit ovat niiden toiminnan kaikinpuolisesta hyv<8a>ksytt<8a>vyydest<8a> yhteiskunnassa. *** Demokratia ja markkinatalous molemmat toimivat luottamuksen ja vastuullisuuden varassa. Kusti Eskolan aikaan h<8a>nen kaltaisensa miehet edustivat sidosryhmi<8a><8a>n, taustaansa ja aatteitaan mit<8a> moninaisimmissa teht<8a>viss<8a>. Nykyisess<8a> maailmassa vaatimukset ovat toiset ja toimintatavat ovat niiden mukana muuttuneet. P<8a><8a>tt<8a>j<8a>t toimivat entist<8a> kovemman taloudellisen kilpailun ja yh<8a> ankarampien tehokkuusvaatimusten, mutta samalla my<9a>s median armottoman l<8a>pivalaisun kohteena. Mutta ehk<8a> yhteinen piirre nykyiselle toimintaymp<8a>rist<9a>lle ja Eskolan ajalle on, ett<8a> vastuullisissa teht<8a>viss<8a> toimivien henkil<9a>iden on <d0> sen lis<8a>ksi ett<8a> heid<8a>n on pystytt<8a>v<8a> taloudellisesti hyviin tuloksiin <d0> my<9a>s n<8a>kyv<8a>sti edustettava tiettyj<8a> arvoja, joita yhteiskunnassa pidet<8a><8a>n oikeina. Jos ep<8a>ill<8a><8a>n, ett<8a> t<8a>m<8a> vaatimus ei t<8a>yty, ty<9a>n taloudelliset tuloksetkaan tuskin osoittautuvat kest<8a>viksi.

Title: Launch of the second part of the Bank of Finland's history work
text: Speech by President Erkki Liikanen at the unveiling of the second part of the Bank of Finland's historical work 19.3.2012 in Helsinki . Speech . Monday19 March 2012,10:00AM President and CEO Erkki Liikanen Speech at the unveiling of the second part of the Bank of Finland's historical work Money Museum on 19.3.2012 at 10.30 a.m. EET. President Koivisto, ladies and gentlemen, "On a Friday morning, the first day of December in 1939, Finance Minister VainoTanner entered through the main door of the Bank of Finland on Snellman Square to go and meet the bank's president, Risto Ryti. The purpose of Tanner's visit was to persuade Ryti to resign as the bank's president and become prime minister. While Tanner was talking to Ryti, the President of the Republic, MrKallio, also arrived and had come to negotiate on the same issue. On the previous day, Finland had gone to war with the Soviet Union. Soviet troops had crossed the border early thursday morning and Helsinki had been bombed." Thus begins the second part of the history of the Bank of Finland, which will be announced today; Parliament Bank. The description of the known stage of Finnish history continues: "Risto Rytipititi was primarily a banker and was initially unwilling to become prime minister, but when PresidentKallio continued his persuasion as late as Friday afternoon, Rytilopulta agreed. The government he quickly assembled was appointed the same day, and the next day2.12. it met in its first session. Due to the risk of bombing, the session was held in the gold vault of the Bank of Finland." Hilkka Nieminen had started her work at the bank on Hilka's day 27.11, three days before the Winter War. Igniting. The bank of Finland's operations were affected at all levels by the war years. The bank's almost complete independence came to an end and the activities of the Bank of Finland and the Ministry of Finance were practically merged. Restraint in lending to the state had to be abandoned. Currency regulation brought a lot of new tasks to the bank. The bank's branch network was also changed for the duration of the war. The bank's front-line branches were established to handle, among other things, the payment of soldiers' daily allowances from 1942 to 1944. Hilkka Nieminen also served in the Bank of Finland's regional branches in Olonets, Karhumaki and aaninen. Hilkka Nieminen worked at the bank for 37 years and during six governors. Welcome Hilkka Nieminen to this event! In order to replace Ryti in the duties of the Governor of the Bank of Finland, the Board of Governors appointed J. W. Rangell, a close colleague of Ryti's board of directors. Risto Ryti returned as President after resigning as Governor of the Bank of Finland in the autumn of 1944. In the spring of 1945, Prime Minister Paasikivi, in talks with President Mannerheim, had considered the resignation of Ryti and Rangell to be a necessary signal to the Allies. In May, the banking council wrote a letter to Ryti asking if he would ask for his resignation and when a resignation was expected. This is how the process that led to Ryti's resignation at the end of June began. The same thing happened with Rangell. The war guilt trial was held opposite the bank at the House of the Estates. The bankers, led by Risto Ryti, watched the accused move up the stairs of the House of the Estates from the window. There was a desire for new faces in the leadership of the country. The same requirement applied to the Bank of Finland. Ryti was replaced as Director General by Sakari Tuomioja, then Minister of Finance. Rangell was replaced on the board by Urho Kekkonen. Politics and the Bank of Finland were close to each other. Of the members of the Executive Board, Urho Kekkonen was prime minister five times. Sakari Tuomioja was also prime minister once. In addition to his position as director-general, Tuomioja held at best two ministerial duties. When Tuomioja started, safeguarding social peace was an important goal. A wide range of social and wage agreements were the main issues of economic policy. In the memory of the nation lived for a long time the cutting of banknotes in 1946. An important turning point in monetary policy was the abandonment of state banknote financing after the Korean economic cycle in 1953. As Director-General, Tuomioja played an important role in Finland's accession to the International Monetary Fund at the beginning of 1948. Sweden joined three years later. West Germany joined only in 1952. Finland became a member before relations between the Monetary Fund and the Soviet Union broke down. The 2nd part of the history of the Bank of Finland, the Bank of Parliament, which is published today, deals with the history of the Bank of Finland from the Winter War to joining the European Economic and Monetary Union. The world, Europe and Finland went through a huge change during this period. A special feature of the current history is that it describes the changes in Finland and the Bank of Finland also in broader international and European contexts. The authors of the history have had access to the archives of the Bank of Finland. This has meant that the difficult and painful phases of Finland and the Bank of Finland are reviewed in a way that contains a lot of new perspectives and new information. Fragments have been featured before, but it has often been difficult to catch the plot. History plays an important role in understanding financial crises. Crises have a lot of common features, but also time-related characteristics. Why has so little been learned from them? It has been said that there are two main reasons for this: Ignorance and arrogance. (ignorance and arrogance). Past crises have not been carefully analysed or learned from. And/or it is believed that the market and risk management have changed so that the risks do not materialize. Let's be so much more learned or smarter that we can avoid the risks this time. The second part of the history of the Bank of Finland, which appears today, alleviates the problem of ignorance. Why was banking legislation in Finland late and even then weak? How could some banks take such huge risks that they brought the entire institution to the brink of destruction or even destruction? It is then up to each generation of decision-makers to assess for themselves how great the risk of arrogance is. Finland has been helped by the experience of a long recession, because so many have carried it as their own capital. But when the experience recedes, is it possible that the same in another form can happen again? The Bank of Finland's 200-year history project ends with a work to be published today. The previous history was made 50 years ago. That classic of Finnish economic history was written by Hugo Pipping. The Bank of Finland has had the great advantage of having two leading authors of the Bank of Finland's 200th anniversary history Researchers. Docent AnttiKuustera is a respected professional in Finnish financial and banking history. Among many other merits, before this project, he had already written the history of cooperative banking and savings banks. Dr. Juha Tarkka, on the other hand, is one of the best experts in Finland on the history of central banks and modern monetary policy and its research. The joint effort of Antti Kuustera and Juha Tarkan has produced, at least for those of us at the Central Bank, a weighty and impressive work of history and, at the same time, a textbook. It comes so close that the reading experience is breathtaking in places. On behalf of the Bank of Finland, I would like to thank Antti Kuustera and Juha Tarkka for their excellent work. On behalf of many of the bank's employees, I would like to thank you for the numerous discussions that have made it easier to understand the current crisis through the experience of history. I would also like to thank the History Committee, which has been chaired first by Bank Director Sinikka Salo and then by Bank Director Seppo Honkapohja. Welcome!
