Title: Interaction between monetary policy and the housing market
text: President Erkki Liikanen: On the interaction between monetary policy and the housing market. Keynote speech at the national housing and community day dinner 10.5.2012 . Speech . Thursday10 May 2012, 11:00 AM Director General Erkki Liikanen Keynote speech at the National Housing and Community Day dinner University of Helsinki, 10.5.2012 ON THE INTERACTION BETWEEN MONETARY POLICY AND THE HOUSING MARKET Speech text and main points of speech (/globalassets/en/media-and.. publications/speeches/documents/el_puhe_120510_asunto_ja_yhdyskuntap_yliopisto.pdf)(PDF) The primary objective of the Eurosystem's monetary policy is price stability. The role of the Governing Council is to set the key interest rate at the level that best supports price stability in the medium term. It is particularly important to keep inflation expectations anchored in line with the objective of price stability. The financial crisis has highlighted the role of central banks in supporting the stability of the financial system. Since the financial crisis, concerns about the stability of financial markets have also been highlighted. The role of central banks in supporting the stability of the financial system will be emphasised in the wake of this crisis. Secondarily, monetary policy can also pursue the stability of the development of the real economy (stable economic growth and high employment) when done without jeopardising price stability. On the other hand, there is a broad consensus that price stability and well-anchored inflation expectations are a prerequisite for stable economic and employment development. The housing market can be a source of economic crisis. The housing market and prices are of great importance from the point of view of the objectives of the Central Bank. The housing market and the development of housing prices are intensifying the economic cycle. The housing market can even be a source of economic crisis. A sharp rise in house prices can lead to over-indebtedness and intensify the upward spiral of the economy to the point of overheating, with the risk of a housing price bubble and the major problems caused by its bursting. A sharp and long-term fall in house prices, on the other hand, intensifies the downward spiral, poses a risk of deflation, weakens the balance sheets of both households and banks, jeopardises the stability of financial markets and could lead to a financial crisis. Economic policy measures conducive to stable developments in asset prices support stable economic development. According to the results of the study, downturns, which are preceded by a strong and wide-ranging credit expansion, are deeper and longer lasting than recessions that are not preceded by a credit boom. According to the International Monetary Fund, the recession that followed the global financial crisis was particularly deep in those countries where household indebtedness increased sharply before the crisis. Let me first turn to the transmission of monetary policy through the various channels to the housing market and prices. I will then describe the overall economic importance of the housing market by looking at the role of house prices in the overheating of the economy, the strong downturn and the recovery from it. The central bank's interest rate hike makes borrowing more expensive, which postpones business investment and household spending. The central bank's interest rate decision affects the short-term (real) interest rate. Raising interest rates makes borrowing more expensive. It postpones business investment and household spending decisions. The change in interest rates also affects the economy through exchange rates and asset prices. Raising interest rates will slow economic growth in the short term and dampen inflation. Changes in interest rates affect inflation approximately .. With a delay of 2 years. A credible commitment by the central bank to the objective of price stability and the anchoring of inflation expectations, as stated above, are key to inflation developments. The transmission mechanism of monetary policy is usually described by looking at the various channels through which changes in interest rates affect the economy. Several of these channels have been identified in the literature. The following is a brief overview of the interest rate, asset price and credit/balance sheet channel from the perspective of the development of housing prices and markets (see, e.g., Mishkin (2007)). In the first place is the interest rate channel. The Central Bank issues money by lending it to banks. Banks continue to lend it to businesses and households. In this way, the interest rate demanded by the central bank on banks affects the general short-term interest rate level.1 As a result of the central bank's interest rate hike, borrowing becomes more expensive, the demand for household housing is dampened, and residential construction slows down, resulting in a reduction in aggregate demand. On the other hand, housing prices are wealth prices. Changes in asset prices reflect future expectations. Monetary policy also influences the economy through the asset price channel. As wealth prices rise, households can increase their consumption, as if consuming part of their increased wealth. A rate hike indirectly curbs asset prices. As the central bank's interest rate hike has a dampening effect on economic growth and inflation, it also indirectly has a dampening effect on asset prices. If the rise in housing prices is expected to slow down, the demand for housing and, consequently, supply, i.e. construction, will slow down. The slowdown in residential investment, on the other hand, supports housing prices. The more flexibly housing construction adapts, the more subdued the price volatility of dwellings will be. Households' balance sheets and lending have an impact on the transmission of monetary policy. Thirdly, recent economic literature highlights the credit constraints of households and businesses, i.e. the fact that it is not possible for housekeepers to obtain credit on unlimitedly favourable terms. Access to credit and its conditions, as well as costs, are influenced by the borrower's income prospects and financial situation, which is often described on the borrower's balance sheet. Due to credit constraints, the effects of monetary policy are also transmitted to the economy through households' balance sheets and access to credit. Credit constraints provide a number of elements for the analysis of the transmission of monetary policy. Here we will go through a few of them. Uncertainty about the borrower's solvency causes financial market rigidity. One is financial market rigidity. It means that lenders charge borrowers a risk premium as compensation for the fact that the loan may not be repaid. Financial market rigidities are caused by incomplete information between the lender and the borrower: The lender does not have definite information about the borrower's solvency. The better the borrower's ability to pay the loan is estimated, the lower the risk premium the borrower will have to pay. For example, households pay a margin on their mortgages, which is affected by, among other things, the (estimated) borrowing capacity of the household in question. The risk premiums caused by uncertainty vary from one economic cycle to the next. Risk premiums live according to the economic cycle. In a downturn, the balance sheets of households and firms deteriorate, which means that they have to pay a higher risk premium on their loans. Risk premiums are increasing because lenders want compensation for the fact that borrowers' ability to repay their loans has decreased, and the risk of default on the loan has increased. In an upturn, on the other hand, balance sheets strengthen and risk premiums decrease as borrowers' ability to repay their loans has improved. This mechanism is called a financial accelerator (accelerator)2 . A household's debts and assets affect the amount and price of credit. The collateral value of a dwelling is an important factor in a household's access to finance. When the price of a home, i.e. its collateral value, rises, the balance sheet constraint is loosened, and the household has the opportunity to borrow more money (or get a loan with a smaller margin). Financial market rigidities affect the amount of credit and the price to be paid for it. A household's balance sheet limits the amount of credit and affects the price paid for it. Due to credit constraints, the nominal interest rate on mortgages has an impact on household interest payments, disposable income and, consequently, demand. In Finland and other countries where a large proportion of mortgages are tied to variable market rates, changes in the central bank's key interest rate are quickly and strongly transmitted through changes in market interest rates to households' disposable income. As the benchmark mortgage rate rises, households' disposable income, and hence demand, decreases if the household does not have the opportunity to increase borrowing in this situation. On the other hand, in Finland, for example, some of the mortgages are so-called mortgages. straight-line loans, in which case an interest rate increase extends the remaining maturity of the loan without affecting the monthly disposable income. In this case, the household, as it were, takes on additional credit so as not to have to reduce demand. Interest rate fixing is one of the factors that can intensify or dampen cyclical fluctuations. Housing prices play an important role in the overheating of the economy, the subsequent downturn and the recovery phase In an upturn, central banks contain inflation by raising the policy rate, while the simultaneous rise in asset prices intensifies the upward spiral of the economy and increases household indebtedness, which poses a risk to macroeconomics as a whole. A fall in house prices is often preceded by a strong boom, even an overheating of the economy, when asset prices rise and household indebtedness, as measured by the debt-to-income ratio or gross domestic product, increases. In an upturn, the monetary policy rate is raised to contain inflation developments and to keep inflation expectations anchored. While raising interest rates curbs inflation and dampens economic growth, other financial factors are at the same time counterproductive and intensifying the upturn. For example, rising house prices and other asset prices in a boom increases households' net worth3 , increases borrowing opportunities, lowers the price of credit and, consequently, increases aggregate demand, which in turn amplifies the rise in asset prices. In other words, financial factors amplify the upward spiral and sustain the growth of household indebtedness. In an upturn, rising house prices sustain households' wealth. Debt in relation to wealth does not increase, but may rather decrease if the rise in housing prices sharply increases the value of housing assets. For the household, an improvement in the net worth position increases the financial room for manoeuvre and may even overheat the economy. At the same time, households' debt burden relative to GDP and household disposable income in an upturn often increases. As a result, the household sector is exposed to risk as house prices fall, unemployment rises and incomes fall. The high level of household indebtedness poses a risk to the macroeconomic situation as a whole. The risk of a housing bubble increases as the economy overheats. In the worst case scenario, the economy will overheat so that a housing price bubble will be created. House price bubbles are often associated with financial market deregulation or financial innovation, which unexpectedly improves access to finance and/or reduces the price to be paid for it, while at the same time there is no change in households' balance sheets or expected income. The deregulation housing bubble was created in Finland in the late 1980s. Between 1987 and 1989, house prices rose by an average of 23% per year. In the same years, the stock of mortgage loans grew by an average of 20% per year. A bubble can also arise if housekeepers have over-optimistic expectations for the future, credit terms are loosened or lenders' risk appetite increases. Then the economic upturn may be unsustainable and the economy will be born a housing price bubble that sooner or later bursts. In some countries, financial factors can overheat the economy. Kotitalouksien tuntuva velkaantuneisuus on riski koko makrotaloudelle. Asuntokuplan riski kasvaa talouden ylikuumentuessa. Pahimmassa tapauksessa talous ylikuumenee niin, ett<8a> syntyy asuntohintakupla. Asuntohintakuplat liittyv<8a>t usein rahoitusmarkkinoiden s<8a><8a>nn<9a>stelyn purkamiseen tai rahoitusinnovaatioihin, jolloin rahoituksen saatavuus yll<8a>tt<8a>en paranee ja/tai siit<8a> maksettava hinta laskee, vaikka samaan aikaan kotitalouksien taseissa tai odotettavissa olevissa tuloissa ei tapahdu muutosta. S<8a><8a>nn<9a>stelyn purkamiseen liittyv<8a> asuntokupla syntyi Suomessa 1980-luvun lopulla. Vuosina 1987<d0>1989 asuntohinnat nousivat keskim<8a><8a>rin 23 prosenttia vuodessa. Asuntoluottokanta kasvoi samoina vuosina keskim<8a><8a>rin 20 prosenttia vuodessa. Kupla voi my<9a>s synty<8a>, jos taloudenpit<8a>jill<8a> on ylioptimistiset tulevaisuudenodotukset, luottoehtoja l<9a>ys<8a>t<8a><8a>n tai luotonantajien riskinottohalu lis<8a><8a>ntyy. Silloin talouden noususuhdanne voi olla kest<8a>m<8a>t<9a>n ja taloudessa syntyy asuntohintakupla, joka ennemmin tai my<9a>hemmin puhkeaa. Rahoitustekij<8a>t voivat joissain maissa ylikuumentaa talouden. Lis<8a>ksi voi olla maakohtaisia, esimerkiksi asunto-ja rahoitusmarkkinoihin liittyvi<8a> tekij<9a>it<8a>, jotka lis<8a><8a>v<8a>t asuntomarkkinoiden ylikuumenemisriski<8a>. Esimerkiksi euroalueella rahoitustekij<9a>iden merkitys ja niiden vaikutusten voimakkuus vaihtelee maittain. Rahoitustekij<8a>t voivat joissakin maissa ylikuumentaa talouden, vaikka ohjauskorkoa samanaikaisesti nostetaankin. Ohjauskoron noston vaikutukset voivat kumoutua, jos samanaikaisesti kotitalouksien rahoituksen saatavuus paranee ja asuntolainamarginaalit pienenev<8a>t. Ohjauskorkojen muutosten v<8a>littyminen kotitalouksien maksamiin korkoihin vaihtelee euroalueen maissa huomattavasti. Maissa, joissa vaihtuvakorkoisten lainojen osuus on suuri, ohjauskoron muutokset v<8a>littyv<8a>t kotitalouksien lainanhoitokuluihin nopeasti ja voimakkaasti, mik<8a> voi pienent<8a><8a> talouden ylikuumenemisriski<8a>. Voimakas h<8a>iri<9a> taloudessa voi laukaista kotitalouksien velkaantuneisuuden koko talouden ongelmaksi ja aiheuttaa finanssikriisin. Kotitalouksien noususuhdanteessa voimakkaasti kasvanut velkaantuneisuus paljastuu koko talouden ongelmaksi, jos talouteen kohdistuu ep<8a>suotuisa sokki, joka k<8a><8a>nt<8a><8a> asuntohinnat laskuun. Esimerkiksi pieness<8a> avotaloudessa vientikysynn<8a>n romahtaminen voi aiheuttaa taantuman, johon liittyy asunto-ja muiden varallisuushintojen lasku. Vaikka asuntohintojen lasku ei v<8a>ltt<8a>m<8a>tt<8a> ole voimakkaan laskusuhdanteen ensisijainen syy, laskevilla asuntohinnoilla on silti laskusuhdannetta voimistava vaikutus. Asuntomarkkinat voivatmy<9a>s olla laskusuhdanteentaifinanssikriisin keskeinenl<8a>hde4. N<8a>inon silloin,kun asuntohintakupla puhkeaa ja kotitaloudet ovat sit<8a> ennen noususuhdanteessa velkaantuneet voimakkaasti. Ep<8a>suotuisan sokin vaikutukset ovat osoittautuneet voimakkaiksi ja pitk<8a>kestoisiksi, jos sokki kohdistuu talouden velkaantuneeseen sektoriin. IMF:n (2012) mukaan Yhdysvalloista alkanut globaali finanssikriisi on johtanut voimakkaaseen laskusuhdanteeseen nimenomaan niiss<8a> maissa, joissa kotitaloudet ovat tuntuvasti velkaantuneet. Useassa maassa globaalia finanssikriisi<8a> edelsi luottoekspansioon perustuva talouden ylikuumeneminen. Kun samalla tulevaisuuden tulo-odotukset olivat korkeat ja varallisuushinnat nousivat, taseet pysyiv<8a>t kunnossa, vaikka velkaa otettiin koko ajan lis<8a><8a>. Velkaantumisen kasvu oli perustunut ylioptimistisiin k<8a>sityksiin odotettavissa olevista tuloista. Globaali finanssikriisi muutti odotuksia nopeasti. Kun realismi voitti ja velkaantumisen kasvun rajat alkoivat tulla vastaan, asuntohinnat k<8a><8a>ntyiv<8a>t laskuun ja kotitalouksien taseet alkoivat heiket<8a>. Useassa maassa asuntohintojen k<8a><8a>ntyminen laskuun tuli yll<8a>tyksen<8a> eik<8a> siihen ollut varauduttu. USA:ssa asuntojen reaalihinnat k<8a><8a>ntyiv<8a>t laskuun ensimm<8a>ist<8a> kertaa sitten 1930-luvun suuren laman. Asuntohintojen lasku supistaa kotitalouksien varallisuutta, hidastaa talouskasvua s<8a><8a>st<8a>misen lis<8a><8a>ntyess<8a> ja lis<8a><8a> finanssikriisin riski<8a>. Asuntohintojen aleneminen pienent<8a><8a> kotitalouksien taseessa olevan varallisuuden arvoa. Jos asuntohintojen lasku on voimakasta ja pitk<8a>aikaista, asuntovarallisuuden arvo saattaa laskea alemmaksi kuin asuntovelan nimellinen m<8a><8a>r<8a>. Asuntovelan lyhent<8a>minen on tyypillisesti hidasta. Kun asuntohinnat laskevat, monet kotitaloudet pyrkiv<8a>t lis<8a><8a>m<8a><8a>n s<8a><8a>st<8a>mist<8a><8a>n ja maksamaan asuntovelkaa nopeammin pois, jotta nettovarallisuus ei p<8a><8a>sisi laskemaan voimakkaasti eik<8a> ainakaan muuttuisi negatiiviseksi. N<8a>in kotitalouksien velkaantuminen purkautuu. Koko talouden tasolla kotitaloussektorin velkaantumisen purkaminen voi olla v<8a>ltt<8a>m<8a>t<9a>nt<8a>, mutta sill<8a> on talouskasvua hidastava vaikutus, kun kotitalouksien kysynt<8a> s<8a><8a>st<8a>misen kasvaessa luonnollisesti v<8a>henee. Asuntohintojen lasku heikent<8a><8a> my<9a>s pankkien taseita ja lis<8a><8a> finanssikriisin riski<8a>. Asuntohintojen laskun seurauksena kiinteist<9a>ihin liittyvien saamisten arvo on alentunut (erityisesti pankkien haltuun ottamat kiinteist<9a>t ja roskalainat) ja n<8a>iden arvonalennusten kirjaaminen rasittaa pankkien taseita, lis<8a><8a> pankkisektorin sopeutustoimien tarvetta ja heikent<8a><8a> luotonantomahdollisuuksia. Asuntosektorin ongelmat uhkaavat pahimmillaan koko rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a>n vakautta. Laskusuhdanteessa keskuspankki laskee ohjauskorkoaan hintavakauden yll<8a>pit<8a>miseksi. Ep<8a>suotuisasta sokista aiheutuneessa laskusuhdanteessa inflaatio ja inflaatio-odotukset vaimenevat. T<8a>ss<8a> tilanteessa keskuspankki laskee ohjauskorkoaan hintavakauden yll<8a>pit<8a>miseksi. Koronlasku v<8a>littyy asuntomarkkinoille ja asuntovelallisille asti edellisess<8a> luvussa kuvatulla tavalla. Koronlasku tukee asuntomarkkinoita, asuntohintoja sek<8a> kotitalouksien kysynt<8a><8a>. Koronlasku tukee asuntomarkkinoita, asuntohintoja ja kotitalouksien kysynt<8a><8a>. Voimakkaissa laskusuhdanteissa ja talouskriisiss<8a> rahoitusolot voivat kiristy<8a> keskuspankin koronlaskusta huolimatta poikkeuksellisen paljon. Rahoitusolojen kiristyminen on seurausta kotitalouksien ja usein my<9a>s pankkisektorin taseisiin kohdistuvista heikkenemispaineista, joiden takia asuntolainoista maksettavat korkomarginaalit kasvavat ja rahoituksen saatavuus heikkenee. Syntyy ep<8a>suotuisaa talouskehityst<8a> voimistava kierre. Finanssikriisiss<8a> osa koronlaskun vaikutuksista ei v<8a>lity kotitalouksille. Supistuvan talouden ja kiristyv<8a>n rahoituksen kierre voi johtaa talouden rajuun hidastumiseen. Rahoitusolot kiristyv<8a>t sit<8a> enemm<8a>n mit<8a> korkeampi velkaantuneisuus on. Osa keskuspankin koronlaskun my<9a>nteisist<8a> vaikutuksista kumoutuu rahoitusolojen kiristymisen takia. Varsinkin kriisitilanteessa rahapolitiikan v<8a>littyminen kotitalouksien lainoistaan maksamiin korkoihin voi h<8a>iriinty<8a>. T<8a>ss<8a> tilanteessa kotitalouksien lainoistaan maksamat marginaalit voivat kasvaa, rahoituksen ehdot tiukentua ja rahoituksen saatavuus heiket<8a> voimakkaasti. Suomessa EKP:n koronlaskut ovat kuitenkin v<8a>littyneet voimakkaasti suurimmalle osalle asuntovelallisista, koska Suomessa asuntolainojen korot on tyypillisesti sidottu lyhyeen markkinakorkoon. Markkinakorkojen aleneminen pienent<8a><8a> kotitalouden velanhoitokuluja tai tasaer<8a>lainan tapauksessa lyhent<8a><8a> lainan maksuaikaa (velkaantumisen purkaminen). N<8a>ille kotitalouksille koronlaskut antavat enemm<8a>n taloudellista liikkumavaraa, mik<8a> tukee asuntohintoja, kotitalouksien kysynt<8a><8a> ja vaimentaa tuotannon laskua. Kriisiss<8a> keskuspankkien on korkopolitiikan ohella turvauduttava ep<8a>tavanomaisiin toimenpiteisiin. Viimeaikaisessa kriisiss<8a> rahapoliittiset korot on useassa maassa laskettu hyvin alhaalle. Keskuspankkien mahdollisuudet vaimentaa laskusuhdannetta tavanomaisen rahapolitiikan avulla ovat t<8a>llaisessa tilanteessa luonnollisesti rajoitetut. T<8a>rke<8a><8a> on ollut varmistaa poikkeuksellisen alhaisten ohjauskorkojen v<8a>littyminen kotitalouksille ja yrityksille tilanteessa, jossa rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a>n ep<8a>varmuus vaikeuttaa rahapolitiikan kyky<8a> ohjata markkinakorkoja. Keskuspankit ovat tukeutuneet ns. ep<8a>tavanomaisiin toimiin rahapolitiikan v<8a>littymisen varmistamiseksi ja luotonannon tukemiseksi. Velkaantuneisuuden kasvun takia kiristyneet rahoitusolot hidastavat talouden toipumista. Talouden k<8a><8a>ntyminen nousuun merkitsee, ett<8a> varallisuushinnat nousevat, yritysten ja kotitalouksien taseet kohenevat ja velkaantuneisuus v<8a>henee. T<8a>ll<9a>in my<9a>s lainoista maksettavat riskilis<8a>t pienenev<8a>t ja rahoituksen saatavuus paranee. Noususuhdanteessa syntyy kasvavan talouden ja kevenevien rahoitusolojen my<9a>nteinen kierre. Jos voimakkaan laskusuhdanteen taustalla on asuntohintakuplan puhkeaminen, my<9a>nteiseen kierteeseen p<8a><8a>semist<8a> edelt<8a><8a> asuntohintojen usein pitk<8a>aikainen lasku. Viime vuosina asuntohinnat ovat laskeneet usean vuoden ajan esimerkiksi Yhdysvalloissa ja euroalueen maista Espanjassa ja Irlannissa. Suomessa 1990-luvulla asuntohinnat laskivat runsaat puoli vuosikymment<8a>. Asuntohinnat saavuttivat huippunsa vuoden 1989 puoliv<8a>liss<8a> (1989 Q2), jonka j<8a>lkeen ne laskivat 40 prosenttia noin nelj<8a>ss<8a> vuodessa. Vaikka asuntohinnat olivat alimmillaan vuoden 1993 alussa (1993 Q1), varsinainen nousu alkoi vasta vuonna 1996. Asuntohintakuplan puhkeamisesta toipuminen edellytt<8a><8a> asuntohintojen korjaantumista ja kotitalouksien ylivelkaantumisen purkautumista. Asuntohintakuplan puhkeamisen j<8a>lkeen talouden toipuminen edellytt<8a><8a> asuntohintojen korjaantumista ja usein my<9a>s kotitalouksien ylivelkaantumisen purkamista. Kotitalouksien velkaantumisen purkaminen voi johtua my<9a>s luottoehtojen kiristymisest<8a>, tulo-odotusten vaimenemisesta ja taloudellisen ep<8a>varmuuden lis<8a><8a>ntymisest<8a>. Suomessa asuntohinnat laskivat vain hetkellisesti finanssikriisin k<8a>rjistytty<8a>. Toisaalta esimerkiksi Suomessa asuntohinnat laskivat vain hetkellisesti globaalin finanssikriisin k<8a>rjistytty<8a> vuoden 2008 lopulla ja alkoivat hyvin pian taas nousta. Suotuisaan kehitykseen voi olla useita syit<8a>, kuten elvytt<8a>v<8a>n rahapolitiikan nopea ja voimakas v<8a>littyminen kotitalouksille, kotitalouksien kriisi<8a> edelt<8a>neen velkaantumisen kohtuullisuus sek<8a> Suomen pankkisektorin hyv<8a> kriisinsietokunto. Asuntohintojen nopea toipuminen viittaisi my<9a>s siihen, ett<8a> Suomessa ei ennen globaalia finanssikriisi<8a> ollut syntynyt asuntohintakuplaa. Kun talouden toipuminen alkaa, voimakkaassa laskusuhdanteessa kasvanut velkaantuneisuus alkaa hiljalleen laskea. Kotitalouksien, kuten my<9a>s talouden muiden sektoreiden, velkaantuneisuus on keskeinen syy, miksi toipuminen on hidasta. Velkaantuneisuuden purkaminen vie aikaa. <d3>Velka on veli otettaessa, veljenpoika maksettaessa.<d3> Velkaantuneisuuden kasvun takia kiristyneet rahoitusolot hidastavat ja rajoittavat talouden toipumista. Rahoitusolojen kireys rajoittaa kotitalouksien taloudellista liikkumavaraa ja luotonottoa sek<8a> vaimentaa kotitalouksien kysynt<8a><8a>, mik<8a> taas hidastaa talouden toipumista. Ilman kriisin lis<8a><8a>m<8a><8a> velkataakkaa kotitaloudet voisivat lis<8a>t<8a> kysynt<8a><8a>ns<8a> talouden toipumisvaiheessa enemm<8a>n ja vahvistaa n<8a>in talouden elpymist<8a>. Asuntohintojen nousu tukee talouden toipumista kasvattamalla kotitalouksien nettovarallisuutta, mik<8a> parantaa rahoitusolojen kevenemisen edellytyksi<8a>. Asuntohintojen nousun aikaansaama kotitalouksien taseiden vahvistuminen ja kevenev<8a>t rahoitusolot voimistavat kotitalouksien kysynt<8a><8a> ja suhdannenousua. Yhteenvetona haluan korostaa, ett<8a> asuntomarkkinat ovat t<8a>rkeit<8a> keskuspankin kannalta, sill<8a> asuntohintojen nousu voimistaa talouden yl<8a>suuntaista kierrett<8a>, kun taas niiden lasku voimistaa alasuuntaista kierrett<8a>. Asuntomarkkinat voivat jopa olla talouskriisin l<8a>hde, jos talous ylikuumenee ja syntyy asuntohintakupla. Asuntohintakuplan puhkeaminen laskee tuotantoa voimakkaasti ja vaarantaa rahoitusj<8a>rjestelm<8a>n vakauden. Noususuhdanteessa syntyy kasvavan talouden, kevenevien rahoitusolojen ja nousevien varallisuushintojen kierre. Vaikka kotitaloussektorin velkataakka kasvaa, niin kasvaa my<9a>s asuntovarallisuuden arvo. Pitk<8a><8a>n kest<8a>v<8a>ss<8a> noususuhdanteessa unohtuu usein, ett<8a> asuntohinnat voivat my<9a>s laskea. Asuntohinnat laskevat tyypillisesti tilanteessa, jossa my<9a>s tuotanto laskee voimakkaasti, ty<9a>tt<9a>myys lis<8a><8a>ntyy ja kotitalouksien tulo.odotukset heikkenev<8a>t voimakkaasti. Kotitaloussektorin velkaantuneisuus on kasvanut Suomessa 2000-luvulla. Vuonna 2005 kotitalouksien velka oli 95 prosenttia saman vuoden k<8a>ytett<8a>viss<8a> olevista tuloista. Vuonna 2011 velka oli noussut jo 114 prosenttiin (sis<8a>lt<8a>en kotitalouksien osuuden asunto-osakeyhti<9a>iden lainoista). Nousua oli siis l<8a>hes 20 prosenttiyksikk<9a><8a> 6 vuodessa. Vaikka Eurooppalaisessa vertailussa suomalaisten kotitalouksien keskim<8a><8a>r<8a>inen velkaantuneisuus ei ole poikkeuksellisen korkea, voimakkaasti velkaantuneiden kotitalouksien osuus on kasvanut. Vuoden 2010 lopussa noin 4,5 prosentilla velkaantuneista kotitalouksista velkaa oli yli 500 % k<8a>ytett<8a>viss<8a> olevasta rahatulosta. Suomessa on vaarana, ett<8a> talouskasvu nojaa liikaa velkaantumiseen. Kotitaloussektorin kasvanut velkaantuneisuus on huolestuttavaa talouden vakaan kehityksen kannalta. Title: Speech at The Days of Old Literature
text: Director General Erkki Liikanen: Speech at the Old Literature Days, Sastamala 29.6.2012 . Speech . Friday 29June 2012,11:00AM Director General Erkki Liikanen Old Literature Days Sastamala 29.6.2012 MY DISCOVERIES FROM OLD LITERATURE For a literary lover, it will not be necessary for a long time to justify the charm of old books. But what is the charm actually based on? Is it a matter of time travel, a peek into a world that no longer exists? Or will they give us a new perspective on today's problems that plague our minds? Or do we find that the problems are basically the same, even though the era and context have changed? Surely it is all this. One of the joys of reading an old book is the joy of discovery and surprise. Perceptions of what the supposedly familiar writer has in mind are shattered. Such a discovery is especially liberating when it comes to the classics of political or economic philosophy, about which a schematic and one-sided picture has formed in public discourse. In the early days of the Industrial Revolution, a well-known social philosopher wrote the following words: "As the division of labour develops, the functions of the majority of workers, i.e. the majority of the people, will be limited to a few simple actions, often one or two. But the understanding of the majority of people necessarily takes shape in accordance with their usual actions. On a man whose whole life is spent performing a few simple tasks, whose effects may be repeated in the same way, or almost similar, there is no opportunity to use their understanding or practice ingenuity in finding ways to eliminate difficulties, which may never happen. Therefore, he naturally loses habituation to such an effort and usually changes so stupid and ignorant as it is possible for a human being to become. The numbness of his mind makes him, not only unable to enjoy or participate in rational conversation, but also unable to experience noble and tender feelings, and thus to make the right decisions even with respect to the ordinary responsibilities of private life. He is completely incapable of assessing the great interests of his fatherland, and unless he is specifically modified, he is also incapable of defending his country in war. The monotony of his life naturally discourages the courage of his mind and causes him to abhor the irregular, uncertain, and adventurous life of a soldier. It also sags his body and makes him unable to use his strength and perseverance for anything other than what he has grown up with. His special professionalism thus seems to have been acquired at the expense of intellectual, social and military virtues. But in every developed civilized country, this is the state into which the working poor, that is, the majority of the people, will inevitably sink, unless the government does anything to prevent it." Who was the author of this? No, it was not Karl Marx. It was Adam Smith in question, and the excerpt is from chapter 1 of the fifth book of the world famous "The Wealth of Nations". Smith, who has come to be seen as an advocate of a free market economy, suddenly shows a social mind and understands the impact of people's work on their mental and social being. The snippet does not change the fact that Smith saw private profiteering as the driving force behind economic life. Well-known is Smith's summary of the principle of operation of a market economy: "We do not expect a butcher, a brewer or a baker to deliver our dinner to us out of benevolence, but for their own benefit." According to Smith, economic competition was the force that, like the "invisible hand," directed private profiteering to serve fellow human beings with purchasing power waiting for dinner. This side of Smith's ideas was the starting point for the development of modern economics and is therefore better known than his moral concern about the consequences of economic development. The fact that the moral and social aspects of Smith's thinking have been overshadowed by the defence of free trade and competition is an example of how the classics of political philosophy often do. Their ideas are condensed into "isms" and the richness and diversity of the original ideas is then reduced to slogans and thought diagrams. Such ossifications are shackling, and therefore their unraveling, opening classical works, becomes a refreshing and liberating experience for the reader. The ideas of Smith and other enlightenment philosophers, on which our conceptions of the principles of society and the economy are based, often without us even being aware of it, seem to be particularly topical right now. But if we want to understand our own way of thinking, we have to go back to its roots. * We Finns have our own great enlightenment philosophers, Anders Chydenius and J.V. Snellman. They have been hoisted on top of the nation's closet a long time ago and their ideas have been put into their own ideological compartments. But when you really read the writings of these great men, they amaze with their versatility and freshness. Of course, both were children of their time, but they also speak to modern humans. When you discard ossified preconceptions and look at what they actually wrote, you will notice that their thoughts were much more nuanced than one would expect. Chydenius is known as an economic liberal who fought for the right of the cities of Ostrobothnia to conduct foreign trade on their own account. Let's remember that in his main work "National Victory" he demanded complete freedom to conduct a business and opposed restrictions on foreign trade. He has been seen as a pioneer of Adam Smith's economic thinking, and not without reason. When reading Chydenius's texts more broadly, the social pathos of this spirit man and the resulting demand for social justice suddenly come to the fore. This is even more prominent in Chydenius than in Smith's writings. In one of his first writings, in his response to a writing competition from the Swedish Academy of Sciences on the reasons for emigration, Chydenius described the position of workers in 1763 Sweden like this: "To slave in the work of others as long as they can, to be evicted into poverty in their old days, and to die in misery, that is the laurels that should attract the working masses to love their motherland." And in the "National Victory", two years later, Chydenius continued in this way: "The factory worker is really as well dressed of his own preparations as anyone else; but the workers in the spinning-room often shiver half-naked, and others walk through the streets begging in raggedness, saying that they are foreigners who used to wish they were at home again, than that in Sweden they would stand before strangers' doors and at last die of misery." Today, some consider the programmes of the free market economy and equality to be opposite to each other. From the point of view of Chydenius, there was no confrontation. Chydenius was a representative of the optimism of the 1700s, who believed that economic freedom in itself led not only to prosperity, but also to equality. The background to this was that he saw social inequality as the result precisely of the privileges of the estates and the fact that the power of the state was used to promote the strongest interests in society and to oppress the disadvantaged. As a result, for Chydenius, economic liberalism and the development of social conditions were inseparable parts of the same program. His economic policy agenda was directed against restrictions of competition and monopolies and rationing measures granted by the state. At the same time, he called for the equality of people before the law and the abolition of legions of estates. As he grew older, he engaged in widespread controversy about improving the position of agricultural workers, where the main demand was to extend freedom of contract to relations between masters and wage earners. In today's language, he pushed for employment contracts. Snellman, on the other hand, is best known for his language-based conception of nationality and education programme. At the same time, it is remembered that he was also a practical economic politician. As a senator, Snellman carried out a monetary reform, as a result of which Finland received its own monetary system in the 1860s. Snellman is considered a conservative, and as he grew older, Snellman clearly became more and more conservative. In "Political Science", a work that Snellman published in 1842 shortly before starting his career as a journalist in Kuopio, Snellman deals extensively with many political, cultural and economic as well as ethical issues. Especially the more radical passages in the book surprise the reader and crush the conservative image that has emerged or constructed of Snellman over the decades. Snellman advocated the freedom to conduct a business, partly for the sake of economic efficiency, but above all for the sake of individual freedom. One can hear echoes of Chydenius's thoughts when Snellman writes about the freedom to conduct a business, that under it "The road to financial independence is then not anyone's prerogative, it is open to all." However, he was not as optimistic about the consequences of freedom as Chydenius. Snellman speculated that the implementation of the freedom to conduct a business would lead to the concentration of property. According to the 37th chapter of "Political Science": "The holders of property can vary, and a man who has left the crowd can, with energy and deliberation, rise to the highest level of prosperity. Nevertheless, wealth accumulates in relatively few hands, and there is little known middle ground between lavish wealth and poverty, or, at best, between wealth and providing man with an evenly dosed stockpile of supplies sufficient for the needs of the day." Snellman cannot accept such an outcome, but continues: "However, economists' own helplessness gives little hope for the future. The unequal distribution of property is a ghost that haunts them, because it moves on its own basis in economics. They cannot deny that the freedom to conduct a business, which has caused the danger, has also increased production and national wealth. Thus they are in the same trouble as the exorcist of spirits, who has incanted the disgusting powers of the mana, but has forgotten how to get rid of their painful company." Perhaps it will be interesting to hear what Snellman's solution to the problem of wealth concentration was: "An unfavorable ratio can only be smoothed out by the owner paying tax to the state and the state taking care of the training of employees and the maintenance of those who are insufficient in strength due to youth and old age. The owner must be forced to make greater sacrifices in this matter, even arousing disquiet about the security of property. It can only be secured by civilising the majority and protecting the old age of the worker from misery. I have referred above to how an employee should be guaranteed earnings that correspond to his or her work. I cannot conceive that coercion by law produces better results than the moral compulsion imposed on the owner by the workers, on the basis of their civilisation and their awareness of their human rights, in combination with his own interests." Snellman's vision of the future of the market economy and his criticism of economists seems almost prophetic given how early it was written, before the revolutions of 1848, long before the birth of the labor movement and social policy. * Both classics of Finnish social philosophy are thus characterized by concern for the realization of social justice, although their ideas about the state's ability to solve the problems of economic inequality were different. Chydenius does not seem to have expected much more from the state than harmful interference for the benefit of the strongest, while for Snellman the state is more of a solution than a problem. Unlike Chydenius, Snellman was not an individualist, for in his opinion man realized himself precisely as a citizen. Snellman's conception of freedom reflects the influence of German idealism and its ethics of duty, and about him "Acts of freedom are not for the individual, but for humanity." (Political Science, Chapter 36) This also meant economic freedom and its use, in a civilized state. Although perceptions of the role and possibilities of state power differ, Chydenius and Snellman's political programme also had much in common. One unifying factor was their interest in political publicity and freedom of speech. Both were radical in their time on this issue and their ideas also had a great practical impact. It was thanks to Chydenius that the world's first freedom of the press law was enacted in Sweden-Finland in 1766. Chydenius was a member of the Diet at the time, and he had written a report on the subject, in which he explained that state affairs should be allowed to be the subject of free public debate. The idea was unprecedentedly radical at the time, but according to Chydenius "it is not (necessary) to prove that reasonable freedom of writing and the press is one of the strongest fundamental pillars on which a free form of government can rest." In the opinion of Chydenius "The freedom of a nation is not that almighty estates are allowed to act arbitrarily, but requires that the enlightenment of the nation binds their hands and prevents them from acting autocratically". This notion of the importance of publicity as a key element of political freedom connects Chydenius' Finnish Enlightenment with another great name, Snellman. However, Snellman takes the importance of freedom of speech and public debate much further. In his philosophy, national publicity was the most important component of political freedom, even more important than formal state bodies. For Snellman, the spiritual life of the nation, which is realized in public discourse, formed such a strong force that, alongside it, before long, all forms of real power would prove to be only apparent and transient. This was also the basis for the political nature of Snellman's education programme and his becoming a journalist shortly after graduating from "Political Science". With regard to freedom of expression, one has to wonder, by the way, how topical Snellman's ideas about the protection of the individual in the media spotlight are still. You would think that this theme is new and raised by the mass media and the commercial press of our time, but so only Snellman already in his "Political Science" (its 29th chapter) analyzes this question as well. Snellman's position on the matter is harsh. He wrote: "In many of the countries with greater freedom of the press, the private lives of public figures are already subject to public scrutiny. There can be no absolute legal basis for the procedure, as little is the case, on the other hand, with the decoupling of private life from the aftermath. Freedom of the press itself is based on custom as well as the right of the individual to escape the public description of his or her private life. A person should not behave, even in his private actions, in such a way that he has to shun publicity. If public opinion demands gentleness in this matter, it is a concession to the individual beyond what he is strictly entitled to demand." This was not written by a british tabloid journalist, but by a man who started Finnish political journalism in saima magazine in Kuopio in 1844. * What is remarkable is the joy of discovery that one experiences when one opens a text written many generations ago and finds in it an idea that speaks of things that are topical right now. A characteristic feature of the classics is that they open with a new reading, always from a new perspective, depending on the situation where the reader is and who the reader is. In the spring, Bj9arn Wahlroos published the book "Markets and Democracy". The book goes through a considerable number of old books. It is no surprise that he deals with Adam Smith and his ideas about the importance of competition and the pursuit of profit more than his concern for social development. Wahlroos also writes about Alexander Hamilton, one of the creators of the U.S. Constitution, and strongly declares himself a supporter of Hamilton's ideas. Hamilton's writings are central to the famous work "Federalist papers." In his influential writings, Hamilton called for a strong federal state. One of his big ideas was to bring together state debts as federal debt to improve U.S. creditworthiness. Hamilton served as the first U.S. Secretary of the Treasury. He and the first Secretary of State, later President Thomas Jefferson and Hamilton were unyielding contenders, even enemies. Thomas Jefferson insisted on a state as small as possible. State interference for him had to be limited to an absolute minimum, everything else would only cause damage. After reading the writings of both, there are many more Jeffersons than Hamilton in Wahlroos. We may have read the same books, me and Wahlroos, but found different passages there, sometimes even a different plot. That's what can happen with old books. * Great thinkers often wrestle with the same questions. We need competition and freedom to conduct a business, because it creates incentives for economic growth and prosperity. But at the same time, we need solidarity and the smoothing out of differences in starting points, because only then can a society be created. Achieving a balance between competition and solidarity has been and is a major challenge. The work must be rewarded, otherwise there will be no incentives for development. But solidarity is needed, without it, communities will not be able to hold together. Marginalisation also entails high costs. In the old books you can find thoughtful positions on many issues that are burningly topical. Nowadays, attempts are being made to establish new words in the Finnish political language, precisely the kind that George Orwell warned against. Let me take one example: immigration-critical. It is not found in old books. But of course immigration was discussed before. What did the Ostrobothnian vicar Anders Chydenius write about immigration and religious freedom? "That all strangers, of whatever age and estates, and of whatever sex and creed they may be, who wish to emigrate to Sweden and the provinces under it, in order to live there, and to support themselves annually, have complete liberty to do so, at least in the greater cities of the kingdom, and the promise of the same royal security and protection as all the other subjects of the Swedish empire, from the day they to royal Majesty those who swear allegiance." "That the Royal Majesty should assure all strangers entering the earth of complete freedom of conscience for themselves, their children, and their descendants, and that they should receive unhindered, quietly, and without indignation to our domestic congregations, to conduct their own worship." "It's not new; wise rulers are well understood by such immigrations to increase the power and value of their kingdom." This is what Chydenius wrote in 1779. It is worth reading old books. They give you perspective. In the spring, a selection of Anders Chydenius' most important texts was published in English under the title "Anticipating The Wealth of Nations: The selected works of Anders Chydenius". This welcome book foreshadows the extensive scientific editing of Chydenius' collected works, which is about to be published. It is good that the ideas of our central social philosopher can now also be studied in English. So, after Snellman's compilations have been published in both Swedish and Finnish, is it time to make an English selection of his central work available as well d0 starting with "Political Science", for example?
