Talet om behovet av "motvikt" till en stark ECB skall dremot tolkas som politisk retorik, av det relativt harmlsa slaget. Det finns i en Maastricht-baserad Emu ingen plats fr en politisk motvikt till en lagstadgat sjlvstndig centralbank; dremot finns det plats fr politikorienterad konkret dialog. Emu-deltagarnas intresse fr en fortsatt konsolidering av de offentliga finanserna kan vl ocks betecknas rimligt, om inte brinnande helhjrtat. Sjlvfallet hade det varit bttre fr stabilitet, tillvxt och sysselsttning om Emu.lnderna hade gtt in fr en kraftfullare konsolidering av den offentliga sektorn i frening med en genuin strukturpolitik, i synnerhet som pgende hgkonjunktur skulle ha gjort det lttare. Intresset fr konkreta diskussioner om strukturpolitik synes dessvrre ha svalnat i takt med att konjunkturprognosen uppskrivits. Men detta gller lika mycket utanfr Emu. Den enda egentliga verraskningen var, inte eurons kursutveckling, utan debatten om eurons kursutveckling. Den debatten vill jag inte bidra till hr. Jag tror frresten, att europeerna s smningom fattar, att euron per 1.1.99 blev vrldens nststrsta valuta, att en sdan valuta mste flyta, att en flytande valuta skall fluktuera, att varje vrldsvalutas kursutveckling alltid till vervldigande del bestms av annat n inhemska frhllanden och frutsttningar, och slutligen att det primra r en valutas inhemska stabilitet och kpkraft. Detta var, som vi vet, kriteriet fr bedmningen av D-markensstyrka, och det kriteriet r nnu mera relevant fr euron, som r en verklig vrldsvaluta. Lt mig i frbigende notera, att eurons fluktuationer gentemot USD inte varit enorma eller onormala, varken a priori eller i jmfrelse med D-markens utveckling gentemot dollarn de senaste rtiondena. 4. Samtidigt som vi sett en remarkabel monetr och finansiell konvergens, faktiskt ver hela EU och inklusive Emu, har Emu inte visat sig vara ett homogent omrde vad realekonomi och realekonomisk konvergens betrffar. Vi ser att Emu-deltagarnas cykliska situationer varierar betydligt. Inget att frvna sig ver. Detta r precis vad som frutsgs i bl.a. svensk och finlndsk Emu-debatt. Mjligheten av sk asymmetriska "chocker" var en central punkt, och det r en variant av denna asymmetriska utveckling vi upplever. Vid nrmare eftertanke borde vi redan frn brjan ha insett, att detta var det enda sannolika utvecklingsmnstret. S olika r deltagarlndernas produktionsstrukturer, handelsstrukturer, institutioner, politiska traditioner, osv. Premissen framver br rimligtvis vara, att Emu-deltagarnas ekonomier normalt inte kommer att vara cykliskt synkroniserade, ens i den sk. krnan (ett begrepp jag inte har sympati fr men som mhnda r en praktisk benmning geografiskt). ven bortsett frn de realekonomiska olikheterna lnderna emellan kommer det alltid att freligga ett samspel mellan inhemsk politik och frtroendefaktorer och drmed ekonomiska framtidsutsikter. Lt oss ta detta som ngot naturligt, oundvikligt och permanent -ja, rent av nskvrt. Det r mjligt, att chocker eller strningar med inhemskt ursprung i finanspolitiken eller arbetsmarknaden avtar med tiden, till fljd av Emus interna dynamik, men detta skulle knappast kompensera den asymmetriska utveckling som bottnar i realekonomiska faktorer. Vi fr allts ven framver utg ifrn, att den gemensamma penningpolitikens rntesttning inte kontinuerligt kommer att knnas skrddarsydd eller "riktig" fr ngon enskild deltagare. (Detta har fr vrigt varit en finlndsk utgngspunkt frn brjan.) 5. Detta har konsekvenser. Fr det frsta: Kombinationen en penningpolitik plus lndervis varierande ekonomiska lgen br rimligtvis vara, att vrig ekonomisk politik dvs. annan n penningpolitik, i huvudsak mste hllas p nationell bas. Fr det andra: I en sdan omgivning skall sk. "koordinering" av ekonomisk politik inom Emu i bsta fall betyda att Emu-gemenskapen gradvis mobiliserar och institutionaliserar ett starkare tryck p varje enskilt land att konsolidera sig finansiellt och driva en stark strukturpolitik, m.a.o. driva en politik som bidrar till euroomrdets stabilitet och expansion. -Lyckligtvis finns det i en Maastricht-baserad monetr union inte nmnvrt utrymme fr det som kallas fiskal federalism. Det r ju inte meningen, att Emu skall kompensera fr eller neutralisera den dynamik och det produktivitetsdrivande strukturomvandlingstryck som uttryckligen efterstrvas med en enhetlig intern marknad. Lt mig I anslutning till den heterogena realekonomiska utvecklingen i Emu berra en relaterad politiksynvinkel. I vissa EU-lnders Emu-debatt, dock icke den danska, har man tenderat att som kriterium fr deltagande i en monetr union uppstlla krav, inte blott p monetr och finansiell konvergens utan ven p real konvergens och uppnendet av cyklisk synkronisering, och uttryckligen cyklisk synkronisering p en varaktig, permanent bas. Detta r inte serist. Det finns ingenting sdant som permanent realekonomisk konvergens. Det skulle i s fall beskriva en strukturellt fastfrusen lndergrupp, utan all ekonomisk och politisk dynamik. -Ngot sdant kommer aldrig att existera, och jag kan inte tnka mig att ngot land skulle nska delta i en sdan (planekonomisk) konstruktion. 6. Tillbaka till konstellationen av en penningpolitik och divergent ekonomisk utveckling. Stabiliseringsbehov av nationell karaktr kommer att uppst trots att ECB-rntan sttes riktigt, och "riktigt" betyder: fr Emu-omrdet som en helhet. Det samma gller tillvxt-och strukturproblematiken. Alla icke-nskade fljder av divergenser kan i princip blott tgrdas med annat n penningpolitik, dvs. uttryckligen d nationell finans-och strukturpolitik. De frsta 18 mnadernas erfarenheter av Emu antyder, att kraven p nationell finanspolitik och p arbetsmarknaden kommer att ka, inte minska, till fljd av Emu, till fljd av tendensen till divergerande ekonomisk utveckling. Detta kan lta paradoxalt, men skall anses som sunt och inte helt ovlkommet. 7. Frgan om det r mjligt att via annan politik kompensera frlusten av en nationell penningpolitik har varit central i svl akademisk som praktisk Emu-debatt, nationellt och internationellt. Det intuitiva svaret i populra debatter har mestadels varit ett klart nej. Detta r smickrande fr centralbanker. Men lt oss vara rliga. Vem kan pminna sig om att en enda ansedd nationalekonom under de senaste tio ren skulle ha tillskrivit penningpolitiken sdan verkningsfrmga och sdan precisionsstyrning som mngen i Emu-debatternas hetta menar att ett land frlorar i och med Emu-medlemskap? Man kan inte frlora det man inte har. I den avreglerade, marknadsdrivna, successivt alltmer globaliserade vrld, som vi levt i lngt innan bokstavskombinationen Emu blev uppfunnen, har centralbankerna och regeringarna varit tvungna att leva med insikten, att penningpolitiken ensam inte kan leverera kombinationen stabilitet, tillvxt och sysselsttning, fr att inte tala om andra mlsttningar. De flesta utvecklade lnders centralbanker valde att binda, eller lagstiftningsvgen frpliktades att binda, penningpolitikens mjligheter till ett ml, prisstabiliteten, fre Maastricht och inte till fljd av Maastricht. -Likas r det universellt accepterat, att penningpolitikens mjligheter till framgngsrik kortsiktig konjunkturpolitisk fine-tuning redan lnge varit obefintliga. Detta r inte att underknna eller nedvrdera penningpolitikens vrde innanfr eller utanfr Emu. Men penningpolitiken har bara ett instrument, centralbanksrntan, och penningpolitiken kan inte differentieras enligt omrde eller sektor. 8. Invndningar av samma karaktr kan riktas mot finanspolitiken, srskilt nr det gller finanspolitikens mjligheter till kortsiktig konjunkturpolitisk styrning, fine-tuning, via variationer i budgetsaldot (dvs. verskott/underskott) , men faktum r, att variationer i budgetsaldot i princip r ett tillgngligt instrument i finanspolitiken och att finanspolitiken innehller andra mjligheter att pverka den inhemska ekonomiska utvecklingen, nmligen via ndringar i relativa priser. En sdan pverkan sker ju hela tiden ver ett brett flt av statsbudgeten med dess avgifter, skatter, std och bidrag, etc. Mnga av dessa har ven stabiliseringspolitisk relevans. Och det som vagt kallas strukturpolitik, r till stor del finanspolitik, drfr att den drives via statsbudgeten. Jag delar de flesta ekonomers skepticism gentemot diskretionr konjunkturutjmnande finanspolitik ven i Emu.sammanhang, men samtidigt tror jag, att man i Emu-sammanhang inte skall frbig finanspolitikens mjligheter .fr det r finanspolitiken vi har att ty oss till vid lnderspecifika stabilitetsproblem i Emu. De nrmaste rens utveckling kan i detta hnseende visa sig intressant inom Emu. I dag vet vi inte hur stora krav kan komma att stllas p det finanspolitiska beslutsfattandet -och p analysen. Vi fr sjlvfallet utg ifrn, att finanspolitikens svrigheter kommer att visa sig vara asymmetriska; det typiska problemet r hur man skall kunna strama t ekonomin tillrckligt -den motsatta situationen tar nog den politiska processen lttare hand om. Hur som helst, finanspolitikens relevanta begrnsningar kommer inte att hrrra frn Maastricht eller den sk. tillvxt-och stabilitetspakten utan frn inhemska sk. "politiska realiteter". 9. Arbetsmarknaden r det andra omrdet vars prestation i Emu-sammanhang fr en strategisk betydelse. Orealistiskt hga avtal behver ju inte till fullo eller ens delvis reflekteras i priser, men kan nd verka direkt p sysselsttningen, via den frutsedda effekten p kostnadsniv och lnsamhet. Personligen r jag inte enormt bekymrad fr att arbetsmarknadens parter inte skulle kunna hantera Emu-situationen realistiskt, men detta r frsts ngot som framtiden fr visa. Emu-medlemskapet har inneburit en principiell frndring p arbetsmarknaden i den meningen, att varken stat eller centralbank har teoretiska eller praktiska instrument med vilka de skulle kunna skydda eller kompensera arbetsmarknadens parter fr konsekvenserna av misslyckade avtal. Orealistiskt hga lneavtal trffar bda parter direkt, den ena i form av arbetslshet, den andra i form av snkt lnsamhet, och det finns inget stt fr den offentliga sektorn att skydda parterna mot konsekvenserna av sina egna beslut. -Detta r nog en frbttring i den institutionella ramen, och drfr r jag som sagt inte speciellt orolig fr att arbetsmarknadens parter inte skulle klara av lnebildningen, svl dess niv som flexibiliteten. Ett av de nationella kriterierna p en fungerande arbetsmarknad i Emu-sammanhang mste vara, att den ven under perioder med kande efterfrgan p arbetskraft frmr producera mttliga avtal. Lika viktigt, men inte direkt Emu-relaterat, r att f till stnd en trendmssig hjning av sysselsttningsgraden. Jag skall inte hr g in p den komplexa strukturproblematik som ligger i bakgrunden, annat n att sga, att vi hr har ett exempel p finanspolitikens existerande roll, och dess potentiella roll. Det r ju uppenbart, att arbetsmarknadens svrigheter att spontant absorbera de arbetslsa i hgsta grad hnger ihop med hga skattesatsers samverkan med diverse bidragssystems utformning.  Drmed tangerar vi samhllspolitiska frgestllningar av betydligt principiell karaktr, som inte hr under dagens tema, ty svl innanfr som utanfr Maastricht och Emu hr de till den nationella politiksfren. De skall hra till den nationella sfren, och enbart dr kan de tekniskt hanteras. 10. Fr mig ter det sig sjlvklart, att Emu ensam och som sdan inte avgr ngon nations framtid eller de. En monetr union r trots allt nrmast och framfr allt uttryckligen en monetr union. Dom verkligt stora utmaningarna fr varje ekonomi ligger annorstdes, i skrandet av kunskapskapital, socialt kapital, vlfrdssamhllets funktionsduglighet och finansieringsbas i en alltmer ppen ekonomi, osv. Men, ett stort, strngt stabilitetsorienterat valutaomrde a la Maastricht har, och inte enbart fr sm lnder som Finland, en enormt vrdefull funktion: Den s.a.s. pacificerar den monetra sfren, s att nationell politik kan koncentrera sig p det som politik skall handla om, nmligen frutsttningarna fr tillvxt, sysselsttning, frdelning, vlfrdssamhllets normer och mekanismer, etc, i stllet fr att slsa handlingsutrymme, resurser och debatt p spekulativa kapitalrrelser och dessas strande effekter p samhllet via rntepolitik och finanspolitik. Jag tycker nog att detta skapar fundamentalt genuinare frutsttningar fr en samhllspolitiskt orienterad politisk process och politisk debatt. -Det skall vl t.o.m. en centralbankir f sga. Fr Finlands del var det en otacksam situation att sitta med en liten nationell valuta, stndigt utsatt fr inhemska och utlndska placerares skiftande bedmningar kring relativ avkastning. Fr vr del innebar Emu-medlemskapet, att vi med en gng klippte av en potentiellt destabiliserande lnk mellan valutamarknadden och rntepolitiken. Sjlvfallet var detta en enorm vinst fr oss, sedan vi vl hade lyckats skapa de inhemska frutsttningarna fr stabilitet. Det r en bedmningsfrga, s hr ex post, huruvida Finland vergick till Emu, frn en i grunden flytande valuta eller en fastkursvaluta (inom ERMI). Jag anser, att bda r srbara fr ven externa strningar och drmed innehller en potentiellt besvrlig lnk mellan valutamarknad och inhemsk rntepolitik. 11. Jag vill sluta cirkeln med fljande: Det finns ingen politikregim utan risker. Men man kan byta en risk mot en annan risk. Genom Emu-medlemskap eliminerar Finland, fr att nu anvnda Finland som exempel, risken av att internationella kapitalrrelser destabiliserar ekonomin, men det r klart att Finland d i stllet exponerar sig fr eventuella politikmisstag frn ECBs sida, och Finland exponerar sig ocks mera gentemot vriga Emu-deltagares eventuella ansvarslsa finanspolitik. Utanfr Emu r vi tminstone inte lika direkt utsatta fr ECBs eller Emu-regeringars eventuella politikmisstag, men i gengld r vi mera utsatta fr risker av egna misstag och fr internationella kapital.rrelser. Eftersom jag personligen skulle bedma risken av oansvarig eller radikalt misslyckad politik frn ECBs sida som obetydlig, och att finansiell konsolidering och finanspolitiskt frnuft i stort sett kommer att glla inom Emu.kretsen, s r det uppenbart hur riskbalansen ter sig. Min bedmning pverkas av det faktum, att Maastricht-avtalet innehller tv viktiga skyddsmekanismer, som r viktiga fr varje deltagare, men mhnda speciellt fr sm lnder. Fr det frsta: De relativt strngt skrivna Maastricht-normerna fr balans i den offentliga sektorn, i frening med det faktum, att regeringarna i och med Emu-intrde fr ett direkt intresse av sunda finanser i andra Emu-lnder. Fr det andra: Att penningpolitikens mlsttning skrevs konkret in i lagstiftningen samtidigt som ECB gjordes sjlvstndigt, och mlsttningen drmed skyddades mot ptryckningar. Dessa "skringar" gr att man, s lngt det i verkligheten verhuvud r mjligt, fr en rimlig skerhet fr vad man byter sig till, nr man ger bort nationell penningpolitisk autonomi.

Title: Speech at the Finance 2001 seminar
text: President Matti Vanhala's speech at the Finance 2001 seminar . Speech . Thursday26 October 2000, 12:00 AM FUNDING 2001 SEMINAR Finlandia Hall 26.10.2000 Pss Director Matti Vanhala The strong growth momentum that has continued for many years has matured into a phase of the Finnish economy that is beginning to test balance and in which our ability to secure our own growth and employment development is tested. The external conditions are not bad. As regards the global economy and its core, growth forecast for the euro area is also strong for next year. Of course, it is always true that we can realistically assess the global economy." It is an ever-changing cross-wave of adjustment processes, in which the real economy and the financial markets - with their pockets and exchange rates - are in constant interaction. The excesses are always verifiable. We have to reconcile ourselves, partly because of the fact that there is no other world. At a time when globalisation has been the subject of fierce criticism in the autumn, the partly tangible pavements as arguments, as in Prague, should be seen as a fact that the so-called 'green belt' is not a matter of fact. globalisation took place a long time ago. In this case, the individual economy is not capable of disengaging or isolating itself, but its framework and trends must be adapted to the economic policies of each country. This is how the trends and forces of change in the global economy take shape and change the management of the world economy. the external conditions of our economy are reasonable. Of course, the price of raw material is the price of raw material. ... Analysts and participants in the market are fairly generally of the opinion that current price levels are not sustainable. ... ljymarkets are adapting. Through qualifier fluctuations and in any time frame, nsin happens, we do not know. However, it is already essential for the inflation dynamics of the importing countries that the market price is expected to come down to a significant level below the average level. Exchange rate developments are also an essential issue for inflation dynamics in the euro area. The most common analysis in the world, whether private or official, indicates that the euro is undervalued. In the markets, the forecasts for the appreciation of the euro are often based on assumptions about the euro area and the US economy, in particular the assumed us balance of payments adjustment. I will not comment on the forecasts. However, if, as predicted, the euro were to strengthen as part of the overall adjustment mechanism of the global economy, this would of course play a role in the inflation dynamics of the euro area as a whole and, of course, in the middle east of Finland. It is possible, from a relatively probable angle of view, that in the medium term, the fall in the price of raw materials and the appreciation of the euro, perhaps in different timeframes, but nevertheless, both support the dismantling of cost pressures and price stability in the euro area. In economic policy, however, such a scenario cannot be relied upon. We can hope that it will come to fruition, but it is still only an opportunity for the future, and even if it does not happen - of course - it would cancel out on the price and wage fronts by then, in terms of compensation, perhaps the inflationary pssksis and the subsequent production and employment losses that have already been made. On the other hand, the negative consequences of such solutions for growth and employment are accentuated in the event that the global economy would have been estimated too optimistically if the price of raw heat were to prove to be more fatal to world economic growth than expected, if monetary corrections began to erode public confidence, etc. In other words, we are looking ahead to 2001, and we will have to look at our own economic forecasts and economic policy sssjs. In the press: As finland's economic growth is forecast to continue to be very strong and inflation in Finland has also diverged from the average in the euro area, and when interest rate policy is dimensioned against Finland in view of the expansionary euro area as a whole, the domestic setting of economic policy is extremely demanding. From Finland's point of view, a monetary policy that is still permissive is combined with fiscal policy, in which, in fact, the advancement is built on moderate and, at the same time, pro-employment income solutions. Economic policy is therefore ambitious and market solutions play a key role. *** The monetary policy of the euro is adapted and dimensioned for the euro monetary area, as the monetary policy of the markka was designed for the Finnish national economy. Country-specific developments within the euro area are in parallel. Thus, the interest rate is not equal to one euro country, nor is it the same as, for example, the interest rate. In Finland, it was possible to conduct a regional monetary policy. Consequently, monetary policy on a country-by-country basis cannot bear the burden that it traditionally was entitled to bear, but rather ensure stable economic development on the shoulders of fiscal policy and the markets, i.e. the fiscal policy and the markets. to the national parliament. However, we cannot say that the monetary policy of the euro area is a "vsssss" for Finland. It is in the interest of all the euro area countries that the monetary policy of the region should be tailored solely and exclusively to the region as a whole. In addition, the ECB's interest rate policy in Finland has gradually begun to bite into the real economy through the demand for credit from households and non-financial corporations. *** Has the ECB's monetary policy been right for the euro area as a whole? Throughout its 22-month existence, the single monetary policy has been growth-friendly. Because price stability was not threatened for a long time. Monetary policy remains permissive. In real terms, short-term interest rates are still at a fairly low level. Longterm interest rates have remained stable over the period of monetary policy tightening. In addition, liquidity is ample, which is the rate at which monetary and credit aggregates grow. How does the monetary policy stance fit in with the fact that inflation in the euro area has risen significantly in recent months? The most recent 12-month change in consumer price inflation was 2.8%, while the operative mssritelm of the ECB's price stability target is "less than 2%, as a result of the average period of time"! When the objective of price stability was set, in 1998, it was considered clear that the euro economy would from time to time be subject to external shocks, such as a sharp downward or high volatility in the price of raw materials. These are changes in relative prices, spatial or permanent changes that should not be included and could not be accounted for by monetary policy, and why there are no changes in relative prices, the losses of which cannot be compensated for by any attempt. The greater absoluteness is that the changes in relative prices are attributable to the so-called inflation rate of general inflation. through multiplier effects. The threat is evident when various parties in the economy are forced to seek compensation for the loss of income caused, for example, by the loss of income. the rise in the price of sljy, or the inflationary effects of the weakening of the euro. -Experience has shown that it is realistic that external price shocks that cut real incomes are susceptible to a wave of compensatory attempts and, through Sisk, to an increase in inflation expectations and actual inflation. Every effort must be made to achieve the economic policy of the situation. This kind of consideration underlies the ECB's interest rate policy. Overall, the risk of changing inflation expectations has increased. The monetary policy stance has been changed accordingly, not dramatically, not in a way that stifles economic growth, but in small steps in a tighter direction. This is an expression of a series of small rate hikes. ... The increase in prices is not a justification for monetary policy tightening, even if the price index rises above the ECB's price stability target of 2%. The interest rate hikes carried out have not been based on it, but the reason has been that light monetary conditions add to the risk that the rise in the price of sljy triggers a chain reaction in which, on the grounds of rising prices, prices are raised, thereby increasing inflation expectations. -After that, it will be more difficult to return to the state of price stability. Monetary policy should not undertake to finance price pressures arising from the multiplier effects of the price of sljy. That is why the calls for monetary policy to relax the difficulties caused by the rise in the price of sljy are unfounded: it would not lead to less difficulties, but would lead to greater difficulties. It is absolutely essential for inflation expectations, and thus for the management of inflation to be realised, that the broad general money market and the corporate sector - can rely on the central bank consistently acting in favour of the objective which it has been given priority by law, namely price stability. In this context, it is worth pointing out that monetary policy cannot be merely communication, i.e. rhetoric and signalling, but that, in the face of inflationary pressures, the tightening of the grip on monetary policy means a real slowdown in demand and growth in the real economy. A sharp monetary policy is most likely to be faced if the solutions of other economic policies, or other parts of the economy, are inflation-oriented or inflation-tolerant. Therefore, price stability cannot be the sole objective of the central bank if good economic development is pursued. The postponement of the key ECB interest rate to 4.75% a couple of weeks ago caused some bitter comments on the suitability of raising the interest rate in a context of slowing economic growth in the euro area. -It has to be said that, so far, forecasts for economic growth in the euro area are slowing down quite slightly, while inflation risks have increased markedly. The ECB is obliged by law to uphold price stability as a matter of priority. The position in which the ECB is criticised for its adherence to the policy of law is likely to be repeated whenever it tightens the monetary policy stance in accordance with the mandate laid down in the act. *** Let me now turn to the transparency of monetary policy, because the subject has been so much of a topic of discussion for the markets. The European Central Bank was accused of a lack of transparency even before it became a monetary authority. Still, the subject is chelseh. Maximum transparency is not at the heart of the traditions of central banks or other public administrations. However, in a market-driven world of real-time information flow, transparency is an important advantage for the central bank. It increases the effectiveness of monetary policy. It also increases the efficiency of the market. It puts pressure on the quality of the central bank's performance. It is a natural element of the central bank's self-determination. Over the years, each central bank has developed its own culture of publicity and information. Their differences in the market and universities are analyzed and commented on. Firstly, what is essential to transparency, what is secondary or even irrelevant? -It is essential that unambiguous information is communicated to the general public about what monetary policy aims to achieve (price stability) and that the central bank ensures that the general public has confidence in policy coherence - assuming, of course, that the central bank is ready for a coherent policy even when the time comes. In this respect, the interests of the Central Bank and the general public are identical. Everything else is secondary, then. The central bank's role is not to worry long as to ensure that market operators correctly anticipate the timing and frequency of interest rates. Shepherding inflation expectations is the job of the central bank, not assisting the markets in guessing the timing and sizing of interest rate policy. Secondly, if there is greater transparency about the basis and considerations of monetary policy, it is the expression of differences of analysis and opinion between the members of the monetary policy collegiums. In recent years, central banks such as the Central Bank of England and Sweden have deliberately adopted an open line, and pluralism has been well received. At the European Central Bank, we have emphasised the unambiguous and identical nature of communication, and in this case the markets and the media have also been condemned by all differences in nuance, and in the opinion of the authorities. *** All in all, making an assessment of the success of monetary policy in the euro area is rather premature. Attempts have been made to size interest rate policy to the future, in particular the nskym of price stability, and not to the actual sizing has been strongly criticised. There are always different schools of thought on the methods of implementation, but this is secondary. There have been messages about communication in the market; in this regard, it will hopefully be refined in interaction with the ksytsnch who serves the needs of different parties. Even in monetary union, however, economic policy is not just monetary policy. The changed norms of the global economy will not be conducive to economic development in the euro area unless national policies are strongly supported by stable monetary policy and the expansion of the real economy. The dominant force in the global economy is the constant pressure for structural change. Flexible economic structures and institutions that allow and favour the transfer of resources to the perss of productivity, of course, provide a better basis for growth, employment and well-being. These are structural policy priorities for which government decisions do not affect monetary policy stances in the short term. On the other hand, the general fiscal stance may have an impact on the sizing considerations of interest rate policy. The sizing of national fiscal policy in the euro area should now become cyclical, which in terms of managing cost and price pressures cannot be a good thing. text: President Matti Vanhala's speech at the Op Bank Week's pss celebration . Speech . Monday24 September 2001,12:00AM Are the goals and structures of the welfare society in harmony? The Bank of Finland's recent forecast calculation shows how quickly the economic picture can change. The Bank of Finland predicted gdp growth of 3.9% in 2001. Now, the bank is forecasting 1.5 percent, and that figure could prove to be high as well. The only thing that is certain about the forecasts is that they will not be realised as such, say economists; otherwise, we would not be talking about forecasts, but statistics. According to the forecasts of the kevsslls, tyshchis was to continue to decline; now the basis for the year became 9.4 percent. That's a high number. No matter how well a society cares about it, it is a social issue and a problem. One of the most important characteristics of a functioning welfare society is a high degree of employment, e.g. because of the fact that employment and self-determination feed each other. It is also clear that the financing of the welfare state at a high level of employment also makes it possible to have a high tax rate. A high tax rate, on the other hand, is likely to make it more difficult, or even more difficult, to dismantle the tax system in groups where its consequences and impact are most acute. Phosss themes of the evening. *** So now we are moving on to slower growth. We do not know how long we will have to wait for the global economy to recover from the recession that began a year ago. The tragedy of the week before last in New York has brought into the picture certainty, which is impossible to take into account in economic forecasts. However, we can consider two things to be given from Finland's point of view. In place of foreign demand, economic policy cannot be used to "programme" a replacement for domestic demand, nor can movements in the opposite direction between domestic and foreign demand be programmed from market problems. Secondly, the strong economic performance of the last 7 years partly represented the recovery from the recession. In the event that the international economy recovers faster than expected, the Finnish economy will not be able to return to the growth rates of the years. In the future, growth will be at a lower level than the average, trend. We are therefore entering tighter waters, because there will be social changes in the future, which in fact require strong economic growth and employment. By changes I mean, of course, the change in the structure of the system and, with it, with a high degree of certainty, the increase in expenditure on energy and treatment. Resource pressures are getting tougher. In economic and social policy, the bar is rising. How are we going to ensure that, in the face of structural change, essential welfare services are provided? *** There is a broad consensus that the welfare services of society are ssilytettsvsvs vshinchsnk in the current state of affairs. It does not follow that there will be a consensus on structural policy measures or institutional changes necessary for the preservation of the welfare state. Or that the readiness for change would be so early that the decline of the public sector would not be badly triggered. What are the key elements? The problem areas of the long-term period are outlined with concrete test calculations. In recent years, this has been done by the Minister of Finance, the Bank of Finland and other institutions. Last May, the Minister of Finance published calculations to address the problem areas, dividing the future into two periods, 2001-2007 and 2007-2050. The year 2007 has been chosen on the basis that the change in the structure of the economy is beginning to have a real impact on economic development. Consequently, the development of the previous situation creates a good or bad place for the control of the pressures caused by the change in the structure without damage. The ministry's bracketing of critical years of finance indicates that, under conditions of good economic growth (starting at just over 3% in 2001, attenuating to 2.2% in 2007), and as productivity increases at an annual rate of 2%, the public sector surplus would allow for some reduction in the national debt, although the tax burden would be somewhat reduced. However, open employment would not be reduced to more than 7%. d Under the option of slower economic growth (gdp growth will slow down from 1.7% to 1.2%), the surplus of public finances would gradually melt away and the government would start to increase its debt. By 2007, open employment would rise to 14%! Nsms are, of course, "just calculations", as you think, and the assumptions that come out of the assumptions made. However, they are not misleading, but rather describe with a great deal of veracity the region whose guerrilla development will hit. Time has passed since May. During this time, the economy has changed, and in the recent forecast revision by the Bank of Finland, we are in fact only moving in the terrain of the weaker option; in 2001, GDP growth would only be in the order of 1%, and employment would rise as early as next year. International development bodes well for a slow cyclical recovery. Developments in the current and next year do not reflect the trend up to 2007; perhaps 2001 and 2002 give too little of a picture of the future. A more serious possibility than in the past, however, is that the age of the change in the structure at the turn of the decade will become thin. In this situation, the financing of public finances, including welfare services, becomes correspondingly burdensome and difficult for the economy, as expenditure as a percentage of GDP and the tax rate with it rises very high. Even under the option of favourable economic development, the overall tax rate will return to 46%, while the weaker one will return to 50% in the long term calculations of the Finance Minister. To top it all off, it is possible to verify that the expenditure pressures brought about by the change in the structure will be estimated at the bottom. In recent years, the Bank of Finland has also conducted studies on the sustainability of public finances in various sectors. The message is the same: The long-standing policy of consolidating public finances, in conjunction with the most dramatic economic development, has created more solid positions for the state budget and a certain margin of manoeuvre, within which, depending of course on the economic situation, it is possible, without interfering with the criteria for expenditure, at least on a temporary basis, to reduce the tax burden without the sustainability of public finances will be jeopardised. But even in conditions of favourable economic development, that room for manoeuvre is not great. It doesn't e.g. it is possible to sign up for tax taxation, the so-called tax burden. a reduction in the tax wedge, which, according to the general consensus, would be required to increase the rate of employment with regard to taxation. The central government's expenditure economy, as well as in recent years, the rebalancing of central government finances and the partial amortisation of central government debt depend on a high tax rate. My own premonition and leadership of all of the above is as follows: When the expenditure economy of the state and municipalities, as well as revenue, is under severe pressure in general, then as the structure changes, it will prove difficult for ssrimms to finance the welfare state in its current form. From the point of view of the clear peasantry, it can be concluded that if welfare expenditure for a long period of time, for decades, is significant, then the economy will also create a new financial base. If funding is not forthcoming, welfare services will not be realised. The public sector with its welfare services is beginning to decline. *** So what is the solution? There is only one vsyls: that the economy itself produces finance, literally. This means that the economy must become more efficient and produce more with the resources that it has. There are two central points in the city. First of all, it would be possible to significantly increase the degree of employment, even for the reasons for this. Secondly, there would be a great deal of economic flexibility in all respects. In a highly technologicalised and integrated ('globalising') world, economic growth is realised in the form of a constant stream of structural changes and competitive pressure. Structural changes in the economy are always progressing at a rapid pace. sms is vsistsmssnch. Productivity and economic growth are generated by the fact that resources are transferred to higher productivity, i.e. produce more. The more flexible the economy is in relation to the economy, the more slippery the resources follow productivity, the more economic growth and income the economy generates, and the more the economy is able to provide itself with welfare services, among other things. Weak productivity developments, due to inefficiencies or undercapacity of resources, correspondingly undermine the standard of living, including the financial base of welfare services. Because of the obvious facts, it is essential that all resources are used, especially in an efficient manner, and that they move as sensitively and obstructively as possible from one object to another. Why, in order to be achieved, tough competition in the hysdyke market, efficiency-oriented public administration and d in view of the situation, d in particular a more efficient and labour market, is required. From the point of view of financing the welfare state, the employment rate is key. It is obvious if, indeed, the level of employment is to rise from the current levels, where open employment is just over 9% and including hidden employment, around 16%. A broad sense of employment cannot be compatible with the generally accepted objectives of society. It is a human dimension in which a large-scale socialisation of people takes place. It jeopardises the provision of welfare services in the form and scope that society wants. The challenge is to make the labour market more efficient by: That the employment rate is as high as possible, that it occurs in all income and education groups, including the lower income and education groups, that the power of employment moves as efficiently as possible in terms of productivity. Nshyness is necessary. The structurally deepened tyshchchy cannot be resolved quickly. It will have to be accepted that not all groups of employees can be returned by any action. There are reasons to point out at this stage that the functioning of the labour market is determined by a great many factors, of which the key factors are not so-called. within the reach of the market participants, not in principle not in the same way. There is therefore no reason to point the finger of blame at the wage market participants, who have sufficiently assumed their responsibilities in wage settlements after the recession and have played a key role in the stabilisation of the Finnish markka and low inflation, which was essential for the recovery of the Finnish economy. It is only so that the recession of the early 90s made the incentives for companies and the setting of the labour market permanently new. The low-wage service sector was priced out of the labour market, as a result of the combined effect of universality and tax and social benefit systems. First, the low productivity force at the onset of the recession became a tyshchch. Since then, strong export-led growth made it possible to finance the survival of this power. The development of employment was qualitatively good, but poor in terms of quality, and alongside the tyschllis, the hard core of tyschism was born, formed by the low-skilled, the educated and those living outside the growth centres. At the same time, the shortage of labour and the tyschchy, i.e. the problem of tys market mismatch, has been the intensifying manifestation of the mid-80s, which indicates a deterioration in the functioning of the labour market. The accumulation of work in certain groups and the mismatch problems in the tys market indicate that it is not a question of friction, but of a significant structural nature in Finland. This means that there is no functioning labour market for a significant part of the labour market. A wide range of measures are needed. Different groups of tyshchch are bitten by different means. Training and active employment measures will always be part of the toolbox, but the main challenge will be to improve the incentives for work and the functioning of wage formation. In a fully functioning employment market, the employment of different groups of employees does not depend on the level of employment or the level of competence. Everyone wants to work on the salary that is available on the labour market. Those jobseekers who have something to offer will be satisfied with a lower salary than the more competitive jobseekers. Of course, there is no such thing as a market. In different countries, the emphasis on labour market targets is different. The labour markets in the countries of The United States are very flexible, but they are weighed down by social manifests, which we are unfamiliar with, at least in the Nordic countries. The Finnish system is a long way from the basic model of a flexible labour market. At the level of the national economy as a whole, however, wage flexibility can be considered good in recent years. Broad employment has clearly moderated the earnings development of the national economy. While wage moderation has supported the price competitiveness of the export industry, the easing of income taxation has ensured an increase in the purchasing power of the wage earner. The credit goes to the parties in the labour market. As we can see from the employment statistics, despite wage moderation, our labour market is not satisfactory. However, even if the employment rate is classified outside the open sector, even if it is classified outside the open employment sector, the broader measure which has now fallen to just over 16 per cent is still a permanent loss of employment. The functioning of the labour market is hampered by a series of interlinked and mutually reinforcing structural defects which, in terms of the anti-economic tysills ability, deserve serious attention. (1) Exclusion of trained and low-productivity groups from the labour market. sms is a well-known state of affairs in all respects, which is the result of the combined influence of many structures of the welfare state and the labour market. (2) There is a wide range of support systems for architecture which, in order to progression to the combined income tax, undermines the competitiveness of the wage and salary and thus prolongs the absence of employment from the labour market. These are, in my view, the main skeins of problems which will continue to threaten the dismantling of the labour market and which, at the same time, will ensure the entry of new, younger workers to replace those who are leaving. *** My point is that, in the case of aid schemes, priority must be given to looking at structures and mechanisms of action more than the level of support, although the latter must not override itself if welfare expenditure competes with each other in the real process of making a contribution. The problematic nature of the issue is widely understood. However, breaking the traps and replacing them with strong incentives is not, even technically, a simple exercise in thought. It is likely that only support architects and market experts can work together to tackle it effectively. My own impression is that it is possible to install incentives for employment in the most difficult segments of the labour market by changing the form and structure of the aid. It is not easy, but on the other hand, it will not be easy to finance employment in the future, and it will not be easy in the future without cutting welfare expenditure in other areas. The welfare state must guarantee a sufficient safety net for all its members, while permanent mattresses should be distributed prudently. Improving the incentives for work is also about modifying the support systems so that they become clearer in the future, with the help of which the individual will be able to get back on its own feet. A support system should not be allowed to provide a permanent form of support, not to allow discouragement and abandonment. At the moment, the most significant incentive problems relate, on the one hand, to income traps created by the combined effect of taxation and subsidies, where it is not economically viable to receive work, and, on the other hand, to the system of incentives which, up to the official stage, make it economically unprofitable to work. There has been talk of income traps for a long time, both in public and at political level, but progress in solving the problem has been slow. The combined effect of progressive taxation and incomerelated subsidies and contributions (housing, labour market and subsistence allowances, as well as the maintenance fee) will continue to lead to situations where the additional income goes one hundred percent to the state coffers and receives it is only significantly above the average income of the national economy at the wage level. Attempts have been made to dismantle the revenue traps, but the political charges involved are such that the results have been modest or substandard. The moderate approach to income tax in recent years has been a step in the right direction, but has not been able to address very much of the incentive problem. A wide range of measures have been put forward to solve the problem of incentives. There has been talk of a negative income tax and the combination of forms of aid as a citizen's salary. There are reasons to continue the debate. *** The equalisation of wage development between different groups of employees is one of the stated objectives of the Finnish agreement system, which is served by many aspects of the wage agreement system. In proportion to the situation, the objectives have been achieved. In recent years, with exceptions, a Finnish wage earner has received more or less the same pay rises in recent years, regardless of where he works, or whoever is in demand for the skills he represents. There are undeniable institutional advantages to centralised agreement. However, the share of wage drift in wage increases has declined sharply in recent decades, and its also shrunk into the space in which the adjustment of relative wages can fit in. It should be noted that the flexibility of the pay structure is a matter of different wage trends for different groups of employees. Kuluvan ja ensi vuoden kehitys ei vlttmtt kerro vuoteen 2007 ulottuvaa trendi; kenties vuodet 2001 ja 2002 antavat liian heikon kuvan tulevaisuudesta. Aikaisempaa varteen otettavampana mahdollisuutena on kuitenkin pidettv sit, ett evt ikrakenteen muutoksen kohtaamiseen vuosikymmenen vaihteen lhestyess muodostuvat laihoiksi. Siin tilanteessa julkisen talouden rahoittaminen, mm. hyvinvointipalvelujen yllpitminen, muodostuu taloudelle vastaavasti raskaammaksi, ja vaikeaksi, kun menot suhteessa bkt:hen ja veroaste sen mukana nousevat hyvin korkealle. Suotuisankin talouskehityksen vaihtoehdossa kokonaisveroaste palaa valtiovarainministerin pitkn aikavlin laskelmissa 46 prosenttiin, heikommassa perti 50 prosenttiin. Kaiken lisksi on mahdollista, ehk todennkist, ett ikrakenteen muuttumisen tuomat menopaineet arvioidaan tn pivn alakanttiin. Mys Suomen Pankissa on viime vuosina tutkittu julkisen talouden kestvyytt eri nkkulmista. Viesti on sama: Pitkn harjoitettu valtiontalouden konsolidointipolitiikka yhdess mynteisen talouskehityksen kanssa on luonut valtiontaloudelle vankemmat lhtkohdat ja tietty pelivaraa, jonka puitteissa on, talousnkymist tietenkin riippuen, mahdollista menoperusteisiin puuttumatta ainakin tilapisesti alentaa verorasitusta ilman ett valtiontalouden kestvyytt vaarannetaan. Mutta suotuisankaan talouskehityksen oloissa tuo pelivara ei ole suuri. Se ei esim. mahdollista niin merkittv tyhn kohdistuvan veroverotuksen keventmist, ns. verokiilan kaventamista, jota yleisen ksityksen mukaan tyllisyysasteen nostaminen verotuksen osalta edellyttisi. Valtion menotalous samoin kuin viime vuosina nhty valtiontalouden tasapainottuminen ja valtiovelan osittainen kuolettaminen on korkean veroasteen varassa. Oma aavistukseni ja johtoptkseni kaikesta edellisest on seuraava: Kun valtion ja kuntien menotalouteen, samoin kuin tuloihin, muutenkin kohdistuu kovia paineita, niin ikrakenteen muuttuessa nykymuotoisen hyvinvointiyhteiskunnan rahoittaminen tulee osoittautumaan rimmisen vaikeaksi. Selken talonpoikaisjrjen perusteella voidaan todeta, ett jos hyvinvointimenot pitkksi aikaa, vuosikymmeniksi, merkittvsti lisntyvt, on talouden synnytettv mys uutta rahoituspohjaa. Ellei rahoitusta lydy, hyvinvointipalvelut eivt toteudu. Julkinen sektori hyvinvointipalveluineen alkaa rappeutua. *** Mist siis ratkaisu? On vain yksi vyl: ett talous itse tuottaa rahoituksen, kirjaimellisesti. Se tarkoittaa, ett talouden on tehostuttava, ja tuotettava enemmn niill resursseilla jotka sill on. Mielestni tss on kaksi keskeist lhtkohtaa. Ensiksikin tyllisyysastetta olisi kyettv merkittvsti nostamaan, nistkin syist. Toiseksi, talouden kaikenpuolista joustoa olisi listtv voimakkaasti. Vahvasti teknologistuvassa ja yht vahvasti integroituvassa ("globalisoituvassa") maailmassa talouskasvu toteutuu jatkuvana rakennemuutosten virtana ja kilpailupaineessa. Rakennemuutokset etenevt taloudessa aina eptasaisesti. Tm on vistmtnt. Tuottavuus ja talouskasvu syntyvt siit, ett voimavarat siirtyvt korkeamman tuottavuuden perss, siis tuottavat enemmn. Mit joustavampi talous tss suhteessa on, sit liukkaammin resurssit seuraavat tuottavuutta, sit enemmn talouskasvua ja tuloja talous tuottaa ja sit enemmn talous kykenee suomaan itselleen mm. hyvinvointipalveluja. Heikko tuottavuuskehitys, tehottomuudesta tai resurssien vajaakytst johtuva, vastaavasti nakertaa elintasoa, mm. hyvinvointipalvelujen rahoituspohjaa symll. Nist, sinns ilmeisist tosiasioista johtuen on olennaisen trket, ett kaikki resurssit ovat kytss, nimenomaan tehokkaassa kytss, ja ett ne mahdollisimman herksti ja esteitt liikkuvat kohteesta toisen. Mik toteutuakseen edellytt kovaa kilpailua hydykemarkkinoilla, tehokkuushakuista julkista hallintoa ja  tmn pivn tilannetta ajatellen  eritoten tehokkaampia ja tyllistvmpi tymarkkinoita. Hyvinvointiyhteiskunnan rahoittamisen kannalta tyllisyysaste on oleva avainasemassa. Tm on ilmeist, jos todellakin tyttmyys kntyy nousuun nykytasoilta, jolla avoin tyttmyys on runsaat 9 prosenttia ja piilotyttmyys mukaan lukien 16 prosentin paikkeilla. Nin laaja tyttmyys ei voi olla sopusoinnussa yhteiskunnassa yleisesti hyvksyttyjen tavoitteiden kanssa. Se on inhimillinen vryys, jossa toteutuu laajamittainen ihmisten yhteiskunnallinen syrjytyminen. Se vaarantaa hyvinvointipalvelujen tuottamisen yhteiskunnan haluamassa muodossa ja laajuudessa. Nin on jo tn pivn, mutta ongelma krjistyy ikrakenteen muuttuessa. *** Tymarkkinat olisi siten saatava toimimaan tehokkaammin. Haasteena on tymarkkinoiden tehostaminen siten, ett tyllisyysaste saadaan mahdollisimman korkeaksi, ett nin tapahtuu kaikissa, mys alemmissa tulo-ja koulutusryhmiss, ett tyvoima mahdollisimman tehokkaasti liikkuu tuottavuuden perss. Nyryys on tarpeen. Rakenteelliseksi syventynyt tyttmyys ei ole ratkaistavissa nopeasti. Joudutaan hyvksymn se, ett kaikkia tyttmien ryhmi ei milln toimilla en saada palautetuksi tyelmn. On syyt tss vaiheessa korostaa sit, ett tymarkkinoiden toimivuus mrytyy hyvin monesta tekijst, joista ert keskeiset eivt mitenkn ole ns. tymarkkinaosapuolten ulottuvilla, eivt periaatteessa eivtk kytnnss. Siten ei ole aihetta suunnata syyttvi sormia kohti tymarkkinaosapuolia, jotka kyll ovat kantaneet vastuunsa laman jlkeisiss palkkaratkaisuissa ja keskeisesti vaikuttaneet Suomen markan vakautumiseen ja alhaiseen inflaatioon, mik Suomen talouden toipumiselle oli olennaista. Kvi vain niin, ett 90-luvun alun lama jrjesti yritysten kannustimet ja tymarkkinoiden asetelmat pysyvsti uusiksi. Matalapalkkainen palvelusektori tuli hinnoitelluksi tymarkkinoilta pois, yleissitovuuden ja vero-ja sosiaalietuusjrjestelmien yhteisvaikutuksesta. Ensin alhaisen tuottavuuden tyvoima laman alkaessa joutui tyttmksi. Sen jlkeen vahva vientivetoinen kasvu mahdollisti sen, ett kyseisen tyvoiman pysyminen tyttmn kyettiin rahoittamaan. Tyllisyyskehitys muodostui laadullisesti hyvksi mutta mrllisesti huonoksi, ja tyllisten rinnalle syntyi tyttmyyden kova ydin, jonka muodostavat heikosti koulutetut, ikntyneet ja kasvukeskusten ulkopuolella asuvat tyttmt. Samanaikainen tyvoimapula ja tyttmyys, eli tymarkkinoiden kohtaanto-ongelma, on ollut 80-luvun puolivlist voimistuva ilmi, joka kertoo tymarkkinoiden toiminnan heikkenemisest. Tyttmyyden kasautuminen tiettyihin ryhmiin sek tymarkkinoiden kohtaanto-ongelmat kertovat, ettei kyse ole kitkatyttmyydest, vaan suomalainen tyttmyys on merkittvsti rakenteellista. Tm tarkoittaa, ett merkittvlle osalle tyntekijist ei ylipns ole olemassa toimivia tymarkkinoita. Tarvitaan vistmtt monenlaisia toimia. Eri tyttmien ryhmiin purevat erilaiset keinot. Koulutus ja aktiiviset tyllistmistoimet tulevat aina olemaan keinovalikoiman vlttmttmi osia, mutta keskeisin haaste tulee olemaan tynteon kannusteiden ja palkanmuodostuksen toimivuuden parantaminen. Tydellisesti toimivilla tymarkkinoilla eri tyntekijryhmien tyllisyys ei riipu ist tai osaamisen tasosta. Kaikki tyt haluavat lytvt sit  sill palkalla, joka tymarkkinoilla on tarjolla. Ne tynhakijat, joilla on vhemmn tarjottavaa, tyytyvt pienempn palkkaan kuin kilpailukykyisemmt tynhakijat. Aivan nin tydellisi tymarkkinoita ei tiettvsti ole olemassa. Eri maissa tymarkkinatavoitteet painottuvat eri tavoin. Eriden maiden tymarkkinat ovat merkittvn joustavia, mutta niill on painolastinaan yhteiskunnallisia ilmiit, joita ainakin Pohjoismaissa vierastamme. Suomalainen jrjestelm on varsin kaukana joustavien tymarkkinoiden perusmallista. Koko kansantalouden tasolla voidaan palkkajoustavuuden kuitenkin katsoa viime vuosina olleen hyvn. Laaja tyttmyys on selvsti maltillistanut kansantalouden ansiokehityst. Samalla kun maltillinen palkkakehitys on tukenut vientiteollisuuden hintakilpailukyky, on kevenev tuloverotus taannut palkansaajan ostovoiman kasvun. Tst kunnia kuuluu tymarkkinaosapuolille. Kuten tyttmyystilastoista havaitsemme, palkkamaltista huolimatta tymarkkinamme eivt ole tyllistneet lhestulkoon tyydyttvsti. On syntynyt joukkotyttmyytt; runsaan 9 prosentin tyttmyysprosentti kuvaa vain ns. avointa tyttmyytt. Tyllistymismahdollisuutensa pysyvsti menettnyt pitkaikaistytn on kuitenkin edelleen tytn vaikka hnet luokiteltaisiin avoimen tyttmyyden ulkopuolelle, siihen laajempaan mittariin joka tt nyky on laskenut vasta runsaaseen 16 prosenttiin. Tymarkkinoiden toimintaa vaikeuttaa joukko toisiinsa kytkeytyvi ja toisiaan ruokkivia rakennevikoja, jotka talouden vastaista tyllistmiskyky ajatellen ansaitsevat vakavaa huomiota. (1) Vhn koulutetun ja heikon tuottavuuden omaavien ryhmien sulkeminen tymarkkinoiden ulkopuolelle. Tm on kaikin puolin tunnettu asiaintila, joka on seurausta monien hyvinvointivaltion ja tymarkkinoiden rakenteiden yhteisvaikutuksesta. (2) Laajan tukijrjestelmn arkkitehtuuri, joka yhdistettyn tuloveron progressioon heikent tynteon kilpailukyky ansioiden lhteen ja siten pit tyvoimaa poissa tymarkkinoilta. (3) Tyllisten palkkakehityksen tiukka yhdenmukaisuus, ts. palkkajouston puute mit tulee henkilkohtaiseen, ammattiryhmkohtaiseen ja alakohtaiseen kehitykseen. Makrotasolla kohtuullisen joustava palkkaneuvottelujrjestelm ktkee taakseen puutteellisen ruohonjuuritason joustavuuden. Palkat eivt eriydy tymarkkinoiden eri osa-alueiden kysynt/tarjontatilanteen perusteella. (4) Elkejrjestelmn kannustinongelmat, joiden ansiosta tosiasiallinen elkkeelle jmisik on seitsemn vuotta virallista elkeik alempi (58 vs 65). Nm ovat mielestni ne keskeiset ongelmavyyhdit, jotka jatkossakin uhkaavat est tyttmyyden purkamisen ja jotka samalla varmistavat uusien, nuorempien tyttmien tulon elkkeelle poistuvien tilalle. *** Ksitykseni on, ett tukijrjestelmien kohdalla on ensisijaisesti tarkasteltava rakenteita ja toimintamekanismeja enemmn kuin tuen tasoa, jos kohta jlkimmist ei saa ohittaa itsestn selvn jos hyvinvointimenot kilpailevat toistensa kanssa todellisessa ptksenteossa. Asian ongelmallisuus on laajasti ymmrretty. Loukkujen purkaminen ja korvaaminen vahvoilla kannustimilla ei kuitenkaan ole edes teknisesti mikn yksinkertainen ajatusharjoitus. Todennkisesti siihen voivat tuloksellisesti pureutua vain tukiarkkitehdit ja tymarkkina-asiantuntijat yhteisvoimin. Oma mielikuvani on, ett tyllistymiskannustimien asentaminen tymarkkinoiden vaikeimmille lohkoille on mahdollista muuttamalla tuen muotoa ja sen rakennetta. Helppoa se ei ole, mutta toisaalta tyttmyyden rahoittaminen ei sekn ole jatkossa helppoa eik vlttmtt nykymitassa mahdollista leikkaamatta hyvinvointimenoja muilla lohkoilla. Totesin omana ennakkoluulonani, ett tukijrjestelmien kohdalla on enemmn kysymys rakenteesta ja toimeenpanotekniikasta kuin tasosta. Nin voitaneen ajatella kunnes on muusta nytt ja kokemuksia. Ei silti olisi viisasta, edes poliittisen oikeaoppisuuden nimiss, ummistaa silmin silt tosiasialta, ett oli tuen tekniikka mik tahansa, sen taso joko kannustaa tyllistymist tai ei ja siksi vaikuttaa tyttmyyden laajuuteen. Tmn nkkohdan painoa lis se, ett verokiilan kaventaminen vain osittain rahoittaa itsens eik sen tyllistmisvaikutuksen laajuudesta voi olla etukteen varmuutta. Hyvinvointivaltion pit taata kaikille jsenilleen riittv turvaverkko, pysyvi patjoja sen sijaan on syyt jakaa harkiten. Tynteon kannusteiden parantamisessa on mys kyse tukijrjestelmien muokkaamisesta siten, ett niist tulee selkemmin vliaikaisia jrjestelmi, joiden avulla yksil psee palaamaan omille jaloilleen. Tukijrjestelmt eivt saisi tarjota eivtk aiheuttaa pysyv elmnmuotoa, eivtk sallia lannistumista ja luopumista. Tmn hetken merkittvimmt kannusteongelmat liittyvt toisaalta verotuksen ja tukien yhteisvaikutuksena syntyviin tuloloukkuihin, jossa tyn vastaanottaminen ei taloudellisesti kannata, toisaalta elkejrjestelmiin, jotka tekevt viralliseen elkeikn saakka tyskentelemisen taloudellisesti kannattamattomaksi. Tuloloukuista on puhuttu pitkn, julkisuudessa ja poliittisella tasolla, mutta edistyminen ongelman ratkaisemisessa on ollut hidasta. Progressiivisen verotuksen ja tulosidonnaisten tukien ja maksujen (asumis-, tymarkkina-ja toimeentulotuet sek pivhoitomaksu) yhteisvaikutus johtaa edelleen tilanteisiin, jossa listulo menee sataprosenttisesti valtion kassaan eik tyn vastaanottaminen kannata kuin merkittvsti kansantalouden keskitulon ylittvll palkkatasolla. Tuloloukkuja on yritetty purkaa, mutta asiaan liittyvt poliittiset lataukset ovat sit luokkaa, ett tulokset ovat olleet vaatimattomia tai tilapisi. Tuloverotuksen maltillinen keventminen viime vuosina on ollut oikeansuuntaista, mutta ei ole kyennyt kovin paljon vhentmn kannustinongelmaa. Kannustinongelman ratkaisemiseksi on esitetty monenlaisia keinoja. On puhuttu negatiivisesta tuloverosta ja tukimuotojen yhdistmisest kansalaispalkaksi. Tt keskustelua on syyt jatkaa. *** Palkkakehityksen tasaaminen eri palkansaajaryhmien vlill on suomalaisen sopimusjrjestelmn julkilausuttuja tavoitteita, jota monet palkkasopimusjrjestelmn piirteet palvelevat. Tss suhteessa tavoitteet on saavutettu. Vhisi poikkeuksia lukuun ottamatta suomalainen palkansaaja on viime vuosina saanut jokseenkin samat palkankorotukset riippumatta siit, miss tehtviss hn tyskentelee, tai minklainen on hnen edustamansa osaamisen kysynt tymarkkinoilla. Keskitettyyn sopimiseen liittyy institutionaalisesti kiistattomia etuja. Yhdistettyn yhteniseen palkankorotusnormiin se johtaa kuitenkin siihen, ett suhteellisten palkkojen joustavuus  yksiliden, yritysten, toimialojen vlill  voi toteutua vain sopimuskorotukset ylittvien palkankorotusten, eli palkkaliukumien kautta. Palkkaliukumien osuus palkankorotuksista on kuitenkin vhentynyt viime vuosikymmenin voimakkaasti, ja sen myt on kutistunut se tila, johon suhteellisten palkkojen sopeutumisen tytyy mahtua. Suomalainen palkkarakenne on jykistynyt. Palkkarakenteen joustavuuden puute on pitkn plle erinomaisen ongelmallinen asia niin tyllistmisen kuin resurssien tehokkaan ohjautumisen kannalta. Talouskasvu toteutuu jo nyt ja viel vahvemmin jatkossa jatkuvan rakennemuutoksen kautta, vistmttmn seurannaisena jatkuva eriytyminen ja suuret joskin mys vaihtelevat erot tuottavuuden tasossa eri alojen ja ammattiryhmien vlill. Tuottavuushakuinen palkkaliukuma ei luo inflaatiopaineita, juuri sen takia ett pohjalla on tuottavuuden nousu. Jos resurssit liikkuvat tuotavuuden perss, tuloksena on resurssien tehokkaampi kytt kansantaloudessa. Ns. sopimuskorotukset, jos ne perustuvat kansantalouden keskimriseen tuottavuuskehitykseen, mrittelevt pitklti palkkaratkaisujen kotimaiset inflaatiovaikutukset. Palkkajoustavuuden parantaminen vaatii mrtietoista yhteistyt tymarkkinoiden kehittmiseksi. Siirtyminen liittokohtaisiin sopimuksiin ei ratkaisisi asiaa, sill palkkajoustavuuden ongelmat eivt ole pelkstn tai edes primrisesti toimialojen vlisess palkkakehityksess. Palkkarakenteen joustavuutta tarvitaan yht lailla liittojen sisll, tyntekij-ja toimipaikkatasolla. Jos tyllisyytt tavoitellaan, joudutaan hyvksymn se, ett palkat nousevat nopeammin niiss tehtviss, joilla tyvoimasta on pulaa, kuin tehtviss, joilla tyvoimaa on runsaasti tarjolla. On syyt huomata, ett palkkarakenteen joustavuudessa on kyse eri tyntekijryhmien erivist palkkatrendeist. Usein palkkajoustavuudella tarkoitetaan toista asiaa, eli tyntekijiden palkkojen joustamista suhdanteiden tai yrityksen voittojen mukaan. Jlkimmisen kaltaiselle joustavuudelle on oma sijansa, mutta normaalisti vakavaraisen yrityksen edellytykset suhdannesyklin ylittvn tulontasaukseen ovat paremmat kuin yksittisen tyntekijn. *** Ikntyvien tyntekijiden tyss pysymisen kannusteista on viime aikoina keskusteltu runsaasti. Erityisesti keskustelun kohteina on ollut tyttmyyselkejrjestelm ja osa-aikaelkejrjestelm. Tllaisten jrjestelmien osalta on syyt muistaa, ett se, mik oli jrkev tietyss taloudellisessa tilanteessa, ei vlttmtt sovellu nykytilanteeseen. Tyttmyyselkejrjestelm on voinut aikanaan olla sosiaalisesti perusteltu keino vakauttaa tymarkkinoilta pysyvsti pudonneiden yksiliden elmntilanne. Tilanne on kuitenkin viime vuosina muuttunut ja muuttuu jatkuvasti. Suuret ikluokat ovat tulossa tyttmyyselkkeen piiriin. Niden ikluokkien rakenteellinen tyttmyys on merkittvsti alempi kun sotien aikana syntyneiden, joten tyttmyyselkkeen kaltaiselle jrjestelmlle on vhemmn sosiaalisia tarpeita. Tyttmyyselke tarjoaa nykyiselln mahdollisuuden vrinkyttn ernlaisena varhaiselkkeen, varhennetun vanhuuselkkeen sijasta. Ikluokkien kasvaessa tllaisen vrinkytn kustannukset ovat nousemassa samalla kun jrjestelmn sosiaaliset perusteet vhenevt. Jotta elkkeelle jmisik voitaisiin merkittvsti nostaa, tyttmyyselkejrjestelmn uudelleen harkinta lienee vlttmtnt. Osa-aikaelke on sinns arvokas jrjestelm, joka sekin vrin mitoitettuna voi kannustaa ennenaikaiseen elkkeelle jmiseen. *** Maailmalla on lukuisia esimerkkej siit, miten erilaisilla toimintamalleilla on saavutettu hyvi tuloksia tyllisyyden hoidossa. Yhteist on kuitenkin se, ett jrjestelmn on rakennettu riittvsti joustavia elementtej, jotka varmistavat tymarkkinoiden toiminnan. Kun tymarkkinat toimivat, paranee mys tyllistmistoimien teho. Tss valossa on arvioitava mys muiden pohjoismaiden hyvi kokemuksia ns. aktiivisesta tyllistmisest  mm. tyllisyyskoulutuksesta ja velvoitetyllistmisest. Nist kokemuksista on syyt oppia. Niiden siirtminen suoraan suomalaiseen yhteiskuntaan yht onnistuneesti ei kuitenkaan vlttmtt ole helppoa. Onnistuakseen aktiivisen tyllistmisen tulee kyet palauttamaan syrjytymisuhan alla oleva yksil tukitoimien piirist takaisin normaaleille tymarkkinoille. Suomalaiset kokemukset ovat tss suhteessa vhemmn rohkaisevia kuin muissa pohjoismaissa. Suomalaisten tymarkkinoiden kyky luoda pysyvi typaikkoja heikommin kilpailukykyisille ei ole hyv. Aktiivisten tyllistmistoimien teho riippuu siten normaalien tymarkkinoiden toiminnasta. Ilman tymarkkinoiden toiminnan merkittv kehittymist ei aktiiviseen tyllistmiseen kannata ladata paljoa toiveita. *** Arvoisat kuulijat. Kunnianhimoiset tavoitteet talous-ja yhteiskuntapolitiikassa edellyttvt nykymaailmassa, ett kaikkia keinoja kytetn tehokkaasti, kuten sken suorittamani rakenneongelmien lpikynti osoitti. Maailma on muuttunut yht vaativaksi kuin tavoitteemme ovat kunnianhimoisia. Hyvinvointiyhteiskunta ei toteudu, jos voimavaroja jtetn kyttmtt. Suuret tyttmyysluvut ja syrjytyminen ilmentvt tt tosiasiaa. On melkoisen todennkist, ett asteittain ja viimeistn vestn ikrakenteen muuttumisen myt yhteiskunnan kasvavien hyvinvointipalvelujen rahoittaminen tulee yhteiskunnan poliittisessa ptksenteossa vaikeutumaan. Mikli lhivuosien talouskasvu toteutuu hitaana, tm on sitkin todennkisemp. Rakennevikoihin tarttuminen on hyvin suurella todennkisyydell edellytys sille, ettei julkisen sektorin rappio pse alulle.

Title: Speech at the University of Helsinki
text: Speech by Director Matti Vanhala at the University of Helsinki . Speech . Thursday18 October 2001, 12:00 AM Making monetary policy Europe-centric? Although the theme of the lecture series "Good markka ? welcome to the euro" is derived from the change of money at the turn of the coming year, the market perceived Finland as a euro country already in 1997. From the point of view of economic policy, we switched from the mark to the euro base on May Day 1998. It was then that the p??chs of Finland's participation in the monetary union was born. The average exchange rates of the participating countries were settled. A floating currency group was formed in a single formation, which at the turn of the year had one common interest rate. This meant that the possibility of adjusting the interest rate on the basis of one's own country's economic cycles was exhausted. In economic policy as well as in the industrial sector and in the labour market, since May Day 1998 there were new, excellently clear points of reference for monetary policy and quite clear standards for monetary policy in general. The transition from a national currency to a Europe-based single currency was a fundamental solution that goes beyond the economy and economic policy. Yet its monetary significance is easy not only to overstate. In general, the so-called monetary policy framework is attached to its own monetary unit. self-sufficiency. Interest rate and exchange rate policy in Finland always played a central role. Exchange rate policy was often resorted to out of the crisis. That is why we have seen our own monetary policy as valuable, but in fact that is why monetary policy is so-called 'monetary policy'. Self-sufficiency was a very relative k?site for us. Finland's economic growth is based on foreign trade and the international economy. The internationalisation of monetary policy, and with it the cross-border movement of money, is part of the monetary policy framework and naturally influences the choices that can be made in monetary policy, apart from the conditions and constraints arising from domestic economic management. A country-specific interest rate and exchange rate policy ? sometimes referred to as the self-efficacy of monetary policy ? implies freedom of choice in principle and a certain degree of security, neither of which is appropriate even in the integrated modern world. Nevertheless, it is the case that, with its own separate currency, the actual adoption of the 'self-efficacy' of a country's monetary policy presupposes that its own economy, in accordance with the standards of economic policy and economic development laid down in the EU Monetary Union, is required to develop and be used in accordance with the standards of economic policy and economic development. The fact that monetary policy is maintained on a national basis does not therefore mean that good economic development can be achieved more easily and with fewer inputs. ? ?m? is not at all paradoxical, but is the leader of a healthy peasant country. *** Monetary union, combined with the EU's internal market, will lead to deeper integration and dynamism in both markets and politics.
