Kysymys on (kuitenkin) kehityksest 90.luvun alun valuuttamyllerrysten jlkeen, kelluvan kurssin oloissa. Ruotsin ja Englannin kehitys todistavat siit, miten ratkaisevaa on talouden sisinen kyttytyminen: kotimainen hinta-ja kustannus-dynamiikka, tymarkkinoiden jousto tai sen puute, julkisen talouden kestvyys ja tuohon kehykseen sijoitetun talouspolitiikan uskottavuus. Tanska on 80-luvun perunakuurinsa jlkeen kehittynyt vakaasti perti kiinten kurssin oloissa  koska talouskehitys ja talouspolitiikka (ml. valuuttakurssipolitiikka) ovat olleet keskenn sopusoinnussa. Sveitsi on perinteellinen esimerkki siit, ett elm on rahaliittojen ja kurssikytkentjen ulkopuolella. Japanin vaikeudet puolestaan eivt johdu siit, ett maalla on oma raha. Ja niin edespin. Johtopts: Moni regiimi toimii, jos ehdot ovat kohdallaan. Pienen erillisen valuutan asema ei silti ole kansainvlisill rahoitusmarkkinoilla kiitollinen. Inflaatioalttius samoin kuin muut talous-ja tymarkkinapoliittiset virheet mobilisoivat herksti sek kotimaista ett kansainvlist keinottelua, talouden vaikeuksia syventen. Ja vaikka kotimainen talous ja talouspolitiikka olisivat kunnossa, on pieni valuutta muita enemmn alttiina niille salkkusopeutuksille, joita joka piv maailman rahoitusmarkkinoilla tehdn tuottojen toivossa. Ruotsin kruunun kehitys tn vuonna on tst esimerkki. Isommatkin valuutat joutuvat elmn globaalisten rahaliikkeitten kanssa. Nist syntyvien kurssiliikkeitten ja talouspolitiikassa tavoiteltujen stjen vlill on ajoittain ristiriitatilanteita, joiden kanssa on vain tultava toimeen  ja tullaan toimeen, koska niin pomaliikkeet kuin valuuttakurssijousto ovat globaalisen ja kansallisen talouskehityksen kannalta kriittisen trkeit. Tosiasia on silti sekin, ett pienet valuutat ja varsinkin syrjisiksi reunavaluutoiksi koetut valuutat ja niden prssit heilahtelevat herkimmin kun maailmalla sijoituskohteiden ja valuuttojen suhteellisia tuottonkymi uudelleen arvioidaan, juuri niiden rahoitusmarkkinoiden pienuudesta johtuen. Tst uhasta psimme kerta heitolla eroon siirtymll rahapolitiikassa euro-pohjalle. Siin on rahaliiton ers hyty Suomen kannalta, sen keskeisen tosiasian ohella, ett rahaliitto ankkuroi Suomen talouden vakaan rahanarvon ympristn pysyvll tavalla. Oman rahayksikn korvaaminen riittvn suurella (ts. Euroopan laajuisella) yhteisell valuutalla, jonka vakaudesta on riittvt takeet, eliminoi kotimaisen inflaatiohuolen ja samalla rauhoittaa talouspolitiikan kenties hankalimman ja arvaamattomimman rintaman, nimittin kansainvlistyneen rahatalouden. Mielestni niden tosiasioiden merkityst on vaikea yliarvioida. Suomi sstyi korko-ja valuuttakurssihiriilt kun Venjn rahatalous romahti elokuussa 1998. Kuluvan vuoden levottomuus globaali-valuuttojen markkinoilla ei heijastunut Suomeen maakohtaisena ongelmana. Rahatalouden "pasifisoinnin" myt talous-ja yhteiskuntapolitiikassa voidaan keskitty niihin asioihin, joista politiikassa pitisi olla kysymys ja joiden ksittelyyn poliittinen prosessi luontuu, sen sijaan ett poliittinen energia kulutettaisiin inflaation ja pomaliikkeiden ehkisemiseen ja niiden seurausten korjaamiseen. Rahapolitiikan rintamalinjojen rauhoittaminen ei kuitenkaan tule ilmaiseksi. Jos valitsemme yhden riskin pois, saamme muita riskej tilalle. Rahaliitossa valuuttamarkkinahirit eivt voi kohdata Suomea erikseen, eivtk valuuttamarkkinat ole euron kaltaiselle suurelle valuutalle keskeinen hirin lhde. Sen sijaan rahaliitossa kyll altistumme yhteisen rahapolitiikan mahdollisille virheille, samoin kuin meidn ja muiden maiden mahdollisille finanssipolitiikan virheille. Ja tietenkin olemme eriden kansallisten ratkaisujemme kuten tymarkkinaratkaisujen seurauksille enemmn alttiina kuin ennen -kun emme voi entiseen tapaan paikkailla virhe-arvioita valuuttakurssilla. Tm on kuitenkin aikaisempaa terveempi asetelma. Markkinataloudessa taloudellinen ptksenteko tapahtuu yritysten, kotitalouksien, tyntekijiden ja heidn edustajiensa toimesta. Pttjien tulee itse kohdata omien ptstens seuraukset. EU:n rahaliitossa keskuspankilla tai valtiolla ei yksinkertaisesti ole keinoja tulla apuun korjaamaan eprealistisesti tehtyj ratkaisuja. Viranomainen ei voi suojata pttji niden omien ratkaisujen seurauksilta. Tm on institutionaalisesti terve asetelma. Rahaliitto on ennen kaikkea rahaliitto  ainakin aluksi  ja siksi raha-ja finanssipolitiikan perinteelliset ongelmat ja eponnistumiset olivat rahaliittoa luotaessa keskeisell sijalla. Kukaan ei halua krsi toisen virheist ja laiminlynneist. Jokainen rahaliittoon mukaan menev maa halusi siksi takeet siit, mit raha-ja finanssipolitiikkaa yhdess noudatetaan sitten kun omasta kansallisesta rahapolitiikasta luovutaan. Rahaliiton synnyttjt ovat Maastrichtin sopimukseen yrittneet kirjata raha-ja finanssipolitiikan normit mahdollisimman velvoittavasti. Mielestni on niin, ett sikli kuin takeita ylipns voidaan st, se on Maastrichtissa tehty. Juuri sen takia normit toisaalta nyttvt jykilt, toisaalta antavat vakautta hakeville talouksille, kuten Suomelle, kohtalaiset takeet talouspolitiikan normeista koko alueella. Voidaan tietysti vitt, ett mitkn normit eivt ole takuuvarmasti kaikissa oloissa paineenkestvi. Ehkp niin; kenties 10 vuoden kuluttua voimme paremmin arvioida, saimmeko mit lhdimme hakemaan.  Toistaiseksi on eletty kohtalaisesti sopimusten hengess. Rahapolitiikassa on thdtty hinta-vakauteen, tiukasti mutta ilman kkijyrkkyytt. Valuuttakurssipolitiikassa ei ole sorruttu aktivismiin. Finanssipolitiikka on ollut kautta alueen vakauttamishenkist, mutta alusta alkaen tiukemmasta otteesta olisi nyt taantumassa monelle jsenmaalle ja alueelle kokonaisuutena hyty. Suomessa finanssipolitiikan ote on ollut pttvisen vakauttava, josta Suomelle lankeaa merkittv hyty, julkisen talouden suuremman taantumasietoisuuden kautta. (Tss suhteessa heitot "mallioppilaan" roolista heijastavat talouden todellisuudesta suurta tietmttmyytt. Suuretko tulisivat Suomen avuksi kun taantuma iskee?) *** Kun rahaliiton onnistumisia ja saavutuksia jatkuvasti arvioidaan, on ehk aivan erityisesti korostettava, ett rahaliitto yksin ei ratkaise minkn maan taloudellista tulevaisuutta. Sen tarkoituksena ei ole eik saa olla jsenmaiden talouksien kaikinpuolinen synkronointi ja yhdenmukaistaminen. Talouksien rakenteissa ja instituutioissa on eroja, talouspolitiikan tavoitteissa on eroja, kansalliset poliittiset suhdanteet elvt, jne. Talouskehitys ei tule koskaan olemaan yhdenmukainen kautta alueen. Tt ei kuitenkaan pid luokitella ongelmaksi. Heikosta talouskehityksest ei pid palkita, esim. tulonsiirroilla korkean tyllisyyden ja kasvun mailta. Silloin luotaisiin uusia rakennejykkyyksi entisten plle  vaikka suunnan pitisi olla pinvastainen, talouspolitiikankin kilpailullisuutta edistv. Talouden tehostumista ja joustoa lisv kansallinen politiikka kautta alueen on olennainen edellytys sille, ett sismarkkinat tuovat maksimaalisen hydyn. On suosittava sen suuntaista kansallista politiikkaa siinkin tapauksessa, ett jsenmaiden taloudet kulkevat eri tahdissa. Toimiva poliittinen prosessi ei saa olla integraatiossa rasite; siksi on syyt puhua mys talouspolitiikan kilpailullisuudesta. Globalisoituneessa maailmassa talouskasvu toteutuu jatkuvan rakennemuutoksen kautta. Parhaassa tapauksessa rahaliiton ja sismarkkinoiden yhdistelm tuo Euroopan talouteen uutta potkua, joustoa ja dynamiikkaa, kun valuuttariski on poistunut ja kilpailu asteittain tehostuu sismarkkinoiden myt, jota EU:n laajentuminenkin edistisi merkittvll tavalla. *** Kun rahaliiton jsenyys on niin periaatteellinen ja peruuttamaton ratkaisu, voidaan  edell sanottuun liittyen  kohtuudella kysy, miten se suhtautuu niihin talous-ja yhteiskuntapoliittisiin haasteisiin, jotka nimenomaan Suomi kohtaa keskipitkll ja pitkll thtyksell. Suomen keskeiset haasteet hahmottuvat harvinaisen selvin. Ne ovat rakenteellisia ja yhteiskunta-poliittisia luonteeltaan. Ne kytkeytyvt ikrakenteen nopeaan muuttumiseen, siit johtuvaan elke-ja hoitomenojen vistmttmn kasvuun, ja siksi kysymykseen, miten hyvinvointiyhteiskunnan rahoituspohja turvataan. Varsin yleisen ksityksen mukaan tm edellytt tyllisyysasteen nostamista, suhdanteista riippumatta ja ennen kuin ikrakenteen muutos alkaa vaikuttaa vuosikymmenen puolenvlin jlkeen. Tyllisyysasteen nostaminen osoittautui kovaksi phkinksi hyvienkin suhdanteiden vallitessa. Kuluneen 7 vuoden korkeasuhdanne jtti avoimen tyttmyyden vajaan 10 %:n tasolle, ns. laajemman tyttmyysasteen ollessa reippaasti yli 15 %:ssa. Uskon tyllisyysasteen nostamisen ja hyvinvointipalvelujen turvaamisen osoittautuvan oletettuakin kovemmaksi phkinksi, koska lhtkohdat niden haasteiden kohtaamiseen syntyvt lhivuosina oletettua alhaisemman talouskasvun oloissa, jolloin valtion ja kuntien menopaineet muutenkin mm. tyttmyyden myt kasvavat, julkisen talouden tasapainon ja menovolyymin ollessa jo nyt korkean veroasteen varassa. Tarve veroasteen nostamiseen on siten keskipitkll aikavlill melko realistinen uhka  viittaan valtiovarainministerin vaihtoehtoislaskelmiin  kun taas tyllisyysasteen nostaminen pinvastoin edellyttisi veroasteen laskemista. Nill evill ja ennusteilla julkisen sektorin rappion ehkiseminen, puhumattakaan hyvinvointipalvelujen kohentamisesta, tulee olemaan vaikeata. Kun puhumme tyllisyysasteen nostamisen trkeydest, tarkoitamme oikeastaan, ett tyikisen vestn osalta yhteiskunnan tuen varassa elvn vestn osuuden tulisi merkittvsti supistua. Tm tsmennys auttaa oivaltamaan sen, ett hyvinvointivaltion rahoitusyhtlist tulee viimeistn muutaman vuoden kuluttua vastaan kaksi keskeist todennkisyytt: Jos tymarkkinoiden sek vero-ja tukijrjestelmien muutoksin ei saada tyllisyysastetta merkittvsti korkeammaksi, edess on julkisen sektorin ja sen mukana hyvinvointipalvelujen rappio. Tmn voi sanoa niinkin, ett joko tymarkkinat tyllistvt tai hyvinvointiyhteiskunta rappeutuu. Jos tyllisyysaste ei nouse merkittvsti, joudutaan aikaa myten valitsemaan, rahoitetaanko tyikisten tyttmyytt vai muun vestn hoivamenoja ja julkisia palveluja. *** Mit tekemist nill asioilla on rahaliiton kanssa? Rahaliiton merkitys on siin, ett rakennepoliittisten ja yhteiskuntapoliittisten ratkaisujen etsint rauhoitetaan rahatalouden hiriilt. Suomen vahva ja vakaa talouskehitys 90-luvun alun kriisin jlkeen ovat seurausta vakaushakuisen talouspolitiikan arkkitehtuurin omaksumisesta, johon keskeisesti kuuluu julkisen talouden vakauttaminen suhdannesietoiselle pohjalle, vakaan rahan arvon konsensus ja vakaan rahanarvon mandaatilla varustettu itseninen keskuspankki. EU:n rahaliitto rakennettiin tmn arkkitehtuurin mukaisesti. Suomen intressi on, ettei tm rakennelma talouden ja politiikan myrskyiss murru, koska se tarjoaa kansalliselle rakenne-ja yhteiskuntapolitiikalle suotuisammat puitteet tyllisyys-ja hyvinvointitavoitteiden edistmiseen.

Tuesday 7 May 2002, 12:00 AM On the challenges of economic policy Forecasts for the international economy have become rather optimistic in recent months. Both the United States and Europe are considered to have passed the trough, and growth forecasts, especially in the United States, have been eagerly whipped up for the past year and next year. In addition, the estimates of the future are rather mysnteisis. Nevertheless, it is to be borne in mind that, although confidence indicators have generally developed in a positive way, there is no real increase in investment in the United States than in Europe. The forecast is also justified, even if some setbacks in strengthening growth are to be expected, and despite the fact that the US economy is struggling for a longer period of time due to private sector indebtedness problems and the Japanese economy is recovering steadily. In the euro area, last year's recession was more subdued than in the United States, and the forecasted recovery is also more moderate. The strengthening of the business cycle will start in conditions of higher than forecast prices, which will have an impact on the pace of decline in inflation in the euro area. All in all, as long as wage negotiations in the euro area and are slowly becoming more intense do not create cost pressure, inflation in the euro area will move towards 2% and below over time. In fact, it will never be clear. It is of paramount importance to economic developments in the euro area that inflation and inflation expectations remain low. This is a key objective of the ECB's monetary policy. Only then can monetary stability be secured that will allow the successful conduct of the euro area's fiscal and growth-friendly monetary policy. *** According to economic forecasts, the Finnish economy is emerging from a trough at the turn of last year. However, the economy is still looking for a more solid foundation. As far as investment is concerned, there is no international demand for investment. A return to growth means a return to moderate levels of growth in the summer, not to the highs of the 90s. The international economy is the same; the projected recovery means a return to a moderate growth rate. There are reasons why the growth of the Finnish economy cannot continue to exceed the average growth rate in the euro area in the future. It should also be borne in mind that the growth of the Finnish economy has fluctuated strongly compared to most euro area countries. The financing problems of the public sector would manifest themselves in the creeping deterioration of welfare services, and not in the combination of public sector financing problems. The state's finances should be strengthened, to which it is now sliding from forecast estimates and political debate. *** In order to safeguard the budgetary position, an increase in the employment rate is certainly necessary. Tax increases do not support this objective. The degree of stubbornness does not rise in itself. In all probability, this would require a wide range of measures, of which reducing the tax wedge is only an important but essential means. Therefore, space should be deliberately created for a reduction in the tax burden on tyshs. This will put the central and local government spending economy more centrally in the past. *** Problems of long-term balance in public finances can already be mapped out with concrete and sufficient accuracy. At the same time, government debt in relation to GDP first falls and then rises sharply. This means that the public sector is currently on a steep trajectory. The calculations also show that the longer-correcting pss will stay longer, then they should be carried out more drastically. When drastic changes are not realistic, a delay in correcting the direction of public finances would probably lead to a reduction in government expenditure, i.e. welfare services - other options than would not exist. One might, of course, ask whether there will be a flexibility on the labour market which would really increase the degree of employment by a significant means. Tuesday 7 May 2002, 12:00 AM Talouspolitiikan haasteista Kansainvlisen talouden ennusteet ovat viime kuukausina muuttuneet melko optimistisiksi. Niin Yhdysvalloissa kuin Euroopassa katsotaan aallonpohja ohitetuksi ja etenkin Yhdysvaltain kasvuennusteita on innokkaasti hivutettu ylspin tlle ja ensi vuodelle. Mys eurojrjestelmn piiriss arviot tulevaisuudesta ovat melko mynteisi. On silti pidettv mieless, ett vaikka luottamusindikaattorit ovat yleisesti ottaen kehittyneet mynteisesti, ei viel ole varsinaista nytt investointien kynnistymisest sen enemp Yhdysvalloissa kuin Euroopassa. Mynteinen ennuste on perusteltu, vaikka tilapisi takaiskuja kasvun vahvistamisessa onkin odotettavissa ja siit huolimatta ett, Yhdysvaltojen talous krsii pidemmll aikavlill yksityisen sektorin velkaantumisongelmista ja Japanin talouden toipuminen on epvarmaa. Euroalueella viime vuoden taantuma oli Yhdysvaltoja vaimeampi ja mys ennustettu palautuminen on maltillisempi. Suhdanteiden vahvistuminen alkaa ennustettua korkeampien ljynhintojen oloissa, mik vaikuttaa euroalueen inflaation hidastumistahtiin. Kaiken kaikkiaan, kunhan euroalueella kynniss olevat ja hiljalleen kynnistyvt palkkaneuvottelut eivt aiheuta sissyntyist kustannuspainetta, on euroalueen inflaatio ajan kanssa liikkumassa kohti 2 % ja sen alle. Itsestn selv se ei koskaan ole. Euroalueen talouskehityksen kannalta on ensiarvoisen trket, ett inflaatio ja inflaatio-odotukset pysyvt alhaisina. Tm on silyv EKP:n rahapolitiikan keskeisen tavoitteena. Vain nin voidaan turvata vakaat rahataloudelliset olot, jotka mahdollistavat euroalueen tyllisyytt ja kasvua tukevan rahapolitiikan menestyksellisen harjoittamisen. *** Talousennusteiden mukaan Suomen talous on nousemassa viime vuodenvaihteeseen ajoittuneesta aallonpohjasta. Talous nytt kuitenkin edelleen hakevan tukevampaa pohjaa. Investointien kynnistymisest ei ole toistaiseksi nytt eik kansainvlinen kysynt viel kanna. Suomen Pankin ennusteen mukaan kasvu nopeutuisi asteittain viennin vetmn lhivuosina. Kotitalouksien kulutus ja tyllisyys ovat silyneet Suomessa kasvun taittumisesta huolimatta yllttvnkin vahvoina. Thn ovat vaikuttaneet vakaa tulokehitys ja ehk jossain mrin mys tymarkkinoiden toiminnan parantuminen. Viime vuosien maltillisen palkkakehityksen edut ovat tulleet konkreettisina esiin, kun tyttmyys ei ole noussut niin paljon kuin pelttiin. Yritykset ovat pitneet ammattitaitoisesta tyvoimasta kiinni huolimatta kysynnn hiipumisesta. Kasvun palautuminen tarkoittaa paluuta maltillisille kestvn kasvun tasoille, ei 90-luvun jlkipuoliskon huippulukemiin. Kansainvliseen talouteen ptee sama; ennustettu toipuminen tarkoittaa paluuta maltilliseen kasvuvauhtiin. On syyt lhte siit, ett Suomen talouden kasvu ei jatkossa voi pysyvsti ylitt euro-alueen keskimrist kasvua. Lisksi tulee muistaa, ett Suomen talouden kasvun vaihtelu on ollut voimakasta verrattuna useimpiin euroalueen maihin. Nin tulee varmasti olemaan mys jatkossa. *** Suomessa ennuste tarkoittaa paluuta arkeen valtion ja kuntien taloudessa. Pankin uudessa ennusteessa jouduttiin valtion talouden nkymt arvioimaan kokonaan uudelle pohjalle. Viel viime vuoden syksyll nytti mahdolliselta, ett valtiontaloudessa kyettisiin silyttmn rakenteellinen ylijm , joka olisi pari prosenttia bkt:hen suhteutettuna. Mutta nyt alijm nytt suorastaan todennkiselt. Uudessa ennustelaskelmassa ylijmn silyminen nyttisi edellyttvn, ettei mitn uusia menoja ptet. Talouspoliittisen keskustelun valossa tm on eptodennkist, kun harrastusta nytt olevan niiden poikkeuksellisten verotulojen jakamiseen, joita ei itse asiassa en ole. Nykyisill talousennusteilla ja ennuste-epvarmuuksilla valtiontalous olisi ohjattava ylijmiseksi. Lhivuosien jatkeena on joka tapauksessa alati kasvavat paineet julkiseen menotalouteen. Lhtkohdat ikrakenteen tuomien rahoitusrasitusten kohtaamiselle luodaan tn vuonna ja lhivuosina, jos ne aiotaan luoda. Mit velkaisempana nm ongelmat kohdataan, sit kovemmat menoleikkaukset ja/tai verojen korotukset uhkaavat, kun tulot eivt en riit sek tyikisen vestn tyttmyyden rahoittamiseen ett elkityvn vestn jyrksti kasvaviin elke-ja hoitomenoihin. Vuosi vuodelta lhtkohdat nist haasteista selviytymiseen heikkenevt. Kytnnss julkisen sektorin rahoitusongelmat ilmenisivt hyvinvointipalvelujen hiipivn rappeutumisena, eivtk julkisen sektorin rahoitusongelmien yhtkkisen krjistymisen. Valtion-taloutta olisi vahvistettava siit, mihin se nyt nytt liukuvan ennustearvioista ja poliittisesta debatista ptellen. *** Julkisen talouden rahoitusaseman turvaaminen edellytt varmuudella tyllisyysasteen nostamista. Verojen korotukset eivt tue tt tavoitetta. Tyllisyysaste ei nouse itsestn. Todennkisesti siihen tarvittaisiin monenlaisia toimia, joista verokiilan kaventaminen on vain ers mutta keskeinen keino. Nin ollen tyhn kohdistuvan verotuksen alentamiselle olisi tietoisesti luotava tilaa. Julkisen talouden tasapaino-ja ylijmtavoitteet olisi ymmrrettv "verokiilan kaventamisen jlkeen". Tm saattaa valtion ja kuntien menotalouden entist enemmn avainasemaan. *** Julkisen talouden pitkn aikavlin tasapaino-ongelmia voidaan jo tn pivn konkreettisesti ja riittvll tarkkuudella kartoittaa. Valtiovarainministeri julkisti omat arvionsa viime vuoden toukokuussa. Suomen Pankissa on samanlaisin perusolettamuksin viime kuukausina haarukoitu erityisesti julkisen talouden rahoitusaseman kehityssuuntia. Nm laskelmat kertovat ensinnkin sen, ett suhteellisen mynteisikin perusolettamuksia kytten koko julkinen sektori liukuu alijmiseksi; ensin valtiontalous, sitten yhteenlaskettu julkinen sektori ja sen jlkeen sosiaaliturvarahastot. Voidaan tietysti kysy, mist tulee tymarkkinoille se jousto, joka nostaisi tyllisyysastetta todella merkittvsti. Title: The 4th Nordic Financial Summit: Regional Tactics for Global Integration
text: Governor Matti Vanhala: The 4th Nordic Financial Summit: Regional Tactics for Global Integration . Speech . Friday 13September 2002, 12:00 AM Economic Policy for European Recovery In turbulent times we tend to be overwhelmed by the most recent events and indicators. Let me therefore start by taking stock of the current situation and the outlook, in an effort to put things in perspective. -For years, before 2001, all forecasters talked about the risk of a hard landing of the U.S. economy. It was felt, particularly outside the stock exchanges, that stock prices defied gravity. Over-investment and indebtedness in the corporate sector, about household spending and borrowing on the back of inflated asset prices, etc. were recurrent themes. A hard landing in the U.S. was thought to be onerous, something possibly quite destabilising for the global economy, not only the financial markets. But when the long-awaited correction in the U.S. economy finally appeared, there was an initial sense of shock, followed by a brief spell of wishful thinking (the sharp V). In Europe there was no anticipation of great spillovers. This changed, as forecasts were repeatedly adjusted down. But again, with some encouraging U.S. numbers at the start of this year (2002), optimism about a rapid takeoff returned. Now we are disappointed about the second quarter, and disappointed about what we antici-pate about the third quarter, both for the U.S. and for Europe. Gloom is spreading again. We tend to be overwhelmed by the latest twists and turns in the indicator flow by what economists call noise. Let me therefore offer the following, perhaps equally biased opinion: What we now see unfolding is, at least so far, really a milder version of the hard landing scenario that we originally thought most likely for the U.S. economy. Common sense told us then, and should tell us now, that in any economy, once households and companies get overextended, at some stage confidence dissipates and collective consolidation takes over. We always knew that consolidating balance sheets is a lengthy process, which by definition takes place in a slower than anticipated growth environment. Of course, we have not seen everything yet, but what we have seen so far is not, in terms of past cyclical behaviour in the U.S. and in Europe, quite as dramatic as the hard landing, at least so far, and in view of the "bubble". Real adjustment and balance sheet consolidation go hand in hand. They are needed and necessary, and they take time. These realities we cannot and should not try to eliminate, by means of short-term economic policy tuning or otherwise. Adjustment may be facilitated, perhaps, but it has to take place. All this is obvious. Why, then, state it again? It is because with some frequency there are calls for expansionary macro-economic policy, either fiscal expansion or monetary easing, in order to get the economy to recover. One variation of the theme is the suggestion that macro policy adjustments provide a "signal" that would have an impact on the confidence of consumers and companies, therefore on domestic demand. Signals about what? The jargon of "signalling" has been taken over from a different context, i.e. communicating policy intention or policy nuances to financial markets. What we are dealing with now, in Europe, is real adjustment and structural problems. I must say that I am personally increasingly sceptical about the virtue of such virtual policies. The fact is that macro-economic policies cannot eliminate the need for real adjustment. Not only the U.S., but also and perhaps in particular the European economy, is facing a process of inevitable adjustment. Of course, the deterioration in the outlook for the European economy is to a great extent a reflection and consequence of adjustment in the Unites States, but this is not the whole story; the European economy has serious structural problems of its own. In any case, we can no longer say that the European economy would live a separate life. Europe is not separate from but part of the global economy, with the U.S. economy being the anchor, both in product markets and in money and capital markets. European companies are, so to speak, also part of the Unites States economy directly, not only via trade flows, and, the same has applied for a long time to U.S. corporate involvement in Europe. Looking at trade flows alone gives a misleading impression of separate economies. In other words, adjustment processes in the United States economy become part of Europe's own forecast. But the even more important point is that the European economy is beset by all manner of structural rigidities that limit its growth potential both in and beyond the current phase of the cycle. This being the case, macro-economic signalling and encouragement do not address the issues at hand. Virtual policies are not enough. They are likely to be harmful to the extent that they deflect policy makers and the public away from the structural issues that really are the key and which need to be addressed. Expansionary macro-economic policy makes things worse, if it is a substitute for structural measures, and if it comes on top of missed public sector consolidation opportunities of recent years. For the future, we need stronger public sectors, even if we were not taking into account the ageing of the population, something that of course makes the consolidation requirement even stronger. Confidence in the sustainability of the public sector finances is important. Also for interest rates. Nor should we want to endanger long-term monetary stability by "comforting" households and corporations with literally excessive liquidity liquidity that they do not have any use for and the use of which might in a consolidation phase merely feed into various asset markets or have other undesirable effects. Let me also remind you of the fact that in any developed financial system a central bank has only one interest rate at its disposal, namely its policy rate, not the yield curve nor the credit spreads. In times of diverging credit quality, interest rate policy would not in any case be of much consolation to those companies squeezed by increasing credit spreads. Summing it up: We should not look to fiscal and monetary expansion as a means to help the economy avoid or postpone real adjustment. Accepting the reality of business cycles and the inability of macro policy to compensate for the swings, of course does not mean that Europe would be condemned to inferior economic performance. The recipe is to bring flexibility and strong incentives into a stable macro-economic environment. Global integration deepens all the time, even in the absence of institutional arrangements that may serve to accelerate it, such as the EU, WTO, etc. Knowledge and technology are the fundamental drivers in the background. Economic growth will increasingly take the shape of structural change. The pressures in that direction will in all likelihood intensify. This is a good thing in the long term. (EU enlargement is likely to help.) Higher growth and employment levels will be seen wherever resources, i.e. capital and labour, move easily from low productivity to high productivity sectors, in a continuous never-ending process. As an aside, I should say that this is not equivalent to more insecurity in society, rather the contrary. The European economy is still very compartmentalised. The diversity of institutions, the sheer mass of large differences and small nuances in norms and procedures, and in market access, make an enormous difference. The market is fragmented. Even within the EMU, with a common currency as a unifying factor, we can still observe price differentiation to an amazing extent in product markets. The rigidity of the labour markets is widely acknowledged. Even today, with the monetary union firmly in a place, we can still not speak about a unified financial market; this we shall see only with greater corporate cross-border integration in the financial sector, and with a harmonisation of the legal and institutional framework determining the usability and availability of financial assets and services cross-border. All the challenges of bringing mobility and flexibility into the European economy are well recognised. This is what the Financial Services Action Plan, Risk Capital Action Plan, etc. and perhaps in particular the Lisbon initiative are all about. The Lisbon initiative adopted by the heads of state, as you will be aware, aims at nothing less than transforming the EU into the most dynamic and competitive, knowledge based economy by 2010, capable of an average annual growth rate of 3 % per annum. With the starting point we now have, this is extremely ambitious. Are we making progress? We are making slow progress, in the financial markets and in other areas. But what about mobility and flexibility in the labour markets? Our labour markets are not efficient. An efficient labour market is one that produces a high rate of employment, not the high rate of unemployment that we seem to face as a permanent phenomenon in Europe, regardless of the cyclical situations. Clearly, in the European welfare state context, the so-called labour market partners cannot alone bring about such efficiency in the labour market. The performance of the labour markets is probably more fundamentally determined by the norms and the design of social support systems and by the tax system. Labour market flexibility is both politically and technically a challenging area of policy, precisely because of the link to the design of support systems. Maybe there is no politically correct way to achieve results. Nevertheless, we might bear in mind comparisons between U.S. and European performance also as regards labour markets: Superior U.S. performance in terms of gdp per capita in the 90's is only in part due to more efficient absorption of new technology. Superior U.S. performance also reflects superior absorption of labour.

Tuesday 22 October 2002, 12:00 AM Markkinavetoisella palkanmuodostuksella ty?llisyys yl?s The last two years have once shown how exuberant economic development can be. Two years ago, there was a period of intense economic growth, driven by the US economy and affecting the entire world economy. That boom was also an overachievement. We are now experiencing a period of slower economic growth, which is once framed by the US economy. It is unthinkable that Europe should be able to develop its economic cycle on its own, just as in Finland economic growth could be 'created' on its own accord, in isolation from the environment. The same applies to the object of the seminar: the successes of cities and regions - e.g. Vaasa region until 2015. The development of the regions also depends on the dynamics of general economic development. In my speech, I intend to focus on the conditions for the development of this. It is an unfortunate fact that Finland has a future of slow economic growth. Since the recession of ten years ago, we have a large-scale employment rate of 9% and 16%, depending on the method of measurement. In a context of low growth, we would be able to finance the work and at the same time cope with the massive financial pressure in the public sector caused by the slow growth. It is not possible to promise that we will be able to rise to the challenge with honour. What is certain is that it will require an improvement in the efficiency of the economy in the meantime. As we move to dismantle the problems, it is wise to adopt as a point and a fact that Finland is irrevocably integrated into the world economy and that economic growth is achieved internationally and nationally through constant structural change. Those national economies, or regions where resources (power and labour force) are shifted in a productivity-oriented manner to those sectors and enterprises with higher productivity and profitability, will be more successful. National economies and regions will wither away. The challenges of Finland's economic policy, the ty?tchism and the crisis to which Mr ?sken referred, have created a link of fate for the functioning of the labour market and the financing possibilities of the welfare state. Over the past year, it has been widely acknowledged in the debate on economic policy that the financial problems arising from the ageing of the economy can only be solved in the context of the current much higher employment rate. The first condition for safeguarding the so-called welfare state is therefore to improve the functioning of the labour market so that the level of employment is significant. When the tupo is again very topical, in my speech I am going to touch on the relationship between wage formation and the flexibility required for economic growth and employment in the world of structural change. *** Negotiations on the next few years' collective agreements are about to begin. Wage demands are presented and justified by the increase in productivity in the national economy, which has created new distributions, part of which belongs to wage earners. In the negotiations, careful calculations of productivity development are carefully examined and, on that basis, attempts are made to determine the wage-earning capacity of the national economy. If the agreements are implemented as a comprehensive overall income policy solution, it is expected that the agreed wage increase will be more or less the same for the majority of wage earners in the country. The Finnish labour market is likely to be motivated by a simple desire to promote an increase in the wage gap. However, the argument that the average productivity growth in the national economy must be compensated to the employment sector or company in which they are employed, regardless of productivity developments, has a richer history. It is based on the traditional Scandinavian model of inflation, the so-called inflationary model. EFO model. The idea behind the model was that collective wage increases would lead to declining and poorly profitable companies and industries shifting their workload and the freed-up work power to more profitable, more solvent companies. According to the Ministry, this would be one way of managing the restructuring of the economy and directing the resources of labour to the most productive sector. There are great risks involved in this way of working. Destroying jobs is much easier than creating new ones. It is clear that large wage increases can force firms in difficulty to work. An obstacle to growth may be the small size of the domestic market (telecommunications) or the lack of inputs other than labour (forest industry). As far as the demand for labour force increases in growth sectors, it is not clear that this demand is precisely the problem of the power released from the sectors. Typically, it is typically the case that redundancies in the sectors are primarily directed at the productive workforce, i.e. the people with the weakest adaptation and competitiveness, who are the most difficult to integrate into new sectors and are therefore the most at risk of prolonged employment. In the ty? market, the so-called "market" is born. structural mismatch. However, when the constant change in the structure of the economy requires a constant flow of resources from declining sectors to growing sectors, how should the economy function? An alternative is the management of labour resources through wage flexibility. In a flexible economy, companies compete for labour by offering a salary that is commensurate with their ability to pay. Sectors that are doing well and capable of growing are able to pay higher wages and thus attract the most adaptable and low-income sectors. The growth sectors are getting the power they need, while the declining sectors are slowly losing out and contracting. Resources are moving, but redundancies are not partly needed. The end result is the same as what the same wage standard aims to do, but not what the wage standard aims to do. Another reason why productivity alone does not qualify as a wage norm is that productivity is not the same as profitability. Productivity and increasing productivity are, of course, the successes of an individual company and of the nation as a whole. However, it is only one of the factors affecting the profitability of the company and the correct level of wages (i.e. balancing the demand and supply of the ty?marks). The same is the change in the prices of finished products and the availability of power. With an emphasis on productivity, and a wage norm based on an inflationary norm that is in some way defined, leads to a p?n?h Finland's productivity development in recent years provides an illustrative example. The strong growth in the productivity of the national economy has been a long time on the shoulders of one industry. This industry is the electronics industry, which increased its productivity by about 20% per year in the second half of the last decade. However, in the electronics industry, significant part of productivity growth has typically been channelled into lower prices of finished products, resulting in slower development of income generation and profitability than productivity. The use of productivity growth as a wage norm therefore requires diligence ? at the level of the sector as well as at the level of the economy as a whole. Productivity growth does not adequately reflect the development of the sector's profitability and need for employment power, nor does faster productivity growth in one industry mean that it has accumulated more wage-earning space than in a sector that has been slower to increase its productivity. And finally, ? productivity is basically a job-and-function-specific expression rather than a sector-specific one. The tax wedge is a serious matter. An effective training system is essential in all circumstances, etc. Economic policy is a whole, the parts of which fit together naturally. *** Growing concerns about the continuity and quality of public welfare services have recently been highlighted in public debate. It's easy to share your concerns. Meeting the need for services in a situation where public revenues are constrained by intensifying international tax competition will be a challenge that is not certain to be overcome. Many recent calculations show that the level of employment can only be sufficiently financed by the funds and that the level of service is sufficient if the employment rate can be increased from the current level of just under 68%, to around 75% or more. This is an ambitious goal, but it is achievable. This requires action in many areas of economic and economic policy. Kaikki ehdotukset, tulivat ne milt suunnalta tahansa, on melko laajalla rintamalla tuomittu nykyisiin institutionaalisiin kytntihin ja rooleihin sopimattomina. Kuitenkin ne kaksi haastetta, jotka alussa mrittelin lhtkohdaksi, nimittin ikntyminen ja ympriststmme tuleva, alati voimistuva rakennemuutospakko, ovat molemmat menestyksellisesti kohdattavissa vain joustavamman talouden oloissa. 90-luvun talouspolitiikassa oli valittava palautuminen ja konsolidointi keskeiseksi tinkimttmksi tavoitteeksi. Olemassa olevia rakenteita oli varjeltava ja vahvistettava. Tss onnistuttiin hyvin ja tupolla oli tss keskeinen, arvokas rooli. Miksi tupolla ei voisi olla yht arvokas rooli tymarkkinoiden joustavoittamisessa? *** Kaksi vuotta sitten nytti silt, ett Suomi oli ikntymss merkittvsti vauraampana kansakuntana kuin mik nyt vaikuttaa todennkiselt. Muutos uuden talouden optimismista nykyiseen, moninaisten riskien varjostamaan talouskuvaan on ollut jyrkk. Onko nykytunnelmissa mukana ripaus pessimismikin? Se on mahdollista, mutta mielestni ei kovin todennkist. Jos jotain voidaan tapahtuneesta oppia niin se, ett suunniteltaessa talouden kulurakennetta vuosien ja vuosikymmenien perspektiivill optimistinen perusasenne on syyt unohtaa. Pelivaraa pit jd riittvsti. Toinen lksy on se, ett talouden rakenteet pit saada merkittvsti joustavammiksi. Maailma tulee joka tapauksessa muuttumaan seuraavien vuosikymmenten aikana tavalla, jota emme tnn osaa ennakoida. Mit vhemmll kitkalla Suomi mukautuu ja taloudellisesti hydynt ympristn muutokset, sit paremmat mahdollisuudet on onnistua mys yhteiskuntapoliittisten tavoitteiden saavuttamisessa. Tm edellytt onnistumista monella rintamalla yht aikaa. Taloudellisesti se on mahdollista, jos se osoittautuu poliittisesti mahdolliseksi. Kysymykseen, mill tulo-, vero-ja sosiaalipolitiikan yhdistelmll suomalaisen hyvinvointivaltion kestvyys parhaiten turvattaisiin ja sen tavoitteet tytettisiin, ei kelln voi olla valmista vastausta. Keskustelua on kuitenkin syyt jatkaa avoimin mielin ja tuloshakuisesti.

Title: Speech at seminar on Capital Market Union
text: Board member Olli Rehn: Speech at seminar on Capital Market Union. Helsinki, 27 th March 2017 . Speech . Monday27 March 2017, 2:45PM Olli Rehn Board Member of the Bank of Finland Seminar: Capital Markets Union (CMU) What are the priorities and means? Helsinki, 27 March 2017 WHY CAPITAL MARKETS UNION? RESILIENCE,STABILITY,INVESTMENT Ladies and Gentlemen, I am glad to have the opportunity to comment on Director-General Olivier Guersent's inspiring and important keynote speech. As a former cabinet colleague in the last millennium, I have learnt to know Olivier as a creative and trustworthy colleague, which are indeed the best qualities for a senior policy maker. He played a key role as head of cabinet of Michel Barnier in the EU's response to the crisis in financial regulation and supervision. And the work goes on, as weove heard today. As a result of crisis management often ad hoc, as the instruments of crisis management had to be created from the scratch the Eurozone was able to weather the rock-bottoms of the debt crisis in 2010 12 and, with the ECB's "whatever it takes" pledge in July 2012, return to the path of recovery and growth. Since then, the Eurozone has experienced soon four years of continuous, even though mostly modest growth. One key reason for the slow recovery and the double-dip recession of 2011 12 was the fact the financial repair in Europe was badly delayed compared to the US. Only after the decision to build a banking union in June 2012, to restructure the Spanish banking sector around the same time, to establish the permanent European Stability Mechanism in the fall 2012, and to conduct the Asset Quality Reviews in 2013 14, did the health and resilience of the Eurozone banking sector start to heal properly. As Olivier Blanchard, one of the leading economists of our time, coined it after the crisis, oIt has become a clichz to say that macroeconomic thinking understated the role of financial factors in economic fluctuations.o Thus the health of the financial sector does indeed matter. Most importantly, it matters to the real economy, to our capacity to deliver sustained growth and create jobs. That is why we should be concerned if there are plans to roll back these reforms, or water them down. Capital Markets Union to boostinvestment and bring resilience The Capital Markets Union is designed to broaden the funding of EU businesses, especially SMEs, by increasing market-based finance across borders to companies that are providing jobs and growth. Another rationale for the CMU is that the more diverse the sources of funding are, the more resilient the financial system is to economic shocks. While the goals of the CMU better funding to support jobs and economic growth are easy to agree upon, the means to it are more contentious. Among the many measures, there are some that touch on delicate issues, such as taxation and insolvency proceedings. Compromises are needed, but suboptimal outcomes in order to pursue quick wins should be avoided. The basic goal of the CMU to diversify sources of finance to the real economy in order to support growth and jobs should set the minimum requirements for any outcome. Regulation, supervision and macro-prudential policy The political will for enhanced global coordination in financial regulation seems to be in short supply today. I find it regrettable that only a decade after the financial crisis, many of its lessons seem already forgotten. This has happened despite the fact that it took seven years before the Eurozone GDP again reached the pre-crisis level, and the social and fiscal problems caused by the crisis are still very much felt. The alternative to blind deregulation is continuous reform. The European Commissionos approach to do a built-in review of the financial legislation is much more sensible than one of a regulationdderegulation cycle. The comprehensive review of the financial regulatory framework in the EU is in fact the first global case in point of such built-in review approach. It enables us to adjust the legislation once its effects have become known and apparent, and to do this in a gradual, piecemeal fashion, instead of repealing and replacing entire legal acts. Moreover, such an approach enables us to take into account new developments like FinTech. Advances such as the distributed ledger technology hold great promise, but have also disruptive potential, which must be carefully monitored. For this, the Commission just launched a public consultation on FinTech to gain better understanding of how to develop policy approach towards technological innovation in financial services. One lesson learnt from the financial crisis is the creation of the EUos macro-prudential framework. The crisis taught us that even when individual financial actors in isolation are prudent, the financial system as a whole might be at risk. Developing the macro-prudential approach and some instruments for it are indeed very significant achievements. But we need to review the current setup in the light of the experience gained in implementing some recent macro.prudential decisions. For example in Finland, the macro-prudential authority, the board of the Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority, has decided to take measures to set a floor for risk weights for housing loans in the banks which are using internal risk (IRBA) models. This would increase the amount of capital these banks will have to hold against their housing loans. The preferred legal instrument for this task is Article 458 of the CRR. However, actually using the Article 458 has proven to be a very burdensome process that is not suited for its purpose. Finnish features: obranchificationo and alevel playingfield One particular feature of the Finnish banking system has recently been something called obranchificationo, or increased dependence on foreign branches. Nordea transformed its Finnish subsidiary to a branch in January this year, and Danske has already started organizational restructuring to become a branch by the end of this year. Taken together, these two banks represent ca. 40% of the total deposit and lending volume in Finland, and the overall share of branches would be ca. 50%. This poses major challenges to banking regulation and supervision, which have not been adequately taken into account in the current EU legislation. The review of EU legislation should provide a good opportunity to find ways and means to address this shortcoming. Systemically important branches can play a central role in a countryos financial system and thus for its financial stability, especially if they cover close to 50% of the entire system. This implies that larger powers of the ohosto country supervisor would support the financial stability of host and home countries alike, and reduce the room for regulatory arbitrage. The progress made since 2012 in creating the banking union has meant big strides towards creating a level playing field for the banking and financial industry across the EU, especially in the Eurozone. In our view one should indeed have only a minimum scope for regulatory arbitrage within the EU and globally. For our part, we are neutral to bankso decisions concerning their home country. Any financial institution knows that in Finland we play by the European rules, which are well-known and transparent. However, it is also clear that we lose some of the benefits of banking union, if the bulk of banking services in Finland is provided by banks coming from countries that do not belong to the SSM. Ladies and Gentlemen, According to Aristotle, learning from experience was one of the main virtues. This applies to financial regulation, too. In other words, after what we have gone through in the last 10 years, there can be no factual ground to believe that looser supervision or weaker regulation of the financial and banking sector would lead to stronger growth. Opening up new space for asset bubbles again would not be supportive for sustainable growth. Instead, ensuring financial stability in a preventive way, together with conducting sound monetary and fiscal policy, and carrying out structural reforms, is the best recipe for sustained growth and job creation. That is the recipe we should follow, both in Finland, in Europe and also globally.

Title: Welcome Address to the UEFA Congress
text: Board Member Olli Rehn: Welcome Address to the UEFA Congress, Helsinki, 5 th April 2017. . Speech . Wednesday5 April2017, 10:00 AM Board Member Olli Rehn Bank of Finland Welcome Address to the UEFA Congress, Helsinki, 5 th April 2017. Dear Alexander .eferin, President of UEFA, Dear Gianni Infantino, President of FIFA, Leaders and Delegates of National Associations of UEFA, Ladies and Gentlemen, Welcome to Helsinki! Regards from the Helsinki football stadium. We just had our weekly morning training game of the Eduskunta team, of the Finnish Parliament, and the staff of the Finnish F.A. Thatos a great way to start a working day you are welcome when next time in Helsinki on a Wednesday morning! So I will provide you with some fresh "locker room talk" now. It is a great pleasure for me to welcome and address you on behalf of the Republic of Finland, where we are celebrating the 100th anniversary of our independence. We are truly honored and delighted to host the 41st UEFA Congress the leading decision-making forum in European football in our country in this very special year, and I want to warmly thank the UEFA and its President Alexander .eferin for the decision. The Finnish Football Association turns 110 years old this year. It was one of the civil society organizations that are always essential in sustained nation-building, thus paving the way for independence. Likewise, the Bank of Finland recently celebrated its 200th anniversary, having been founded in 1811, which makes it the 4th oldest central bank in the world. Today, football is by far the largest sport in Finland when measured by the number of active members and players. I am proud of our grassroots, youth academies and football development. It has a major impact on the community spirit and in the personal and civic development of young people, both in this country, all over Europe and globally. Football is larger than "only" a sport. It requires both individual skill and excellent teamwork, which makes it a microcosm of life in general. The social skills and stamina you gain from such team sport are invaluable later in life. Thatos what makes the "chess of green grass" so fascinating. I trust that you, as delegates in this key European football forum, recall your key role and keep this educational and civil society dimension in mind, when developing the world of football further. While money and business aspects are inevitable in any modern sport, not least in football, the community dimension should not disappear from our beloved sport. Ladies and Gentlemen, Football and Europe belong together. It is the most European sport of all. Like for many others, football started to draw my mental map of Europe, and I believe that is the case for many young boys and girls, then and now. In my hometown Mikkeli the local football club organized a European league for Under-11 in its football school. I made my debut in Manchester United in 1968 at the age of six. In following years I played for Tottenham and Benfica, and then captained Real Madrid for two years and finally won the league title in my senior year, before having to retire from the European League at the age of 11. Career-wise, itos been downhill ever since! Your congress is taking place at a moment of big political uncertainty in global and European governance. Geopolitical problems, the refugee crisis, Brexit, the new US administration, and authoritarian tendencies in many countries all these issues overshadow our time and our actions. In these turbulent times that we live today, it is ever more important in the European football body UEFA to recall the core values of the European endeavor. By this I am referring to the rule of law and human dignity. Thatos why ensuring high ethical standards and solid codes of conduct are critical for the future of European football. I trust the proposals today on reforms, openness and transparency meet this call. Thatos at least what we, rank-and.file members of the enterprise, expect from our leaders. Immigration poses another major challenge for everyone in Europe. Here, football can play a positive role in supporting the integration of young immigrants into our societies. I know it from my own experience that a football team can provide an excellent way of getting into new social settings, especially when studying or working abroad. My veteran team in Helsinki, FC Soppa, does its own part in this integration, with more senior and middle-aged immigrants. The campaign "No to racism! No  racismo!" has been very important, and I hope that this will be followed by further actions in terms of guiding the football clubs and youth academies to positively meet this challenge. In the Helsinki football fields I witness a growing number of youngsters of immigrant origin, and I very much welcome that both for societal reasons, and of course to give new dynamism to the game itself! Ladies and Gentlemen, With these words, let me wish you a stimulating and successful 41st UEFA Congress. Enjoy Helsinki and make good decisions, for European football! Title: Opening Keynote at Future Digital Finance Forum
text: Board Member Olli Rehn: Opening Keynote at Future Digital Finance Forum Helsinki 26 Apr 2017 . Speech . Wednesday26 April2017, 9:20AM Slides (/globalassets/fi/media-ja-julkaisut/puheet/documents/170426-olli-rehn-future-digital-finance-forum. . opening-keynote.pptx) (PDF) Olli Rehn, Board Member of the Bank of Finland, Future Digital Finance Forum 2017, Helsinki WHERE DOES FINLAND STAND AND MOVE IN DIGITAL FINANCE? [Slide 1] Ladies and Gentlemen, It is a great pleasure for me to address your conference which focuses on a very topical future issue, digital finance. I find your choice of venue particularly interesting. This building used to be a repair shop for trams. It's a beautiful place and, in a way, a cool setting for a conference about digital finance. We now live in a world where machines, such as trams, are like computers that are fixed, not by mechanical repairs, but by a reboot or a software update. The world around us is becoming digital, and run by software. The financial industry is no different. In fact, the financial industry has all the hallmarks of becoming profoundly disrupted by digital technology. Why? Because financial services are intangible, immaterial, and easily encoded into numbers. Finance is essentially a numbers business, and computers are made for crunching numbers. As everyone here knows, of course, the disruption has already started and is well underway. That is why we are here today. In this opening keynote, I want to say a few words on where Finland stands in digital finance, and where we should be moving, at least from the standpoint of Finland's central bank, the Bank of Finland. This is a special year for us, since Finland, as an independent country, turns 100 years old. But where does Finland stand in the world of digital finance? [Slide 2] Our country has long been at the forefront of digital banking. The first telephone banking service started here as early as 1982. Internet banking was launched already in 1997. Online banking has grown fast and is now used by almost 90% of the population, more than almost anywhere in the world. [Slide 3] We are among the digital world leaders not only in finance and banking, but in most sectors of society. The latest Digital Economy and Society Index, published by the EU, puts us in the top 2 in Europe, ahead of almost all other EU countries. [Slide 4] In one of the dimensions of the index, Digital Public Services or eGovernment, Finland was number one for many years in a row, but this year we were overtaken by our neighbours, Estonia. The best way to regain the top position is to learn from them, so we have started to work together on something called X-Road, which is a central data exchange platform for all eGovernment services. [Slide 5] Another example of innovative eGovernment in Finland is the National Income Register, which is under development, and which will go live in 2019. It's something unique in the whole world, a real time database of all wages and salaries in the country, with restricted access of course. This kind of database makes public services such as benefits and taxation much easier, and it opens up new possibilities for financial services. [Slide 6] So when it comes to digital readiness, innovation, and skills, we have every reason to believe the people in this country can create some of the best digital products and services for the financial industry. We also have a long tradition in banking and finance. The first savings banks started operating in the 1820's and the first insurance companies in the 1870's. The Helsinki Stock Exchange was founded in 1912.The Finnish markka was issued in 1860 and was used until the turn of the millennium, when Finland joined the euro as a founding member. [Slide 7] But the oldest financial institution in Finland is the Bank of Finland, established in 1811. It is the fourth oldest central bank in the world. A central bank is perhaps not always seen as an innovator, but there are actually grounds to say that a central bank also plays an important part in the world of FinTech and digital finance. The traditional responsibilities of a central bank are monetary policy and the issuance of currency. Moreover, the central bank also plays an important role as part of the banking system. First, we are a bank for banks and an operator of market infrastructure. As such, we are constantly participating in the development of faster and better systems that enable the settlement of payments and securities trades across Europe. Second, we act as a catalyst for technological development in the financial industry. We work closely with all players in the industry to facilitate innovation, and support the development of new technologies and services. Third, we are overseers. We have to make sure security requirements adapt to a changing industry, so that the financial market continues to operate reliably and efficiently, not least from the customers' point of view. Fourth, we do macroeconomic research on the impact of digitalization on productivity. And we analyze what kind of new business models are brewing in the banking and financial industry. What about innovations of our own? [Slide 8] The central bank has one consumer product: cash. We issue banknotes, which is still the only legal tender and the most familiar and most trusted form of money to many people. But the use of cash in Finland has been decreasing during the last 15 years. Cash is the only remaining form of money today that is not digital, so many people are now asking: will cash become digital, too? This is something that we at the Bank of Finland, along with many other central banks around the world, are now exploring. Physical cash will probably not completely disappear, but there may be a case for a new form of money, some kind of digital version of legal tender and cash. This question is far from simple, and for now, largely a theoretical one. But it is also a fascinating question, and we are always happy to hear your thoughts and ideas on it. Cooperation is key also in financial and technological innovation. We think the best way to create state-of-the-art financial services is to bring together all players in the industry, as well as new startups, regulators and academics. Policymakers' task is to provide a level playing field and sound platform for fin-tech development. [Slide 9] One example of closer cooperation is the Innovation Help Desk by the Financial Supervisory Authority, Finanssivalvonta. Hopefully it will help small companies better understand regulation and to get started with their business. Don't hesitate to use it! Ladies and Gentlemen, Dear Friends, This conference is another great example and an excellent opportunity to share ideas and experiences. Many thanks to Hub13 for organizing this event. Hopefully there will be more such occasions in the future. Perhaps there could even be room for a more permanent setting, maybe some type of FinTech centre, or digital finance institute, in Finland, who knows? Let's keep the discussion going and the ideas flowing. Thank you! Title: Olli Rehn's speech during a panel discussion
text: Board member Olli Rehn: Reforming Europe is also a matter for the Finns. Speech in the panel discussion. Helsinki, 9.5.2017. . Speech . Tuesday 9 May 2017,2:00PM Olli Rehn, Member of the Board of Directors, Bank of Finland Speech in panel discussion Reforming Europe is also a matter for Finns Europe-psivs 9.5.2017 Eero Waronen's memorial seminar Helsinki THE REFORM OF EUROPE IS ALSO... S A MATTER FOR THE FINNS In the run-up to the year's European elections, many supporters of European integration had time to breathe a sigh of relief at the french election result. Emmanuel Macron's election victory and the election opportunity for France and Europe to reform. But that's by no means a guarantee that it's so ksy. If reforms are not possible, there may be a path of slow stature, which in the next elections would open the way for the ssriike to win and come to power. It is worth wondering why Joschka Fischer, the former German Foreign Minister and veteran of realo green, wrote in his book Epsonened Europe, published a couple of years ago: "If there is a real threat to existentialism in Europe, then the majority of the czech countries will not want to give up the project, not so. The end of Economic and Monetary Union could probably be ruled out in September. The real danger is not its shocking end, but the fading of the foundation of the idea of Europe, the vslish solidarity of the peoples of Europe." Why should it be that the unity of the peoples of Europe and the vitality of the European Union should not be stifled under the burden of crises? Euroscepticism has its roots in the socialism, and the only viable way to overcome it is to bring about a substantial improvement in the level of poverty. For the long term, it is a question of the ability to do things in the Member States, which have the power and responsibility to carry out reforms that are crucial for economic growth and employment. It also applies to France, as does Italy. This applies very well to Finland, which is in the process of correcting the competitiveness of Finnish labour and production, which strengthens the pull of exports and creates jobs. But it is also a question of how well or badly the EU works. That is why the current year has been used to prepare reforms that will help the EU to perform better. In order to tackle the refugee crisis, we need the ability to share the burden and ensure the length of the external borders. Greater cooperation is needed for the security of Europe. It is also a further consolidation of the economic stability of the euro area, despite the significant progress already made in recent years. Germany and France, the founding members of the EU, have a special responsibility. Both have their own strengths. Germany is europe's economic engine, while France is a major producer of safety. Germany, in particular, has a more permanent solution to the refugee crisis, where it needs the help of other Member States. For France d and for Europe as a whole d is, in turn, how the euro area works and is capable of creating the conditions for sustainable growth and greater employment. It is possible to build an entity from elements such as Chamsh, on which the eu reform programme can form. Even in Finland, it is hardly worth lulling yourself into d pels, or hoping, depending on the angle of the d sks angle, d in the mood that the EU would stagnate, and that reforms would not be mobilized in the lshi years. It might be better to start preparing for the eu reform next year 2018. And there are reasons to assume that it will move in the direction of deeper cooperation. In the debate, it is not worthwhile for the Finns to take up hedgehog defence or to be on the sidelines, but to contribute to the way in which the reform of Europe proceeds in the years. What kind of stability union for the euro area would we build? How are the social rights of the tysntekijside safeguarded in the "gig economy"? How do you focus on the energy economy? How will Europe's defence capabilities be developed? How to safeguard human rights and manage the flow of refugees to Europe? These questions are particularly appropriate for reflection on european issues. Europe's cause is also that of the Finns, and it always comes before us. Paremminkin voisi olla hydyllist ryhty valmistautumaan siihen, ett EU:n uudistaminen lhtee kuin lhteekin liikkeelle ensi vuonna 2018. Minklaista euroalueen vakausunionia rakentaisimme? Miten tyntekijiden sosiaaliset oikeudet turvataan "keikkataloudessa"? Miten pstn kestvn energiatalouteen? Title: Book review  Paul De Grauwe, The Limits of the Market
text: Board member Olli Rehn: Book review Paul De Grauwe, The Limits of the Market . Publication . Friday 26May 2017,9:09 AM Member of the Board Olli Rehn Bank of Finland Book review in Helsingin Sanomat Paul De Grauwe, The Limits of the Market. The Pendulum between Government and Market. Oxford University Press, 2017. 192 s. 21.5.2017 According to the old adage, revolutions devour their own children. Similarly, one of Europeos leading economists, Paul De Grauwe, asserts that the market economy will consume itself unless the state, i.e. public power, again imposes limits on markets. He also warns that a nave belief in the state's ability to manage the economy runs the risk of overshooting the mark with a recoil that returns policy to unbridled markets as in the early 1980s. Thus, a tension is created in this oscillating dynamic of market and state power. Belgian native De Grauwe, currently chair in European Political Economy at the London School of Economics, considers the pendulum swing between the market and the state in this small, but weighty, book. He provides a clear case for mixed economies, an economics of balance. De Grauwe distinguishes between two approaches to long-term economic development, the linear and the cyclical. Linear change is embodied in e.g. the theories of Karl Marx, Vladimir Lenin, Karl Polanyi and Joseph Schumpeter. These economists analyse capitalismos development path and transitions to new societal models. In contrast, De Grauwe offers a cyclical interpretation in which the dominant economic ideology shifts periodically. He argues that a critical turning point emerges whenever the dominance of the market or the state becomes so overwhelming that it eliminates the otheros countervailing effect and leads to an unhealthy hegemony over the economy. De Grauwe notes that wide swings between state and market dominance have occurred over the past two centuries. He asks if this oscillation will continue. If it does, the expansion of the market over the last three decades should lead to the state reasserting the dominant role in determining the direction of economic development. De Grauwe compares the Great Depression of the 1930s and the Great Recession of the late 2000s. Both periods saw the state constrain the market and strengthen the role of the public sector in managing the economy. Growth and employment in the global economy, however, recovered significantly faster after the 2008 financial crisis. De Grauwe credits the contribution of economics to this remarkable achievement. The diagnoses of the causes of the financial crisis were largely correct, and the resulting monetary and fiscal stimulus policies implemented with international cooperation helped prevent a deflationary cycle and restore overall demand. His observations are a sound reminder of the importance of economics and why, despite the familiar criticisms of recent years for the inability of economists to predict the financial crisis, we still need the dismal science. De Grauwe provides several examples of the market economy limitations. Income inequality may undermine the legitimacy of the market economy. The herding behaviour of financial markets may lead to instability. Climate change is the result of neglecting economic externalities. An entire chapter is devoted to the debt crisis in the eurozone. It is an updated version of De Grauweos 2011 insightful diagnosis of the darkest moments in the euro crisis, an article that should already be regarded as a modern classic in economics. Tackling the unnatural increases in sovereign interest rates of certain euro countries, he boils the problem down to the constraints of the ECB, due to its perceived mandate, to actively respond to market panics as the lender of last resort. He finds this to be the fundamental casting defect in the eurozone architecture. As an antidote to this original sin of the EMU, De Grauwe argues that the ECB needs to act as the lender of last resort, even if it was never made explicit in the Maastricht treaty. In other words, a central bank must do what a central bank must do: the function of lender of last resort must be carried out in a monetary union, for the sake of financial stability that is essential for sustainable growth and job creation. De Grauweos article responded to the views of many economic policymakers and was presented in an analytically unequivocal manner. Recall ECB President Mario Draghi addressed a London investment conference in July 2012 and said: oThe ECB is ready to do whatever it takes to preserve the euro. And believe me, it will be enough.o With that speech and the subsequent OMT decisions in August-September 2012, the ECB removed the denomination risk of a breakup of eurozone as a factor in market perceptions, and interest rates began to fall. De Grauwe sometimes beats a dead horse in making his case. For example, he repeatedly praises Nordic achievements. Quite rightly, he emphasises the importance of high productivity as a primary source of real-economy competitiveness and prosperity. But this is self-evident when economic policy is otherwise prudent and an economy faces no asymmetric shocks. Where De Grauwe misses somewhat is in his underestimation of the importance of cost competitiveness. As seen in Finlandos structural recession of 2011d2015, even high-productivity countries can suffer a loss of cost competitiveness. Finlandos Competitiveness Pact is helping to restore lost competitiveness of Finnish labour and production, as well as make up for the lost ground caused by the structural recession. Finland is also an example of a pragmatic mixed economy where the amplitude of pendulum swings has for decades been smaller than in most Western industrialized countries. This has been more of a benefit than disadvantage for us. Even with its flaws, De Grauwe's treatment of markets and public policy as a pendulum swing (or swings) afeels more realistic in light of the previous century's empirical experience than most explicatory models based on the linear interpretation. He prescribes greater international policy coordination for dealing with economic problems, a view regrettably not in wide acceptance at the moment. Whatever the case, economists should have no lack of work teasing out the causes and magnitude of future pendulum swings. Olli Rehn (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tagOlli Rehn)

text_original: Johtokunnan jsen Olli Rehn: Suomen tauti ja miten siit selvittiin. Kolumni, Maaseudun Tulevaisuus, 2.6.2017. . Speech . Friday 2June 2017, 3:45 PM Kaksi vuotta on pitk aika politiikassa ja taloudessa. Ilmeisesti mys taloustieteess. Nin kirjoitti nobelisti Paul Krugman otsikolla The Finnish Disease eli Suomen tauti New York Times -lehden blogissaan 1.6.2015: Kannattaa korostaa, miten kerta kaikkiaan surkean huonoa Suomen suoritus talouspolitiikassa on ollut. Miksei Suomi nouse kuopastaan? Velka ei ole ongelma: lainaa saa halvalla. Mutta kaikki on kiinni euron aiheuttamasta pakkopaidasta. Olin vannonut ministerinvalani ja aloittanut ty-ja elinkeinoministeriss pari piv aiemmin. En tarttunut Krugmanin heittoon velkaelvytyksest, mutta se toimi kieltmtt kannustimena kri hihat ja ryhty tihin Suomen talouden nostamiseksi. Siihen tarvittaisiin mrtietoista talouspolitiikkaa ja laajaa yhteistyt tymarkkinoilla. Menneet kaksi vuotta ovat olleet Suomen taloudessa ja tymarkkinoilla vaiherikasta aikaa. Olisivat voineet olla vielkin vaiherikkaampia, mutta onneksi sopu on silynyt. Tnn, kaksi vuotta Krugmanin madonlukujen jlkeen, Suomen talous kasvaa taannoisia ennusteita nopeammin ja uusia typaikkoja syntyy. Itsetyytyvisyyteen ei ole aihetta ja pulmia riitt, mutta pahimman ohi on psty. Kestvn kasvuun on evit, kunhan emme itse mokaa sit ja jatkamme uudistusten tiell. Mik on auttanut kntmn talouden kurssin? Yhdistelm sek ulkoisia ett kotimaisia tekijit. Euroalueen elpyminen, EKP:n kevyt rahapolitiikka ja raaka-aineiden suotuisa hintakehitys ovat tukeneet kasvua. Suomessa talouspolitiikka on lopettanut vapaan pudotuksen ja kovaa maata on saatu jalkojen alle. Kotimainen kysynt ja rakennusinvestoinnit ovat pitneet kasvua yll ja nyt mys viennin veto ja tuotannolliset investoinnit ovat lhteneet liikkeelle ja vahvistavat kasvun pohjaa. Viime vuonna neuvoteltu kilpailukykysopimus on mainettaan parempi vline suomalaisen tyn kilpailukyvyn parantamiseksi. Se on vahvistanut luottamusta. En lhde arvuuttelemaan niiden motiiveja, jotka vhttelevt kikyn merkityst. Mit sopimus merkitsee Suomen taloudelle? Se korjaa kustannuskilpailukykymme noin 4 prosenttiyksikll kauppakumppaneihimme verrattuna yksikktykustannuksilla mitattuna. Suhteessa Ruotsiin ja Saksaan parannus on viel suurempi. Tm kasvattaa tyllisyytt arviolta kymmenill tuhansilla henkilill lhivuosien aikana. Paikallisen sopimisen lisminen on kiky-sopimuksen yksi tavoite. TEM:in yhteistoiminta-asiamiehen, varatuomari Harri Hietala kokoamien tietojen mukaan tyaikapankkia koskevat mrykset otettiin useimmille sellaisille toimialoille, joissa niit ei ennestn ollut. Samoin selviytymislauseke otettiin lhes kaikkiin alakohtaisiin tes/ves.sopimuksiin. Mrykset, joilla alistetaan paikallinen sopiminen liitoille, ovat olleet melko harvinaisia. Nyt nit mryksi poistettiin entisestn. Tehdyill muutoksilla on tymarkkinoilla olennaista merkityst, koska kilpailukykysopimuksen kattavuus on yli 90 prosenttia kaikista palkansaajista. Nyt sovitut laajennukset tyaikapankkien osalta merkitsevt sit, ett tyajan jrjestmisest voidaan meill sopia typaikoilla hyvin laajasti. Tllainen sopiminen mahdollistaa typanoksen kohdentamisen ilman liskustannuksia sellaisiin tyntyteisiin ajankohtiin, jossa sille on tarvetta. Sopiminen auttaa mys ottamaan huomioon tyntekijiden yksillliset tarpeet tyaikajrjestelyiss. Kilpailukykysopimus sislt mys 24 tunnin vuotuisen tyajan pidennyksen. Sopimusteksti ei edellyttnyt sit, ett tst sovittaisiin paikallisesti. Erit merkittvi palvelualoja ja osaa julkisesta sektorista lukuun ottamatta niin kuitenkin toimittiin. Paikallisesti sovittavilla ratkaisuilla voi olla suuri merkitys tuottavuuden ja tyllisyyden parantamisessa, mink vuoksi sit on syyt edist edelleen. Luottamuksen vahvistaminen sek liitto-ett yritystasolla on tsskin avainasemassa. Kiky-sopimus on mys vastausta Krugmanin eurokritiikkiin ja osoittaa, ett suomalainen sopimusyhteiskunta pystyy sopeutumaan rahaliiton oloihin. Jos siihen kyetn jatkossakin, kestv kasvua ja parempaa tyllisyytt on lupa odottaa. Lainaan lopuksi toista eturivin taloustieteilij, joka kiteytt Suomen haasteen nin: Suomalaisia tymarkkinoita tuskin kehitetn vallankumouksen voimin; tytyy toivoa, ett jonkinlainen evoluutio muiden Pohjoismaiden esikuvan suuntaan osoittautuisi Suomessa mahdolliseksi. Tavoitteena voisi olla mrtty palkkakoordinaatio (vientialat palkkajohtajana), yritystasolle hajautettu palkanmuodostus ja nykyist paremmin turvattu tyrauha. Nin toteaa professori Sixten Korkman kirjassaan Vr talouspolitiikkaa, eik liene vrss. Sek Etlan ett PT:n entisen tutkijana hn sit paitsi tuntee Suomen tymarkkinat perin pohjin, ja molemmilta puolilta. Voisiko olla, ett Suomi prj maailmantalouden murroksessa paremmin Korkmanin kuin Krugmanin opeilla? Kirjoittaja on filosofian tohtori ja Suomen Pankin johtokunnan jsen.
