And, as is fitting to remember, the banking activity that began in the voih?? grew strongly in those days. S???banking began as early as the 1820s, but it was not until the second half of the century that the activity grew strongly and began to expand to small localities as well. At that time, the establishment of S???chibanks was strongly linked to local government and local government. For decades, the activities were rather small-scale and even long-term amateurish. But in many cases it was the only financial service available in small towns. From the very beginning, the Sshshchaks profiled themselves as institutions of the broad strata of the people, unlike commercial banks. The S??shbanks were some kind of ty?v?enbanks. For example, according to the first clause of the s???ch bank issued in connection with the establishment of the Lammi S???bank, the bank eet intends to guarantee to persons of all categories of s??ty, especially to employees and servants, to have the s???chns? deposited and interest to be given. ee Lammi's Sshshchbank was founded in the early stages of industrialization in our country, in a strong wave of expansion of banking in 1877. If you wish, you can add a lot of symbolism to the year, because in the same year in Finland you had to abandon the old silver standard and switch to the gold standard, which was then implemented the following year. ?m? marked the modernization of monetary conditions. The gold standard was once the most developed monetary system in the world. The new monetary system will contribute to the integration of Finland into L?nsi-Europe, where the gold standard was already widely used. Until the time of the World Wars, s???chabanks were only open a few hours a week. More often than not, they were attended by key and influential people in the locality, whose p??? activities were normally something completely different. Today, it would be said that the banks were networked. But the lack of a professional staff did not automatically mean incompetence, and certainly not carelessness. Despite individual setbacks, the large-scale s???bank crisis in Finland did not take place until the 1990s. For example, during the shortage period of the 1930s, many commercial banks were in dire straits, but in general the situation of s??chbanks was better. The important role of the S??chbanks was therefore not to finance the large-scale industry that would be formed, but as banks for households and small businesses. They were also capable of expanding monetary economics. In accordance with their original ideology, they promoted the use of financial services. Finland's first bank transfer system began in the 1910s as a project of the S??shbanks, although it was abandoned as early as 1922. In relation to the Czech Republic, the s???banks were the former. Since then, information technology has developed rapidly. Since banking is basically a game of information, a game of numbers, it has had a major impact on the development of the banking sector. Information technology will play a greater role in the financial sector in the future. And, as has been made clear from the speeches made in public, change can also be a threat and a possibility. Today, we are talking about digitalisation. The digitalisation of banks has received a great deal of attention in the light of recent public statements. Digitalisation refers to the wide-ranging and profound use of information technology in financial services, so that business models and consumption patterns change. Financial services are moving more to the web and mobile devices that move with people. In the future, financial services will be used more and more, wherever people move and do business at any given time. This brings both threats and opportunities. For the consumer, one of the most obvious changes brought about by digitalisation is the development of payments. Is it the new s?nn?t of the old game or a completely new game? Payments are still commonplace, but for years now it has been more common to use various payment cards. Payment methods have become additional, as various mobile applications have been introduced alongside card payments and k?teinen. They are already commonplace for the younger generations. Payments from one bank to another are also changing, and have already partly become, real-time. In terms of payment services, banks have also gained competitors from outside the traditional banking sector, from small and large technology companies. The new payment services are also merging with the services in such a way that you hardly notice them. In the largest cities, ordering food at home, stopping or driving a taxi is easily done so that there is no payment transaction at all between the seller and the buyer, but everything happens automatically in the background. This makes financial management more challenging than before, as people can become able to spend money without even real noticing it. The importance of financial literacy is emphasised in a digitalising world. It is forced to respond to the changing reality, and the financial sector is being shaped not only by digitalisation, but also by the harmonisation of legislation in the EU. The effects of the eu's revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2) will begin in Finland over the next few years. The purpose of the directive is to clarify the legal framework for payment so that it is better suited to the digitalising economy. The directive will promote competition in the financial sector and, in that way, the emergence of better services and the creation of lower prices. Consumers are also being advertised with completely new kinds of obvious things, such as bitcoin and other so-called cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin was originally developed as a payment v?line, but its use for the purpose of the payment has become very v?h?ic. At the moment, it seems that bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies are of more interest to people as investments than in payments. However, there are reasons why it is a speculative investment of t?ys. This means that the value of bitcoin is not guaranteed by anyone, and it does not give any actual return, such as dividends or interest. The expected return is based solely on the increase in value, and such investment activities always involve significant risks. Bitcoin's market price has fluctuated very strongly, and the recent rapid price rise points to a classic price bubble similar to tulip mania. Teko?ly and machine learning also play a role in the digitalisation of the financial sector. In the banking sector, teko?ly? has already been applied, for example, to securities trading and, somewhere, to the making of credit securities. Teko?ly will replace many of them, but certainly not all of them. It will make it possible to create new types of financial services in Chechnya that have not previously been available, and which we cannot even imagine. In the last few days, however, we are talking about the same financial services as always, i.e. loans, deposits and payments. The combination of services is hundreds of years old, and knowledge of the financial industry and understanding of customer needs will continue to be the core competence of a banking professional. Banking is at its best when teko?ly and tunne?ly meet each other. Good ladies and gentlemen, The Finnish economy is finally experiencing a period of growth. Our growth rate is currently among the fastest in the euro area. Over the past year, the good news about individual enterprises has been confirmed as growth for the economy as a whole. Growth has broadened from consumption-driven demand to investment and export revival. In the meantime, all tangible investment will increase. From the point of view of the long term, it is important that research and development activities do not take place. The stapleships of Finnish companies are clearly better than before. The existence of banks in finland's small towns has by no means been a matter of v?h?p?chi. The success of the Bank and its activities are always strongly intertwined. Already one of the greatest classics of economics, Joseph Schumpeter, wrote in the 1930s about the economic development of banking. It will not be possible to finance business and household purchases if there are no institutions providing funding. And without investment, there will be no economic development. Modern banking is as old as industrialisation, and it is by no means a coincidence. A well-functioning financial system is a prerequisite for economic development. However, the banking system will not accept the economy and society if it operates inefficiently. Efficiency has been sought in the financial sector through information technology for decades, and digitalisation is bringing new technology, new ways of working and competition in addition to the past. However, S??chbanks have a significant strength that makes it difficult for a technology company or a global financial player relying on digital channels to compete. I mean locality. During its 200-year history, s??shbanks have faced many different forces of change and crisis, but as local actors they can also find their place in the new era. Their continuity is based on the trust that customers have in s??chbanks and trust, as we know, is the basis of everything in banking. Good ladies and gentlemen! Finally, I would like to thank the Lammi S??shbank for the opportunity to participate in the celebration of your bank's landmark event and wish you the best of success, confidence and stability in the future! Wednesday8 November 2017, 7:00 PM Johtokunnan jsen Olli Rehn Suomen Pankki Suomen kasvunkymt ja rahoitusalan haasteet Lammin Sstpankki 140 vuotta, 8.11.2017, Hmeenlinna (pdf) (/globalassets/fi/media-ja-julkaisut/puheet/documents/2017-11-08-lammin-sp-140v-suomen-kasvunakymat. ja-rahoitusalan-haasteet.pdf) SUOMEN KASVUNKYMT JA RAHOITUSALAN HAASTEET Arvoisat lammilaiset, hyvt naiset ja herrat, Kiitn kutsustanne saapua Lammin sstpankin 140-vuotisjuhlille, tnne Hmeen sydmeen. Tllaiset merkkivuodet saavat meidt aina pyshtymn hetkeksi ja miettimn menneiden sukupolvien aikaansaannoksia. Etenkin itsenisyytemme 100-vuotisjuhlavuonna pieni historian muistelu on paikallaan, sellaisenkin historian, joka on vanhempaa kuin Suomen itsenisyys. Tuohon vanhempaan historiaan kuuluu muun muassa sstpankkien toiminnan kynnistyminen. Taloudellisessa mieless Suomen historia on ollut menestystarina. Maamme oli 1800-luvun lopulla Euroopan kyhimpi kolkkia. Vastaperustettu Lammin sstpankki sijaitsi kyhss maassa, jonka teollistuminen oli juuri alkanut. Sittemmin olemme kirineet taloudellisessa kehityksess krjen tuntumaan, jossa olemme pysyneet viimeksi kuluneen vuosikymmenen takaiskuista huolimatta. Elintason nousua on vaikea yksiselitteisesti mitata. Rauhan aikana reaalinen bruttokansantuote henkil kohti on silti vhintnkin tyydyttv elintason mittari, ja tmn mittarin mukaan elintasomme on noussut monikymmenkertaiseksi muutamassa sukupolvessa. Tst voimme hyvll omallatunnolla tuntea pient kansallisylpeyttkin. Aivan ensimmisi sstpankkeja ei Lammin sstpankki ollut, mutta se on suunnilleen yht vanha kuin Suomi kehittyvn kansakuntana ja dynaamisena kansantaloutena. Kun pankkinne perustettiin, Kiven Seitsemn veljest oli uusi, melkein painotuore kirja. Jean Sibelius oli koulupoika, joka vasta muutaman vuoden pst kirjoittaisi nuottiviivoille ensimmiset svellyksens. Kansallisen kulttuurin orastaessa mys moderni elinkeinoelm alkoi muodostua kaskisavujen rinnalle. Sahateollisuus kasvoi. Rautatiet nopeuttivat matkustamista 1860-ja 1870-luvuilta alkaen. Ja, kuten tnn sopii muistaa, lhes tyhjst alkanut pankkitoiminta kasvoi voimakkaasti noina aikoina. Sstpankkitoiminta alkoi jo 1820-luvulla, mutta vasta vuosisadan jlkimmisell puoliskolla toiminta kasvoi voimakkaasti ja alkoi laajeta mys pienille paikkakunnille. Sstpankkien perustaminen oli tuolloin vahvasti sidoksissa paikallishallintoon ja kunnalliseen elmn. Toiminta oli vuosikymmenien ajan melko pienimuotoista ja pitklti harrastelijamaistakin. Mutta se oli useissa tapauksissa ainoa rahoituspalvelu, joka pienill paikkakunnilla oli saatavilla. Alusta alkaen sstpakit profiloituivat laajojen kansankerrosten laitoksiksi, toisin kuin liikepankit. Sstpankit olivat jonkinlaisia tyvenpankkeja. Esimerkiksi Lammin sstpankin perustamisen yhteydess annettujen sntjen ensimmisen pykln mukaan pankki tarkoittaa walmistaa henkilille kaikista styluokista, erittin tymiehille ja palvelioille, saada sstns tallitetuksi ja korkoa antawaksi. Lammin Sstpankki perustettiin maamme teollistumisen alkuvaiheissa, pankkitoiminnan voimakkaassa laajenemisaallossa vuonna 1877. Tst vuosiluvusta voi halutessaan lyt runsaasti symboliikkaa, sill samana vuonna Suomessa ptettiin luopua vanhasta hopeakannasta ja siirty kultakantaan, mik toteutettiinkin sitten seuraavana vuonna. Tm merkitsi rahaolojen modernisoitumista. Kultakanta oli aikanaan maailman kehittynein rahajrjestelm. Uusi rahajrjestelm osaltaan integroi Suomea Lnsi-Eurooppaan, jossa kultakanta oli jo laajasti kytss. Maailmansotien vliseen aikaan saakka sstpankit olivat auki vain muutamia tunteja viikossa. Useimmiten niiss oli mukana paikkakunnan keskeisi ja vaikutusvaltaisia henkilit, joiden ptoimena oli normaalisti jokin aivan muu. Nykyn sanottaisiin, ett pankit olivat verkostoituneita. Mutta ammattimaisen henkilkunnan puute ei automaattisesti tarkoittanut taitamattomuutta, eik varsinkaan varomattomuutta. Yksittisist takaiskuista huolimatta mitn laajamittaista sstpankkikriisi ei Suomessa muodostunut ennen 1990-lukua. Esimerkiksi 1930-luvun pulakaudella monet liikepankit olivat pahoissa vaikeuksissa, mutta yleisesti ottaen sstpankkien tilanne oli parempi. Sstpankkien merkittvin rooli ei siis ollut niinkn muodostuvan suurteollisuuden rahoittamisessa, vaan kotitalouksien ja pienyritysten pankkeina. Ne olivat mys omiaan laajentamaan rahataloutta. Alkuperisen ideologiansa mukaisesti ne edistivt sstvisyytt, mutta samalla ne tulivat edistneeksi rahoituspalveluiden kytt. Suomen ensimminen tilisiirtojrjestelm alkoi 1910-luvulla sstpankkien hankkeena, josta tosin luovuttiin jo 1922. Tsskin suhteessa sstpankit olivat edellkvijit. Tietotekniikka on sen jlkeen kehittynyt nopeasti. Koska pankkitoiminta on pohjimmiltaan tietojenksittely, numeropeli, sill on ollut suuri vaikutus pankkisektorin kehitykseen. Tietotekniikalla tulee olemaan rahoitusalalla tulevaisuudessa yh suurempi merkitys. Ja kuten julkisuudessa esitetyist puheenvuoroista on kynyt selvksi, muutos voi olla samalla sek uhka ett mahdollisuus. Nykyn puhutaan digitalisaatiosta. Pankkien digitalisaatio on saanut osakseen runsaasti huomiota eriden viimeaikaisten julkisten kannanottojen vuoksi. Digitalisaatiolla tarkoitetaan tietotekniikan hydyntmist finanssipalveluissa laaja-alaisesti ja syvllisesti niin, ett liiketoimintamallit ja mys kulutustottumukset muuttuvat. Finanssipalvelut siirtyvt yh enemmn verkkoon ja mobiililaitteisiin, jotka liikkuvat ihmisten mukana. Finanssipalveluja kytetn tulevaisuudessa yh enemmn siell, miss kulloinkin liikutaan ja asioidaan. Tm tuo sek uhkia ett mahdollisuuksia. Kuluttajalle yksi selkeimmin nkyvist digitalisaation tuomista muutoksista on maksamisen kehittyminen. Onko kyseess vanhan pelin uudet snnt vai kokonaan uusi peli? Kteismaksut ovat edelleen tavallisia, mutta jo vuosia sitten erilaisten maksukorttien kyttminen on ollut viel tavallisempaa. Maksutapoja on tullut lis, kun korttimaksamisen ja kteisen rinnalle ovat tulleet erilaiset mobiilisovellukset. Ne ovat jo arkipiv nuoremmille sukupolville. Maksujen vlittminen pankista toiseen on mys muuttumassa, ja on jo osin muuttunut, reaaliaikaiseksi. Maksupalveluissa pankit ovat saaneet kilpailijoita mys perinteisen pankkisektorin ulkopuolelta, nimittin pienist ja suurista teknologiayrityksist. Uudet maksupalvelut mys sulautuvat palveluihin niin, ett niit tuskin huomaa. Suurimmissa kaupungeissa ruuan tilaaminen kotiin, pyskiminen tai taksilla ajaminen tapahtuu tn pivn helposti niin, ett myyjn ja ostajan vlill ei nkyv maksutapahtumaa ole lainkaan, vaan kaikki tapahtuu automaattisesti taustalla. Tm tekee taloudenhallinnasta aiempaa haastavampaa, sill ihminen voi tulla kyttneeksi rahaa edes kunnolla huomaamatta sit. Talouslukutaidon merkitys korostuu digitalisoituvassa maailmassa. Sntelyn on pakko vastata muuttuvaan todellisuuteen, ja finanssialaa muokkaakin digitalisaation rinnalla mys lainsdnnn harmonisointi EU:n alueella. EU:n uudistetun maksupalveludirektiivin (PSD2) vaikutukset alkavat nky Suomessa vhitellen seuraavien vuosien aikana. Direktiivin tarkoitus on selkeytt maksamisen lainsdnt niin, ett se sopii paremmin digitalisoituvaan talouteen. Direktiivi edesauttaa kilpailua rahoitusalalla ja sit kautta parempien palvelujen syntymist ja edullisempien hintojen muodostumista. Kuluttajille mainostetaan mys aivan uudenlaisia ilmiit, kuten bitcoinia ja muita niin kutsuttuja kryptovaluuttoja. Bitcoin on kehitetty alun perin maksamisen vlineeksi, mutta sen kytt thn tarkoitukseen on jnyt hyvin vhiseksi. Tll hetkell vaikuttaa silt, ett bitcoin ja muut kryptovaluutat kiinnostavat ihmisi enemmn sijoituksina kuin maksuvlinein. On kuitenkin syyt pit mieless, ett kyseess on tysin spekulatiivinen sijoituskohde. Tm tarkoittaa sit, ett bitcoinin arvoa ei takaa kukaan, eik se anna mitn varsinaista tuottoa, kuten osinkoa tai korkoa. Tuotto-odotus perustuu pelkstn arvonnousuun, ja sellainen sijoitustoiminta sislt aina merkittvi riskej. Bitcoinin markkinahinta on heilahdellut erittin voimakkaasti, ja viimeaikainen nopea hinnannousu viittaa tulppaanimanian kaltaiseen klassiseen hintakuplaan. Tekoly ja koneoppiminen ovat mys trkess roolissa finanssialan digitalisaatiossa. Tekoly on pankkisektorilla sovellettu jo esimerkiksi arvopaperikauppaan ja jossain mrin luottoptsten tekemiseen. Tekoly tulee korvaamaan monta tytehtv, mutta ei varmasti kaikkia. Sen avulla voidaan ehk luoda tysin uudenlaisia rahoituspalveluita, joita ei aiemmin ole ollut tarjolla, ja joita emme viel osaa edes kuvitella. Viime kdess kyse on kuitenkin samoista rahoituspalveluista kuin aina ennenkin, eli lainoista, talletuksista ja maksamisesta. Tm palvelukombinaatio on satoja vuosia vanha, ja rahoitustoimialan tuntemus ja asiakkaiden tarpeiden ymmrtminen on pankkialan ammattilaisen ydinosaamista jatkossakin. Pankkitoiminta on parhaimmillaan silloin, kun tekoly ja tunnely kohtaavat toisensa. Hyvt naiset ja herrat, Suomen taloudessa eletn vihdoin kasvun aikaa. Kasvuvauhtimme on tll hetkell euroalueen nopeimpien joukossa. Kuluneen vuoden aikana yksittisi yrityksi koskevat hyvt uutiset ovat vahvistuneet koko talouden kasvuksi. Kasvu on laaja-alaistunut kulutusvetoisesta kysynnst mys investointeihin ja viennin virkoamiseen. Tll hetkell kaikki aineelliset investoinnit kasvavat. Pitkn aikavlin kannalta on trke, ettei tutkimus-ja kehitystoiminta en vhene. Suomalaisten yritysten nkymt ovat aiempaa selvsti paremmat. Pankkien toimiminen Suomen pienillkin paikkakunnilla ei suinkaan ole ollut vhptinen asia. Pankin ja sen toimintaympristn menestys ovat aina voimakkaasti toisiinsa kietoutuneet. Jo yksi taloustieteiden suurimmista klassikoista, Joseph Schumpeter, kirjoitti 1930-luvulla pankkitoiminnan vlttmttmyydest taloudelliselle kehitykselle. Elinkeinoelmn ja kotitalouksien trkeit hankintoja ei pystyt rahoittamaan, jos ei ole rahoitusta tarjoavia instituutioita. Ja ilman investointeja ei ole taloudellista kehityst. Moderni pankkitoiminta on yht vanha kuin teollistuminen, eik kyseess suinkaan ole sattuma. Toimiva rahoitusjrjestelm on vlttmtn edellytys taloudelliselle kehitykselle. Pankkijrjestelm ei kuitenkaan hydyt taloutta ja yhteiskuntaa, jos se toimii tehottomasti. Tehokkuutta on haettu rahoitusalalla tietotekniikan avulla jo vuosikymmeni, ja digitalisaatio tuo sit entisestn lis uuden teknologian, uusien toimintatapojen ja lisntyvn kilpailun myt. Sstpankeilla on kuitenkin merkittv vahvuus, jota vastaan digitaalisiin kanaviin turvautuvan teknologiayrityksen tai globaalin finanssialan toimijan on vaikea kilpailla. Tarkoitan paikallisuutta. Lhes 200-vuotisen historiansa aikana sstpankit ovat kohdanneet monta eri muutosvoimaa ja kriisikin, mutta paikallisina toimijoina ne voivat lyt paikkansa mys uudella aikakaudella. Niiden jatkuvuus perustuu siihen luottamukseen, joka asiakkailla on sstpankkeja kohtaan ja luottamus, kuten tiedmme, on pankkitoiminnassa kaiken perusta. Hyvt naiset ja herrat! Viel lopuksi kiitn Lammin sstpankkia mahdollisuudesta osallistua perinteikkn pankkinne merkkipivn viettoon ja toivotan parhainta menestyst, luottamusta ja vakautta jatkossakin! Title: Digital transformation in the financial industry: what's good for the society?
text: Olli Rehn: Digital transformation in the Financial industry: what's good for the society? FIN-FSA's annual conference. Helsinki, 22 November 2017. . Speech . Wednesday22 November 2017, 9:15AM Olli Rehn Member of the Board of Bank of Finland Chair of the Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority (FIN-FSA) FIN-FSAos annual seminar on financial services Helsinki, 22 November 2017 (Presentation PDF (/globalassets/fi/media-ja-julkaisut/puheet/documents/2017-11-22-fin-fsa-digital. transformation-in-the-financial-industry.pdf)) Digitaltransformation in the financial industry: whatos good for thesociety? Ladies and Gentlemen, Welcome also on my behalf to the financial services seminar of Finanssivalvonta (Fiva), the Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority. This time our over-arching subject is the digital transformation in the financial industry, which I believe is about as topical a theme as it can get in this field. We are not at Fiva however taking purely a technology-or institution-driven view. Instead, we want to look at the digital transformation in the financial industry from the citizenso point of view, i.e. from the standpoint of what is good for the society and for the citizen, be she a consumer, client or investor. Today, there is much excitement and even hype around e.g. cryptocurrencies and initial coin offerings that resembles at least for a pre-middle-aged chap like me the boom period of the new economy around the turn of the millennium. Therefore, it is of paramount importance to try to identify what is real and in turn what is hype in the digital transformation of the financial industry. I will aim at doing precisely that today, based on the work done by the economists, regulators and other experts in the Bank of Finland and the Finnish FSA. I will divide the relevant issues and developments in three categories: (1) those that clearly increase societal welfare and should be benefitted from, such as mobile and real-time payments -as long as we take care of enhancing the financial literacy required in this brave or grave new world; (2) those that should be watched, or even prevented, such as booms and busts related to the cryptocurrencies and initial coin offerings; and (3) those that could and probably should be further developed, such as the blockchain or distributed ledger technology, even if for now the central banks are developing their operations by other means, such as the introduction of new systems enabling real-time payments, like the TIPS and T2S. Before dwelling deeper into these issues, let us look at how digitalization is brewing new business models and changing consumer behaviour. Slide 2:Digitalisation creates new business models Digitalisation is perhaps the single most significant force for change in the financial sector; the other two are regulation and consumer behaviour. This is creating a completely new competitive environment for the sector. Financial services are increasingly shifting online and to mobile devices carried by their owners. In the future, they will be increasingly used wherever and whenever business is done, 24/7. In the coming years, we will see many agile FinTech companies enter the market. Tens of FinTech start-ups have already entered the market with operating models different from incumbents. At the same time global big-tech companies [called GAFA: Google, Apple, Facebook, Amazon] are enlarging their foothold to new business areas, including payments. Regulation is the second driver. The EUos revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2) will clarify payment legislation so that it is better suited to a digitalising economy. The Directive will promote competition in the financial sector, and thereby the creation of better services and formation of lower prices. It will open the market to third parties, i.e. payment initiation service providers and account information service providers. Banks are obliged to open their interfaces to these service providers. Its effects will gradually be visible in Finland in the coming years. This change is probably comparable to what happened in the telecom markets in the early 2000s. In banking, this means in practice that the user experience can be provided by some party other than the bank itself. Consumer behaviouris the third factor shaping how financial services will look in 2022. Consumers are always online. They seek information from various sources, including social media. This puts the consumer at the core of the development of financial services. Future success stories are likely to be those that provide the best user experience and value for the consumer. Slide 3: The playing field of payments is changing: is it an old game with new rules oran entirely new game? Where is the digital transformation currently most visible to the consumer? In the field of payments. As this business field is rapidly changing, we can ask, is it an old game with new rules or an entirely new game? More ways to pay have been born, as various mobile applications have emerged alongside card payment and cash. Some examples of these are the instant payment systems Siirto and MobilePay, and the service launch by ST1 Finance. The latter is a company originating from an industry other than financial services and is proof of the blurring of industry boundaries. We have also seen international tech giants, such as Apple, Samsung and Alipay, entering the Finnish payments market. All this might be just the beginning. In the coming years we are likely to see many new payment services. These new services will not be offered by incumbent actors, but also by FinTech companies. Some of the new services may also be provided by actors that we have not yet seen on the payments playing field. However these companies may be well known on their current playing field, such as retail trade and e-commerce. All of these new payment services that we are going to see have three things in common. First of all, they are real.time. Money is transferred from one person to another in seconds. Secondly, there will be fragmentation. Consumers are using several methods of payment: just as they are now using for communication phone calls, text messages, e-mail, Whatsapp, Skype, Snapchat etc. Thirdly, payments will be seamless. They will be usable in a simple way, for example by confirming payments with fingerprints or facial recognition. The payment action is disappearing from the foreground and becoming an integral part of the customer experience. Slide 4: Importance of payments for Finnish banking sector What is an opportunity for the consumer, looks like a challenge to a banker. Let me illustrate the importance of payments for the Finnish banking sector. The figures that I am presenting are calculated on the basis of published annual financial statements. In 2016, the net income from payments in Finland was a little over 0.5 Billion euro. In 2016, payments constituted 8 percent of total income and 19 percent of operating profit. These figures show that payments are profitable business for banks and make up a significant share of their revenue at the moment. I am not going to make any speculations on the share of payment transactions that will in the coming years be carried out by actors other than incumbent banks. I do, however, want to demonstrate what it would mean if half of the income received from payments today were to vanish while business models remain as they are. This would mean a four percent loss in total income. But as payments are a very profitable business area, it would require a 10 percent increase in net interest income to compensate for the losses. It would be quite an uphill struggle to compensate the losses with current business models, taking into account the current interest levels. This is certainly thought-provoking. Slide 5: Importance of the FinTech ecosystem Finland has the potential to be a leader in this transformation. We have strong skills in digital technology and financial services. We adopted digital banking already in the late 1990s. Next, Finland can be a FinTech nation. FinTechs are key drivers of change and can offer consumers enhanced user experience through innovative services. They have agile product development processes and can quickly develop new services for their customers. We have already seen banks working with the FinTech ecosystem. Partnerships between FinTechs and incumbents are being built. I encourage all of you to engage more in this type of cooperation. Fiva is supporting this work e.g. through our Innovation Help-Desk for FinTech companies, which I encourage you to use in case you work in the field. Cooperation across national borders is important. The Nordic region is the second largest FinTech community in Europe [after the UK]. In the past two years all Nordics have established several Fintech hubs and initiatives. Last week a cooperation agreement was signed between Nordic Fintech initiatives for sharing knowledge and helping FinTech start-ups to scale. I am glad that Finnish universities have become active in both Fintech-related teaching and research. Let me give you some concrete examples: Aalto University has begun its research and teaching in FinTech with a seminar series this autumn; Hanken together with Arcada are offering courses in FinTech; the University of Applied Sciences in Oulu is holding an AppLab programme to train future Fintech professionals. I would also encourage Finnish FinTech start-ups to think globally. Last week the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) organised its FinTech festival. This is the largest FinTech event in the world, with 25 000 people from all over the world visiting. Sweden and Denmark both took part in the event with a delegation between 20 and 30 people. The delegations consisted of FinTech start-ups, representatives of FinTech hubs, regulators and organizations that are helping companies grow internationally. Slide 6: Nordeaos relocation banking sector 400% of GDP There is another factor of positive dynamism in the Finnish financial industry. That is Nordeaos recent decision to relocate its headquarters and balance sheet to Helsinki. This decision, which Nordea obviously took for its own reasons, is a vote of confidence for the Eurozone banking union, and also strengthens the future perspectives of Finnish financial industry, and FinTechs. While Nordeaos balance sheet has been evaluated as healthy in recent stress tests, we naturally analyzed the risks it could carry for Finland. The banking sector will soon be 400% of Finnish GDP, well above the EU average. Our conclusion is that the risks to our country are manageable, thanks to the rules and tools of the banking union. In a possible crisis, any systemically important financial institution, like Nordea, would in the Eurozone be dealt with by the resolution and bail-in rules of the banking union. Moreover, completing the banking union with a common deposit guarantee scheme would be important for a country like Finland with a large banking sector. And needless to say, Nordeaos relocation will mean that new prudential resources are needed for the Fin-FSA, which we are taking care of. Slide 7:Importance of digital skills and financial literacy Digitalisation, in general and in the financial industry, creates the need for a new type of skills. For instance, every citizen needs at least the basic knowledge of cyber security and data protection. People need to understand the importance of protecting their devices and identifying attempts at online fraud [such as phishing, when a website that resembles a real service provider is trying to get the users' credentials to access their accounts]. Citizens should also understand their rights as data subjects. It will become more common to use one's personal data when paying for the use of financial services. Families, schools, authorities and financial service providers have an important role in increasing public awareness of these issues. Account transfers are gradually changing to real-time. Payments are also disappearing into the background and becoming part of the customer experience. This makes financial management more challenging for households and underlines the need to promote financial literacy. Adequate financial literacy skills are a necessity in the digital age. Financial literacy is nowadays promoted by many different parties: financial service providers, authorities and third sector players. It is of the utmost importance that these different parties cooperate. This is the only way to ensure adequate financial literacy throughout the whole of society. We also see that a positive credit register would be a useful tool in financial management and would help prevent householdso over-indebtedness. Slide 8:ICOs and cryptocurrencies price bubble Cryptocurrencies are digital payment instruments that circulate from one holder to another without a centralised accounting system. Today the most known cryptocurrency among consumers is Bitcoin. It was originally developed as a means of payment, but its use for this purpose is very limited. Currently, it appears that bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies interest people more as investments rather than as means of payment. They are purely speculative investment objects. The value of a bitcoin is not guaranteed by anyone, nor does it give any actual return, such as a dividend or interest. Any return is based solely on the expectation that the cryptocurrency can be sold later at a higher price. Such investment always involves major risks. The European Banking Authority (EBA) has already in December 2013 issued a warning on a series of risks deriving from buying, holding or trading cryptocurrencies. It is extremely important to acknowledge that consumers are not protected through regulation when using cryptocurrencies as a means of payment and may be at risk of losing their money. An ICO [Initial coin offering] is a way of collecting risk financing. This refers to the pre-sale of a new cryptocurrency and is reminiscent of crowdfunding. From the perspective of those providing finance, an ICO is a similar kind of speculative investment to existing cryptocurrencies. The European Securities Market Authority issued a warning on ICOs in early November to highlight ICO risks for investors and firms. Today, the Fin-FSA issued a warning on investing in cryptocurrencies and ICOs. The warning is aimed at enhancing consumer awareness of the risks. At the moment, the rise in the price levels of cryptocurrencies [like bitcoin in the picture] suggests there is a visible price bubble that resembles the historical Tulip Mania. Slide 9: Blockchain vs. centralised payment systems The technology underlying cryptocurrencies, called blockchain technology or distributed ledger, has potential for new applications, and versions of the technology have been developed that are more suitable for the financial sectoros use. Currently, promising financial sector areas of application include interbank international credit transfers and securities clearing and settlement operations. They are developed mainly by private actors and are good examples of the diversity of digitalization development in the financial sector. At the Bank of Finland we have, together with other Eurosystem central banks, studied distributed ledger technology. In its present form, it does not yet meet the requirements required by the systems of central bank services. Central bank systems are being developed by other means, however, such as the introduction of new functions and systems enabling real-time payments (TIPS & T2S) this year and next. For the future, it is important that systems are compatible, and that they are standardized and harmonized. Slide 10:Summary Ladies and Gentlemen, Let me conclude. Finland has sound, realistic chances of becoming a winner in the currently ongoing and accelerating digital transformation in the financial industry. If we proceed wisely, this can be turned to the benefit of the whole society. This calls for encouraging innovation and building a flourishing FinTech ecosystem to Finland. And it calls for a dynamic and competitive financial industry that can turn the innovations to products and services that genuinely enhance our economic and social welfare. But it also calls for confidence and trust, rock-solid financial stability and adequate consumer protection. This, in turn, is the core business of the Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority. We aim at ensuring the right balance between innovation and technology, on one hand, and customer protection and financial stability, on the other hand. And as financial services are going more online, there is a growing need for digital skills and true financial literacy. Here, cooperation between all key players is most important. I trust the financial industry and other stakeholders share these worthy goals, and we can work well together in reaching them. In this spirit, let me wish you a stimulating, productive conference and most interesting discussions today. Thank you! Olli Rehn:Digitaltransformation in the financial industry: what's goodfor the society?FIN-FSA's annual conference,22 November 2017. After a loeng period of dsmpad tillvsxt, a turnaround has taken place and right now it is good for the economy in Finland. The viability of future developments depends on global economic developments, but also on national decisions. The Vsrld economy and the euro area The outlook for the global economy has been broadly met and the risks of a renewed trend have diminished. At the same time, however, it is important to note that there is a great deal of uncertainty about the vsrld economy, the economic importance of which is difficult to pray for. These are the risks of Catalonia, the polarisation of politics and the risk of protectionism in the US and Europe, NAFTA and the risk of conflict (including North Korea's nuclear weapons programme). The financial impact of the euro area has been further stifled. In its macroeconomic statements in September, the ECB made a much larger impact in comparison with the fsregoeende oer. The economic growth of the euro area is now more divided across sectors and sectors. Inflation developments in the euro area sr alltjsmt dsmpad. Underlying inflation remains low. The ECB's monetary policy remains accommodative: central bank balances have remained close to zero for several years, banks have been allocated long-term funding (TLTROs) and substantial securities deposits were launched in January 2015 (the Eurosystem's balance sheet total has grown from 1,000 billion to around 4,200 billion in the space of 10 billion). At its meeting in October, the ECB decided to add nine months to the programme. Net access will continue from January 2018 until the end of September 2018 at a rate of EUR 30 billion per month. Net access will continue until the ECB considers that inflation has returned to a level in line with the objective. All this means that the monetary policy of the euro area will continue with an expansionary baseline and the euro area will be fairly loega snnu quite lsnge. Euro-reform and banking union The euro area is now in a strong way, and it is important to continue the reform process. Most importantly, it is to complement the work on the banking union. This includes a resolution fund and a common guarantee. For Finland, it is particularly important to end the banking union, because in the near future we will have a large banking sector compared to GDP, following Nordea's move to Helsinki. Nordea's decision is a confidence declaration on the euro area's banking union, and its stable business relationships. Economic outlook for Finland Right now, the economy is doing well in Finland: the economy is behind us and the economy has also taken hold of the oerjanuary. The most positive feature of the recent increase is that exports have also picked up. In comparison with the svvriga euroomroedet sr tillvsxten in Finland rstt soe god. Tillvsxten svertrsffade Germany and euroomroedet d and is located nsra Sweden. In Finland, the economic upturn came late d the svriga lsndernas fsrsproeng sr alltjsmt stor. Exports have picked up well and exports were just over 15% below the first half. Finland's exports of goods are on a broad basis regardless of whether the development by country or by product is taken into account. It was precisely the weak exports and decline in industry that formed the most serious bottlenecks in Finland's economy during the economic recession. Now these have also been raised. Thanks to the competitiveness agreement, labour costs are rising in Finland in finland, which is boosting exports and investment. Cost competitiveness has been fsrbsttrats noegot, but a lot of work oeterstoer. Dsrfsr sr it is important to keep a line on the labour market. The pace of development should thus be more similar to that of competitors also in the oeren forwards. When new collective agreements are concluded, hsnsyn is taken to ensure that the work environment is alljsmt sr hsg. The recent agreement between the technology industry and the industrial sector is in principle an important evolutionary step towards local agreements d hope it sr soe in practice also! Employment and the reduction in employment have been close to the economic situation. According to a positive interpretation, the low level of employment so far depends on the fact that companies want to improve their business before investing and recruiting. According to a more negative interpretation, the small market situation is a result of major matching problems, as companies do not find skilled labour. Economic research shows that both interpretations have weight and significance for the loengsam oeterhsmtningen. From a commonpolitical point of view, it makes sense to find solutions for problems, for the sake of employment. Fsrutssttningar fsr ekonomisk tillvsxt d structural issues In the late 1800s, Finland was a poor country compared to the svriga vsstlsnderna. r In 1860, Finland's gross domestic product was only around half of Germany's and three parts of Sweden's GDP. During the 1900s, Finland caught up with the svriga vsst (European) Lsnders. In the 2010s, Finland's stsllning oeter fsrssmrats noegot. However, productivity growth in recent years has stagnated in Finland, partly due to structural change, which is reflected, among other things, in the shrinking of the productive sectors (electrical and electronics industry, forest industry), while the low-productivity sectors (service sectors) have grown. But now investment is shifting on a broad front. The increased investment in machinery and equipment is sr glsdjande, as it leads to higher capital to thesxt, which reduces the future production potential. As is well known, the sxten sr vslkommen, because, as is well known, it is a gateway to new innovations and thus paves the way for technological development and contributes to productivity. Given the economic growth, the development of labour input in Finland does not look promising. As the population of working people is shrinking, it is becoming increasingly important for the financing of today's vslfsrd state that a larger part of this part of the population should be transferred to the labour market. However, the employment rate in Finland s is significantly higher than the Nordic countries: 69% compared to 75%. The chronic imbalance in public finances has led to a sharp increase in public debt. In recent times, it has been difficult to slow down expenditure not only because of the increased expenditure on social security, but also because of the retirement of the large oerkulls and the rising pension expenditure. Only in the last few years, spending has shown signs of a slowdown. In the end The risk of economic development has become better, and Finland's economy is experiencing major economic challenges. I believe that it is particularly important to maintain employment and to reduce structural and youth employment. This is also an extremely important social issue. It is important to improve the labour market and fiscal policy. The Competitiveness Pact stabilised the labour market for the world, and is now helping to improve the competitiveness of Finnish labour and production in the world market. This sr good d but snnu more behsvs. Labour market reforms are of crucial importance, as the population ages and the labour market is changing rapidly: we must improve labour force and develop the 'Finlsndian model' d local agreements. Ladies and gentlemen, In order for us in Finland to be able to update the pace of oeterhsmtnings and the fsrutssttningar for economic growth in the future, the following factors are important, among other things: to improve know-how and innovation activity, to continue with the liberalisation of the domestic goods and services market, and to curb public sector debt." If we succeed in this, Finland's economy will be strong, sven in a Nordic and a European perspective. Tack fsr er uppmsrksamhet! P sitt sammantrde i oktober beslutade ECB-rdet frlnga tillgngskpsprogrammet med ytterligare nio mnader. Nettotillgngskpen fortstter frn januari 2018 fram till slutet av september 2018 i en takt p 30 miljarder euro per mnad. Nettotillgngskpen kommer att fortstta till dess att ECB-rdet anser att inflationen varaktigt har stigit tillbaka till en niv i linje med mlet. Enligt ECB-rdets kommunikation om framtidsorienteringen ("forward guidance"), ska rntehjningar inledas frst efter att nettokpen har avslutats. Allt detta betyder att euroomrdets penningpolitik kommer att fortstta med en expansiv baslinje och lnerntorna kommer att frbli lga nnu ganska lnge. Euroomrdets reform och bankunionen ven om euroomrdet vxer kraftigt nu, r det viktigt att fortstta reformarbetet. Mest vsentligt r det att komplettera arbetet med bankunionen. Ekonomiska utsikter fr Finland Just nu gr det bra fr ekonomin i Finland: lgkonjunkturen ligger bakom oss och tillvxten har terhmtat sig i brjan av ret. Det mest positiva inslaget i tillvxten under den senaste tiden r att ocks exporten har tagit fart. I jmfrelse med det vriga euroomrdet r tillvxten i Finland rtt s god. Exporten har tagit bra fart och exportkningen var drygt 15 % under frsta halvret. Finlands varuexport vxer p bred bas oberoende om man ser till utvecklingen efter land eller efter vara. Det var just den svaga exporten och nedgngen inom industrin som bildade de svraste flaskhalsarna i Finlands ekonomi under den ekonomiska recessionen. Nu har ocks dessa vnt upp. Tack vare frra rets konkurrenskraftsavtal stiger arbetskostnaderna i r lngsammare i Finland n i vra konkurrentlnder, vilket stder exporten och investeringar. Kostnadskonkurrenskraften har frbttrats ngot, men mycket arbete terstr. Drfr r det viktigt att hlla linjen p arbetsmarknaden. Lneutvecklingstakten borde slunda vara lngsammare n i konkurrentlnderna ocks under ren framver. Nr nya kollektivavtal sluts, br hnsyn tas till att arbetslsheten alltjmt r hg. Det nyligen ingngna avtalet mellan teknologiindustrin och industrifrbundet utgr i princip ett viktigt evolutionrt steg i riktning mot lokala avtal  hoppas det r s i praktiken ocks! Sysselsttningskningen och nedgngen i arbetslsheten har varit lngsam i frhllande till den ekonomiska tillvxten. Enligt en positiv tolkning beror den lngsamma terhmtningen av sysselsttningen hittills p att fretagen frst vill frbttra sin lnsamhet innan de brjar investera och rekrytera. Enligt en negativare tolkning r den lngsamma terhmtningen av arbetsmarknaden en fljd av stora matchningsproblem, d fretagen inte hittar yrkeskunnig arbetskraft. Ekonomisk forskning visar att bde tolkningarna har vikt och betydelse fr den lngsamma terhmtningen. Frn samhllspolitisk synvinkel r det drfr logiskt att hitta lsningar fr bda problem, fr sysselsttningens skull. Frutsttningar fr ekonomisk tillvxt  strukturella frgor I slutet 1800-talet var Finland ett fattigt land jmfrt med de vriga vstlnderna. r 1860 var Finlands bruttonationalprodukt endast kring hlften av Tysklands och tre fjrdedelar av Sveriges BNP. Under 1900-talet kom Finland i kapp de vriga vst (europeiska) lnderna. P 2010-talet har Finlands stllning ter frsmrats ngot. Produktivitetsutvecklingen de senaste ren har dock stagnerat i Finland, delvis p grund av strukturomvandlingen, som bland annat tar sig uttryck i att de hgproduktiva sektorerna (el-och elektronikindustrin, skogsindustrin) har krympt, medan de lgproduktiva sektorerna (tjnstesektorerna) har vuxit. Men nu vxer investeringarna p bred front. De kade investeringarna i maskiner och utrustning r gldjande, eftersom de leder till strre kapitaltillvxt, vilket hjer den framtida produktionspotentialen. Med tanke p den ekonomiska tillvxten ser inte utvecklingen av arbetsinsatsen i Finland lovande ut. Men sysselsttningsgraden i Finland r betydligt lgre n i vriga Norden: 69 % mot 75 %. Den kroniska obalansen i de offentliga finanserna har lett till en kraftig kning av den offentliga skulden. Under senare tid har det varit svrt att bromsa utgiftskningen inte bara p grund av de kade utgifterna fr den sociala tryggheten utan ocks till fljd av pensioneringen av de stora rskullarna och de stigande pensionsutgifterna. Frst under de allra senaste ren har utgiftskningen visat tecken p avmattning. Till slut ven om vrt ekonomiska lge har blivit bttre, s str Finland nnu infr stora ekonomiska utmaningar. Srskilt viktigt tror jag att det r att hja sysselsttningsnivn och att minska den strukturella och ungdomsarbetslsheten. Detta r ocks en oerhrt viktig social frga. Det krvs lsningar bde p arbetsmarknaden och i finanspolitiken. Konkurrenskraftsavtalet stabiliserade lget p arbetsmarknaden frra ret, och hjlper nu till att frbttra det finska arbetets och produktionens konkurrenskraft p vrldsmarknaden. Detta r bra  men nnu mer behvs. Arbetsmarknadsreformer r av avgrande betydelse, eftersom befolkningen ldras och tstramningen av arbetsmarknaden sker snabbt: drfr mste vi hja arbetskraftsdeltagandet och sysselsttningen, frbttra kostnadskonkurrenskraften och utveckla "den finlndska modellen"  lokala avtal. Mina damer och herrar, Fr att vi i Finland ska kunna upprtthlla terhmtningstakten och frutsttningarna fr ekonomisk tillvxt i framtiden, s r bland annat fljande faktorer vldigt viktiga: att frstrka kunnandet och innovationsaktiviteten, att fortstta med avregleringen av den inhemska varu-och tjnstemarknaden, och att bromsa skuldsttningen i den offentliga sektorn. Om vi lyckas med detta s str Finlands ekonomi stark, ven i ett nordiskt och ett europeiskt perspektiv. Tack fr er uppmrksamhet! Finnish-business-kannalta_nettiin.pdf) VENJN ECONOMIC SITUATION AND FINLAND'S VENJN TRADE The economic study of the trade flows of countries is known as the gravitational effect, which suggests that neighbouring countries typically trade between countries rather than countries in the middle. In economic history, the foreign trade between the United States and Canada or the Vsjsn and The Vsll of Finland is an example. In addition to relative or competitive advantage, neighbourhood is another of the key factors in trade theory. This gravitational effect also affects the commercial-economic relations between Finland and Vensjsn, which have endured relatively well the difficulties and geopolitical pressures of the Vensjs economy. As a counterweight to Vensjs's power politics, the EU-US economic sanctions and, on the other hand, the Vensjs counter-sanctions have increased the volume of trade, but they have not sunk the sith. Even before the occupation of Crimea, the low point of the Vensjs economy has passed nsills nskym, and recently trade between Finland and Vensjs has recovered. SLIDE 2. The Russian economy has thus entered a recession, but growth is not particularly strong. The Bank of Finland has forecast that the Vensjs economy will grow by 1.5% in the March forecast round. In the first three quarters of the year, GDP growth was 1.6% year-on-year. In recent months, growth rates have slowed down slightly from before. Growth will be based on private consumption and exports in the year, but from next year the volume of exports is not expected to rise rapidly. In 2018 and 2019, growth could be 1.5% higher than previously forecast if the price of sljy remains at its current level. SLIDE 3. The Russian economy is still heavily dependent on the export of hydrocarbons. It has been possible to compensate for the fall in energy prices from the 2010.14 level, for example, by increasing the export of natural gas. In the long run, addiction is, of course, a risk. Many of the factors involved in the Vensjsn intressejs. The fight against climate change will at some point be in demand, at least as a fuel for transport. In addition, the U.S. Shale Revolution is setting some sort of ceiling on world market prices. Technological development in the sector has been so rapid that, at an already current price of about 60 a barrel, production in the United States is growing very rapidly again. There would be no return to a price of more than 100 a barrel. ... Venjjslls has been fighting against addiction for a long time, for example through various reform programmes. Two comprehensive and competing reform programmes were presented to President Putin in the early summer: SLIDE 4. 1) The "market-liberal" program of Alexei Kudrin; incl. privately, to increase the independence of the courts, to improve the business environment, to increase the efficiency of the courts, to increase the number of transactions, etc. 2) the "state-driven" program of Sergei Glaziev (Stolypin Club); the growth of public investment financed by the Central Bank, the weakening of the ruble to ensure competitiveness, not the increase in the amount of public investment financed by the Central Bank, etc. Neither programme is likely to be implemented as such. But, for example, the elskeis withdrawal will certainly return to the political agenda (for civil servants, elskeiks will rise from 6 months/year until it is 65 years for men and 63 years for women). On the other hand, the increase in the price of sljy and the increase in tax revenues may make reforms more attractive. Economic relations between Finland and Vensjsn SLIDE 5. Vensjs's share of Finland's foreign trade has varied quite a lot over the past 15 years. Variations related to the price of sljy and energy: more than 80% of Finland's Vensjsn imports are raw and natural gas. On the other hand, a higher price of sljy usually means a stronger ruble, which helps Finnish exports to Vensjs. In the year, Vensjs's share of Finland's goods exports has been about 5.9%, of imports 16.5%. SLIDE 6. In other words, Finland's exports to Vensjs depend by far the most on Vensjs's purchasing capacity, and specifically on its purchasing capacity in euros. In other words, when the ruble depreciates sharply, it is no wonder that Finnish exports to Vensjslle are staggering. In the year, of course, there has been a different pattern: the ruble has strengthened as the price of sljy has risen, and Vensjsn imports are increasing. The sanctions imposed by the EU on Vensjs have only applied to Finnish exports in very few cases. Similarly, Vensjs's restrictions have focused on food imports and have affected exports of approximately EUR 280 million, which is less than 10% of Finland's total exports to Vensjs (2013). On the other hand, a weakened ruble would have led to the export of nsidenk's products also without sanctions. SLIDE 7. It should be noted that the export of services is also srkess Vensjsn exports. Services account for about a quarter of total exports. The increased purchasing power of Venslsiste is also affected by tourism to Finland, for example. The strengthening of the ruble began last year already last year; there has been an increase in both border crossings and yspymiss. In the first nine months of the year, more than 12% of foreign hotel stays were in Venslsisten. SLIDE 8. At the same time, the number of Germans and Swedes is also growing, thanks to finland's increased attractiveness, reputation and marketing. A special mention is deserved by Chinese tourists, whose mssrs has been growing rapidly for several years. In that year, about 5% of all foreigners in Finland are yspyneists, and the growth of Chinese yspylys is 40%. Summary d SLIDE 9 Economic activity in the euro area is currently strong and growth is projected to continue. The ECB's accommodative monetary policy has contributed significantly to supporting growth and Finnish exports. The competitiveness of Finnish companies has also improved thanks to domestic efforts, which is now improving export performance. The Russian economy is also growing after two worse years, but growth is still slower than before the recession. ... The increase in the price of ljy will support growth and increase the ruble, which will also increase the demand for Finnish products. There is every reason to hope that trade between Finland and Vensjsn vsline will grow favourably in the coming years. The recovery of trade is of great importance for the economy and employment of Finland as a whole. It is particularly important for south-eastern Finland, which has been struggling with adaptation problems caused by global structural change for a long time. Knowledge of the Russian market among Finnish companies is a key issue for the future growth of trade. I encourage you to do so and the Finnish influencers to work together towards this goal. Thank you for your attention. Wednesday29 November 2017,2:30 PM Johtokunnan jsen Olli Rehn Suomen Pankki Venjn talouden tilanne ja Suomen Venjn-kauppa Suomalais-Venlisen Kauppakamarin (SVKK) seminaari Helsinki, 29.11. 2017 (pdf) (/globalassets/fi/media-ja-julkaisut/puheet/documents/2017-11-29-svkk_venajan-talouden-nakymat. suomalaisten-yritysten-kannalta_nettiin.pdf) VENJN TALOUDEN TILANNE JA SUOMEN VENJN-KAUPPA Maiden vlisten kauppavirtojen taloustieteellisess tutkimuksessa tunnetaan gravitaatiovaikutus, jolla viitataan siihen, ett naapurimaat kyvt tyypillisesti enemmn kauppaa keskenn kuin maat keskimrin. Taloushistoriassa Yhdysvaltain ja Kanadan vlinen tai Venjn ja Suomen vlinen ulkomaankauppa on tst esimerkki. Suhteellisen tai kilpailuedun lisksi naapuruus onkin toinen kauppateorian keskeisist kaupan mr selittvist tekijist. Tm gravitaatiovaikutus vaikuttaa ptevn mys Suomen ja Venjn vliseen kaupallis-taloudellisiin suhteisiin, jotka ovat kestneet suhteellisen hyvin Venjn talouden vaikeudet ja geopoliittiset paineet. Venjn voimapolitiikan vastapainoksi ptetyt EU:n ja Yhdysvaltain talouspakotteet ja toisaalta Venjn vastapakotteet ovat kyll vhentneet kaupan volyymia, mutta eivt upottaneet sit. Jo ennen Krimin miehityst alkanut Venjn talouden alamki on nill nkymin ohitse, ja viime aikoina Suomen ja Venjn kauppa on elpynyt. KALVO 2. Venjn talous on siis jttnyt taantuman taakseen, mutta kasvu ei ole viel mitenkn erityisen vahvaa. Suomen Pankki on ennustanut Venjn talouden kasvavan tn vuonna 1,5 % maaliskuun ennustekierroksesta lhtien. Vuoden kolmen ensimmisen neljnneksen aikana BKT:n kasvu oli 1,6 % vuoden takaa. Viime kuukausina kasvuluvut ovat hieman hidastuneet aiemmasta. Kasvu tukeutuu tn vuonna yksityiseen kulutukseen ja vientiin, mutta ensi vuodesta lhtien viennin volyymin ei en odoteta nousevan yht nopeasti. Vuonna 2018 ja 2019 kasvu voi olla aiemmin ennustettua 1,5 prosenttia nopeampaa, jos ljyn hinta pysyy nykyisell tasollaan. KALVO 3. Venjn talous on edelleen erittin riippuvainen hiilivetyjen viennist. Energian hintojen laskua vuosien 2010.14 tasosta on jonkin verran pystytty korvaamaan mm. maakaasun vientimr nostamalla. Pitkll aikavlill ljyriippuvuus on tietenkin riski. Monet tekijt nyttvt toimivan tll alalla Venjn intressej vastaan. Ilmastonmuutoksen vastainen taistelu tulee jossain vaiheessa vhentmn ljyn kysynt ainakin liikenteen polttoaineena. Lisksi Yhdysvaltain liuskeljyvallankumous nytt asettavan jonkinlaisen katon ljyn maailmanmarkkinahinnoille. Alan teknologinen kehitys on ollut niin nopeaa, ett jo nykyisell noin $60 tynnyrihinnalla tuotanto Yhdysvalloissa kasvaa taas erittin nopeasti. Nin ollen paluuta yli $100 tynnyrihintaan ei en olisi. ljyriippuvuutta vastaan on kamppailtu Venjll jo kauan mm. erilaisten reformiohjelmien kautta. Kaksi kattavaa ja kilpailevaa reformiohjelmaa jtettiin presidentti Putinille jo alkukesst: KALVO 4. 1) Aleksei Kudrinin "markkinaliberaali" ohjelma; sislt yksityistmist, tuomioistuinten riippumattomuuden lismist, liiketoimintaympristn parantamista, elkein noston jne. 2) Sergei Glazievin (Stolypin Club) "valtiovetoinen" ohjelma; sislt keskuspankin rahoittamaa julkisten investointien kasvua, ruplan heikentmista kilpailukyvyn takaamiseksi, ei sisll elkein nostoa jne. Kumpaakaan ohjelmaa tuskin pannaan tytntn sellaisenaan. Mutta esimerkiksi elkein nosto palaa varmasti politiikan esityslistalle (virkamiehill elkeik nousee tst vuodesta lhtien 6 kk/v, kunnes se on 65 v miehill ja 63 v naisilla). Toisaalta ljyn hinnan nousu ja verotulojen kasvu saattavat vhentvt uudistusten houkuttelevuutta. Suomen ja Venjn vliset taloussuhteet KALVO 5. Venjn osuus Suomen ulkomaankaupasta on vaihdellut varsin paljon viimeisten 15 vuoden aikana. Vaihtelut liittyvt ljyn ja energian hintaan: Suomen Venjn-tuonnista yli 80 % on raakaljy ja maakaasua. Toisaalta korkeampi ljyn hinta merkitsee yleens vahvempaa ruplaa, mik auttaa Suomen vienti Venjlle. Tn vuonna Venjn osuus Suomen tavaraviennist on ollut noin 5,9 %, tuonnista 16,5 %. KALVO 6. Toisin sanoen Suomen vienti Venjlle riippuu ylivoimaisesti eniten Venjn ostokyvyst, ja nimenomaan ostokyvyst euroissa. Eli kun rupla heikkenee voimakkaasti, ei ole ihme, ett Suomen vienti Venjlle krsii. Tn vuonna on tietenkin kynyt toisinpin: Rupla on vahvistunut ljyn hinnan noustessa, ja Venjn tuonti kasvaa. EU:n asettamat pakotteet Venjlle eivt ole koskeneet Suomen vienti kuin hyvin harvoissa tapauksissa. Vastaavasti Venjn rajoitukset ovat painottuneet elintarvikkeiden tuontiin ja koskeneet noin 280 miljoonan euron vienti, mik on alle 10 prosenttia Suomen kokonaisviennist Venjlle (2013). Toisaalta heikentynyt rupla olisi vhentnyt nidenkin tuotteiden vienti Venjlle mys ilman pakotteita. KALVO 7. On trke huomata, ett palveluiden vienti on trke mys Venjn-vienniss. Palvelut muodostavat noin neljnneksen kokonaisviennist. Venlisten noussut ostovoima nkyy esimerkiksi mys Suomeen kohdistuvassa matkailussa. Ruplan vahvistuminen alkoi nky jo viime vuoden puolella venlisturistien mrss; kasvua on ollut sek rajanylityksiss ett ypymisiss. Tmn vuoden yhdeksn ensimmisen kuukauden aikana yli 12 % ulkomaisista hotelliypymisist oli venlisten. KALVO 8. Samalla mys saksalaisten ja ruotsalaisten ypymiset kasvavat, mit voitaneen pit Suomen kasvaneen vetovoiman, maineen ja markkinoinnin ansiona. Erikoismaininnan ansaitsevat kiinalaiset turistit, joiden mr on kasvanut nopeasti jo usean vuoden ajan. Tn vuonna heit on noin 5 % kaikista ulkomaalaisista Suomessa ypyneist, ja kiinalaisten ypymisten kasvu on lhell 40 prosenttia. Yhteenveto  KALVO 9 Euroalueen talouskehitys on tll hetkell vahvaa, ja kasvun ennustetaan jatkuvan. EKP:n elvyttv rahapolitiikka on osaltaan merkittvsti tukenut kasvua ja Suomen vienti. Suomalaisten yritysten kilpailukyky on parantunut mys kotimaisten toimien ansiosta, mik nkyy nyt kohentuneena vientimenestyksen. Mys Venjn talous kasvaa jlleen kahden huonomman vuoden jlkeen, mutta kasvu on kuitenkin hitaampaa kuin ennen taantumaa. ljyn hinnan nousu sek tukee kasvua ett nostaa ruplaa, mik osaltaan lis mys suomalaisten tuotteiden kysynt. On syyt toivoa, ett nkisimme Suomen ja Venjn vlisen kaupan kasvavan suotuisasti mys tulevina vuosina. Kaupan elpymisell on mynteinen merkitys koko Suomen talouden ja tyllisyyden kannalta. Erityisen trke tm on Kaakkois-Suomelle, joka on pitkn krsinyt globaalin rakennemuutoksen aiheuttamista sopeutumisongelmista. Venjn markkinoiden tuntemus suomalaisten yritysten piiriss on kaupan tulevan kasvun kannalta avainkysymys. Kannustan teit siihen ja suomalaisia vaikuttajia yhdess toimimaan tmn tavoitteen eteen. Kiitos mielenkiinnostanne.
