Yksi pankkiryhm kaatui lhes kokonaan. Toimialaa jouduttiin muutonkin saneeraamaan voimakkaasti. Pankkisektorin henkilst puolittui 90-luvun alkupuoliskolla. Pankkitoiminnassa korostuivat riskien hallinta ja vakavaraisuuden varmistaminen. Osuuspankkiryhm uudisti ryhmrakenteen, muodosti yhteenliittymn. Osa pankeista ji ulkopuolelle muodostaen oman Paikallisosuuspankkiryhmn. Kaiken kaikkiaan pankkitoimiala tehostui ja tehosti toimintaansa niin, ett tll hetkell Suomen pankit ovat maailman edistyksellisimpien ja tehokkaimpien joukossa. Viimeisen kymmenen vuoden kokemukset osoittavat mys, miten suomalainen maaseutuyhteis on jlleen kerran onnistunut sopeutumisessa. Peltyt uhkakuvat eivt ole toteutuneet. Maataloudessa tyskentelevien mr on tosin nopeasti supistunut, mutta tuotannon mr on pysynyt joko ennallaan tai kasvanut. Mys maataloudessa on nhtviss merkittv tuottavuuden kasvu. Syrjisest sijainnistaan huolimatta Kiuruvesi on onnistunut lytmn oman "osaamisalueensa", mik on tehnyt mahdolliseksi onnistuneen siirtymisen stelytaloudesta vapaiden markkinoiden ankaraan maailmaan. Sadan vuoden aikana tapahtunutta muutosta voi hyvin havainnollistaa numeroilla ja ripit tarkastellen. Vkiluku oli 1900-luvun alussa noin 10 000 ja oli kasvanut 60-luvulle noin 16 000:een, se alkoi nyt pienenty takaisin kohti 10 000 asukasta. Tn aikana mys Kiuruveden elinkeinorakenne muuttui. Kun viel 1940-luvulla yli 90 prosenttia asukkaista sai elantonsa maa-ja metstaloudesta, on se tnn 24 prosenttia. Maatalouden merkitys on edelleen suuri. Tmn johdosta on syyt panna ilolla merkille maatalousyrittjien kehittmisen ja uudistumisen halu. Tilakoot ovat suurentuneet ja tiloja on modernisoitu investoimalla uuteen tekniikkaan. Menestyst osoittaa, ett Kiuruvesi on maamme suurin maidon ja naudanlihan tuottaja. Sadassa vuodessa palvelujen tuottamiseen tarvittava vestn osuus on noussut 2 prosentista 52 prosenttiin  eli erilaisissa palveluissa niin kunnan, kaupan ja liikenteen parissa vki on 25 kertaistunut verrattuna sadan vuoden takaiseen aikaan. Ja tnn Kiuruvesi el lhes 20 kertaa enemmn teollisuudesta kuin sata vuotta sitten, teollisuuden parissa oli 1 prosentti koko tyvest ja nyt noin 19 prosenttia. Toimintaymprist lhitulevaisuudessa Tt piv ja lhitulevaisuutta kuvastavat Euroopan edistyv integraatio, voimakas kansainvlistyminen ja maailmantalouden ennennkemtn vauhti. Keskusteluissamme ovat aivan tavanomaisina aiheina EU-direktiivit ja niiden vaikutukset, lastemme ja lastenlastemme opiskelut tai tyt ulkomailla, Amerikan talouden tai jopa Kiinan kova kasvu. Todellakin, suuri muutos on tapahtunut maailmankuvassamme. Liittyminen Euroopan Unioniin ja talous-ja rahaliittoon EMU:uun toivat muutoksia maatalouden harjoittamiseen, lhes kaikille elinkeinoelmn aloille ja jopa poliittiseen ptksentekoon. Yh useampi meihinkin vaikuttava asia ratkaistaan Brysseliss. Eik EU:sta ulkona oleminen tt olisi paljon muuttanut. Suomi on pienen kansantaloutena tysin riippuvainen siit, mit tapahtuu ymprillmme ja maailmantaloudessa. Tst hyvi esimerkkej ovat Tanska tai vaikka Ruotsi. Molemmat noudattavat kytnnss samoja pelisntj omassa rahapolitiikassa kuin mekin, vaikka ovat euroalueen ulkopuolella. Talous-ja rahaliitto vaikuttaa suoraan pankkitoimintaan. Nin mys tnn juhlivaan Kiuruveden Osuuspankkiin. Sen lisksi, ett nyt meill on kytss yhteinen raha koko euroalueella, on meill korko ja rahan mr sek muut rahatalouden edellytykset samat eri puolilla Eurooppaa. Lisksi rahoitusmarkkinat yhdentyvt vauhdilla Euroopassa. Pankkialalle tulee entist enemmn ylikansallista, ulkomaista tarjontaa. Jo nyt tarjolla on helposti markkinoitavia ja hallittavia tuotteita; maksu-tai luottokortteja ja kulutusluottoja. Monimutkaisempia ja hyv asiakastuntemusta edellyttvi tuotteita, kuten erilaisia pitkaikaissstmisen tuotteita ja asuntoluottoja, tulee ajan kanssa. Niiden tuotannossa mittakaavaedut ovat suuret ja jakelussa saatavat marginaalit yh kasvavan kilpailun johdosta pienet. Pankeille on tulossa uusia, monimutkaisia vakavaraisuusmryksi ja riskienhallintavaateita. Kirjanpitokin ja sen snnkset muuttuvat entist kansainvlisemmiksi. Ulkomaiset ovat tulleet suomalaisille pankkimarkkinoille yritysjrjestelyin, joko fuusioin tai yritysostoin. Viimeinen esimerkki on viime viikolla tapahtunut Sampo Pankin myynti Den Danske Bankille. Oman mausteensa tulee luomaan yhteninen maksualue, SEPA. Se helpottaa kaikenlaisten maksujen hoitamista euroalueella yli kansallisten rajojen. Se lis kilpailua rahoituspalveluissa. Kuluttajat hytyvt tst, ja palvelujen tarjonta ja kilpailukyky joutuvat yh uudelleen koetukselle. Kansainvlisen kehityksen lisksi on markkinoille tulossa uusia kotimaisia pankkeja. Tapiola Pankki on vasta aloittanut ja S-Pankki on tulossa jo ensi vuonna. Pankkikilpailuun tulee uutta vri. Asiakkaille nm muutokset ovat hydyllisi. Jokaiseen tarpeeseen lytyy palvelua ja tuotteita. Tavanomaisten pankkipalvelujen plle tulee koko ajan uusia tuotteita  knteiset asuntolainat, korkokatot, optiot, erilaiset vakuutussstmistuotteet ja listaa voisi jatkaa vaikka kuinka pitklle. Kilpailu pit hinnat ja muutkin ehdot hyvin. Onko alueellisesti toimivalla, koko markkinoihin nhden pienell pankilla evit vastata nihin haasteisiin? Nkymt pidemmlle tulevaisuuteen Pankeilla on vlineet palvella asiakkaitaan ajasta ja paikasta riippumatta. Kiuruveden Osuuspankin historiakirjassa on hyv, havainnollistava kertomus siit, miten tlt kotoisin oleva, maailmalla eri puolilla asunut Paula Pennanen kytt Kiuruveden Osuuspankin pankkipalveluja banaanipuun oksien alla Keniassa. Mielenkiintoinen yksityiskohta on, ett hnen palkkapankkinsakin on juhliaan viettv pankki! Asiakkaat kyttvt nit shkisi pankkipalveluja enenevsti, vaikka eivt olisi Keniassakaan. Ne helpottavat elm monella tavoin. Pankin konttorin sijainti ei en ole yht ratkaiseva kuin aiemmin. Pankista on tullut monelle kotitaloudelle ernlainen taloudenhoitaja. Tiliotteista nhdn tulot ja menot. Samalla syntyy tilinpitoa menneist ajoista ja voidaan tehd varojen kyttn liittyvi suunnitelmia ja ptksi. Varallisuustilannetta voi tarkastella on-line milloin tahansa. Paikallisesti toimivalla pankilla on luontaisia vahvuuksia kilpailussa. Pankkitoiminnassa tulee aina olemaan asioita, joissa paikallinen asiakastuntemus ja vlitn asiakaskohtaaminen ovat korvaamattomia. Nin on useissa henkil-ja yritysasiakkaiden palveluissa, erityisesti PK-yritysten rahoituksessa. Palvelut ja tuotteet voidaan rtlid palveluvalikoimasta parhaiten sopiviksi kullekin. Henkilasiakkaiden kohdalla pankkien toiminta on muuttunut maksujen vlittmisest vaativaan asiakasneuvontaan. Niss asioissa ei ole helppo toimia pelkill shkisill nettipalveluilla. Kiuruveden Osuuspankilla on erinomaiset mahdollisuudet prjt. Asiakkaat saavat palvelut nykyaikaisella tavalla. Kaikessa pankkitoiminnassa olennaista on terve varovaisuus. Siin ksitelln enimmkseen toisten varoja, siis tallettajien ei pankin omia varoja, ja sen vuoksi toiminnassa ei voi ottaa liiallista riski. Menestyksen avain on jatkossakin asiakastuntemus ja -palvelu. Osuuspankkiin liittyy viel se, ett kyseess on oma yritys, jossa toimivalla johdolla on oma vastuu. Erittin trke rooli on mys pankin hallintoelimill, johtokunnalla ja hallintoneuvostolla. He ovat vastuussa, ett pankin johto osaa asiansa ja toiminnan plinjat ovat oikeat. Tt tyt ja vastuuta on syyt korostaa ja arvostaa, sill sen vaikutukset nkyvt vasta vuosien, joskus vasta vuosikymmenten pst. Lopuksi, mutta ei vhemmn trken, yksi menestyksen perusedellytys, tai niin kuin prssianalyytikot tv.kommenteissa toteaisivat "fundamentti", on paikallispankin riippuvuus omasta alueesta ja sen ihmisist. Pankki prj pitkll aikavlill yht hyvin, ja vain yht hyvin tai huonosti kuin sen toimintaymprist prj. Alueen vest ja vireys on kaiken edellytys. Kaikki alueen hyvinvointi pohjautuu lopultakin menestyviin ja vahvoihin elinkeinoihin. Asukkaiden perustarpeista ja viihtyvyydest tulee huolehtia. Kyse ei ole vain sairaan-tai vanhusten hoidosta, kouluista taikka kunnan palvelujen saatavuudesta, vaan mys pehmemmist asioista kuten kulttuuripalveluista. On suuri haaste huolehtia alueen vireydest, kun vest vhenee ja ikntyy. Sama tilanne on koko Yl-Savossa. Vastuu hyvien toimintaedellytysten luomisesta on ensisijaisesti yhteiskunnallisilla pttjill, mutta pelkstn ei auta jd odottamaan julkisen hallinnon toimenpiteit. Kehittmiseen on osallistuttava mys yritysten, yrittjien ja yksityisten ihmisten. Paikallispankilla on merkittv rooli alueen toimeliaisuuden vahvistamisessa. Tm on mys pankin oma etu. Se ei kuitenkaan vlttmtt tarkoita rahoituksellista osallistumista, vaan kannustamista uusiin hankkeisiin sek uudistushakuisen ja mynteisen ilmapiirin vahvistamiseen. Nin pankki voi osaltaan huolehtia alueen kehittmistehtvst.

Title: Bank Manager's speech "Increasingly global threats to the economy"
text: Bank Manager Pentti Hakkarainen's speech "The economy faces more global threats" . Speech . Friday 8December 2006,12:00 AM Bank Manager Pentti Hakkarainen KHT-psivs 8.12.2006 Speech liittyvs kalvosarja (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and. interviews/documents/kht_yhdistys.pdf) (PDF) The world economy and trade have been gaining momentum in recent years. However, some industrialised countries are already showing signs of a slowdown in growth. In the United States, growth has slowed down due to the slowdown in the housing market. By contrast, growth in the euro area has remained relatively strong and investment has recovered. In Asia, China continues to grow at a rapid rate of around 10%. In Japan, too, economic growth has been at a comfortable pace in the year, although the figures for the 3rd quarter show a slight slowdown due to the slowdown in private consumption. In total, the global economy is growing at a rapid rate of about 4%. Economic growth is global, with the main industrialised countries and the major emerging economies. According to forecasts, economic growth will continue to be strong during the Lshi years, even though the peak of the economic cycle has passed. At the same time, the focus of growth is shifting towards developing economies. There are threats to economic growth. Particular risks have often been cited as the rapid slowdown in economic growth in the United States, the financial equilibrium of the world economy, the price of sljy and the abundance of money. These risks have been identified years ago and have been the subject of several analyses. There have been warnings about the "wolf coming", and there has been no collapse, not even a recession. Has it been numbed to the fact that, despite the risks and threats, economic growth will simply continue? A new setting for the global economy The global economy is a new setting. Global markets d i.e. freer movement of pssoms, goods and jobs Thanks to d and nside, the enhanced division of labour has led to a new situation. Everything seems to affect everything and vslichchssti. When the Finnish economy is caught up in the good momentum of the global economy, and the stalemate is concerned, we must take into account the risks that could have a negative impact on global economic growth, in addition to the staple factors of our own economy. Their impact is formerly on our own economic crises and challenges. There are good points for the mysterious development of the world economy. Economic growth will continue unless it is offset by any of the above threats: the stagnation of economic growth in the United States, the lack of financial imbalances in the global economy, the high price of sljy and the biases caused by the abundance of money. Any nsist, alone or in combination with others, can trigger a sharp slowdown in economic growth. However, it is difficult to assess whether or how it will be achieved. There are no perceived, unambiguous models for the new global economic situation that can be used to predict the outcome. This certainty is also created by the fact that the signals that previously characterised the beginning of the change, such as large current account balances, indebtedness and the rapid growth of monetary transactions, do not now lead to anything. So what would be the consequences of the looming developments? U.S. economic growth Private consumption has been the engine of economic growth in the United States. Private consumption has been boosted by the housing market, rising house prices and growth in lending. The increase in the value of the dwellings has made it possible to take on additional debt, which may have been used for consumption. Indeed, the indebtedness of American households has risen rapidly. When assessing the continuation of economic growth, there are reasons to monitor and pay attention to the housing market. The effects of house price developments are twofold. Firstly, the effects are macroeconomic and, secondly, they are related to investor participation. During 2005, house prices rose faster than at any time in the last 25 years. Statistics for August showed for the first time since 1995 that the selling price of houses had fallen. The fall in prices has an impact on private consumption and, consequently, on the growth of the national economy and the demand of the world economy. Investing in fixed assets is an internationalized investment in the world's lungs. Falling prices in the US housing market could also lead to a decline in investment in the rest of the world's fixed market. The impact through investor engagement is lightning fast and vslichn. Financial equilibrium in the world economy The financial equilibrium in the global economy has changed. For the past 10 years, the current account balance of the United States, the world's wealthiest economy, has been financed by Japan, especially the rapidly developing and industrialising Asian countries. In recent years, the countries have also become financiers. The annual us current account deficit is a trillion dollars. In that year, the excess of current account balances in the exporting countries corresponded to just over half of the total. In the shi years, the share of these countries may continue to grow. In the global economy, the circulation of money has changed. Whereas in the 1970s and 80s the funds of the sljyn producers were allocated to other emerging economies d e.g. latin American countries d now the money returns to the sljy-buying countries in the form of various investments. In the same way, China has already invested a trillion dollars of its foreign exchange reserves in American debt securities. And at the current rate, it will not be many years before the dollar reserves of the exporting countries are significantly larger. In fact, the current account financing of the United States is more sensitive to the price and changes in interest rates. At the same time, the surpluses of the member states' reserves on the financial markets provide exceptionally high liquidity, which has been discussed for years and the magnitude of the inflation risk it poses. ... ljy price development ... Despite its recent decline, the price of ljy is likely to remain relatively high. World consumption of sljy has grown strongly and faster than raw sljy production and processing capacity. The gap between capacity and consumption has narrowed to a historically low level, so there is a lot of speculation and certainty surrounding the price. Even small supply-related problems can easily increase the price. The highest price peaks occurred six months ago, when the Lebanese crisis and world politics dragged on Iran's nuclear programme. Although the uncertainty previously associated with sljy's production capacity has improved slightly, it is expected that the price of sljy will remain high based on the supply-demand balance and futures prices quoted on derivatives markets. Money mssrs The amount of money in the world economy is exceptionally high. The financial superintendents of the emerging and producing countries have been channelled into international financial markets. Indeed, long-term interest rates are already at a low level, in Europe at the same level as the short 12 months' money and in the United States even lower than short money. Real interest rates are also exceptionally low, and the amount of money has not so far accelerated inflation. The large money supply is also well illustrated by the narrowing of credit risk premia. When there is a lot of money, it goes to one of the riskier destinations, reducing the premium to be paid for the risk. Indeed, the abundance of money and low interest rates can lead to three biases. Firstly, the risks are priced too low, secondly, asset values become oversized, creating bubbles, and thirdly, 'leverage' is increasing in business and fixed investment in order to tow returns. If it develops too long, it reduces the resilience of the financial markets. Various changes in d or simply changes in the d sljy market, in us private consumption or asset values, or only in mere market expectations can upset the balance of financial markets. However, the economy is bright The bright economic crises are overshadowed by the four threats mentioned above: a sharp slowdown in the US economy, financial imbalances in the world economy, high prices and high financial liquidity. For the first time, this has recently become more probable than before, but growth in key economic areas is still quite strong and broad, including in the United States. Although in the global economy the interdependence of different countries is high, there are, among other things: Asian guerrilla trade has increased considerably and dependence on the US economy has increased. Thanks to China, Korea and Japan, Asia can act as an engine for economic growth, even if there is a regression in the United States. The conditions for a favourable soft landing option in the global economy have been outlined, for example, in the declarations of the G8. According to them, the scenario for good economic growth is that, at the same time as the US economy is rebalancing, asian countries' own domestic demand will increase. The unbalanced global economy is unravelling at the same time as economic growth as a whole can continue as the Countries of Asia move from export-driven growth to a more balanced growth phase based on more domestic demand. In these scenarios, EU countries face a particular challenge in terms of increasing the flexibility and real competitiveness of their economies. This analysis of the development of the world economy is well in line with this analysis. At the same time, it can be said that Finland, despite its current economic situation, is no exception among the EU countries. If you look at finland's economic situation more closely, you will see that we face the same challenges in terms of increasing real competitiveness and flexibility as the rest of the EU. The challenges faced by the Finnish economy Finland's economic figures are good. The comparison figures for the year are excellent, partly due to last year's tys conflict in the paper industry. Gdp is likely to grow by around 5% this year and is likely to continue to slow down slightly, but at a good level of around 3%. Economic growth is broad-based, consisting of appropriately different components, consumption, exports and investments. In Finland, investment in machinery and equipment is clearly lower than in competitor countries and the euro area in general. If this means a slowdown in the use of new innovations and better production techniques, it may be detrimental to the longer-term development of the economy. Finland's terms of trade d i.e. the ratio of export and import prices d has been falling almost as a trend for a longer period of time. Export prices in many sectors have developed poorly: the prices of telecommunications equipment have been on a downward trend, and the price development of products from the forest industry has not been high either. The bright spots have been ersst metals and sljy products, whose world market prices have risen. Overall, however, the development of export prices has been modest. At the same time as import prices rise, the terms of trade weaken and, therefore, the increase in welfare is lower than gdp growth figures could be. We will have to take more to pay our former import bills. To sum up the Finnish economy, it can be said that it is very wiped out. Moderately sound economic growth continues to be driven by steadily growing private consumption, supported by good consumer confidence. The high level of private investment during the year is due to long-term housing construction, and the slowdown in this area is slightly reversing the growth rate in the Lshi years. Demand in the export market is growing by 8-9% a year and, therefore, the pull of our exports will also continue. The problem is the reasonably high level of employment, although according to the latest data, the number of vacancies has increased at the same time. It communicates the structural problems of the labour market: the tys does not meet the author. Finally The next government will be able to enjoy a good economic situation. It is often pointed out that mistakes are made at very good times, by failing to take the necessary measures to ensure the continuity of economic growth. Good rankings in the international competitiveness comparison may be a good idea, but they should not be lulled. The world economy is constantly changing and national economies are competing for their positions and economic well-being. Our success will continue to require vigilance in matters that lie within the national dimension of fiscal policy, income policy, education and infrastructure projects such as logistics and energy supply. These sectors are constantly in a position to strengthen national competitiveness. Taking care of national competitiveness is very much a chore, as the challenges of iksnging will begin to be faced, especially around 2010, when the age class entering the labour market will already be smaller than the age class that will be leaving. Therefore, economic growth is only possible if we know how to do things smarter, more efficiently and more productively than before. Business services, such as auditing and financial consultancy, are an example of the high-value sectors on which the growth of countries such as Finland will increasingly be based in the future. The future of these services will depend on the number of offices of successful companies operating in Finland in the future and on how the international competitiveness of these service industries will be ensured. The internationalisation of Finnish experts and their links to the forefront of the development of their field are excellent. It is not only for the companies and experts themselves providing professional services concerned, but also for the Finnish economy, because high-quality business services are one of the prerequisites for the success of our entire industry.
text_original: Pankinjohtaja Pentti Hakkaraisen puhe "Taloudella yh globaalimmat uhat" KHT-pivill . Speech . Friday 8December 2006,12:00 AM Pankinjohtaja Pentti Hakkarainen KHT-piv 8.12.2006 Puheeseen liittyv kalvosarja (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and. interviews/documents/kht_yhdistys.pdf) (PDF) Maailmantalous ja -kauppa ovat olleet viime vuosina enntyksellisess vauhdissa. Kasvun hidastumisesta on kuitenkin havaittavissa jo merkkej joissakin teollisuusmaissa. Yhdysvalloissa kasvu on hidastunut asuntomarkkinoiden hiipumisen myt. Euroalueella kasvu on sen sijaan jatkunut suhteellisen vahvana ja investoinnit ovat elpyneet. Aasiassa Kiina jatkaa ripe noin 10 prosentin kasvuvauhtia. Japanissakin talouskasvu on tn vuonna ollut mukavassa vauhdissa, vaikka 3. vuosineljnneksen luvut osoittavat hienoista hidastumista yksityisen kulutuksen vaimenemisen vuoksi. Kaikkiaan maailmantalous kasvaa nopeaa noin 4 prosentin vauhtia. Talouskasvu on yh laaja-alaista, sislten keskeiset teollisuusmaat ja suuret kehittyvt taloudet. Talouskasvu jatkuu ennusteiden mukaan vahvana lhivuosina, vaikka suhdannehuippu onkin ohitettu. Samalla kasvun painopiste on siirtymss kohti kehittyvi talouksia. Talouskasvulle on uhkia. Erityisin riskein usein on mainittu Yhdysvaltojen talouskasvun nopea taittuminen, maailmantalouden rahoituksellinen eptasapaino, ljyn hinta ja rahan paljous. Nm riskit on tunnistettu jo vuosia sitten ja ne ovat olleet esill useissa analyyseiss. Nit "susi tulee" varoituksia on esitetty, ja mitn romahdusta, edes taantumaa ei kuitenkaan ole tapahtunut. Onko turruttu siihen, ett huolimatta riskeist ja uhista talouskasvu vain jatkuu? Maailmantalouden uusi asetelma Maailmantaloudessa nytt olevan uusi asetelma. Globaalit markkinat  eli pomien, tavaroiden ja tyn aiempaa vapaampi liikkuminen  ja niden ansiosta tehostunut tynjako ovat johtaneet uuteen asetelmaan. Kaikki tuntuu vaikuttavan kaikkeen ja vlittmsti. Kun Suomen talous on kiinni hyvss maailmantalouden vedossa, ja hytynyt tst, on meidn huomioitava oman kansantaloutemme sisisten tekijiden lisksi ne riskit, jotka voivat vaikuttaa kielteisesti maailman talouskasvuun. Niiden vaikutus on entist vlittmmpi omiin talousnkymiimme ja haasteisiimme. Maailmantalouden mynteiselle kehitykselle on hyvt lhtkohdat. Talouskasvu jatkuu, ellei kasvua taita jokin edell mainituista uhista: Yhdysvaltojen talouskasvun pyshtyminen, maailmantalouden rahoituksen tasapainottomuus, ljyn korkea hinta ja rahan paljouden aiheuttamat vinoumat. Mik tahansa nist, yksin tai yhdess toisten kanssa, voi laukaista talouskasvun voimakkaankin hidastumisen. Kuitenkin sen arviointi, mik nist toteutuu tai miten, on vaikeaa. Thn uuteen maailmantalouden tilanteeseen ei ole koettuja, yksiselitteisi malleja, joiden avulla voisi ennakoida lopputuloksen. Epvarmuutta luo mys se, ett aiemmin muutoksen alkua kuvanneet signaalit kuten suuret vaihtotasealijmt, velkaantuneisuus ja rahamrien nopea kasvu, eivt nyt nyt johtavan mihinkn. Mit siis pitisi nist uhkaavista kehityskuluista seurata? Yhdysvaltojen talouskasvu Yhdysvaltojen talouskasvun moottorina on toiminut yksityinen kulutus. Yksityist kulutusta osaltaan on yllpitnyt asuntomarkkinat, asuntojen hintojen nousu ja lainoitusmrn kasvu. Asuntojen arvon kohoaminen on mahdollistanut lisvelan ottamisen, joka on voitu kytt kulutukseen. Amerikkalaisten kotitalouksien velkaantuneisuus onkin noussut nopeasti. Arvioitaessa talouskasvun jatkumista on syyt seurata ja kiinnitt huomiota asuntomarkkinoihin. Asuntojen hintakehityksen vaikutukset ovat kahdenlaiset. Ensinnkin vaikutukset ovat makrotaloudellisia ja toiseksi vlittmn sijoittajakyttytymiseen liittyvi. Vuoden 2005 aikana asuntojen hinnat nousivat nopeammin kuin viimeisen 25 vuoden aikana kertaakaan. Tmn vuoden elokuun tilastot osoittivat ensimmisen kerran asuntojen myyntihinnan laskeneen sitten vuoden 1995. Hinnanlasku vaikuttaa yksityiseen kulutukseen ja sit kautta kansantalouden kasvuun ja maailmantalouden kysyntn. Suomen talousnkymien omat haasteet Suomen talousluvut ovat hyvt. Tmn vuoden vertailuluvut ovat erinomaiset, osin viime vuoden paperiteollisuuden tyselkkauksen vuoksi. Suomessa kone-ja laiteinvestoinnit ovat selvsti alempana suhteessa BKT:hen kuin kilpailijamaissa ja euroalueella yleisestikin. Jos tm merkitsee uusien innovaatioiden ja paremman tuotantotekniikan kytn hidastumista, voi se olla haitallista talouden pidemmn aikavlin kehityksen kannalta. Valopilkkuina ovat olleet ert metallit ja ljytuotteet, joiden maailmanmarkkinahinnat ovat nousseet. Kokonaisuudessaan vientihintojen kehitys on kuitenkin ollut vaatimatonta. Kun samaan aikaan tuontihinnat nousevat, heikkenee vaihtosuhde ja nin ollen hyvinvoinnin lisys on pienempi kuin bruttokansantuotteen kasvuluvuista voisi ptell. Joudumme viemn yh enemmn, jotta saamme maksettua entisen tuontilaskumme. Yhteenvetona Suomen taloudesta voi todeta, ett hyvin pyyhkii. Kohtuullisen terveen talouskasvun taustalla on edelleen tasaisesti kasvava yksityinen kulutus, jota tukee hyv kuluttajaluottamus. Tmn vuoden korkeat yksityiset investoinnit johtuvat pitklti asuntorakentamisesta, ja siin tapahtuva hidastuminen taittaa hiukan kasvuvauhtia lhivuosina. Vientimarkkinoiden kysynt kasvaa 8-9 prosenttia vuodessa ja nin ollen mys vientimme veto jatkuu. Ongelmana on kohtuullisen korkealle jmhtnyt tyttmyys, vaikka viimeisten tietojen mukaan avoimien typaikkojen mr on samalla kasvanut. Tm viestii tymarkkinoiden rakenteellisista ongelmista: ty ei kohtaa tekijns. Lopuksi Seuraava hallitus psee nauttimaan hyvst taloudellisesta lhttilanteesta. Usein muistutetaan, ett virheet tehdn juuri hyvin aikoina siten, ett talouskasvun jatkuvuuden turvaamiseksi tarvittavat toimet laiminlydn. Hyvt sijoitukset kansainvlisess kilpailukykyvertailussa voivat lmmitt mielt, mutta niihin ei pid tuudittautua. Maailmantalous muuttuu jatkuvasti ja kansantaloudet kilpailevat asemistaan ja taloudellisesta hyvinvoinnista. Menestymisemme vaatii valppautta jatkossakin asioissa, jotka ovat itsenisess kansallisessa ptntvallassa eli finanssipolitiikassa, tulopolitiikassa, koulutuksessa sek infrastruktuurihankkeissa kuten logistiikassa ja energiahuollossa. Nill aloilla on jatkuvasti kyettv vahvistamaan kansallista kilpailukyky. Kansallisesta kilpailukyvyst huolehtiminen on erittin trke, koska ikntymisen haasteet alkavat tulla vastaan erityisesti vuoden 2010 tienoilla, jolloin tymarkkinoille tuleva ikluokka on jo pienempi kuin sielt poistuva ikluokka. Nin ollen talouskasvu on mahdollista vain, mikli osaamme tehd asioita entist fiksummin, tehokkaammin ja tuottavammin. Liike-elmn palvelut, kuten tilintarkastustoiminta ja talousasioiden konsultointi, on esimerkki niist korkean lisarvon aloista, joihin Suomen tapaisten maiden kasvu jatkossa enenevsti perustuu. Niden palvelujen tulevaisuus perustuu siihen, kuinka paljon menestyvien yritysten pkonttoreita jatkossa toimii Suomessa ja miten niden palvelutoimialojen kansainvlisest kilpailukyvyst huolehditaan. Nin suomalaisten asiantuntijoiden kansainvlistyminen ja yhteydet oman alansa kehityksen eturintamaan ovat erinomaisen trkeit asioita. Se on sit paitsi asianomaisten asiantuntijapalveluja tuottavien yritysten ja asiantuntijoiden itsens kannalta, mys Suomen kansantalouden kannalta, koska korkeatasoiset liike-elmn palvelut ovat yh trkempi osa koko elinkeinoelmmme menestyksen edellytyksi.

Title: Bank Director's speech "Increasingly global threats to the Finnish economy"
text: Bank Manager Pentti Hakkarainen's speech "The most global threats to the Finnish economy" at an economic seminar in Loimaa . Speech . Tuesday 2 January 2007, 12:00 AM Bank Manager Pentti Hakkarainen Yritsvs Varsinais-Suomi ry and Loimaan Kunjsrjests ry Economic Seminar Loimaa 2.1.2007 Speech liittyvs kalvosarja (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and. interviews/documents/070102ph_talousseminaari.ppt) (ppt) The world economy and trade have been gaining momentum in recent years. However, some industrialised countries are already showing signs of a slowdown in growth. In the United States, growth has slowed down due to the slowdown in the housing market. By contrast, growth in the euro area has remained relatively strong and investment has recovered. In Asia, China continues to grow at a rapid rate of around 10%. In Japan, too, economic growth has been at a comfortable pace in the year, although the figures for the 3rd quarter show a slight slowdown due to the slowdown in private consumption. In total, the global economy is growing at a rapid rate of about 4%. Economic growth is global, with the main industrialised countries and the major emerging economies. According to forecasts, economic growth will continue to be strong during the Lshi years, even though the peak of the economic cycle has passed. At the same time, the focus of growth is shifting towards developing economies. Finland's economic figures are also good. The comparison figures for the year are excellent, partly due to last year's tys conflict in the paper industry. Gdp is likely to grow by around 5% this year and is likely to continue to slow down slightly, but at a good level of around 3%. Economic growth is broad-based, consisting of appropriately different components, consumption, exports and investments. A NEW SETTING FOR THE GLOBAL ECONOMY The global economy is a new setting. Global markets d i.e. freer movement of pssoms, goods and jobs Thanks to d and nside, the enhanced division of labour has led to a new situation. It is difficult, even impossible, for an individual national economy to isolate itself or to function independently from the rest of the world. When the Finnish economy is caught up in the good momentum of the global economy, and the stalemate is concerned, we must take into account the risks that could have a negative impact on global economic growth, in addition to the staple factors of our own economy. Their impact is formerly on our own economic crises and challenges. There are good points for the mysterious development of the world economy. Economic growth will continue unless it is met by one of the commonly identified threats: the stagnation of economic growth in the United States, the lack of financial imbalances in the global economy, the high price of sljy and the biases caused by the abundance of money. Any nsist, alone or in combination with others, can trigger a sharp slowdown in economic growth. Which of the threats materializes or how? There are no perceived, unambiguous models for the new global economic situation that can be used to predict the outcome. This certainty is also created by the fact that the signals that previously characterised the beginning of the change, such as large current account balances, indebtedness and the rapid growth of monetary assets, do not now lead to the corrections experienced in the past. So what would be the consequences of the looming developments? U.S. ECONOMIC GROWTH Private consumption has been the engine of economic growth in the United States. Private consumption has been boosted by the housing market, rising house prices and growth in lending. The increase in the value of the dwellings has made it possible to take on additional debt, which may have been used for consumption. Indeed, the indebtedness of American households has risen rapidly. When assessing the continuation of economic growth in the UNITED STATES, attention has been paid to house price developments. This has a macroeconomic impact and through investor participation. Price change has an impact on private consumption and, consequently, on the growth of the national economy and on global demand. During 2005, house prices rose faster than at any time in the last 25 years. Statistics for August showed that the sale price of houses fell for the first time since 1995. Investing in fixed assets is an internationalized investment in the world's lungs. Falling prices in the US housing market could also lead to a decline in investment in the rest of the world's fixed market. The impact through investor engagement is lightning fast and vslichn. Why has economic growth not yet stalled? The responses include a well-developed strategy, improved corporate profits, efficiently functioning financial markets and economic dynamics. Reference has also been made to the delay; the development of the housing market will have an impact only after some time. A more likely slowdown in economic growth will not have as strong an impact on the global economy as it has in the past. As a result of globalisation, the highly developed Asian economies have increased their central trade and private consumer demand, and dependence on the US economy has increased. FINANCIAL BALANCE OF THE WORLD ECONOMY The financial equilibrium in the global economy has changed. For the past 10 years, the current account balance of the United States, the world's wealthiest economy, has been financed by Japan, especially the rapidly developing and industrialising Asian countries. In recent years, the countries have also become financiers. The annual us current account deficit is a trillion dollars. In that year, the excess of current account balances in the exporting countries corresponded to just over half of the total. In the shi years, the share of these countries may continue to grow. In the global economy, the circulation of money has changed. Whereas in the 1970s and 80s the funds of the sljyn producers were allocated to other emerging economies d e.g. latin American countries d now the money returns to the sljy-buying countries in the form of various investments. In the same way, China has already invested a trillion dollars of its foreign exchange reserves in American debt securities. And at the current rate, in a few years, the dollar reserves of the exporting countries will be significantly larger than those of the Asian countries. U.S. current account financing is now more sensitive to the price and interest rate changes. At the same time, the surpluses of the member states' reserves on the financial markets provide exceptionally high liquidity, which has been discussed for years and the magnitude of the inflation risk it poses. ... PRICE DEVELOPMENT OF LJY ... The increase in the price of ljy has been based on different factors than in the past. In the previous crisis, the OPEC countries raised the price by limiting production. Now the world's consumption of sljy has grown strongly and faster than the production and processing capacity of raw sljy. The gap between capacity and consumption has narrowed to a historically low level, so there is a lot of speculation and certainty surrounding the price. Even small supply-related problems can easily increase the price. The highest price peaks occurred six months ago, when the Lebanese crisis and world politics dragged on Iran's nuclear programme. Although the uncertainty previously associated with sljy's production capacity has improved slightly, it is expected that the price of sljy will remain high based on the supply-demand balance and futures prices quoted on derivatives markets. MONEY MR The amount of money in the world economy is exceptionally high. The financial superintendents of the emerging and producing countries have been channelled into international financial markets. Indeed, long-term interest rates are already at a low level, in Europe at the same level as the short 12 months' money and in the United States even lower than short money. Real interest rates are also exceptionally low, and the amount of money has not so far accelerated inflation. The large money supply is also well illustrated by the narrowing of credit risk premia. When there is a lot of money, it goes to one of the riskier destinations, reducing the premium to be paid for the risk. Indeed, the abundance of money and low interest rates can lead to three biases. Firstly, the risks are priced too low, secondly, asset values become oversized, creating bubbles, and thirdly, 'leverage' is increasing in business and fixed investment in order to tow returns. If it develops too long, it reduces the resilience of the financial markets. Various changes in d or simply changes in the d sljy market, in us private consumption or asset values, or only in mere market expectations can upset the balance of financial markets. HOWEVER, THE ECONOMY IS BRIGHT The bright economic crises are overshadowed by the four threats mentioned above: a sharp slowdown in the US economy, financial imbalances in the world economy, high prices and high financial liquidity. For the first time, this has recently become more probable than in the past, but growth in key economic areas is still quite strong and broad. Although in the global economy the interdependence of different countries is high, there are, among other things: Asian guerrilla trade has increased considerably and dependence on the US economy has increased. Thanks to China, Korea and Japan, Asia can act as an engine for economic growth, even if there is a regression in the United States. The conditions for a favourable soft landing option in the global economy have been outlined, for example, in the declarations of the G8. According to them, the scenario for good economic growth is that, at the same time as the US economy is rebalancing, asian countries' own domestic demand will increase. The unbalanced global economy is unravelling at the same time as economic growth as a whole can continue as the Countries of Asia move from export-driven growth to a more balanced growth phase based on more domestic demand. In the global economy soft landing scenario, EU countries face a particular challenge in increasing the flexibility and real competitiveness of their economies. This analysis of the development of the world economy is well in line with this analysis. At the same time, you can: to state that Finland, despite its current economic situation, is no exception among the EU countries. If you look at finland's economic situation more closely, you will see that we face the same challenges in terms of increasing real competitiveness and flexibility as the rest of the EU. CHALLENGES FOR THE FINNISH ECONOMY In Finland, investment in machinery and equipment is clearly lower than in competitor countries and the euro area in general. If this means a slowdown in the use of new innovations and better production techniques, it may be detrimental to the longer-term development of the economy. Finland's terms of trade d i.e. the ratio of export and import prices d has been falling almost as a trend for a longer period of time. Export prices in many sectors have developed poorly: the prices of telecommunications equipment have been on a downward trend, and the price development of products from the forest industry has not been high either. The bright spots have been ersst metals and sljy products, whose world market prices have risen. Overall, however, the development of export prices has been modest. At the same time as import prices rise, the terms of trade weaken and, therefore, the increase in welfare is lower than gdp growth figures could be. We will have to take more to pay our former import bills. In summary, finland's economic growth can be expected to continue. Moderately sound economic growth continues to be driven by steadily growing private consumption, supported by good consumer confidence. The high level of private investment during the year is due to long-term housing construction, and the slowdown in this area is slightly reversing the growth rate in the Lshi years. Demand in the export market is growing by 8-9% a year and, therefore, the pull of our exports will also continue. Our problem is a reasonably high level of employment, even though, according to the latest data, the number of vacancies has increased at the same time. It communicates the structural problems of the labour market: the tys does not meet the author. FINALLY The next government will be able to enjoy a good economic situation. It is often pointed out that mistakes are made at very good times, by failing to take the necessary measures to ensure the continuity of economic growth. Good economic growth is driven by strong developments in the world economy. The world economy is constantly changing and national economies are competing for their positions and economic well-being. Our success depends on the flexibility to face the tightening conditions. We are constantly in a position to strengthen national competitiveness in matters that are in the hands of the national balance, i.e. fiscal policy, incomes policy, education and infrastructure projects such as logistics and energy supply. Taking care of national competitiveness is very much a chore, as the challenges of iksnging will begin to be faced, especially around 2010, when the age class entering the labour market will already be smaller than the age class that will be leaving. Therefore, economic growth is only possible if we know how to do things smarter, more efficiently and more productively than before.

SUOMEN TALOUSNKYMIEN OMIA HAASTEITA Suomessa kone-ja laiteinvestoinnit ovat selvsti alempana suhteessa BKT:hen kuin kilpailijamaissa ja euroalueella yleisestikin. Jos tm merkitsee uusien innovaatioiden ja paremman tuotantotekniikan kytn hidastumista, voi se olla haitallista talouden pidemmn aikavlin kehityksen kannalta. Suomen vaihtosuhde  eli vienti-ja tuontihintojen suhde  on liki trendinomaisesti laskenut jo pidemmn aikaa. Joudumme viemn yh enemmn, jotta saamme maksettua entisen tuontilaskumme. Yhteenvetona voi Suomen talouskasvun odottaa jatkuvan. Kohtuullisen terveen talouskasvun taustalla on edelleen tasaisesti kasvava yksityinen kulutus, jota tukee hyv kuluttajaluottamus. Tmn vuoden korkeat yksityiset investoinnit johtuvat pitklti asuntorakentamisesta, ja siin tapahtuva hidastuminen taittaa hiukan kasvuvauhtia lhivuosina. Vientimarkkinoiden kysynt kasvaa 8-9 prosenttia vuodessa ja nin ollen mys vientimme veto jatkuu. Ongelmamme on kohtuullisen korkealle jmhtnyt tyttmyys, vaikka viimeisten tietojen mukaan avoimien typaikkojen mr on samalla kasvanut. Tm viestii tymarkkinoiden rakenteellisista ongelmista: ty ei kohtaa tekijns. LOPUKSI Seuraava hallitus psee nauttimaan hyvst taloudellisesta lhttilanteesta. Usein muistutetaan, ett virheet tehdn juuri hyvin aikoina siten, ett talouskasvun jatkuvuuden turvaamiseksi tarvittavat toimet laiminlydn. Hyvn talouskasvun taustalla on voimakas maailmantalouden kehitys. Maailmantalous muuttuu jatkuvasti ja kansantaloudet kilpailevat asemistaan ja taloudellisesta hyvinvoinnista. Menestymisemme edellytt riittv joustavuutta kohdata tiukentuvia oloja. Prjtksemme on jatkuvasti kyettv vahvistamaan kansallista kilpailukyky asioissa, jotka ovat itsenisess kansallisessa ptntvallassa eli finanssipolitiikassa, tulopolitiikassa, koulutuksessa sek infrastruktuurihankkeissa kuten logistiikassa ja energiahuollossa. Kansallisesta kilpailukyvyst huolehtiminen on erittin trke, koska ikntymisen haasteet alkavat tulla vastaan erityisesti vuoden 2010 tienoilla, jolloin tymarkkinoille tuleva ikluokka on jo pienempi kuin sielt poistuva ikluokka. Nin ollen talouskasvu on mahdollista vain, mikli osaamme tehd asioita entist fiksummin, tehokkaammin ja tuottavammin.

FINANCIAL MARKETS... STdb NEW RISK Graph 10: Spreads between unsecured and secured credit in euro area banks' markets A new risk to the development of the world economy is the financial markets, in terms of speed and seriousness, and the liquidity crisis that has been in place in the late summer. The situation becomes particularly problematic if the financial markets' security is prolonged or deepened again. H?irishish has been widely accused of having developed into a wild affair in the United States of housing finance. However, the problems are probably not confined to mortgages, but the causes of the turmoil in the financial markets are much more fundamental and widespread. A NEW MODEL FOR CREDIT MANAGEMENT TO BE REVIEWED Graph 11: Subprime mortgages and secured debt obligations Mortgage problems highlighted other problems in the financial markets and weaknesses in an approach that has become more popular in recent years. The financing system, the addition of credit and the transfer of credit-related risks, has developed operating models and new policies. In spite of the humility, however, the new activities went into overly complex structures and structures, as well as products that cannot be managed. Risk has been transferred by trading real loan receivables and derivatives. The overall risk is increased by the growth of derivatives alone. In addition, the risks have increasingly been sold outside banks under regulatory control. The risk is often also felt by those who do not have sufficient expertise in risk management. Stock markets are often said to be anticipating economic developments. The relationship between the valuation of shares and the growth of the economy is illustrated by the so-called "stock valuation". Gordon's growth model. The model is named after the developer Myron J. Gordon. Assuming a stable dividend payment policy, the model can be used to calculate the valuation of stocks as a function of the rate at which dividends grow and the prevailing interest rate. The K?nchen model can be used to assess the rate of growth of dividends and thus of the economy at which the current exchange rate level implicates. Although the calculation is sensitive to different assumptions, the current exchange rate level implicates significant economic growth for the l?hi years. TIGHTER CONDITIONS FOR LOANS Graph 14: Risk premiums on loans to non-financial corporations recovering The price of financing by non-financial corporations is reflected in the quotations on the national market for bonds issued by non-financial corporations. The price of the company's risk is obtained as the difference between the yield of the bond and the yield on government debt securities. The liquidity crisis in the money markets has led to a tightening of the conditions on corporate bonds and a widening of interest margins. This was due to investors' willingness to risk, as well as the trend towards unambiguous and manageable risks. In particular, there was a high demand for government debt securities. As a result, corporate risk spread strongly first across all creditworthiness categories, but partially narrowed back. Investors and lenders are ready to finance companies with clear business and projects. Companies will receive money, but under stricter conditions and at a higher cost. However, the risks are still clearly narrower than the margins of the long term. Graph 15: Bank risk in relation to sovereign risk MFIs themselves have also experienced a rise in the cost of their financing. The risk premium paid by banks compared to government debt securities has increased well above the long-term level. The risk has widened both in the United States and europe. Banks have accounted for the turbulence in the financial markets in relative terms more than other large companies in terms of credit risk and share prices. THE CAUSE OF THE LIQUIDITY CRISISdb THE AVERAGE COMPETITION BETWEEN BANKS Graph 16: Unsecured and secured interest rates on euro area banks' markets Significant and ?ys' new manifestation at a time of financial turbulence has been n?hty in the money market. Short money, as traded on the unsecured depo market of Sith banks, has become more expensive in the past. Banks have been reluctant to lend to each other without collateral. The price of three months' money to the bank briefly rose from 0.60 to 0.70 percent to one percent. At first, this kind of h?iri?tila wasn't even possible, but that's how it was born and has also gone on longer than expected. LIKVIDITEETTIKRIISIN SYYN PANKKIEN KESKININEN KILPAILUKIN Kuvio 16: Vakuudeton ja vakuudellinen korko euroalueen pankkien vlisill markkinoilla Merkittvin ja tysin uusi ilmi rahoitusmarkkinoiden turbulenssin aikana on nhty rahamarkkinoilla. Lyhyt raha, sellaisena kuin sit pankkien vlisill vakuudettomilla depomarkkinoilla kaupataan, on kallistunut ennennkemttmsti. Pankit ovat olleet haluttomia lainaamaan toisilleen ilman vakuuksia. Kolmen kuukauden rahan hinta pankille nousi hetkess 0.60 -0.70 prosenttiyksikk. Tllainen hiritila ei ensinnkn pitnyt edes olla mahdollinen, mutta niin se syntyi ja on mys jatkunut odotettua pidempn. Markkinaraportit ovat perustelleet pankkien vlisen rahanhinnoittelun hirit luottamuspulalla. Kyse voi olla eptietoisuudesta siit, mik on vastapuolen tila, likviditeettiasema ja luottokelpoisuus. Likviditeettikriisi voimistaa pankkien keskininen kilpailu. Kukin rahoituslaitos on antanut asiakkailleen sitoumuksia tulevien hankkeiden rahoittamisesta. Likviditeettitilanteen kiristyess pankki haluaa silytt oman kykyns antaa rahoitusta hyvn. Pankki ei tllin anna rahoitusta edes lyhytaikaisesti kilpailevalle rahalaitokselle muuten kuin helposti likvidoitavassa muodossa eli vakuudellisena luottona tai ns. repokauppana. Johtoptst, ett likviditeettikriisin syyn on tavanomaiseen pankkien kilpailuun kuuluva kyttytyminenkin, vahvistaa mys se, ett useilla suurilla kansainvlisill pankeilla on enntyksellisen suuret kteisvarat. Ne eivt ole kuitenkaan halukkaita lainaamaan varojaan toisilleen, ei edes hyvin vakavaraisille pankeille, vaan varautuvat itse rahoittamaan asiakkaitaan. MARKKINOIDEN INFLAATIO-ODOTUS MALTILLINEN Kuvio 17: Markkinoiden inflaatio-odotukset (2 vuotta) Rahoitusmarkkinoilta johdetut inflaatio-odotukset ovat edelleen maltillisia, vaikkakin aivan viime kuukausien aikana nousseet. Mys lhiajan korko-odotukset ovat maltillistuneet huomattavasti rahoitusmarkkinoiden turbulenssin aikana. JOHTOPTKSET Kuvio 18 Maailmantalous kasvaa voimakkaasti. Tuleva polku on ilmeisesti kuoppaisempi kuin viime aikojen maantieteellisesti laaja, vakaa ja vahva kasvu. Useat talouskasvun uhkat ovat edelleen olemassa ja pikemminkin vahvistuneet, kuten kansainvlisen hintarypshdyksen vaara. Uutena uhkana on rahoitusmarkkinoiden toiminnan hiriintyminen. Ja aina ylltyksetkin ovat mahdollisia. Rahoitusmarkkinahirit heikentvt nyt talouskasvua, kun viime vuosina juuri suotuisat rahoitusolot ovat keskeisesti vahvistaneet poikkeuksellisen pitkn jatkunutta kansainvlisen talouden korkeasuhdannetta. Talous on hytynyt elvyttvst rahapolitiikasta maailmanlaajuisesti ja rahaa on riittnyt sek investointeihin ett kulutukseen. Ylijmtalouksista raha on liikkunut jouhevasti alijmtalouksiin. Vaikka rahoitusmarkkinat normalisoituisivat nopeastikin, jo koettujen hiriiden vaikutuksen suunta on selv. Kuinka vahvasti kasvu hidastuu, sit on viel liian varhaista sanoa. Lopullisempia johtoptksi voidaan tehd vasta, kun nyt nhtvn rahoitusmarkkinoiden hirin kesto ja seuraukset on selvill nykytilannetta paremmin  antaa siis odottaa ainakin ensi vuoteen! Varmaa on ainakin: -Riskien alihinnoittelu on oiennut, mutta ehk ei riittvsti. -Riskienhallinta saa ansaitsemansa arvon. -Monimutkaisten instrumenttien ja toimintamallien sek vaikeasti hallittavien riskipositioiden suosio on vhentynyt. -Lhitulevaisuuden talouskehityksess ja rahoitusmarkkinoilla on varauduttava suuriin heilahteluihin. Globaalissa taloudessa ulkoiset ehdot ovat kullekin maalle samanlaiset, mutta eroja on maiden kyvyss vastaanottaa talouden muutoksia. Maalle, joka haluaa menesty globaalissa taloudessa, on kilpailukyvyst ja joustavuudesta huolehtiminen elintrke.

Title: Recession in sight?
text: Bank Manager Pentti Hakkarainen: Lama nskyvisss? Helmet Business Mentors Oy's Sijoittajapsivs . Speech . Thursday8 November 2007, 12:00 AM Bank Manager Pentti Hakkarainen Helmet Business Mentors Oy:n Sijoittajapsivs Kalastajatorppa 8.11.2007 Speech liittyvs kalvosarja(/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and. . interviews/documents/071108ph_helmet.pdf) LAMA NKYVISS? Good ladies and gentlemen It is a pleasure to participate in the investor survey and to present ideas on the economy. I was asked to talk about whether there will be a recession, and if so, what. I edited my title to "Lama nskyvisss?". Note the question mark in the title. The first response to Alan Greenspan's statement was about a month ago. Hsn estimates that, with a 40% probability, the US economy will plunge into recession. According to the opinion, it is therefore also probable that it will not fall into recession. I will not confine myself to referring only to Mr Greenspan's statement, but I will respond in more depth. Let me start by talking about the world economy. Then I also describe the threats or risk paths that could jeopardise developments. Well-functioning financial markets and economic development are interlinked. For this reason, risk must be considered at the level of the world economy and the various national economies, as well as at the level of the financial markets. The global review is relevant, not only for those interested in the global economy, but for all of us, because in today's world we cannot avoid global impacts and risks. Just as pssomat or information moves in the global market in real time from one place to another, there are also different kinds of information that move quickly across countries. On the other hand, differences arise in the ability of different countries to adapt to international changes. THE INTERNATIONAL ECONOMY'S NKYMT MY... NTEISET Graph 3: The structure of global growth The world economy's staples are the same; -Asia and a number of emerging economies continue to enjoy strong economic growth and are also good for the years, -In the United States, the slowdown in economic growth already last year, the turmoil in the financial markets weakened economic developments and, if it continues for a long period of time, may even plunge the country into recession, -in Europe growth is leveling off, although at least in that year the global economy is strongly on the move, and in Finland the GDP growth figures for the current year are even better than expected, more than 4%, but growth is expected to slow down to around 3% next year and around 2.5% next year percent. Economic growth is exceptionally broad-based geographically. There is growth in both industrialised and emerging economies, even in the developed countries of the Country, including Africa. It is fastest in the emerging economies of Asia. China alone is already responsible for about a third of global GDP growth. The country's share of the world's national product was about 16% last year, adjusted for the price level. Growth rates in the United States, Europe and Japan are clearly lower than in the rest of the world economy, but their weight in the global economy remains high, with half (44%). This year is in economic history at a time when China's contribution to global economic growth overtook the United States for the first time, including without a purchasing power adjustment. MULTIPLE THREATS TO ECONOMIC GROWTH Figure 4: Threats to global economic growth The current economic growth has been made possible by the new financial situation in the national economies and, in the past, by large international trade flows. The specificities of the global economy are under threat that could also dampen global economic growth: -large current account surpluses and deficits may turn out to be mid-term, and will unravel sharply -the adjustment pressures of expanding world trade may increase the risk of trade war and protectionism and the impact of financial markets on the stability and growth of economies. THE TUNE ADJUSTMENT OF CURRENT ACCOUNT BALANCES Graph 5: Current account balances in the global economy In the global economy, the financing of national economies is in a completely new situation. Countries formerly considered to be kchyhin or developing countries finance prosperous national economies. China, many other asian countries, as well as Vensjs and other sljynproducing countries, finance the United States. The financial superintendents are persis from strong export-driven economic growth and also from rapidly rising sljy incomes. They are channelled to the financial markets of the industrialised countries in the form of investments, which has made it difficult for them to finance even large current account balances. As a result, the global financial balance is more sensitive than ever to changes in interest rates and exchange rates. Indeed, the global economy may be plunged into crisis by the uncontrolled or liquid unwinding of financial surpluses and sub-sectors. A particularly problematic situation would first arise in the United States, where consumer demand would increase and the Ssssss rate would rise. This development would be reflected in the global economy, in particular because of the weakening dollar, which analysts consider to be a natural part of the forced adjustment of the current account. THE DANGER OF PROTECTIONISM Figure 6: Order books are strong World trade is the busiest in economic history. Its growth has been over forecasters for several years now. The reason is the strong pace of investment in emerging economies. For industrialized countries, this means strong export demand and nsky, in particular, in world trade in psomahysdykes. The companies' order books are exceptionally thick, which is likely to strengthen the profitability of these companies. In Finland, especially the metal processing and machinery and metal products industries have been in a frenzy. In the face of fierce global competition, there is a risk of protectionism. Production is shifted to locations with the competitive advantage of a lot of power, large reserves of raw materials or a large market. Developed economies are tempted to protect their own industrial production and competitive position with protectionism. Competition will be hindered, which will lead to a halt to productivity growth. The effect of moderating competitive price developments will be eliminated. The most serious danger is the derailment into a global depression. Economies that are most specialised in the long term and dependent on high-growth markets, such as Finland. HINTARY... PSHDYS LHIVUOSINA? Figure 7: Rising prices of Chinese products As a result of high demand, the prices of raw materials have risen to pre-existing levels. However, they have so far not been reflected in the prices of finished products in the corresponding mssrin. Now the threat of an acceleration of the general price trend has increased. It is therefore appropriate to analyse the characteristics of this risk a little more. A significant factor in price increases over the past ten years or so has been the "Chinese appearance". Despite high demand, Chinese industry has been able to produce higher quality hysdykes, even at lower prices. The main price developments in global competition may already have a negative impact on the labour and hysdyke markets. After a long decline, the prices of Chinese products have started to rise rapidly during the year, especially in the United States. In the past, the rise in the price of raw materials has not been reflected in the prices of finished products, but now it is a signifier. In addition, inflation has accelerated in China itself. sms puts price pressure on all Chinese hysdyke and service production. Employment in the global economy is not growing as fast as it has in recent decades. Over the past two decades, the power of the workforce has doubled worldwide. The changed role of China and India has been particularly affected, but it has also been influenced by the emergence of the former Bloc countries as market economies. The level of wages will rise in the countries as growth in the labour market slows down and, on the other hand, the level of education also rises. Figure 8: Broad-based pressures on commodity prices Another root cause of price pressures is the rise in the prices of primary products and raw materials. ... The prices of products have tripled and the prices of metals have doubled in real terms during the current decade. The real prices of agricultural products are currently about a third higher than in 2000. The reason for the rise in prices has rapidly increased demand. Another significant feature is that, according to the main estimates, the increase is not due to a shortage of primary products or raw materials, but that their production capacity has not only been increased sufficiently rapidly. The rise in the prices of primary products and raw materials is projected to slow down over a long period of time, with the supply increasing. However, the models used in the forecasts are not so accurate that they can be used to make a sufficiently reliable estimate of price trends over the past few years. It is to be expected that the price development of energy, base metals and agricultural products in the shia period will be accompanied by changes of magnitude, even by small efficiencies in the security of supply, as there is no surplus capacity in reserve to buffer the changes. FINANCIAL MARKETS... ST NEW RISK Graph 9: Spreads between unsecured and secured credit in euro area banks' markets Sustainable economic growth requires well-functioning financial markets, which also buffer the economy. However, in developed financial markets, there may be excesses that can undermine economic development. A new risk to the development of the world economy is the financial markets, in terms of speed and seriousness, and the liquidity crisis that has been in place in the late summer. The situation becomes particularly problematic if the financial markets' security is prolonged or deepened again. Hsirishish has been widely accused of having developed into a wild affair in the United States of housing finance. It is true that it triggered the financial markets first in the United States and that confidence spread in investment and loan portfolios and risk positions to Europe as well. However, the problems are probably not confined to mortgages, but the causes of the turmoil in the financial markets are much more fundamental and widespread. A NEW MODEL FOR CREDIT MANAGEMENT TO BE REVIEWED Graph 10: Subprime mortgages and secured debt obligations Mortgage problems highlighted other problems in the financial markets and weaknesses in an approach that has become more popular in recent years. The financing system, the addition of credit and the transfer of credit-related risks, has developed operating models and new policies. They have improved the functioning of financial markets and increased access to finance and improved risk management. In spite of the humility, however, the new activities went into overly complex structures and structures, as well as products that cannot be managed. Risk has been transferred by trading real loan receivables and derivatives. The overall risk is increased by the growth of derivatives alone. For example, credit default derivatives have grown from a few hundred million dollars to 35,000 billion in about five years. In addition, the risks have increasingly been sold outside banks under regulatory control. The risk is often also felt by those who do not have sufficient expertise in risk management. In short, it is a question of banks transferring all their loan receivables to the front. This happened not only in mortgages, but also in consumer, credit card and business loan receivables. In this area, the development of credit and financial receivables has been dizzying. According to the creditworthiness assessor Standard & Poor's, banks accounted for about half of corporate credit in the United States in 2000 and about 20% in the middle of the year. In Europe, the corresponding figures are around 90% in 2000 and less than half. Problems in the financial markets are tightening the terms of loans, raising the interest rate and reducing access to finance. If implemented, such a development will make it more difficult for companies to invest. The effects also extend to export demand and private consumption. The longer-term problems will continue to be significant d and at the same time a more unpredictable d effect on the confidence of businesses and households in future economic development. TIGHTER CONDITIONS FOR LOANS Graph 11: Risk premiums on loans to non-financial corporations recovering The price of financing by non-financial corporations is reflected in the quotations on the national market for bonds issued by non-financial corporations. The price of the company's risk is obtained as the difference between the yield of the bond and the yield on government debt securities. The liquidity crisis in the money markets has led to a tightening of the conditions on corporate bonds and a widening of interest margins. This was due to investors' willingness to risk, as well as the trend towards unambiguous and manageable risks. In particular, there was a high demand for government debt securities. As a result, corporate risk spread strongly first across all creditworthiness categories, but partially narrowed back. Investors and lenders are ready to finance companies with clear business and projects. Companies will receive money, but under stricter conditions and at a higher cost. However, the risks are still clearly narrower than the margins of the long term. Graph 12: Bank risk in relation to sovereign risk MFIs themselves have also experienced a rise in the cost of their financing. The risk premium paid by banks compared to government debt securities has increased well above the long-term level. The risk has widened both in the United States and europe. Banks have accounted for the turbulence in the financial markets in relative terms more than other large companies in terms of credit risk and share prices. THE CAUSE OF THE LIQUIDITY CRISIS THE AVERAGE COMPETITION BETWEEN BANKS Graph 13: Unsecured and secured interest rates on euro area banks' markets Significant and sys' new manifestation at a time of financial turbulence has been nshty in the money market. Short money, as traded on the unsecured depo market of Sith banks, has become more expensive in the past. Banks have been reluctant to lend to each other without collateral. The price of three months' money to the bank briefly rose by 0.60 d0.70 % to one. At first, this kind of hsiristila wasn't even possible, but that's how it was born and has also gone on longer than expected. Market reports have justified the pricing of money by banks on the basis of a lack of confidence. It may be a question of awareness of the counterparty's status, liquidity position and creditworthiness. The liquidity crisis is intensifying competition between banks. Each financial institution has given its clients commitments to finance future projects. In view of the tightening of the liquidity situation, the bank wants to use its own capacity to provide good financing. The bank does not provide financing, even for a short period of time, to a competing MFI, other than in an easily liquidated form, i.e. a secured credit or a so-called "secured credit". as a repo shop. The management that the cause of the liquidity crisis is also the use inherent in normal competition between banks, confirms the fact that many large international banks have pre-existing assets. However, they are not willing to lend their funds to each other, not even to very solvent banks, but are prepared to finance their customers themselves. JOHTOPT... KSET Chart 14 The global economy is growing strongly. A recession cannot be long-probable, but on the other hand, its possibility cannot be ruled out. Future economic development appears to be more bumpy than recent geographically broad, stable and strong growth. A number of threats to economic growth exist and, on the contrary, have intensified, such as the risk of international price escalation. A new threat is the longer-term disruption of the functioning of the financial markets. And there is always the possibility of overshooting. Even if the financial markets return to normal quickly, the direction of the impact of the Hsirisides already experienced will be clear. How strongly growth will slow down is still too early to say. More definitive conclusions can only be made when the duration and consequences of the financial markets are now clearer than the current situation d let's wait until at least next year! In a global economy, external conditions are the same for each country, but there are differences in the ability of countries to absorb economic changes. Major fluctuations in the economic development of the future and in the financial markets must be prepared for. For a country that wants to succeed in a global economy, it is a matter of maintaining competitiveness and flexibility.
