Title: Restoring the functioning of the financial markets
text: Vice Chairman of the Board pentti Hakkarainen: The functioning of the financial markets must be restored. Helsinki 15.1.2009 . Speech . Thursday15 January 2009, 12:00 AM Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen SOLUTION 09 seminar, Finlandia Hall, Helsinki 15.1.2009 Speech Membranes (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and. . interviews/documents/090115_ph_ratkaisu09.ppt) (PPT) Puheen Membranes (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and. . interviews/documents/090115_ph_ratkaisu09.pdf) (PDF) RESTORING THE FUNCTIONING OF FINANCIAL MARKETS "In order to prevent a protracted recession, the functioning of the financial markets must be restored. In international economic policy, the need for coordination is currently great. There is a serious risk of international protectionism spreading," said Pentti Hakkarainen, Vice-Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Finland, speaking on Thursday at the Solution 09 event in Helsinki. "Due to the crisis, the financial markets around the world have increasingly come under the control of the state. The influence of the public authorities on banking has been further enhanced by guarantees, redundancies and takeovers. In order to ensure stability, there has been a risk of competition becoming more competitive and inefficient in the future," Hakkarainen said. In Hakkarainen's opinion, supranational financial supervision is needed at EU level with sufficient powers. Cooperation at EU level is necessary to enable more effective supervision of large, cross-border financial conglomerates. The problems of the current decentralized national control of pssos are considerable. oThe control of national groupings is accompanied by blind spots, inefficiency and psflexibility. In addition, different supervisory cultures and supervisory structures are holding back integration. There is no balance between countries on the responsibilities, powers and risks of supervision and crisis management. o In Finland, supervision has been intensified in conjunction with the Financial Supervisory Authority and the Insurance Supervisory Authority. The new Financial Supervisory Authority (FIVA), of which Pentti Hakkarainen chairs the Board of Directors, started its operations at the turn of the year. In his speech, Hakkarainen warned against economic nationalism. Cross-border financial activity is over-the-top in the face of new challenges. If international financial markets do not function satisfactorily, this will be particularly damaging to small and open economies such as Finland." If international action is not taken to restore the viability of the market, countries will be forced to take national measures to safeguard their own position, which will make the international market more difficult than it used to be. Miksli nsin ksy, you have to react in Finland as well." "Another major problem, in addition to the reduced availability of international finance, is that the corporate bond market has dried up. It is a question of whether banks are able to replace the above-mentioned market with financing. o Finland's bank support measures must ensure the ability of banks to increase their significant lending. I'm talking about it, because at the moment we need more banks than we used to. It is in society's interest that banks are prepared to accept government investments and guarantees. Of course, public support is always remunerated, but the conditions must not be too strict. There must be a balance in order to restore the functioning of the financial markets. o The problems to be solved in relation to bank support are pricing, effects on competition and conditionality of aid. "Notwithstanding the urgent need for state intervention, the measures must be well thought out and it must be ensured that the credit risk assessment is made in accordance with the financial system itself.'

The crisis has also revealed the weak points of international financial supervision. Banking is international, but supervision is national. Cross-border measures must be stepped up in the monitoring of risks in order to improve the health of banking. However, control is not a magic wand, waving which eliminates problems. There are still many other obstacles to overcome. I will come back to the monitoring issues towards the end of my speech. Let me start by saying a few words about where we are in crisis and how we have come about. At the beginning of the crisis, many believed that the problems in the financial markets were hitting the financial sector. This wish or belief has now turned out to be a vssrs. Problems are afflicting all economic areas, and there is no economic operator who would not be affected in any way, either directly or directly, by the effects of the crisis. Another peculiarity of the crisis is speed. A change in one financial market is immediately passed on to another market. (Slide 1: Risky banks in the market) The evolution of interest rates in the banks' markets reveals the timing of the crisis. In the United States, risk premiums jumped by as much as 4% and in Europe by more than 2%. Since then, of course, the risks have clearly narrowed, but they are still exceptional. Hsiris is at the very core of the financial system. Reorganising bank structures A new dimension of the crisis began when the depreciation of the financial markets and other difficulties pushed the restructuring of the banking sector. The most obvious change in the situation has been in the United States, where the market in the industry has changed as fundamentally as it did during the Finnish banking crisis 15 years ago. The main housing finance institutions are federally owned and investment banking as a separate industry has ceased to exist. Interestingly, many very first-class banks have run into great difficulties. There are also major changes in Europe, with the partial or full nationalisation of several banks. The share of governments in the banking system has also increased through the provision of guarantees to banks. Further structural changes in d the organisation of the sector d are to be expected. In addition to banking structures, business models are undergoing a major change. Over the past decade, the "originate and distribute" model of "loans and transfers") has developed and grown particularly rapidly, as well as being intrinsically linked to the manufacture of various debt and derivative instruments in concrete walls. The risk did not come from transfer and decentralisation, but ended up in places where there was no ability to manage it. The model led to the risk of the total uncontrollable increase in the number of cases of exclusion from control. Economic growth is slowing down The global economy was already experiencing a slowdown before the start of the financial market crisis. The economic slowdown has been reinforced by the financial markets. Companies, in particular, have become channels of exploitation for the nsiden hsiriside. The tightening of financing conditions affects all economic operators. Rising financial prices are raising the return on investment requirements for companies, and many plans that were previously considered promising are now looking bad. The investments made will not be as profitable as was calculated when entering the project, as the cost of financing is now a worse burden than expected. The price of corporate finance has risen and its availability has decreased. Investments have had to be postponed and orders cancelled. Greater difficulties in accessing finance may arise as, among other things, companies' own balance sheets deteriorate during a downturn and reduce their creditworthiness. The willingness of banks to finance risky long-term investments has clearly diminished. Talousnskymst A more difficult problem for Finnish companies than obtaining financing is the rapid contraction in exports, which is a consequence of the slowdown in global economic growth. According to the latest data from the Business Cycle Review of the Confederation of Finnish Industries, the order backlog collapsed towards the end of 2008. (Slide 2: GDP forecasts for 2009) The economic forecasts for 2009 follow the clearest trend: what is the more recent forecast, the future economic development is gloomier. There is also a contraction in world trade, with consequences for export-driven countries such as Finland. The hope expressed at the beginning of the crisis that the emerging asian economies would have a saving effect as a replacement for the contraction in US demand is not coming true. Confidence indicators are also at a historically low level. The same downturn is occurring on all continents. So we can talk about a global recession. Indeed, the trend of the global economy in the lshi years is essential for our own economy. The options can be described using different letters: V, you and L. The so-called V model is the most positive of the models and describes the rapid rise from recession to new growth. The letter "U" represents a slightly longer recession, after which policy measures begin to take effect and growth is again quite rapid. One option, described by the letter L, is a longer recession or even a recession. The risks to this development have increased. Regardless of which of the previous economic crises takes place, it would be irresponsible of us to assume that the economy is in its own right. Through our own actions, we actively seek to influence the fact that, whether the development is in accordance with the V, U or L model, we survive as much damage as possible. Extraordinary measures from central banks The government has intervened with extraordinary force in the functioning of the market. Recently, there have been reports of central banks pumping money into the market and of massive stimulus packages from governments in different countries. The central banks have been in circulation with firepower. The efforts have been well-informed and international coordination has worked well. The already normally lively dialogue between the various central banks has only intensified over the course of the crisis. Interest rates have been cut even at the same time, which can be considered historical. The European Central Bank has cut the key interest rate four times a month. The Fed, the Bank of England and the Swedish Riksbanken have cut interest rates more. Market rates are followed, which has naturally eased the position of debtors and reduced financing costs. All central banks have also increased the supply of finance and extended maturities. The European Central Bank's monetary policy implementation mechanism has also been changed in a direction that strengthens liquidity. The market itself has been given the level of liquidity. The ECB provides banks with short-term credit against collateral for as much as they need. Banks are therefore preparing for a worsening of the situation by increasing their central bank debt and depositing funds in the form of over-ysn deposits with the central bank. When you get one percent lower interest rate on a deposit than what the MFI pays for a loan it takes out from a central bank, it is exceptionally expensive to secure a standby fund to safeguard one's own solvency in all situations. Actions of governments The governments of the various countries have acted with great efforts to counteract the effects of the crisis and to ensure that the containment arrangements are in place. In the United States, the rescue programme exceeds USD 2 000 billion. In Europe, banks have 2,000 billion in funding guarantees and 250 billion in cash injections. In Finland, the government is prepared to guarantee up to EUR 50 billion in unsecured bank funding. However, in the light of current knowledge, there is no first bank that needs or is more than willing to use such a guarantee. In Finland, preparations have also been made for the withdrawal of banks with state funds, just in case. In Finland, banks' liquidity and solvency have remained well in international comparison. Still, there is a challenge for banks to compensate for the drying up of the international loan market with domestic lending. It is in society's interest that banks are prepared to accept government investments and guarantees. Of course, public support is always remunerated, but the conditions must not be too strict. There must be a balance in order to restore the functioning of the financial markets. The national economy should not be allowed to fall into a spiral in which credit is not worthwhile for fear of a downturn and in which a downturn is coming because of the lack of funding for investment. It is precisely for this kind of situation that massive state guarantees and pssomitus are intended. As a result, the conditions attached to this must be such that banks can also use them to maintain sound lending. In several countries, ideas have emerged to set up asset management companies, i.e. junk banks, and programmes to buy banks' problem assets. The problems to be solved in order to ensure the functioning of financial markets are pricing, competitive effects and conditionality of aid. Nevertheless, there is a need for urgent state intervention, the measures must be well thought out and it must be ensured that the credit risk decision is made in accordance with the financial system itself. The example of Japan is worthwhile. The country did not take the necessary reorganisation measures to set up banking structures and a state-funded asset management company until many years later. It prolonged the crisis and increased the costs to society as a whole. It is necessary to have the courage to take measures quickly in order to achieve a real recovery. Means towards a better economic situation It is difficult to get out of a crisis. The construction of the future is slowed down by the fresh experience of difficult times and by the fear of taking new vigorous action to avoid sowing seeds for a new crisis. There is no going back to the pre-crisis world, as economic growth in recent years was built on the great imbalances of the world economy: the indebtedness of Asia, the indebtedness of the United States and the underestimation of risks by the world financial system. the structure could not withstand the deterioration of the economic cycle, and now it is time to reverse the growth by looking elsewhere. There is a wide range of measures to prevent the crisis from protracted and to stimulate the economy. The general point for recovery measures has been that the measures are selected and temporary. The most common means are investments in infrastructure and housing production. State guarantees, credits and tax cuts are also widely used. Those countries that are sub-countries are demanding the most drastic stimulus measures from countries such as Germany. Finland's recovery will, of course, not have the same global impact as Germany's. (Slide 3: Balance of public finances in eu countries) Public finances are forced to use funds beyond their normal capacity. The three per cent farm deficit in public finances can be classified as still healthy, but in many economies the current limit has been exceeded or exceeded. It is not just the small countries that are at stake, but also the larger economies. Large deficits lead to a situation in which the economies of the states should only be rebalanced for a long period of time and excessively strict fiscal policies during periods of economic difficulties. It is also essential to ensure that the expenditure items of the sub-employees do not give rise to permanent mechanisms, but are, for example, one-off investments. It is only a natural way out when growth takes off and supports the reduction of the sub-population. In any case, in order to prevent the recession from being prolonged, the functioning of the financial markets must be restored. The influence of public authorities in banking has been amplified to ensure stability, but there may be a risk of competition becoming more competitive and inefficient. There is therefore a great need for coordination of international economic policy at a time, so that national rescue programmes do not fragment the already integrated financial markets and international protectionism. In any case, cross-border financial activity faces new challenges. If international financial markets do not function satisfactorily integrated, this will be to the detriment of small and open economies such as Finland in particular. The real threat would therefore be the return of national financial markets. If international action is not taken to restore the viability of the market, countries will be forced to take national measures to safeguard their own position, which will make the international market more difficult than it used to be. Miksli nsin ksy, must also in Finland react. Does monitoring help? At the same time, at international level, we are looking for the causes of the crisis and ways to prevent similar events. One of the steering points is that the financial markets need more and more effective international supervision and cooperation. (Slide 4: Person) Financial actors and researchers have come up with different solutions on how supervisors should have a tighter grip on financial activities. It has been suggested that the range of complex financial innovations should be reduced to standardised products, such as the market. In addition, it has been required that the PFI's psoma and requirements be tightened for a long period of time and that various off-balance-sheet items and separate associations be taken into account. The proposals are justified. However, it is possible to ensure that they do not lead to excessive costs and backward developments. The standardisation of financial products must not be too long in order to make room for innovation and the intensification of financial markets. On the other hand, it is not a good idea to burden the controls with a kind of work that increases the costs of the supervisees, but does not improve the risk prevention. Increasing the level of transparency, i.e. information obligations, is probably the most effective way of promoting market confidence and, at the same time, efficiency. There should be no undue tightening of the community requirements, including liquidity buffering, in order to: the cost of financing will not increase unduly. In the case of off-balance-sheet items and separate companies, the possibilities of circumvention of the law and the negative consequences for all financial activities must be taken into account. The international operation of financial institutions requires enhanced supervision. Supranational supervision must be strengthened by ensuring cross-border powers for the supervisory authorities. In Europe, there are, for example, de Larosizre .tysryhmsn, eurojs system, CEPS, etc. the development of European supervision based on national supervisory responsibilities. Possible pss options include: (1) whereas the existing cooperation between national supervisors extends the legal and powers of either the colleges or the committees (CEBS, CESR and CEIOPS); (2) building supervisory cooperation similar to the European System of Financial Supervisors, the European System of Financial Supervisors, which has a central body and the national supervisory authorities carry out supervision in their territories; or (3) conferring on the European Central Bank the supervisory responsibility of large international financial institutions. Already during this period, a decision on the guidelines for the development of supervision is to be expected. The report of the Larosizre group will be completed in March, and the G20 activities will be scheduled so that they will be presented in April. The time is all right for improving the control structures. Finally The economic forecasts for Chechnya and for next year have deteriorated. In all countries and in all economic regions worldwide, trade has slowed down, growth has stalled and employment is rising. The challenge for economic policy now is to reconcile actions that have a positive impact and are targeted, but which do not erode the conditions for long-term sustained growth. The economic challenges concern society as a whole. Grants for scientific research are awarded. There are good reasons for supporting research in difficult times as well. In exceptional times, the usual ways of working are not enough, but rather a deeper approach to fundamental issues. This is precisely why the importance of research is emphasised. Even if the research does not provide direct answers to economic policy or other current problems, the research nevertheless sprouts the new ideas on which the future is built. This applies as much to economic policy as it does to technology, business and human sciences.

Haasteita rahoitusmarkkinoiden toimimattomuuden rinnalle tuo se, ett talous supistuu ja nkymt heikkenevt. Vakavaksi haasteeksi nyttvt muodostuvan elvytyspakettien aiheuttamat ongelmat julkiselle taloudelle ja maailmalla leviv protektionismin uhka. Synkkien talousuutisten keskell on silti hyv muistaa, ett meneilln oleva finanssikriisi ei suinkaan ole ensimminen, vaan erilaisia kriisej, romahduksia ja paniikkeja on koettu ennenkin. Lopputuloskin on aina ollut sama  kriisist on selvitty. Tt kuvaa hyvin Hyman Minsky kirjassaan Stabilising an unstable economy (1986). Maailmassa on itse asiassa nhty yli sata paikallista pankkikriisi 70-luvulta lhtien. Tlle kriisille erityinen piirre on sen maailmanlaajuinen ulottuvuus. Ongelmat koettelevat kaikkia talousalueita eik sellaista taloudellista toimijaa olekaan, jota kriisin vaikutukset eivt koettelisi jollain tavoin joko suoraan tai epsuoraan. Toinen erityispiirre kriisille on nopeus. Toisella rahoitusmarkkinalla tapahtuva muutos vlittyy saman tien toiselle markkinalle. Tutkimuksissa on havaittu, ett mit arvopaperistetumpi markkina on, sit voimakkaampia ja sekunnilleen samanaikaisia ovat esimerkiksi arvopapereiden arvonmuutosten vaikutukset. Rahoitusmarkkinoiden hiriiden esiinmarssi Kriisi lhti liikkeelle Yhdysvaltojen subprime-asuntolainamarkkinoilta ja levisi nopeasti kaikkialle rahoitusmarkkinoille. Euroopassa merkittv alkusysys hiriiden esiintulolle oli Britanniassa asuntoluottopankki Northern Rockia kohdannut talletuspako. (Kalvo 1: Riskilist pankkien vlisill markkinoilla) Koron kehitys pankkien vlisill markkinoilla paljastaa kriisin synnyn ajankohdan. Tarkkaan ottaen elokuun 9. pivn vuonna 2007 yliyn korot nousivat ja euroalueen pankit alkoivat vaatia erityist riskilis  marginaalia  keskinisille vakuudettomille lainoilleen. Pankkien vliset tehokkaat lyhytaikaiset rahamarkkinat ovat perustuneet pasiassa juuri vakuudettomiin transaktioihin, lainoihin ja talletuksiin. Suomessakin kytss oleva viitekorko euribor, kuvaa juuri tt vakuudettomien luottojen markkinan korkoa. Marginaalit vakuudettoman ja vakuudellisen rahoituksen vlill eli ns. riskilist olivat olleet lhes kaikissa luottoluokissa muutamia prosentin kymmenyksi ja sadasosia eli lhes olemattomia. Riskilisien yhtkkisen kasvun on yleisesti nhty kuvaavan toimijoiden vlille syntynytt keskinisen luottamuksen puutetta. Tm on varmasti yksi selitys. Kuitenkin mys niill markkinoilla, joilla osapuolet tuntevat toisensa ja toistensa riskit lpikotaisin, hinnoittelu muuttui rajusti. Liian runsaasta rahoituksesta siirryttiin oikeastaan toiseen rimmisyyteen, likviditeettikriisiin. Siin ei kyse ollut vain siit, ett pankit eivt luottaneet toisiinsa, vaan mys siit, ett ne eivt tysin luottaneet en omaankaan maksuvalmiuteensa. Lisksi pankkien vlinen kilpailu krjisti ongelmaa. Pankkien intresseiss ei ollut auttaa kilpailijoitaan  toisia pankkeja  antamalla nille likviditeetti. Kriisi krjistyi syyskuussa 2008, kun suuri yhdysvaltalainen investointipankki Lehman Brothers ajautui konkurssiin. Tmn seurauksena pankkien jo muutenkin heikentynyt luottamus toistensa ja osin mys omaan maksuvalmiuteen romahti. Riskilisien kasvussa ja kaikissa valuutoissa ja niiden rahamarkkinoilla voidaankin nhd selke piikki ylspin syyskuun puolivlin jlkeen. Yhdysvalloissa riskilist pomppasivat jopa 4 prosenttiyksikkn ja Euroopassa yli 2 prosenttiyksikkn. Riskilist ovat sittemmin toki selvsti kaventuneet, mutta ne ovat edelleen poikkeuksellisia. Hiri on yh aivan rahoitusjrjestelmn ytimess. Pankkirakenteet uusiksi Kriisin uusi ulottuvuus alkoi, kun rahoitusmarkkinoiden arvonalennukset ja muut vaikeudet syssivt pankkialan rakennemuutokseen. Selvimmin tilanne on muuttunut juuri Yhdysvalloissa, miss toimialan markkinat ovat muuttuneet yht perusteellisesti kuin Suomen pankkikriisiss 15 vuotta sitten. Keskeiset asuntorahoituslaitokset ptyivt liittovaltion omistukseen ja investointipankkitoiminta erillisen toimialana on kytnnss lakannut olemasta. Mielenkiintoista on, ett monet aivan ykksluokan pankit ovat ajautuneet suuriin vaikeuksiin. Mys meill Euroopassa on nhty suuria muutoksia, kun useita pankkeja on kansallistettu osittain tai kokonaan. Valtioiden osuus pankkijrjestelmss on kasvanut mys pankeille annettujen pomatakuiden kautta. Edelleen rakennemuutoksia  toimialajrjestelyit  on lisntyvsti odotettavissa. Pankkirakenteiden lisksi liiketoimintamallit ovat voimakkaassa muutoksessa. Viimeisen vuosikymmenen aikana erityisen nopeasti kehittynyt ja kasvanut "mynn laina ja siirr sen luottoriski" -malli ("originate and distribute") sek thn olennaisesti liittynyt erilaisten velka-ja johdannaisinstrumenttien tehtailu trmsi betoniseinn. Riski ei hvinnyt siirrolla ja hajauttamisella vaan joutui paikkoihin, joissa sen hallintaan ei ollut kyky. Malli johti riskien kokonaismrn hallitsemattomaan lisntymiseen, kun sit ji eri tavoin valvonnan ulkopuolelle. Talouskasvu taittuu Maailmantaloudessa oli hidastumisen merkkej jo ennen rahoitusmarkkinoiden kriisin alkamista. Rahoitusmarkkinoiden hirit ovat entisestn vahvistaneet talouden hidastumista. Erityisesti yritykset ovat joutuneet niden hiriiden vlittymiskanaviksi. Rahoitusehtojen kiristyminen vaikuttaa kaikkiin talouden toimijoihin. Rahoituksen kallistuminen nostaa investointien tuottovaatimuksia yrityksiss, ja monet aikaisemmin lupaavina pidetyt suunnitelmat nyttvt nyt huonoilta. Toteutetut investoinnit eivt ehk ole niin kannattavia kuin hankkeeseen ryhdyttess laskettiin, koska rahoituskustannukset muodostuvat nyt odotettua pahemmaksi rasitteeksi. Yritysrahoituksen hinta on noussut ja sen saatavuus on heikentynyt. Investointeja onkin jouduttu lykkmn ja tilauksia perumaan. Rahoituksen saatavuudessa saattaa ilmet aiempaa suurempia vaikeuksia, kun muun muassa yritysten omat taseet heikkenevt laskusuhdanteessa ja laskevat yritysten luottokelpoisuutta. Pankkien halukkuus rahoittaa riskialttiina pitmin investointeja on selvsti vhentynyt. Talousnkymt Rahoituksen saamista vaikeampi ongelma suomalaisille yrityksille on viennin nopea supistuminen, joka on seurausta maailmantalouden kasvun hidastumisesta. Viimeisimmt Elinkeinoelmn keskusliiton suhdannekatsauksen tiedot kertovat tilauskannan romahtaneen loppuvuodesta 2008. (Kalvo 2: BKT-ennusteet vuodelle 2009) Vuotta 2009 koskevat talousennusteet noudattavat selke trendi: mit tuoreempi ennuste on, sit synkemmlt tuleva talouskehitys nytt. Mys maailmankaupan nhdn supistuvan, mill on seurauksia vientivetoisille maille kuten Suomelle. Kriisin alkupuolella esitetty toive Aasian nousevien talouksien pelastavasta vaikutuksesta Yhdysvallan kysynnn supistumisen korvaajana ei ole toteutumassa. Mys luottamusindikaattorit ovat historiallisen alhaalla. Sama laskusuhdanne nkyy kaikilla mantereilla. Voidaan siis puhua maailmanlaajuisesta taantumasta. Maailmantalouden lhivuosien kehityssuunta onkin oman taloutemme kannalta oleellista. Vaihtoehdot ovat kuvattavissa eri kirjainten avulla: V, U ja L. Niin sanottu V-malli on malleista positiivisin ja kuvaa nopeaa nousua taantumasta uuteen kasvuun. U-kirjain kuvaa hieman pidemp taantumaan, jonka jlkeen politiikkatoimet alkavat vaikuttaa ja kasvu on taas melko nopeaa. Yhten vaihtoehtona, jota kuvaa L-kirjain, on pidempi taantuma tai jopa lama. Riskit thn kehitykseen ovat lisntyneet. Riippumatta siit, mik edell mainituista talousnkymist toteutuu, olisi vastuutonta, ett olettaisimme talouden kntyvn itsestn. Meidn on omalla toiminnallamme pyrittv aktiivisesti vaikuttamaan siihen, ett olipa kehitys V-, U-tai L-mallin mukainen, selvimme mahdollisimman vhin vaurioin. Poikkeuksellisia toimia keskuspankeilta Julkinen valta on puuttunut poikkeuksellisella voimalla markkinoiden toimintaan. Viime aikoina on uutisoitu sek keskuspankkien pumppaavan rahaa markkinoille ett eri maiden hallitusten massiivisista elvytyspaketeista. Keskuspankit ovat olleet liikkeell tulivoimaisella kalustolla. Markkinakorot ovat seuranneet mukana, mik on luonnollisesti helpottanut velallisten asemaa ja vhentnyt rahoituskustannuksia. Kaikki keskuspankit ovat lisnneet mys rahoituksen tarjontaa ja pidentneet maturiteettia. Euroopan keskuspankin rahapolitiikan toimeenpanomekanismia on mys muutettu likviditeetti vahvistavaan suuntaan. Markkinoiden on annettu itse mritt likviditeetin taso. EKP tarjoaa pankeille lyhtyaikaista luottoa vakuuksia vastaan niin paljon kuin ne tarvitsevat. Pankit ovatkin varautuneet tilanteen pahenemiseen lismll keskuspankkivelkaansa ja tallettamalla varoja yli yn -talletuksina keskuspankkiin. Kun talletuksesta saa yhden prosenttiyksikn matalamman koron kuin mit rahalaitos maksaa keskuspankista ottamastaan lainasta, on tllainen valmiuskassan varmistaminen oman maksukykyns turvaamiseksi kaikissa tilanteissa poikkeuksellisen kallista. Hallitusten jret toimet Eri maiden hallitukset ovat toimineet jrein ottein kriisivaikutusten torjumiseksi ja varmistaakseen rajoitusjrjestelmn hirittmyyden. Yhdysvalloissa pelastusohjelman suuruus ylitt 2 000 miljardia dollaria. Euroopassa pankkien varainhankinnan takaukset ovat 2 000 miljardia euroa ja pomitukset 250 miljardia euroa. Suomessa hallitus on varautunut takaamaan jopa 50 miljardin euron edest pankkien vakuudetonta varainhankintaa. Tosin meill ei nykytietmyksen valossa ole ensimmistkn pankkia, joka tarvitsisi tai olisi yliptn halukas tllaista takausta kyttmn. Pankkien pomittamiseenkin valtion varoin on Suomessa varauduttu varmuuden vuoksi. Suomessa pankkien maksuvalmius ja vakavaraisuus ovat pysyneet kansainvlisess vertailussa hyvin. Silti on haaste, pystyvtk pankit korvaamaan kansainvlisten lainamarkkinoiden kuivumisen kotimaisella luotonannolla. Yhteiskunnan intressiss on, ett pankit ovat valmiita ottamaan vastaan valtion pomasijoituksia ja takuita. Julkinen tuki on tietysti aina vastikkeellista, mutta ehdot eivt saa olla liian ankaria. Pasia on oltava, ett rahoitusmarkkinoiden toimintakyky palautuu. Kansantalouden ei pid antaa ajautua kierteeseen, jossa luottoja ei kannata mynt lhestyvn laskukauden pelossa ja jossa laskukausi on tulossa siksi, ettei investointeihin ole saatavissa rahoitusta. Juuri tllaisten tilanteiden vlttmiseen massiiviset valtiontakaukset ja pomitukset on tarkoitettu. Sen johdosta nihin liittyvien ehtojen tulee olla sellaiset, ett pankit voivat mys niit kytt terveen luotonannon yllpitmiseen. Useissa maissa on esille noussut ajatuksia omaisuudenhoitoyhtiiden eli roskapankkien perustamiseksi ja ohjelmia pankkien ongelmasaamisten ostamiseksi. Rahoitusmarkkinoiden toiminnan varmistamiseen liittyvi, ratkaistavia ongelmia ovat hinnoittelu, kilpailuvaikutukset ja tuen ehdollisuus. Siit huolimatta, ett valtion toimenpiteet on tarpeellista toteuttaa pikaisesti, toimenpiteiden on oltava hyvin harkittuja ja on varmistettava, ett luottoriskiptsten teko silyy finanssijrjestelmll itselln. Kannattaa pit mieless Japanin esimerkki. Maassa ei tehty tarvittavia tervehdyttmistoimia pankkijrjestelmn rakenteiden ja valtion rahoittaman omaisuudenhoitoyhtin perustamiseksi kuin monen vuoden jlkeen. Se pitkitti kriisi ja lissi kustannuksia koko yhteiskunnalle. Pankkijrjestelmss on uskallettava tehd ikvi toimenpiteit nopeasti, jotta todellinen toipuminen psee kyntiin. Keinot kohtiparempaa taloustilannetta Kriisist ulospsy on vaikeaa. Tulevaisuuden rakentamista hidastaa vaikeiden aikojen tuoreet kokemukset sek pelko tehd uusia reippaita toimia, jottei uudelle kriisille kylvettisi siemeni. Kriisi edeltvn maailmaan ei ole paluuta, sill viime vuosien talouskasvu rakentui maailmantalouden suurten tasapainottomuuksien varaan: Aasian ylijmien, Yhdysvaltojen velkaantumisen ja koko maailman rahoitusjrjestelmn harjoittaman riskien aliarvioinnin varaan. rakennelma ei kestnyt suhdanteiden heikkenemist, ja nyt on kasvun peruta etsittv muualta. Kriisin pitkittymisen estmiseen ja talouden elvyttmiseen on laaja keinovalikoima. Yleisen lhtkohtana elvytystoimille on ollut, ett toimenpiteet ovat vlittmi, valikoituja ja vliaikaisia. Tavallisimpia keinoja ovat investoinnit infrastruktuuriin ja asuntotuotantoon. Valtion takaukset, luotot ja verokevennykset ovat mys laajalti kytss. Ne maat, jotka ovat alijmisi, vaativat rajuimpia elvytystoimia ylijmmailta, kuten Saksalta. Suomen elvytyksell ei luonnollisestikaan ole vastaavanlaista globaalia vaikutusta kuin Saksalla. (Kalvo 3: Julkisen talouden tasapaino eriss EU-maissa) Julkiset taloudet joutuvat kyttmn varoja yli tavanomaisen kestokykyns. Kolmen prosentin tilapinen alijm julkisessa taloudessa voidaan luokitella viel terveeksi, mutta nykyiselln tm raja on monissa talouksissa ylittynyt tai ylittymss. Kyseess eivt ole vain pienet maat vaan mys suuremmat kansantaloudet. Suuret alijmt johtavat tilanteeseen, jossa valtioidentaloudet tulee tasapainottaa krsivllisesti vain pitkll aikavlill ja vltt liian tiukkaa finanssipolitiikkaa talousvaikeuksien aikana. Olennaista on mys varmistaa, ett alijmien menoert eivt aiheuta pysyvi mekanismeja vaan ovat esimerkiksi kertaluontoisia investointeja. Ulospsyyn on luonnollinen tie vasta, kun kasvu lhtee liikkeelle ja tukee alijmien supistamista. Jottei taantuma pitkittyisi, on rahoitusmarkkinoiden toimintakyky joka tapauksessa palautettava. Julkisen vallan vaikutuksen lisntyminen pankkitoiminnassa on ollut vlttmtnt vakauden varmistamiseksi, mutta vaarana voi jatkossa olla kilpailun vristyminen ja tehottomuus. Kansainvlisess talouspolitiikassa onkin tll hetkell suuri koordinaation tarve, jotteivt kansalliset pelastusohjelmat pirsto jo yhdentyneit rahoitusmarkkinoita ja kansainvlinen protektionismi levi. Rajat ylittv rahoitustoiminta on joka tapauksessa uusien haasteiden edess. Jos kansainvliset rahoitusmarkkinat eivt toimi tyydyttvsti integroituneina, siit koituu vahinkoa etenkin pienille ja avoimille talouksille kuten Suomelle. Todellinen uhkakuva olisikin kansallisten rahoitusmarkkinoiden paluu. Ellei markkinoiden toimintakyky pystyt kansainvlisin toimin palauttamaan, maat joutuvat tekemn oman asemansa turvaamiseksi kansallisia toimia, jotka vaikeuttavat kansainvlisten markkinoiden tilaa entisestn. Mikli nin ky, on mys Suomessa reagoitava. Auttaako valvonta? Samaan aikaan kansainvlisell tasolla etsitn kriisin syit ja keinoja vastaavien tapahtumien ennaltaehkisyyn. Yksi johtopts on selv  finanssimarkkinoilla kaivataan lis lpinkyvyytt ja tehokkaampaa kansainvlist valvontaa ja yhteistyt. (Kalvo 4: Henkilt) Rahoitusalan toimijat ja tutkijat ovat esittneet erilaisia ratkaisuja, miten valvojilla tulisi olla tiukempi ote rahoitustoiminnasta. On ehdotettu, ett monimutkaisten finanssi-innovaatioiden kirjo pitisi supistaa standardoituihin tuotteisiin, joilla kauppaa kytisiin esimerkiksi prsseiss. Lisksi on vaadittu, ett rahalaitosten pomaa ja vaatimuksia pit kirist ja erilaiset taseen ulkopuoliset ert ja erillisyhtit on huomioitava. Ehdotukset ovat perusteltuja. On kuitenkin pystyttv varmistamaan, etteivt ne johda liiallisiin kustannuksiin ja takaperoiseen kehitykseen. Finanssituotteiden standardoiminen ei saa olla liian pitklle viety, jotta innovoinnille ja rahoitusmarkkinoiden tehostamiselle j tilaa. Toisaalta valvontaa ei kannata kuormittaa sellaisella tyll, joka lis valvottavien kuluja, mutta ei vlttmtt paranna riskien ennaltaehkisy. Lpinkyvyyden eli tiedonantovelvoitteiden lisminen lienee tehokkain tapa edist markkinoiden luottamusta ja samaan aikaan yllpit tehokkuutta. Pomavaatimuksia, mukaan lukien likviditeettipuskurointia, ei tule kirist tarpeettomasti, jotta rahoituskustannukset eivt kasva kohtuuttomasti. Taseen ulkopuolisten erien ja erillisyhtiiden sntelyss huomioitava lainkiertmisen mahdollisuudet ja tst johtuvat kielteiset seuraamukset kaikkeen rahoitustoimintaan. Rahoituslaitosten kansainvlinen toiminta edellytt tehostamista valvonnassa. Ylikansallista valvontaa tulee vahvistaa varmistamalla rajat ylittv toimivalta valvontaviranomaisille. Euroopassa on tyn alla mm. de Larosire .tyryhmn, eurojrjestelmn, CEPS:n jne. toimesta eurooppalaisen, kansallisiin valvontavastuisiin perustuvan valvonnan kehittminen. Mahdollisia pvaihtoehtoja ovat 1) nykyisen kansallisten valvojien yhteistyn lisminen joko valvontaryhmien (colleges) tai komiteoiden (CEBS, CESR ja CEIOPS) juridista ja toimivaltaa listen, 2) valvontayhteistyn rakentaminen Euroopan keskuspankkijrjestelmn kaltaiseksi, European System of Financial Supervisors, jolla on keskuselin ja kansalliset valvontaviranomaiset hoitavat valvonnan alueillaan taikka 3) antamalla Euroopan keskuspankille suurten kansainvlisten rahalaitosten valvontavastuu. Jo tmn kevn aikana on odotettavissa ptksi valvonnan kehittmisen linjauksista. Larosiren tyryhmn raportti valmistuu maaliskuussa, G20-maiden toimet on aikataulutettu niin, ett ptsesityksi ksitelln huhtikuussa. Aika on kaikkinensa otollinen valvontarakenteiden parantamiselle. Lopuksi Tt ja ensi vuotta koskevat talousennusteet ovat huonontuneet. Kaikissa maissa ja kaikilla talousalueille koko maailmassa kauppa on hidastunut, kasvu taittunut ja tyttmyys nousee. Talouspolitiikan haasteena on nyt sovittaa yhteen toimet, joiden vaikutukset ovat vlittmi ja kohdennettuja, mutta jotka eivt rapauta pitkn aikavlin pysyvmmn kasvun edellytyksi. Talouden haasteet koskevat koko yhteiskuntaa. Tnn jaetaan tieteellisen tutkimuksen apurahoja. Tutkimuksen tukemiselle on hyvt perusteet mys vaikeina aikoina. Poikkeuksellisina aikoina eivt nimittin totutut toimintatavat riit, vaan on mentv syvemmlle, peruskysymyksiin. Juuri siksi tutkimuksen merkitys korostuu. Vaikka tutkimus ei antaisikaan suoria vastauksia talouspoliittisiin tai muihin ajankohtaisiin ongelmiin, niin tutkimuksesta kuitenkin versovat ne uudet ideat, joiden varaan tulevaisuus rakennetaan. Tm koskee yht hyvin talouspolitiikkaa kuin teknologiaa, liiketoimintaa kuin ihmistieteitkin.

Let me start by saying a few words about where we are now in the financial crisis and how it has come about. (Slide 1: How did the financial crisis unfold?) The functioning of financial markets affects the functioning of the real economy. Similarly, it is also myss otherwise; the state of the economy and the state of the economy affect how well the financial system works. Since Director General Jukka Pekkarinen's presentations on the oNational Economy and Finlando, I will discuss general economic issues and focus on the financial markets. In the midst of the gloomy economic news, it is good to remember that the current financial crisis is by no means the first, but that various crises, collapses and panics have been experienced before. The end result has always been the same d crisis has been overcome. Chch describes himself well by Hyman Minsky in his book Stabilising an unstable economy (1986). In fact, there are more than a hundred local banking crises in the world, from the 70s to lshtien. The emergence of Hsiriside (Slide 2. Risky bank markets in the euro area) The crisis originated in the US subprime mortgage market and quickly spread to other financial markets. The evolution of interest rates on the banks' markets reveals the timing of the crisis. Strictly speaking, on 9 August 2007, interest rates rose and euro area banks began to demand a particularly high-risk d margin on their d medium-sized unsecured loans. The efficient short-term money market for banks in Chechnya has been based precisely on unsecured transactions, loans and deposits. The reference rate euribor, which is also used in Finland, describes precisely the interest rate on the unsecured credit market. Margins on unsecured and secured financing, i.e. the so-called "greenback". the risk liquors had been lshes in all credit grades a few tenths of a percent and hundredths, i.e. lshes non-existent. The crisis was exacerbated last autumn, when risk premiums jumped by as much as 4% to one in the United States and by more than 2% to one in Europe. Since then, of course, the risks have clearly narrowed, but they are still exceptional. Hsiris is still at the very heart of the financial system. The business of banks is changing The financial markets are being restructured in the banking sector. In the United States, the industry has changed as fundamentally as it did during the Finnish banking crisis 15 years ago. The main housing finance institutions are federally owned and investment banking as a separate industry has ceased to exist. Yllstsvsss is that several first-class banks ran into great difficulties. In Europe, too, many banks have been subsidized, even nationalised. Further structural changes in d the organisation of the sector d are to be expected. Banks' own business models are also undergoing a change. Over the past decade, the "originate and distribute" model of "mysnns loan and transfer credit risk" has developed and grown particularly rapidly, as well as the factories of various debt and derivative instruments in concrete walls. The risk did not come from transfer and decentralisation, but ended up in places where there was no ability to manage it. The model led to an uncontrolled increase in the overall risk, as it was variously excluded from control. (Slide 3: Banking in Compression: odeleveragingo) Banks' balance sheets are under pressure. Write-downs of securities and other assets, as well as the strong deleveraging of leveraging, weaken the lending capacity of banks. Financial conditions are weakened by the financial sector The global economy was already experiencing a slowdown before the start of the financial market crisis. The tightening of financing conditions affects all economic operators. Rising financial prices are raising the return on investment requirements for companies, and many plans that were previously considered promising are now looking bad. The investments made will not be as profitable as was calculated when entering the project, as the cost of financing is now a worse burden than expected. The availability of corporate finance has decreased. Greater difficulties arise when firms' own balance sheets deteriorate in a downturn and reduce their creditworthiness. The willingness of banks to finance investment is likely to weaken the economy. In the worst case scenario, investments will have to be postponed and orders will have to be cancelled. Central banks active The government has intervened with extraordinary force in the functioning of the financial markets. Recently, there have been reports of central banks pumping money into the market and of massive stimulus packages from governments in different countries. The central banks have been in circulation with firepower. The actions have been conscious and international coordination has worked well. The already normally lively dialogue between the various central banks has only intensified over the course of the crisis. Interest rates have been cut even at the same time, which can be considered historical. (Slide 4: The price of secured and unsecured money in the euro area interbank market) The European Central Bank has cut the key interest rate five times in recent months. The Fed, the Bank of England and the Swedish Riksbanken have cut interest rates more. Market interest rates have followed suit, which has naturally eased the position of debtors and reduced financing costs. (Kalvo 5: ECB:n liquiditytioperaatiot) In addition to the fall in interest rates, central banks have also increased the supply of finance and extended maturity. The European Central Bank's monetary policy enforcement mechanism includes the level of liquidity provided by the markets themselves. The ECB provides banks with short-term credit against collateral for as much as they need. Banks are therefore preparing for a worsening of the situation by increasing their central bank debt and depositing funds in the form of over-ysn deposits with the central bank. When you get one percent lower interest rate on a deposit than the MFI pays for a loan it borrows from a central bank, it is expensive to have a ready-to-use fund. Massive government actions (Slide 6: Treasury investments and guarantees) Their governments have acted with great vigour to mitigate the effects of the crisis. In the United States and Europe, rescue programmes are large and extensive in the past. The national economy should not be allowed to fall into a spiral in which credit is not worthwhile for fear of a downturn and in which a downturn is coming because of the lack of funding for investment. (Slide 7. Bank withdrawals with public funds and their maximum in countries) It is precisely for this kind of situation that massive state guarantees and pssomitus are intended. As a result, the conditions attached to this must be such that banks can also use them to maintain sound lending. In Finland, banks' liquidity and solvency have remained well in international comparison. Nevertheless, it is a challenge to ensure the drying up of the international corporate lending market through domestic lending. It is therefore in the interest of society that banks are prepared to finance companies in order to ensure their activities in the event of unforeseen events and to accept government investments and guarantees. Of course, public support is always remunerated, but the conditions must not be too strict. The objective is the functioning of the financial markets. Bank systems to intervene in structures (Slide 8: Bank write-offs and own balance sheet dated 24.2.2009) In the balance sheets of MFIs, write-downs and pssoma needs have led to extensive ownership arrangements. In several countries, ideas have emerged to set up asset management companies, i.e. junk banks, and programmes to buy banks' problem assets. The problems to be solved in order to ensure the functioning of financial markets are pricing, competitive effects and conditionality of aid. Nevertheless, there is a need for urgent state intervention, the measures must be well thought out and it must be ensured that the credit risk decision is made in accordance with the financial system itself. The example of Japan is worthwhile. The country did not take the necessary reorganisation measures to set up banking structures and a state-funded asset management company until many years later. It prolonged the crisis and increased the costs to society as a whole. It is necessary to have the courage to take measures quickly in order to achieve a real recovery. In the context of the financial crisis, the new environment It is not easy to get out of a crisis, because the construction of the future can be slowed down by the fresh experience of difficult times and the fear of taking new vigorous action so as not to sow seeds for a new crisis. There will be no return to the financial world in the run-up to the crisis. The exceptional volume of funding was based on major imbalances: the indebtedness of asia, the indebtedness of the United States and the underpricing of risks by the global financial system. In addition to the influence of public authorities in banking, it is necessary to ensure stability. However, there may be a risk that competition will become more intense and inefficient in the future. Indeed, there is a great need for coordination in international economic policy at the moment, so that national rescue programmes do not fragment the already integrated financial markets and protectionism spread. If international financial markets do not function satisfactorily integrated, this will be to the detriment of small and open economies such as Finland in particular. The real threat would therefore be the return of national financial markets. Tighter controls (Slide 13. Persons who have been subject to additional supervision) At international level, one of the leaders is clear d the financial markets need more capacity and more effective supervision and cooperation. Financial actors and researchers have come up with different solutions on how supervisors should have a tighter grip on financial activities. It has been suggested that the range of complex financial innovations should be reduced to standardised products, such as the market. In addition, it has been required that the PFI's psoma and requirements be tightened for a long period of time and that various off-balance-sheet items and separate associations be taken into account. The proposals are justified. However, it is possible to ensure that they do not lead to excessive costs and backward developments. The standardisation of financial products must not be too long in order to make room for innovation and the intensification of financial markets. On the other hand, it is not a good idea to burden the controls with a kind of work that increases the costs of the supervisees, but does not improve the risk prevention. Increasing the level of transparency, i.e. information obligations, is probably the most effective way of promoting market confidence and, at the same time, efficiency. There should be no undue tightening of the financial requirements, including liquidity buffering, in order to avoid an unreasonable increase in financing costs. In the case of off-balance-sheet items and separate companies, the possibilities of circumvention of the law and the negative consequences for all financial activities must be taken into account. The international operation of financial institutions requires enhanced supervision. Supranational supervision must be strengthened by ensuring cross-border powers for the supervisory authorities. In Europe, european committees such as the de Larosizre working group, the euro system and the EU committees have been working on the development of European supervision. Already during this period, a decision on the guidelines for the development of supervision is to be expected. The report of the Larosizre group was completed in March, the G20 activities are scheduled so that they will be presented in April. The time is all right for improving the control structures. Finally The financial crisis will come out in due course. This needs to be balanced against the massive efforts to be made and the sufficiency of the funds needed for the long term. The efforts of central banks and governments to intervene in the financial system are therefore very difficult. If mistakes are made, the rescue will happen. Nevertheless, they must have the courage to take the initiative to ensure that the financial markets do not hit the real economy with force. At the same time, the Company will ensure that no new Hsiris is created. Financial systems have moved from exceptionally cheap and easy times to a tighter time. This is due to a tightening of the conditions for financing and a reduction in availability. In business financing, be prepared for the fact that the challenging period may continue for a longer period. The situation will only stabilise when the real economy recovers. text: Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen: Reorganisation of the funding system. Kallavesi.seminar, 30.3.2009 Kuopio . Speech . Monday30 March 2009, 12:00 AM Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen, Bank of Finland KALLAVESI SEMINAR 2009 oMiten from North Savo to the worldo 30.3.2009 Kuopio. Speech reference. Speech liittyvst Membranes (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and. . interviews/documents/30032009_pentti_hakkarainen_kuopio.pdf) (PDF) REORGANISATION OF THE FINANCIAL SERVICES SYSTEM oThe economic downturn will be overcome in due course. However, a return to the conditions of strong economic growth of a few years ago should not be longed for, as they were based on the soaring economic growth of the world economy and the financial balance between the various economies and the high level of indebtedness of the various national economies and many economic operators," says Pentti Hakkarainen, Vice-President of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Finland. According to Hsne, after difficult times, it is necessary to adapt to the new era, especially in the financial sector. "The management of the financial crisis must balance the massive efforts made by the financial crisis with the need for a long period of time. Central banks and governments must be courageous in their efforts to ensure that the financial markets do not hit the real economy with force. At the same time, the shortcomings of the pitss monitoring and ssnging that have emerged will be corrected," says Hakkarainen. oThe financial system will enter a new phase and the excesses underlying the financial crisis will be eliminated. The strong economic development provided a breeding ground for the expansion of financial activities. Indeed, the financial industry grew faster than other industries and the general economy. The contraction in world trade and industrial production has slowed down. Since the crisis, the state of the financial markets has improved substantially," said Pentti Hakkarainen, Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Finland, in his speech at the unveiling of the 100th anniversary of Maaningan Osuuspankki. "Although the worst economic pitfalls have already been overcome, we are still in difficult waters and short-term setbacks are possible." The global economy is undergoing major structural changes. Economic growth priorities are shifting to Asia and other emerging economies. At the same time, the conditions for the success of various industries are changing. For example, commodity and energy prices have remained high even during the global recession. It is obvious that we will have to operate in new circumstances. Banks operating in Finland have weathered the financial market crisis well. Their solvency and profitability are on average better than those of European banks. The recession has been transmitted to Finland through the export market, i.e. the real sector. Banks are taking the brunt of the recession through the financial condition of their customers. Another challenge is low interest rates. It has been justified in the cyclical situation. However, it reduces banks' net interest income, the core income of basic banking. From the point of view of the Finnish economy, it is of paramount importance for companies to pay in the export market. As an export-dependent industrialised country, Finland experienced the effects of the collapse of world trade particularly strongly. Hakkarainen points out that it is important to ensure that competitiveness is strengthened. Cooperation ensures well-being The export dependence of the economy can also be viewed from the regional angle: "When a municipality is not directly dependent on the demand for only one product or on exports and, through it, on fluctuations in the global economy, it can be possible to cope with a difficult economic situation. However, this presupposes that the affairs of one's own municipality are handled in an exemplary manner and that cooperation with the regions is known." Hakkarainen stressed that North Savo has the potential for excellent cooperation. Maaninka offers its inhabitants a safe, comfortable and clean environment, as well as short opportunities for services and places in larger localities. A country can be a growing municipality if it maintains its vitality and close links with Siilinjsrve and Kuopio and the service and education offered by them and the region as a whole. Siilinjsrvi and Kuopio play a key role in Maaninga's success. The competition for where the trained vski will live and work in the future is becoming more and more intense and the level of demands is increasing. A wide range of stimuli is required for good action and living conditions. In addition to the traditional nature, people are looking for nice social networks and good cultural and hobby services. This is not something that a municipality can offer on its own, but it is a package of the whole sub-region that has been developed together. In order to strengthen the well-being of the region, cooperation must be carried out without prejudice at all levels, both in municipal administration and in the business sector. Networking between companies is particularly important when it comes to seeking a wider market. There is a possibility of reforming work models. The development of the nature of the work can be used to support the employment situation in the region. We are not just talking about the possibility of etching, but technological advances make it possible for people to communicate and communicate flexibly in real time, as well as the importance of physical physicality. Entire parts of the tys chain can be produced regardless of location, including in services that require a high level of expertise, such as elderly care. Taking into account the need to diversify the economic structure, consider the opportunities for developing the connections of companies in the region with the University of Kuopio. Experience shows that universities play an incalculable role as catalysts for knowledge-based economic growth. One problem d not only in Northern Savonia but throughout Finland d is that very few young people with higher education become entrepreneurs. Based on their local knowledge, the banks in the region could help to build contacts for idea-rich young people and encourage entrepreneurs.

Title: Economic Outlook 20092011
text: Deputy Governor Pentti Hakkarainen: Economic Outlook 2009d2011. Helsinki Diplomatic Association political lunch 30 November 2009 . Speech . Monday30 November 2009,12:00AM Deputy Governor Pentti Hakkarainen Helsinki Diplomatic Association political lunch Helsinki 30 November 2009 Slides (PDF) (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and. interviews/documents/091130_ph_hda.pdf) MAIN POINTS OF THE LUNCHEON SPEECH: ECONOMIC OUTLOOK 2009d2011 Globally andin Europe The global economy has shown some signs of stabilising. In the large economies of Asia economic growth has remained brisk. In the third quarter of the current year, output also began to grow in many developed economies. The state of the financial markets has improved fundamentally since the spring. Government measures to stabilise the financial markets have proved a success, they made it possible to prevent a collapse of the financial system. The lowering of policy interest rates by central banks was necessary to stabilise the financial markets. The expansionary impact of fiscal policy has also been considerable. In many European countries, automatic fiscal policy stabilizers have cushioned the negative impacts on domestic demand and employment from the collapse in world trade. Given the scale of the global economy, it has been an important feature that fiscal policy has been relaxed simultaneously in different parts of the world. Fiscal and monetary policy have worked together to support economic recovery. The fact the economic situation is stabilised does not mean the economy will quickly return to the status quo before the crisis. Growing public debt is causing increasing concerns over the sustainability of the public finances. Finland and her economy According to the Bank of Finland forecast annual GDP volume will contract 7,2 % this year, remain unchanged next year and grow 1,6 % in 2011. Based on the forecast Finnish GDP in 2011 will still be well below the level of 2008. It is possible there will be no return to the earlier trend in GDP. As an industrial economy dependent on exports, the collapse in world trade has hit Finland particularly hard. The scale of the slump in Finnish exports was due partly by the fact that the bulk of exports consists of capital goods (and their components). The Finnish economy will likely recover later and more slowly than many others. The fundamentals for a positive export development are in place since companieso balance sheets are healthy and they use modern advanced technology in their production and currently there is some unused capacity available. There is, however, no reason to simply assume that recovery in the world economy will automatically restore things to how they were before the recession. As in other countries, the accumulation of debt by the public sector in Finland is justified to soften the impact of the recession. A sustained period of increasing indebtedness is, however, not possible. Before long it will be necessary to reach a sustainable level of public debt in relation the GDP.

Title: The economy is part of national security
text: Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen: The economy as part of national security. Security Policy Seminar, Kajaani 27.3.2010 . Speech . Saturday 27March 2010, 12:00 AM Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen, Bank of Finland Security Policy Seminar Kajaani 27.3.2010 Minister, good people of Kainuu, ladies and gentlemen It is a pleasure to come to Kajaani. For the first time in matters of security policy, Kajaani became familiar with the army, the Kainuu Brigade, where I was conscripted. I'm also familiar with Kajaani, because I've been able to move around often and I've gotten a lot of good friends through it. My topic is The economy as part of national security. I will examine the importance of the economy for national security from the central banker's nsks angle. Tsms is, of course, a narrow nskskulma. Hopefully, however, it will be in line with previous introductions, which together have covered a wide range of economic and security policy areas. An economy at the bottom of the economy provides security. This is the case for every person, every company and the state as a whole. It comes to security threats, crises and wars, which is very often a matter of economic interest. A faltering economy increases the country's dependence on foreign policies and may even jeopardise the security of the guerrillas. When the state's economy is in order, the financial system is functioning and citizens can count on the stable development of their own economy, the conditions for national security are in place. Public finances State security and self-determination require sufficient financial resources. Economic stability is a prerequisite for other stability. Finland is a good example of the importance of a nation's economic development. A couple of centuries ago, Finland was an autonomous part of the Russian Empire. Autonomy was the economic, financial autonomy of pssos. Already at that time, the importance of our own economic management was understood, and financial autonomy also developed into its own political economy. Statesman Johan Vilhelm Snellman's monetary reforms in the 1860s to whichssivst stability. At the same time, the state was revived and the status of the Finnish language was established. It all laid the foundation for self-made and self-determination of Finland. Under Snellman, government indebtedness was reduced. The debt was kept well under control. It was taken only for productive investments, lhinns for the construction of the railway network. The debt was not taken out for consumption. Its mssrs was held in an appropriate proportion to foreign trade and state revenues. In terms of calculations, the ratio of less than 15% of total production was maintained until the beginning of the Guerrilla War. In other respects, too, the management of the economy was exemplary. In 1862, the first bond was issued on the German market. After that, the Finnish government acquired foreign loans in accordance with the sssnnsns with bonds. Nsin acquired foreign pssoma contributed to finland's economic development. Bonds issued in foreign financial centres increase the awareness of Finland. This kind of lssnsolo in the financial markets strengthened Finland's autonomous and, more importantly, sys' position in the financial markets. As an interesting aside from that time, there were many still well-known international bankers and banks at the time. Among them were Rothschild, A.O. Wallenberg and his bank SEB, seks Credit Lyonnais and Bank of New York. Nsms names have remained in finland's loan affairs in modern times. Another interesting observation from history is the assessments already made at that time about the creditworthiness of countries. sms reflects the appreciation that Finland has received. Credit Lyonnais bank classified countries into different categories based on their creditworthiness in 1898. In the best category of borrowing countries, oPays don't les finances sont de premier ordreo included Germany, England, Russia, Switzerland, the United States, Sweden and Denmark, among others, Finland. The second highest category is the Netherlands, Japan, Italy and Austria, for example. In the third category were Brazil, Argentina, Spain and Portugal. After all, the division of nsytss yllstsvsn the same as nsins psivins! Of course, the development of its own economic institutions, such as its own central bank and its own currency, was part of Finland's maturation into national self-sufficiency. What is interesting, however, is that one's own money, the mark, was not used to break away from the rest of the world, but to the other. In the 1800s, the financial world lived first in the conditions of the silver standard and then the gold standard. At that time, national monetary policy, which was separate from the other countries, was not one of the characteristics of the self-state. The ideal of the time was participation in a universal monetary system based on a common measure of value, gold or silver. The aim was to integrate into the international market after the money, the ruble, which had been coined in Finland until then, had proved to be dangerously epsvakaa after the Crimean War and the Polish revolt. Rahoitusjsrjestelms Efficient and reliable operation of the financial system is a key basis for the functioning of society. It is the bloodstream of society and if there are minor blockages or problems, then the lifeblood of society can be seriously affected. Financial markets must be able to function in all circumstances. The recent financial crisis also showed how essential financial management and supervision are. In addition to its own complexity, the fact that the business in the sector is interlinked. In addition, financial activities have become very international everywhere, not in Finland. The operation of an individual MFI can cause serious problems for the entire sector through the Nssytksks, and hsirist can also come from outside the country entirely. The Bank of Finland as a central bank d as a bank of banks d contributes to ensuring the efficient and reliable operation of the financial system. In addition, the Financial Supervisory Authority supervises financial operators, the solvency of banks and insurance companies, as well as the functioning of the securities markets. In addition to the solvency and liquidity of banks and other financial institutions, the effectiveness of payment systems is subject to supervision. The role of the Central Bank is particularly important. Due to the financial system, the financial markets must be prepared for all possible scenarios. It is a key area of national security of supply. In cooperation with the National Emergency Supply Agency, the Bank of Finland has been conducting crisis exercises in the financial sector for a few years. The most recent financial sector exercise, oFATO 2009o, was organised just last autumn and involved more than 70 organisations and more than a thousand people. The importance of the funding system and its individual actors is not exactly an observation or manifestation of recent years. Juho Kusti Paasikivi's books of 14.4.1923, among others, contain an interesting entry. In his discussions with Jakob Wallenberg, he recorded that banks have sufficient risk buffers. It is important to have secret reserves to cover the first losses and to ensure the bank's operations. President Risto Ryti, for his part, stated at the same time that it is not enough for us to have a good money system, and that it is also required that our monetary system be such that it is trusted abroad. As far as foreign contacts are concerned, economic security in today's world certainly does not mean autarchy, isolation from the rest of the world. North Korea, for example, is hardly the safest country in the world, even though it has sought to impose its own economic isolation. As the great son of Kajaani Lyseo, President Urho Kekkonen, said, osecurity is not about putting a fence, but about opening doorso. He stressed the importance of trust and the fact that security is enhanced through international cooperation. Paasikivi, Ryti and Kekkonen's policies are, in the light of the economic crisis, formerly tsrkesmpis. Banks and other financial actors need to be reliable and take into account the international dimension. International and control and related structures will be strengthened. If more workable solutions are found in Finland as well, the better conditions for securing financial stability exist. That is why reforms that seem far-fetched, such as those of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and the European Commission, and even those of President Obama's administration, are moving forward. They include ways to ensure the sound functioning of banks and to strengthen their risk tolerance. This is why there are bank disasters, or at least a reduction in the cost to taxpayers of bank crises. Man in the street In today's world, we are also able to rely on good economic management and the functioning of the financial markets. That's why the question for the man in the street is: Is the worst in Finland over? According to surveys, a Finn responds to the shsn: it is enough. In Finland, however, there is a discrepancy between consumer confidence and the economic figures describing the actual development. The finnish economy is still weaker than most European countries. Finland's economic recovery from the global economic downturn is likely to start more slowly than the average in the euro area. Admittedly, government debt is lower than in many countries, but now, as in the rest of the euro area, indebtedness is d in the middle of the euro area. It is not possible to have a very long period of time in a situation where revenue is not sufficient for expenditure. However, the fact is that consumer confidence has only only strengthened and the economic crisis is not generally felt. Is it because the economic crisis was seen as the result of the difficulties of the international economy and that the development is now favourable? Another impressive factor is probably the fact that the prices and prices of wealth items, such as housing, have risen recently. In addition, for many households with a high income, the situation has improved, with borrowing rates at an exceptionally low level, the prices of many household goods falling and the overall increase in purchasing power. Employment has increased, but so far pelsttys vshemmsn. In other words, many households are doing well together. Consumer confidence has generally been a good predictor of future economic developments. Hopefully even now okansa tietso, and the Finnish consumer is right, despite the gloomy economic figures and the still very weak economic forecasts. Summary I have spoken of the importance of good housekeeping for security and self-efficacy. One current example of a country in financial difficulties is Greece. The country's public finances are in dire straits, there are questions about the condition of the banks and the man in the street is rioting. Greece's economic policy stance threatens to move out of its own control. At the same time, its economic situation has become a matter of common concern for the whole of Europe. The problem is not only the cost of borrowing money. The country must succeed in putting its economy in order. Serious efforts and national decision-makers have demonstrated their readiness to act responsibly. It is in the interests of Europe as a whole that Greece succeeds as far as possible in restoring market confidence and also in taking the necessary economic stabilisation measures. I would like to summarise my point in a few key points: d good economic management is a prerequisite for national security d and self-reliance d d an economic policy that strengthens security is only possible in international cooperation; d In the current economic climate, the priorities for economic security are the restoration of public finances on a long-term basis and the strengthening of international cooperation structures in economic policy in general and in the field of financial supervision in particular. Saturday 27March 2010, 12:00 AM Johtokunnan varapuheenjohtaja Pentti Hakkarainen, Suomen Pankki Turvallisuuspolitiikan seminaari Kajaani 27.3.2010 Arvoisa ministeri, hyvt kainuulaiset, hyvt naiset ja herrat On ilo tulla Kajaaniin. Suomi on hyv esimerkkimaa siit, miten suuri poliittinen merkitys kansakunnan taloudellisella kehityksell on. Pari vuosisataa sitten Suomi oli autonominen osa Venjn keisarikuntaa. Autonomia oli posin taloudellista, finanssiautonomiaa. Jo tuolloin oman taloudenpitomme merkitys ymmrrettiin, ja finanssiautonomian pohjalta kehittyi mys oma poliittinen elm. Sit otettiin vain tuotannollisiin investointeihin, lhinn rautatieverkoston rakentamiseen. Velkaa ei otettu kulutukseen. Sen mr pidettiin sopivassa suhteessa ulkomaankauppaan ja valtion tuloihin. Wallenberg ja hnen pankkinsa SEB, sek Credit Lyonnais ja Bank of New York. Nm nimet ovat pysyneet Suomen laina-asioita hoitamassa nykypiviin. Toinen mielenkiintoinen havainto historiasta on jo tuolloin tehdyt arviot maiden luottokelpoisuudesta. Tm kertoo Suomen saamasta arvostuksesta. Credit Lyonnais -pankki luokitteli maita eri kategorioihin niiden luottokelpoisuuden perusteella vuonna 1898. Parhaassa velanottajamaiden luokassa Pays dont les finances sont de premier ordre oli muun muassa Saksan, Englannin, Venjn, Sveitsin, Yhdysvaltojen, Ruotsin ja Tanskan joukossa Suomi.
