Title: Unifying Financial Sector Supervision  Finlands Experience
text: Deputy Governor Pentti Hakkarainen: Unifying Financial Sector Supervision Finlandos Experience. Bilateral meeting at Banka Slovenije, Ljubljana 19 July 2010 . Speech . Monday19 July2010,12:00AM Deputy Governor Pentti Hakkarainen, Bank of Finland Summary of the presentation at Banka Slovenije 19 July 2010 Slides (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and.. interviews/documents/190710_pentti_hakkarainen_-_banka_slovenije.ppt)(ppt) Slides (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and.. interviews/documents/100719_pentti_hakkarainen_banka_slovenije.pdf) (pdf) UNIFYING FINANCIAL SECTOR SUPERVISION FINLANDoS EXPERIENCE My intention today is to present an overview of our experience of unifying the financial supervision. The new Financial Supervisory Authority is at the same time an independent institution and an integral part of the Bank of Finland. This may sound like a contradiction in terms, but I will explain later why it is not. It is less than two years since the escalation of the financial crisis in September 2008. We all remember the collapse of Lehman Brothers and the subsequent rescue of the American International Group (AIG) by the US authorities. In the euro area, heads of state and government as well as central bank governors held emergency meetings to prevent a collapse of the banking system. Not only banks but even some countries like Iceland faced unprecedented problems, with repercussions all over Europe. In Finland, our financial supervision authority had to take special actions on the branches of the Icelandic banks operating in our country. The financial system as a whole, however, remained stable. Due to the potential adverse effects of global financial market disturbances, people were nevertheless nervous. This was reflected in a temporary increase in the currency in circulation. Preparations for managing a worsening situation pushed us to work hard. At the Bank of Finland and at the Financial Supervision Authority this was a truly hectic time. Our cooperation with the Ministry of Finance was also intense, when new legislation was put forward to parliament in order to guarantee the stability of the financial system. Internationally, we are still in a mode of crisis management, and it is too early to evaluate the success of our ongoing work. There are, however, serious questions to be asked about how we got into the financial mess. From a central banking and supervision perspective, we should look at the work that we did, and we should not hesitate to try to identify what we possibly have done wrong, and what we should do better in the future. One and perhaps the most important lesson of the lessons from the financial crisis is the need to ensure that important activities and trends do not escape the eyes of supervisors. Another lesson is that supervision should not suffer from inadequate coordination between central banks and financial supervisors. This second lesson implies that there was not enough dialogue between micro and macro supervision, and that micro-supervisorso knowledge of the risk exposures of individual institutions was not available to macro-supervisors. The third lesson is that the authorities responsible for the financial stability must have appropriate powers to act promptly if needed. Let me now turn to the unfolding of the financial and economic crises, and some conclusions that we at the Bank of Finland feel should be made. The different phases of a financial and economic crisis typically follow the pattern which starts from growing indebtedness, leads to the bursting of the asset price bubble, is followed by a banking crisis and as a result, bank lending dries up. The final phase is a sovereign debt crisis, with potential feedback to the banking sector and renewal of the banking crisis. The point here is that successfully preventing this chain of events from occurring requires intensive cooperation between various authorities. One of the main functions of the central banks is to provide sufficient liquidity to the financial system. Although this is of course of utmost importance, it is not, by itself, sufficient to extinguish all flames of the big "financial fire". As we all know, the tightly interlinked financial systems of today require international cooperation to safeguard financial stability. The financial crisis has intensified the development of common euro area and EU supervisory frameworks. The Bank of Finland monitors the financial system as a whole and its objective is to maintain stable, reliable and effective financial and payment systems in Finland. The Financial Supervisory Authority (FIN-FSA), operating in connection with the Bank of Finland, supervises individual banks, insurance companies and securities markets, i.e. covering all the relevant institutions operating in the financial markets. FIN-FSA was founded in 2009, but its predecessor, called the Financial Supervision Authority, was connected to the Bank of Finland already in 1993. In 2009 the Insurance Supervisory Authority became part of new organization the Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority. The decision to merge financial and insurance supervision was taken prior to the financial crisis but experiences of financial crisis confirmed the need for comprehensive supervision of financial sector risks and close cooperation with the central bank. FIN-FSA is an autonomous authority which is independent of political decisions but operates administratively in connection with the Bank of Finland. FIN-FSA has its own board of non-executive directors. The board consists of five members (Bank of Finland, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Social Affairs and Health two independent members) and the Deputy Governor of the Bank holds the chairmanship of the board of the FSA. The annual FSA-budget is approved by FSA board and confirmed by the Bank of Finland. Clearly great benefits derive from the institutional arrangement in Finland. The combination of macro and micro prudential oversight and supervision is just "what the doctor ordered" after the financial crisis. We had this in place already in 2009 in a comprehensive manner. There is no duplication of work and this is an important aspect for endeavoring to work as efficiently as possible. The Bank of Finland and the FSA also share common data, exchange information and cooperate in both analysis and stress testing. The administrative services are shared, or more precisely provided to the FIN-FSA by the Bank of Finland. Based on our experience although preliminary the new FIN-FSA works well as an independent authority and close to the central bank by covering all relevant financial institutions. It also seems to fit nicely to the proposed and forthcoming European supervisory and regulatory framework.

Title: Financial activities to be harnessed  for the common good
text: Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen: Financial activities must be harnessed d for the common good. Keynote speech at the 60th anniversary of the Turku School of Economics, Turku 3.9.2010 . Speech . Friday 3September 2010, 12:00 AM Vice Chairman of the Board Pentti Hakkarainen, Bank of Finland Turku School of Economics 60th anniversary Turku 3.9.2010 Introduction It is a pleasure to congratulate the prestigious Turku School of Economics. My assessment of the school's excellence was confirmed in concrete terms when my wife was a professor at the university and hsn told about the activities of the school. In short, the Turku School of Economics is of great regional importance and is highly valued at national level. Based on the data of the joint admissions, the Turku School of Economics was one of the most sought-after study places in Finland in the field of economics and economics. The title of my speech printed in the program became more precise during the preparation of the speech. The key issue is whether financial activities are more important than other business activities. If necessary, what are the means? The intensification and supervision of the financial sector has therefore given rise to intense debate for and against. The German Finance Minister, Wolfgang Schsuble, said that it was necessary to stress to the management of the banks that financial institutions are for society, not otherwise. The financial crisis clearly demonstrated the need to tighten the harness. Why, however, is there opposition? Role of financial institutions The function of financial institutions in society is ssrimmsisen tsrkes. They invest the funds of others. This includes the selection of good investment and investment targets on behalf of the Sssstsj and, most recently, on behalf of society as a whole. Success in ensuring that the best investment projects are funded is a prerequisite for economic prosperity, renewal and growth. Thanks to banking, the assets of individual assets can be liquid, even if the bank has invested them in long-term assets. Tsms is also ssrimmsisen tsrkess. If depositors' assets were to become epslikvid, payment transactions and the market economy as a whole would come to a standstill. The activities of financial institutions always involve risks. They are prepared for, for example, by taking care of sufficient liquidity resources and solvency. However, the financial institutions' own resources and liquidity reserves in relation to their total assets are relatively small. That, too, is part of the nature of the activity. The financial crisis we have experienced in recent years has shown more clearly than expected how well-functioning the financial system is, and how far even small hsirists in the financial world can be affected. If a financial institution fails, the damage to customers will be significant. If the institution in question is so large or so extensively networked that it is osystematically significant, the damage is multiplied and spreads beyond its own customer base to society as a whole. For crises to spread, it is sufficient to simply link financial institutions. Then, among market participants, depositors and creditors, the situation will spread, and the effects could spread worldwide in hours or minutes. Management and supervision of financial institutions The authorities, whose job it is to represent the nsks corner of society as a whole, must take responsibility for the tightness of the harness of financial institutions. Why do the authorities have to intervene in the private sector, and that it is not enough for depositors to monitor where the money they receive as deposits in their bank is used and otherwise? The financial crisis showed that market discipline and self-discipline are not sufficient to ensure the functioning of the financial system. The supervision of a financial institution is difficult in terms of contention and impossible for private clients or business partners because of the fact that the activity involves a certain degree of activity. The bank accepts short-term, small and large deposits and issues them in the form of larger and longer-term loans at its own discretion. Another problem is that the motives of the management and owners of banks are not the same as those of depositors and are not in line with the objectives of the authorities. What are the harnesses used to shackle financial institutions? Firstly, a licence is required to set up a bank, for example. Secondly, it is ensured that authorised financial institutions conduct their business without jeopardising the stability of the financial system. This applies to the scope of operations, the required solvency, risk management methods and the information to be reported to supervisors and markets. Thirdly, by supervising financial institutions, they are guaranteed that they operate in accordance with the rules of procedure and the generally agreed rules of play. The four-year-old means is crisis management, which ensures the functioning of core functions, deposits and payments systems in the event of a crisis situation and minimises the impact of a crisis situation on the financial system and society. In the case of financial institutions, the normal liquidation and bankruptcy procedure is far too slow due to the rapid outflow of funds in a crisis situation. Lessons from the financial crisis Although many of the financial crisis was different, there were still many features of the traditional financial crisis, such as over-indebtedness and the growth of short-term financing. The crisis was triggered by the illusion that the world had changed in such a way that the need for solvency and liquidity reserves could always and in all circumstances be satisfied by efficient financial markets. Significant changes in the financial system and their impact were widely underestimated. Financial institutions are more international and many financial institutions have sought growth from financial and investment activities and new risk-taking opportunities. The complexity and complexity of financial instruments have increased the complexity and complexity of financial instruments. At the same time, incentive models have become more short-lived and risk-taking. Although some of the risks were identified, they were not taken seriously. Risk-taking took on proportions. Risk was taken as an addition to traditional banking in new, unknown areas. It was believed that the risks were manageable. The estimate turned out to be vssss. One might be surprised at the interesting fact that, at the very beginning of the financial crisis, financial firms that had only briefly previously been assessed as one-class players collapsed; Northern Rock, an expert in traditional, safe banking in England, Lehman Brothers, one of the leading investment banks for decades, and the first-class insurance company American International Group, aka AIG, and Fortis, a banking and insurance company that has been operating excellently across national and business boundaries in the Benelux countries. Why wasn't he a rookie yellow-nosed man? The four examples are just a scratch on the surface of what happened in the depths of the financial crisis. And although banking in Finland has remained stable, neither finland's, nor any country's economy, could remain immune to the effects of the financial crisis. The financial crisis continues to affect the functioning of financial systems, the development of the world economy, exports and the national economy as a whole. Changes to the harness of financial institutions; sssntely Since the end of the financial crisis, significant reforms are now being made to the management, supervision and crisis management at the global, EU and national levels. The aim is to strengthen the financial system and minimise the likelihood of future financial crises. The G20, a club of the largest countries that has agreed on the basic lines of reform, has emerged as a key forum at global level. The concrete work is then done at national political and official level, in Europe for a long time in the EU. The reform, which is currently under way, is a recommendation prepared by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, the so-called 'green light'. Basel III, the implementation of which will require banks and other credit institutions to improve their solvency and liquidity. The package is structured in many different parts and its exact contents are finalised in the early days. In addition to the package, the balance is also becoming stricter in many other respects, including management incentives, the activities of credit rating agencies, the trading of derivative products and the accounting of financial instruments. According to preliminary estimates, the impact of the new crisis on financial institutions would be significant. This would increase bank liquidity requirements and bank liquidity reserves and favour the use of long-term financing in fundraising. The banks have not only taken a dim view of the changes, but have considered the proposals to be costly. They have tried to argue that costs are a burden on the national economy as a whole and on the world economy as well. The gloomiest estimates have been presented by an influential institute representing the financial sector from the Institute for International Finance (IIF). However, the estimates are exaggerated in that they are only the costs, but not the basis of a stable financial system. In recent years, however, we have been able to illustrate the costs of the financing system. If and when the evidence of such losses can be confirmed, the net losses planned for the sssning will be positive for the economy as a whole. According to a report published by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision(ssketch), tightening prudential and liquidity requirements would be a clear financial freeze over a long period of time. In the short term, the reforms are expected to reduce overall production only marginally. The results of a study carried out by the Bank of Canada are similar. Canada's financial institutions are coping well with the crisis and are solvent, so one might think that the reform would be pointless for Canada. However, Nsin is not. The country could not cope with the effects of the global financial crisis and recession, so according to a central bank study, the country is also noticeably nervous about improving its sclerosis at international level. Similar benefits of global stability can also be expected in the Nordic countries, quite apart from the fact that our banks have, on the whole, coped well with the turmoil of recent years. Changes to the supervision of financial institutions It is not enough, but also on the control side, and now with rapid steps in the United States and Europe. There are therefore reasons to strengthen monitoring clearly. It has been too fragmented for the d too national d nor too national financial system, i.e. the so-called 'financial system'. there has been insufficient investment in the monitoring of systemic risks. There is talk of macroprudential supervision, which is the subject of so-called macroprudential measures against individual banks. microcontrollability. An example of the internationalisation of supervision is the construction at EU level of the European Systemic Risk Board (ESRB), which is responsible for macro-supervision. At the same time, the relationship between financial supervisors and central banks has been intensified, and the EU Risk Council is made up of representatives of both the central banks and the supervisors. Last night there was fresh information from the European Parliament on this matter; Compromises have been negotiated and progress is being made. Europe is also creating new supervisory authorities for the banking, insurance and securities markets. Cooperation is intensifying at national level, for example, in the United States and great Britain, supervisory responsibilities have been transferred to the Central Bank as a result of the lessons of the crisis. The corresponding structure is already in place in Finland, where the Financial Supervisory Authority operates in conjunction with the Bank of Finland, but in cooperation with the Central Bank of Finland. The development of macroprudential and supranational supervision is now firmly advanced, and efforts are being made to equip the authorities with effective powers and powers. Changes to crisis management As monitoring and surveillance evolve, there are still reasons to prepare for crisis management and to develop crisis management systems in the d vshs, as in the construction sector, where, despite construction and fire inspections, there is also a need for effective fire brigades. In the EU, it is precisely crisis management that is theoretically an Achilles' heel, because sharing the responsibility for bailing out international banks is a more difficult issue than in a single country or, for example, in a federal state such as the United States. However, it has been possible to deal with the situations that have arisen. Indeed, one of my encouraging experiences during the financial crisis has been how well the cooperation between the authorities and the international authorities has always worked, if necessary. The most important thing about changes in crisis management is that the authorities must be able to intervene in good time in the financial arrangements. Both at the global, EU and Nordic level, there is a lack of cooperation in the management and resolution of crises that transcend the borders of the region. The object of development of the Czech Republic is the power of the authorities to intervene in a timely manner in the activities of financial institutions when problems begin to grow. Only by intervening in time can the cost of possible rescue operations be minimised if there is ultimately a need for rescue operations to ensure stability. Finally Good ladies and gentlemen, Financial institutions and markets must be steered and sshnew, but there must not be too many shackles. The harness should be appropriate to ensure competition and productivity. There has been concern that the requirements for this would be tightened too much, which would lead to an unreasonable increase in financing costs or to a reduction in the size of financial institutions. I believe, however, that the fear that financial institutions will not be able to meet healthy lending demand in the future is unfounded. And the whole project is aimed at reoccurring credit bubbles and over-indebtedness, as was the case 5 years ago in the United States and in many, many other countries. Much reproached incentives must be sized correctly. The length of the incentives and corporate governance recommendations will help to ensure that the management, board and owners of a financial company bear responsibility for the operation of the financial institution. As I quoted wolfgang Schsuble at the beginning, MFIs exist for society, not otherwise. When it comes to financial education, it is also worth mentioning that there are always reasons to confirm and ensure the correct business values. We must ensure a high level of integrity and an ethically sound approach to financial institutions and markets. Business schools have a very important role to play. They teach them how to take responsibility, pay sufficient attention to building good ethics and values, and train competent and fair bankers - and also supervisors - for the future. I wish good luck and success to the 60-year-old Turku School of Economics d and at the same time to the University of Turku d for decades to come.

Rahoituslaitokset ovat yh kansainvlisempi ja moni rahoituslaitos on hakenut kasvua vlitys-ja sijoitustoiminnasta ja uusista riskinottomahdollisuuksista. Rahoitusinstrumenttien monimutkaisuus ja moniportaisuus ovat lisnneet lpinkymttmyytt ja rahalaitosten vlisi kytkksi. Samalla kannustinmalleista on tullut yh lyhytjnteisempi ja riskinottoa suosivia. Vaikka osa riskeist tunnistettiin, niihin ei suhtauduttu vakavasti. Riskinotto sai ksittmttmt mittasuhteet. Riskej otettiin perinteisen pankkitoiminnan lisksi mys uusilla, tuntemattomilla alueilla. Elettiin siin uskossa ett riskit ovat hallittavissa. Arvio osoittautui vrksi. Ihmetyst voi hertt se mielenkiintoinen piirre, ett heti finanssikriisin alkuun kaatuivat sellaiset finanssiyritykset, jotka oli vain hetke aiemmin arvioitu ykksluokan toimijoiksi; perinteisen, turvallisen pankkitoiminnan osaaja Northern Rock Englannissa, vuosikymmenet johtavien investointipankkien joukkoon kuulunut Lehman Brothers ja ensiluokkaisena pidetty vakuutusyhti American International Group eli AIG sek erinomaisesti yli kansallisten ja liiketoiminnallisten rajojen toiminut pankki-ja vakuutustoimintaa harjoittanut Fortis Benelux-maissa. Mikn nist ei ollut toimintaansa aloitteleva keltanokka. Nm nelj esimerkki ovat vain pintaraapaisu siit, mit tapahtui finanssikriisin syvereiss. Ja vaikka Suomessa pankkitoiminta on pysynyt vakaana, ei Suomen, kuten ei minkn maan talous, voinut pysy immuunina finanssikriisin vaikutuksille. Finanssikriisi vaikuttaa edelleen rahoitusjrjestelmien toimivuuteen, maailmantalouden kehitykseen, vientiin ja koko kansantalouteen. Muutoksia rahoituslaitosten valjaisiin; sntely Finanssikriisin jlkeen sntelyyn, valvontaan ja kriisinhallintaan ollaan nyt tekemss merkittvi uudistuksia sek maailmanlaajuisesti, EU-tasolla, ett kansallisesti. Tavoitteena on vahvistaa rahoitusjrjestelmi ja minimoida tulevien finanssikriisien todennkisyys. Keskeiseksi globaalitason foorumiksi on noussut G20, suurimpien maiden muodostama klubi, joka on sopinut uudistusten peruslinjoista. Konkreettinen ty tehdn sitten kansallisella poliittisella ja viranomaistasolla, Euroopassa pitklti mys EU:ssa. Merkittvin vireill oleva sntelyuudistus on Baselin pankkivalvontakomitean valmistelema suositus, ns. Basel III, jonka toteutuessa pankkien ja muiden luottolaitosten on parannettava vakavaraisuuttaan ja maksuvalmiuttaan. Tm sntelypaketti sislt monta eri osaa ja sen tarkka sislt viimeistelln lhiaikoina. Tmn paketin lisksi sntely on tiukentumassa mys monessa muussa suhteessa, koskien muun muassa johdon kannustinjrjestelmi, luottoluokituslaitosten toimintaa, kaupankynti johdannaistuotteilla ja rahoitusinstrumenttien ksittely kirjanpidossa. Alustavien arvioiden mukaan uuden sntelyn vaikutukset rahoituslaitoksiin olisivat merkittvt. Sntely kasvattaisi pomavaatimuksia ja pankkien maksuvalmiusreservej ja suosisi pitkaikaisen rahoituksen kytt varainhankinnassa. Pankkien jrjestt eivt ole suhtautuneet muutoksiin pelkstn mynteisesti, vaan ovat pitneet ehdotuksia kalliina. Ne ovat pyrkineet argumentoimaan, ett kustannukset rasittavat koko kansantaloutta ja maailmantalouttakin. Synkimmt arviot on esittnyt rahoitusalaa edustava vaikutusvaltainen Institute for International Financelta (IIF). Arviot ovat kuitenkin siin mieless liioiteltuja, ett ne sisltvt vain kustannukset, mutta eivt vakaan rahoitusjrjestelmn hytyj. Olemme kuitenkin voineet viime vuosina havainnollisesti todeta, kuinka suuria kustannuksia rahoitusjrjestelmn epvakaus voi aiheuttaa. Jos ja kun tllaisten tappioiden todennkisyytt voidaan vhent, sntelyyn suunniteltujen muutosten nettohydyt ovat koko talouden kannalta positiiviset. Baselin pankkivalvontakomitean skettin julkaiseman raportin mukaan kiristyvist vakavaraisuus-ja likviditeettivaatimuksista olisi pitkll aikavlill selke taloudellinen hyty. Lyhyellkin aikavlill uudistusten arvioidaan supistavan kokonaistuotantoa vain niukasti. Kanadan keskuspankin tekemn tutkimuksen tulokset ovat samankaltaiset. Kanadan rahoituslaitokset selvisivt kriisist hyvin ja ovat vakavaraisia, joten voisi ehk ajatella ett sntelyuudistus olisi Kanadan kannalta turha. Nin ei kuitenkaan ole. Maa ei voinut vltty maailmanlaajuisen finanssikriisin ja taantuman vaikutuksista, joten maa mys hytyy keskuspankin tutkimuksen mukaan tuntuvasti siit, ett sntely parannetaan kansainvlisell tasolla. Vastaavia globaalin vakauden tuomia hytyj on odotettavissa mys Pohjoismaissa, kokonaan riippumatta siit, ett pankkimme tll ovat selvinneet kokonaisuutena ottaen hyvin viime vuosien myllerryksest. Muutoksia rahoituslaitosten valvontaan Hyvt snnt eivt yksin riit, vaan mys valvonnan puolella edetn nyt ripein askelin sek Yhdysvalloissa ett Euroopassa. Valvontaa onkin syyt vahvistaa selvsti. Se on ollut liian pirstoutunutta  liian kansallista  eik rahoitusjrjestelmn muodostamaan kokonaisuuteen eli ns. systeemiriskien valvontaan ole panostettu riittvsti. Puhutaan makrovakauden valvonnasta, joka tydent yksittisiin pankkeihin kohdistuvaa ns. mikrovalvontaa. Esimerkki valvonnan kansainvlistymisest on, ett EU-tasolle rakennetaan rajoitusjrjestelmn makrovalvonnasta vastaava riskineuvosto, European Systemic Risk Board (ESRB). Yhteistysuhdetta rahoitusvalvojien ja keskuspankkien vlill on samalla ryhdytty tiivistmn, ja mainittu EU:n riskineuvosto koostuukin sek keskuspankkien ett valvojien edustajista. Eilen illalla asiassa saatiin Euroopan parlamentista tuoretta tietoa; kompromissit on neuvoteltu ja asia etenee. Euroopassa perustetaan mys uudet valvontaviranomaiset pankki-, vakuutus-ja arvopaperimarkkinoille. Yhteisty tiivistyy niin ikn kansallisella tasolla, esimerkiksi Yhdysvalloissa ja Isossa-Britanniassa valvontavastuuta on kriisin opetusten seurauksena siirretty keskuspankille. Vhn vastaava rakenne on jo kytss tll Suomessa, miss Finanssivalvonta toimii Suomen Pankin yhteydess, ptksenteossaan itsenisen, mutta hyvss kytnnn yhteistyss keskuspankin kanssa. Makrovakauden ja ylikansallisen valvonnan kehittminen on nyt vahvasti etenemss, ja viranomaisille pyritn saamaan tehokkaita vlineit ja valtuuksia. Muutoksia kriisinhallintaan Vaikka sntely ja valvonta kehittyy, mys kriisien hallintaan on edelleen syyt varautua ja kriisinhallintajrjestelmi kehitt  vhn kuin rakennusalalla, jossa rakennusmryksist ja palotarkastuksista huolimatta tarvitaan mys tehokkaita palokuntia. EU:ssa juuri kriisinhallinta on teoriassa ernlainen Akilleen kantap, koska kansainvlisten pankkien pelastusvastuun jakaminen on vaikeampi kysymys kuin yhden maan sisll tai esimerkiksi Yhdysvaltojen kaltaisessa liittovaltiossa. Kytnnss eteen tulleet tilanteet on kuitenkin pystytty hoitamaan. Yksi rahoituskriisin aikaisista rohkaisevista kokemuksistani onkin ollut, kuinka hyvin viranomaisten vlinen ja kansainvlinen yhteisty on tarvittaessa lopulta aina toiminut. Olennaisinta kriisinhallinnan muutoksissa on, ett viranomaisten kytss on oltava vlineet puuttua ajoissa epkohtiin rahoitusjrjestelmss. Sek globaalilla, EU-ett mys pohjoismaisella tasolla tiivistetn yhteistyt liittyen alueen rajat ylittvien kriisien hallintaan ja selvittmiseen. Trke kehittmiskohde on viranomaisten valtuudet puuttua ajoissa rahoituslaitosten toimintaan, kun ongelmat alkavat kasvaa. Vain ajoissa puuttumalla voidaan minimoida mahdollisten pelastustoimien kustannukset, jos pelastustoimiin lopulta on mentv vakauden turvaamiseksi. Lopuksi Hyvt naiset ja herrat, Rahoituslaitoksia ja -markkinoita tulee ohjastaa ja snnell, mutta kahleita ei saa olla liikaa. Valjaiden pitisi olla tarkoituksenmukaisia, jotta varmistetaan kilpailu ja tuottavuus. Huolenaiheena on esitetty, ett pomavaatimuksia kiristetn liikaa, jolloin rahoituskustannukset kasvaisivat kohtuuttomasti tai rahoituslaitokset supistaisivat toimintaansa. Uskon kuitenkin, ett pelko siit, etteivt rahoituslaitokset vastaisuudessa pystyisi vastaamaan terveeseen luotonantokysyntn, on turha. Ja koko hankkeen tarkoituksenahan on est sellaisten luottokuplien ja ylivelkaantumisen uusiutuminen, jollainen viel 5 vuotta sitten oli kynniss Yhdysvalloissa ja monissa, monissa muissakin maissa. Paljon moititut kannustimet on mitoitettava oikein. Kannustinjrjestelmien sntelyn ja hyvn hallintotapaan liittyvien suositusten pit osaltaan varmistaa, ett finanssiyrityksen johto, hallitus ja omistajat kantavat vastuun rahoituslaitoksen toiminnasta. Kuten alussa lainasin Wolfgang Schublen sanoja, rahalaitokset ovat olemassa yhteiskuntaa varten, ei toisinpin. Meidn tulee varmistaa korkea integriteetti ja eettisesti vahva toimintaymprist rahoituslaitoksille ja -markkinoille. Tss kauppakorkeakouluilla on erittin trke rooli. Tll opetetaan vastuunottoa, kiinnitetn riittvsti huomiota hyvn etiikan ja arvojen rakentamiseen ja koulutetaan tulevaisuutta varten osaavia ja reiluja pankkiireita -ja mys valvojia. Title: The financial sector to a new regulatory environment
text: Vice Chairman of the Board pentti Hakkarainen: The financial sector to a new sssntely-ympsssn. OP-Pohjola.group's top management strategy 30.9.2010, Helsinki. . Speech . Friday 1 October 2010, 12:00 AM Pentti Hakkarainen, Vice Chairman of the Executive Board, Bank of Finland OP-Pohjola Group's Top Management Strategy Board Helsinki 30.9.2010 Speech liittyvst Membranes (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and. . interviews/documents/op_pohjola_300910.ppt) (ppt) Puheeseen liittyvst Membranes (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and. . interviews/documents/op_pohjola_300910.pdf) (pdf) The financial sector in a new ssntely-environmentsssn Introduction It is a pleasure to be part of OP-Pohjola's top management strategy. My title oFinance sector for the new sssntely-ympsssno gives me the opportunity to talk about very topical issues. Just over a week ago, the European Parliament voted on the new European supervisory authorities. The official ECOFIN meeting, i.e. the meeting of EU finance ministers, will discuss bank taxes and the new Basel proposals, which will be confirmed at the G20 meeting in November. Financial sector shunting The key issue is whether financial activities are more important than other business activities. The intensification and supervision of the financial sector has given rise to intense debate for and against. The function of financial institutions in society is ssrimmsisen tsrkes. They invest the funds of others. This includes the selection of good investment and investment targets on behalf of the Sssstsj and, most recently, on behalf of society as a whole. Success in ensuring that the best investment projects are funded is a prerequisite for economic prosperity, renewal and growth. Banks have large balance sheets in their own pockets. Business is also sensitive in other respects because of its dependence on economic development. The problems of banking easily extend far and wide. Hsirist poses widespread problems, not only for the bank itself, but also for the financial sector as a whole and for the rest of society. The adverse effects also extend beyond borders. The financial crisis occurred outside Finland, but largely as a result of it, our total output plummeted by an unprecedented 8% in 2009. Fortunately, in Finland, a strong financial sector prevented a downward spiral in which a weakening economy hits the financial sector and a weakening financial sector restricts economic activity. Background to the tightening of the situation As a result of the financial crisis, anti-banking sentiment has increased. Although in Finland the matter is not nsin, in many countries the mood has become tense. The German Finance Minister, Wolfgang Schsuble, said that it was necessary to stress to the management of the banks that financial institutions are for society, not otherwise. Last Wednesday, britain's national television and radio company, the BBC, published a study on how different countries view banks. In the international survey, about 2/3 of the respondents are in favour of the financial sector. By contrast, just under half, around 44%, would be prepared to support a bank in difficulty. The financial crisis we have experienced in recent years has shown more clearly than expected how well-functioning the financial system is, and how far even small hsirists in the financial world can be affected. As a result of the financial crisis, the industry will undergo major changes in three directions. As a first step, we will increase controls. Measures to cover the costs of the crisis have already been implemented in some countries and, more generally, new levies and taxes are planned for the financial sector. In addition, the basel reforms to strengthen solvency and financial position will have an impact on the financial sector and the economy as a whole, including in Finland. Control Control is being developed. The financial crisis showed two significant shortcomings in supervision. The first is that, although individual enterprises were supervised by micro-control, the whole system of adequate monitoring, macro-control, was ignored. A good example is the development of housing finance in the United States, where the companies subject to supervision complied with the sssntsjs, but the activity was diverted to the blind spot of supervision by the additional system, leading to a skewed development of the entire system. Another shortcoming in Europe has been that financial supervision has been too heavily built on national supervisors and that there has not been sufficient supervision of international MFIs and integrated financial markets. A week ago, the European Parliament adopted a new regulatory control structure in Europe. The reform, which will be carried out as early as the beginning of next year, will correct the shortcomings of supervision. Macro-supervision will be improved by the establishment of a European Systemic Risk Board. It ensures the monitoring and management of systemic risks. In addition, new EU supervisory authorities will be set up in micro-supervision for banking and insurance companies and the securities markets. This will strengthen the supervision of financial markets and institutions operating across national borders and, in particular, the resolution of potential problems. Fees and taxes The financial crisis caused high costs for several different countries. Fortunately, we did not have to rely on state aid. Public support has been massive in the United States and many European countries. The euro area committed to supporting the financial sector has been 18%, 20% of GDP in the United States, 20% in the United Kingdom and 7% in the euro area. Ireland is a brand of ssries; Before the financial crisis, government debt was about 20% of GDP and after supporting the country's banking sectors, it is expected to rise to 100%. Supporting the banking sector in various forms has entailed high costs for many countries. By the end of 2009, costs amounted to 3.6% of GDP in the United States, 6.1% in the United Kingdom and 4.8% in Germany. It is understood that the banking sector should be obliged to repay the aid it has received and to prepare for the costs of possible future financial crises. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) was commissioned by the G20 group to investigate various forms of bank tax. In September, the Fund finalised its report on the matter. The report will go to the G20 in November. In addition, there is a debate on fees in the European Union. In the financial sector, three types of contributions have already been implemented or three types of levies are planned: a stability levy, a tax on the financial sector and a tax on financial transactions. The financial market stability levy has already been implemented in Sweden. It is due to enter into force next year in the UK and Germany, and certainly in France. The payment is based on balance sheet liabilities, as in Sweden, the UK and Germany, or risk-weighted receivables as planned by France. The financial sector tax is a kind of VAT tax for the industry. Different variations of the combination of salaries and profits of a financial enterprise have been outlined as the tax base. Although the financial sector tax has been the subject of other bank charges and tax proposals in the public domain, it is possible, on the basis of background discussions and preparations, that it will enter into force in one form or another. The financial transaction tax is related to the Tobin tax that raises the tax. It is quite attractive, since the tax would be levied on large volumes and would be very small per transaction. However, a number of experts consider the form of taxation to be difficult to implement, harmful side effects and contrary to consistent tax principles. Despite Chelsk, there are supporters of a tax on financial transactions, including: Germany and France are pushing the issue forward. Sssntely The financial sector will be supplemented by the Sssntelys. The Basel-Ssnnsks have evolved. At the end of the 1980s, the first prudential requirements in relation to credit risk were introduced. A decade ago, an operational risk was developed and operational risk was introduced into Basel II, as well as the discretion of the supervisor and the requirements of market discipline. The solvency criteria of the new Basel III require the addition of MFIs to have a real own balance sheet, set an absolute limit on the indebtedness of MFIs and the growth of the balance sheet, and require a stronger financial position. The new solvency ratios will not change the 8% limit for solvency. On the other hand, the quality requirements of their own pssoma are tightened and banks are required to keep the buffers that exceed the requirement. Own pssom must be used to cover the losses of the MFI. The msssss of the right own pssoma must be increased from 2% to 7% during the transfer period. The new ceiling for indebtedness and growth for financial institutions, the minimum self-sufficiency requirement, is based on correct, non-risk-adjusted balance sheet figures. It is a pittance in case risk-weighted solvency calculations would allow for excessive indebtedness, as in the case of the financial crisis, for several MFIs. From the point of view of the balance sheet, the bank must have sufficient of its own bank to avoid small changes in the assets on the balance sheet. The budgetary position will be strengthened by two new quantitative requirements. Firstly, the liquidity requirement ensures that the bank has highly liquid assets to cover a drastic, short-term financial market situation. Secondly, the permanent fundraising requirement will reduce the MFI's dependence on short-term financing. Effects of tightening financial slump The reform of controls will have a particular impact on solving supranational and system-wide problems. Supervisory responsibility and activities are the responsibility and activities of the national financial supervisory authority. The new stability contributions and bank taxes will burden the profitability of the financial sector. There is already a need for additional pressure in the financial sector due to overcapacity in the financial sector, tight banking competition and low interest rates. The requirements relating to the financial position favour the acquisition of deposits and, as a result, profitability is weakened on the side of the bank due to fierce competition, as banks have to pay higher interest rates on deposits. The competitive position in the financial sector is also changing. Well-run banks strengthen their competitive position when competitors are faced with new requirements. When the solvency of banks operating in Finland is strong and liquidity requirements can also be implemented during the transition period, they are the winners in the world of the new ssntele. Structural changes will take place in the industry. Investment banking and, in particular, investment and investment activities, i.e. so-called investment and investment activities. trading is weakened by the increasing computational risk weights of its activities and thus require a substantial increase in its own pssoma. The position of SSIs will be challenged, especially for lenders, as the requirement of self-sufficiency will place a strain on their business. Traditional general banking with a strong weight of bank banking will gain a comparative advantage because the requirements will favour them, or at least burden them, as they will be burdened by the requirements. The net macroeconomic impact is also long-term, the likelihood that the financial crisis will take place and the costs incurred will be reduced. Nsin is also in the countries and financial markets where the financial crisis took place. For example, in Canada, where banking activity remained strong, a study has been carried out by the Central Bank on the basis of which international sector reforms have been adopted to determine whether the Canadian economy is also affected. The rules, controls and bank taxes are also made and calibrated in such a way that they are for the benefit of all for a longer period of time. This and regulatory oversight are in place to ensure the functioning of the financial markets in all circumstances. However, this is not enough and good governance is needed for the MFIs' own activities. However, in the end, the responsibility for the good management and success of the business is always borne by the bank's management and governing bodies, as well as by the owners. They must be sufficiently aware of the risks involved in the operation of their financial institution.

Friday 1 October 2010, 12:00 AM Johtokunnan varapuheenjohtaja Pentti Hakkarainen, Suomen Pankki OP-Pohjola-ryhmn ylimmn johdon strategiapiv Helsinki 30.9.2010 Puheeseen liittyvt kalvot (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and. . interviews/documents/op_pohjola_300910.ppt) (ppt) Puheeseen liittyvt kalvot (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and. . interviews/documents/op_pohjola_300910.pdf) (pdf) Finanssiala uuteen sntely-ympristn Johdanto On ilo olla mukana OP-Pohjolan ylimmn johdon strategiapivss. Otsikkoni Finanssiala uuteen sntely-ympristn antaa mahdollisuuden puhua hyvin ajankohtaisista aiheista. Reilu viikko sitten Euroopan parlamentti ptti uusista Euroopan valvontaviranomaisista. Tnn epvirallinen ECOFIN eli EU:n finanssiministerien kokous keskustelee pankkiveroista ja Baselin uusista sntelyehdotuksista, jotka etenevt vahvistettavaksi marraskuussa G20 maiden kokoukseen. Finanssialan sntely Keskeinen kysymys on, pitk rahoitustoimintaa snnell enemmn kuin muuta yritystoimintaa. Rahoitusalan sntelyn ja valvonnan tehostaminen on herttnyt voimakasta keskustelua puolesta ja mys vastaan. Rahoituslaitosten tehtv yhteiskunnassa on rimmisen trke. Ne sijoittavat muiden varoja. Thn tehtvn kuuluu hyvien investointi-ja sijoituskohteiden valikointia sstjien ja viime kdess koko yhteiskunnan puolesta. Onnistuminen tss tehtvss niin, ett parhaat investointihankkeet lydetn ja ett juuri ne saavat rahoituksensa, on taloudellisen hyvinvoinnin, uudistumisen ja kasvun edellytys. Pankkien taseet ovat niiden omiin pomiin nhden suuret. Liiketoiminta on muutoinkin herkk, koska siihen sisltyy riippuvuus talouskehityksest. Pankkitoiminnan ongelmat ulottuvat helposti kauas. Hirit aiheuttavat laajoja ongelmia, eik vain pankille itselleen vaan herksti koko rahoitussektorille ja muulle yhteiskunnalle. Haitalliset vaikutukset ulottuvat mys yli rajojen. Finanssikriisi tapahtui Suomen ulkopuolella, mutta paljolti sen johdosta kokonaistuotantomme romahti vuonna 2009 enntykselliset 8 prosenttia. Suomessa onneksi vahva rahoitussektori esti negatiivisen kierteen syntymisen, jossa heikkenev talous iskee rahoitusalalle ja heikkenev rahoitusala rajoittaa talouden toimintaa. Sntelyn kiristymisen taustaa Finanssikriisin johdosta pankkivastaisuus on lisntynyt. Vaikka Suomessa asia ei ole nin, monessa maassa tunnelmat ovat kiristyneet. Saksan valtiovarainministeri Wolfgang Schuble totesi, ett on tarpeen korostaa pankkien johdolle, ett rahalaitokset ovat yhteiskuntaa varten, ei toisinpin. Viime keskiviikkona Britannian kansallinen televisio-ja radioyhti BBC julkisti tutkimuksen siit, miten eri maissa suhtaudutaan pankkeihin. Kansainvlisess kyselyss noin 2/3 vastaajista kannattaa rahoitustoimialan sntely. Sen sijaan vain vajaa puolet, noin 44 prosenttia, olisi valmis tukemaan vaikeuksiin joutunutta pankkia. Viime vuosina kokemamme finanssikriisi on osoittanut selvemmin kuin osattiin odottaa, kuinka elintrke hyvin toimiva rahoitusjrjestelm on, ja kuinka laajalle pienetkin hirit rahoitusmaailmassa voivat vaikuttaa. Finanssikriisin johdosta tulee toimialalle suuria muutoksia kolmesta suunnasta. Ensimmiseksi listn ja parannetaan valvontaa. Kriisin kustannusten kattamiseksi on toteutettu jo joissakin maissa ja yleisemmin suunnitellaan finanssialalle uusia maksuja ja veroja. Lisksi Baselin sntelyuudistukset vakavaraisuuden ja rahoitusaseman vahvistamiseksi tulevat vaikuttamaan finanssitoimialaan ja koko talouteen, mys meill Suomessa. Valvonta Valvontaa kehitetn. Finanssikriisi osoitti valvonnassa kaksi merkittv puutetta. Ensimminen on se, ett vaikka yksittisi yrityksi valvottiin mikrovalvonnalla, huomiotta ji koko jrjestelmn kehityksen riittv seuranta, makrovalvonta. Hyv esimerkki on Yhdysvaltojen asuntorahoituksen kehitys, jossa valvonnan kohteena olevat yritykset noudattivat sntj, mutta toiminta ohjautui lisntyvss mrin valvonnan katvealueelle johtaen koko jrjestelmn vinoon kehitykseen. Toinen puute on Euroopassa ollut se, ett rahoitusvalvonta on liian voimakkaasti rakentunut kansallisten valvojien varaan ja tm ei ole ollut riittv kansainvlisesti toimivien rahalaitosten ja integroituneiden rahoitusmarkkinoiden valvonnassa. Viikko sitten Euroopan parlamentti hyvksyi Euroopan uuden viranomaisvalvontarakenteen. Jo ensi vuoden alusta toteutettavalla uudistuksella korjataan valvonnan puutteita. Administration, management and personnel of the Good Mortgage Association. Welcome invited guests. It is an honor to congratulate the 150-year-old MFI. Over time, and especially in recent years, we have seen how many institutions that are considered to be financially sound have collapsed. Not many companies have been in the 150s. It is no wonder that the long period of time includes very problematic and demanding situations for businesses. In Finland, there have been many difficult stages for financial operations during the existence of the Mortgage Association. The ordeal began immediately after the deflation of the 1860s and, as a result, massive credit losses. In addition, periods of inflation have arisen in connection with the world wars. This period has also been marked by several major economic downturns and exchange rate collapses. The long and fine history of the Finnish Mortgage Association tells us how difficult and over-the-top difficulties can be p??sem?t?nesh. The management and administration of the mortgage association have always been able to cope with the means to survive. They have been able to further develop the activities of the Mortgage Association in changed circumstances, including the international financial crisis experienced in recent years. Finland's strong financial sector prevented a vicious circle This is a good opportunity to give fair recognition to the banks and financial institutions operating in Finland. As a national economy, we were caught up in the excess of financial transactions elsewhere, since the international financial crisis, which had originated outside Finland, also extended to our economy. The ferocity of the shock is illustrated by the fact that our total production fell by a former 8% last year. In Finland, banks had fortunately remained in the traditional banking business, and had not sought returns with excessive risks. Finland's strong financial sector prevented the emergence of a dangerous spiral in which a weakening economy weakens financial activity and, if it gets into difficulties, deepens the problems of the economy in the past. This cycle would continue in itself, if it were not stopped. Although there were difficulties in Finland, the worst that had to be prepared for did not materialise. In many countries, financial markets were too heverish to receive h?irish and digest the real economy. In Finland, financial activity remained well at its rootel and it has not been necessary to stress to the management of the banks, in the words of the German Finance Minister Wolfgang Sch?uble, that financial institutions are for society, not otherwise. Among those deserving of recognition is the Mortgage Association. I will return to the glorious history of the Mortgage Association and assess the future of its business and financial activities. Rahalaitokset valjaisiin In the wake of the financial crisis, there have been calls for financial institutions to now be put in shackles, or at least in sufficient gears. I am right to think that the question is why financial institutions should be shackled more than companies. Financial activities play a central and cherke? function in society. Its mission is to finance profitable projects and, through it, to strengthen economic growth. Modern society needs a well-functioning financial system with payment services. The meaning of this has been illustratively compared with blood circulation. Even a small blockage can cause great damage. Financial activities always involve risk. The MFI's borrowing and lending conditions differ in principle. In a large balance sheet, the risks are diversified and partly cancel each other out. But there is always a risk in the MFI itself to bear. In addition, additional risks are taken consciously in order to increase profits. Banking also differs from many other types of business in that it usually has a large balance sheet and a small own balance sheet. During the financial crisis of recent years, banking risks have once materialised. Even banks with very traditional banking activities collapsed. It is also the case that many of the financial institutions in difficulty were well-known, long-established and first-class banks ? not yellow-nosed ? not yellow-nosed ones starting their operations. The difficulties of individual MFIs were not confined to themselves. The effects extended widely to the rest of society and the real economy, as well as to other countries altogether. The international financial crisis showed how great the social disadvantages and costs of financial transactions can be. The final bill will be borne by the rest of society, and ultimately by the taxpayer. That is why the political forces and the people are demanding that this must not happen again. For all these reasons, financial activities must be supervised more than other business activities in which the laws of free competition and the market economy are sufficient. In the 1980s, this was developed in an internationally consistent direction, taking into account more closely the risk of lending ? the bank's receivables ? from the angle of the bank. The Basel solvency ratio was developed with the Basel II requirements in 2004, which, in addition to the previous one, took into account market risk and operational risk. As a lesson from the financial crisis, s??nt?j? is being reformed into Basel III requirements. The analysis now goes beyond mere solvency. The Sshnn?ks are due to be confirmed at the upcoming G20 meeting in November with the aim of bringing them into force as early as 2013. The requirements will gradually increase during the transfer period and will enter into force by 2019. Control Good enough, the s??nn?ks are not enough on their own. Just as with transport, compliance with the transport sector must also be monitored. Supervision of financial activities has evolved thanks to banking crises. The financial crisis that we have just experienced revealed two fundamental shortcomings that hampered the success of supervision. The first was that, although individual actors were supervised, the whole was not controlled and the system could develop into a skewed one. The powers of the national authority did not extend beyond problems of an international nature. Now the basic shortcomings of control are being rectified. At the end of September, the European Parliament adopted a new EU supervisory structure and new institutions; The European System of The Risk Board and the ESAs for banking, insurance and securities markets. They will start operating from the beginning of next year. In the European system, the Risk Board oversees the market and activities as a whole, i.e. macro-prudential. It issues recommendations and warnings when the development of all or part of the system threatens to become too risky and dangerous. In the United States, similar powers and functions are created in the Central Bank. New authorities will also be set up and supervisory powers will be strengthened and extended. A model for the modern fixed credit bank in Finland is the Finnish Housing Hypothetic Bank, founded in 1927 and merged with the Finnish Mortgage Association in 1979. Where does the future of the Mortgage Association take you? However, if implemented correctly, the reforms will benefit both the financial institutions themselves and the economy as a whole. Title: Presentation by Pentti Hakkarainen, Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors
text: Presentation by Pentti Hakkarainen, Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors, Finnish Commerce Federation 25.1.2011 . Speech . Tuesday 25January 2011, 1:00 AM Pentti Hakkarainen, Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors Lunch of the Board of the Finnish Commerce Federation 25.1.2011 The presentation body, which it follows mutatis mutandis. CURRENT AFFAIRS IN THE FINANCIAL MARKETS As a member of the Board of the Federation of Commerce, thank you for your first invitation to your lunch and for the opportunity to give a lengthy presentation on current financial market issues. I had the hope that I would start the future of the financial markets and the fate of the euro. The presentations on freedom and the wider area of the kata. I have read my presentation for four episodes; new Basel .ssnnsks for banks, a new European framework for financial supervision, mechanisms for resolving the economic crisis in the European Union and, finally, more generally, the economic framework. I will start with the reform of the Basel Sssnnssch. THE ADVANTAGE OF BASEL III FINLAND On the basis of the lessons learned from the financial crisis, international funding and supervision have been tightened up strongly. So far, the Czech reform package, the so-called Chelei reform package. Basel III, to improve banks' risk tolerance against institutional and macroeconomic shocks. Basel sssnnsssn reform has a more central impact in three areas; the banks' solvency will be reduced and the quality of their own bank assets will be improved, their financial position will be strengthened and an absolute indebtedness ceiling will be imposed on them. Although the reforms will incur costs for banking, they are in finland's interest from the nskskulma of our economy. The reliable operation of banks is vsltsmschnchnch for both consumers and businesses. In addition, it is srkess for the entire national economy. The financial system must properly manage basic tasks such as the payment of financing and payments, reliable pricing of financing and risk sharing. In a well-functioning system, money is channelled into profitable projects and ensures the well-being of the national economy. It is not enough that the system only works well in good times. The risk-bearing capacity and overall confidence of financial market participants must be sufficient to cover even the highest levels of risk-bearing capacity. For its part, the Bank of Finland ensures the reliability and stability of the financing system. It published a report on the stability of finland's financial system. According to the report, in 2011 stability is threatened by the following risks in particular: 1) The worsening of the debt crisis is crippling the international financial market, which also makes it more difficult for Finnish actors to finance and finance. 2) The debt crisis halts the global economic recovery, which is holding back consumption, investment and foreign demand, as well as weakening the performance of financial firms. 3) The continued increase in the level of debt of Finnish households makes households more vulnerable to rising interest rates and negative effects on the economy. Dear listeners, you are wondering if you will take care of what is happening in the international market and take care of the internal borders. Especially since the first two of the threats mentioned in the above report are those occurring outside Finland. And if so, the question is what can be done about them? The answer comes from an illustrative examination of the development of our economy in recent years. The crisis in the international financial markets that took place in 2008 showed very well how strongly we too are affected by the hsirst that is taking place elsewhere. Our national product plummeted by eight per cent under the influence of long-term Hsirisides born elsewhere. It is therefore in our interest to improve the efficiency and supervision of international financial markets. Fortunately, the Finnish financial system held up well and was able to prevent the emergence of a vicious downward spiral in the economy. Whenever criticism of the profitability of banks grows, it is good to remember, on the other hand, that the strength of Finnish financial institutions reduces the problems. This is the case, because we are certainly not protected from the international economy and financial system. The effects of the new crisis on the growth of the national economy and the price of lending have already been extensively assessed and studied. When the sssnnsksis was designed, they were also available for comment by the industry. The new requirements may lead to higher loan margins and, consequently, to a weakening of economic growth. Estimates vary quite widely, but according to the latest and most in-depth analyses, GDP may fall on average 0.2. d 0.4 % of units. However, there are reasons to point out that the tightening solvency and liquidity requirements will have an impact on the cost of borrowing, if there were no change, there would be no intensification in banking and productivity growth, and if the yield requirement for one's own bank would not be lowered. It is estimated that there is an upward pressure of around 0.25 to 0.50 per cent on loan margins. However, the dynamic nature of the banks and the competition in the sector should ensure that the cost is not borne, at least not entirely, by the borrowers. Impact assessments should be treated with great caution. The assumptions at the base of them are subject to change. Also, cause-and-effect relationships that have worked in the past did not do the same. Interested parties can consult the Bank of Finland's special issue of The Euro & Economy financial system on stability 2010, where the impact is assessed and the issue is examined. REFORM OF EUROPEAN FINANCIAL SUPERVISION FILLS GAPS There were two major shortcomings in financial supervision. One was that, although individual MFIs were supervised and complied with, the whole system could develop in ovinoono to increase the risk of the financial sector and, more broadly, to the financial sector as a whole. An example is American housing finance, which crisis and spread around the world, causing unforeseen losses and damage. Another fundamental shortcoming was that controls were excessively based on national controls. The financial markets have been operating internationally for a long time. For companies in the sector, national borders are not the same. Even the domestic financial bank is increasingly dependent on the international financial markets and the financial institutions operating in the various countries. In spite of all this, supervision was the sole responsibility of the national supervisory authorities. The situation was bad not only for supervision, but also for banks operating in several countries. At the time of the problems, various solutions had to be found. Two significant shortcomings were remedied with the establishment of the European Systemic Risk Board (ESRB), the European Union supervisory authorities for financial, insurance and securities markets, the European Banking Authority (EBA), the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA) and the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) in the early part of the year. The ESRB's task is to monitor the market as a whole. Where appropriate, it can address policies and biases that may cause major overall economic damage. An example of this is the strong growth of credit unions, which can lead to a fixed price bubble. The main task of the new EU supervisory authorities, the EBA, EIOPA and ESMA, is to coordinate the work of the national financial supervisory authorities, to promote the coordination of the supervisory system and, lastly, to resolve disputes where the national supervisory authorities are unable to cooperate. Eu authorities do not replace national financial supervisors, but need the help of national supervisors in order to function well. Then there is the sovereign debt crisis. CRISIS IN THE STABILITY OF THE EUROPEAN ECONOMY AND FINANCIAL MARKETS Many countries have, in one way or another, gone beyond their means and become indebted in such a way that their ability to pay off debt has been reduced. This has also happened in the euro area. However, the crisis has been a crisis of economic and financial stability, not a crisis of individual currency or currency area. In Europe, the economic crisis in Greece began less than a year ago. At that time, there was no ready-made operating model on how to intervene in the situation. Initially, the imf's involvement was discouraged. Following the negotiations, the rescue package for Greece was built by the IMF, eu member states and the European Commission in cooperation with the ECB. The expertise and experience of the Imf in creating financial packages and, in particular, the accompanying economic programme, was the lifeblood to deal with the acute situation. In May, the Greek crisis led to the creation, if necessary, of a space-based european financial stability system with a capacity of EUR 750 billion. The system includes contributions from the European Financial Stability Facility (EFSF), the European Financial Stability Mechanism (EFSM) and the IMF. Ireland found itself in a predicament after Greece. At first, the country seemed to be asking for help. However, as the plight grew, it had to bend over and ask for outside help. Having learned from the Greek case, the aid package was achieved quite quickly with the help of new support mechanisms. The economic programme, which is a condition for financing, is strict. Compliance with the programme is closely monitored by the IMF and the EU Commission. The responsibility for balancing the economy and putting it on a sustainable path is always in the country itself. Ladies and gentlemen, there are threats in the public eye of Portugal and Spain falling into an economic crisis. Both countries have given assurances that they will take the necessary steps to avoid relying on external financial assistance. In the case of greece and ireland, if the countries themselves cannot get their economies in order, there is a hystyhe in the case of Greece and Ireland. The financial arrangements implemented will help to narrow down the problems and the pressure on other countries. In addition, the financial packages and operating models have been tested and more complete. A good sign is that, in the context of the crisis in the EU, there has been a growing readiness to resolve the situation. Significant successes have been the creation of the EFSF and the EfSM, the European Financial Stability Mechanism. Although they are a means of dealing with economic problems, they provide the basis for a permanent crisis management mechanism between the EU and the euro area. Europe's permanent crisis management mechanism is currently a negotiating process. At the latest in March, the matter is due to be referred to the European Council. According to preliminary political resolutions, the permanent arrangements are to enter into force in the middle of 2013. Its task is not only a solution to crises, but also a pre-emptive solution to them. Despite the successes, the delicate situation is not over. The economic position of many countries deteriorated severely as a result of the recession. This confidence in the debt sustainability of a number of European countries is destabilising the financial markets. Although governments and financial institutions have established risk tolerance, the differences between countries and banking groups are large and there has been no exit from security. The problem of over-indebtedness will not be eliminated by a single financial package. The only way out is to get the economy on a sustainable path. For several countries, it will be several years away. Then it wasn't until then that the debt problems were resolved successfully. Finally, ladies and gentlemen, we have just received new economic forecasts, including from the IMF. On the basis of these, I will characterize the economy. THE ECONOMY'S TENT ARE MY... NTE MORE THAN EXPECTED A YEAR AGO The international economy is recovering at a rapid pace, at around five per cent. However, economic growth is very different and different in different parts of the world. China, India and many emerging economies are growing strongly. Developing countries did not all even fall into recession in 2008 d 2009. Even those who experienced economic distress have recovered rapidly from the crisis. There are considerable differences between developed economies and countries. The United States has seen stronger-than-expected growth. The latest data on the growth of consumer demand are likely to confirm that the accelerated growth in the autumn is at a fairly low ebb. However, there are still potential problems in the housing market and lending due to the high level of employment. In Europe, too, development is heterogeneous. Germany is clearly the economy with the strongest growth. Government debt problems and large public deficits weigh on sentiment. Rebalancing the economies of many peripheral countries is likely to reduce their economies in the short term. The growth of the Finnish economy generally translates into exports and shifts to consumption and eventually to investment. Exports d especially in traditional industries that have been transformed into the chimney industry d have been able to pull better than expected. The growth in demand in world trade and in our export markets gives us hope that exports will continue at a rapid pace. Consumer demand has remained relatively strong. The Consumer Confidence Index supports the fact that it continues to do so. Productive investment, however, is still waiting. Many industries have a combination of capacity and several companies have the opportunity to meet the demand for production units outside Finland. Finland's major challenge will be to maintain the balance of public finances in the coming years. In particular, the deficit in the sustainability of public finances, which according to the latest calculations by the Ministry of Finance amounts to 5% of GDP, requires either an increase in central government revenue or a reduction in expenditure. Studies show that spending is a better way of rebalancing the economy, because increasing taxes can have a stronger negative impact on economic growth. A major overhaul of public expenditure is a major overhaul, regardless of how the international economic cycles are. Thank you. Now is the time to ask questions, please.

EUROOPAN RAHOITUSVALVONNAN UUDISTAMINEN KORJAA PUUTTEITA Rahoitusvalvonnassa oli kaksi merkittv puutetta. Yksi oli se, ett vaikka yksittisi rahalaitoksia valvottiin ja ne noudattivat snnksi, koko jrjestelm saattoi kehitty vinoon listen riski sek toimijoille ett laajemmin koko finanssialaan.
