Title: The financial game alone is not enough - the outlook for the economy and financial markets
text: Vice Chairman of the Board Pentti Hakkarainen: The financial game alone is not enough for the economy and the financial markets. Presentation to the Technology Industries of Finland Finance Group 3.2.2011 . Speech . Thursday3 February 2011, 12:00 PM Pentti Hakkarainen, Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors Presentation to the Technology Industries of Finland Finance Group Helsingisss3.2.2011 In summary, may differ from what is spoken. Presentations (pdf) (/globalassets/en/media-ja. publications/speeches/documents/030211_basel_iii_ja_rahoitusmarkkinat_hakkarainen.pdf) The financial game alone is not enough to d the economy and the financial markets I would like to thank you for the first opportunity to present a briefing at your meeting. I know the activities of the tysry group and Jssenis well, because when I was at the head of finance at Outokumpu Oy, I was also in the tyssen tysryhmsn jssen. My topic is the new Basel-ssnnsks, their contents and their impact. After that, I will discuss the state of the financial markets. Finally, I will describe the economy more generally. BaselIII In the early 1990s, the first Basel solvency pacts introduced international prudential requirements for banks' own funds in relation to credit risks. Among other things, they received more detailed weightings and weightings for credit and market risks in the 2004 Basel II requirements. On the basis of the lessons learned from the financial crisis, international financial planning and supervision have been heavily tightened. So far, the Czech reform package, the so-called Chelei reform package. Basel III, improves the risk tolerance of banks. It was achieved quickly. At the end of last year, a timetable for the entry into force of the new Basel III requirements was agreed. Pitkshksn, After the transition period up to 2019, banks will be required to have a better quality than before, both in terms of liquidity and in terms of own financing. An absolute ceiling is also set on the indebtedness of the MFI. The quality of your own pssoma will be improved. The requirement of financial standing is currently at eight per cent, but in the future it will require a real, genuine own pssoma in the present. In this case, the unrestricted primary own pssss must be used at seven per cent, of which the absolute minimum is 4.5 per cent and the so-called "minimum". as a fixed buffer of 2,5 % individual. This means that, although the solvency requirement is formally suffixed, the MFI must be set at 10.5%. Another important requirement is to strengthen the budgetary position. On the one hand, banks need to maintain a liquidity coverage ratio and, on the other hand, ensure their own financial base by not relying too much on short-term money market financing (net stable funding ratio). The leverage ratio prevents an excessive increase in the bank's balance sheet in relation to its own balance sheet. The Bank must have a primary own balance sheet of three per cent of the non-risk-weighted balance sheet. A financial institution with a low risk weight of lending cannot become excessively indebted. Any new requirements will have an impact on the MFI's profitability and lending capacity, as well as on economic growth. A lot of calculations have been put forward. In the last few months, the Institute of International Finance, the Institute of International Finance, assessed, before the final agreement was reached, that banks' profitability would plummet and their lending capacity would decline substantially, and that economic growth would slow down by up to 1.5 d 4% when the requirements came into force. As the final Basel III requirements have taken shape, the impact assessments have also become more precise. The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and several central banks, including the Bank of Finland, have done so. According to them, the direct effects are, after all, quite moderate. In the aggregate economy, they would affect GDP by about 0.2 d 0.4 % of GDP. The cost impact of lending is estimated to be that of a margin widening of around 0.25 d 0.50 % and less. In any case, impact calculations should be approached with great caution. Banks operate in an ever-changing, dynamic market. They are constantly developing their own operations and, as a result of competition, are improving productivity. As a result of competition, banks may also be forced to abandon the wide margin and accept a lower return requirement for their own bank. Those interested in impact assessments can consult the Bank of Finland's stability report Euro&Economy 2010, which contains a review of the matter. In your mind, it is a question of what you can do in business financing and how to prepare for possible cost increases. The answer is that it should be ensured that the company has more than one financial partnership. Competitive tendering between financial institutions and a number of financial instruments will help to ensure the best conditions, whatever the cost implications of the system. I would also like to say that, although the reforms will entail costs for the banks, they are in the interests of a small country as a whole, such as Finland. The crisis in the international financial markets that took place in 2008 showed very well how strongly we too are affected by the hsirst that is taking place elsewhere. Financial market staples The international financial system will take years to recover from the global economic and financial crisis. The financial position of several countries weakened due to the recession. Even confidence in the debt sustainability of a number of European countries is destabilising the financial markets. Although governments and financial institutions have confirmed their risk tolerance, the differences between countries and banking groups are large and there has been no exit from security. Fortunately, the Finnish financial system has endured well and has been able to prevent the downward spiral of severe economic downturn. emergence. Whenever criticism of the profitability of banks grows, it is good to remember, on the other hand, that the strength of Finnish financial institutions reduces the problems. This is the case, since we are certainly not protected by the international economy and financial system. The receivables of Finnish financial institutions from the most indebted countries in Europe are limited. There is a risk that the problems of these countries would be directly seized by the Finnish financial system. In any case, Finnish banks have survived the financial and economic crisis, and their profitability and solvency have remained at a good level. If the Finnish economy grows as predicted, the credit losses to banks caused by the recession will be reduced to bank credit losses. Greece was the first to experience a crisis. At first, it did not want the IMF to be involved in solving the problems at all. After lengthy negotiations, it was included in the Greek rescue package. In that situation, the imf's knowledge and experience in creating financial packages and the accompanying economic programme were the lifeblood. After Greece, there was a crisis in Ireland, which first refused to ask for help, but was eventually forced to give in. The International Monetary Fund was now involved from the outset in the management of the crisis. The program is strict. The IMF requires the economy to be put on a sustainable path. It will closely monitor compliance with the programme. In the end, however, the responsibility for balancing the economy always lies with the country itself. A lot of threats have been put forward, including for Portugal and Spain. Efforts have been made in these countries to rebalance their economies. It is possible that market confidence in the sustainability of countries' budgetary positions will be undermined. They would be temporarily dependent on credits from the European Union and the International Monetary Fund. The experience of the Greek and Irish cases has also been hystys. They contribute to capsizing the problems and the pressure elsewhere. In addition, the financial packages and operating models have been tested and more complete. Availability of financing and conditions for pinching In financial markets, euro area countries have been divided into grains and chaff as borrowers, especially over the past year (Figure 2). The prices of sovereign credit risks have diverged strongly, reflecting the creditworthiness assessed by the market. However, in the last few weeks, market expectations of solutions to sovereign debt problems have narrowed in such a way that yield differentials on bonds issued by different countries have narrowed (Figure 3). However, this is partly due to the fact that the interest rate on German debt has risen slightly more than that of most euro area countries (Figure 4). The sensitivity of the financial markets is also illustrated by the increase in the cost of bank financing, in particular the so-called "greenfields". for banks located in peripheral countries. It is understood that the weakening of the conditions for the own financing of MFIs is correspondingly reflected in the terms and conditions of their continued credits. An interesting fact is the rapid increase in the two-year interest rate on the euro. At the same time, it has exited from the dollar rate (Figure 6). It can be assumed that in the future the European MFIs will also be able to make loans. In the case of short-term interest rates, market expectations and analyst forecasts have also intensified in the direction of a slight increase in interest rates (Figures 7 and 8). One of the thermometers that describes the much-used money market conditions during the crisis is the spread between the interest rates on unsecured and secured borrowing money between banks, the so-called "green card". interbank market. The narrowing of the interest rate differential shows that the very core of the financial markets has improved, although the situation has not improved before the financial market crisis. At the same time, the financial market, which is still sensitive, will at the same time become a large number of new loan issues. Government and bank bonds are projected to enter the market at around 800 d 1,000 billion. Eur. As the financial industry as a whole adapts to the new era and its lending capacity decreases rather than increases, the risk of collapse is a real cause for concern. Finally, a good financial grouping, The financial game is not enough to strengthen economic growth and growth, and investment is needed. The international economy is recovering at a rapid pace, at around five per cent. However, economic growth is very different and different in different parts of the world. Not all developing countries even faced a crisis, and even those who experienced it have recovered rapidly from the crisis. China, India and many emerging economies are growing strongly. Among the developed economies, the United States has seen stronger-than-expected growth. The latest data on the growth in consumer demand are likely to confirm that the accelerated growth in the autumn is at the bottom of the year. However, there are still potential problems in the housing market and lending due to the high level of employment. In Europe, development is also heterogeneous. Germany is clearly the economy with the strongest growth. Government debt problems and large public deficits weigh on sentiment. Rebalancing the economies of many peripheral countries is likely to reduce their economies. The growth of the Finnish economy generally translates into exports and shifts to consumption and eventually to investment. Consumer demand has remained relatively strong and the Consumer Confidence Index also supports it to continue to do so. Productive investment is still a cause for expectation, as many industries still have capacity and many companies have the option of churning out production units outside Finland. The challenge is to ensure an increase in productive investment. For more than a decade, they have been many of our competitors. According to the Ministry, the country is already at such a stage of development that industrialisation has already passed and we need to invest in service industries. However, Chams is a dangerous road. As a small, open economy with a limited and apparently shrinking power, Finland will only increase its productivity. To ensure this, self-domination and productive investment are vital. In addition, a comparison could be made between countries that can be compared with Finland in terms of the productive structures of the economy and the levels of investment in finland. In fact, in Germany, for example, and even in Sweden, which cannot be sustained, industrial investment in machinery and equipment in relation to the size of the national economy is clearly higher than in Finland. Tm tarkoittaa sit, ett vaikka vakavaraisuusvaatimus muodollisesti silyy entisen, on rahalaitoksen kytnnss vahvistettava sit 10,5 prosenttiin. Toinen merkittv vaatimus on vahvistaa rahoitusasemaa. Vaikka valtiot ja rahoituslaitokset ovat vahvistaneet riskinsietokyky, erot eri maiden ja pankkiryhmien vlill ovat suuria ja epvarmuuksista ei ole irtauduttu. Aina kun kritiikki kasvaa pankkien kannattavuutta kohtaan, on hyv toisaalta muistaa, ett suomalaisten rahoituslaitosten vahvuus pienent ongelmia. Tm on trke, sill emme todellakaan ole suojassa kansainvlisen talouden ja rahoitusjrjestelmn hiriilt. Suomalaisten rahoituslaitosten saamiset Euroopan velkaantuneimmista maista ovat rajalliset. Tm vhent riski, ett niden maiden ongelmat suoraan tarttuisivat Suomen rahoitusjrjestelmn. Suomalaiset pankit ovat muutenkin selvinneet rahoitus-ja talouskriisist vhisin kolhuin, ja niiden kannattavuus ja vakavaraisuus ovat pysyneet hyvll tasolla. Jos Suomen talous kasvaa ennustetusti, taantuman pankeille aiheuttamat luottotappiot nyttisivt jvn vhisiksi. Kreikka kriisiytyi ensimmisen. Alkuun siihen ei toivottu Kansainvlisen valuuttarahaston (IMF) osallistumista ongelmien ratkaisuun ollenkaan. Pitkien neuvottelujen jlkeen se tuli Kreikan pelastuspakettiin mukaan. Kansainvlisen valuuttarahaston osaaminen ja kokemus rahoituspakettien ja siihen liitettvn talousohjelman luomisesta oli tuossa tilanteessa elintrke. Kreikan jlkeen kriisiytyi Irlanti, joka ensin visteli avun pyytmist, mutta joutui lopulta taipumaan. Kansainvlinen valuuttarahasto otettiin nyt heti alusta mukaan kriisin hallintaan. Ohjelma on tiukka. IMF edellytt talouden saattamista kestvlle uralle. Se seuraa tarkoin ohjelman noudattamista. Lopulta vastuu talouden tasapainoon saattamisesta on kuitenkin aina maalla itselln. Paljon uhkakuvia on esitetty mys Portugalin ja Espanjan osalta. Niss maissa on tehty toimia talouksien tasapainottamiseksi. On mahdollista, ett markkinoiden luottamus maiden rahoitusaseman kestvyyteen horjuu. Ne joutuisivat tilapisesti riippuvaisiksi Euroopan Unionin ja Kansainvlisen valuuttarahaston jrjestmist luotoista. Tllinkin Kreikan ja Irlannin tapauksien kokemuksista on hyty. Ne osaltaan kapseloivat ongelmia ja vhentvt painetta muualle. Lisksi rahoituspaketit ja toimintamallit ovat testattuja ja yh valmiimpia. Rahoituksen saatavuus ja ehdot puristukseen Rahoitusmarkkinoilla euromaat ovat jakaantuneet luotonottajina jyviin ja akanoihin erityisesti viime vuoden aikana (kuva 2). Valtioiden luottoriskien hinnat ovat eriytyneet voimakkaasti kuvaten markkinoiden arvioimaa luottokelpoisuutta. Kuitenkin aivan viime viikkoina ovat valtioiden velkaongelmien ratkaisumalleihin liittyvt odotukset nkyneet markkinoilla siten, ett tuottoerot eri maiden liikkeelle laskemien joukkovelkakirjoista ovat kaventuneet (kuva 3). Osin tm johtuu kuitenkin siit, ett Saksan velan korko on hiukan noussut enemmn kuin useimpien euromaiden korot (kuva 4). Rahoitusmarkkinoiden herkk tilannetta kuvaa mys pankkien rahoituksen kallistuminen, erityisesti ns. periferiamaissa sijaitsevien pankkien osalta. On ymmrrettv, ett rahalaitosten oman rahoituksen ehtojen heikkeneminen nkyy vastaavasti niiden edelleen myntmien luottojen ehdoissa. Mielenkiintoinen seikka on euron kahden vuoden koron nopea nousu. Samalla se on irtautunut dollarin korosta (kuva 6). Voi olettaa tmn nkyvn jatkossa eurooppalaisten rahalaitosten myntmiss lainoissa. Mys aivan lyhytaikaisten korkojen osalta markkinaodotukset ja analyytikoiden ennusteet ovat voimistuneet hienoisen koronnousun suuntaan (kuvat 7 ja 8). Yksi kriisiajan paljon kytetyist rahamarkkinaoloja kuvaavista kuumemittareista on vakuudettoman ja vakuudellisen lainarahan korkoero pankkien vlisell, ns. interbank-markkinoilla. Korkoeron kaventuminen osoittaa, ett aivan rahoitusmarkkinoiden ytimess toiminta on parantunut, joskaan viel tilanne ei ole parantunut ennen rahoitusmarkkinakriisi edeltvn kuntoon. Thn rahoitusmarkkinankymn, joka edelleen on herkk, tulee samaan aikaan suuri mr uusien lainojen liikkeeseen laskuja. Valtioiden ja pankkien joukkovelkakirjoja markkinoille ennustetaan tulevan noin 800  1.000 mrd. euron arvosta. Yritysrahoituksen hankkimista suunnittelevien on syyt olla varuillaan, etteivt yrityksen omat rahoitushankkeet syrjydy massiivisten valtioiden ja pankkien velkojen puskemana. Kun koko rahoitustoimiala sopeutuu uuteen aikaan ja sen luotonantokapasiteetti pikemminkin pienenee kuin kasvaa, on tm syrjytymisriski todellinen huolen aihe. Lopuksi hyvt rahoitustyryhmn jsenet, Finanssipeli ei riit talousnkymien ja -kasvun vahvistamiseksi,tarvitaan investointeja. Kansainvlinen talous elpyy ripe vauhtia, noin viiden prosentin tasolla. Talouskasvu on kuitenkin hyvin eritahtista ja erilaista eri puolilla maailmaa. Kehittyvt maat eivt kaikki edes joutuneet kriisiin ja nekin jotka sen kokivat, ovat toipuneet kriisist vauhdilla. Voimakkaasti kasvavat Kiina, Intia ja monet kehittyvt taloudet. Kehittyneiden talouksien joukossa Yhdysvallat on lhtenyt ennakoitua voimakkaampaan kasvuun. Viimeisimmt tiedot kulutuskysynnn kasvusta ovat omiaan vahvistamaan ksityst, ett syksyll kiihtymn lhtenyt kasvu on kestvll pohjalla. Kuitenkin siell on viel jljell mahdollisia ongelmia asuntomarkkinoilla ja -luototuksessa sek korkean tyttmyyden johdosta. Euroopassa kehitys on mys heterogeenist. Saksa on selkesti voimakkaimmin kasvanut talous. Valtioiden velkaongelmat ja julkisten talouksien suuret vajeet painavat tunnelmaa. Monien periferiamaiden talouden tasapainottaminen on omiaan supistamaan taloutta. Suomen talouden kasvu lhtee yleens viennist ja siirtyy kulutukseen ja lopulta investointeihin. Vienti  ja perinteisill, monen jo savupiipputeollisuudeksi tuomituilla aloilla  on lhtenyt ennakoitua parempaan vetoon. Maailmankaupan ja vientimarkkinoidemme kysynnn kasvu antavat toiveita viennin jatkumisesta ripen. Kulutuskysynt on pysynyt varsin vahvana ja mys kuluttajien luottamusindeksi tukee nkemyst sen jatkuvan sellaisena. Tuotannolliset investoinnit antavat viel odotuttaa, sill edelleen monilla toimialoilla on kyttmtnt kapasiteettia ja useilla yrityksill mahdollisuus hydynt Suomen ulkopuolella olevia tuotantoyksikitn. Haaste on varmistaa tuotannollisten investointien kasvu. Jo reilun vuosikymmenen ajan ne ovat olleet monia kilpailijamaitamme vhisempi. Usein kuulee vitteen, ett Suomi ei en tarvitse panostuksia tuotannolliseen pomaan teollisuudessa. Maa on tmn vitteen mukaan jo sellaisessa kehitysvaiheessa, ett teollistuminen on jo ohitettu ja meidn tulee panostaa palvelutoimialoihin. Tm on kuitenkin vaarallinen tie. Pienen avoimena kansantaloutena, jolla on rajallinen ja ilmeisesti supistuva tyvoima, Suomi prj vain tuottavuuttaan nostamalla. Tmn varmistamiseksi pomavaltaistuminen ja tuotannolliset investoinnit ovat elintrkeit. Lisksi vertailuun voisi ottaa maita, joita voidaan talouden tuotantorakenteiden osalta verrata Suomeen, ja niden investointitasoja. Yllttv onkin, ett esimerkiksi Saksassa ja jopa Ruotsissa, joita ei voine pit jlkeenjneempin, teollisuuden kone-ja laiteinvestoinnit suhteessa kansantalouden kokoon ovat selvsti korkeammat kuin Suomessa. Siksi loppuun totean, ett oivatkaan finanssijrjestelyt  vaikka niit tss rahoitustyryhmss varmasti arvostammekin  eivt riit, vaan tarvitsemme tuotannollisia investointeja tulevaisuuden talouskasvua varmistamaan. rahoitusmarkkinat (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tag=rahoitusmarkkinat) Hakkarainen (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tag=Hakkarainen)

Title: Economic development lines; three positives and four challenges
text: Vice Chairman of the Board pentti Hakkarainen: Economic development lines; three of them and four challenges. City Centre Economic Seminar, Helsinki 2.3.2011 . Speech . Wednesday2 March 2011,4:00 PM Pentti Hakkarainen, Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors Presentation at the Centre Party Economic Seminar in Helsinki2.3.2011 The body of the presentation, may differ from the presentation held. Presentation (/globalassets/en/media-and.. publications/speeches/documents/talouspolitiikan_keskeiset_haasteet_pentti_hakkarainen.pdf) membranes (pdf) Economic trends; three mysnteists and four Challenging Under the topic "The key challenges of economic policy and Finland's position in the global economy", I will select a few trends that have been developing for several years and will be long in the future, which could fashionably be called megatrends. The big news of the moment; Unrest in the Arab world and their impact on the price of sljy, inflationary pressures, economic crises in individual countries, etc., to the sidelines. Three of the trends I have chosen are mysnteist and four will, in the worst case, cause major problems if they are not addressed in time. Hysdynnsn International Monetary Fund's (IMF) Global Economic Outlook Update published a month ago and the Global Financial Stability Report (Market Update), the Bank of Finland's own analyses and a speech by Erkki Liikanen, Director of The International Monetary Fund, on global economic change in the OP-Pohjola Group's research paper 14.2.2011. Recent economic developments include a rapid recovery of the world economy, the ability, in concert with several countries and institutions, to solve problems, and the involvement of our traditional export industry in the boom in the world economy in highly competitive markets. The challenging trends are, first of all, that the financial crisis is not behind the tsys and that negative overruns are still possible. Another major challenge is to get the over-indebted countries back on a sustainable economic path, including in Europe. In addition, Finland has two specific issues of its own; public debt must be brought under control and a solid basis must be laid for future economic development. The development has brought about a new situation, a new normality, such as Mohammad El-Erian, Director of PIMCO has described himself as permanent. There are several long-term joys and difficulties, but in this context I will only mention the above. The following presentation, Dr. Jaakko Kiander, will discuss, among other things, issues related to the elskejs system. Global economic recovery (slide 2) The global economy recovered rapidly from the recession caused by the financial crisis. Growth slowed down somewhat in the second half of last year. According to the latest data, growth should still remain positive around the turn of the year in most industrialised countries. The recovery after the recession was initially driven by exceptionally strong fiscal stimulus measures and the slowdown in the stock cycle; during the recession, companies had emptied their stocks. However, the effects of these factors are not permanent. The recovery will only continue permanently where the conditions are in place for private demand to strengthen. In industrialised countries, private demand is associated with security. Businesses and households are indebted and indebted (deleveraging). The availability of borrowed money has decreased compared to the situation before the recession. Households cannot expect a high level of demand when their income development is subdued and the employment situation remains weak. Business investment, on the other hand, is weighed down by the economic security of the economy and the high level of production capacity. Since the crisis, global economic growth has clearly focused on emerging economies, where private consumption and investment have increased significantly since the recession. The downturn in the emerging economies of the Member States is both short and subdued compared to developed industrialised countries (slide 3). Emerging economies have increased their dependence on foreign funding. Their claims abroad have increased, as have their foreign exchange reserves. Emerging economies are collectively vulnerable to the hsirish of international financial markets. There are also other factors behind the development. The export structure of the rapidly developed countries has diversified and their central trade has increased. The income level of citizens has risen and the importance of domestic demand has increased. An interesting development trend is that China is expected to soon become the world's largest economy (Slide 4). This is the result of a process of apprehension that has progressed rapidly since the turn of the millennium. In 2000, China's economy was just over half the size of the U.S. economy. On the other hand, this is not a historically new issue. China lost its position as the largest economy in the world only in the late 1800s. International Cooperation (Slide 5) Another mysterious development is the nshty international cooperation. In August 2007, the functioning of banks, i.e. the interbank market, was seriously supported by central banks from around the world capable of well-coordinated and simultaneous action. Not only the national central banks belonging to the euro system took part in the cooperation, but also the central banks of the United States, England, Switzerland, Sweden, Japan and Canada, among others. In the area of financial market slumping that followed the financial crisis, good examples of cooperation are the joint efforts of the G20 countries, the bank's tightening of the Basel III SsNnssss, and the EU's efforts to reform financial supervision, fiscal policy, the management of economic crises and structural policies. Part of the work has already been implemented and is in operation. Progress has also been made which, until a few years ago, seemed impossible for Chys to achieve. The capacity to solve international problems has improved and I believe that it will remain so. However, there is still a lot to be done. Export water in our core industries (slide 6) The third bright spot can be the rapid growth of Finnish exports. It has returned to its peak level in the 2000s. Thanks to the pull of exports, the Finnish economy is also recovering. Total production grew by about 3.1 per cent last year. According to several forecasts, Finland's total production will increase by about 2.5 d 3 % in the lshi years. Finland's economic recovery was relatively slow compared to many other countries. This was due to the structure of our production and, at the same time, our exports. Finland's exports have focused on investment hysdys, the demand for which in the world has been weak in many respects due to overcapacity. However, during 2010, our exports clearly started to pick up. Growth was strong in sectors that have sometimes been mistakenly described as sectors of the past, such as metal processing and the chemical industry. Ladies and gentlemen, move on to the challenges of the economy and economic policy. Long to prepare for the impact of this and to take timely action to make our economy more resilient. Economies are (over)indebted (Slide 7) The recession severely weakened public finances in most industrialised countries, as the deterioration of the real economy rapidly reduced the tax base. Automatic stabilisers and active stimulus measures also increased public deficits. It is precisely in the industrialised countries that the public deficit has grown. In industrialised countries, the size of the public sector is larger than in developing countries. In the industrialised countries, the ratio of gross government debt to GDP increased from around 70% last year to around 95% last year. At the same time, in emerging economies, public debt has remained around 35% of GDP. The general government deficit in the industrialised countries is declining only slowly over the past few years, and public debt continues to rise. The problem is exacerbated by the fact that economic growth rates are weak in many of the countries with high public debt. In many countries, the problems have grown to such an extent that it is not enough to reverse the recovery measures alone, but there is a need for strong restructuring and structural changes. Financial markets in a state of flux The functioning of financial markets has improved, but the situation remains fragile. This reflects developments in euro area government bond markets (Slide 8). The euro brought advantages to many countries in the form of a lower and more stable interest rate. Nsms psssivst on the same interest rate terms as the best and most creditworthy issuers. Interest rate differentials narrowed to vsssis and the favorable situation lasted for a decade. As the financial crisis turned more and more into a debt crisis, the situation on the eurobond debt market turned into a debt crisis. More attention is now being paid to the creditworthiness of countries. As a result, the interest paid by the over-indebted countries has jumped to their own levels. As a result, they will have to pay a much higher risk for their borrowing. The o fever indicator, which is a good indicator of the financial markets, is the price of secured and unsecured financing in the banks' market. Tslls so-called. in the interbank market, the spread in interest rates between these forms of financing was small before the financial crisis during the well-functioning period (slide 9). The interest rate differential used to spread, especially at the time of Lehman's bankruptcy. Although the spread has now narrowed, it has become more broad than before. It will continue to communicate the security of the market. Balance of Finland's general government finances (slide 10) Market confidence in the long-term sustainability of public finances is particularly sensitive during the financial market situation that I have described. Without policy changes, Finland's public debt will rise rapidly in the 2020s as the growth of expenditure related to entrepreneurship accelerates. The sustainability gap in public finances amounts to 5% of GDP, according to a report published by the Minister of Finance in late 2010. The general government balance should be improved by 2015 in order to ensure that public finances are on a sustainable footing in the long term. According to the Bank of Finland's september 2010 estimate of the sustainability gap is slightly higher, at around 6% of GDP. An element in our country's preparation for the challenge is to improve productivity. In the middle is also an effort to extend the tysur. The problem of the sustainability of public finances will not be solved simply by the lengthening of the labour market or by improving the productivity of public services. The deficit in the sustainability of public finances has already grown to such an extent that further structural reforms are needed d as well as a reassessment of expenditure and revenue. Weak productivity development and investment in machinery and equipment (slide 11) Our fourth challenge is the change in the structure of production and the relocation of our production. For example, the production capacity of paper and board production in Finland from 2005 to 2009 was about one fifth. The electronics industry has also seen numerous closures of sites and relocations of production abroad. There is a risk that some of the production that has been shut down in Finland during the recession will be permanently removed. This applies in particular to part of the metal products and engineering industries, which are subcontractors to large companies. The recession may have permanently turned the subcontracting chains of companies into a loss for Finnish production. It is therefore essential to ensure that the economy is able to make investments and increase productivity. In Finland, due to the age of sestsn ikssn ikssn vsestsn mssss is shrinking for decades. In the autumn, we must take care of the increase in productivity, part of which is the self-domination, i.e. investment in machinery and equipment. Nsin is also a part of our traditional industries. Investment is accompanied by improvements in productivity and also by the so-called "greenfield". the improvement in overall productivity is tightly intertwined with them. It is not isolated. When companies invest in machinery and equipment, it is in their interest to constantly develop new ways of getting better returns from their production and processes. There will be a solid foundation for improving Ns productivity. As a result of this development, it is worrying that, although private investment combined with gdp has remained stable in relation to total output since the recession of the 1990s, investment in machinery and equipment has continued to decline. Finland's investment rate in machinery and equipment is clearly below the euro area. Given the large weight of industry in the Finnish economy, it is important that investment in machinery and equipment in Finland is lower than in Germany, and even lower than in Sweden. This is not a one-year observation, but the situation has continued in the mid-1990s. There is a great danger that our productive capacity has been and will continue to do so. The arguments for a low level of investment cannot be justified because we are at a longer stage of development of our society than the countries (Slide 12). The growth rate of industrial productivity excluding the electronics industry has slowed down in the 2000s. However, the rest of the industry faced a recession earlier and, on the other hand, was able to adapt its operations to the changed situation quickly. This means that productivity increased in 2009 after the contraction in 2008. In contrast to the Sshks and electronics industries, productivity did not plummet until 2009 (Foil 13). Conclusion(Slide 14) Good listeners Under the pressure of major development lines affecting the economy, Finland must continue to do so. The growth of the global economy, international cooperation in solving economic problems and the return of Finnish exports to growth path give us numerous opportunities. It is essential that we take into account the major development lines that also affect us. Firstly, the over-indebted countries and the high levels of debt of the various economic players have an impact. Secondly, access to finance will not be as good and easy as it was before the financial crisis. The budgetary position of non-financial corporations and households must be sufficiently strong. By ensuring the sustainability of public finances and the conditions for productive investment, our country will be in a state of turmoil even in the worst of times, and a solid foundation will be laid for mysntic economic development. Valitsemastani trendeist kolme on mynteist ja nelj tuovat pahimmassa tapauksessa suuria ongelmia, ellei niihin puututa ajoissa. Hydynnn Kansainvlisen valuuttarahaston (IMF) kuukausi sitten julkaistua Maailmantalouden ennustetta (World Economic Outlook Update) ja rahoitusmarkkinoiden vakausanalyysi (Global Financial Stability Report, Market Update), Suomen Pankin omia analyysej ja pjohtaja Erkki Liikasen puhetta Maailmantalouden muutoksesta OP-Pohjola-ryhmn tutkimusstin teemapivss 14.2.2011. Talouden viimeaikaisia mynteisi kehityskulkuja ovat maailmantalouden ripe elpyminen, kyky kansainvlisesti usean maan ja instituution kanssa yhteistoimin ratkoa ongelmia sek perinteisen vientiteollisuutemme pseminen mukaan maailmantalouden nousuun kovasti kilpailuilla markkinoilla. Haasteellisia trendej ovat ensiksikin, ett finanssikriisi ei ole tysin takana ja tten kielteiset ylltykset ovat edelleen mahdollisia. Toinen suuri haaste on, ylivelkaantuneiden valtioiden, mys Euroopassa, saaminen takaisin kestvlle talousuralle. Niden lisksi Suomella on kaksi omaa erityiskysymyst; julkisen talouden velkaantuminen on saatava hallintaan ja tulevalle talouskehitykselle on luotava vankka pohja. Kehityksess on tultu uuteen tilanteeseen, ehk uuteen normaaliin kuten Mohammad El-Erian, PIMCO:n johtaja on kuvaillut, joka taitaa jd pysyvksi. Useampia pitkn aikavlin ilonaiheita ja vaikeuksia on, mutta tss yhteydess ksittelen vain edell mainittuja. Seuraava esitelmitsij, tohtori Jaakko Kiander, ehk ottaa esille muun muassa elkejrjestelmn liittyvi asioita. Maailmantalouden elpyminen (kalvo 2) Maailmantalous elpyi vauhdilla finanssikriisin aiheuttamasta taantumasta. Kasvu hidastui jonkin verran viime vuoden toisella puoliskolla. Uusimpien tietojen perusteella kasvu nyttisi silti jatkuneen positiivisena vuodenvaihteen tuntumassakin  mys useimmissa teollisuusmaissa. Taantuman jlkeen koetun elpymisen taustalla olivat aluksi sek poikkeuksellisen voimakkaat julkisen talouden elvytystoimet ett varastosyklin kntyminen; yritysten oli tydennettv taantuman aikana tyhjennettyj varastojaan. Niden tekijiden vaikutukset eivt kuitenkaan ole pysyvi. Elpyminen jatkuu pysyvmmin vain siell, miss edellytykset yksityisen kysynnn vahvistumiselle ovat olemassa. Teollisuusmaissa yksityisen kysynnn lhiaikojen nkymiin liittyy epvarmuutta. Yritykset ja kotitaloudet ovat velkaantuneita ja velkaantuneisuutta vhennetn (deleveraging). Lainarahan saatavuus on heikentynyt taantumaa edeltneeseen tilanteeseen verrattuna. Kotitalouksien ei voi odottaa lisvn kysyntns voimakkaasti, kun niiden tulokehitys on vaimeaa ja kun tyllisyystilanne on edelleen heikko. Yritysten investointeja puolestaan painaa talousnkymien epvarmuus sek on runsas kyttmtn tuotantokapasiteetti. Maailmantalouden kasvu on kriisin jlkeen painottunut selvsti kehittyviin talouksiin, joissa yksityinen kulutus ja investoinnit ovat taantuman jlkeen lisntyneet tuntuvasti. Taantuma jikin kehittyviss talouksissa sek lyhyeksi ett vaimeaksi kehittyneisiin teollisuusmaihin verrattuna (kalvo 3). Kehittyvt taloudet ovat vhentneet riippuvuuttaan ulkomaisesta rahoituksesta. Niiden saatavat ulkomailta ovat kasvaneet, kuten mys niiden valuuttavarannot. Kehittyvt taloudet ovat yh vhemmn haavoittuvaisia kansainvlisten rahoitusmarkkinoiden hiriille. Kehityksen taustalla on mys muita tekijit. Nopeasti kehittyneiden maiden viennin rakenne on monipuolistunut ja niiden keskininen kauppa on kasvanut. Kansalaisten tulotaso on noussut ja kotimaisen kysynnn merkitys on kasvanut. Mielenkiintoista kehitystrendiss on se, ett Kiinan arvioidaan pian nousevan maailman suurimmaksi taloudeksi (kalvo 4). Tm on seurausta kiinniottoprosessista, joka on edennyt hmmstyttvn nopeasti vuosituhannen vaihteen jlkeen. Viel vuonna 2000 Kiinan talous oli kooltaan vain hieman yli puolet Yhdysvaltain taloudesta. Toisaalta kyse ei ole historiallisesti uudesta asiasta. Kiina menetti asemansa maailman suurimpana taloutena vasta 1800-luvun lopulla. Kansainvlinen yhteisty (kalvo 5) Toinen mynteinen kehitys on nhty kansainvlisess yhteistyss. Vlittmsti elokuussa 2007 pankkien vlisen, eli interbank-markkinan toiminnan hiriintyess vakavasti keskuspankit eri puolilta maailmaa kykenivt hyvin koordinoituun ja samanaikaiseen toimintaan. Yhteistoimintaan osallistuivat, ei vain eurojrjestelmn kuuluvat kansalliset keskuspankit vaan mys muun muassa Yhdysvaltojen, Englannin Sveitsin, Ruotsin, Japanin ja Kanadan keskuspankit. Finanssikriisi seuranneen rahoitusmarkkinoiden sntelyn alalla hyvi esimerkkej yhteistoiminnasta ovat G20 maiden yhteistoimet, pankkisntely kiristv Basel III -snnst sek toimet EU:ssa rahoitusvalvonnan, finanssipolitiikan, talouskriisien hallinnan ja rakennepolitiikan uudistamiseksi. Osa nist on jo toteutettu ja tydess toiminnassa. Tsskin on saatu aikaan edistyst, joka viel joitakin vuosia sitten tuntui tysin mahdottomalta saavuttaa. Valmiudet kansainvlisten ongelmien ratkaisemiseksi ovat parantuneet ja uskoisin pysyvsti. Kuitenkin tsskin on viel paljon tehtv. Vienti vet perustoimialoillamme (kalvo 6) Kolmantena valopilkkuna voi ottaa Suomen viennin nopean kasvun. Se on palautunut lhes jo 2000-luvun huipputasolleen. Viennin vedon ansiosta mys Suomen talous on elpymss. Kokonaistuotanto kasvoi viime vuonna noin 3,1 prosenttia. Useiden ennusteiden mukaan Suomen kokonaistuotanto kasvaa lhivuosina noin 2,5  3 prosenttia. Suomen talouden elpyminen kynnistyi verraten myhn moniin muihin maihin verrattuna. Tm johtui tuotantomme ja samalla vientimme rakenteesta. Suomen vienti on painottunut investointihydykkeisiin, joiden kysynt maailmalla on ollut monelta osin laimeaa ylikapasiteetin vuoksi. Vuoden 2010 mittaan vientimme alkoi kuitenkin selvsti vauhdittua. Kasvu oli ylltten voimakasta aloilla, joita on joskus luonnehdittu virheellisesti menneisyyden aloiksi, kuten metallien jalostuksessa sek kemianteollisuudessa. Hyvt naiset ja herrat, siirrytn talouden ja talouspolitiikan haasteisiin. Niden vaikutuksiin pit varautua ja ajoissa tehd toimia, joilla parannetaan taloutemme kestokyky. Taloudet ovat(yli)velkaantuneita (kalvo 7) Taantuma heikensi julkisen talouden nkymi tuntuvasti useimmissa teollisuusmaissa, kun reaalitalouden kehityksen heikkeneminen supisti nopeasti veropohjaa. Mys automaattiset vakauttajat ja aktiiviset elvytystoimenpiteet kasvattivat julkisia alijmi. Julkiset alijmt ovat kasvaneet nimenomaan teollisuusmaissa. Teollisuusmaissa julkisen sektorin koko on kehittyvi maita suurempi. Teollisuusmaissa julkisen talouden bruttovelan BKT-suhde kasvoi taantumaa edeltneelt noin 70 prosentin tasolta viime vuonna jo 95 prosentin vaiheille. Samaan aikaan kehittyviss talouksissa julkinen velka on pysynyt 35 prosentin tuntumassa suhteessa bruttokansantuotteeseen. Julkisen talouden alijmt nyttvt teollisuusmaissa supistuvan lhivuosina vain hitaasti, ja julkinen velka jatkaa viel kasvuaan. Ongelmaa pahentaa se, ett talouskasvun nkymt ovat heikot monissa niist maista, joissa julkinen velka on suuri. Useissa maissa ongelmat ovat kasvaneet niin suuriksi, ettei elvytystoimien peruuttaminen yksin riit vaan tarvitaan voimakasta saneerausta ja rakenteellisia muutoksia. Finanssimarkkinat jnnittyneet Finanssimarkkinoiden toiminta on parantunut, mutta tila on edelleen herkk. Tt kuvastaa kehitys euroalueen valtioiden joukkovelkakirjamarkkinoilla (kalvo 8). Euro toi usealle maalle etua matalamman ja vakaamman koron muodossa. Nm psivt samoille korkoehdoille parhaiden ja luottokelpoisimpien liikkeellelaskijoiden kanssa. Korkoerot kaventuivat vhisiksi ja suotuisa tilanne kesti vuosikymmenen. Finanssikriisin muuttuessa enenevsti maiden velkakriisiksi muuttui tilanne euromrisill velkamarkkinoilla. Maiden luottokelpoisuuteen kiinnitetn nyt aiempaa enemmn huomioita. Tmn johdosta ylivelkaantuneiden maiden maksamat korkot ovat hypnneet omille tasoilleen. Ne joutuvat siis maksamaan lainanotostaan aiempaa selvsti korkeampaa riskilis. Rahoitusmarkkinoita hyvin kuvaava kuumemittari on pankkien vlisen markkinan vakuudellisen ja vakuudettoman rahoituksen hinta. Tll ns. interbank-markkinalla kyseisten rahoitusmuotojen korkoero oli ennen finanssikriisi -hyvin toimivana aikana -mitttmn pieni (kalvo 9). Korkoero levisi ennen nkemttmksi erityisesti Lehmanin konkurssin aikaan. Vaikka korkoero on nyt kaventunut, nytt se jneen aiempaa levemmksi. Tm viestii edelleen markkinoiden epvarmuudesta. Suomen julkisen talouden tasapaino (kalvo 10) Markkinoiden luottamus julkisen talouden pitkn aikavlin kestvyyteen on erityisen trke tllaisen kuvaamani herkn rahoitusmarkkinatilanteen aikana. Ilman politiikkamuutoksia Suomen julkinen velka lhtee nopeaan nousuun 2020-luvulla, kun ikntymiseen liittyvien menojen kasvu kiihtyy. Julkisen talouden kestvyysvaje on 5 % BKT:st valtiovarainministerin loppuvuonna 2010 julkistaman raportin mukaan. Julkisen talouden rahoitusasemaa pitisi kohentaa tmn verran vuoteen 2015 menness, jotta julkinen talous olisi kestvll pohjalla pitkll aikavlill. Suomen Pankin syyskuussa 2010 tekem arvio kestvyysvajeesta on hieman suurempi, noin 6 % BKT:st. Trke elementti maamme valmistautumisessa ikntymishaasteeseen on tyn tuottavuuden parantaminen. Keskeist on mys pyrkimys pident tyuria. Julkisen talouden kestvyysongelma ei ratkea pelkstn tyurien pitenemisell tai julkisten palvelujen tuottavuuden paranemisella. Julkisen talouden kestvyysvaje on kasvanut jo niin suureksi, ett lisksi tarvitaan muitakin rakenteellisia uudistuksia  sek vistmtt mys menojen ja tulojen uudelleenarviointia. Heikko tuottavuuskehitys ja vhiset kone-ja laiteinvestoinnit(kalvo 11) Neljs haasteemme on tuotantorakenteen muutos ja tuotantomme siirtyminen muualle. Esimerkiksi paperin-ja kartonginvalmistuksen tuotantokapasiteetti vheni Suomessa vuodesta 2005 vuoteen 2009 noin viidenneksell. Mys elektroniikkateollisuudessa on nhty lukuisia toimipaikkojen sulkemisia ja tuotannon siirtymisi ulkomaille. On riski, ett osa taantuman aikana Suomessa alas ajetusta tuotannosta siirtyy pysyvsti pois. Tm koskee erityisesti sit osaa metallituote-ja konepajateollisuudesta, joka toimii alihankkijana suurille yrityksille. Taantuma on voinut pysyvsti muuttaa yritysten vlisi alihankintaketjuja suomalaisen tuotannon tappioksi. Onkin olennaista varmistaa elinkeinoelmn edellytykset investoinneille ja tuottavuuden lismiselle. Suomessa vestn ikntymisen vuoksi tyikisen vestn mr supistuu lhivuosikymmenet. Tst syyst meidn on huolehdittava tyn tuottavuuden kasvusta, jonka trke osa on pomavaltaistuminen, eli investoinnit koneisiin ja laitteisiin. Nin on mys perinteisill teollisuuden aloillamme. Investointeihin liittyy tuottavuuden parantaminen ja mys ns. kokonaistuottavuuden koheneminen kietoutuu tiukasti niihin. Se ei ole irrallinen. Kun yritykset investoivat koneisiin ja laitteisiin, on niiden intressiss jatkuvasti kehitt uusia keinoja saada tuotannostaan ja prosesseistaan entist parempaa tuotosta. Nin tuottavuuden parantamiselle tulee vankka pohja. Kehityksess on huolestuttavaa, ett vaikka yksityiset investoinnit yhteens ovat 1990-luvun laman jlkeen pysytelleet vakaina suhteessa kokonaistuotantoon, niihin sisltyvt kone-ja laiteinvestoinnit ovat vhentyneet edelleen. Suomen investointiaste koneisiin ja laitteisiin onkin selvsti euroalueen alapuolella. Huomioiden teollisuuden suuren painon Suomen taloudessa, on yllttv, ett investoinnit koneisiin ja laitteisiin ovat Suomessa alemmat kuin Saksassa, ja jopa alemmat kuin Ruotsissa. Tm ei ole yhden vuoden havainto vaan tilanne on jatkunut 1990.luvun puolivlist. Suuri vaara on, ett tuotantokykymme on rapautunut ja rapautuu edelleen. Perusteita alhaiselle investointiasteelle ei voi lyt siit, ett olisimme yhteiskuntamme kehitysvaiheessa pidemmll kuin nm maat (Kalvo 12). Teollisuuden tyn tuottavuuden kasvuvauhti ilman elektroniikkateollisuutta on hidastunut 2000-luvulla. Tosin muu teollisuus kohtasi taantuman aiemmin ja pystyi toisaalta sopeuttamaan toimintansa muuttuneeseen tilanteeseen nopeasti. Tm nkyy siten, ett tyn tuottavuus kntyi vuoden 2008 supistumisen jlkeen kasvuun jo vuonna 2009. Shk-ja elektroniikkateollisuudessa sit vastoin tyn tuottavuus romahti vasta 2009 (Kalvo 13). Lopuksi(Kalvo 14) Hyvt kuulijat Niden talouteen vaikuttavien suurten kehityslinjojen puristuksissa Suomen on prjttv jatkossakin. Maailmantalouden kasvu, kansainvlinen yhteisty talousongelmien ratkaisussa ja Suomen viennin palaaminen kasvu-uralle antavat meille lukuisia mahdollisuuksia. Olennaista on, ett huomioidaan isot kehityslinjat, jotka vaikuttavat mys meihin. Ensinnkin ylivelkaantuneilla valtioilla ja talouden eri toimijoiden suurilla velka-asteilla on vaikutuksensa. Toiseksi rahoituksen saatavuus ei ehk tule olemaan yht hyv ja helppoa kuin ennen finanssikriisi. Yritysten ja kotitalouksien rahoitusaseman tulee olla riittvn vahva. Kun varmistetaan julkisen talouden kestokyky ja edellytykset tuotannollisille investoinneille, maamme tulee prjmn pahemmassakin myllerryksess ja mynteiselle talouskehitykselle luodaan vankka pohja. Title: Economic and financial market outlook
text: Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen: Economic and financial markets nskymis. Yls-Savo Chamber of Commerce, Iisalmi 16.5.2011 . Speech . Monday16 May 2011, 3:00PM Pentti Hakkarainen, Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors Presentation at the seminar of the Yls-Savo Chamber of Commerce department in Iisalmi 16.5.2011 Presentation slides (pdf) (/globalassets/en/suomen_pankki/news/speeches/Documents/160511_Yls-Savon_kauppakamariosasto.pdf) Economic and financial markets Welcome ladies and gentlemen. First of all, I congratulate the MPs elected from Yls-Savo. It is important to get good representatives of the country's affairs from the region. Although the staples of the economy are partly mysntes, there is also a great deal of sign of the developments that will be required in difficult matters. Recent economic developments include a rapid recovery in the global economy. This is a good illustration of the industrial purchasing psllikks index (Figure 2). This indicator shows that the economy started to rise sharply after the recession of 2009. During 2010, the trend stalled and the year's shopping survey gives reason to expect the economy to continue to develop in a positive way. However, there are two different rates of global economic growth (Figures 3 and 4). Emerging economies are growing at a steady pace of around six per cent, and there was not even an actual recession. The slowdown in emerging economies is both short and subdued compared to the developed industrialised countries. The developed economies, the countries, are experiencing a slower growth rate of a couple of per cent. After the dip, the economies are only just reaching the level of gdp of a couple of years ago. The change in the growth dynamics of the world economy is obviously permanent. Growth is increasingly focused on emerging economies, especially those of Asian countries. Since the recession, private consumption and investment have increased substantially. An interesting development trend is that China is estimated to be emerging back as the world's largest economy already during the Lshi years (Figure 5). It lost its status as the largest economic power as it did about 150 years ago. In the Lshi years, it regains its number one status. It is estimated that the global economy will enter a new normal, with a sustained strengthening of the position of the emerging economies. It also supports fiscal developments (Figure 6). In the industrialised countries, public finances are increasingly indebted. Ten years ago, the public debt of the countries was about 65% of total production and has now risen by 100%. A completely different development has occurred in emerging economies. Their debt ratio has declined and is expected to decline further in relation to their GDP. Looking at global indebtedness and developments in different countries, we should not limit ourselves to public sector debt (Figure 7). Imf data show that debt problems during the financial crisis are not confined to specific debt crisis countries. In addition to the public sector, the state of households, enterprises and financial institutions needs to be examined. Debt problems are wide-ranging and affect different sectors within the economies. Finland is doing well in comparison, as the indebtedness of one sector is not high. The situation of MFIs is quite different in different countries (Figure 8). The problems of banks are not confined to certain countries. In addition, there are major differences between the enclave countries and the risk of doing business. In several countries, many banks are vulnerable in terms of sovereign bond investments, credit risk, fundraising costs, profitability or solvency. The banks operating in Finland are in good shape by the indicators. However, even here, the uncertainty surrounding the quality of European banks' balance sheets and the fear that problems will spread can exacerbate the situation. From this angle, bank stress testing is particularly common in Europe. On the basis of the results, care must be taken to ensure that banks are restructured or closed down in a controlled manner. The changeover to the euro partly created the illusion that the countries participating in the monetary union would be on an equal footing in terms of creditworthiness (Figure 9). During the debt crisis, the creditworthiness and financing costs of different countries have become more differentiated. Finland is among the good countries and we must do our part to ensure that our economy does not become too indebted and that we lose good creditworthiness and good financing conditions. The links between the Finnish monetary economy and the rest of Europe are great (Figure 10). There is a risk that, when we look at the impact of debt crisis countries on us, we will focus only on investments in crisis countries. A mere examination of them underestimates the negative effects. Operating in an integrated financial market would not limit the damage of the worst-case scenarios to economies struggling with debt problems. Finns' investments in the EU area total 310 billion and in the euro area 120 billion, so all the hsirist would be transported in an unpredictable way to us as well. Another important channel through which the uncontrolled management of the problems of debt-crisis countries is affected is the possible increase in the cost of financing banks. Banks operating in Finland have to finance around EUR 40 billion themselves on the wholesale market (Figure 11). It has been estimated that the failure to rebalance the financial packages and economies of Greece, Ireland and Portugal could lead to a substantial increase in market interest rates. The cost of fundraising for Finnish banks would be rapid. As a whole, the Finnish financial system remains stable (Figure 12). Only indebtedness has remained a threat to stability. Although, on the whole, it is still reasonable compared to many other economies, there are worrying features. Many households are heavily indebted (Figure 13). One way of looking at this is to look at how many households owe more than three times the annual income they have. The mssrs of such households already accounts for 17% of all households with over-indebtedness, and they already account for half of all household debts. A bright spot of economic development in Finland is the rapid growth of exports (Figure 14). Thanks to the pull of exports, the Finnish economy is also recovering. Total output grew by about 3.1% last year and continues to grow at a rate of 4% in lshes and around 2.5% in the lshi years. Despite the slowdown in growth, there are challenges in the state of Finland's public finances. Government expenditure is clearly higher than revenue (Figure 15). According to a report published by the Minister of Finance at the end of 2010, the deficit in the sustainability of public finances is 5% of GDP. This means that the general government balance should be improved by 2015 in order to maintain a sustainable budgetary base over a long period of time. The problem of the sustainability of public finances will not be solved simply by the lengthening of the labour market or by improving the productivity of public services. The deficit in the sustainability of public finances has already grown to such an extent that further structural reforms are needed d as well as a reassessment of expenditure and revenue. The growth of the global economy and the return of Finnish exports to a growth path give us numerous opportunities. However, there are concerns about the decline in investment (Figure 16). In Finland, you should take care of the investment conditions for companies. Investment in machinery and equipment is now higher than the average in the euro area and, for example, in Germany and Sweden. At worst, this leads to the erosion of the productive pssoma. Our economy needs to be sustained in order to overcome the economic problems in the Nsks district (Figure 15). srkess is to ensure that the productivity of the company is increased. When the tysvsestsn mssrs does not grow, it should also be extended by tysur; from the beginning, the middle and the end. While ensuring the sustainability of public finances and the conditions for productive investment, our country will be in a state of turmoil even in the worst of times, and a solid foundation will be laid for mysntic economic development. Ladies and gentlemen, I will answer your questions as you please.

Monday16 May 2011, 3:00PM Pentti Hakkarainen, johtokunnan varapuheenjohtaja Alustus Yl-Savon kauppakamariosaston seminaarissa Iisalmessa 16.5.2011 Esitelmn kalvot (pdf) (/globalassets/fi/suomen_pankki/ajankohtaista/puheet/Documents/160511_Yl-Savon_kauppakamariosasto.pdf) Talouden ja rahoitusmarkkinoiden nkymi Tervetuloa hyvt naiset ja herrat. Ensimmiseksi onnittelen Yl-Savosta valittuja kansanedustajia. On trke saada alueelta hyvt edustajat pttmn maan asioista. Vaikka talouden nkymt ovat osin mynteisi, on samalla paljon merkkej kehityskuluista, jotka tulevat edellyttmn ptksi vaikeissa asioissa. Talouden viimeaikaisia mynteisi kehityskulkuja ovat maailmantalouden ripe elpyminen. Tt kuvaa hyvin teollisuuden ostopllikkindeksi (kuva 2). Tm indikaattori osoittaa, ett talous lhti nousuun syvn vuoden 2009 taantuman jlkeen. Vuoden 2010 aikana kehitys taittui ja tmn vuoden ostopllikkkysely antaa perusteen odottaa talouden kehittyvn edelleen mynteisesti. Maailmantalouden kasvussa on kuitenkin kaksi eri vauhtia (kuvat 3 ja 4). Nousevat taloudet kasvavat tasaisen ripesti noin kuuden prosentin vauhdilla, eik niss edes koettu varsinaista taantumaa. Hidastunut vaihe ji nousevissa talouksissa sek lyhyeksi ett vaimeaksi kehittyneisiin teollisuusmaihin verrattuna. Kehittyneet taloudet, lnsimaat, ovat hitaammassa parin prosentin kasvuvauhdissa. Notkahduksen jlkeen lnsitaloudet ovat vasta saavuttamassa parin vuoden takaisen kokonaistuotannon tason. Maailmantalouden kasvudynamiikan muutos on ilmeisen pysyv. Kasvu painottuu enenevsti nouseviin, erityisesti Aasian maiden talouksiin. Niiss yksityinen kulutus ja investoinnit ovat taantuman jlkeen lisntyneet tuntuvasti. Mielenkiintoista kehitystrendiss on se, ett Kiinan arvioidaan jo lhivuosien aikana nousevan takaisin maailman suurimmaksi taloudeksi (kuva 5). Tmn suurimman talousmahdin aseman se menetti niinkin vastikn kuin noin 150 vuotta sitten. Lhivuosina se saa ykksaseman takaisin. On arvioitu, ett maailmantaloudessa tullaan uuteen normaaliin, jossa nousevien talouksien asema on vahvistunut pysyvsti. Tt tukee mys julkisen talouden kehitys (kuva 6). Teollisuusmaissa julkinen talous on enenevsti velkaantunut. Kymmenen vuotta sitten lnsimaiden julkinen velka oli noin 65 prosenttia kokonaistuotannosta ja nyt se on noussut jo lhelle 100 prosenttia. Kokonaan toinen kehitys on tapahtunut nousevissa talouksissa. Niiss velan mr on alentunut ja odotetaan edelleen alenevan suhteessa niiden BKT:hen. Tarkasteltaessa maailmantalouden velkaantuneisuutta ja eri maiden kehityst, ei tule rajoittua vain julkisen sektorin velkaan (kuva 7). Kansainvlisen valuuttarahaston tiedot kertovat, ett finanssikriisin jljilt velkaongelmat eivt rajoitu vain tiettyihin velkakriisimaihin. Lisksi julkisen sektorin lisksi on tarkasteltava kotitalouksien, yritysten ja rahoituslaitosten tilaa. Velkaongelmat ovat laaja-alaisia ja koskettavat talouksien sisll eri tavoin eri sektoreita. Suomi prj hyvin tss vertailussa, sill yhdenkn sektorin velkaantuneisuus ei ole hlyttv. Rahalaitosten tilanne on varsin erilainen eri maissa (kuva 8). Pankkien ongelmat eivt nekn rajoitu vain tiettyihin maihin. Lisksi maiden sisll on suuria eroja liiketoimintaan sisltyviss riskeiss. Useissa maissa ovat monet pankit haavoittuvia valtioiden joukkovelkakirjasijoitusten, luottotappioriskien, varainhankinnan kustannusten, kannattavuuden tai vakavaraisuuden suhteen. Suomessa toimivat pankit ovat nill mittareilla hyvss kunnossa. Kuitenkin niidenkin kohdalla eurooppalaisten pankkien taseiden laatua koskeva epvarmuus ja pelko ongelmien levimisest voivat pahentaa tilannetta. Tst nkkulmasta on erittin trke Euroopassa meneilln oleva pankkien stressitestaus. Tuloksien perusteella tulee huolehtia pankkien pomittamisesta tai elinkelvottomien rahalaitosten uudelleenjrjestelyist tai alasajosta hallitulla tavalla. Euroon siirtyminen loi osittain harhan siit, ett rahaliittoon kuuluvat maat olisivat samanveroisia luottokelpoisuudeltaan (kuva 9). Velkakriisiss eri maiden luottokelpoisuus ja rahoituskustannukset ovat eriytyneet taas. Vaikka tm on kokonaisuutena edelleen kohtuullinen verrattuna moniin muihin talouksiin, on siell huolestuttavia piirteit. Monet kotitaloudet ovat voimakkaasti velkaantuneita (kuva 13). Talouskehityksen valopilkkuna Suomessa on viennin nopea kasvu (kuva 14). Viennin vedon ansiosta mys Suomen talous on elpymss. Kokonaistuotanto kasvoi viime vuonna noin 3,1 prosenttia sek jatkaa tn vuonna lhes 4 prosentin ja lhivuosina noin 2,5 prosentin vauhtia. Kasvunkymist huolimatta Suomen julkisen talouden tilaan liittyy haasteita. Valtion menot ovat selvsti tuloja suuremmat (kuva 15). Valtiovarainministerin loppuvuonna 2010 julkistaman raportin mukaan julkisen talouden kestvyysvaje on 5 % BKT:st. Tm tarkoittaa sit, ett julkisen talouden rahoitusasemaa pitisi kohentaa tmn verran vuoteen 2015 menness, jotta julkinen talous olisi kestvll pohjalla pitkll aikavlill. Julkisen talouden kestvyysongelma ei ratkea pelkstn tyurien pitenemisell tai julkisten palvelujen tuottavuuden paranemisella.
