Title: Where are our capital markets going?
text: Vice Chairman of the Board Pentti Hakkarainen: Where are our facebook markets going? Securities Breakfast of the Federation of Finnish Financial Services, Helsinki 13.10.2011 . Speech . Thursday13 October 2011, 2:00 PM Where is our local market going? Presentation figures (pdf) (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches/documents/phkalvosarja_13.10.2011.pdf) Dear listeners, thank you for the opportunity to share my thoughts on the situation in the local market, on the needs and opportunities for development. I am not going to comment on exchange rates or yields and not to repeat the ideas already put forward in the securities market development reports d as in the excellent 2009 and last Spring d reports. In the presentation, I will make suggestions and questions on the development of the local market, combining my experience with that of a company acquiring pssom, a bank providing money and mortgage market services, and now an authority that supervises and monitors the market in general. POUR OWN MARKET IS OF CONSIDERABLE IMPORTANCE The fundamental pillars of society and a growing economy are well-functioning financial markets, which, in addition to an efficient and solvent banking system, have a reliable payment business and a money and a financial market that efficiently allocates the euro. A well-sound banking system and a well-functioning local market and marketplace support the operating conditions for companies and the financial management of private individuals. This will improve the competitiveness of the economy. From the nsks angle of companies, they provide opportunities for the acquisition of both equity and foreign pssoma, i.e. debt financing. The local market allocates investment assets to profitable investments. It also serves as a measure of economic performance and growth expectations. The Finnish market is not small in relation to the size of the country. The size of our stock market relative to total economic output (GDP) is higher than in Japan and lshes on a par with Sweden and the United States. This is probably due to the fact that there are an exceptionally large number of large companies in Finland, which are: leading in their fields - even internationally considered d and are listed in the Helsinki psrss. Institutional investors, such as institutions, are also large in international comparisons. (Figure 1) PTO DEVELOP YOUR OWN MARKET... S PRIMARY MARKET The local market as a whole is often discussed. However, when they are developed, attention has been paid to the fact that the market consists of both the primary market and the secondary market. The primary market is to acquire and allocate pssom to investment targets. The market is from the nsks angle of the issuers of securities to the skkest. Development efforts will be directed towards things that can facilitate and encourage entry into the public marketplace. On the secondary market, securities are traded. They are tsrkest especially from the investor's nskskulma. The development measures relate to increasing trade in the region, for example by reducing the cost of trade, improving investor information and investor protection. The development of the local market should not be focused solely on encouraging equity or investment activities, i.e. focusing on the secondary market. It is also necessary to examine the development needs of the primary market. Both of them work together, strengthening each other in the best-case scenario, but at worst they weaken each other if there are weaknesses in the actions of one of them. There is always a need for development, as the market is a place in a changing social and economic climate. Changes are taking place, in particular as a result of internationalisation, market integration and competition in marketplaces. The known tightening of sclerosis in the banking and insurance sectors is likely to change the average affordability of financing. It is obvious that the importance of market-based financing and efficient marketplaces is emphasised in business financing. ENSURING A COMPETITIVE MARKETPLACE The trends in the stock market are bad, but the situation in our securities markets is not at all unhappy. There are no reasons to ring death knells, even though there are threats of decline in development. Competition from trading venues for the most traded shares has intensified significantly. In addition to the cost of trade, there is competition for the speed of trade. The trading volume of the most liquid shares in the Helsinki Psrss has gradually shifted to multilateral trading venues (MTF) outside the market. The stock market's bottom line in recent years has also contributed to the helsinki psrss euromsrsistan exchange, which has dropped to half of the years before the financial crisis. (Figure 2) However, the structure of the share exchange has changed in such a way that, although the value-measured exchange has decreased, the volumes have even risen in terms of volumes. In view of the good level of trade compared to previous decades, there is no point in lamenting the current situation. (Figure 3) Helsinki's pocket list is slowly getting shorter, and the mssrs of the money fetched from the primary market is vshsinen. In relation to the ssss, the omens of the future of the psrss are bad. (Figures 4 and 5) In recent years, IPOs in helsinki have dried up completely. Corporate bonds are also pre-agreed and invested in debt securitiesoprivate, not investments for the general public, which would be the subject of a wider deal. Government loans are also sold mostly on the international market. Institutional investors, such as investment funds or financial institutions, have diversified their investments globally and the debt financing of Finnish companies is acquired in addition to the international financing of the company. Domestic small investors are active, but their demand alone is not enough to keep up with the market. There are threats in the development process and measures are taking the Finnish marketplace to wither away. From the point of view of economic growth and otherwise developing society, the marketplace will become vibrant and competitive. Since the size of the national economy or our location does not provide a natural basis for growth, special care must be taken to ensure the operating conditions of the marketplace. This development can be based on the competitive advantages that the marketplace has. We have such competitive advantages. In many industries, Finland has leading companies and special expertise, even from an international point of view. Knowledge of these industries and good analysis will bring an advantage to our local market that we will be able to increase. The quality of the analyst profession is a market place for Helsinki's success, as well as a competitive infrastructure. It is crucial for the future of the Finnish equity and debt market that companies and the public sector act as issuers of securities domestically. Securities can be offered on the international market, but also to domestic investors and sssstsj. A marketplace, be it a marketplace or a marketplace or method of trading promissory notes, must be adequately marketed. It is the case that companies larger than international interest can be kept on the domestic marketplace. Tsms is tsrkess not only in terms of the exchange and income of the Helsinki marketplace, but also because of its reputation and attractiveness. KOTIINPINVETOA? If the current trend continues, there is a risk that the trade will move more away from Finland. If the marketplace is abroad, even if only in another Nordic country, it becomes more difficult for all companies - and especially small and medium-sized enterprises - to acquire their own and foreign premises. As financing conditions tighten and market problems arise, investors' interest in the periphery will decline. With the exception of large first-class companies, Finnish companies are not well known on the international market, if at all. I would therefore like to highlight the emphasis on domesticity, i.e. the home bias factor, related to investment activities. Should larger institutions invest more heavily in domestic investment? As I mentioned earlier, in exceptional circumstances, access to foreign financing may become more difficult and even completely blocked, as happened three years ago. At that time, it became clear that domestic markets and investors were needed despite the internationalisation of financial markets. It's easier to be able to do that analyze the profitability and creditworthiness of enterprises. This makes it easier to obtain and discuss information. There are a large number of institutional investors in Finland, although very few are really big for the size of our economy. Tyselskeyhtist, KEVA and the State Elskerahasto all represent a high level of professionalism and competence in their investment activities. They are not only investors, but lend to companies in various forms. In recent years, the number of companies and institutions has increased the domestic focus on their investments. Likewise, they have been active in the commercial paper market. In addition, they have been involved in the development of the local market. The question is often raised as to whether employment institutions could continue to increase their participation in domestic investments. There is no unequivocal answer. In investment activities, diversification is used to reduce risky returns. Mechanically, neither domesticity nor overweight should be implemented. The emphasis on only one market can increase the risk, and it is not always optimal to invest in a return-risk analysis, even if the market is well known. It is obvious that the greater emphasis on Finland among the tyselske plants, KEVA and VER today would also be from the nsks angle of the pssoma market. But is there any justification or obstacle to their self-interest in increasing domestic investment? Earlier, I mentioned the competitive advantage of knowing investment targets and markets. In addition, their business d and the sustainability of the entire system d is based on the fee income received from Finnish companies and other employers. Even if the return and risk of the investment in Finland and some other country are not the same, even if the return and risk of the investment in question are the same. Domestic bias would contribute to securing funding opportunities for the economy, increasing economic growth, improving employment and, ultimately, strengthening premiums written. The introduction of such an aggregate amount as one of the criteria that guide investment activity can provide a good basis for channelling funds to the domestic market. As far as taxation is concerned, I do not intend to discuss it more than by stating that taxes relating to investment or trade must not differ from other countries. With more severe taxation, the trade will move elsewhere and the marketplace Helsinki will become more attractive. Foreign operators account for about three quarters of a stake in the exchange. Trade is easily and quickly transferred elsewhere if the activities are taxed more heavily than others. PRIORITY MARKET FOR SME BONDS The Helsinki Psrssi has been looking for ways to facilitate the listing of new companies. They have not yet taken fire. The local market for growth companies will continue to receive attention to enable psssy. This is an excellent opportunity for broad cooperation in order to develop the domestic market. There are good reports on the development of the securities markets, such as those published by the Psrssisstis in recent years. They have analysed the obstacles and potential incentives associated with the IPO. I look forward and confidently to the proposals recently set up by Minister Hsksmies. It is hoped that, in addition to the stock market, proposals will emerge, for example, to expand the options for acquiring corporate finance. Companies need a market where, regardless of size, they can obtain foreign financing on a larger scale than is currently the case. One possibility would be a debt market for small and medium-sized enterprises, similar to the deutsche bsrsen yllspitsmsn bond market. In Germany, a trading platform for SME bonds was set up last winter and operates as a trading platform. In Germany, the minimum issue size is EUR 30 million. Lower limit for emissions could be smaller. In the SME bond market, the disclosure obligations are more limited than in the case of prance-listed bonds, similar to those in the alternative stock market. In Germany, the issues are handled by listing partners and the nsms are also operated by the marketing authorities. Banks or brokerage firms could act as market makers in the same way as the stock market. The trading platform operates under the supervision of the German supervisory authority BaFin and, through it, receives additional reliability. TIGHTENING SNTELY CREATES AN OPPORTUNITY The tightening of banking and insurance companies highlights the need for a well-functioning banking market in the financial services of both banks and companies. The new measures are likely to change the behaviour of both lenders and borrowers, as well as the functioning of the domestic market. The tightening of the solvency limits of banks and insurance companies is expected to bring with it a longer period of time. The financial markets and the crisis in the financial sector are becoming less frequent and their damage is lower. The cost of the reform is an increase in the price of financing provided by MFIs and insurance companies and possibly also a decline in the availability of long-term credit, at least compared to the situation prevailing on the global financial markets before the current financial crisis in 2008. As a result of Basel III, bank credit margins will rise unless banks lower their return targets for invested cash (ROE). In connection with the insurance company's future ssting (solvency II), the use of risk weights in loans and investments is also likely to increase the margins of corporate bonds compared to the past. All in all, the traditional balance sheet of a bank or insurance company loan is becoming more expensive. As a result, there is a growing need to raise a larger share of financing on the current financial and domestic markets. DETERIORATION OF FINANCIAL CONDITIONS Syndicated loan markets and bond markets serve as funding channels for investments by companies operating in international markets. Under normal circumstances, the market operates well from the issuers' corner, but in crisis situations, the market closes quickly. Over the past year, Finnish companies have prepared themselves quite well for the weakening availability of international financing. They have entered into new syndicated credit agreements in the year, amounting to 11 billion. the value of the euro and the amount of contractual limits will rise by about 35 billion. Eur. In Finland, the limits for similar contracts are just under 5 billion. Eur. Companies also used the international bond market quite a lot during the first half of the year. Domestic commercial paper markets function quite well, but the corporate bond market is narrower and issuances are rare. Indeed, the amount of corporate bonds is smaller than that of commercial paper in circulation. In particular, the long-term domestic bond market for companies should be given a boost. (Figure 6) I will come back to the question of home bias. Is there one reason why Sweden has a wider domestic bond market because the restrictive mssrsys of open currency positions in the insurance sector have discouraged investment in foreign assets? The diversification of investment in the insurance sector outside the home country was rapidly accelerated after the introduction of the euro as the currency risk was eliminated. Or is it the case that in Sweden, the importance and notoriety of investment choices have weighed more heavily than in Finland? There are more reasons for this, rather than making quick management decisions. LAINSDNT... IMPACT OF PROJECTS The reform of the Securities Markets Act and related acts has progressed and efforts have been made to take into account the competitiveness of the Finnish securities market as market structures change and the harmonisation of supervision and supervision. Efforts by the various market participants are also needed, for example, to develop multi-tiered management of securities. Nsms so-called. issues relating to nominee registration should be resolved in such a way as to safeguard the competitiveness of our securities markets and the access of the various authorities. Nsin has been made elsewhere as well, and examples of workable solutions are lacking. When entering the nominee register, care must also be taken to ensure that issuers and companies have access to information. Their investor relations activities and disclosure obligations to investors are subject to a good system for identifying and knowing their shareholders. The development of the national market and the infrastructure that is an integral part of its operation is expanding not only in Finland, but also in the EU, where a number of projects are under way, such as amendments to the Directive on the markets for financial instruments (MiFID Review), the Central Counterparties and Over-the-Counter (OTC) Derivatives Directive (EMIR) and the Central Securities Depository (LCSD). KAUPANKYNNIN JLKEINEN ARVOPAPERIPROSESSI Central securities depositories (CSDs) and CCPs are systemically significant infrastructure actors. In this context, the question arises, how is the business of these operators concentrated in Europe and what is the position of Finnish operators? From the nsks corner of Finnish banks, companies or investors, it is unlikely that infrastructure services are or what their opening hours are. The integration of the infrastructure into the wider European context is to be welcomed from the point of view of operational efficiency. The final stages of the systems, such as issuers and investors, must be guaranteed the activities and services of the local market. In addition to efficiency, services must also be of the same quality, availability and price as elsewhere. The worst outcome of infrastructure integration would be a deterioration in the operating conditions and a loss of influence on one's own markets. The common objective of developing the infrastructure of the European markets is to create a single securities market that will lead to economies of scale and increased competition. As part of this goal, the Target2-Securities project (T2S) is part of this goal. Target 2 Securities creates opportunities for the Finnish market, but also challenges. T2S also has the opportunity to ssilys as part of the European securities market and to offer a pan-European market to investors and issuers. T2S can increase costs in a short period of time, but hysdys can be obtained over a longer period of time. Combining thirty separate settlements into a single system brings the entire market from nskskulma sssstsjs, although not all of them are affected by the change. Kevin Milne, head of Post Trade at the London Presidency, criticised the September SIBOS at the T2S meeting, there were negative discussions and pointed out that similar discussions were taking place when the British central securities depository Crest prepared its own system for the success of the Taurus d project. In spite of the epsilyism presented on the market, the crest system was very successful. FINALLY To sum up, Finnish and especially growth-oriented companies need a functioning and reliable financial and financial market in their home countries for their operations. It is not only tax-related means that are being developed. When looking for them, it is necessary to take into account both the primary and secondary markets. Encouraging and increasing domestic ownership would be one of the ways in which the possible use should be considered. In the case of institutional investors, this is done in the right way, taking into account the totality of the business; all the risks, costs and hustle and bustle. Now is an opportunity that should not be missed. H (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tagHakkarainen)

Title: Risks of central banking during the financial crisis
text: Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen: Risks of central banking operations during the nanny crisis . Speech . Tuesday 1 November 2011,11:00AM STUDIA MONETARIA LECTURE 1.11.2011, BANK OF FINLAND MONETARY MUSEUM Presentation Pictures (pdf) (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches/documents/ph_studiamonetaria_1.11.2011.pdf) The central bank has a risk In central banking, there is always a risk. It is not possible to fully quantify and any losses. The central bank sometimes faces greater damage in order to carry out operations that can also result in financial losses. Nsin has happened in history and will continue to happen in the future. Recent news may have included losses of more than FF 20 billion last year by the Swiss National Bank or a loss made by the Bank of Japan in transactions in listed fund units (ETFs). A more recent example is from finland, where the Bank of Finland had to bear losses in the 1980s and 1990s. The Central Bank acts a bit like a fire brigade. When it is calm, nskyvs action is not necessary. But even in a quiet time, you need to be prepared for real action. The fire brigade cannot only take care of itself. Fires sometimes have several fires and choices have to be made, try to prevent the fire from spreading and limit the damage to bystanders themselves and their equipment. Stages of the economic crisis (Figures 2, 3 and 4) Economic distress often comes from above and beyond. However, studies show that there are clear stages in the progression of the crisis. In general, rapid indebtedness and a sharp rise in the prices of assets, often fixed assets, foreshadow the economy. The price bubble bursts and banks incur credit losses, the effects on the real economy and the recession begins. The recession, with its credit losses, weakens the position of banks. Losses affect the solvency of MFIs and their lending capacity deteriorates. At the same time, the state's tax revenues and expenditures are rising, leading to a predicament of public finances. A vicious circle is in danger of being created if the plight of public finances continues to weaken the banks and if a vicious circle of favourable development of the real economy is formed. It is important that the weakening of the financial system is stopped so that the economy as a whole does not fall into a credit crunch and the conditions for economic growth are met. The financial crisis hit Europe from the United States just over four years ago in August 2007. In the short-term loan market, the banks' activities were dominated. The situation was triggered by the ability of a few funds to buy complex financial products and pay the investor who redeems their shares. The signs of a sovereign debt crisis began in the euro area in 2008 when interest rates on long-term government bonds diverged. Since then, the spreads on bond yields issued by different countries have only widened. sms describes the crisis as now getting worse. Despite a number of measures to strengthen the functioning of the financial markets, such as the liquidity system of central banks, the situation on the money markets is worrying. The financial system is threatening to reorganise the banks' interbank market. The gap between secured and unsecured short-term interest rates has widened. Although interest rate differentials are not at the level of Lehman's bankruptcy, they reflect the vulnerability of the financial markets. Central Bank monetary policy function(Figure 5) The main task of central banks is to ensure price stability. Ensuring that the value of money is preserved creates the conditions for economic operators to operate efficiently. Tssss is the policy rate tsrkes vsline. Central banks, such as the European Central Bank, react with their key interest rates to changes in the economy, ensuring price stability and, through this, creating the conditions for economic growth. Even during the financial crisis, the value of money is taken care of. In addition, central banks, as banks, provide financing to financial institutions through both normal and customary transactions. The allocation of liquidity ensures the liquidity of banks and the convergence of monetary policy. Regular monetary policy measures (Figure 6) During the financial crisis, central banks were faced with specific measures in addition to the fact that normal measures d such as a rapid reduction in the policy rate d helped to alleviate market interference. Nsin happened in all the economies of the world. In addition, as of August 2007, the eurojs system responded to the financial markets with regular measures. In its usual role as a bank for banks, the Central Bank provides short-term financing to solvent banks in exchange for collateral. During the financial crisis, monetary policy measures had to be adjusted to take account of deteriorating market conditions. The Eurojs system ensured the liquidity of banks through the so-called fixed interest rate and distribution auctions. Banks receive financing from the Central Bank in the amount they want. In addition, the normal one-week funding period was extended. The longer-term refinancing operations provided one-, three- and six-month and one-year financing. The usual operations also include the fact that the pool of assets eligible as collateral for refinancing operations was extended over time. The lowest credit rating of a bond in accordance with the standing sssnnss was downgraded from A to BBBd. Other common measures include covered bond purchase programmes in 2009 and 2011 and the securities market programme launched a year ago. Securities were bought and made on the secondary market. The aim of these measures is to address market failures and to ensure that monetary policy is resolved. I will come back to this presentation in a more recent way. Increased central bank balance sheets (Figures 7, 8, 9 and 10) There has been public talk of central banks pumping money into the market. The review has referred to the growth of central bank balance sheets. Central bank balance sheets have increased during the financial crisis. However, there are differences in growth, both in terms of size and size. The balance sheets of the Fed in the United States and the Bank of England in the United States have clearly grown more than those of the euro system. The Fed's balance sheet has tripled during the financial crisis. However, this is not an isolated measure, but a number of ordinary measures taken in response to the crisis. In addition to ensuring the liquidity of MFIs, the Fed has participated directly in the local market, increasing the size of the money and ensuring the functioning of the market. The most significant measures and programmes have been the purchase of commercial paper, the refinancing operations of central banks in the so-called "green paper". swaps, the local financing programme, the purchase of fixed-backed bonds and the purchase of federal debt securities. Some of the actions have already been set up immediately for a specific period of time, others for an indefinite period, and each of them has its own objectives. With its own covered bond purchase and securities market programmes, the EurojS system has operated in a much more limited way than the Us Federal Reserve. Together, the two programmes have raised some 220 billion worth of bonds and the impact of the purchases in relation to the size of the balance sheet is smaller than the correspondingly fed's actions have been. Another key difference is that the euro system has neutralised the impact of purchases of money through finesse operations. Eurojs system bond purchases play a role in the growth of the euro system's balance sheet, but it is nevertheless marginal. A large part of the increase in the balance sheet has been due to non-standard refinancing operations; the balance sheet has increased as the setelists has increased and the price of gold has risen. Inflation as a threat? (figure 11) The growth of central bank balance sheets and central bank money has no mechanical link with inflation. This is the case with recent developments in the balance sheet and the persistently low medium-term inflation expectations. One explanation is that only a small part of the increase in the balance sheet has been offset by changes in the amount of central bank money held by banks. Some of the usual measures have led to an increase in central bank money. The liquidity of the banks has been ensured. They have held a surplus of liquidity. In the absence of broad-money growth or credit, inflationary pressures have remained subdued. Allocation of responsibilities in the EurojS system (Figure 12) The proceeds and potential losses arising from the implementation of the monetary policy of the Eurojs system are distributed according to the key to the entire system. With a single monetary policy and currency in economic and monetary union, the central banks of the eurosystems operate uniformly in monetary policy matters in all euro area countries. This will ensure that monetary policy has the same and equal impact throughout the euro area. As a result of this, the national central banks which implement monetary policy within the framework of the euro system have equal rights to the revenues of the single monetary policy and, accordingly, an obligation to bear the risks. The Bank of Finland bears the risk (Figures 13, 14, 15 and 16) The Bank of Finland has its own balance sheet and its own result. According to the law, the bank operates under the guarantee and care of parliament. However, the bank itself bears the responsibility for the risks of central banking operations. Its activities do not depend on the state budget, but the bank receives the proceeds from its own activities and uses the proceeds to cover its expenses. In addition, it makes provision for its profits to cover potential losses. The Bank of Finland faces risks due to the implementation of monetary policy and the investment of financial assets. The types of risk include credit, interest rate and currency risk. All cases are managed in modern ways and in accordance with generally good risk management principles. The balance of the bank's performance is setelists and the bank's banking activities and investment activities. For example, of the total revenues of 565 million euros in 2010, about 200 million came from setelistss and other central banking activities. Additional interest income from investment activities amounted to approximately EUR 255 million. Operating expenses were paid out of the proceeds and, after the provisions made, EUR 195 million of the 283 million result was paid to the state. The Bank of Finland's results could also be referred to as the Bank of Finland, as the bank does not operate to make a profit. The result varies a lot from year to year. A key factor influencing the result is the general level of interest rates. As the risks associated with the operations may be realised, it is necessary to accumulate provisions and strengthen the balance sheet in order to ensure that the bank can withstand losses in worse times. Similarly, losses from bad years may have to be digested for a long period of time. This is well illustrated by the fact that the losses made in the 1980s and 1990s led to the fact that, after 1984, it was not until 2000 that the Bank produced a result from which part could be recognised as revenue to the State. In accordance with the law, half of the annual profit is transferred to the state and half to the bank's reserve fund for future years. The Board of Governors may decide otherwise if the financial situation of the Bank or the size of the reserve fund so justifies it. Over the past five years, the Bank has transferred two-thirds of its profits to the state, totalling some 1.1 billion. Part of the balance sheet depends on the activities of third parties (Figures 16 and 17) The Central Bank cannot influence all the items on its balance sheet. This includes, in particular, the bank's deposits with the central bank. The euro is one of the three main world currencies. This is probably a key reason why the demand for the euro-set list has clearly exceeded expectations. The value of euro banknotes in circulation exceeds 800 billion. All NCBs receive a share of the total banknote in their balance sheets according to the key and a share of the banknote earnings in their earnings, respectively. The amount of euros issued by the Bank of Finland is about 11 billion. Since the bank receives the pssoma key's share of the total euro-set-list d now lshes 14 billion d and this is clearly higher than what was in the markka period. Depending on the assumptions, the future euro-settle will amount to approximately EUR 425 million or even EUR 985 million. The TARGET account changes the size of the balance sheet(Figure 18) The TARGET account is a joint payment system account of the central banks of the EU. It is used to pay for all monetary policy operations and to make large-scale bank transactions. As a result, very large sums of money are circulating in the accounts. The TARGET account rocks the Bank of Finland's balance sheet quite a bit, while the balances of the account can fluctuate by several tens of billions. When banks operating in Finland make or additional deposits with the central bank, this is a change in the balance sheet. At the end of September, the balance sheet totalled EUR 72 billion, compared with EUR 40 billion at the end of the month. The background to this is that banks are increasing their deposits from 8 billion to 46 billion at the end of September. Government reserve holdings reduced by 7 billion In total, net deposits amounted to EUR 31 billion as an increase in the balance sheet. The reason for banks' good payment status and large deposits with central banks is that they themselves receive deposits from other banks and companies. Through the receipt of deposits and, accordingly, through the TARGET account, the Bank of Finland does not take any risk. If deposits increase, the bank of Finland's receivable from the European Central Bank will increase accordingly. Shared and own risks in operations(Figures 19 and 20) The main risks on the Bank of Finland's balance sheet are related to the implementation of monetary policy on the one hand and the management of its own financial assets on the other. The first ones are carried according to the pssoma key as part of the euro system. As such, and entirely at the bank's own risk, the Member States. All risks are assessed and taken into account against the risk buffers on the balance sheet. Monetary policy refinancing operations are the normal form of central bank financing. This is what banks receive in liquidity auctions and must be secured by a valid security. Guarantees are valued psivitchin. Bonds are purchased on the secondary market at market prices. Covered promissory notes have collateral. Bonds purchased under the Securities Markets Programme will only be held until maturity and their valuation will be subject to a change in valuation if the change in value is final. Financial assets amount to EUR 17 billion, of which gold accounts for EUR 1.9 billion and foreign reserve assets for EUR 4.5 billion. The rest is euromsssish wealth. The biggest risk in the Bank of Finland's financial assets is currency risk. In addition, investments involve interest rate risk. The risk of both, assessed by well-established, commonly used risk models (VaRs), has been kept at the same level during the crisis. The large rise in the price of gold has led to an increase in its var value as a measure of risk, and thus increased the overall risk. It should be noted, however, that against the price risk of gold, unrealised profit has been generated in the revaluation account of the balance sheet. The price of gold could fall by about 80 percent before it would cause an expense entry in the bank's income statement. As a result, it is justified to consider gold and its price risk separately from other risks. Financial assets are also associated with credit risk. However, it has been kept low by investing well in low-credit-risk assets. More than 97 percent of investments are classified in category A or better. All d own and shared d risks are managed (Figures 21, 22) Risk management includes all identified risks, both in the euro system and in one's own actions. These are managed by means of limits, decentralisation, hedging and sizing in such a way that the bank's balance sheet can meet. In order to provide sufficient certainty, stress and scenario analysis must be carried out with assumptions that are possible even if they are not verifiable. The risks are managed by species and even by financial means, so that the individual outcome is not excluded from control and ignored. Risks are combined into an overall risk, which is examined in the risk buffers on the balance sheet. When the risks are assessed using generally used methods (VaR and Expected Shortfall), the Bank of Finland's total risk is limited to the provisions on its balance sheet and other own resources. The provisions that can be cancelled and the revaluation account are sufficient to cover the identified risks. The risks arising from the monetary policy measures of the euro system are a fraction of the risks otherwise associated with one's own activities. The market risk, which consists of the foreign exchange, interest rate and credit risks of the financial assets, is related to the Bank's own operations and the largest part of the overall risk. Summary (Figure 23) There can be no risk, no losses, in the operation of the central bank. The risk buffers in the balance sheet have to be used to prepare for the favourable realisations of bad times. When you accumulate well over the years, you will end up with the balance sheet and will also allow you to implement the state's justified claim for recognition of revenue. At the same time, the operational capacity of the Central Bank is ensured in all circumstances. When it comes to resolving the financial crisis, the division is clear. The central bank can play its part through monetary policy, as well as through its usual and ordinary transactions. These measures will only be effective if the rest of the economic policy is at a sustainable footing. That is why it is the case that governments succeed in balancing public finances in solving the economic problems of the world and europe. H (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tagHakkarainen)

Tuesday 1 November 2011,11:00AM STUDIA MONETARIA -LUENTO 1.11.2011, SUOMEN PANKIN RAHAMUSEO Esityksen kuvat (pdf) (/globalassets/fi/media-ja-julkaisut/puheet/documents/ph_studiamonetaria_1.11.2011.pdf) Keskuspankilla riskej Keskuspankkitoiminnassa on aina riskej. Nit ja mahdollisia tappioitakaan ei voida kokonaan vltt. Keskuspankki joutuu joskus suuremman vahingon vlttmiseksi tekemn toimia, joista voi tulla mys taloudellisia tappioita. Nin on tapahtunut historiassa ja tulee tapahtumaan jatkossakin. Viimeaikaisista uutisista on voitu lukea Sveitsin keskuspankin viime vuoden yli 20 miljardin frangin tappioista tai Japanin keskuspankin tekem tappio prssiss noteerattujen rahasto-osuuksien (ETF) kaupoissa. Lheisempi esimerkki meill on kotimaasta, jossa Suomen Pankki joutui kantamaan tappioita 1980-ja 1990 -luvuilla. Keskuspankki toimii hiukan kuin palokunta. Kun on rauhallista, nkyv toiminta ei ole tarpeen. Mutta rauhallisenakin aikana on varauduttava tositoimiin. Sammutus-ja pelastustiss palokunta ei voi pit huolta vain itsestn. Tulipaloissa on joskus useita palopeskkeit ja valintoja on tehtv, yritten est palon leviminen ja rajoittaa sivullisille aiheutuvia vahinkoja itsen ja kalustoaan sstmtt. Talouskriisin vaiheita (kuvat 2, 3 ja 4) Talousahdinko tulee usein ylltten. Tutkimusten mukaan kriisin etenemisess on kuitenkin selkeit vaiheita. Yleens nopea velkaantuminen ja varallisuuserien, usein kiinteistjen, hintojen voimakas nousu ennakoivat talouden hiriit. Hintakupla puhkeaa ja pankeille aiheutuu luottotappioita, vaikutukset nkyvt reaalitaloudessa ja taantuma alkaa. Taantuma luottotappioineen heikent pankkien asemaa. Tappiot syvt rahalaitosten vakavaraisuutta ja niiden luotonantokyky heikkenee. Samaan aikaan valtion verotulot vhenevt ja menot kasvavat johtaen julkisen talouden ahdinkoon. Paha noidankeh on vaarassa synty, jos julkisen talouden ahdinko heikent edelleen pankkeja ja tst muodostuu voimistuva kierre reaalitalouden epsuotuisaan kehitykseen. On trke, ett rahoitusjrjestelmn heikentyminen saadaan pysytetty, jottei koko talous ajaudu luottolamaan ja talouskasvun edellytykset hvivt. Finanssikriisi kantautui Yhdysvalloista Eurooppaan jo reilut nelj vuotta sitten elokuussa 2007. Pankkien vlisell lyhytaikaisella lainamarkkinalla toiminta jtyi ylltten. Tilanteen laukaisi muutamien rahastojen kyvyttmyys mritt monimutkaisia finanssituotteita sisltvien salkkujensa arvoa ja maksaa osuutensa lunastavalle sijoittajalle. Valtioiden velkakriisin merkit alkoivat nky euroalueella 2008 kun pitkaikaisten valtioiden joukkovelkakirjojen korot eriytyivt toisistaan. Eri maiden liikkeeseen laskemien joukkolainojen tuottoerot ovat sen jlkeen vain voimistuneet. Tm kuvaa kriisin nyt pahenevan. Huolimatta useista rahoitusmarkkinoiden toimintaa vahvistavista toimista, kuten keskuspankkien likviditeettijrjestelyist, tilanne nytt huolestuttavalta rahamarkkinoilla. Rahoitusjrjestelmn hirit uhkaavat krjisty uudelleen pankkien vlisill interbank -markkinoilla. Vakuudellisten ja vakuudettomien lyhytaikaisten korkojen ero on kasvanut. Vaikka korkoerot eivt ole Lehmanin konkurssin ajan tasolla, ne kuvaavat rahoitusmarkkinoiden olevan haavoittuvassa tilassa. Keskuspankin rahapolitiikan tehtvt(kuva 5) Keskuspankkien keskeisin tehtv on huolehtia hintavakaudesta. Varmistamalla rahan arvon silyminen luodaan talouden toimijoille edellytykset tehokkaaseen toimintaan. Tss on ohjauskorko trke vline. Keskuspankit, kuten Euroopan keskuspankki, reagoivat ohjauskorollaan talouden muutoksiin varmistaen hintavakauden ja tt kautta luoden edellytykset talouskasvulle. Finanssikriisin aikanakin huolehditaan rahan arvon silymisest. Lisksi keskuspankit pankkien pankkina antavat sek tavanomaisin ett eptavanomaisin toimin rahoitusta rahalaitoksille. Likviditeetin jaolla varmistetaan pankkien maksuvalmius ja rahapolitiikan vlittyminen. Eptavanomaisia rahapolitiikan toimia (kuva 6) Keskuspankit joutuivat finanssikriisiss erityisiin toimiin sen lisksi, ett tavanomaisilla toimilla  kuten ohjauskoron nopealla laskemisella  osaltaan kyettiin helpottamaan markkinahiriit. Nin tapahtui kaikissa maailman talouksissa. Mys eurojrjestelm vastasi rahoitusmarkkinoiden hiriihin heti elokuusta 2007 lhtien eptavanomaisilla toimilla. Tavanomaisessa tehtvssn pankkien pankkina keskuspankki antaa lyhytaikaista rahoitusta vakavaraisille pankeille vakuuksia vastaan. Finanssikriisiss rahapoliittisia toimia jouduttiin mukauttamaan huonontuneet markkinaolot huomioivaksi. Eurojrjestelm varmisti pankkien maksuvalmiutta eptavanomaisin toimin niin sanotuilla kiinten koron ja tyden jaon huutokaupoilla. Niss pankit saavat keskuspankista rahoitusta haluamansa mrn. Lisksi tavanomaisen viikon pituisen rahoituksen juoksuaikaa pidennettiin. Ylimrisill pidempiaikaisilla rahoitusoperaatioilla annettiin yhden, kolmen ja kuuden kuukauden sek vuoden rahoitusta. Eptavanomaisiin toimiin liittyy mys se, ett rahoitusoperaatioiden vakuudeksi kelpaavien omaisuuserien joukkoa laajennettiin vliaikaisesti. Pysyvn snnksen mukainen alin hyvksyttv joukkolainan luottokelpoisuusluokitus laskettiin A:sta BBB:een. Eptavanomaisia toimia ovat mys katettujen joukkovelkakirjojen osto-ohjelmat (covered bond purchase program) vuosina 2009 ja 2011 sek vuosi sitten kevll aloitettu arvopaperimarkkinaohjelma (securities market program). Arvopaperiostot tehtiin ja tehdn jlkimarkkinoilla. Toimien tavoitteena on puuttua markkinoiden toimintahiriihin ja varmistaa rahapolitiikan vlittyminen. Palaan nihin esitelmssni viel myhemmin. Kasvaneetkeskuspankkien taseet (kuvat 7, 8, 9 ja 10) Julkisuudessa on puhuttu keskuspankkien pumppaavan rahaa markkinoille. Tarkastelussa on viitattu keskuspankkien taseiden kasvuun. Keskuspankkien taseet ovatkin finanssikriisin aikana kasvaneet. Kasvuissa on kuitenkin eroja sek koon ett sislln suhteen. Yhdysvaltojen Fedin ja Britannian Bank of Englandin taseet ovat kasvaneet selvsti enemmn kuin eurojrjestelmn tase. Yhdysvaltojen keskuspankin Fedin tase on lhes kolminkertaistunut finanssikriisin aikana. Kuitenkaan kyse ei ole yksittisest toimesta vaan monista kriisin johdosta tehdyst eptavanomaisista toimista. Rahalaitosten maksuvalmiuden varmistamisen lisksi Fed on osallistunut suoraan pomamarkkinoille listen rahan mr ja varmistaen markkinoiden toimivuutta. Merkittvimpi toimia ja ohjelmia ovat olleet yritystodistusten osto, keskuspankkien vliset rahoitusoperaatiot ns. swapit, mraikaisen rahoituksen ohjelma, kiinteistvakuudellisten joukkolainojen ostot ja liittovaltion velkapaperien osto. Osa toimista on jo heti ptetty tietyksi mrajaksi, osa toistaiseksi voimassaoleviksi ja nill toimilla on kullakin omat tavoitteet. Eurojrjestelm on omilla katettujen joukkolainojen osto-ja arvopaperimarkkinaohjelmillaan toiminut huomattavasti rajoitetummin kuin Yhdysvaltojen keskuspankki. Yhteens kahdella ohjelmalla on hankittu noin 220 miljardin euron arvosta joukkolainoja ja ostojen vaikutus taseen kokoon suhteutettuna on pienempi kuin vastaavasti Fedin toimet ovat olleet. Toinen keskeinen ero on, ett eurojrjestelm on neutraloinut ostojen rahanmr lisvn vaikutuksen hienostoperaatioilla. Eurojrjestelmn joukkolainaostoilla on oma roolinsa eurojrjestelmn taseen kasvussa, mutta tm on kuitenkin marginaalinen. Suuri osa taseen kasvusta on aiheutunut muista kuin eptavanomaisista rahoitusoperaatioista; tase on kasvanut, kun setelist on lisntynyt ja kullan hinta on noussut. Inflaatio uhkana? (kuva 11) Keskuspankkitaseiden ja keskuspankkirahan kasvulla ei ole mekaanista yhteytt inflaatioon. Tm ptee eurojrjestelmn taseen viimeaikaiseen kehitykseen ja matalalla pysyneisiin keskipitkn aikavlin inflaatio.odotuksiin. Yksi selitys on se, ett vain pieni osa taseen kasvusta on vlittynyt muutoksiin pankkien hallussa olevan keskuspankkirahan mrss. Osa eptavanomaisista toimenpiteist on johtanut keskuspankkirahan kasvuun. Tll on varmistettu pankkien maksuvalmius. Ne ovat pitneet hallussaan ylimrist likviditeetti. Kun tm ei ole johtanut kasvuun lavean rahan mrss tai luottojen mrss, ovat inflaatiopaineet pysyneet tst vaimeana. Eurojrjestelmn vastuut jaetaan (kuva 12) Eurojrjestelmn rahapolitiikan toteuttamisesta tulevat tuotot ja mahdolliset tappiot jaetaan koko jrjestelmss poma-avaimen mukaan. Kun talous-ja rahaliitossa on yhteinen rahapolitiikka ja raha, eurojrjestelmn keskuspankit toimivat tysin yhdenmukaisesti rahapolitiikan asioissa kaikissa euromaissa. Nin varmistetaan ett rahapolitiikka vaikuttaa samalla tavalla ja yhdenvertaisesti koko euroalueella. Tmn johdosta rahapolitiikkaa toteuttavilla eurojrjestelmn kuuluvilla kansallisilla keskuspankeilla on yhtliset oikeudet yhteisen rahapolitiikan tuloihin ja vastaavasti velvollisuus kantaa riskit. Suomen Pankki vastaa riskeistn (kuvat 13, 14, 15 ja 16) Suomen Pankilla on oma tase ja oma tulos. Lain mukaan pankki toimii eduskunnan takuulla ja hoidossa. Kuitenkin pankki itse kantaa vastuun keskuspankkitoiminnan riskeist. Sen toiminta ei riipu valtion budjetista vaan pankki saa tuottonsa omasta toiminnastaan ja kattaa tuotoilla kulunsa. Lisksi se tekee tuloksestaan varauksia, joilla mahdollisia tappioita voidaan kattaa. Suomen Pankilla on riskej johtuen rahapolitiikan toteuttamisesta ja rahoitusvarallisuuden sijoittamisesta. Riskityypit ovat luotto-, korko-ja valuuttariski. Kaikkia nit hallinnoidaan moderneilla ja yleisesti hyvien riskienhallintaperiaatteiden mukaisilla tavoilla ja vlineill. Pankin tuloksen plhteet ovat setelist ja pankkien pankkina toimiminen sek sijoitustoiminta. Esimerkiksi vuoden 2010 kokonaistuotoista, jotka olivat 565 miljoonaa euroa, noin 200 miljoonaa tuli setelistst ja muusta keskuspankkitoiminnasta. Sijoitustoiminnasta saatiin liskorkotuottoa noin 255 miljoonaa euroa. Tuotoista maksettiin toimintakulut ja tehtyjen varausten jlkeen jneest 283 miljoonan tuloksesta tilitettiin valtiolle 195 miljoonaa euroa. Suomen Pankin tuloksesta voisi kytt mys nimityst ylijm, sill pankki ei toimi voittoa tuottaakseen. Tulos vaihtelee vuosittain paljon. Keskeinen tulokseen vaikuttava tekij on yleinen korkotaso. Koska toimintaan liittyvt riskit saattavat realisoitua, on trke hyvin vuosina kerrytt varauksia ja vahvistaa tasetta, jotta pankki kest huonompien aikojen tappioita. Vastaavasti huonojen vuosien tappioita saatetaan joutua sulattelemaan pitknkin aikaa. Tt kuvaa hyvin se, ett 1980-ja 1990 -luvuilla tehdyt tappiot johtivat siihen, ett vuoden 1984 jlkeen vasta vuonna 2000 pankki tuotti tuloksen, josta voitiin tulouttaa osa valtiolle. Lain mukainen pperiaate on, ett vuosivoitosta puolet siirretn valtiolle ja puolet jtetn pankin vararahastoon tulevien vuosia varten. Tst psnnst pankkivaltuustolla on mahdollisuus ptt toisin, jos se pankin taloudellisen aseman tai vararahaston suuruuden vuoksi on perusteltua. Viimeisen viiden vuoden aikana pankki on siirtnyt valtiolle kaksi kolmasosaa tuloksestaan, yhteens noin 1,1 miljardia. Osa taseesta riippuu kolmansien toiminnasta(kuvat 16 ja 17) Keskuspankki ei voi vaikuttaa kaikkiin taseensa eriin. Nit ovat erityisesti setelistn mr sek pankkien talletukset keskuspankkiin. Euro on yksi maailman kolmesta keskeisest valuutasta. Tm lienee keskeinen syy sille, ett eurosetelistn kysynt on ylittnyt selvsti odotukset. Liikkeeseen laskettujen eurosetelien arvo ylitt 800 miljardia. Kaikki kansalliset keskuspankit saavat poma-avaimen mukaisen osuuden setelistn kokonaismrst taseeseensa ja vastaavasti osuuden setelitulosta tulokseensa. Suomen Pankin liikkeeseen laskemien eurojen mr on noin 11 miljardia. Koska pankki saa poma-avaimen mukaisen osuuden koko eurosetelistst  nyt lhes 14 miljardia  ja tm on selvsti suurempi kuin mit oli markka-ajan setelist. Eurosetelistst tuleva ylimrinen hyty on oletuksista riippuen vhintn noin 425 miljoonaa tai jopa 985 miljoonaa euroa. TARGET-tili muuttaa taseen kokoa(kuva 18) TARGET -tili on EU-alueen keskuspankkien yhteinen maksujrjestelmtili. Sen kautta maksetaan kaikki rahapolitiikan operaatiot sek tehdn suuria pankkien vlisi rahansiirtoja. Tmn vuoksi tileill liikkuu pivittin hyvin suuria summia. TARGET -tili heiluttaa Suomen Pankin tasetta melkoisesti, kun tilin pivsaldot voivat vaihdella useita kymmeni miljardeja. Kun Suomessa toimivat pankit vhentvt tai lisvt talletuksiaan keskuspankissa, tm nkyy muutoksena taseessa. Syyskuun lopussa taseen loppusumma oli lhes 72 miljardia euroa, kun se oli keskuun lopussa 40 miljardia. Taustalla on se, ett pankit lissivt tekemin y-ja mraikaistalletuksia 8 miljardista keskuun lopusta syyskuulle 46 miljardiin. Vhimmisvarantotalletukset pienenivt 7 mrd. Kaikkiaan nist talletuksista tuli nettona 31 miljardia taseen kasvuksi. Pankkien hyvn maksuaseman ja suurten keskuspankkitalletusten taustalla on, ett ne itse vastaanottavat talletuksia muilta pankeilta ja yrityksilt. Talletusten vastaanottamisen ja vastaavasti TARGET-tilin kautta Suomen Pankki ei ota riski. Jos talletukset kasvavat, Suomen Pankin saaminen Euroopan keskuspankilta kasvaa vastaavasti. Toiminnassa jaettuja ja omia riskej(kuvat 19 ja 20) Suomen Pankin taseen keskeisimmt riskit ovat toisaalta rahapolitiikan toteuttamiseen ja toisaalta oman rahoitusvarallisuuden hallintaan liittyvi. Ensimmiset kannetaan poma-avaimen mukaisesti osana eurojrjestelm. Jlkimmisist ovat sellaisenaan ja kokonaan pankin omalla vastuulla. Kaikki riskit arvioidaan ja huomioidaan taseen riskipuskureita vasten. Rahapolitiikan jlleenrahoitusoperaatiot ovat tavanomaista pankkien keskuspankkirahoitusta. Tmn pankit saavat likviditeettihuutokaupoissa ja niiden vakuudeksi on toimitettava hyvksyttv tysi vakuus. Vakuudet arvostetaan pivittin. Joukkovelkakirjat ostetaan toissijaisilta markkinoilta markkinahintaan. Katetuissa velkakirjoissa on vakuus. Arvopaperimarkkinaohjelmaan ostetut joukkovelkakirjat ovat erntymiseen saakka pidettvi ja niiden arvostukseen tehdn muutos vain, jos arvonmuutos on lopullinen. Rahoitusvarallisuus on 17 miljardia, josta kullan osuus on 1,9 miljardia ja varsinainen valuuttavaranto 4,5 miljardia. Loppu on euromrist varallisuutta. Suomen Pankin rahoitusvarallisuuden suurin riski on valuuttariski. Lisksi sijoituksiin liittyy korkoriski. Niden molempien riski arvioituna vakiintuneilla, yleisesti kytetyill riskimalleilla (VaR) on pidetty kriisin ajan samalla tasolla. Kullan suuri hinnan nousu on nostanut sen riskimittarina kytetty VaR-arvoa ja nyttisi siten lisnneen kokonaisriski. On huomattava kuitenkin, ett kullan hintariski vastaan on muodostunut realisoitumaton voitto taseen arvonmuutostilille. Kullan hinta voisi laskea noin 80 prosenttia ennen kuin se aiheuttaisin kulukirjauksen pankin tuloslaskelmaan. Tmn johdosta kultaa ja sen hintariski on perusteltua tarkastella erilln muista riskeist. Rahoitusvarallisuuteen liittyy mys luottoriski. Se on kuitenkin pidetty pienen sijoittamalla luottokelpoisuudeltaan hyvin vhriskiin kohteisiin. Yli 97 prosenttia sijoituksista on luokiteltu A-tai parempaan luokkaan. Kaikki  omat ja jaetut riskithallitaan(kuvat 21 ja 22) Riskienhallinta sislt kaikki tunnistetut, niin eurojrjestelmn kuin omien toimien, riskit. Niit hallinnoidaan limiiteill, hajauttamalla, suojaamalla ja mitoittamalla siten, ett pankin tase voi niist vastata. Jotta riittv varmuus saadaan, tehdn lisksi stressi-ja skenaarioanalyysej sellaisilla olettamuksilla, jotka ovat mahdollisia vaikka eivt olekaan todennkisi. Riskit hallinnoidaan lajeittain ja jopa rahoitusvlineittin, jotta mitn yksittist epsuotuisaa tulemaa ei jisi valvonnan ulkopuolelle ja huomiotta. Riskit yhdistetn viel kokonaisriskiksi, jota tarkastellaan taseen riskipuskureihin. Kun riskit arvioidaan yleisesti kytettviss olevilla menetelmill (VaR ja Expected Shortfall), Suomen Pankin kokonaisriski on rajallinen sen taseen varauksiin ja muihin omiin pomiin nhden. Purettavissa olevat varaukset ja arvonmuutostili riittvt kattamaan tunnistetut riskit. Eurojrjestelmn rahapolitiikan toimista johtuvat riskit ovat murto-osa muutoin omaan toimintaan liittyvist riskeist. Markkinariski, joka koostuu rahoitusvarallisuuden valuutta-, korko-ja luottoriskist, on pankin omaan toimintaan liittyv ja kaikkein suurin osa kokonaisriskist. Yhteenveto (kuva 23) Keskuspankin toiminnassa ei voida vltt riskej, eik tappioitakaan. Nihin huonojen aikojen epsuotuisiin toteutumiin joudutaan varautumaan taseen riskipuskureilla. Kun nit kerrytetn hyvin vuosina, kest tase riskit ja mahdollistaa mys valtion perustellun tulouttamisvaateen toteuttamisen. Samalla keskuspankin toimintakyky varmistetaan kaikissa olosuhteissa. Finanssikriisin ratkaisemisessa tynjako on selv. Keskuspankki voi tehd oman osuutensa rahapolitiikalla, sek sen tavanomaisilla ett eptavanomaisilla toimilla. Nm toimet ovat tehokkaita vain, jos talouspolitiikka muilta osin on kestvll pohjalla. Siksi onkin trke, ett maailman ja Euroopan taloudellinen ongelmien ratkaisuissa hallitukset onnistuvat julkisten talouksien tasapainottamisessa. Title: Economic outlook in a new phase
text: Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen: The economy in a new phase, Autumn meeting of the Helsinki Region Chamber of Commerce 16.11.2011 . Speech . Wednesday16 November 2011,4:00 PM In a new phase of the economy Presentation background text and body Figures (pdf) (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches/documents/111116_hgin_seudun_kauppakamari.pdf) Good listeners, I will take you to the nskym of the economy through five themes. Firstly, the escalation of the financial crisis comes at a bad stage in terms of the fragile recovery of the global economy. Secondly, the international economy has deteriorated throughout the year. The third theme is the specific characteristics of global problems, in which Europe is the middle country. For the fourth time, I will tell you about the measures that have been taken to solve the problems and, finally, recent information on the current situation of the Finnish economy (Figure 2). Now not the usual recession Cyclical fluctuations are part of the normal functioning of market economies. In addition to the usual cyclical fluctuations, economies sometimes find themselves in a more serious predicament. The anatomy of economic downturns is very similar regardless of when they occurred. Typically, during the overheating phase of the economy, indebtedness increases and the prices of fixed assets, and the prices of other assets, such as shares, rise sharply. When a price bubble based on epSrealist expectations bursts at some point, lenders will incur credit losses. The financial sector's difficulties are exacerbated by the crisis and the recession is deepening as before. Banks' lending capacity is deteriorating and contributing to a weakening of economic activity. The weakening of economic development reduces central government tax revenues and public finances run into problems (Figure 3). The close link between public finances and financial institutions makes this situation particularly dangerous for macroeconomic development. The plight of public finances is hitting the financial sector back, as well as through government bond holdings held by banks, and through the deterioration of sovereign credit ratings, which are also rapidly reflected in the credit ratings of banks in that country. This kind of spiral is fatal to economic development. That is why the political authorities, governments and central banks, as well as other economic authorities, are forced to intervene severely in the functioning of the economy and the markets, with the aim of breaking the vicious circle that is intensifying itself. It is obvious that the current economic crisis is not a normal economic downturn. The situation is complicated by the fact that, at the same time, public finances are in difficulties through over-indebtedness, when the financial markets are running seriously. It is known from previous financial crises that recessions accompanied by a financial crisis are much longer lasting than normal economic downturns. We must now prepare for a bad time which will last longer and which will be accompanied by problems arising from employment, lending and the housing market d in particular as a result of falling house prices (Figure 4). Weakened staples The escalation of the sovereign debt crisis comes at a particularly bad time. This is partly due to the fact that economic growth this year has been weaker than expected in all the major economic areas. Economic activity has been subdued, especially in the developed, i.e. lsns, economies. The statistical figures on total production reflect the unsophisticated development (Figure 5). The economy has continued to weaken in recent months. The published gdp figures are a thing of the past, and future developments can only be judged by various economic indicators. Typically, the so-called economic development has been correlated very well with the so-called economic development. indicators of purchasing clerical surveys, which foreshadow future production trends. In the meantime, industrial purchasing PSI is generally showing a slowdown in the growth of the various economies, and that many economies are even entering recession (Figures 6 and 7). Erityispiirteenspako riskeists The slowdown in economic growth is a global problem. Actual economic growth has been clear from forecasts around the world. At the same time, the state of public finances has deteriorated and the situation continues to be bleak in many euro area countries and elsewhere in the EU and the world. In solving economic problems, it has not worked to increase confidence. During the summer, the squabbles in the United States over the years of squabbling over the state of affairs and the poor implementation of the negotiations at several summits in Europe have increased the security of the economy. As the condition of governments and MFIs has been accompanied by a decline in creditworthiness d ratings have been progressively reduced d and additionally reduced, developments have led to a shift in financing towards secure safe-haven destinations and even to the flight of risk from projects and investments (Figure 8). The world economy has been plunged into a new situation as a result of the new crisis. Financing conditions have tightened significantly and the price of financing has risen. Businesses and households are now remarkably cautious in their actions and are considering consumption and investment measures very carefully. Compared to the situation in 2008, when the financial markets, in part, and serious hsirist severely cut back on normal investment and consumption, there is much that is better. That's when the crisis hit from behind the tree, and there was no time to prepare for it. Governments and central banks have now had ready-made policies and action has been taken swiftly. However, the situation is weaker because, as the sovereign debt crisis deepens, the new necessary decisions require a greater degree of responsibility and risk, and in many countries there is no political readiness or desire. In addition, the ability of states to cover additional liabilities or to take stimulus measures has deteriorated as the crisis has progressed, so there are now more funds available than three d four years ago (Figure 9). The proper functioning of financial markets is key to economic development. Therefore, in order to ensure the creditworthiness of financial institutions, it is necessary to ensure that they are sufficiently solvent. The long term of solvency will allow for possible impairment and other losses and allow for the continuation of sound lending. In terms of financing governments and restructuring banks, the current market situation is challenging. Many countries are prevented from borrowing from the market. Despite political considerations and attempts to solve problems, interest rates on bonds issued by debt-bearing countries have risen to levels where it is not possible to acquire debt (Figure 10). Banks in the deposit and loan market, i.e. the so-called "bonds". interbank d market, the situation is still fragile. The situation is well illustrated by the difference between secured and unsecured interest rates. The usual central bank activity and fundraising before the crisis was unsecured. In August 2007, the situation changed when problems arose with the value of a few European funds and the redemption of shares. Banks began pricing average unsecured transactions in a whole new way. The interest rate differential between unsecured and secured loans widened at the time of Lehman's bankruptcy, but stabilised more recently without returning to its previous levels. Now the interest rate differential has widened again and risen to a worrying level, taking into account the fact that the liquidity of the financial institutions is properly secured by central banks. Eurojs systems central banks provide solvent banks with financing against collateral at their request, but despite this, the interbank market is fragile (Figure 11). Europe needs action Weak growth in the euro area will not help to resolve the debt crisis. Economic growth is clearly weaker than previously anticipated. The European Commission's recent estimate for real GDP growth in the euro area next year is only 0.5%. In view of the current state of the financial markets, the solution to Europe's economic problems requires exceptionally wide-ranging and strong action (Figure 12). In order to put the economies of European countries on a sound footing, action is required in three areas; the first is to ensure the functioning of the financial institutions, the second is to rebalance the economies of the states, and the third area is to improve the efficiency of economic policy decisions (Figure 13). First, the MFIs must bring the solvency measured by the nuclear power (the so-called nuclear capital adequacy). Core Tier1) to 9% vhhimsista level. Those banks that do not now have a plan by the end of the current year and implement a solvency increase by the end of mid-2012. Secondly, countries with debt problems must adjust their economies in accordance with EU-IMF programmes and, in addition, all euro area countries must pursue a balanced fiscal policy. National fiscal policy is monitored more closely at EU level. If the general government deficit or the debt ratio becomes excessive, economic sanctions are more likely to follow from the slippage. Thirdly, the political decision-making of the euro area in economic matters will be strengthened. The European Parliament adopted a package of laws, the so-called 'green card'. six packs, on the basis of which, inter alia, sanctions, pre-emptive mechanisms and the expenditure of the Member States will be strengthened. Challenges in Finland as well Finally, good listeners, The Finnish economy has also weakened in terms of global economic growth. According to recent data published yesterday by Statistics Finland, output fell by 0.6 per cent in September from the month before. In the first three quarters of this year, growth has been only 0.3 d 0.6 % and from the previously forecasted growth rates for the whole year. The weak growth rates for exports and industrial production also confirm the picture of a sharply slowdown in economic activity over the course of the current year (Figure 14). Indicators of industrial and consumer confidence predict that the weak trend will continue in the recent era. Industry confidence has been weighed down especially by the weakening of order backlogs. Households' confidence in Finland's economy and general employment development has also faltered (Figures 15 and 16). The slowdown in the world economy and trade has weakened economic development. However, private consumption and d, which follows closely, have continued to grow relatively steadily until September. The rapid growth is probably still driven by the continued trend in employment and, even with low interest rates, the favourable purchasing power of households (Figure 17). However, if the international economy continues to slow down, it is likely that the growth in consumption by Finnish households will also weaken considerably. Our country's ability to look beyond an acute crisis? Good corporate executive listeners, in the face of economic downturns and severe financial crises, Finland has also been concerned about the operating conditions for a vibrant industry. One of the key factors in the success of Finnish enterprises is to take care of productivity growth and ensure investment in productive production. This is not just an area of research and development. Investments in machinery and equipment that expand production capacity continue to be a factor that boosts productivity. When a company makes an investment of one million or ten million euros, in order to obtain a return on the investment and, in the face of competition, the company is forced to continuously develop the productivity of that process. In spite of the weak statures, it is therefore essential to try to look beyond the current problems and to invest in creating new growth. H (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tagHakkarainen)

Title: Economic Outlook  Flee from Risks
text: Deputy Governor Pentti Hakkarainen: Economic Outlook Flee from Risks . Speech . Thursday1 December 2011,4:00 PM Deputy Governor Pentti Hakkarainen Speech at Fibox 20 Gala Dinner in Helsinki on 1st December 2011 The main content of the speech. Ladies and Gentlemen, We celebrate FIBOX's 20 years anniversary during difficult economic time. Economy is stumbling and struggling to its feet, and we bankers have been blamed for complicated financial innovations, subprime crisis, too risky business and so on. Now we have problems of excessive debts. We have not found a big bazooka which would be effective to shoot all troubles away. THE WORLD ECONOMY The world economy and its outlook have deteriorated this year. This is the case in all major economies (slide 2). Weak developments in the spring were partly related to one-off factors. The natural disaster in Japan in March had not only domestic implications but also caused breakages in world-wide production chains. The car and electronics industries, having a lot of subcontracting, were suffering from supply shortages. In addition, turmoil in North Africa raised the price of oil. Higher energy prices slowed growth in consumerso real incomes and spending in advanced economies. It has become evident that the growth slowdown was not only due to temporary events but there are more broad.based factors affecting the world economy. World trade did not recover as expected and firmso output expectations continued to fade. Downward revisions to data on recent economic performance of major economies bring more uncertainty about growth prospects. The difficult debt ceiling negotiations in the United States and the euro area debt crisis further undermined confidence. In particular, trust in political decision-making suffered a serious blow in the markets. Gloomy forecasts have also begun to erode household and business confidence. Other indicators of expectations have been declining as well in many countries. Purchase managerso indices foresee very sluggish industrial output. And as you know, purchase managers' indices (PMIs) have been very good in predicting what kind of economic development takes place afterwords i.e. the correlation with the actual GDP growth has been almost 1:1. We have seen increased uncertainty also in the financial markets. This has hit stock markets world-wide. Price of risk has raised in both government and corporate bond markets. At the same time, demand has shifted towards osafe haveno investments. Investors are buying German and US government debt securities and gold, which have lifted their prices to record high levels. The uncertainty will eventually result in weak economic activity. Based on experience from economic history, faltering confidence may lead to a decline in household consumption and corporate investment. It is likely that this time having a serious financial crisis as a part of current economic slump, a correction will take time. (Slide 3) Research shows that rebounding from recessions, which are accompanied by financial crisis, is slow. It takes a long time to solve problems of high unemployment, reduce leveraging and downsize overheated sectors. SOVEREIGN DEBT CRISIS We see excessive debt levels in various parts of the world, however mostly in advanced economies. Before the financial crisis the countries' debt-to-GDP -ration was close to 60 %, but now the level exceeds 100 %. We have incurred debt amounts of war time without a war. And Europe is the epicenter of the sovereign debt crisis. This hampers the functioning of euro area financial markets. In the European financial sector, there are signs of a weakening of mutual confidence among financial institutions. In interbank markets the risk spreads have widened and the prices of credit default swaps have risen. The write.downs relating to sovereign debt holdings and equity exposures weaken banks' balance sheets. This worsens banks' lending capacity. From companies' point of view this will raise financing costs and may even hinder their access to financing. The longer uncertainty in financial markets prevails, the stronger its implications are for the real economy. In addition to financing channels, adverse effects the crisis spread through trade channels, to the entire world economy. We can compare the current situation with what we had in 2008. We have now less means at our disposal to stimulate our economies. The economic outlook is weak and contains more downside risks. However, there are some positive things. The current situation has not come as a total surprise like in 2008. Another positive thing is also that the corporate-sector balance sheets are still quite sound in both Europe and the United States. In addition, many companies have increased their cash reserves to be able to meet unforeseen needs. Also banks have been able to prepare themselves for the situation and strengthen their balance sheets and liquidity positions. Moreover, with lessons learned from financial market problems in 2008, central banks have the readiness to provide liquidity to financial institutions. POLITICAL DECISIONS Restoring confidence in politicianso ability to make decisions is a key to stabilising the situation. One of the difficulties is the fact that the debt problems are broadly based in several European countries. Greece, Portugal and Ireland have already fallen into a government debt trap. Although, the root cause of the problems were different the outcome is an excessive debt-to-GDP ratio in all cases. An obvious threat is that other countries will follow. Market confidence in the debt-servicing ability of Italy and Spain has already weakened. Italy is suffering from its very high public debt level creating questions of the sustainability of its economic standing. One country that has been in the headlines recently is France. However, discussions on the countryos economy have been very different in nature as those on Italy and Spain: whether the credit rating of French government bonds remains in the top AAA category or whether it will be downgraded. The debt problem is the Achilleso heel of some European countries. There is no way to solve the problem quickly and easily. Resolution requires long-term policy changes, not only in regard to public-sector debt but also private-sector indebtedness. Measures taken by a troubled country no longer necessarily suffice to remedy the situation; a broad-based common commitment is required. An important step in this direction would be a swift implementation of the crisis.management decisions already agreed upon. CONCLUSIONS (slide 4) Ladies and Gentlemen Let me now summarise what I have told you tonight by highlighting some key characteristic of the current economic situation. Global economy is growing but at a slower pace . Growth disappointments in advanced economies in 2011 . Deteriorating public finances in the euro area and elsewhere . Uncertainty on political decision making in the US and Europe . Growing anxiety over sovereign states and financial institutions in the euro area and elsewhere . Run away from risky assets. . Salutations Let me come back to the years when FIBOX was established, in the other words year 1991. That time the future outlook for companies in international business was not at all bright. However FIBOX went through all difficulties, it grew and prospered. The company was able to do so during economically very uncertain period. Today we do have uncertainties in front of us again I am convinced that FIBOX will carry on its activities withstanding all challenges and storms there may arise, as it has done during preceding two decades.
