text: Speech by Pentti Hakkarainen, Vice Chairman of the Executive Board, at the unveiling of The Last Marks, Helsinki 27.1.2012 . Speech . Friday 27 January 2012, 5:00 PM Welcome invited guests and representatives of the information services. Welcome to the book written by Antti Heinonen and the Bank of Finland to the unveiling ceremony of The Last Marks! Even though the use of markka banknotes and coins was already used ten years ago, marks are still a matter of importance to us Finns. The markka was a key national symbol for a long time before finland's self-style, and the motifs and spirits in the illustrations of the markkaseteles were for many Finns. Many of us have marks in their possession. According to a survey commissioned by the Bank of Finland in December from Taloustutkimus, 65% of Finns d either themselves or lshipiirillssn d still held marks. At the end of 2011, the total number of redeemable marks was approximately FIM 1.7 billion at the end of 2011. Of this amount, there were 746 million banknotes, 591 million coins and 332 million commemorative coins. The Bank of Finland's obligation to redeem markka banknotes and coins will expire in just over a month's time on 29.2.2012. After that, the marks have enssily and commemorative value. However, very few are going to return their aging marks. According to this survey, 97% of markholders do not intend to exchange their marks for euros. Assuming that the marks held by people are evenly distributed, approximately 50 million marks redeemed on the basis of the figure would be returned in January-February. In recent years, the markka has returned at an annual rate of about 10 million. However, some mark holders want to exchange their marks for euros. However, you shouldn't wait with the exchange. The Bank of Finland recommends exchanging marks for euros primarily in its own bank. At the event, the Bank of Finland has the pleasure and honour of publishing the book oThe Last Markato, written by Antti Heinonen. The work is interesting for both those who are interested in the history of markka cedars, numismatists who collect marks, and those interested in making banknotes. Edita Oy is responsible for the high-quality printing and graphic design of the book. The author of the book, Antti Heinose, combines the possible target groups of the book mentioned above, and hsn has expanded the nsks angle of the book from a reference book intended purely for numismatists to a direction of interest to a wider readership. Antti Heinonen has an exceptionally fine and long international career in the banknote industry. For a while, he will chair the G10 central bank group, which works to promote banknotes worldwide. For more than ten years, he used to be the Banknote Director of the European Central Bank. In 2001 d 2002, Heinonen chaired the committee responsible for coordinating the euro exchange, so ten years ago we can thank you for the smooth use of the euro throughout the euro area. Prior to the transfer to the European Central Bank, the Bank of Finland was responsible for the payment servicing of the Bank of Finland. Lissksi hsn was the secretary of the subject matter and design committees of the last series of markka vouchers. In addition to the text, the book is rich in illustrations, to which jaakko Koskentola, the chief curator of our monetary museum, has made a great contribution by photographing all the banknotes in the book. The completion of the book has also been influenced by numerous experts from both the Bank of Finland and beyond. I am pleased that a large part of this is at the event. The Bank of Finland is publishing Antti Heinonen's The Last Marks because we considered the publication to serve two purposes. Firstly, the book covers the history of the Finnish notes, from the 1945 model to the issue of euro banknotes in 2002. Secondly, the book serves as a follow-up to a work published in 1952 by the Institute of Economic Research of the Bank of Finland on domestic banknote types that appeared in Finland in 1809d11. In addition to the fact that the work now being published describes the history of Finnish paper money and the life cycle of markkatels in 1945d 2002 from both domestic and international angles, the work sisslss also contains a lot of numismatically interesting details as well as information about the printing technology of banknotes and the development of the authenticity technique. With the publication of this book, the Bank of Finland wants to celebrate in a dignified way the time of redemption of the marks. At the same time, the 10th anniversary of the euro banknotes is also celebrated. Next, I will give the floor to the author of the book, Antti Heinonen, who will present his book on author Antti Hekskulma. After Antti, Professor Yrjs Sotamaa from the Aalto University School of Art and Design has agreed to give a commentary on the work. Towards the end of the event, invited guests and journalists will have the opportunity to present questions and comments. Seppo Honkapohja of our Board of Trustees will open a new rotating exhibition at the Monetary Museum, which will be related to the subject matter of the book to be published. Antti is not good! Friday 27 January 2012, 5:00 PM Hyvt kutsuvieraat ja tiedotusvlineiden edustajat. Tervetuloa Antti Heinosen kirjoittaman ja Suomen Pankin julkaiseman Viimeiset markat -teoksen julkistamistilaisuuteen! Vaikka markkaseteleiden ja -kolikoiden kytt maksuvlinein pttyi jo kymmenen vuotta sitten, markat ovat meille suomalaisille edelleen lheinen asia. Markka oli keskeinen kansallinen symboli jo pitkn ennen Suomen itsenisyytt ja markkaseteleiden kuvituksissa esiintyneet kuva-aiheet ja henkilt olivat monille suomalaisille trkeit. Monella meist on markkoja viel mys hallussaan. Suomen Pankin joulukuussa Taloustutkimukselta teettmn kyselyn perusteella 65 prosentilla suomalaisista  joko itselln tai lhipiirilln  oli edelleen hallussaan markkoja. Tm ei sinns ole yllttv, sill Suomen Pankin tilastojen mukaan lunastettaviksi kelpaavia markkoja oli vuoden 2011 lopussa liikkeess yhteens noin 1,7 miljardin markan arvosta. Tst summasta seteleit oli 746 miljoonaa, kolikoita 591 miljoonaa ja juhlarahoja 332 miljoonaa markkaa. Suomen Pankin velvollisuus lunastaa markkaseteleit ja -kolikoita pttyy reilun kuukauden kuluttua 29.2.2012. Sen jlkeen markoilla on en kerily-ja muistoarvoa. Hyvin harva kuitenkin aikoo palauttaa vanhenevia markkojaan. Mainitun kyselytutkimuksen mukaan perti 97 prosenttia markkojen haltijoista ei aio vaihtaa markkojaan euroiksi. Olettaen, ett ihmisten hallussa olevat markat jakautuvat tasaisesti, tmn luvun perusteella lunastettavia markkoja palautuisi tammi-helmikuussa noin 50 miljoonaa. Viime vuosina markkoja on palautunut noin 10 miljoonan vuosivauhdilla. Osa markkojen haltijoista kuitenkin haluaa vaihtaa markkansa euroiksi. En vaihdon kanssa ei kuitenkaan kannata odotella. Suomen Pankki suosittelee markkojen vaihtamista euroihin ensisijaisesti omassa pankissa. Tss tilaisuudessa Suomen Pankilla on ilo ja kunnia julkaista Antti Heinosen kirjoittama teos Viimeiset markat. Teos on mielenkiintoinen niin markkaseteleiden historiaa harrastaville, markkoja kerileville numismaatikoille kuin seteleiden valmistuksesta kiinnostuneille. Kirjan korkeatasoisesta painojljest ja graafisesta ilmeest vastaa Edita Oy. Kirjan tekijss Antti Heinosessa yhdistyy edell mainitut mahdolliset kirjan kohderyhmt ja hn on laajentanut kirjan nkkulmaa puhtaasti numismaatikoille tarkoitetusta hakuteoksesta mys laajempaa lukijakuntaa kiinnostavaan suuntaan. Antti Heinosella on poikkeuksellisen hieno ja pitk kansainvlinen ura setelialalla. Tll hetkell hn toimii puheenjohtajana G10-keskuspankkien muodostamassa ryhmss, joka toimii setelivrennsten ehkisemiseksi maailmanlaajuisesti. Tt ennen hn oli yli kymmenen vuoden ajan Euroopan keskuspankin setelijohtaja. Heinonen toimi vuosina 2001 2002 eurokteisen vaihdon koordinoinnista vastanneen komitean puheenjohtajana eli hnt voimme kiitt kymmenen vuotta sitten koko euroalueella sujuvasti tapahtuneesta euron kyttnotosta. Ennen siirtymistn Euroopan keskuspankkiin hn vastasi Suomen Pankissa osastopllikkn maksuvlinehuollosta. Lisksi hn oli viimeisten markkasetelisarjojen aihepiiri-ja designtoimikuntien sihteeri. Tekstin ohella kirja on rikas mys kuvitukseltaan, johon suuren panoksen on antanut rahamuseomme intendentti Jaakko Koskentola valokuvaamalla lhes kaikki kirjassa olevat setelit. Kirjan valmistumiseen ovat mys mytvaikuttaneet lukuisat asiantuntijat niin Suomen Pankista kuin sen ulkopuolelta. Heist suuri osa onkin ilokseni lsn tss tilaisuudessa. Suomen Pankki ptti julkaista Antti Heinosen Viimeiset markat -teoksen, koska katsoimme julkaisemisen palvelevan lhinn kahta tarkoitusta. Ensinnkin kirja kattaa Suomen markkamristen seteleiden historian vuoden 1945 mallista aina vuonna 2002 tapahtuneeseen euroseteleiden liikkeeseen laskuun. Toiseksi kirja toimii jatko-osana Suomen Pankin taloustieteellisen tutkimuslaitoksen vuonna 1952 julkaisemalle teokselle Suomessa vuosina 18091951 esiintyneist kotimaisista setelityypeist. Sen lisksi, ett tss nyt julkaistavassa teoksessa kuvataan Suomen paperirahan historiaa ja markkaseteleiden elinkaarta vuosina 19452002 niin kotimaisesta kuin kansainvlisest nkkulmasta, niin teos sislt mys paljon numismaattisesti kiinnostavia yksityiskohtia sek tietoa seteleiden painotekniikasta ja aitoustekijiden kehityksest. Julkaisemalle tmn kirjan Suomen Pankki haluaa juhlistaa arvokkaalla tavalla markkojen lunastusajan pttymist. Samaan yhteyteen ajoittuu mys euroseteleiden kyttnoton 10-vuotismerkkipiv, mik mys antaa aihetta juhlaan. Seuraavaksi annan puheenvuoron kirjan tekijlle Antti Heinoselle, joka esittelee kirjaansa tekijn nkkulmasta. Antin jlkeen Aalto-yliopiston taideteollisen korkeakoulun professori Yrj Sotamaa on ystvllisesti lupautunut antamaan kommenttipuheenvuoron teoksesta. Tilaisuuden loppupuolella kutsuvierailla ja toimittajilla on mahdollisuus esitt kysymyksi ja kommentteja. Viimeiset markat -teoksen julkistamistilaisuuden ptt johtokuntamme jsen Seppo Honkapohja avaamalla uuden vaihtuvan nyttelyn tll rahamuseossa, joka liittyy lheisesti julkaistavan kirjan aihepiiriin. Title: What are the central banks' actions in the European debt crisis?
text: Pentti Hakkarainen, Vice-President of the Executive Board: What is the action taken by central banks in the context of the European debt crisis? Finnish Legal Association, 8.3.2012 . Speech . Thursday8 March 2012,4:00 PM Welcome to the Finnish Legal Association. In my speech, I will discuss the actions of central banks in the current debt crisis. Figure 2 The division between governments and central banks is clear. Governments have taken care of the country's economic policy as a whole and central banks have been given a significant but narrow monetary economy. The role of central banks is to conduct monetary policy and to ensure that the financial markets function reliably and stably, so that monetary policy is translated into the financial markets in the desired way. In the midst of 2011, when the monetary policy escalation occurred in the middle of 2011, we at the European Central Bank and the euro-system national central banks also had to react. Monetary policy escalation was significant in 2011 Photos 4-8 In the middle of 2011, several signs suggested that the market was doing badly. In late 2011, the spread between unsecured and secured interest rates increased from 0.5% to 1.0%. The difference in interest rates can be used as a thermometer to show how the banks' market operates. Interest rates on government bonds also differentiated and the average interest rate in the euro area compared to, for example, the lowest interest rate on government bonds in Germany, broadened during 2011. The deterioration in the functioning of the money markets and the significant divergence in the interest rates on euro area government bonds on the euro area market were conducive to a balanced revision of monetary policy. Figure 9 In order to ensure monetary policy convergence, the European Central Bank and the national central banks of the euro area, the Bank of Finland, among others, had to take the necessary measures in the second half of 2011. The functioning of the market for government and corporate bonds was ensured by the central bank's purchase programme and the key interest rate was cut twice in late 2011, in November and December. In addition, two 3-year credit operations were opened in December 2011 and February 2012. In the second half of 2011, more extensive collateral was also announced to be provided to the central bank to obtain financing. When an MFI applies to the Central Bank for financing, it must always provide collateral. The collateral is assessed and a separate haircut is taken. The collateral value will be cut so that the central bank would not incur a loss but would cover all financing in all circumstances, including in the undesirable situation where the central bank would have to liquidate the collateral. Money markets and liquidity Photos 11 and 12 As regards refinancing operations, money market activity improved and liquidity increased. The European Central Bank's euro-denominational refinancing operations raised the monetary financing to the monetary financial institutions. During the years of the financial crisis, the amount of monetary financing has been higher than before, and now, due to the last refinancing operations in December and February, the maturity of financing and the length of loans to banks increased. The most significant part is the 3-year operation. Euribors have declined since the refinancing operations and the markets have calmed down during the year. Photos 14 and 15 As regards short-term money markets and long-term loan markets, the size of monetary policy bond purchase programmes compared to other financing related to monetary policy implementation is only a fraction. The purchase programmes have ensured that there will be no vssristymi on the bond market which would lead to a situation where, for example, a certain type of creditworthy company in Germany and Italy would be placed in a different financial position. The length of the funding should be carried out in a concerted manner, regardless of where the euro area is operated. Government bond rates in Italy and Spain fell as a result of their bond purchase programmes and financing operations and 3-year operations. Photos 16 and 17 It should be noted that, although we are talking about very high interest rates in Italy and Spain, in the longer term, which takes account of the whole euro period, they are not so far from the average of the interest rate that the countries have paid and managed to cope well with interest rates. Indeed, if you look at the 10-year average interest rate in Italy and the current rate, or, conversely, the two-year average interest rate in Italy and the current rate, you can see that there is not a big difference. In fact, the two-year interest rate is below the average that Italy has paid throughout the euro period. The same picture could be drawn of Spain. Photos 18 and 19 The differences in the development of the countries are significant. They are a good illustration of what the country itself has done to balance its economy. Ireland can be considered a good example of a country that has followed the economic programme set by the lenders. In addition to the fact that its funding has been secured, public confidence in Ireland's creditworthiness has been strengthened. In the market, Irish interest rates have come down. The interest rate differentials between the highest-rated countries and Germany also reflect how well their public finances have been managed. As a good thing, Finland is one of the countries that receives funding by a very narrow margin compared to, for example, Austria or France. Monetary policy risks Figure 21 The activities of central banks always involve risks. Central banks are forced to take action which already entails a risk of risk and loss, sometimes even a loss, in order to keep the financial system up and running. These risks are constantly taken into account in the activities of central banks by means of modern instruments. There are two types of risk. The biggest risk is always how successful monetary policy is. Risk management in the implementation of monetary policy and the financing of banks is at the forefront. Financial risk for financial institutions is also managed on the basis of two key criteria. The first step is to ensure that the financial institution applying for the loan is financially sound. Secondly, criteria are set for collateral against which the Central Bank provides credit. The valuation of collateral is such that the central bank can liquidate it in the event that the bank becomes insolvent during the loan period. Photos 22-24 As a result, collateral is valued at its market value, from which a special collateral valuation is added to the collateral, so that the cost of the liquidation of the collateral does not incur a loss for the central bank. An example is the price and collateral value of the Greek 10-year bond and its evolution. The fact that a Greek government bond of EUR 10 million would be valid as collateral for the same value is not correct. The guarantee would be worth barely a couple of million, and in addition, the person acquiring the financing would have to be solvent. The haircut is affected by the maturity of the collateral offered, the speed of realisation and the creditworthiness. Collateral is received in excess of what MFIs apply for financing. Figure 25 In addition to credit operations, central banks have risks associated with their own financial assets and securities purchase programmes. This is taken into account in the risk management of investment activities, limits, minimum rating requirements, etc. are set. Risks come under scrutiny against the central bank's risk buffers. Figure 26 To conclude, the main risks to central banking are always macroeconomic. In connection with this, for example, the Bank of Finland in the early 1990s found itself in a situation where, in order to bear greater damages and losses, the central bank would bear the risks and losses that were not compensated by any outsider. As a result, the central bank can function well in the years that the central bank can strengthen the risk buffers so that they are used in worse years when such special measures are required. text_original: Johtokunnan varapuheenjohtajan Pentti Hakkarainen: Mitk oat keskuspankkien toimet Euroopan velkakriisiss? Suomen Lainopillisen Yhdistys ry, 8.3.2012 . Speech . Thursday8 March 2012,4:00 PM Hyvt Suomen Lainopillisen Yhdistyksen jsenet, tervetuloa. Ksittelen puheenvuorossani keskuspankkien toimia meneilln olevassa velkakriisiss. Kuva 2 Hallitusten ja keskuspankkien vlinen tynjako on selv. Hallitukset pitvt huolen maan talouspolitiikasta kokonaisuutena ja keskuspankeille on jtetty merkittv, mutta kapea rahatalous. Keskuspankkien tehtvn on hoitaa rahapolitiikkaa ja varmistaa, ett rahoitusmarkkinat toimivat luotettavasti ja vakaasti, jotta rahapolitiikka vlittyy toivotulla tavalla rahoitusmarkkinoille. Kun rahapolitiikan vlittymisess esiintyi hiriit kesll 2011, mys me Euroopan keskuspankissa ja eurojrjestelmn kansallisissa keskuspankeissa jouduimme reagoimaan. Rahapolitiikan vlittyminen hiriintyi merkittvsti kesll 2011 Kuvat 4-8 Kesll 2011 useat merkit viittasivat siihen, ett markkinat voivat jty pahasti. Vuoden 2011 loppukesll vakuudettomien ja vakuudellisten korkojen vlinen erotus kasvoi 0,5 prosentista lhes 1,0 prosenttiin. Niden korkojen vlinen erotus voidaan nhd ernlaisena kuumemittarina, joka kertoo pankkien vlisen markkinan toiminnasta. Mys valtiolainojen korot eriytyivt ja euroalueen keskikorko verrattuna esimerkiksi alimpaan valtionlainakorkoon, Saksan korkoon, leveni vuoden 2011 aikana. Rahamarkkinoiden toiminnan heikkeneminen ja euroalueen valtiolainojen korkojen huomattava eriytyminen pomamarkkinoilla olivat omiaan estmn rahapolitiikan tasapainoisen vlittymisen. Kuva 9 Rahapolitiikan vlittymisen varmistamiseksi Euroopan keskuspankki ja euroalueen kansalliset keskuspankit, Suomen Pankki muiden mukana, joutuivat tekemn vuoden 2011 jlkipuoliskolla tarvittavia toimia. Valtioiden ja yritysten liikkeeseen laskemien joukkolainojen markkinoiden toimivuutta varmistettiin keskuspankin osto.ohjelmalla ja ohjauskorkoa laskettiin kahdesti loppuvuonna 2011, marras-ja joulukuussa. Lisksi kynnistettiin kaksi 3 vuoden luotto-operaatiota, jotka toteutettiin joulukuussa 2011 ja helmikuussa 2012. Vuoden 2011 jlkipuoliskolla ilmoitettiin mys laajemmista vakuuksista, joita toimitetaan keskuspankille rahoituksen saamiseksi. Kun rahalaitos hakee keskuspankista rahoitusta, sen tulee aina toimittaa vakuudet. Vakuuksia arvioidaan pivittin ja niist otetaan viel erillinen aliarvostus. Tll vakuusarvoa leikataan siten, ettei keskuspankille tulisi tappiota vaan tmn vakuuden arvo kattaisi kaiken rahoituksen kaikissa tilanteissa, mys siin ei-toivotussa tilanteessa, jossa keskuspankki joutuisi realisoimaan vakuuden. Rahamarkkinat ja likviditeetti Kuvat 11 ja 12 Rahoitusoperaatioiden osalta rahamarkkinoiden toiminta parani ja likviditeetti lisntyi. Euroopan keskuspankin euromriset jlleenrahoitusoperaatiot nostivat keskuspankkirahoituksen mr rahalaitoksille. Finanssikriisivuosina keskuspankkirahoituksen mr on ollut aikaisempaa runsaampaa ja nyt viimeisten joulukuussa ja helmikuussa toteutettujen jlleenrahoitusoperaatioiden vuoksi rahoituksen maturiteetti ja lainojen pituus pankeille kasvoivat. Merkittvimmn osan muodostavat 3 vuoden operaatiot. Euriborit ovat laskeneet rahoitusoperaatioiden jlkeen ja tmn vuoden puolella markkinoilla on tapahtunut rauhoittumista. Kuvat 14 ja 15 Lyhytaikaisten rahamarkkinoiden ja pitkaikaisten lainamarkkinoiden osalta voidaan todeta, ett rahapolitiikan joukkovelkakirjojen osto-ohjelmien koko verrattuna muuhun rahapolitiikan toteuttamiseen liittyvn rahoitukseen on vain murto-osa. Osto-ohjelmilla on varmistettu, ett joukkolainamarkkinoilla ei tapahdu sellaisia vristymi, jotka johtaisivat tilanteeseen, jossa esimerkiksi tietyntyyppinen luottokelpoinen yritys Saksassa ja Italiassa joutuisi tysin erilaiseen rahoitukselliseen asemaan. Rahoituksen pitisi toimia yhtlisesti riippumatta siit, misspin euroaluetta toimitaan. Italian ja Espanjan valtiolainakorot laskivat niden joukkolainaosto-ohjelmien sek rahoituksen jrjestmisoperaatioiden ja 3 vuoden operaatioiden johdosta. Kuvat 16 ja 17 On huomattava, ett vaikka puhutaan Italian ja Espanjan hyvin korkeista koroista, niin pidemmll, koko euroajan huomioivalla aikavlill, ne eivt ole niin kaukana siit keskiarvosta, millaista korkoa nm maat ovat maksaneet ja pystyneet selvimn korkotasoista hyvin. Tarkasteltaessa Italian 10 vuoden keskikorkoa ja tmn hetken korkoa, tai vastaavasti Italian kahden vuoden keskikorkoa ja tmn hetken korkoa, voidaankin huomata, ettei ero ole suuri. Itse asiassa kahden vuoden korossa ollaan alle sen keskiarvon, jota Italia on maksanut koko euroaikana. Saman kuvan voisi piirt Espanjasta. Kuvat 18 ja 19 Maiden vliset kehityserot ovat merkittvi. Ne osoittavat hyvin sen, mit maa on itse tehnyt taloutensa tasapainottamiseksi. Irlantia voidaan pit hyvn esimerkkin maasta, joka on noudattanut lainanantajien asettamaa talousohjelmaa. Sen lisksi, ett sen rahoitus on varmistunut, niin yleinen luottamus Irlannin luottokelpoisuuteen on vahvistunut. Markkinoilla Irlannin korot ovat tulleet alaspin. Parhaiten luokiteltujen maiden korkoerot suhteessa Saksaan mys kuvastavat sit, miten hyvin niiden julkinen talous on hoidettu. Hyvn asiana voidaan todeta Suomen kuuluvan joukkoon, joka saa rahoitusta varsin kapealla marginaalilla verrattuna esimerkiksi Itvaltaan tai Ranskaan. Rahapolitiikan riskeist Kuva 21 Keskuspankkien toimintaan liittyy aina riskej. Keskuspankit joutuvat tekemn toimia, joihin sisltyy jo lhtkohtaisesti riski-ja tappiovaara, joskus varsinainen tappiokin, jotta rahoitusjrjestelm saadaan pidetty toiminnassa. Nm riskit otetaan jatkuvasti huomioon keskuspankkien toiminnassa nykyaikaisten vlineiden avulla. Riskej on kahdenlaisia. Suurin riskilhde on aina se, miten rahapolitiikassa onnistutaan. Rahapolitiikan toteuttamiseen ja pankkien rahoittamiseen liittyv riskienhallinta on etukteen snnelty. Rahalaitoksille mynnettvn rahoituksen riskej hallitaan kahden keskeisen kriteerin perusteella. Ensimmiseksi varmistetaan, ett lainaa hakeva rahoituslaitos on vakavarainen. Toiseksi asetetaan kriteerit vakuuksille, joita vastaan keskuspankki antaa luottoa. Vakuuksien arvostus on sellainen, ett keskuspankki voi realisoida ne siin tapauksessa, ett pankki tulee laina-aikana maksukyvyttmksi. Kuvat 22-24 Nin ollen vakuudet arvostetaan pivittin markkina-arvoon, josta otetaan lisksi vhennyksen erityinen vakuusarvostus, jotta vakuuksien realisointitilanteen kustannukset eivt aiheuttaisi tappiota keskuspankille. Esimerkkin todettakoon Kreikan 10 vuoden joukkolainan hinta ja vakuusarvo ja sen kehitys. Se ksitys, ett 10 miljoonan euron Kreikan valtion velkakirja kelpaisi samasta arvosta vakuudeksi ei pid paikkansa. Vakuus kelpaisi juuri ja juuri parista miljoonasta ja lisksi rahoituksen hankkijan pit olla vakavarainen. Aliarvostukseen vaikuttavat tarjottavan vakuuden juoksuaika, realisointinopeus sek luottokelpoisuus. Vakuuksia vastaanotetaan yli sen, mit rahalaitokset hakevat rahoitusta. Kuva 25 Luotto-operaatioiden lisksi keskuspankeilla on riskej, jotka liittyvt omaan rahoitusvarallisuuteen ja arvopapereiden osto-ohjelmiin. Nm huomioidaan sijoitustoiminnan riskienhallinnassa, asetetaan limiitit, minimiluokitusvaateet jne. Riskit tulevat tarkasteluun keskuspankin riskipuskureita vastaan. Kuva 26 Thn loppuun totean, ett keskuspankkitoiminnan suurimmat riskit ovat aina makrotaloudellisia. Siihen liittyen esimerkiksi Suomen Pankki 1990-luvun alussa joutui tilanteeseen, jossa suurempien vahinkojen ja tappioiden vlttmiseksi keskuspankin kannettavaksi ji riskej ja tappioita, joita kukaan ulkopuolinen ei korvannut. Tmn johdosta on trke, ett keskuspankki voi toiminnassaan hyvin vuosina vahvistaa riskipuskureita, jotta ne ovat kytettviss huonompina vuosina, jolloin tllaisiin erityistoimiin joudutaan. Title: State of the financial markets and prospects for corporate finance
text: Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen: The state of the financial markets and the nskymst of corporate finance, meeting of the Entrepreneurship Delegation of the Confederation of Finnish Industries, Helsinki 9.5.2012 . Speech . Tuesday 8 May2012,3:00 PM Ladies and gentlemen, welcome! My topic is the state of the financial markets and the nancy of corporate finance. Director Jussi Mustonen gave an overview of the current economic situation in the morning. The presentations are a good background to take a closer look at the state of the financial markets. Nikhym is affected by the fact that there is growth in the global economy. In the United States, growth is in the order of 2.5 d 3 %, but the state of housing finance and the housing market, high employment rates and federal debt and deficit problems remain uncorrected. China's economic growth is faster, but it has certainly slowed down in the first half of the year. China's main threat is overheating, marked by a very strong increase in credit and rising house and other fixed prices. From the point of view of the world's economy, too, it is a question of how to rebalance the Chinese economy without being forced to adjust too hard. The positive signs of the Japanese economy last year were not permanent, and now the period of very slow, non-existent growth of the past decades continues. At the end of last year, Europe and the euro area entered a recession, which is expected to continue this year. Economic growth is forecast for the euro area towards the end of the year, but at a very slow pace. Figure 3 There is nshty polarization in the sovereign credit market. Good, creditworthy countries can easily get money. For some countries, the so-called safe-haven approach means that money comes at low interest rates and on excellent terms. For some countries, access to finance has become more difficult. These countries do not receive financing other than on a very short-term basis or at interest rates that are clearly higher than usual. Long-term access to finance for the crisis-stricken economies of Erside is also hindered. In the early part of the year, the situation in the sovereign credit market calmed down. Credit risk prices in Portugal and Ireland continued Decline. Figure 4 As a result of the evolution of banks' credit risks, there has been a slight increase in credit risk in the financial sector as a whole. The figure also shows that banks in countries where the country's own credit risk premium has increased are priced higher. For example, the Greek Bank Alpha and the Portuguese Bank Banco Comercial have increased the cost of servicing their own domestic debt. The average cost of credit risk in the banking sector as a whole is around 2% per annum when covered by five-year credit default swaps. Figure 5 An excellent thermometer for the financial markets is how risk is priced in the banks' markets. The difference in interest rates between secured and unsecured bank lending illustrates well the risk. At the time of the Lehman crisis in autumn 2008, the interest rate on a secured repo transaction was kept at normal unsecured bank lending to pay a margin of up to 1.5% in a short-term transaction. In the past, an unsecured loan was priced at the same level as a repo shop. The change used to beskemshchn. We are used to pitsn banks without collateral as sure covers of liability if, for example, we need a guarantee of liability for the liability period of a construction project. In the market for banks, the banks did not trust each other unsecured, but required collateral through a repo transaction. If the secured transaction could not be carried out, the previously non-existent interest rate differential spread and the additional risk price had to be paid. The situation calmed down during 2009 d 2011, until at the end of last year the spread in interest rates started to wide again and the market returned to collapsing. Figure 6 In addition to government and bank market risk indicators, it is useful to look at corporate credit risk prices and how they are priced on the market compared to governments and the financial sector. It is obvious that there was an error in the pricing of credit risk in the early 2000s, and the price was generally too low for the risk. At the heart of the financial crisis, credit risk is priced at a much higher price. The differences between the sectors have also widened and the risk is priced more precisely. It is interesting to note that, during the financial crisis, it has now been more expensive to cover the credit risk of the financial sector than other companies and industries. Banks' own financing is therefore, on average, more expensive than that of companies. As a result, it can be assumed that banks will in future price their lending better to cover the costs of their own financing. Figures 7 and 8 Lending is likely to tighten not only on the basis of prices. The central banks have carried out studies on how the banks will tighten their own lending conditions over the next few months. It can be seen that, over the last two quarters, the share of the large euro area banks intending to tighten the criteria for corporate loans has clearly increased. Fortunately, banks in Finland are solvent and profitability has remained good. Figure 9 In addition to the profitability and solvency of the banking sector, financial market stability is also predicted by the number of bankruptcies initiated, the evolution of bank receivables and the number of credit write-offs by banks. The number of bankruptcies filed and the amount of receivables of banks has increased, but the levels have remained very stable and the average level has remained lower. To sum up, the MFI sector in Finland is profitable and solvent, and no major threats to stability are foreseen. Business financing is good on the basis of this. Figure 11 There are a few observations to be made on the structure of interest-bearing liabilities of companies. The total interest-bearing debt of non-financial corporations has remained stable in recent years, despite the fact that there have been major crises in the international financial markets. The indebtedness of companies operating in Finland is on average the same as in Europe, and according to what has previously been reported, the number of bankruptcies has not increased substantially even with the collapse of GDP during 2008d 2009. The Finnish financial market is quite bank-oriented. Bank financing has remained stable since 2009. Another observation is that in the structure of corporate debt, the share of long-term bonds has increased. The latest data indicate a slight reduction in the financing of tyselskeyhtiside to enterprises, which shows that there are no bottlenecks in companies' access to finance similar to those in 2008 d 2009, when tel re-lending by tyselskeyhtiside played a role in securing business financing. Photos 12 and 13 In the euro area, the annual growth rate of loans to non-financial corporations is zero. As far as Finland is concerned, the development is more dramatic. In Finland, loans to non-financial corporations have grown at a growth rate of 5d 7 % during 2010d 2011, significantly higher than the average in the euro area. The development of the loan portfolio of Finnish non-financial corporations should also be examined in such a way that loans from housing companies are considered separately. Figure 14 The development of loans to non-financial corporations can also be examined according to the size of corporate loans. In the first half of the year, slightly more loans of less than one million euros from Finnish monetary financial institutions have been issued than in the corresponding period a year earlier. For larger loans of more than one million euros, the number of new contracts signed has been about the same as a year earlier. Figure 15 For businesses, the price of a loan is still attractively low. However, the integers are driven by segregation. A number of companies still receive a loan on favorable terms. Then there are many companies that cannot get a loan on a broad margin or otherwise on acceptable terms. The maturity of the loans is shorter than in the past. This is part of the explanation for the fact that the average interest rate on the entire stock of corporate bonds has come down sharply and is at a historically low level. Figure 16 The financing of the corporate sector in the commercial paper market for credit institutions is lower than at its peak in 2008. The commercial paper market is recovering from the worst phase of the crisis and the stock is at the levels it was at in 2005 d 2007. Figure 17 There will be new challenges for the financial markets and corporate finance, even though the situation in Finland is still good. Slow economic growth is likely to weaken the financial position of firms and the willingness of banks to finance them. Low interest rates put a strain on banks' profitability. As I said earlier, looking at the euro area, the price of MFI self-financing on the market is higher than in the average corporate sector. It is difficult for banks to withdraw money from the market on more favourable terms than they have to pay for themselves. As a lesson in the crisis, banks are reshaping their business models in a safer direction and the importance of basic banking is growing. It can contribute to the provision of business finance. Another threat to corporate finance is that banks are increasingly targeting the domestic market. The international lending arrangements of many large Finnish companies have met with the fact that international banks have been involved in loan syndicates. Figure 18 It has been pointed out that the tightening of banking slump, solvency and liquidity requirements and other banking measures are undermining the ability of MFIs to finance financing. This will happen, but the impact of the changes will be smaller than what has been publicly stated. MFIs operating in Finland already have good solvency. Their need to adapt and prepare for higher requirements in the future is lower than in the rest of Europe. Of the new requirements, the biggest changes will be brought about by the new liquidity requirements. The effects of the changes in bank credits on bank credit interest rates have been estimated to be in accordance with the Bank of Finland's reports approximately 0,25 % of the individual if the bank does not make any other changes in its business. Banks operate in a dynamic environment. In the competition, they have developed their own activities and productivity. On that basis, the impact may be smaller than the current calculations. For those interested in the enclave of the impact assessments, see the Bank of Finland's euro & economy publication in December 2010, which, on the basis of a stability analysis, has made estimates of the magnitude of the impact. The key finding is that, although rising financial prices may reduce GDP in a short period of time, the new requirements for the economy as a whole are unsustainable. As the likelihood of banking crises decreases and banks operate more stable, the national economy will have a better chance of growth and there will be a positive net effect. Other studies are also available, including: The Bank of Canada has made similar estimates. Good ladies and gentlemen, There are good conditions for business financing in the future, and the current state of business financing is good for us. The credit crunch is not marked by the nsks circless and while in the rest of the euro area the growth rate of banks' loans to non-financial corporations has slowed down, it is clearly growing. The growth in loans to non-financial corporations is due to the fact that international financial institutions have become more waterlogged and MFIs operating in Finland have taken a larger share of the lending system than before. In addition to bank financing, companies have received financing from the domestic bond market. The stock of loans marketed domestically has grown by one fifth, or about one billion euros. In addition, some EUR 1.5 billion worth of new financing has been raised on the international bond market during the first quarter of the year. When the domestic commercial paper market and the bank market are functioning well, it can be believed and expected that the business finance market will remain quite well. The most important way, for you good business representatives and entrepreneurs, to ensure good financing conditions is to ensure that financial institutions are put out to tender and that the best conditions are always sought from financial institutions. It is certainly the best guarantee of the pricing problems that may arise for the MFI as a result of the tightening of the financial institutions. Tuesday 8 May2012,3:00 PM Hyvt naiset ja herrat, tervetuloa! Aiheenani on rahoitusmarkkinoiden tila ja yritysrahoituksen nkymt. Johtaja Jussi Mustonen piti aamupivll katsauksen ajankohtaisesta taloustilanteesta. Hnen esitelmns pviestit ovat hyv tausta tarkastella tarkemmin rahoitusmarkkinoiden tilaa. Nkymiin vaikuttaa se, ett maailmantaloudessa on kasvua. Yhdysvalloissa kasvu on 2,53 prosentin luokkaa, mutta asuntorahoituksen ja -markkinoiden tila, korkea tyttmyysaste sek liittovaltion velka-ja vajeongelmat ovat edelleen korjaamatta. Kiinan talouskasvu on nopeampaa, mutta alkuvuonna se on tosin hidastunut. Kiinan keskeisen uhkana on ylikuumentuminen, josta merkkein ovat hyvin voimakas luotonannon lisntyminen ja asuntojen sek muiden kiinteistjen hintojen nousu. Maailman taloudenkin nkkulmasta on trke, miten Kiinassa talous saadaan tasapainotettua ilman liian kovaan sopeutukseen ajautumista. Kuva 3 Valtioiden luottomarkkinoilla on nhty polarisoitumista. Hyvt, luottokelpoiset valtiot saavat helposti rahaa. Niin sanottu turvasatamahakuisuus johtaa joidenkin valtioiden osalta siihen, ett raha tulee enntyksen alhaisilla koroilla ja erinomaisilla ehdoilla. Joidenkin maiden osalta rahoituksen saanti on vaikeutunut. Nm maat eivt saa rahoitusta muuta kuin hyvin lyhytaikaisesti tai tavanomaista selvsti korkeammilla koroilla. Eriden kriisiytyneiden talouksien pitkaikainen rahoituksen hankinta on tysin estynyt. Alkuvuonna valtioiden luottomarkkinoiden tilanne rauhoittui. Portugalin ja Irlannin luottoriskihinnat jatkoivat laskuaan. Kuva 4 Pankkien luottoriskien kehityst kuvaavasta kyrst on nhtviss, ett koko rahoitussektorin luottoriski on hiukan noussut. Kuvasta havaitaan mys, ett niiden maiden pankkien, joissa maan oma luottoriskipreemio on kasvanut, luottoriskit hinnoitellaan korkeammalle. Esimerkiksi kreikkalainen Alpha-pankki ja portugalilainen Banco Comercial-pankki krsivt siit, ett oman kotimaan velanhoidon kustannukset ovat kasvaneet. Koko pankkisektorin keskimrinen luottoriskin hinta on noin 2 prosenttia vuodessa kun se katetaan viiden vuoden luottoriskijohdannaisilla. Kuva 5 Erinomainen rahoitusmarkkinoiden kuumemittari on se, miten riski hinnoitellaan pankkien vlisill markkinoilla. Vakuudellisen ja vakuudettoman pankkien vlisen lainanannon korkoero kuvaa hyvin tt riski. Lehmanin kriisin aikaan syksyll 2008 vakuudellisen repo-kaupalla toteutetun transaktion koron plle piti normaalissa vakuudettomassa pankkien vlisess lainanannossa maksaa jopa 1,5 prosentin marginaali mys lyhyess yhden kuukauden transaktiossa. Aiemmin vakuudeton laina hinnoiteltiin lhes samalle tasolle kuin repo-kauppakin. Muutos oli ennennkemtn. Olemme tottuneet pitmn pankkeja ilman vakuuttakin varmoina vastuunkattajina, jos tarvitsemme esimerkiksi rakennusprojektin vastuuajan korvausvelvollisuuden takuun. Pankkien vlisill markkinoilla pankit keskenn eivt yhtkki en luottaneetkaan toisiinsa vakuudettomasti, vaan vaativat repo.kaupan transaktion kautta vakuuden. Mikli vakuudellista kauppaa ei voitu toteuttaa, aiemmin lhes olematon korkoero levisi ja lisriskihinta piti maksaa. Tilanne rauhoittui 20092011 vlisen aikana, kunnes viime vuoden lopulla korkoero alkoi taas levet ja markkinat nyttivt hyytyvn uudelleen. Kuva 6 Valtioiden ja pankkien vlisen markkinan riskimittareiden lisksi on hyv tarkastella yritysten luottoriskihintoja ja miten ne hinnoitellaan markkinoilla verrattuna valtioihin ja rahoitussektoriin. On ilmeist, ett luottoriskin hinnoittelussa tapahtui 2000-luvun alkuvuosina virhe, ja hinta oli yleisesti liian pieni riskiin nhden. Finanssikriisin myt luottoriski hinnoitellaan huomattavasti kalliimmin. Mys toimialojen vliset erot ovat kasvaneet ja riski hinnoitellaan tarkemmin. Mielenkiintoista on havaita, ett rahoitussektorin luottoriskin kattaminen on nyt finanssikriisin aikana ollut kalliimpaa kuin muiden yritysten ja toimialojen. Pankkien oma rahoitus on siis keskimrin kalliimpaa kuin yritysten. Tmn johdosta voi olettaa, ett pankit hinnoittelevat jatkossa lainanantonsa paremmin kattamaan oman rahoituksensa kustannukset. Kuvat 7 ja 8 Luotonanto kiristynee muutoinkin kuin hintojen perusteella. Keskuspankit ovat tehneet selvityksi siit, miten pankit tulevat kiristmn seuraavien kuukausien aikana omia lainanantoehtojaan. Kuva 9 Pankkisektorin kannattavuus-ja vakavaraisuusnkymien lisksi rahoitusmarkkinoiden vakautta ennakoi mys se, miten paljon konkursseja on laitettu vireille ja miten pankkien jrjestmttmien saamisten mr kehittyy ja kuinka paljon pankit ovat joutuneet tekemn luottotappiokirjauksia. Vireille pantujen konkurssien lukumr sek pankkien jrjestmttmien saamisten mr on kasvanut, mutta tasot ovat pysyneet hyvin vakaina ja keskimrist alempina. Yhteenvetona voi todeta, ett rahalaitossektori on Suomessa kannattava ja vakavarainen, eik vakauteen ennakoida suuria uhkia. Yritysrahoituksen nkymt ovat tlt pohjalta hyvt. Kuva 11 Yritysten korollisten velkojen rakenteesta voi tehd muutamia havaintoja. Yritysten korollisen velan kokonaismr on pysynyt vakaana viime vuodet siit huolimatta, ett kansainvlisill rahoitusmarkkinoilla on nhty suuria kriisej. Suomessa toimivien yritysten velkaantuneisuus on keskimrin vhisemp kuin Euroopassa eik aiemmin ilmi tulleen mukaisesti myskn konkurssien mr ole kasvanut olennaisesti edes bruttokansantuotteen romahtaessa vuosien 20082009 aikana. Suomalainen rahoitusmarkkina on varsin pankkikeskeinen. Pankkien rahoitus on pysynyt vakaana sitten vuoden 2009. Toinen havainto on, ett yritysten velan rakenteessa pitkaikaisten joukkovelkalainojen osuus on kasvanut. Viimeisimmt tiedot kertovat tyelkeyhtiiden rahoituksen yrityksille hiukan supistuneen, mik osoittaa, ett yritysten rahoituksen saannilla ei ole samanlaisia pullonkauloja kuin vuosina 20082009, jolloin tyelkeyhtiiden tel-takaisinlainauksella oli trke rooli yritysrahoituksen varmistamisessa. Kuvat 12 ja 13 Euroalueella yrityslainojen vuosikasvu on lhell nollaa. Suomen osalta tm kehitys on mynteisemp. Suomessa yrityslainat ovat kasvaneet vuosien 20102011 aikana 57 prosentin kasvuvauhtia eli merkittvsti enemmn kuin euroalueella keskimrin. Suomalaisten yritysten lainakannan kehityst tulee tarkastella mys siten, ett asunto.osakeyhteisjen lainat katsotaan erilln. Kuva 14 Yrityslainojen kehityst voidaan mys tarkastella yrityslainojen koon mukaan. Suomalaisista rahalaitoksista alle yhden miljoonan euron lainoja on tmn vuoden alkupuolella mynnetty hiukan enemmn kuin vuotta aikaisemmin vastaavana aikana. Suurempien, yli miljoonan euron lainojen osalta uusia sopimuksia on mrltn tehty suunnilleen saman verran kuin vuotta aikaisemmin. Kuva 15 Yrityksille lainan hinta on edelleen houkuttelevan matala. Kokonaislukujen taustalla on kuitenkin eriytymist. Useat yritykset saavat lainan edelleen edullisilla ehdoilla. Sitten on monia yrityksi, jotka eivt saa lainaa levellkn marginaalilla tai muutoin hyvksyttvill ehdoilla. Lainat ovat juoksuajaltaan lyhyempi kuin aiemmin. Tm on osaltaan selitys sille, ett yrityslainojen koko kannan keskikorko on tullut selvsti alaspin ja on historiallisen alhaisella tasolla. Kuva 16 Yritysten kyttpoman rahoitus luottolaitosten vlittmill yritystodistusmarkkinoilla on pienempi kuin aivan huippuvuonna 2008. Yritystodistusmarkkinat elpyivt kriisin pahimmasta vaiheesta ja kanta on niill tasoilla, joilla oltiin vuosina 20052007. Kuva 17 Rahoitusmarkkinoille ja yritysrahoitukseen tulee uusia haasteita, vaikka tilanne Suomessa onkin viel hyv. Hidas talouskasvu on omiaan heikentmn yritysten taloudellista asemaa ja vhentmn pankkien halua rahoittaa yrityksi. Matalat korot rasittavat pankkien kannattavuutta. Kuten aiemmin totesin, euroalueen tarkastelussa rahalaitosten itsens markkinoilta hankkiman jlleenrahoituksen hinta on korkeampi kuin keskimrin yrityssektorilla. Pankkien on vaikea vlitt markkinoilta hankkimaansa rahaa edullisemmilla ehdoilla kuin mit se itse joutuu maksamaan. Kriisin opetuksena pankit muokkaavat liiketoimintamallejaan entist turvallisempaan suuntaan ja peruspankkitoiminnan merkitys kasvaa. Tm voi osaltaan vhent yritysrahoituksen tarjontaa. Yritysrahoitukselle toinen uhka on se, ett pankit suuntautuvat entist enemmn kotimarkkinoille. Monien suurten suomalaisten yritysten kansainvliset lainajrjestelyt ovat kohdanneet tmn siin, ett kansainvlisi pankkeja on aiempaa vhemmn mukana lainasyndikaateissa. Kuva 18 On vitetty, ett pankkisntelyn kiristyminen, vakavaraisuus-ja likviditeettivaatimukset ja muut pankkisntelyn toimet heikentvt rahalaitosten kyky rahoituksen vlittmiseen. Nin osaltaan tapahtuu, mutta sntelymuutosten vaikutukset ovat ehk kuitenkin pienempi kuin mit on julkisuudessa esitetty. Suomessa toimivilla rahalaitoksilla on hyv vakavaraisuus jo nyt. Niiden sopeutumistarve ja varautuminen tiukempiin vaatimuksiin jatkossa on pienemp kuin muualla Euroopassa. Uusista vaatimuksista ehk kaikkein suurimpia muutoksia tuovat uudet likviditeettivaatimukset. Sntelymuutosten vaikutukset pankkiluottojen korkoihin on arvioitu olevan Suomen Pankin selvitysten mukaisesti noin 0,25 prosenttiyksikk, jos pankki ei liiketoiminnassaan tee muita muutoksia. Pankit toimivat dynaamisessa ympristss. Kilpailussa niden on kehitettv omaa toimintaansa ja tuottavuuttaan. Tll perusteella vaikutukset voivat jd viel nykyisi laskelmia pienemmiksi. Niille, jotka ovat kiinnostuneita niden vaikutusarvioiden sisllst voivat tutustua Suomen Pankin Euro & talous -julkaisuun joulukuussa 2010, jossa on tehty vakausanalyysin pohjalta arvioita niden sntelyvaikutusten suuruudesta. Keskeinen havainto on, ett vaikka rahoituksen kallistuminen voi laskea BKT:ta lyhyell aikavlill, koko kansantaloudelle uudet vaatimukset ovat hydyllisi. Kun pankkikriisien todennkisyys pienenee ja pankit toimivat vakaammin, saa kansantalous paremman kasvun mahdollisuuden ja nin tll on positiivinen nettovaikutus. Muitakin tutkimuksia on saatavilla, mm. Kanadan keskuspankki on tehnyt samanlaisia arvioita. Hyvt naiset ja herrat, Yritysrahoitukselle on hyvt toimintaedellytykset jatkossa, ja yritysrahoituksen nykytila on meill hyv. Luottolaman merkkej ei ole nkpiiriss ja vaikka muualla euroalueella pankkien yrityslainakannan kasvuvauhti on hidastunut, meill se on selvss kasvussa. Yrityslainojen kasvussa on mukana sit vaikutusta, ett kansainvliset rahoituslaitokset ovat vetytyneet ja Suomessa toimivat rahalaitokset ovat ottaneet nist lainajrjestelyist aiempaa suuremman osan. Pankkirahoituksen lisksi yritykset ovat saaneet rahoitusta kotimaisilta joukkovelkakirjamarkkinoilta. Kotimaassa markkinoitujen lainojen kanta on kasvanut lhes viidenneksell eli noin miljardilla eurolla. Mys kansainvlisilt joukkovelkakirjamarkkinoilta on hankittu uutta rahoitusta tmn vuoden ensimmisen neljnneksen aikana noin 1,5 miljardin euron arvosta. Kun kotimaiset yritystodistusmarkkinat ja pankkien vlinen markkina nyttvt toimivan hyvin, voidaan uskoa ja odottaa yritysrahoituksen markkinankymien pysyvn aika hyvin. Keskeisin keino, teille hyvt yritysten edustajat ja yrittjt, varmistaa hyvt rahoituksen ehdot on huolehtia siit, ett rahalaitoksia kilpailutetaan ja haetaan aina parhaat ehdot rahalaitoksilta. Se on varmasti paras tae mys vltt ne hinnoitteluun liittyvt ongelmat, jotka mahdollisesti rahalaitosten tiukkenevan sntelyn kautta rahalaitokselle tulee. Title: Economic outlook and Finnish financial markets
text: Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen: The economy and the Finnish financial markets . Speech . Thursday10 May 2012, 4:00 PM Presentation by Pentti Hakkarainen, Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Suomen Arvo-osuusj?rjestelm? 20th anniversary seminar, Helsinki 10.5.2012 Good ladies and gentlemen! You received an invitation to entertain yourself at an evening party to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the Finnish Book-Cooperative System. The entertaining evening entertainment made me wonder how my subject, the economic sector and the Finnish financial markets, makes me entertained in the economic situation. I can use a story to back up what I'm saying, but let's get back to it in a nutshell. Figure 2 The first development of the world economy is that it is currently at a very different pace. The global economy slowed down towards the end of last year. N?in occurred in China, Japan and Europe. As an exception, in the United States, n?ht is a sign of growth. China's growth in the first quarter of the year has been the slowest in three years and the question is whether the economy has overheated. The data on the growth of other economies also show that growth is not very solid. Figures 3 and 4 The often very proactive purchasing indices of the economy strengthened in the major economies, with the exception of Europe. The household confidence index also strengthened, and the latest data on world trade indicate that it is growing , albeit at a slower pace than in the past. Signals from the stock market confirm n?kymi?. Expectations of global economic growth also create expectations of the stabilisation of financial markets. The beginning of the year has been a time of rising stock prices. In recent weeks, however, the situation has changed and, especially in Europe, stock prices have fallen. The eps uncertainties of global economic growth resurfaced. There are unresolved problems in the big economies: solving the US housing market, the tyshchen and federal deficits, how to balance China's potentially overheated economy, and how to continue the Japanese economy. At the same time, the means should be used to strengthen the European economy so that it emerges from recession. The downward risk common to all economic areas - in the terms of an economist - is the problem of the European debt crisis. Figures 5 and 6 Finland's economic growth slowed down last year. The first quarter of the year was a period of very weak growth. The growth amounted to 0.1 per cent. The weakness is wide-ranging, as consumption and construction investment stagnated. The Bank of Finland's latest forecast expects growth of around 0.4 per cent for the year and 1.8 per cent for next year. In Finland, the consumer confidence indicator (CCI) returned to its average level in the early part of the year, when optimism about an improvement in the global economic situation turned positive. Figures 7 and 8 Business confidence also improved during the first quarter of the year. However, the confidence indicators dipped in all sectors in April, and on the whole it is weaker than the average. Industrial production is stagnating, and recent data on new orders in industry are not improving. Output of export industries by industry is clearly below the levels of 2007 and 2008. In particular, the production of the s?hk?electronics industry, but also of the forest industry, has declined by tens of percent. Only production in the chemical industry has remained more or less unchanged. Figure 9 The problems of exports and the pull of domestic demand have become sub-balance of trade over the past year and the current account has become a sub-balance of supply in the past year. It can be said that Finland is indebted abroad. The trade balance was initially substandard due to trade in goods, but the recent high level of household consumption and investment in housing has contributed to a significant deterioration in the current account. The current account balance sheet has reasons to react if it can substantially increase the risk of access to finance or is the result of balanced economic development. The risks are now related to the deficit of public finances and the rate of household indebtedness, which will be given special attention. The competitiveness of domestic production is essential for the external balance and should be ensured in order to ensure healthy growth of the national economy. Good listeners, going to the financial markets and, in particular, to the national market and its future. The Finnish financial system is particularly bank-oriented. The decline in access to finance, not to mention the threat of a credit crunch, has not been marked for a while. The profitability of firms and the high level of investment have curbed corporate indebtedness. Indeed, indebtedness is lower than the european average. In this respect, the number of bankruptcies filed has also remained fairly stable. The companies withstood the severe recession of 2008? 2009 well and have been in good shape. Tuesday 18 September 2012, 4:30 PM Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen Seminar of etera's board of directors and management group Helsinki 18.9.2012 THE FUTURE OF THE EUROPEAN BANKING SYSTEM NKYMT d BANKING MUST NOT STIFLE COMPETITION In the case of global financial market crises, the risks of the euro area and their resolution play a key role. In late summer, the functioning of the financial markets showed signs of stabilisation, with stock prices rising and government bond markets falling yields on peripheral government bonds. However, the situation is not over. Future developments are risked by governments, central banks and other public authorities. The division has been refined by the conditionality of the ECB's direct monetary policy purchase programme (OMT): governments must first take their own measures to rebalance the economy and only then do monetary policy measures have to be justified. As part of the resolution of the crisis d and above all with a view to longer-term stability d financial market stability and supervision. However, it is essential to ensure that there is no excess that would stifle competition and the efficient functioning of the financial markets. I will examine the measures and their impact on the European banking system from the point of view of the European banking system. The economic crisis in Europe is full of solutions to the problems of financial absorption, the slow pace of political decision-making and the implementation of stabilising measures, the development of the real economy and, more broadly, the mutually reinforcing negative spiral of the institutions. The problems are exacerbated by the fact that d as the spanish and Italian examples show d the financial position of states and banks and, in particular, the market's confidence in creditworthiness are now closely interlinked. [SLIDE 1] This results in two ways: on the one hand, governments are seen as being responsible for supporting their banking sectors, while banks, through their sovereign bond investments, are closely linked to the development of risk in the country in which they are located. International economic development has deteriorated, which has also been exacerbated by the European debt crisis. Treatment. The weakening of the economy is having a negative impact on the banking sector, both through the intensification of credit losses and deteriorating government bond investments. It has not been possible to credibly break the link between sovereign risk and the banking sector. In order to remedy the situation, a number of difficult political decisions have already been made, now their rapid implementation is vsltsmschn. However, in the euro area's bank-centric financing model, one of the obstacles to normalisation of financing is the still very challenging situation in the banking sector, especially in crisis countries. In addition, the borrowing of banks in several countries depends on the issuance of secured debt securities, the success of attracting deposits and the financing of central banks. The commonality in Europe has been reduced and the cross-border funding has become significantly reduced. The dichotomy hampers the operating conditions of the banking sector and the ability of banks to support the development of economic growth through the provision of finance. The poor situation of banks in countries with economic problems is a direct factor in the development of credit and prices. [SLIDE 2] In Nsisss countries, the interest rate differentials on corporate credit, for example, to the 3-month euribor nshden are much greater than in countries with higher credit ratings. Loan and deposit stocks are shrinking in GIIPS countries. Indeed, the problems in the crisis countries in terms of funding control are temporarily exacerbating the polarised development of the euro area's real economy. [SLIDE 3] Securing the relevance of funding is a priority. The current crisis shows that there are reasons to build a financial system that is sufficiently resilient to shocks, whose transmission mechanisms are limited to states and which, through its actions, supports the effective allocation of the ssoms even in worse economic times. In order to achieve this, the supervision and supervision of financial institutions will be tightened and the stability of financial systems will be improved and the impact of future financial institutions on the financial system and the real economy will be mitigated. The number of sclerical projects is significant. In mid-month, the European Commission unveiled its long-awaited proposal for a directive on bank crisis management and restructuring of banks (EU framework for bank recovery and resolution). The fundamental aim of the reform is to ensure that even the largest banks facing a crisis can, if necessary, be closed down or restructured without unjustifiable costs for taxpayers. In addition to banks, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision is in the process of extending the systemic institution to cover the insurance company (SII). The authorities are trying to alleviate the problems associated with systemically significant banks with more stringent requirements than are commonly imposed on banks. The expansions include, for example, the ability of a hedged bank to provide simple risk management services to its customers. At the beginning of the year, the question of the structure of the banking sector also came up on the agenda of the European Union. ECONOMY NATIONAL SECURITY NdbK... ANGLE Economic stability and security go hand in hand. Economic stability includes issues such as sound public finances, price stability and stable performance financial market. Of course, there is much more to it than that, such as a high level of employment and adequate social safety nets. Economic In order to achieve stability, it is necessary to have confidence, predictability and stable political conditions. Safety, on the other hand, includes: ? that citizens may live freely and without fear; ? that they do not need to fear external threats, terrorism and crime, and ? that preparations have been made for major accidents or natural disasters. In the welfare state, people's security has been strengthened by creating social safety nets, in case of accidents, illness and other situations. Economic stability can be lost in many autumns. The cause may be external or sissy-born. The external cause may be a collapse in world trade, a crisis, a natural disaster or something else that cannot be influenced by one's own economic or other policies. In many cases, economic stability has been lost through sissy. There can be many reasons, such as mismanagement, support for certain special groups, or just a lack of long-termism. Conflicts of interest or weakened trust in political institutions and in the institutions of society have exacerbated the situation. An economy at the bottom of the economy provides security. This is the case for every person and company. The same applies to the States, although the situation is different in some respects from that of private operators. The state is eternal in every autumn, so that in september it can keep up with its debt forever. The prerequisite is that the economy grows. The tendency to increase debt arises from the fact that, politically, it is always easier to increase expenditure than to reduce it and reduce taxes than to raise it. In order to finance wars, n?in has often been done. Finland also has experience. As a result of the Crimean War, Ven?j? had to resort to banknote financing, as a result of which the exchangeability of the ruble for silver had to be abolished. The confusion of monetary conditions made Finland's trade relations with its traditional trading partners Sweden and northern Germany more difficult. The quest for monetary stability gave rise to a process as a result of which Finland in 1860 received its own currency, the mark, which in November 1865 was linked to the silver standard. An interesting detail is that the silver value of the French franc, 4 . grams of silver, coincidentally, was exactly the same as the mark. Sovereignty implies the right to tax, the right to print one's own money and the right to declare war. Kun vuoden Lehman Brothersin konkurssin jlkeen maailmankauppa supistui ja investoinnit pyshtyivt, Suomen kokonaistuotanto putosi vuonna 2009 yli kahdeksan prosenttia. Tappiopuskureiden ja alhaisten korkojen ansiosta yksityinen kulutus notkahti ja tyllisyys heikkeni vain lievsti. Verotulojen alenemisen vuoksi tappiopuskureita ei ole viel kyetty nostamaan entiselle tasolleen. Siit syyst Suomi on nyt paljon haavoittuvampi vastaavansuuruiselle uudelle hirille. Euroopan valtionvelkakriisin patoaminen ja luottamuskriisin pysyttminen on siit syyst suomalaisille veronmaksajille rimmisen trke. Ennen muuta pidettv huolta, ett taloudellista vakautta ei omilla toimilla tuhota. Bank of Finland (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tag=Bank of Finland)

Title: Finland's Economy and Future in a Changing Europe seminar
text: Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen: Finland's economy and future in a changing Europe seminar, Raahe 12.12.2012 . Speech . Friday 21 December 2012, 2:00 PM Ladies and gentlemen, I will focus on the market situation and the international economy first. After that, I will share my thoughts with you on the state of the Finnish economy and the challenges of the lshi years. Let's set aside time for questions and discussion. [Figure 2] The financial crisis has dragged on the long-term economy. The international economy is still struggling with the consequences of the financial crisis. The crisis was preceded by strong debt-driven growth and an increase in balances. It is now a matter of digesting debt and balances, which is a slow process. Experience shows that a financial crisis typically follows a long period of subdued economic activity. Nsin is ksymssss tsllskin times. The crisis has led to the economic growth of the long-term developed economies. The figure shows the development of gdp in different countries since 2008. In many emerging economies, the crisis has been overcome considerably. Nsin is e.g. in China. In the United States, the level of production surpassed its pre-crisis level last year. In the euro area and Japan, GDP is still around 2.5% below its pre-crisis level. In Finland, the economic drop is large, and total output in Finland is still significantly lower than before the financial crisis. The current economic crisis has been going on for 5 years now. On the basis of historical experience, it is possible that we are only halfway through the crisis. [Figure 3] The large price volatility experienced in the financial markets in recent years has been indicative of investors' confidence. Compared with the last summer, the stock market situation has changed in a brighter and more stable direction, and there have been cautious signs of the security of the stock market. [Figure 4] In addition, there have been cautiously positive signs in the national bond market, for example in the sovereign bond market. For example, the spreads between Spanish and Italian government bonds against Germany have fallen. Interest rates on Finnish government bonds have held up well with german interest rates. The difference has remained at only a few tenths of a point. This reflects the strong confidence of the markets in the Finnish economy. Confidence in the good management of the economy is of paramount importance to public finances. One per cent of the interest rate would mean an additional cost of one billion euros. [Figure 5] However, the cautious optimism of the financial markets has not, at least not yet, been much in line with the indicators of the real economy. In particular, indicator data for industrial production and world trade point to a weak situation towards the end of the year. Purchasing indices point to a further contraction in industrial output, particularly in Japan and the euro area [Figure 6] Growth forecasts in key economic areas have been revised for the worse - more recent forecast is, it's going to be worse next year. In crisis, therefore, the recovery has been epstasaic and fragile. At the beginning of the year, sentiment in the international economy improved. In late spring, however, the nittyms have become gloomier. Growth forecasts have been revised in a bad direction. This has partly reflected the problems of the European economy. In addition, growth in the USA and China, for example, has become more reliable than before. On the other hand, inflation forecasts for next year have remained fairly stable. For its part, it shows that there is a high level of confidence in the actions of central banks even during the crisis. Ladies and gentlemen, I am now bringing you from the international economy to the situation in Finland. Finland's real GDP growth has slowed down strongly during 2012. In the third quarter of the year, GDP was more than 1% lower than a year earlier. Indeed, economic growth has been at a standstill in the middle of the year. The development of exports has been weak and the growth of industrial production has been at a halt for two years now. The value of exports is still about 15% lower than just before the financial crisis. Finnish exports have weakened the impact of international economic development on the Finnish export market. This is also due to the specific problems of the electronics industry and the paper industry, as well as the weakened cost competitiveness of Finnish industry. Business cyclical expectations have continued to darken in recent months. Order backlogs have weakened and production expectations for the shia times are more cautious than before. Economic growth is also held back by the slowdown in domestic demand. Construction has slowed down and the growth of household consumption has slowed down. Indeed, consumer confidence in the state of the economy has weakened during the autumn. The rapid decline in economic growth has begun in the nskys also market. The trend of the tysllis msss has probably declined during the current autumn and the employment rate has increased. The employment rate was 7.9% in October. The increase in employment has been particularly affected by the fact that periods of employment have been registered during the autumn as in the past. [Figure 8] The slowdown in economic growth is in the coffers of the state. The growth in tax revenues stopped in the early summer. In particular, the accrual of the joint tax has been weak in the year. Substantial tax increases in 2011 and 2012 d in total around 2 billion d have not even raised revenues to levels prior to the financial crisis. What makes the situation worrying is that government expenditure has continued to grow at a rate of between 5% and 6%. The government's revenue has now risen by 6.5 billion. to the euro, up from 2 billion at the beginning of the year. euros lower. However, the situation of public finances is better than in 2009 and 2010, and the adjustment measures made will improve the situation. However, they do not change trends in revenue and expenditure. The financial situation of municipalities is similar: according to the Tax Administration's data, the growth in municipalities' tax revenues has stopped. The municipalities are therefore financing their expenditure at a time when they are increasing their debt. Deteriorating economic growth and budgetary imbalances pose major challenges to economic development over the past few years. Let's move on to the structural challenges facing the Finnish economy. [Figure 9] Last year, the current account was lower than in 1993. In 2011, alijsmss accumulated 3.1 billion. EUR, or 1.6% of GDP. In 2002 and 2011, the current account balance deteriorated by around 10% to one per cent of GDP. The current account deficit means that the total expenditure of the national economy is greater than income. Thus, the national economy becomes indebted to the rest of the world on a net basis. [Figure 10] In addition to public finances, households are also getting into debt. The picture shows how the strength of demand in households has prolonged economic growth in recent years. When interest rates have been low, households have been prepared to increase their debt burden. The expenditure of Finnish households has been higher than their income. This is exceptional in international comparisons. Since the onset of the financial crisis, households in Finland have continued to spend and invest more in housing than their income. Households' debt has continued to grow. In the euro area, average household debt growth has decelerated markedly. It is, of course, a good thing that the activities of the financial system in Finland are not seriously affected and that the activities of households are not seriously affected. the economic situation has allowed debt to increase. At the same time, however, there is a risk that household income will be based on over-optimistic expectations for the future. At the same time, the growth in households' expenditure relative to their income has contributed to the fact that Finland's current account fell short last year. [Figure 11] In addition to household indebtedness, the current account development is affected by export developments. Among the main export sectors, the development of exports from the forest and electronics industries has been weak since the turn of the millennium. Their share of total production has decreased. At the same time, the value of their exports has decreased. [Figure 12] The current account has also been weakened by the weakening of the terms of trade. This means that the prices of imported products have risen in relation to the prices of exported products. The weakening of Finland's terms of trade has been exceptional in international comparisons. Import prices have been pushed up by higher prices of energy and other raw materials. Export price developments, on the other hand, have been subdued for paper products, especially electronic products. The fall in export prices in the electronics industry is a consequence of the way in which price statistics take account of improvements in product characteristics. When product characteristics improve, it nskyy as a decrease in the price index. Nsin ksy, even if the price of one of the average products sold remains unchanged. The price indices are therefore o qualitycorrectedo. At the same time, the decrease in price indices means that, in the statistics, the volume of exports, i.e. the value of exports, increases in relation to the value of exports. This has implications for the development of exports and GDP, as well as for the international comparison of cost competitiveness. [Figure 13] Dear listeners, in my speech I have cited the cause of the deterioration of the current account. The reasons for this are: Problems in the paper and electronics industry . Energy dependence and rising price of sljy . Recent strength of household consumption and housing investment relative to income . In addition, the current account is affected by the deficit of public finances and the deterioration of cost competitiveness, which is further affected by the current account. On the other hand, it should be noted that the current account structure is not the cause of the deterioration of the current account. Its , finland would continue to sssstss for the large classes of iksksization, which in turn would be the most important account in the current account. According to current forecasts, the current account balance will remain slightly undersized for years. [Figure 14] Indeed, the deterioration of the current account has been due, among other factors, to a decline in competitiveness. The volume of production in the Finnish manufacturing industry has grown rapidly in relation to many other countries. This has meant a rapid increase in productivity. However, the development of the value of output has been considerably weaker, as the price development has been epsedull. The loss of the terms of trade mentioned above is the weakening of the terms of trade. Cost competitiveness is often measured by individual costs. In the case of Finland, however, their development also gives an illusory picture of the development of cost competitiveness. This is precisely due to the deterioration of the terms of trade. The favourable development of individual costs in the Finnish manufacturing sector is counterproductive when you look at how much labour costs have risen in relation to the value of production. This means that the profitability of industrial enterprises has declined in relation to the average of its competitors. [Figure 15] The question you have in mind is whether the current account deficit is a problem for an economy such as Finland' s. It is a problem if it significantly increases the risks associated with the availability and conditions of financing for the national economy and/or is the result of balanced domestic economic development. The small deficit of Finland's current account is not an acute problem, at least not yet, because foreign financing has not become more difficult. However, debt-driven economic development is not balanced over a long period of time. Dependence on external funding increases vulnerability. There are lessons to be learned from the financial crisis: indebtedness and loss of cost competitiveness lead to deadlock. Economic growth based on household and public debt is not sustainable in a situation where, in order to prepare for the indebtedness of households and the public sector, it would be justified for the future. [Figure 16] Good ladies and gentlemen, When external balance is a problem, what is the point of doing? The balanced development of the economy as a whole requires action in a number of areas. Household indebtedness can be brought under control, for example, by further reducing the right to tax on mortgage interest and by steering the activities of the financing system, e.g. by making it possible to limit the loan-to-value ratio of mortgages. In addition, public deficits will be reduced and cost competitiveness must be improved. Coordination of wage formation should be brought to the level of the economy as a whole. At the same time, promoting local flexibility in wage formation supports both competitiveness and the adaptation of the economy to changing circumstances.
