Title: Opening of the Stock Exchange in Helsinki 100 Years exhibition
text: Vice Chairman of the Board Pentti Hakkarainen: Opening of the shrssi Helsingisss 100 years conference 29.1.2013 . Speech . Tuesday 29January2013,10:00AM Psrsi Helsingisss 100 years -nsyttely opening 29.1.2013 Bank of Finland Monetary Museum WHERE ARE OUR PMYMARKETS GOING? Dear listeners, the monetary museum's now-opening nsyttelysss will present the centenary activities of the Psrssi in Helsinki. At the start of Psrssi's operations, the acquisition of shares played a significant role. Times have changed and in recent years the role of psrss as a procurement channel for pssoms is d only spatially d vsshended, but its role in the vslittsjsns of information is tsrkes. However, in the midst of the tightening of the financial markets, there are now reasons to ask whether the bush will return to its roots? In my opening remarks, I will share some of my thoughts on the situation in the local market, on the needs and opportunities for development. A well-sound banking system and a well-functioning local market and marketplace support the operating conditions for companies and the financial management of private individuals. This will improve the competitiveness of the economy. From the nsks angle of companies, they provide opportunities for the acquisition of both equity and foreign pssoma, i.e. debt financing. The local market allocates investment assets to profitable investments. It also serves as a measure of economic performance and growth expectations, as well as information. ENSURING A COMPETITIVE MARKETPLACE The trend in the domestic stock market has been subdued, e.g. trading has contracted and the number of listed companies has decreased. However, the situation in our securities markets is not at all unhappy. There are no reasons to ring death knells, even though there are threats of decline in development. Competition from trading venues for the most traded shares has intensified significantly. In addition to the cost of trade, there is competition for the speed of trade. Approximately one third of the trading volumes of the most liquid shares in the Helsinki Psrss have moved to multilateral trading venues (MTF) outside the market. Helsinki's pocket list has become shorter, and the mssrs of the money sought from the primary market is vshsinen. Institutional investors, such as investment funds or financial institutions, have diversified their investments globally and the debt financing of Finnish companies is acquired in addition to the international financing of the company. Domestic small investors are active, but their demand alone is not enough to keep up with the market. There are threats in the development process and without measures affecting development, the Finnish marketplace will wither away. From the point of view of economic growth and otherwise developing society, the marketplace will become vibrant and competitive. Since the size of the national economy or our location does not provide a natural basis for growth, special care must be taken to ensure the operating conditions of the marketplace. This development can be based on the competitive advantages that the marketplace has. Our competitive advantages include competitive trade systems and an extensive network of cooperation. In addition, Finland has leading companies and special expertise in several industries, even from an international point of view. Knowledge of these industries and good analysis will bring an advantage to our local market that we will be able to increase. It is crucial for the future of the Finnish equity and debt market that companies and the public sector act as issuers of securities domestically. Securities can be offered on the international market, but also to domestic investors and sssstsj. A marketplace, be it a marketplace or a marketplace or method of trading promissory notes, must be adequately marketed. If the current trend continues, there is a risk that the trade will move more away from Finland. If the marketplace is abroad, even if only in another Nordic country, it becomes more difficult for all companies d and in particular small and medium-sized enterprises d to acquire their own and foreign assets. As far as taxation is concerned, I do not intend to discuss it more than by stating that taxes relating to investment or trade must not differ from other countries. With more severe taxation, the trade will move elsewhere and the marketplace Helsinki will become more attractive. PRIORITY MARKETS FOR CORPORATE d INCLUDING SME d BONDS The Helsinki Psrssi has been looking for ways to facilitate the listing of new companies. They have not yet taken fire. The local market for growth companies will continue to receive attention to enable psssy. This is an excellent opportunity for broad cooperation in order to develop the domestic market. Companies need a market where, regardless of size, they can obtain not only equity, but also foreign financing on a larger scale than is currently the case. One possibility would be a debt market for small and medium-sized enterprises, such as the First North list, also in Finland. TIGHTENING OF BANK LOAN TERMS CREATES AN OPPORTUNITY The increased financing costs of banks and the challenges to the profitability of their business at low interest rates have weakened the conditions of corporate loans offered by banks. It stresses the importance of a well-functioning financial market for the financial management of companies. The deterioration in the availability and conditions of a bank loan is likely to change the behaviour of both lenders and borrowers, such as the functioning of the domestic market. There is a growing need to raise a larger share of financing on the financial and domestic markets. LAINSDNT... IMPACT OF PROJECTS Efforts by the various market participants are also needed, for example, to develop multi-tiered management of securities. Nsms so-called. issues relating to nominee registration should be resolved in such a way as to safeguard the competitiveness of our securities markets and the access of the various authorities. Nsin has been made elsewhere as well, and examples of workable solutions are lacking. When entering the nominee register, care must also be taken to ensure that issuers and companies have access to information. Their investor relations and disclosure obligations for investors are required to have a good system for identifying and knowing the shareholders. FINALLY To sum up, Finnish and especially growth-oriented companies need a functioning and reliable financial and financial market in their home countries for their operations. It is not only tax-related means that are being developed. When looking for them, it is necessary to take into account both the primary and secondary markets. Encouraging and increasing domestic ownership would be one of the ways in which the possible use should be considered. In the case of institutional investors, this is done in the right way, taking into account the totality of the business; all the risks, costs and hustle and bustle. Now is an opportunity that should not be missed. Bank of Finland (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tagBank of Finland)

Pentti Hakkarainen brought owhere banks will be needed in the future? Under the heading o, the speech highlights the importance of the financial markets and banks in order to ensure that the latest years have shown that the national authorities should have sufficient resources to intervene in the activities of financial markets and banks in order to ensure that they are in the early stages of these developments. o Lessons have been learned from the financial crisis that it is necessary to strengthen the use of the authorities in order to prejudge the risks d the system of risks that threaten the stability of the entire financial system d system. The Bank of Finland will continue to provide macroprudents such as the loan ceiling and the system risk buffer is made available to the authorities as a tysytetsv in the tyskalupakki. Capacities must be created now before there is a worse time. In his speech, Hakkarainen stated the following: oAlthough there is no need for macroprudential funds in Finland right now, and the financial sector is also in good shape, it is justified to create capabilities in time. Title: The wheels of the world are spinning, is Yl-Savo grinding? Party speech at the 61st Annual Meeting of the European Parliament and of the Council of Yl-Savo Provincial Festival
text: Vice Chairman of the Board Pentti Hakkarainen: The wheels of the world pysrivst, is Yls-Savo grinding? Keynote speech 61. Yls-Savo Provincial Festival, Iisalmi 30.6.2013 . Speech . Sunday 30 June 2013, 4:00 PM Vice Chairman of the Board Pentti Hakkarainen: The wheels of the world pysrivst, is Yls-Savo grinding? Yls-Savo Provincial Festival 30.6.2013 Good ladies and gentlemen, It is a pleasure to participate in traditional provincial celebrations and a speech. Although the celebration is local, it also gives those living elsewhere the opportunity to participate in the discussion of provincial issues. In my speech, I will therefore look at the issues of the region from two nsks angles; whether Yls-Savo is grinding in the wheels of the world and European economy, as well as how and when it comes to psrjsch. To both of these big questions I bring nskemyksis and wishes. The economic shocks naturally come from my current state of affairs, while the hysdynchy of the region's strengths and the ideas of improving the current situation are based on my roots and my close relationship with Yls-Savo, its businesses and its inhabitants. I presented my thoughts outside of the party-political and value choices of the Chels; the same who does, as long as things get done. It should be noted that the final answers and the actual actions are those of you, the good people present, and that they are the ones who are there. We need to build a future for future generations. At the outset, before the topics, I would like to express my thanks to all the organizers of the event d you have done an excellent job. Special recognition should be given to Leo Puurunen and hsnen tysryhmsnss, who have edited the work celebrating the 60th anniversary of the Yls-Savo Provincial Festival, which I have had the pleasure of receiving fresh. Kssills on olainattu aikao In midsummer, I was in Basel, Switzerland, at the annual meeting of the Kansainvslisen jsestelybank BIS. According to its analyses, the international economy is weakening. China's economic growth, which remains strong, is slowing down. In the United States, the expected acceleration in growth has been delayed and has proved to be weaker than expected. In Japan, the new monetary policy stance pushed up the exchange rates, but has not stimulated the real economy. In Europe, the economy will contract in this year, and next year it will not get much stronger. The BIS describes the economic situation in such a way that it is now a borrowed periodo, when the measures required for economic growth must be taken. Central banks have ensured the functioning of the financial system through massive operations. The governments of many countries have taken strong steps to rebalance their economies. Credit must also be paid to the countries of Etels Europe, which are in financial difficulties and where clarity has been achieved. But the work continues, the problems are not over. We have the opportunity to psrjsch even in poor export demand The Finnish economy has been weak for five years now, and the stalemate of the shi years has been weak. The economic problems caused by the recent cyclical changes have proved to be more persistent and structural than expected. The state of the international economy has reduced export opportunities. Export success is also weighed down by our own efforts, which have eroded our competitiveness, as well as the structural problems faced by the paper and electronics industries. As an example of Finland's weak export situation, the value of Finnish exports is still just over 12% below the 2007 level, while the exports of Spain and Ireland, known as crisis countries, have already risen by the same amount above the 2007 level. With this expenditure, Finland will soon be a long-term crisis country. The slowdown in exports has been somewhat hidden, as household consumption has increased in the growth figures of the national economy and the public sector has increased its expenditure. One of the problems is that domestic demand is financed by debt. Growth built on indebtedness has no underlying economic basis. Further indebtedness is likely to slow down economic growth in the future. To sum up, two major factors in particular have contributed to this development: the change in the productive structure of the economy and the protracted period of the financial crisis. They have put our economy in a very difficult situation. Finland is a small country in the entire global economy. However, when our exports are directed around the world, we have a chance to keep up with poor export demand, as long as we manage our competitiveness. Contributions to the whole region Similarly, the development of the surrounding world treats Yls-Savo. That too, when we take care of the competitiveness of the region. There are two subdivisions of Chechnya; industry and the public sector. Yls-Savo's traditional strength has been its economic and public sector cooperation in regional development. Yls-Savo has previously been involved in this kind of joint effort throughout the country, as the representatives of the Association of Finnish Local and Regional Authorities, the Finland Chamber of Commerce and several ministers, among others, have stated in various contexts. Over the past decades, a good foundation has been laid for business success. Indeed, even on a global scale, it is a number of first-class companies. A vibrant industry and strong companies have provided opportunities for a wide range of public services. In ensuring the operating conditions for economic activities, it should be borne in mind that the entire public sector and all municipal costs are ultimately borne solely and exclusively by private sector operators; enterprises, entrepreneurs and selfemployed persons. It is the case that there is not enough concern about public sector costs. It is thought that the money always comes from somewhere else. It is not. Only regionally profitable economic activities can bear the costs of municipalities in a sustainable way. The success of the economic sector in Yls-Savo has not been fruitful and the results have not been achieved in the public sector. Although efforts have been made, there still seems to be hope that it will be time to deal with the problems. Unfortunately, this kind of thinking is giving local push-making away to outsiders altogether. The restructuring of Chelschi would only take place under duress and by measures planned by others. The responsibility for getting things done on time is the responsibility of the present day. If you do not act yourself and in time, there is a risk of a double problem. First of all, the cooperation between the municipalities in the region would be directed from elsewhere, and then the people in the area would not be asked how and how public services are provided. Schools, hospitals, cultural services and many other services for each of us are provided elsewhere. Secondly, the inefficient public sector increases the cargo of enterprises, entrepreneurs and the self-employed. Such a deterioration in the operating conditions will take economic activity elsewhere and thus weaken the region's employment, tax revenues and services. Now is the time, in the spirit of the provincial festival, to make a contribution to the cooperation of the whole region. Blowing on the common coals of the municipalities will strengthen the region, regardless of where the conditions of the future lie. A combination of municipal forces as such is not enough, but there is still a need for good cooperation between enterprises and between enterprises, municipalities and educational institutions located in the region. WHY BANKS SNNELLN? Banks are heavily criticised and sensitive. They play a key role in the functioning of the economy and therefore there are reasons for their activity. The key issue is whether financial activities are more important than other business activities. If it is necessary to do so, then the question is how. The strengthening of the financial sector's shilling and supervision is a debate for and against. The German Finance Minister, Wolfgang Schsuble, has stated that it is necessary to stress to the management of the banks that financial institutions are for society, not otherwise. The financial crisis clearly demonstrated the need to tighten up the banks' spending. Why, however, is there opposition? The function of financial institutions in society is tsrkes. Banks lend and invest the funds of their depositors and financiers. They select investment and investment targets on behalf of the Ssssssj and, most recently, on behalf of society as a whole. Success is a prerequisite for economic prosperity, renewal and growth. Thanks to banking, the funds of individual companies can be withdrawn, even if the bank lends and invests funds in long-term objects. Tsms is the ssrimmsisen tsrkess for the establishment of trust in banks. The activities of financial institutions always involve risks. They are prepared for with liquidity reserves and solvency. However, the liquidity reserves of financial institutions and their own resources in relation to their total assets are relatively small. That, too, is part of the nature of the activity. The financial crisis we experienced showed how well-functioning the financial system is. Likewise, it is nshty how widespread even small hsirist in the financial world can have an impact. If a financial institution fails, the damage to customers will be significant. In addition, the damage is easily multiplied and spreads beyond its own clientele to society as a whole. The spread of crises may be sufficient simply to ensure that financial institutions are connected. Among market participants, depositors and creditors, the impact can spread worldwide in minutes. It has been learned from the past that customer supervision, market discipline and self-discipline are not sufficient to ensure the functioning of the financing system. In addition, the authorities, whose job it is to represent the whole corner of society, must take part in ensuring the reliable conditions for the functioning of financial institutions and financial markets. MILL RAHOITUSLAITOKSIA SNNELLN? Firstly, a licence is required to set up a bank, for example. Secondly, it is ensured that authorised financial institutions conduct their business without jeopardising the stability of the financial system. This applies to the scope of operations, the required solvency, risk management methods and the information to be reported to supervisors and markets. Thirdly, by supervising financial institutions, they are guaranteed that they operate in accordance with the rules of procedure and the generally agreed rules of play. The four-year-old means is crisis management, which ensures the functioning of core functions, deposits and payments systems in the event of a crisis situation and minimises the impact of a crisis situation on the financial system and society. The normal liquidation and bankruptcy procedure in the case of financial institutions is far too slow a road, due to the specific nature of their activities. The objectives of this process can be summarised in two key points. Firstly, the aim is to reduce the likelihood of financial crises and their social costs. Secondly, the aim of the social support network is to ensure that the banking system can effectively carry out the social function. WITH PANKKIUNIONI TUO? The crisis revealed weaknesses in the banking sector, as well as in the case of individual banks and in the banking system as a whole. It revealed how interconnected the different actors are. In a highly international banking sector, the problem of an individual bank can quickly catch on with other banks across borders and across borders. There is no going back to the banking sector at national level. Banks and their international business and integrated financial markets are the basis of today's economy. The single monetary policy, integrated financial markets and the effective functioning of banks require the same level of financial supervision and resolution. National supervision is not sufficient to supervise banks. National resolution is not capable of resolving the crisis situations of international banks. A single monetary policy is not the key to cleaning up the problems of individual countries facing banking or economic crises. The euro area crisis countries, in particular, have been struggling with the fate of banks and governments. Problems in the banking sector have put a strain on public finances, and fiscal problems in the country have made it difficult for banks to play a role, especially in raising funds. The affiliation between the Bank and its home country has led, at worst, to the osysksy spiralo. The financial markets are congruent and international. All banks - even domestic ones - operate in the nsills market. However, supervision, including the activities of the authorities, has become national. Since then, it has followed the development that has taken place in the financial markets. Now the sts sth The banking union is a response to the supervision and resolution required of the actual business activities of banks. When financial institutions operate internationally, their supervision and crisis resolution must also be at the same international level. In the banking union, a bank's problems can be dealt with by supervisory and resolution authorities without running into difficulties in the home country. Similarly, problems in the bank's home country do not put the bank in trouble when it is supranationally supervised. WHAT DOES THE BANKING UNION CONSIST OF? The functioning of the banking union is based on a common charter. It creates uniform requirements for all EU countries and a control system. The two key pillars of the banking union are single banking supervision and single resolution. Supervision will be attached to the European Central Bank (ECB). Agreement on the creation of a single resolution mechanism has been reached between the European Parliament, the Commission and the Member States. The common deposit guarantee scheme is not in the vslttsmssn stage. The national deposit guarantee scheme will first be harmonised and, in due course, the common deposit guarantee scheme will be considered. The banking union will reduce the likelihood that banks will run into problems. In addition, in the event of a bank's problems with the owners, investors are also responsible for covering the losses. In this way, the need for public bank support, as is familiar from economic history, is eliminated, or at least limited, and significantly reduced. SINGLE BANKING SUPERVISION MECHANISM In mid-2012, the European Council decided to transfer the responsibility for supervising banks to the ECB. The regulation on the SSM entered into force in November 2013 and, following the postponement period, the ECB will start supervision on 4 November 2014. The ECB directly supervises the largest banks, but the ECB also supervises supervisors and instructs all banks to be supervised in the same way, regardless of the country in which they are located. If necessary, the ECB can directly take over any bank in the euro area. The important aspect of the transition is a comprehensive assessment to ensure that the ECB starts its work as a supervisory authority from opuhta. A comprehensive assessment provides a clear and comparable picture of banks' overall risks. The comprehensive assessment is, as the name implies, comprehensive. This is where the common methods of the balance sheet risks are examined, and there are also external, independent experts. Since then, each bank's riskiest receivables will be receivable. The scope of the audit is wide. A total of 128 banks are estimated to have a total risk-weighted exposure of 58 % of the total risk-weighted exposures in their credit portfolios. In total, some 135,000 loans are audited under the strict guidance of the ECB. The ECB is the supervisory authority which competently requires the implementation of this assessment. KRIISINRATKAISU In the future, the work of bank resolution will consist of two parts: the national powers under the Recovery and Resolution Directive and the collective resolution mechanism at EU level. In many Member States, they make it possible to close down even a large bank in an orderly manner without causing the financial markets to do so. This is a significant step forward in the past. Without resolution, banks in trouble were declared bankrupt or bailed out with state funds in the absence of a private sector solution. The recovery and crisis response directive will create the same levels in all EU countries for early entry, orderly reorganisation or closure of a problem bank. Investor responsibility is a significant new tool that will be introduced in all EU countries from the beginning of 2016. The responsibility of the industry in the form of a fund also creates a buffer ahead of public funds. A single resolution mechanism at EU level enables the orderly, rapid and efficient reorganisation or winding-down of even a supranational bank. In the common mechanism, the ECB, in its capacity as supervisor, determines whether a bank is failing or likely to fail and thus the need to move to resolution. Resolution decisions, on the other hand, are made by the Single Mechanism's Resolution Board, which is confirmed by the Commission. In resolution, the pssssssnssns is the implementation of investor responsibility. The responsibility of the industry takes the form of a common fund. In order to ensure the resources for resolution, a common fund will be established within 8 years. WHO' S WHO... HAPPY ABOUT THE BANKING UNION? The banking union directly and vis-a-vis society, banks and customers; companies and individuals. The banking union will promote competition and the operating conditions of banks. Banks across Europe are on the same level of supervision. Even in a region as integrated as the Nordic countries, there have been differences in control. Uniform supervision also brings a longer period of time to the administrative costs of banks. It harmonises transactions with the supervisor and, among other things, the need to report to the authorities of different countries. Although the net impact of the banking union on banks' own financing costs is difficult to accurately assess, the improved credibility of supervision, the clarity of resolution and wider resources are likely to have a negative impact on financing costs. The strengthening of confidence may increase investor interest in banks in the countries participating in the banking union. The comprehensive assessment of The Single Supervisory Authority (SSM), which is currently under discussion, will improve confidence by separating the common chaff. As a result, the position of the banks that have done their job well will be improved. Many of the issues of common supervision and resolution also arise in the context of the common supervision and resolution. Even if there are no problems in the bank's home country, it is essential that joint supervision and resolution can ensure that the problems spread over the countries. As the problems of an individual bank in country A do not escalate into a crisis in the banking sector as a whole, the banks of country B will also be affected. In addition, there are adverse effects on the real economy. This is also in Finland's interest because of the structure and openness of our economy. The basic principle of common resolution is that, in addition to the owners of a problem bank, creditors also bear the costs of resolution. When bank owners and creditors know their responsibilities, they have incentives to take better care of their own interests. They closely monitor and evaluate the bank's activities. In addition, monitoring can be an oversized risk-taking on the part of the bank. Banks bear the costs of single resolution secondarily also as an industry. This is done through the Single Resolution Fund. Despite the contributions, the fund is used jointly by banks in individual countries. Firstly, the common fund is an essential element in ensuring the swift operation of the single resolution and thus preventing the spread of crises in the countries. Secondly, the common fund will encourage banks to monitor each other more, i.e. the activities of other banks. In addition, a common fund throughout the banking union can be used to share the risk that the resolution of one bank entails for other banks. In a country in particular, the resolution of even one large bank could entail high costs for the industry if it had to be borne by the country's own banks. The Resolution Fund ensures an efficient procedure for settling a bank that has run into problems. The aim is not to siphon or support an unviable bank, but to ensure sufficient resources for a controlled liquidation or winding-down process. As an open economy, Finland is vulnerable to Hsirish from outside the country's borders. Finland's advantage in the banking union is that we are involved in the drafting of the stss, in which the psstess on the supervision of European banks, ensuring consistency and equal treatment of banks' supervision and, in the event of problems, their resolution. When talking about hysdys, one should not forget the customer of the bank. Also in the banking union, depositors will continue to be confident that their money is safe in well-supervised banks. And in ssriolos, which are always possible, the banking union ensures the functioning of banking services for society, the company and private individuals. To sum up, the banking union is one of the most important steps in the European Union since the establishment of monetary union and has progressed very quickly. Firstly, in the banking union, supervision and control correspond to the true nature of banks and financial markets, to the cross-border functioning of banks and financial markets. Secondly, its banks also enjoy more uniform operating and competitive conditions in Europe, regardless of the bank's country of origin. Thirdly, the position of the bank's customers will be strengthened under normal circumstances, but above all, the availability of life-long financial services will be ensured in ssriolo. For the fourth time, and one of the most important arguments, the banking union can help to reduce or reduce the potential problems of banking for society. banks (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tagbanks)

MIKSI PANKKEJA SNNELLN? Pankkeja arvostellaan paljon ja herksti. Niill on keskeinen rooli talouden toiminnassa ja siksi niiden toimintaa on syyt snnell. Keskeinen kysymys on, pitk rahoitustoimintaa snnell enemmn kuin muuta yritystoimintaa. Jos tm on tarpeen, niin kysymys on miten. Jos rahoituslaitos kaatuu, vahingot asiakkaille ovat merkittvt. Lisksi vahingot kertautuvat helposti ja levivt sen omaa asiakaskuntaa laajemmalle koko yhteiskuntaan. MILL RAHOITUSLAITOKSIA SNNELLN? Ensinnkin tarvitaan toimilupa, ett voidaan esimerkiksi perustaa pankki. Toiseksi sntelyll varmistetaan, ett toimiluvan saaneet rahoituslaitokset hoitavat liiketoimintaansa vaarantamatta rahoitusjrjestelmn vakautta. Neljs keino on kriisinhallinta, jolla varmistetaan ydintoimintojen, talletusten ja maksujrjestelmn toimivuus hiritilanteessa ja minimoidaan kriisitilanteen vaikutuksia rahoitusjrjestelmn ja yhteiskuntaan. Title: Financial stability and national security
text: Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen: Economic stability and national security. Helsinki, 6.5.2014. . Speech . Tuesday 6 May 2014, 11:00 AM Pentti Hakkarainen Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors Speech at the opening ceremony of the 45th special course of the National Defence Courses in Helsinki on 6.5.2014. ECONOMIC STABILITY AND NATIONAL SECURITY Economic stability includes issues such as sound public finances, price stability and sound financial markets. Of course, there is much more to it than that, such as a high level of employment and adequate social safety nets. Maintaining economic stability requires confidence, predictability and stable political conditions. National security, on the other hand, means that citizens can live freely and without fear, that they fear an external threat, terrorism or crime, and that preparations are made for major accidents or natural disasters. In the welfare state, people's safety has been strengthened by creating social safety nets in the event of accidents, accidents, illness and other situations. Economic stability can be lost in many autumns. The cause may be external or sissy-born. The external cause may be a geopolitical crisis, a collapse in world trade, a sljy crisis, a natural disaster or something else that cannot be influenced by one's own economic or other policies. There is a great deal of experience of the loss of financial stability since sissy, some of them quite recent. There can be many reasons, such as mismanagement, support for certain special groups, or just a lack of long-termism. Nsin has been driven into excessive government indebtedness, high inflation or, through the banking crisis, the collapse of the real economy. Conflicts of interest or weakened trust in political institutions and in the institutions of society have exacerbated the situation. An economy at the bottom of the economy provides security. This is the case for every individual and company. The same applies to the States, although the situation is different in some respects from that of private operators. In former times, economic interests and politico-military interests ran through kssi ksdesss. Before the first world war, world trade and social movements were free. However, the Czech freedom was restricted by d at least from the nskskulma of small countries d the aspiration of the large states to hegemony, as well as in the economic and political spheres. During the wars, protectionism was imposed as a result of the Great Depression. Nationalism and the closure of borders led to hatred with notorious consequences. The post-World War II period differs from the previous eras in that there were now functioning international institutions. On the international political side, the United Nations has managed to delineate conflicts in a completely different way than the League of Nations did at the time. In economic policy, the Imf has played an important role in the international monetary system. A number of other international organisations, such as the World Bank, the World Trade Council and the OECD, have also been involved in promoting international coordination in the field of economic policy. Although there have been disagreements, and although progress has been painfully slow on some issues, there is good reason why coordination and cooperation within the framework of international institutions have kept the world economy together. Although the aim has been economic stability and development, they have at the same time contributed to world peace. The collapse of communism and the end of the cold war had unpredictable consequences for the world economy. In a very short period of time, between 2 and 3 billion people came to open world trade. Adaptation to the change in comparative advantages expanded world trade, changed trade flows and ownership structures. At the same time, a rapid change in information technology was experienced. Together, these factors also changed business models in such a way that the link between production activities and the nationality of the company was weakened. sms has led to the interdependence of states and enterprises. The interests of companies and nation states do not flow in the right direction. At the time, European integration was driven by security interests, but the means were economic. Established in 1951, the Coal and Terssysys transferred the development of these industrial sectors to a supranational level. The idea was that countries (France and Germany) could not go to war if they could not freely withdraw from their own strategic industries. The Czech European Union has thus been built in such a way that a country cannot acquire hegemony. The common institutions and the mssrsenhemmischss are the main concern. European integration and globalisation have increased the countries' central interdependence. At the same time, they have limited the scope for economic policy. The clearest demonstration of this is the abandonment of national monetary policy in favour of the single monetary policy. Efficient and reliable funding systems are the key basis for the functioning of society. It is the bloodstream of society. If there are minor blockages or problems, then the lifeblood of society can be seriously affected. Financial markets must be able to function in all circumstances. The Bank of Finland as a central bank d as a bank of banks d contributes to ensuring the efficient and reliable operation of the financial system. In addition, the Financial Supervisory Authority supervises financial operators, the solvency of banks and insurance companies, as well as the functioning of the securities markets. In addition to the solvency and liquidity of banks and other financial institutions, the effectiveness of payment systems is subject to supervision. The role of the Central Bank is particularly important. Due to the financial system, the financial markets must be prepared for all possible scenarios. It is a key area of national security of supply. In cooperation with the National Emergency Supply Agency, the Bank of Finland has been conducting crisis exercises in the financial sector for a few years. The exercises involve a large number of private organisations and public actors, and more than a thousand people. The financial markets are already long-term integrated. Financial activity transcending European environs but also globally. International and control structures are being strengthened. A number of reforms are being introduced to ensure the sound functioning of banks and to strengthen their risk tolerance. In order to prevent new banking crises, or at least to reduce the cost to taxpayers. The most recent step is to set up a banking union. Single banking supervision will be taken over by the ECB in November of the year. Next year, the Single Resolution Mechanism will be introduced. All eu member states in the euro area will join, but others can join the banking union. Joint supervision directly concerns the largest banks with significant cross-border banking activities in other EU countries. Prior to the transition to joint supervision, the largest banks are subject to a detailed balance sheet assessment and stress tests. The intention is that there should be no non-viable banks under common supervision. Finland's accession to the European Union and also to the euro area was, in due course, largely a factor in strengthening Finland's security. Probably most still think so. However, as part of national security, we must ensure economic stability ourselves and through our own efforts.

Tuesday 6 May 2014, 11:00 AM Pentti Hakkarainen Johtokunnan varapuheenjohtaja Puheenvuoro Maanpuolustuskurssien 45. erikoiskurssin avajaisissa Helsingiss 6.5.2014. TALOUDELLINEN VAKAUS JA KANSALLINEN TURVALLISUUS Taloudelliseen vakauteen kuuluu sellaisia asioita kuin terve julkinen talous, vakaa hintataso ja vakaasti toimivat rahoitusmarkkinat. Paljon muutakin siihen toki kuuluu, kuten korkea tyllisyys ja riittvt sosiaaliset turvaverkot. Taloudellinen vakauden yllpitminen edellytt luottamusta, ennustettavuutta ja vakaita poliittisia oloja. Kansalliseen turvallisuuteen taas kuuluu se, ett kansalaiset voivat el vapaina ja vailla pelkoa, ett heidn pitisi pelt ulkoista uhkaa, terrorismia tai rikollisuutta ja ett suuronnettomuuksien tai luonnonkatastrofien varalle on valmistauduttu. Hyvinvointivaltiossa ihmisten turvallisuutta on vahvistettu luomalla sosiaalisia turvaverkkoja tyttmyyden, tapaturmien, sairauden ja muiden yllttvien tilanteiden varalle. Taloudellinen vakaus voidaan menett monesta syyst. Syy voi ulkoinen tai sissyntyinen. Ulkoinen syy voi olla geopoliittinen kriisi, maailmankaupan romahdus, ljykriisi, luonnononnettomuus tai jotain muuta sellaista, johon omalla talous-tai muulla politiikalla ei voida vaikuttaa. Sissyntyisest taloudellisen vakauden menetyksest on paljon kokemuksia, osa niist varsin tuoreita. Syit voi olla monia, kuten huono hallinto, tiettyjen erityisryhmien tukeminen tai vain pitkjnteisyyden puute. Nin on ajauduttu valtion liialliseen velkaantumiseen, korkeaan inflaatioon tai pankkikriisin kautta reaalitalouden romahtamiseen. Krjistyneet eturistiriidat tai heikentynyt luottamus poliittisiin pttjiin ja yhteiskunnan instituutioihin ovat pahentaneet tilannetta. Kestvll pohjalla oleva talous antaa turvallisuutta. Tm ptee jokaisen yksityishenkiln ja yrityksen kohdalla. Sama ptee mys valtioihin, vaikka niiden kohdalla tilanne on joiltakin osin erilainen kuin yksityisill toimijoilla. Entisin aikoina taloudelliset edut ja poliittis-sotilaalliset intressit kulkivat ksi kdess. Ennen ensimmist maailmansotaa maailmankauppa ja pomanliikkeet olivat vapaita. Tt vapautta kuitenkin rajoitti  ainakin pienten maiden nkkulmasta  suurten valtioiden pyrkimys hegemoniaan sek talouden ett politiikan alalla. Sotien vlisen aikana ajauduttiin suuren laman seurauksena protektionismiin. Nationalismi ja rajojen sulkeminen johtivat vihanpitoon tunnetuin seurauksin. Toisen maailmansodan jlkeinen aika poikkeaa edeltvist aikakausista siin, ett nyt kytss oli toimivia kansainvlisi instituutioita. Kansainvlisen politiikan puolella Yhdistyneet Kansankunnat on onnistunut rajaamaan konflikteja aivan toisella tavalla kuin Kansainliitto aikanaan. Talouspolitiikassa Kansainvlisell valuuttarahastolla on ollut merkittv rooli kansainvlisen rahajrjestelmn koossapitmisess. Lukuisat muutkin kansainvliset organisaatiot, kuten Maailmanpankki, Maailman kauppajrjest ja OECD, ovat olleet mukana edistmss kansainvlist koordinointia talouspolitiikan alueella. Vaikka erimielisyyksi on ollut ja vaikka joissakin asioissa on edetty tuskastuttavan hitaasti, voidaan hyvin perustein vitt, ett kansainvlisten instituutioiden puitteissa tapahtunut koordinaatio ja yhteisty ovat pitneet maailmantalouden koossa. Vaikka tavoitteena on ollut taloudellinen vakaus ja kehitys, niiden kautta on samalla edistetty maailmanrauhaa. Kommunismin romahtamisella ja kylmn sodan loppumisella oli arvaamattomia vaikutuksia maailmantalouteen. Varsin lyhyess ajassa 2-3 miljardia ihmist tuli avoimen maailmankaupan piiriin. Sopeutuminen suhteellisten etujen muutokseen laajensi maailmankauppaa, muutti kauppavirtoja ja omistusrakenteita. Samanaikaisesti koettiin informaatioteknologian nopea muutos. Nm tekijt yhdess muuttivat mys liiketoimintamalleja siten, ett tuotannollisen toiminnan ja yrityksen kansallisuuden vlinen yhteys heikkeni. Tm on vhentnyt valtioiden ja yritysten vlist keskinisriippuvuutta. Yritysten ja kansallisvaltioiden edut eivt en kulje ksi kdess. Euroopan integraatio lhti aikanaan liikkeelle turvallisuusintresseist, mutta keinot olivat taloudellisia. Vuonna 1951 perustettu hiili-ja tersyhteis siirsi niden teollisuusalojen kehittmist koskevat ptkset ylikansalliselle tasolle. Ajatuksena oli, ett maat (lhinn Ranska ja Saksa) eivt voi ryhty sotaan, jos ne eivt voi vapaasti ptt omasta strategisesta teollisuudestaan. Tnnkin Euroopan unioni on siten rakennettu, ett mikn maa ei siin voi saada hegemoniaa. Yhteiset instituutiot ja mrenemmistptkset pitvt siit huolen. Euroopan integraatio ja globalisoituminen ovat lisnneet maiden vlist keskinisriippuvuutta. Samalla ne ovat rajoittaneet talouspolitiikan mahdollisuuksia. Selvin osoitus tst on kansallisesta rahapolitiikasta luopuminen yhteisen rahapolitiikan hyvksi. Rahoitusjrjestelmn tehokas ja luotettava toimintaon yhteiskunnan toimivuuden keskeinen perusta. Se on yhteiskunnan verenkierto. Jos tss on pienikin tukoksia tai ongelmia, voivat hirist vakavasti krsi yhteiskunnan elintrket osat. Finanssimarkkinoiden on pystyttv toimimaan kaikissa oloissa. Suomen Pankki keskuspankkina  pankkien pankkina  varmistaa osaltaan rahoitusjrjestelmn tehokkaan ja luotettavan toiminnan. Lisksi Finanssivalvonta valvoo finanssialan toimijoita, pankkien ja vakuutusyhtiiden vakavaraisuutta sek arvopaperimarkkinoiden toimintaa. Pankkien ja muiden rahoituslaitosten vakavaraisuuden ja maksuvalmiuden lisksi valvonnan kohteena on maksujrjestelmien toimivuus. Siin keskuspankin rooli on erityisen keskeinen. Rahoitusjrjestelmn trkeyden johdosta finanssimarkkinoilla on varauduttava kaikkiin mahdollisiin hiriihin. Se on keskeinen kansallisen huoltovarmuuden alue. Huoltovarmuuskeskuksen kanssa hyvss yhteistoiminnassa Suomen Pankki on jrjestnyt finanssialan kriisiharjoituksia snnllisesti muutaman vuoden vlein. Harjoituksiin osallistuu suuri mr yksityisi organisaatioita ja julkisia toimijoita ja enemmn kuin tuhat ihmist. Rahoitusmarkkinat ovat jo nyt pitklti integroituneet. Rahoitustoiminta ylitt rajat Euroopan sisll mutta mys globaalisti. Kansainvlist sntely ja valvontaa sek nihin liittyvi rakenteita ollaan vahvistamassa. Tekeill on lukuisia uudistuksia, joiden tarkoituksena on varmistaa pankkien terve toiminta ja vahvistaa niiden riskiensietokyky. Nill pyritn estmn uudet pankkikriisit tai ainakin pienentmn niist veronmaksajille aiheutuvia kustannuksia. Viimeisimpn vaiheena tss on pankkiunionin pystyttminen. Yhteinen pankkivalvonta siirtyy EKP:n vastuulle tmn vuoden marraskuussa. Ensi vuonna otetaan kyttn yhteinen kriisinratkaisumekanismi. Mukaan tulevat kaikki euroalueeseen kuuluvat EU:n jsenmaat, mutta muutkin voivat liitty pankkiunioniin. Yhteinen valvonta koskee suoraan suurimpia pankkeja, joilla on merkittv rajat ylittv pankkitoimintaa muissa EU-maissa. Ennen yhteiseen valvontaan siirtymist suurimmille pankeille suoritetaan yksityiskohtainen taseiden arviointi ja stressitestit. Tarkoituksena on, ett yhteisen valvonnan piiriin ei tule elinkelvottomia pankkeja. Suomen liittyminen Euroopan unioniin ja myhemmin euroalueeseen nhtiin aikanaan laajalti Suomen turvallisuutta vahvistavana tekijn. Luultavasti useimmat ovat edelleen samaa mielt. Osana kansallista turvallisuutta meidn tulee kuitenkin itse ja omin toimin huolehtia taloudellisen vakauden silymisest.

Title: Importance of the Banking Union in Finland
text: Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen: The importance of the banking union in Finland, Helsinki 15.5.2014. . Speech . Thursday15 May 2014,3:00PM Pentti Hakkarainen Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors Finance topical seminar at Haaga-Helia University of Applied Sciences 15.5.2014 Presentation slides (/globalassets/en/media-and.. publications/speeches/documents/140515_haagahelia_ph_esitys_pankkiunioni_final.pdf) (PDF) (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches/documents/140515_haagahelia_ph_esitys_pankkiunioni_final.pdf) IMPORTANCE OF THE BANKING UNION IN FINLAND Presentation body; the actual presentation may differ from the text in places The financial crisis we experienced showed how well-functioning the financial system is. Likewise, it is nshty how widespread even small hsirist in the financial world can have an impact. Banks play a key role in the functioning of the economy. They borrow and invest the funds of their depositors and financiers. They select investment and investment targets on behalf of the Ssssssj and, most recently, on behalf of society as a whole. Success is a prerequisite for economic prosperity, renewal and growth. Thanks to banking, the funds of individual companies can be withdrawn, even if the bank lends and invests funds in long-term objects. Tsms is the ssrimmsisen tsrkess for the establishment of trust in banks. If the bank fails, the damage to customers will be significant. In addition, the damage is easily multiplied and spreads beyond its own clientele to society as a whole. It is enough for crises to spread simply because of the linkage of banks. Among market participants, depositors and creditors, the impact can spread worldwide in minutes. Lessons have been learned from the past that customer supervision, market discipline and self-discipline are not sufficient to ensure the functioning of the financial system. In addition, the authorities, whose job it is to represent the social sphere as a whole, must take part of the responsibility for ensuring the reliable functioning of banks and other financial institutions and the financial markets by means of social and supervisory measures. The objectives of monitoring and control can be summarised in two key points. Firstly, the aim is to reduce the likelihood of financial crises and their social costs. Secondly, the aim of the social support network is to ensure that the banking system can effectively carry out the social function. Why do we need a banking union? The financial crisis revealed weaknesses in the banking sector, as well as in the case of individual banks and in the banking system as a whole. It revealed how interconnected the different actors are. In a highly international banking sector, the problem of an individual bank can quickly catch on with other banks across borders and across borders. There is no going back to the banking sector at national level. Banks and their international business and integrated financial markets are the basis of today's economy. The single monetary policy, integrated financial markets and the effective functioning of banks require the same level of financial supervision and resolution. National supervision is not sufficient to supervise banks operating in the international financial markets. National resolution is not capable of resolving crisis situations in large, multinational banks. A single monetary policy is not a means of dealing with the problems of individual countries facing banking or economic crises. The euro area crisis countries, in particular, have been struggling with the fate of banks and governments. Problems in the banking sector have put a strain on public finances, and fiscal problems in the country have made it difficult for banks to play a role, especially in raising funds. The affiliation between the Bank and its home country has led, at worst, to the osysksy spiralo. The banking union is a response to the supervision and resolution required of the actual business activities of banks. When financial institutions operate internationally, their supervision and resolution must also be at the same international level. In the banking union, a bank's problems can be dealt with by supervisory and resolution authorities without running into difficulties in the home country. Similarly, problems in the bank's home country do not put the bank in trouble when it is supranationally supervised. What parts does the banking union consist of? The functioning of the banking union is based on a common charter of requirements and supervisory frameworks established by EU law and other financial instruments in all the Member States. The two key pillars of the banking union are single banking supervision and single resolution. Supervision is currently being built within the framework of the European Central Bank (ECB). Agreement on the SRM has been reached between the European Parliament, the Commission and the Member States. The common deposit guarantee scheme is not in the vslttsmssn stage. The national deposit guarantee scheme will first be harmonised and, in due course, the common deposit guarantee scheme will be considered. The banking union will reduce the likelihood that banks will run into problems. In addition, if the bank encounters problems with the owners, the creditors are also responsible for covering the losses. In this way, the need for public bank support, as is familiar from economic history, is eliminated, or at least limited, and significantly reduced. Single Supervisory Mechanism In mid-2012, the European Council decided to transfer the responsibility for supervising banks to the ECB. The regulation on the SSM entered into force in November 2013 and, following the postponement period, the ECB will start supervision on 4 November 2014. The ECB directly supervises the largest banks, but the ECB also supervises supervisors and instructs all banks to be supervised in the same way, regardless of the country in which they are located. If necessary, the ECB can directly take over any bank in the euro area. It is important that the ECB performs its supervisory functions in a manner specific to monetary policy, as required by the Regulation on the Single Supervisory Mechanism. Indeed, the ECB has already established processes to ensure the separation of monetary policy and banking supervision in its organisation and decision-making. However, while the regions are kept separately, there are good synergies between the various activities where possible and necessary. The important aspect of the transition is a comprehensive assessment to ensure that the ECB starts its work as a supervisory authority from opuhta. A comprehensive assessment provides a clear and comparable picture of banks' overall risks. The comprehensive assessment is, as the name implies, comprehensive. This is where the common methods of the balance sheet risks are examined, and there are also external, independent experts. Since then, each bank's riskiest receivables will be receivable. The scope of the audit is wide. A total of 128 banks are estimated to have a total risk-weighted exposure of 58 % of the total risk-weighted exposures in their credit portfolios. The comprehensive assessment also includes a bank stress test in accordance with the methodology agreed with the European Banking Authority to test the strength of banks in the baseline scenario in line with expected developments and in a more difficult-than-expected situation, i.e. in a stress scenario. The stress scenario describes the impact on the real economy and financial markets of key systemic risks in the banking system. The stress scenario for the current stress test is, on the whole, clearly more severe than that previously carried out for banks in the EU. The impact on real economy growth is clearly greater than in the past, and the favourable developments in the scenario will now continue for three years, i.e. one year longer than before. As a result of the verification carried out under the strict guidance of the ECB, banks may have to increase their write-downs and acquire additional assets. The ECB is the supervisory authority which competently requires the implementation of this assessment. The results of the comprehensive assessment will be published in October 2014. In the baseline scenario of the stress tests, the requirement for banks to have the highest quality nuclear passport is 8%. Banks have recorded deficits in the baseline scenario within six months of the publication of the results. In the most favourable stress scenario, the pssoma requirement is 5.5%, and the time between the observed deficits is nine months. The deficits identified in the stress scenario can be reduced by the limits of the ssrstyi, in addition to the nuclear power plant, also in the primary SSssoma. Single Resolution Mechanism In the future, the work of bank resolution will consist of two parts: the national powers under the Recovery and Resolution Directive and the collective resolution mechanism at EU level. They allow even a large bank operating in many Member States to be shut down in a controlled manner without causing the financial markets to do so. This is a significant step forward in the past. Without resolution, banks in trouble were declared bankrupt or bailed out with state funds in the absence of a private sector solution. The recovery and crisis response directive will create the same levels in all EU countries for early entry, orderly reorganisation or closure of a problem bank. Investor responsibility is a significant new tool that will be introduced in all EU countries from the beginning of 2016. The responsibility of the industry in the form of a fund also creates a buffer ahead of public funds. A single resolution mechanism at EU level enables the orderly, rapid and efficient reorganisation or winding-down of even a supranational bank. In the common mechanism, the ECB, in its capacity as supervisor, determines whether a bank is failing or likely to fail and thus the need to move to resolution. Resolution decisions, on the other hand, are carried out by the SRB, which is confirmed by the Commission or, in some cases, by the Council of the EU. In resolution, the pssssssns is the implementation of investor responsibility. The responsibility of the industry takes the form of a common fund. In order to ensure the resources for resolution, a common fund will be established within 8 years. What is the significance of the banking union in Finland? The banking union directly and exclusively approves society, banks and customers, companies and individuals. The banking union will promote competition and the operating conditions of banks. Uniform supervision also brings a longer period of time to the administrative costs of banks. It harmonises transactions with the supervisor and, among other things, the need to report to the authorities of different countries. Although the net impact of the banking union on banks' own financing costs is difficult to accurately assess, the improved credibility of supervision, the clarity of resolution and wider resources are likely to have a negative impact on financing costs. The strengthening of confidence may increase investor interest in banks in the countries participating in the banking union. A comprehensive assessment of the banks separates the banking sector from the chaff. As a result, the position of the banks that have done their job well will be improved. Many of the benefits of joint supervision and resolution in Finland are also evident in the situation, as they can be used to spread problems across countries. As the problems of an individual bank in country A do not escalate into a crisis in the banking sector as a whole, the banks of country B will also be affected. In addition, there are adverse effects on the real economy. The basic principle of single resolution is that, in addition to the owners of a problem bank, creditors also bear the costs of resolution. When investors know their responsibilities, they will have better incentives to look after their own interests and to monitor and evaluate the bank's activities closely. In addition, monitoring helps banks to take excessive risks. Banks bear the costs of single resolution secondarily also as an industry through the Single Resolution Fund. In spite of the contributions, the joint fund incurs a loss for banks in individual countries. Firstly, the common fund is a tool to ensure the swift operation of the single resolution and thus prevent crises from spreading across countries. Secondly, the common fund will encourage banks to monitor each other more, i.e. the activities of other banks. In addition, a common fund throughout the banking union can be used to share the risk that the resolution of one bank entails for other banks. In a country in particular, the resolution of even one large bank could entail high costs for the industry if it had to be borne by the country's own banks. The Resolution Fund ensures effective procedures for settling a bank in trouble. The aim is not to pssomite or support an unviable bank, but to ensure sufficient resources for a controlled restructuring or winding-down process. As an open economy, Finland is vulnerable to Hsirish from outside the country's borders. Finland's advantage in the banking union is that we are involved in the drafting of the banking process, which involves the supervision of European banks, ensuring the uniformity and equal treatment of bank supervision and, in the event of problems, resolving them. When talking about the impact of the banking union, we should not forget the bank's customer. Depositors will continue to be confident that their money is safe in well-supervised banks. Whenever possible, the banking union helps to ensure the functioning of banking services for society, businesses and private individuals. To sum up, the banking union is one of the most important steps in the European Union since the establishment of monetary union. Firstly, in the banking union, supervision and control correspond to the true nature of banks and financial markets, to the cross-border functioning of banks and financial markets. Secondly, its banks also have more uniform operating and competitive conditions, regardless of the bank's home country. Thirdly, the position of the bank's customers will be strengthened under normal circumstances, but above all, the availability of life-long financial services will be ensured in ssriolo. For the fourth time, and one of the most important arguments, the banking union can help to reduce or reduce the potential problems of banking for society. The construction of the banking union has progressed rapidly. It is important that the elements of the banking union from which the decisions have been made are now implemented in a conscious and consistent manner.
