Nin ollen asiansa hyvin hoitaneiden pankkien asema paranee. Monet yhteisen valvonnan ja kriisinratkaisun hydyt Suomessa ilmenevt mys vlillisin, sill niiden avulla voidaan vltt ongelmien leviminen maiden vlill. Kun yksittisen pankin ongelmat maassa A eivt laajene koko pankkisektorin kriisiksi, mys maan B pankit sstyvt sen vaikutuksilta. Lisksi vltytn haitallisilta reaalitalouden kautta tarttuvilta vaikutuksilta. Yhteisen kriisinratkaisun perusperiaate on, ett ongelmapankin omistajien lisksi mys velkojat kantavat vastuun kriisinratkaisun kustannuksista. Kun sijoittajat tietvt vastuunsa, heill on aiempaa paremmat kannustimet huolehtia omasta edustaan sek seurata ja arvioida pankin toimintaa tarkasti. Lisntyv seuranta auttaa ehkisemn pankkien ylisuurta riskinottoa. Pankit vastaavat yhteisen kriisinratkaisun kustannuksista toissijaisesti mys toimialana yhteisen kriisinratkaisurahaston kautta. Maksuista huolimatta yhteisest rahastosta aiheutuu hytyj yksittisen maan pankeille. Ensinnkin yhteinen rahasto on trke tekij, jolla varmistetaan yhteisen kriisinratkaisun ripe toiminta ja estetn siten kriisien leviminen maiden vlill. Toiseksi yhteinen rahasto kannustaa pankkeja aiempaa enemmn seuraamaan toisiaan, eli muiden pankkien toimintaa. Lisksi koko pankkiunionin yhteisell rahastolla voidaan jakaa riski, joka yhden pankin kriisinratkaisusta koituu muille pankeille. Etenkin pieness maassa yhdenkin ison pankin kriisinratkaisu voisi aiheuttaa toimialalle suuret kustannukset, jos niist jouduttaisiin vastamaan maan omien pankkien voimin. Kriisinratkaisurahastolla varmistetaan tehokkaat menettelyt ongelmiin ajautuneen pankin selvittmiseen. Tarkoituksena ei ole pomittaa tai tukea elinkelvotonta pankkia, vaan varmistaa riittvt resurssit hallittuun uudelleenjrjestely-tai alasajoprosessiin. Avoimena taloutena Suomi on altis maan rajojen ulkopuolilta tuleville hiriille. Suomen etuna pankkiunionissa on se, ett olemme mukana ptksenteossa niiss pydiss, joissa ptetn eurooppalaisten pankkien valvonnasta, varmistamassa pankkien valvonnan yhdenmukaisuuden ja tasapuolisen kohtelun sek ongelmatapauksissa niiden ratkaisun. Pankkiunionin vaikutuksista puhuttaessa ei pid unohtaa pankin asiakasta. Tallettajat voivat jatkossakin luottaa siihen, ett heidn rahansa ovat turvassa hyvin valvotuissa pankeissa. Aina mahdollisissa rioloissa pankkiunioni auttaa varmistamaan yhteiskunnan, yritysten ja yksityishenkiliden elintrkeiden pankkipalveluiden toimivuuden. Yhteenvetona, pankkiunioni on yksi merkittvimmist askelista Euroopan unionissa rahaliiton perustamisen jlkeen. Ensinnkin pankkiunionissa valvonta ja sntely vastaavat pankkien ja rahoitusmarkkinoiden todellista luonnetta, rajat ylittv toimintaa. Toiseksi sen myt pankeilla on entist yhdenmukaisemmat toiminta-ja kilpailuedellytykset pankin kotivaltiosta riippumatta. Kolmanneksi pankin asiakkaiden asema vahvistuu normaalioloissa, mutta ennen kaikkea varmistetaan elintrkeiden rahoituspalveluiden saatavuus rioloissa. Neljnneksi, ja ehk yhten keskeisimpn perusteena, pankkiunionilla voidaan ehkist tai pienent pankkitoiminnan mahdollisia ongelmia yhteiskunnalle. Pankkiunionin rakentaminen on edennyt nopeasti. On trke, ett pankkiunionin osa-alueet, joista ptkset on tehty, toteutetaan nyt mrtietoisesti ja johdonmukaisesti.

Title: From the financial crisis to the Banking Union
text: Vice Chairman of the Board Pentti Hakkarainen: The financial crisis is moving into the banking union. Turku, 26.5.2014. . Speech . Tuesday 27 May 2014, 3:00PM Vice Chairman of the Board Pentti Hakkarainen Turku Chamber of Commerce Lunch Turku, 26.5.2014 Presentation slides (/globalassets/en/media-and.. publications/speeches/documents/140526_turku_kauppakamarilounas_nettiin2.pdf) (PDF) FINANSSIKRIISIST PANKKIUNIONIIN Presentation body; the actual presentation may differ from the text in places THE GLOBAL ECONOMY IS IMPROVING It's nice to come to Turku, because the Bank of Finland has strong roots. The Bank of Finland started its operations more than 200 years ago in 1812 in Turku. The global economy improved in the second half of 2013. However, the end of the financial crisis is long. In the euro area in particular, output remains at a low level and the employment situation in many countries has remained particularly difficult. Reflecting the underspending of resources, inflation in several economic areas has fallen below the central bank's medium-term target. Over the past few years, the adjustment of the euro area economies has progressed. However, the balances are so large that it takes time to digest them. Overall, the focus of economic policy is shifting from the containment of the crisis to the correction of its stature. Production resources d as well as power and pssoma d must be reallocated. Structural change weighs up the ability of economies to adapt to the new environment and places great demands on the economic policies to be pursued. According to the Bank of Finland's March 2014 international economic forecast, growth will be moderate. Of the Member States, GDP in the EU-21 is projected to grow by around 1.5% in 2014 d2016. In the United States, growth is stabilising at around 3%, and in China, growth is forecast to slow down to 6% at the end of the forecast horizon. The subdued nature of the nitty-gritty is also reflected in the Bank of Finland's inflation forecasts. In the EU-21, inflation will continue to fall during the year. Inflation is projected to rise from around 1% in 2014 to 1.6% in 2016. The gradual normalisation of inflation is facilitated by the economic recovery and the output gap contraction and long-term anchoring of inflation expectations. The global economy remains exposed to downside risks. A period of low inflation in the euro area may be longer than projected. Low inflation and the steepness of relative prices may make it more difficult for the economy as a whole to adjust towards a new equilibrium. A new risk of weaker growth than previously estimated is the crisis in Ukraine. So far, its biggest economic impact outside Ukraine has been on Vensjssn, whose otherwise subdued economy is struggling with growth. FINLAND JNOW ON THE BACK FOOT Finland's economic development has remained subdued. In recent months, forecasts have had to be revised in the direction of weaker developments, as the recovery in production has not begun. Although the level of employment in Finland has not increased by nearly as much as in many other European countries, economic growth has been weak even in European comparisons in recent years. Finland's GDP level is now just over 5% lower than at the beginning of 2008, and the cumulative development of production has been more akin to the so-called gdp. GIIPS countries than other high-rated countries in the euro area. The deviation from the previous growth trend in production has grown to a large extent. The level of GDP is now about 15% lower than it would have been if the trend before the financial crisis had continued. The weakness of economic development in recent years has been due in particular to the subdued nature of exports and industrial production. In addition to the weak state of the international economy, it is due to the specific problems of the export sectors and the associated industrial restructuring. The decline in cost competitiveness has also contributed to the deterioration of the conditions for production and production in competition with imports. In addition, the growth potential of the economy is weighed down by the fact that the number of people in the labour market has begun to shrink. The effects of the crisis in Ukraine pose a new challenge. This may result in further structural change in the Finnish economy. It also stresses the need to strengthen the productive potential of the economy through structural reforms, in particular those that support the capacity for economic renewal, including the mobility of labour force. The crisis in Ukraine is being felt in the Finnish economy because it is undermining the economic development of the Russian economy. The Russian economy was in a more vulnerable state even before the Ukrainian crisis. Economic growth in Russia has been slower than before since the onset of the international financial crisis and has slowed down further in the last two years. Now the crisis in Ukraine has also had an impact on the economic development of Vensjs. Eps security has increased, interest rates have risen, share prices have fallen, the ruble has weakened and the psomapako has increased. On the other hand, the price of sljy has remained high, supporting the Vensjs economy. The new Bank of Finland's economic forecast for Vensjs assumes that the assurance is more stable than during the financial crisis in 2008 and 2009: interest rate increases will be more moderate, etc. Nevertheless, economic growth is forecast to reach half a per cent in the year, and imports are projected to contract by 2%. If the crisis escalates further, economic growth could be even weaker than the new forecast. Of the EU countries, Finland is one of the countries that can expect the most financially from the crisis in Ukraine. In Finland, Vensjs's share of exports is the fourth largest among the EU countries. The problems of the Russian economy have already been felt in Finland in recent months. The weakened ruble, falling investment and the increase in eps security reduced Finland's exports. The end of the growth of russian real income and the depreciation of the ruble slowed down the growth of tourism significantly already at the end of 2013. A sharp deterioration in economic development in Russia would cause additional difficulties in many sectors of production in Finland, although estimating the size of the impact is very certain In conclusion, it can be said that the financial crisis has deepened the economic development of the finnish population. The worst of it would have been behind us, but it's still a long way off. The focus of economic policy is shifting from the fight against the crisis to strengthening the basis for growth. The three major challenges facing the Finnish economy are the subdued state of the international economy, industrial restructuring and the ageing of the economy. The process of meeting these challenges has begun, and the next government will have to continue with the work. THE BANKING UNION ADDRESSES THE GAP IN THE STRUCTURE It has been suggested in public that the banking union will not solve Europe's economic problems. Nsms epsilyt are right. The purpose of the banking union is not to remedy the economic problems of governments, but to improve banking supervision and resolution, which have since become international in financial activities. Lessons have been learned from the past that customer supervision, market discipline and self-discipline are not sufficient to ensure the functioning of the financial system. In addition, the authorities, whose job it is to represent the social sphere as a whole, must take part of the responsibility for ensuring the reliable functioning of banks and other financial institutions and the financial markets by means of social and supervisory measures. The objectives of monitoring and control can be summarised in two key points. Firstly, the aim is to reduce the likelihood of financial crises and their social costs. Secondly, the aim of the social support network is to ensure that the banking system can effectively carry out the social function. Banks and their international business and integrated financial markets are the basis of today's economy. The single monetary policy, integrated financial markets and the effective functioning of banks require the same level of financial supervision and resolution. National supervision is not sufficient to supervise banks operating in the international financial markets. National resolution is not capable of resolving crisis situations in large, multinational banks. A single monetary policy is not a means of dealing with the problems of individual countries facing banking or economic crises. The euro area crisis countries, in particular, have been struggling with the fate of banks and governments. Problems in the banking sector have put a strain on public finances, and fiscal problems in the country have made it difficult for banks to play a role, especially in raising funds. The affiliation between the Bank and its home country has led, at worst, to the osysksy spiralo. The banking union is a response to the supervision and resolution required of the actual business activities of banks. When financial institutions operate internationally, their supervision and resolution must also be at the same international level. In the banking union, a bank's problems can be dealt with by supervisory and resolution authorities without running into difficulties in the home country. Similarly, problems in the bank's home country do not put the bank in trouble when it is supranationally supervised. ELEMENTS OF THE BANKING UNION The functioning of the banking union is based on a common charter of requirements and supervisory frameworks established by EU law and other financial instruments in all the Member States. The two key pillars of the banking union are single banking supervision and single resolution. Supervision is currently being built within the framework of the European Central Bank (ECB). Agreement on the SRM has been reached between the European Parliament, the Commission and the Member States. The common deposit guarantee scheme is not in the vslttsmssn stage. The national deposit guarantee scheme will first be harmonised and, in due course, the common deposit guarantee scheme will be considered. The banking union will reduce the likelihood that banks will run into problems. In addition, if the bank encounters problems with the owners, the creditors are also responsible for covering the losses. In this way, the need for public bank support, as is familiar from economic history, is eliminated, or at least limited, and significantly reduced. SINGLE SUPERVISORY MECHANISM In mid-2012, the European Council decided to transfer the responsibility for supervising banks to the ECB. The regulation on the SSM entered into force in November 2013 and, following the postponement period, the ECB will start supervision on 4 November 2014. The important aspect of the transition is a comprehensive assessment to ensure that the ECB starts its work as a supervisory authority from opuhta. A comprehensive assessment provides a clear and comparable picture of banks' overall risks. The comprehensive assessment is, as the name implies, comprehensive. This is where the common methods of the balance sheet risks are examined, and there are also external, independent experts. Since then, each bank's riskiest receivables will be receivable. The scope of the audit is wide. A total of 128 banks are estimated to have a total risk-weighted exposure of 58 % of the total risk-weighted exposures in their credit portfolios. SINGLE RESOLUTION MECHANISM In the future, the work of bank resolution will consist of two parts: the national powers under the Recovery and Resolution Directive and the collective resolution mechanism at EU level. They allow even a large bank operating in many Member States to be shut down in a controlled manner without causing the financial markets to do so. This is a significant step forward in the past. Without resolution, banks in trouble were declared bankrupt or bailed out with state funds in the absence of a private sector solution. The recovery and crisis response directive will create the same levels in all EU countries for early entry, orderly reorganisation or closure of a problem bank. Investor responsibility is a significant new tool that will be introduced in all EU countries from the beginning of 2016. The responsibility of the industry in the form of a fund also creates a buffer ahead of public funds. A single resolution mechanism at EU level enables the orderly, rapid and efficient reorganisation or winding-down of even a supranational bank. In the common mechanism, the ECB, in its capacity as supervisor, determines whether a bank is failing or likely to fail and thus the need to move to resolution. Resolution decisions, on the other hand, are carried out by the SRB, which is confirmed by the Commission or, in some cases, by the Council of the EU. In resolution, the pssssssns is the implementation of investor responsibility. The responsibility of the industry takes the form of a common fund. The Resolution Fund ensures effective procedures for settling a bank in trouble. The aim is not to pssomite or support an unviable bank, but to ensure sufficient resources for a controlled restructuring or winding-down process. IMPACT OF THE BANKING UNION ON THE ECONOMY The banking union directly and exclusively approves society, banks and customers, companies and individuals. The banking union will promote competition and the operating conditions of banks. Uniform supervision also brings a longer period of time to the administrative costs of banks. It harmonises transactions with the supervisor and, among other things, the need to report to the authorities of different countries. Although the net impact of the banking union on banks' own financing costs is difficult to accurately assess, the improved credibility of supervision, the clarity of resolution and wider resources are likely to have a negative impact on financing costs. The strengthening of confidence may increase investor interest in banks in the countries participating in the banking union. A comprehensive assessment of the banks separates the banking sector from the chaff. As a result, the position of the banks that have done their job well will be improved. When talking about the impact of the banking union, we should not forget the bank's customer. Depositors will continue to be confident that their money is safe in well-supervised banks. Whenever possible, the banking union helps to ensure the functioning of banking services for society, businesses and private individuals. FINALLY To sum up, the banking union is one of the most important steps in the European Union since the establishment of monetary union. Firstly, in the banking union, supervision and control correspond to the true nature of banks and financial markets, to the cross-border functioning of banks and financial markets. Secondly, its banks also have more uniform operating and competitive conditions, regardless of the bank's home country. Thirdly, the position of the bank's customers will be strengthened under normal circumstances, but above all, the availability of life-long financial services will be ensured in ssriolo. For the fourth time, and one of the most important arguments, the banking union can help to reduce or reduce the potential problems of banking for society. The construction of the banking union has progressed rapidly. It is important that the elements of the banking union from which the decisions have been made are now implemented in a conscious and consistent manner. As an open economy, Finland is vulnerable to Hsirish from outside the country's borders. Finland's advantage in the banking union is that we are involved in the drafting of the banking process, which involves the supervision of European banks, ensuring the uniformity and equal treatment of bank supervision and, in the event of problems, resolving them. This will contribute to creating the conditions for the efficient functioning of the rest of the economy, and the positive effects will be realised over a long period of time. nanssikriisi (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tagnanssikriisi) pankkiunioni (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tagpankkiunioni)

Mys kustannuskilpailukyvyn heikkeneminen on osaltaan heikentnyt vientituotannon ja tuonnin kanssa kilpailevan tuotannon edellytyksi. Lisksi talouden kasvumahdollisuuksia painaa se, ett tyikisen vestn mr on ruvennut supistumaan. Ukrainan kriisin vaikutukset muodostavat uuden haasteen. PANKKIUNIONI KORJAA PUUTTEEN RAKENTEESSA Julkisuudessa on esitetty epilyj siit, ettei pankkiunioni ratkaise Euroopan talousongelmia. Nm epilyt ovat oikeassa. Pankkiunionin tarkoituskaan ei ole korjata valtioiden talousongelmia vaan parantaa pankkivalvontaa ja kriisinratkaisua, jotka ovat jneet jlkeen rahoitustoiminnan kansainvlistyess. Aiemmasta on opittu, ett asiakkaiden valvonta, markkinakuri ja itsesntely eivt riit rahoitusjrjestelmn toimivuuden varmistamiseksi. Lisksi viranomaisten, joiden tyn on edustaa koko yhteiskunnan nkkulmaa, on otettava sntelyn ja valvonnan keinoin osavastuu pankkien ja muiden rahoituslaitosten sek rahoitusmarkkinoiden luotettavasta toimintaedellytysten varmistamisesta. Sntelyn ja valvonnan tavoitteet voidaan tiivist kahteen keskeiseen seikkaan. Ensinnkin tavoitteena on pienent finanssikriisien todennkisyytt ja niiden yhteiskunnallisia kustannuksia. Toiseksi sntelyll ja yhteiskunnan tukiverkolla pyritn varmistamaan, ett pankkijrjestelm voi tehokkaasti hoitaa trke yhteiskunnallista tehtvns. Pankit ja niiden kansainvlinen liiketoiminta sek yhdentyneet rahoitusmarkkinat ovat nykytalouden perusta. Yhteinen rahapolitiikka, yhdentyneet rahoitusmarkkinat ja pankkien tosiasiallinen toiminta edellyttvt samalla tasolla olevaa rahoitusvalvontaa ja kriisinratkaisua. Kansallinen valvonta ei riit kansainvlisill rahoitusmarkkinoilla toimivien pankkien valvontaan. Kansallinen kriisinratkaisu ei kykene suurten, monikansallisesti toimivien pankkien kriisitilanteiden ratkaisuun. Yhteinen rahapolitiikka ei ole kytettviss pankki-tai talouskriiseihin ajautuvien yksittisten maiden ongelmien ksittelyyn. Etenkin euroalueen kriisimaat ovat krsineet pankkien ja valtioiden vlisest kohtalonyhteydest. Pankkisektorin ongelmat ovat rasittaneet julkista taloutta, ja maan julkisen talouden ongelmat ovat vaikeuttaneet pankkien asemaa, erityisesti varainhankintaa. Pankin ja sen kotivaltion vlinen sidos on johtanut pahimmillaan syksykierteeseen. Pankkiunioni on vastaus pankkien tosiasiallisen liiketoiminnan edellyttmn valvontaan ja kriisinratkaisuun. Kun rahoituslaitokset toimivat kansainvlisesti, mys niiden valvonnan ja kriisinratkaisun tulee olla samalla kansainvlisell tasolla. Pankkiunionissa pankin ongelmat voidaan hoitaa valvonta-ja kriisinratkaisuviranomaisten toimin kotivaltion ajautumatta vaikeuksiin. Vastaavasti pankin kotivaltion ongelmat eivt suista pankkia vaikeuksiin, kun se on ylikansallisesti valvottu. PANKKIUNIONIN OSAT Pankkiunionin toiminta nojautuu yhteiseen sntkirjaan, joka koostuu EU:n lainsdnnn ja muun rahoitussntelyn kaikkiin jsenmaihin luomista yhtenisist sntelyvaatimuksista ja valvontakytnnist. Pankkiunionin kaksi keskeist pilaria ovat yhteinen pankkivalvonta ja yhteinen kriisinratkaisu. Valvontaa rakennetaan parhaillaan Euroopan keskuspankin (EKP) yhteyteen. Yhteisen kriisinratkaisumekanismia koskevista snnksist on psty sopuun Euroopan parlamentin, komission ja jsenmaiden vlill. Yhteinen talletussuojajrjestelm ei ole tss vaiheessa vlttmtn. Kansallisia talletussuojajrjestelmi harmonisoidaan ensin ja aikanaan yhteinen talletussuoja noussee harkintaan. Pankkiunioni pienent todennkisyytt, ett pankit joutuvat ongelmiin. Lisksi pankin joutuessa ongelmiin omistajien lisksi mys velkojat vastaavat tappioiden kattamisesta. Siten taloushistoriasta tutun julkisen pankkituen tarve poistuu tai ainakin rajautuu ja pienenee merkittvsti. YHTEINEN VALVONTAMEKANISMI Eurooppa-neuvosto ptti keskuussa 2012 pankkien valvontavastuun siirtmisest EKP:lle. Yhteist valvontamekanismia koskeva asetus tuli voimaan marraskuussa 2013 ja meneilln olevan siirtymajan jlkeen EKP aloittaa valvonnan 4.marraskuuta 2014. Siirtymajan merkittvin asia on kattava arviointi, jonka avulla varmistetaan, ett EKP aloittaa tehtvns valvontaviranomaisena puhtaalta pydlt. Kattava arvio luo selken ja vertailukelpoisen kuvan pankkien kokonaisriskeist. Kattava arviointi on nimens mukaisesti kattava. Siin tarkastellaan taseiden trkeimmt riskit kytten yhteisi menetelmi ja mritelmi ja kytettviss on mys ulkopuolisia, riippumattomia asiantuntijoita. Tmn jlkeen kunkin pankin riskipitoisimmat saamiset kydn lpi. Tarkastuksen kattavuus on laaja. Yhteens 128 pankkia ksittvn arvion kohteena on luottosalkkujen riskipainotettujen saamisten kokonaismrst 58 prosenttia. YHTEINEN KRIISINRATKAISUMEKANISMI Pankkien kriisinratkaisun tykalut koostuvat jatkossa kahdesta osasta: kansallisesta elvytys-ja kriisinratkaisudirektiivin mukaisista toimivaltuuksista sek EU-tason yhteisest kriisinratkaisumekanismista. Ne mahdollistavat monissa jsenmaissa toimivan suurenkin pankin hallitun alasajon ilman, ett siit aiheutuu hiriit rahoitusmarkkinoille. Tm on merkittv edistysaskel aiempaan kytntn. Ilman kriisinratkaisuvlineit ongelmiin ajautuneet pankit asetettiin konkurssiin tai pelastettiin valtion varoilla yksityisen sektorin ratkaisun puuttuessa. Elvytys-ja kriisiratkaisudirektiivin avulla luodaan kaikkiin EU-maihin yhteniset tykalut varhaiseen vliintuloon, ongelmapankin hallittuun uudelleenjrjestelyyn tai alasajoon. Sijoittajanvastuu on merkittv uusi tykalu, joka tulee kyttn kaikissa EU-maissa viimeistn vuoden 2016 alusta lukien. Mys toimialan vastuu rahaston muodossa luo puskuria julkisten varojen kytn edelle. Yhteinen EU-tason kriisinratkaisumekanismi mahdollistaa ylikansallisenkin pankin hallitun, nopean ja tehokkaan uudelleenjrjestelyn tai alasajon. Yhteisess mekanismissa EKP valvojan ominaisuudessa mritt, onko pankki kaatumassa (failing or likely to fail) ja siten tarpeesta siirty kriisinratkaisuun. Kriisinratkaisuptkset puolestaan tekee yhteisen mekanismin kriisinratkaisuneuvosto, jonka ptkset komissio tai joissakin tapauksissa EU:n neuvosto vahvistaa. Kriisinratkaisussa psnt on sijoittajanvastuun toteuttaminen. Toimialan vastuu toteutuu yhteisen rahaston muodossa. Kriisinratkaisurahastolla varmistetaan tehokkaat menettelyt ongelmiin ajautuneen pankin selvittmiseen. Tarkoituksena ei ole pomittaa tai tukea elinkelvotonta pankkia, vaan varmistaa riittvt resurssit hallittuun uudelleenjrjestely-tai alasajoprosessiin. PANKKIUNIONIN VAIKUTUKSIA TALOUTEEN Pankkiunioni hydytt suoraan ja vlillisesti yhteiskuntaa, pankkeja sek niden asiakkaita, yrityksi ja yksityishenkilit. Pankkiunioni edist pankkien vlist kilpailua ja toimintaedellytyksi. Yhteninen valvonta tuo pidemmll aikavlill mys sstj pankkien hallinnollisiin kustannuksiin. Se yhdenmukaistaa asiointia valvojan kanssa ja vhent mm. tarvetta rtlid raportointia eri maiden viranomaisille. Vaikka pankkiunionin nettovaikutusta pankkien omiin rahoituskustannuksiin on vaikea tarkkaan arvioida, valvonnan uskottavuuden paraneminen, selkemmt kriisinratkaisun vlineet ja laajemmat resurssit vaikuttanevat mynteisesti rahoituskustannuksiin. Luottamuksen vahvistuminen voi list sijoittajien kiinnostusta pankkiunioniin osallistuvien maiden pankkeihin. Pankkien kattava arviointi erottaa pankkisektorin jyvt akanoista. Nin ollen asiansa hyvin hoitaneiden pankkien asema paranee. Pankkiunionin vaikutuksista puhuttaessa ei pid unohtaa pankin asiakasta. Tallettajat voivat jatkossakin luottaa siihen, ett heidn rahansa ovat turvassa hyvin valvotuissa pankeissa. Aina mahdollisissa rioloissa pankkiunioni auttaa varmistamaan yhteiskunnan, yritysten ja yksityishenkiliden elintrkeiden pankkipalveluiden toimivuuden. LOPUKSI Yhteenvetona, pankkiunioni on yksi merkittvimmist askelista Euroopan unionissa rahaliiton perustamisen jlkeen. Ensinnkin pankkiunionissa valvonta ja sntely vastaavat pankkien ja rahoitusmarkkinoiden todellista luonnetta, rajat ylittv toimintaa. Toiseksi sen myt pankeilla on entist yhdenmukaisemmat toiminta-ja kilpailuedellytykset pankin kotivaltiosta riippumatta. Kolmanneksi pankin asiakkaiden asema vahvistuu normaalioloissa, mutta ennen kaikkea varmistetaan elintrkeiden rahoituspalveluiden saatavuus rioloissa. Neljnneksi, ja ehk yhten keskeisimpn perusteena, pankkiunionilla voidaan ehkist tai pienent pankkitoiminnan mahdollisia ongelmia yhteiskunnalle. Pankkiunionin rakentaminen on edennyt nopeasti. On trke, ett pankkiunionin osa-alueet, joista ptkset on tehty, toteutetaan nyt mrtietoisesti ja johdonmukaisesti. Avoimena taloutena Suomi on altis maan rajojen ulkopuolilta tuleville hiriille. Suomen etuna pankkiunionissa on se, ett olemme mukana ptksenteossa niiss pydiss, joissa ptetn eurooppalaisten pankkien valvonnasta, varmistamassa pankkien valvonnan yhdenmukaisuuden ja tasapuolisen kohtelun sek ongelmatapauksissa niiden ratkaisun. Tll osaltaan luodaan edellytyksi muun talouden tehokkaalle toiminnalle, ja mynteiset vaikutukset toteutuvat pitkll aikavlill. nanssikriisi (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tag=nanssikriisi) pankkiunioni (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tag=pankkiunioni)

text: Vice-Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen: Economic development, social reforms and the banking union. Vierumski, 5.11.2014. . Speech . Wednesday5 November 2014,6:00 PM Pentti Hakkarainen Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors The Autumn Unions of OP Federations of Its-Finland Vierumski, 5.11.2014 Esityskalvot (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches/documents/141105_ph_puhe.pdf) (PDF) . ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, STION REFORMS AND BANKING UNION Presentation body; the actual presentation may differ from the text in places [Slide 1] The international financial crisis came to an end six years ago. Since then, the developed countries have, on the whole, experienced weak economic development and long-term growth in the world economy has been dependent on emerging economies. The recovery since the sharp recession of 2008 and 2009 has been uneventful, and many advanced economies have occasionally experienced backward steps. Over the past year, the euro area contributed to international economic growth. However, in recent months, gdp growth has slowed down in the second quarter, and recent indicator data suggest a rapid improvement in the situation. In the Bank of Finland's international economic forecast published in September, global economic growth is projected to be slower this year than previously forecast. However, growth in emerging economies is also expected to pick up over the next two years at its average pace over a long period of time. Is the weakness of the developed economies in recent years of a global nature? Or is there any reason to expect growth to remain slower in the coming years than in previous decades? This has been one of the central themes of the recent international economic debate. It is clear that some of the weakness of the last six years has been cyclical. On the other hand, a number of factors have been highlighted in the debate which could act as a brake on economic growth in the coming years. One of these factors is vsestsn iksning. The growth of the 15d64-year-olds is now slowing down or d especially in Europe d turning into a contraction. The conditions for growth in advanced economies have also been weakened by the indebtedness of households and non-financial corporations. Debts grew rapidly in many countries before the start of the international financial crisis. Since then, debt burdens have been eased, but in several countries the process is still ongoing. In addition to private debt, public debt is also higher than in the past, which contributes to limiting the conditions for a growth-friendly economic policy. The state of the banking system is also one of the factors that can act as a brake on economic growth. As a result of the international financial crisis, banks' ability to finance in many countries declined. Since then, the situation has improved substantially, but the process is still not over. Title: The nuts and bolts of Banking Union  what does participation imply?
text: Deputy Governor Pentti Hakkarainen: The nuts and bolts of Banking Union what does participation imply? Copenhagen, 15 December 2014. . Speech . Monday15 December 2014, 12:00 PM A Keynote Address by Deputy Governor Pentti Hakkarainen at the High-Level Seminar on the Banking Union, Danmarks Nationalbank, Copenhagen on 15 December 2014 Slides (PDF) (/globalassets/fi/media-ja-julkaisut/puheet/documents/141215_banking_union_tanska.pdf) . It is a great pleasure for me to participate in this seminar here at the Danmarks Nationalbank. And Iom very pleased to speak to you today about the establishment of the Banking Union. The recent crises have made it very clear at least that international, highly interconnected financial markets (like we have here in the Nordic region) require a stronger institutional framework than what we have had in recent years. The authorities need proper tools to deal with ailing banks operating in integrated cross-border markets. The creation of these tools has taken major steps forward since, but there is still a lot of work ahead. For the Banking Union, i.e. the Eurozone countries and potential opt-in countries, the work is almost completed. With outside countries cross-border problems may exist even though power and tools of authorities are harmonised through the Bank recovery and resolution directive (BRRD). The key lesson we have learnt is that economic dislocations without proper arrangements to tackle troubled banks have devastating effects on the real economy, taxpayers and the whole society. And regaining growth proves to be painfully slow and long-lasting. In order to avoid collateral damages it is imperative that institutional arrangements for supervision and resolution match the integrated structures of banking business in the real world. BANKING UNION As part of the economic and monetary union and as a remedy for the crisis, the EU leaders agreed in June 2012 on creating a true Banking Union. The Single Rulebook provides a foundation for the Banking Union. It is based on the idea of harmonised regulatory requirements, such as capital adequacy rules for banks. These are achieved through European legislation and lower.level technical standards. The second main pillar of the Banking Union is the Single Supervisory Mechanism which started its practical operations just over a month ago in the beginning of November. The third important pillar is the Single Resolution Mechanism. The SRM will gradually start its practical operation in the beginning of 2015. The Banking Union will help us prevent banking problems. I would argue that there will be fundamental cultural change not only in the supervisory, crisis management and regulatory frameworks for banks but also in the banking industry. In the future, we will avoid the use of taxpayerso money as a rule and bail-out would be only a rare exception. This, in turn, means also better incentives in banking and hence a more stable financial system. THE SINGLE SUPERVISORY MECHANISM The SSM was established to ensure that strong supervisory standards are applied in a consistent manner across the euro area. We also need the SSM to strengthen the confidence and resilience in the banking sector which has been shaken quite severely over the past few years. To achieve these goals, the SSM, with the ECB at its centre, has been entrusted with an extensive set of micro-and macro-prudential powers, covering all key tasks relating to the prudential supervision of credit institutions. The SSM operates as a system, gathering all of the expertise of national supervisors and at the same time possessing a strong decision-making centre. The justification for the two-tier system is that the local supervisors will have an information advantage with respect to local banks. The centralized decision making is required to address cross-border issues and to minimize the risk of excessive forbearance on the part of local supervisors. The shared competence is important also because credit cycles differ nationally and the associated potential problems need to be mitigated through nationally differentiated ways. The SSM uses a risk-based approach to supervision. A common SSM Risk Assessment System has been developed, relying on an integrated and harmonised information base, to direct supervisory resources on the basis of the risk and impact assessment. Common methods and processes have also been developed for assessing the adequacy of bankso capital and liquidity levels. The SSM goes considerably deeper than the work of the EBA in developing the Single Rule book and harmonising supervisory practices at the EU-level as a whole. The SSM possesses early intervention powers in accordance with the Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive. The early intervention powers are significant and make it possible to take action with respect to institutions which are approaching the point of non-viability. The ECBos overall responsibility for supervision is matched by controlling powers over the system as a whole. First, all the components of the system have to act in accordance with a system of guidelines, ECB-specific regulations and manuals of supervisory practices. The supervisory function has the power to overtake direct supervision of any bank or group of banks, if this is deemed necessary in order to preserve financial stability and confidence in the institutional framework. The centre monitors also that adequate supervisory quality prevails in national competent authorities. GOVERNANCE OF THE SSM The governance structure of the SSM has been designed to separate the ECBos monetary policy and supervisory roles, and to make the position of different participating countries as fair as possible. The Supervisory Board is responsible for the supervisory functions of the SSM. While the decisions are formally and finally adopted by the Governing Council of the ECB, the Supervisory Board is, de facto, the main decision-making body in supervisory matters. In prudential supervisory matters, the Governing Council cannot alter the decisions of the Supervisory Board, but only prevent their entry into force. Such a veto power could be exercised when the decision is seen to be in conflict with monetary policy. The special status of the non-Euro Area countries is taken into account in the decision-making mechanism. Non-euro area member states can participate through establishing a close cooperation agreement with the ECB. By giving non-euro area Member States full membership and voting rights in the Supervisory Board they are placed on an equal footing with the euro-area members. A non-euro area country may even announce non-satisfaction at the Governing Councilos decision and can choose not to adopt the decision. For its part, the ECB could then consider breaking up the agreement of close cooperation. DAY-TO-DAY WORK For carrying out the day-to-day supervision of significant banks, Joint Supervisory Teams have been established. They integrate the ECB and national competent authority staff into single supervisory units responsible for the conduct of the on-going supervisory activities, planning of on-site inspections and other supervisory work and for preparing supervisory decisions. The Teams are led by the ECB. There is one Team for each significant banking group, tailored to the needs of each banking group (proportionality). The Joint Supervisory Teams provide a single interface for the supervised banks and a single entry point for applications e.g. concerning internal models to be approved by the supervisor. The SSM adopts best supervisory practices to conduct high-quality supervision with no biases. The participating national authorities get all the information and can take part in supervisory decisions. Moreover, there is a European approach to SSM decision-making without any national bias. SSM VS. NATIONAL INTERESTS Banking, and financial services more generally, is a high value added industry which typically is deemed necessary to have a strong national ownership. One can even say that national banking supervisors have traditionally had a dual role to play: first, to carry out effective supervision and thus promote financial stability but, second, to also promote the interests and competitiveness of the national financial industry. However, when banking is getting more and more globally regulated and less and less restricted within any countryos borders, one can ask whether there are national interests left. In today's economies and also for banks themselves it may be better to aim for a level playing field internationally and enhance competition in the national market than look after the interests of domestic banks only. Over time, the banking union is envisaged to lessen the role that national interests play. The ECB, as an established and strong European institution, is well placed to tackle the emergence of national interests in supervision. It is therefore imperative that the structures and the processes of the SSM support a European perspective and interests. So far, the developments seem to point to this direction. The fact that the ECB can, if deemed necessary, take over the direct supervision of any bank operating in the Banking Union area underlines that the ECB is fully in charge of the SSM. NEW MACROPRUDENTIAL ROLE The crisis has shown that micro-prudential supervision at individual bank level is not sufficient, and that macro and micro risks can actually be mutually reinforcing. This calls for very close cooperation between the macro-and micro-prudential functions. The ECB has powers also in the macro-prudential area, which is a shared competence with national macro-prudential authorities. The ECB will be consulted on national measures and it has the possibility to tighten national measures if they are deemed inadequate. Macro-prudential instruments could also be applied to the euro-area financial system as a whole. The role of the EU macro-prudential supervisor, the European Systemic Risk Board (ESRB), is broader both sector-wise and geographically than the SSM. The ESRB covers all EU member states and the whole financial system rather than only the banking sector. BANK RESOLUTION The Single Resolution Mechanism (SRM) is the necessary complement to the Single Supervisory Mechanism. The SRM creates a single authority consisting of the centre, the Single Resolution Board, and of the national resolution authorities, which are responsible for swift and orderly resolution of banks in the euro area and participating member states. The SRM includes also the Single Resolution Fund at the Banking Union level. The SRM ends the era of the bail-out and moves us to the culture of the bail-in. As from the beginning of 2016, or in some countries even earlier, the BRRD requires bail-in of shareholders and creditors equal to at least 8% of the total liabilities of a failing bank. Only after the threshold of 8% bail-in can money from the resolution financing arrangement be used and only at the very end of the process can public money be used. It is notable that public money can, in exceptional cases, be used to fund resolution functions, not to bail-out nonviable banks. It should be mentioned that in all cases where public money is used the European Commissionos state aid rules have to be applied. These require e.g. the restructuring of the bank. The new powers to bail-in bank debt holders are a crucial element of the future resolution mechanism, which should limit the use of bail-outs significantly. The intention is that in the new regime, bail-in will be the rule, bail-out a rare exception. The BRR Directive requires that national resolution authorities cooperate with each other and that resolution colleges are established from all the resolution authorities of the countries where the bank has business operations. This goes some way to facilitate necessary coordination in crisis situations but may not be sufficient to ensure an orderly resolution of cross-border banks. Therefore, the SRM has a supranational decision making body with full resolution powers, efficient decision making procedures and adequate resolution financing arrangements, with the same institutional and geographical scope as the SSM. SINGLE RESOLUTION BOARD The regulation provides for a single resolution board with broad powers. Upon notification by the European Central Bank that a bank is failing or likely to fail, or on its own initiative, the board would adopt a resolution scheme placing the bank into resolution. It will determine the application of resolution tools and the use of the single resolution fund. Decisions by the board will enter into force within 24 hours of their adoption, unless the Commission or the Council, acting by simple majority on a proposal by the Commission, objected or called for changes. The national resolution authorities will be responsible for the practical implementation of the resolution schemes. The board ensures that the European point of view prevails. The board will consist of a Chair, a Vice-Chair, four full-time appointed executive members and the representatives of the national resolution authorities of all the participating countries. It will exercise its tasks in either a plenary or executive format. Most draft resolution decisions would be prepared in the executive session, composed of the executive director and the appointed members, with the representatives of member states concerned by a particular resolution decision involved in a first stage. SINGLE RESOLUTION FUND The SRM is complemented by the Single Resolution Fund which will be financed via levies on the banking sector itself. The Fund will start from national compartments but it will gradually mutualise to become a truly single European Fund. The fund will ensure the availability of resources for the use of resolution tools and medium-term funding to enable the bank to continue operating while it is being restructured. It has a target level of u55 billion and can borrow from the markets if decided by the Single Resolution Board. It will reach the target level over eight years, starting in 2016. During that transitional period, there will be national compartments which will be progressively merged. The Fund and the decision-making on its use is regulated by the SRM Regulation. The contributions to the Single Fund will also be calculated by the Board under the SRM Regulation. However, the contributions will be collected and transferred by the national resolution authorities in accordance with the IGA. The IGA will also regulate the progressive mutualisation of the national compartments during the transitional period. Indeed, the resources accumulated will be progressively mutualised, starting with 40% of these resources in the first year. The resolution mechanism with its fund makes banks not only less likely to fail but also safe to fail meaning that they can be resolved without cost to the taxpayer and without significant disruption to the financial markets or the economy at large. DEPOSIT GUARANTEE A Pan-European Deposit Guarantee Scheme has also been proposed as an element of the banking union. The planning of such a scheme is still in a very early phase. It has turned out to be more difficult to establish and to take more time than expected since the existing national systems are very heterogeneous. A politically sensitive issue is the possibility of mutualisation of risks, or national funds in a situation in which significant funds have already been gathered in some countries while at the same time none, or very little, have been gathered in other countries. Nevertheless, as long as deposit guarantee systems are predominantly national, a potential risk of contagion may remain between banking sectors and the states. However, one should remember that the deposit insurance system is not to guarantee any bank liability but to facilitate a swift pay back of deposits i.e. it is a temporary financing with the full recourse to the bank in question. A common deposit guarantee scheme may move forward in 2019 when the European Commission is mandated to revisit the issue. THE NORDIC DIMENSION We had our own severe crises in the 1980s and 1990s, but this time our financial sector has survived pretty well, keeping itself in a rather good shape. However, the cross-border characteristics of large banks have increased and their operations has become extremely complex. I donot think the old way of doing things and old structures are able to cope with the new environment. Changes in Nordic banking industry call for a corresponding structure for the supervisory framework and also for the resolution process. The establishment of the SSM is interesting from the perspective of the Nordic banking sector. As a euro area country, Finland automatically participates in the Banking Union. Both Nordea and Danske Bank have significant subsidiaries in Finland, which have brought them under direct supervision of the ECB. It would simplify the supervisory structure greatly if all Nordic authorities would operate under the same SSM roof. Maybe even more important than supervision from the financial markets stability point of view, is the orderly resolution of large problem banks. In the global efforts to contain the otoo-big-to-failo problems, increasing attention has been paid to bankso resolvability. It is therefore natural that the competent authorities in the Banking Union have keen interest in the resolvability of all significant banking institutions operating in the area, whether they are established in the Banking Union or simply operate as subsidiaries. The Nordic banks are in a good shape at the moment but the previous crises have shown how fast things can change. The oAchilles heelo of the Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive is that it is for national purposes, and not handling cross-border problems directly. The most efficient way of resolving cross-border banks is concentrating the decision making and operations under one roof. The European solution for that problem was the creation of the SRM. The SRM will be a very efficient system if resolving the Banking Union member banks is needed, but we have create ways to tackle Nordic bankso issues differently. CONCLUSION As a conclusion and positive end of my presentation, let me recognise the very good progress made in supervisory, crisis management and regulatory areas through the Banking Union. The Banking Union corrects basic flaws we have had in our internationally integrated financial markets. And in doing that, national interests, and I argue that banks' interests as well, are taken care of when matching regulatory and supervisory institutions with the reality of banking business. A structure which for the first time in the history of the European Union will allow the banking supervision and resolution mechanism to be based on a truly European mandate. By giving up a small part of the national sovereignty, the countries belonging to the Banking Union have gained access to the European level decision making on key areas of supervision, crisis prevention and management as well as regulation of European banks. The Bank of Finland, headed by Risto Ryti, also had to face the economic stability of the financial markets. In the early 1930s, the opaha spiralo nsys was made possible. However, Nsin did not happen. One of the reasons for this was that lessons had been learned from the experience of the 1930s. The Czech doctrine was that the liquidity of the banking system must be taken care of by all means to ensure that the circulation of the economy is not interrupted. Professor Ben Bernanke of Princeton University joined the Executive Board of the Federal Reserve System in autumn 2002. It was a challenging time, as the United States was in a state of recession and, partly because of the events of September 2001, there was a high level of certainty. At that time, the possibility of myshs deflation was seriously discussed in the United States. If, in spite of everything, we find ourselves in a deflationary situation, then, according to Bernanke, we must act proactively and aggressively. The measures include, if necessary, even massive purchases on the securities markets. In addition to sovereign securities, purchases can also be made, either directly or directly, by credit to banks, subject to the separate requirement of private debt securities as collateral. It was all said in the autumn of 2002, when the probability of deflationary developments was very low and Bernanke was even accused of exaggeration. Then came the fall of 2008, when Bernanke had already been president of the Federal Reserve for three years. Fortunately, the 2002 speech was still there. Almost all of the measures listed therein were taken. What has been the result? The deflationary spiral has been successfully combated. Bernanke's Czech goal has thus been achieved. This is important for the world economy as a whole, because the fall of the United States into a recession such as that of the 1930s would have dragged the rest of the world into the same abyss. [Figure 10] sms was the third nsks angle on monetary policy. Its lesson is that, in exceptional circumstances, one must be prepared to take extraordinary measures to prevent the economy from falling into a negative spiral, as it did in the 1930s. In other words, monetary policy is not just a cyclical policy but, in some situations, a crisis management policy. It is a bit of a quibble on the part of mssr to consider how much exceptional measures will revive, that is, increase gross domestic product, if the greatest impact is on preventing a further decline in GDP. 4. THE LESSONS OF HIGH INFLATION [Figure 11] In general, the aim of monetary policy has always been to safeguard the value of money. Sometimes it has been successful, sometimes it has not. The 1970s can be seen as an example of industrialization. Whereas in the 1960s inflation in developed industrialised countries had generally been below five per cent, in the 1970s consumer prices in many countries rose by more than 10% per annum, in some countries such as Britain and Japan by 25%. In Finland, too, inflation rose by 20% in the middle of the decade. Nsms are the times that many representatives of the large classes remember well in those days because of the fact that, during the period of interest rates, inflation paid off a large part of the debts. Few people remember that, due to the lack of credit, loans were obtained by the best customers or friends at the same time as the real value of depositors' wealth declined. The transfer of wealth from depositors to the debtor took place without anyone having done so. High inflation is an example of the economic downturn in monetary policy. EpShotization was systemic. It happened lshes in all countries. Germany survived best of all because of the fact that the Bundesbank was itself and its primary objective was to ensure price stability. Elsewhere, the objectives were epsmsssisis. In many countries, the collapse of the Bretton Woods system had led to central banks without a nominal anchor. We were not used to floating courses. An inflation target strategy had not yet been invented. In addition, the epsitsens central banks often had to give in to the will of governments not to tighten monetary policy even if inflationary developments were necessary. In the early 1980s, inflation began to be deliberately beaten. This was relatively successful, but the path to lower inflation (so-called disinflation) was achieved through a recession. The experience of the 1970s involved many things. Monetary policy began to be assessed from the new nsks angle. There was a fairly broad consensus among policy makers and academics that the central banks' objective should be clearly limited to price stability and that central banks should be guaranteed the self-determination to act to achieve this goal. In return, greater transparency and accountability are required of the Central Bank. By the last 1990s, all developed countries had switched to this kind of system. One and more central banks adopted the inflation target. The targeted inflation rate was typically around two per cent. The central bank was required to communicate its policy strategy in such a way that the markets and the general public could anticipate the central bank's future actions. How did ssss succeed? It was a great success, and some people think it was all too well. In the 1990s, inflation rates stabilised at two per cent in most countries and inflation fluctuations were small. Volatility arose from large changes in relative prices, such as fluctuations in the price of sljy and food. At the same time, fluctuations in total output also levelled off. We began to talk about a period of great moderation. The term Great Moderation, which swam into the International Order, was originally coined by Ben Bernanke. But this success kept the seed of a new success. Stable inflation and stable economic growth lowered the risk balance. From countries such as China and the producer countries, investments trickled into the United States, pushing down long-term interest rates. The general fall in yields encouraged the search for new, higher-yielding but at the same time higher-risk investments. When they were not there, they began to be built. Reduced yields and new instruments led to the accumulation of risks in the system, the location of which were not identified. When the existence of risks was foreseen, confidence began to grow. The complex financial system proved to be fragile. [Figure 12] sms was the fourth corner of monetary policy. Its strongest lesson is that, in order to ensure the achievement of its basic objective of price stability, the central bank needs a clear nominal anchor, an inflation target, and a clear strategy explaining how the central bank will act to achieve this target. The second lesson is that financial market stability is a thing of the same as price stability and that price stability is not Vsltsmss ensures the stability of the financial markets. Monetary policy alone cannot safeguard the stability of the financial markets. It requires other policies, such as macroprudential policies and good faith. 5. THE ECB'S RESPONSE TO THE CRISIS The first wave of the financial crisis hit Europe in early August 2007. Hsiris in the money market was leading to the drying up of bank liquidity. The ECB reacted to the hsirisssn vslitchsms by making a sale of just under 100 billion in liquidity to banks in a finest operation. [Figure 13] This was the beginning of a long-standing crisis of confidence, including an increase in EURIBOR rates, even though monetary interest rates had not been affected. The rise in interest rates reflected an increase in risks. The second wave was already much bigger and more serious. It was triggered by the bankruptcy of investment bank Lehman Brothers in September 2008. The effects were dramatic both in the financial markets and in the real economy. World trade and industrial production collapsed, all investment plans were put on hold. In Finland, gdp plummeted by ten per cent, even though we did not have a banking problem. Central banks reacted to the recession by lowering their key interest rates to zero in the short term. The responses to the problems in the financial markets differed from one environment to another. The ECB secured the liquidity of banks by taking steps to provide banks with credit against collateral at a fixed interest rate without restrictions. The maturity of the loans was also extended. Some purchases of securities were made in 2009d 2011. Eurojses system central banks initially bought the so-called "eurobanks". covered bonds will revive the functioning of the market. Government bonds were also bought on the czech market. The purchases were made in the so-called "green belt". to the bonds of crisis countries. There was no question of lightening up at that stage. However, the measures in the balance sheet of the euro system will initially take the form of an increase in the amount of monetary policy credit and, more recently, an increase in monetary policy portfolio investments. On the other side of the balance sheet, this is seen as an increase in banks' central bank deposits. From the banks' point of view, there was the highest level of liquidity, which in the banks' markets pushed down the shortest money market interest rates. [Figure 14] The worsening of the sovereign debt crisis led to a crisis of confidence in the second half of 2011. The process of keeping the euro together began. At the end of the year, the banks' financial markets will be re-established. We began to fear that the panic would recur. At that point, the euro system carried out a massive credit operation. Banks were offered the opportunity to borrow money from the central bank against collateral for three years at a very low interest rate. The crisis of confidence worsened in the summer of 2012. This confidence spread to the Spanish and Italian government bond markets. This was further fuelled by the ongoing debate on the possibility of a break-up of the euro area. In Heinsku in 2012, Mario Draghi gave his well-known speech in London, in which he announced that the Governing Council would do everything in its mandate to keep the euro in place. [Figure 15] During August and September, the Governing Council of the ECB decided on a so-called "green light". a programme of financial purchases, which may be taken into use if necessary. It was a question of a conditional purchase program for government bonds. The condition would be that the country (Spain or Italy) submits to the adjustment programme. There has been no need to take the program into use. In the middle of last year and in September, the Governing Council decided on new measures. These included a programme for the purchase of covered and asset-backed bonds and targeted loans to strengthen corporate finance. It was also announced that it was ready to launch massive purchases of securities if necessary to counter the threat of deflation. In January, the Council then announced the launch of an extended purchase programme. At the beginning of March, the ECB and the eurosystems' central banks will start buying securities of euro area governments, agencies and pan-European institutions on the secondary markets. Purchases under the programme will total EUR 60 billion per month, including purchases of covered bonds and asset-backed securities. The programme will be extended at least until the end of September 2016 and, if necessary, longer until the Governing Council estimates that inflation rates in the euro area are returning to the target level of just under two per cent. Msssllinen keventsminen is the latest monetary policy instrument that has been adopted during a protracted crisis. Initially, the response to the recession was to reduce monetary interest rates in a short period of time to zero. The liquidity of banks is secured by credit operations. The non-functioning of some financial market segments was addressed by purchase programmes (covered bonds, sovereign paper markets in some countries). All the measures have had the intended effects. They have also revived, but of course they have been sufficient to put Europe on a growth path. Realistically speaking, no one expected in a situation where the deleveraging is still in progress and where different countries are known to have different levels of rigidity in the labour market and product markets. The effects of the Mssrsllis keventsm have already been presented. Studies have shown that in the United States and England, the yellowing of the country, especially in the early stages, had a positive impact on gdp and inflation. No one has calculated how much gross domestic product would have fallen and the price level would have fallen if exceptional measures had not been taken at all. Why can it be said with certainty that a rapid fall in interest rates and extraordinary measures have prevented the world economy from entering a recession similar to that of the 1930s. Monetary policy has often been accused of failing to prevent crises from arising. Then it is blamed for not being able to quickly lift the country out of recession. Such criticism assumes, at least in the ranks, that the central bank is omnipotent, that it can do almost anything within its mandate. Let us forget that there are other areas of economic policy, such as fiscal policy and structural policy. If they are not tuned in such a way that they support stable and sustained economic growth, monetary policy alone cannot guarantee it. [Figure 16] sms was the fifth nsks angle on monetary policy. Its lesson is that monetary policy is not omnipotent. Long-term growth comes from productivity. It cannot be guided by monetary policy. Stability is achieved by maintaining a reasonable level of public and private sector indebtedness. Monetary policy can be influenced by interest rate control somewhere in the world, but the interest rate does not bite into the kind of indebtedness that originates, for example, from the pssoma movement or from financial innovation. Ben Bernanke has outlined that the central bank can best promote economic growth in the long term in a stable and low level of inflation. In Washington, we met with Ben Bernanke, the fed's soon-to-be president. Hshnelch the question was asked as to what was the doctrine of the Czechs, which hsn had learned deeply about the depression of the 1930s. Hsn said that the most important thing is to take care of the liquidity of the banks. He also asked why the current crisis has been new compared to previous crises. Hsn replied that it has been new to see how enormously complex the financial sector has become. It is a challenge not only for monetary policy, but also, and in particular, for financial supervision and the sshining of the financial markets. SUUREN INFLAATION OPETUKSET [Kuva 11] Rahapolitiikan tavoitteena on yleens aina ollut rahan arvon turvaaminen. Joskus siin on onnistuttu, joskus ei. 1970-lukua voi pit esimerkkin eponnistumisesta. Kun inflaatio kehittyneiss teollisuusmaissa oli 1960-luvulla ollut yleens viiden prosentin alapuolella, 1970-luvulla kuluttajahinnat nousivat monissa maissa yli 10 prosenttia vuodessa, joissakin maissa, kuten Britanniassa ja Japanissa perti 25 prosenttia. Suomessakin inflaatio nousi lhelle 20 prosenttia vuosikymmenen puolivliss. Nm ovat niit aikoja, joita monet suurten ikluokkien edustajat muistavat hyvin aikoina sen takia, ett snnsteltyjen korkojen aikana inflaatio maksoi suuren osan veloista. Harva muistaa sit, ett luotonsnnstelyn vuoksi lainoja saivat lhinn parhaat asiakkaat tai kaverit samalla kun tallettajien varallisuuden reaaliarvo supistui. Varallisuuden siirto tallettajilta velalliselle tapahtui ilman, ett kukaan olisi tehnyt siit mitn ptst. Suuri inflaatio on esimerkki rahapolitiikan eponnistumisesta. Eponnistuminen oli systeemist. Se tapahtui lhes kaikissa maissa. Saksa selvisi kaikkein parhaiten sen takia, ett Bundesbank oli itseninen ja sen ensisijaiseksi tavoitteeksi oli asetettu hintavakauden turvaaminen. Muualla tavoitteet olivat epmrisi. Monissa maissa Bretton Woods -jrjestelmn murtuminen oli jttnyt keskuspankit ilman nimellist ankkuria. Kelluviin kursseihin ei ollut totuttu. Inflaatiotavoitestrategiaa ei viel ollut keksitty. Lisksi epitseniset keskuspankit joutuivat usein taipumaan hallitusten tahtoon olla kiristmtt rahapolitiikkaa vaikka inflaatiokehitys olisi sit edellyttnyt. Inflaatiota alettiin nujertaa mrtietoisesti 1980-luvun alussa. Siin onnistuttiinkin suhteellisen nopeasti, mutta tie hitaampaan inflaatioon (ns. disinflaatio) kvi taantuman kautta. 1970-luvun kokemus jtti jlkens moneen asiaan. Rahapolitiikkaa alettiin arvioida uudesta nkkulmasta. Vhitellen syntyi aika laaja yksimielisyys politiikantekijiden ja tutkijoiden keskuudessa siit, ett keskuspankkien tavoite tulee rajata selvsti hintavakauteen ja ett keskuspankeille tulee taata itsenisyys toimia tmn tavoitteen saavuttamiseksi. Vastapainoksi keskuspankilta edellytetn aiempaa suurempaa avoimuutta ja tilivelvollisuutta. Viimeistn 1990-luvulla lhes kaikissa kehittyneiss maissa oli siirrytty tllaiseen jrjestelmn. Yh useampi keskuspankki otti kyttn inflaatiotavoitteen. Tavoiteltu inflaatio oli tyypillisesti kahden prosentin paikkeilla. Keskuspankin edellytettiin kertovan toimintastrategiansa siten, ett markkinat ja suuri yleis osaavat ennakoida keskuspankin tulevat toimet. Miten tss onnistuttiin? Onnistuttiin varsin hyvin, joidenkin mielest liiankin hyvin. 1990-luvulla inflaatiovauhti vakiintui useimmissa maissa lhelle kahta prosenttia ja inflaatiovauhdin vaihtelut jivt pieniksi. Volatiilisuus syntyi lhinn suurista suhteellisten hintojen muutoksista, kuten ljyn ja ruoan hinnan vaihteluista. Samaan aikaan mys kokonaistuotannon vaihtelut tasoittuivat. Alettiin puhua suuren maltillistumisen ajasta. Kansainvliseen kyttn uinut termi Great Moderation oli alun perin Ben Bernanken lanseeraama. Mutta tm onnistuminen piti sislln uuden eponnistumisen siemenen. Vakaa inflaatio ja vakaa talouskasvu alensivat riskilisi. Ylijmmaista, kuten Kiinasta ja ljyntuottajamaista, valui sijoituksia Yhdysvaltoihin, mik painoi pitki korkoja alaspin. Tuottojen yleinen aleneminen kannusti etsimn uusia, korkeampituottoisia mutta samalla korkeampiriskisi sijoituskohteita. Kun niit ei ollut, niit ryhdyttiin rakentamaan. Alentuneet tuotot ja uudet instrumentit johtivat siihen, ett systeemiin alkoi kasaantua riskej, joiden mr ja sijaintia ei tunnistettu. Kun riskien olemassaolo aavistettiin, epluottamus alkoi kasvaa. Monimutkainen rahoitusjrjestelm osoittautui hauraaksi. [Kuva 12] Tm oli neljs nkkulma rahapolitiikkaan. Sen trkein opetus on se, ett voidakseen turvata perustavoiteensa, hintavakauden, toteutumisen, keskuspankki tarvitsee selken nimellisen ankkurin, inflaatiotavoitteen, ja selke strategian, joka kertoo, miten keskuspankki toimii tmn tavoitteen saavuttamiseksi. Toinen opetus on se, ett rahoitusmarkkinoiden vakaus on yht trke asia kuin hintavakaus ja ett hintavakaus ei vlttmtt takaa rahoitusmarkkinoiden vakautta. Pelkll rahapolitiikalla ei voi turvata rahoitusmarkkinoiden vakautta. Siihen tarvitaan muitakin vlineit, kuten makrovakauspolitiikkaa ja hyv stely. 5. EKP:N TOIMINTA KRIISIN AIKANA Finanssikriisin ensimminen aalto iski Eurooppaan elokuun alussa 2007. Hiri rahamarkkinoilla oli johtamassa pankkien likviditeetin kuivumiseen. EKP reagoi hirin vlittmsti toteuttamalla myymll ylimrisess hienostoperaatiossa pankeille likviditeetti vajaan 100 miljardin euron edest. [Kuva 13] Tm oli alku pitkaikaiselle luottamuspulalle, mik nkyi mm. euribor-korkojen nousuna, vaikka rahapoliittisille koroille ei ollut tehty mitn. Korkojen nousu kuvasti riskien kasvamista. Toinen aalto olikin sitten jo paljon isompi ja vakavampi. Sen laukaisi investointipankki Lehman Brothersin konkurssi syyskuussa 2008. Vaikutukset olivat dramaattiset sek rahoitusmarkkinoilla ett reaalitaloudessa. Maailmankauppa ja teollisuustuotanto romahtivat, kaikki investointisuunnitelmat pantiin jihin. Suomessa bruttokansantuote romahti lhes kymmenen prosenttia, vaikka meill ei mitn pankkiongelmaa ollutkaan. Keskuspankit reagoivat taantumaan alentamalla ohjauskorkonsa lyhyess ajassa lhelle nollaa. Rahoitusmarkkinoiden ongelmiin reagoitiin eri tavoin eri ympristiss. EKP turvasi pankkien likviditeetin ryhtymll tarjoamaan pankeille luottoja vakuuksia vastaan kiintell korolla ilman mrrajoituksia. Mys luottojen maturiteettia pidennettiin. Vuosina 20092011 toteutettiin jonkin verran arvopaperiostoja. Eurojrjestelmn keskuspankit ostivat aluksi ns. katettuja joukkovelkakirjoja elvyttkseen niden markkinoiden toiminnan. Myhemmin ostettiin jlkimarkkinoilta valtion velkakirjoja. Ostot kohdistuivat tllin ns. kriisimaiden joukkovelkakirjoihin. Mistn mrllisest kevennyksest ei tss vaiheessa ollut kysymys. Toimenpiteet nkyivt kuitenkin eurojrjestelmn taseessa aluksi rahapoliittisten luottojen mrn paisumisena ja myhemmin rahapoliittisten arvopaperisijoitusten mrn lisntymisen. Taseen toisella puolella tm nkyi pankkien keskuspankkitalletusten mrn kasvuna. Pankkien kannalta tm oli ylimrist likviditeetti, joka pankkien vlisill markkinoilla tynsi lyhimmt rahamarkkinakorot alaspin. [Kuva 14] Valtioiden velkakriisin paheneminen johti 2011 jlkipuoliskolla luottamuskriisiin. Euron koossa pysymist alettiin epill. Vuoden lopussa pankkien vliset rahamarkkinat hiriintyivt uudelleen. Alettiin pelt, ett paniikki uusiutuu. Tuossa vaiheessa eurojrjestelm toteutti massiivisen luotto-operaation. Pankeille tarjottiin mahdollisuus lainata keskuspankista rahaa vakuuksia vastaan kolmeksi vuodeksi hyvin alhaisella korolla. Luottamuskriisi paheni kesll 2012. Epluottamus levisi Espanjan ja Italian valtion velkakirjamarkkinoille. Sit vauhditti edelleen jatkuva keskustelu euroalueen hajoamisen mahdollisuudesta. Heinkuussa 2012 Mario Draghi piti Lontoossa tunnetun puheensa, jossa hn ilmoitti, ett EKP:n neuvosto tekee mandaattinsa puitteissa kaikkensa euron silyttmiseksi. [Kuva 15] Elo-ja syyskuun aikana EKP:n neuvosto ptti ns. rahataloudellisten ostojen ohjelmasta, joka voidaan tarvittaessa ottaa kyttn. Kysymys oli valtion velkakirjojen ehdollisesta osto-ohjelmasta. Ehtona olisi se, ett maa (Espanja tai Italia) alistuisi sopeuttamisohjelmaan. Ohjelmaa ei ole tarvinnut ottaa kyttn. Viime vuoden kes-ja syyskuussa EKP:n neuvosto ptti uusista toimenpiteist. Niihin kuului katettujen ja omaisuusvakuudellisten joukkovelkakirjojen osto-ohjelma sek yritysrahoituksen vahvistamiseksi tarkoitetut kohdennetut luotot. Lisksi ilmoitettiin valmiudesta aloittaa tarvittaessa massiiviset arvopaperiostot deflaatiouhan torjumiseksi. Tammikuussa neuvosto sitten ilmoitti laajennetun osto-ohjelman aloittamisesta. Maaliskuun alussa EKP ja eurojrjestelmn keskuspankit alkavat ostaa jlkimarkkinoilta euroalueen valtioiden, valtiosidonnaisten laitosten ja yleiseurooppalaisten laitosten arvopapereita. Ohjelman mukaiset ostot tulevat olemaan yhteens 60 miljardia euroa kuukaudessa, mik sislt katettujen joukkolainojen ja omaisuusvakuudellisten arvopaperien ostot. Ohjelmaa jatketaan ainakin vuoden 2016 syyskuun loppuun saakka ja tarvittaessa kauemminkin, kunnes EKP:n neuvosto arvioi euroalueen inflaatiovauhdin olevan kestvsti palautumassa tavoitteen mukaiselle hieman alle kahden prosentin inflaatiovauhdin tasolle. Mrllinen keventminen on viimeisin rahapoliittinen keino, joka pitkittyneen kriisin aikana on otettu kyttn. Aluksi taantumaan reagoitiin alentamalla rahapoliittiset korot lyhyess ajassa lhelle nollaa. Pankkien likviditeetti on turvattu luotto-operaatioilla. Joidenkin rahoitusmarkkinasegmenttien toimimattomuuteen reagoitiin osto.ohjelmilla (katetut joukkovelkakirjat, joidenkin maiden valtionpaperimarkkinat). Kaikilla nill toimenpiteill on ollut tavoiteltuja vaikutuksia. Ne ovat mys elvyttneet, mutta totta kai ne ovat olleet riittmttmi nostamaan Eurooppaa kasvu-uralle. Realisesti ajatellen kukaan sit tuskin odottikaan tilanteessa jossa velkaantumisen purkaminen on viel kesken ja jossa eri valtiot tunnetusti krsivt erilaisista jykkyyksist tymarkkinoilla ja tuotemarkkinoilla. Mrllisen keventmisen vaikutuksista on jo ehditty esitt epilyj. Tutkimusten mukaan Yhdysvalloissa ja Englannissa mrllisen keventminen varsinkin alkuvaiheessa vaikutti sek bruttokansantuotteeseen ett inflaatioon positiivisesti. Kukaan ei ole laskenut sit, kuinka paljon bruttokansantuote olisi laskenut ja hintataso alentunut, jos poikkeuksellisiin toimiin ei olisi lainkaan ryhdytty. Se, mik varmuudella voidaan sanoa, ett nopealla korkojen laskulla ja poikkeuksellisilla toimilla on estetty se, ett maailmantalous olisi ajautunut 1930-luvun kaltaiseen lamaan. Rahapolitiikkaa on usein syytetty siit, ett se ei ole onnistunut estmn kriisien syntymist. Sitten sit syytetn siit, ett se ei pysty nopeasti nostamaan maata taantuman ikeest. Tllaisessa kritiikiss oletetaan ainakin rivien vliss, ett keskuspankki on kaikkivoipa, ett se pystyy mandaattinsa puitteissa tekemn miltei mit tahansa. Unohdetaan, ett on muitakin talouspolitiikan lohkoja, kuten finanssipolitiikka ja rakennepolitiikka. Jos nit ei ole viritetty siten, ett ne tukevat vakaata ja kestv talouskasvua, rahapolitiikka ei voi sit yksinn taata. [Kuva 16] Tm oli viides nkkulma rahapolitiikkaan. Sen trkein opetus on, ett rahapolitiikka ei ole kaikkivoipa. Pitkn aikavlin kasvu syntyy tuottavuudesta. Sit ei voi ohjata rahapolitiikalla. Vakaus syntyy siit, ett julkisen ja yksityisen sektorin velkaantuminen pysyy kohtuullisena. Siihen rahapolitiikkaa pystyy korko-ohjauksen kautta jossain mrin vaikuttamaan, mutta korko ei pure sellaiseen velkaantumiseen, joka lhtee liikkeelle esimerkiksi pomaliikkeist tai finanssi-innovaatioista. Ben Bernanke on esittnyt, ett keskuspankki voi edist kestv talouskasvua pitkll aikavlill parhaiten pitmll inflaation vakaana ja matalana. LOPUKSI [Kuva 17] Suomen Pankin pankkivaltuusto teki viime vuoden tammikuussa vierailun Washingtoniin ja New Yorkiin. Olin itse mukana matkalla. Washingtonissa tapasimme Fedin kohta vistyvn pjohtajana Ben Bernanken. Hnelt kysyttiin, mik oli trkein oppi, jonka hn oli saanut perehtyessn syvllisesti 1930-luvun lamaan. Hn sanoi, ett trkein asia on pankkien likviditeetist huolehtiminen. Hnelt kysyttiin mys, mik on nykyisess kriisiss ollut uutta aikaisempiin kriiseihin verrattuna. Hn vastasi, ett uutta on ollut huomata, miten valtavan monimutkaiseksi, kompleksiseksi rahoitussektori on kehittynyt. Se on haaste paitsi rahapolitiikalle, mys ja erityisesti rahoitusvalvonnalle ja rahoitusmarkkinoiden snnstelylle. Kiitokset johtokunnan neuvonantaja, tohtori Antti Suvannolle, jonka lukuisiin esityksiin ja artikkeleihin tm puhe perustuu. Finland borde i princip ha goda frutsttningar fr att vnda klken i rtt riktning. Generellt sett, p lng sikt beror den ekonomiska utvecklingen i hg grad p hur vlfungerande institutioner ett land har: rttsvsendet, den offentliga frvaltningen, utbildningssystemet och s vidare. Med de hr goda fundamenten och ngra grna skott  konsumenternas frtroendeindikator har stigit klart under de senaste mnaderna  kan vi nnu inte garantera ekonomisk terhmtning utan vi mste vidta tgrdar. [Bild 8] Frst mste vi strka vr internationella konkurrenskraft. Vi mste genomfra omfattande strukturella reformer som skapar frutsttningar fr tillvxt. Vi mste konsolidera de offentliga finanserna och samtidigt vrna om vlfrdsstatens viktigaste funktioner  och detta utan att ingripa i ekonomins frmga att skapa nya arbetsplatser. [Bild 9] Det r bra att finlndarna har identifierat vad svrigheterna i ekonomin beror p. Problemen kan inte bara skyllas p den internationella finanskrisen och p Europas skuldproblem. En sak som vi inte heller ska glmma bort r att Finland befinner sig i krnan d det gller ekonomiska frgor och utvecklingstgrder i Europa. Stabilitet, trygghet och likvrdiga konkurrensfrhllanden fr business r viktigt. Vi behver inte oroa oss fr sdan valutaspekulation som kan drabba ett land med en liten valuta.
