Alettiin puhua suuren maltillistumisen ajasta. Kansainvliseen kyttn uinut termi Great Moderation oli alun perin Ben Bernanken lanseeraama. Mutta tm onnistuminen piti sislln uuden eponnistumisen siemenen. Vakaa inflaatio ja vakaa talouskasvu alensivat riskilisi. Ylijmmaista, kuten Kiinasta ja ljyntuottajamaista, valui sijoituksia Yhdysvaltoihin, mik painoi pitki korkoja alaspin. Tuottojen yleinen aleneminen kannusti etsimn uusia, korkeampituottoisia mutta samalla korkeampiriskisi sijoituskohteita. Kun niit ei ollut, niit ryhdyttiin rakentamaan. Alentuneet tuotot ja uudet instrumentit johtivat siihen, ett systeemiin alkoi kasaantua riskej, joiden mr ja sijaintia ei tunnistettu. Kun riskien olemassaolo aavistettiin, epluottamus alkoi kasvaa. Monimutkainen rahoitusjrjestelm osoittautui hauraaksi. [Kuva 11] Keskuspankki tarvitsee selken ja helposti viestitettvn tavoitteen rahapolitiikalleen. Lisksi keskuspankki tarvitsee selken strategian, joka kertoo, miten keskuspankki toimii tmn tavoitteen saavuttamiseksi. Rahoitusmarkkinoiden vakaus on trke, sill pelkll rahapolitiikalla ei voi turvata rahoitusmarkkinoiden vakautta. 5. RAHAPOLITIIKKA EI KAIKKIVOIPAA Finanssikriisin ensimminen aalto iski Eurooppaan elokuun alussa 2007. Hiri rahamarkkinoilla oli johtamassa pankkien likviditeetin kuivumiseen. EKP reagoi hirin vlittmsti toteuttamalla myymll ylimrisess hienostoperaatiossa pankeille likviditeetti vajaan 100 miljardin euron edest. [Kuva 12] Tm oli alku pitkaikaiselle luottamuspulalle, mik nkyi mm. euribor-korkojen nousuna, vaikka rahapoliittisille koroille ei ollut tehty mitn. Korkojen nousu kuvasti riskien kasvamista. Toinen aalto olikin sitten jo paljon isompi ja vakavampi. Sen laukaisi investointipankki Lehman Brothersin konkurssi syyskuussa 2008. Vaikutukset olivat dramaattiset sek rahoitusmarkkinoilla ett reaalitaloudessa. Maailmankauppa ja teollisuustuotanto romahtivat, kaikki investointisuunnitelmat pantiin jihin. Suomessa bruttokansantuote romahti lhes kymmenen prosenttia, vaikka meill ei mitn pankkiongelmaa ollutkaan. Keskuspankit reagoivat taantumaan alentamalla ohjauskorkonsa lyhyess ajassa lhelle nollaa. Rahoitusmarkkinoiden ongelmiin reagoitiin eri tavoin eri ympristiss. EKP turvasi pankkien likviditeetin ryhtymll tarjoamaan pankeille luottoja vakuuksia vastaan kiintell korolla ilman mrrajoituksia. Mys luottojen maturiteettia pidennettiin. Vuosina 20092011 toteutettiin jonkin verran arvopaperiostoja. Eurojrjestelmn keskuspankit ostivat aluksi ns. katettuja joukkovelkakirjoja elvyttkseen niden markkinoiden toiminnan. Myhemmin ostettiin jlkimarkkinoilta valtion velkakirjoja. Ostot kohdistuivat tllin ns. kriisimaiden joukkovelkakirjoihin. Mistn mrllisest kevennyksest ei tss vaiheessa ollut kysymys. Toimenpiteet nkyivt kuitenkin eurojrjestelmn taseessa aluksi rahapoliittisten luottojen mrn paisumisena ja myhemmin rahapoliittisten arvopaperisijoitusten mrn lisntymisen. Taseen toisella puolella tm nkyi pankkien keskuspankkitalletusten mrn kasvuna. Pankkien kannalta tm oli ylimrist likviditeetti, joka pankkien vlisill markkinoilla tynsi lyhimmt rahamarkkinakorot alaspin. [Kuva 13] Valtioiden velkakriisin paheneminen johti 2011 jlkipuoliskolla luottamuskriisiin. Euron koossa pysymist alettiin epill. Vuoden lopussa pankkien vliset rahamarkkinat hiriintyivt uudelleen. Alettiin pelt, ett paniikki uusiutuu. Tuossa vaiheessa eurojrjestelm toteutti massiivisen luotto-operaation. Pankeille tarjottiin mahdollisuus lainata keskuspankista rahaa vakuuksia vastaan kolmeksi vuodeksi hyvin alhaisella korolla. Luottamuskriisi paheni kesll 2012. Epluottamus levisi Espanjan ja Italian valtion velkakirjamarkkinoille. Sit vauhditti edelleen jatkuva keskustelu euroalueen hajoamisen mahdollisuudesta. Heinkuussa 2012 Mario Draghi piti Lontoossa tunnetun puheensa, jossa hn ilmoitti, ett EKP:n neuvosto tekee mandaattinsa puitteissa kaikkensa euron silyttmiseksi. [Kuva 14] Elo-ja syyskuun 2012 aikana EKP:n neuvosto ptti ns. rahataloudellisten ostojen ohjelmasta, joka voidaan tarvittaessa ottaa kyttn. Kysymys oli valtion velkakirjojen ehdollisesta osto-ohjelmasta. Ehtona olisi se, ett maa (Espanja tai Italia) alistuisi sopeuttamisohjelmaan. Ohjelmaa ei ole tarvinnut ottaa kyttn. Viime vuoden kes-ja syyskuussa EKP:n neuvosto ptti uusista toimenpiteist. Niihin kuului katettujen ja omaisuusvakuudellisten joukkovelkakirjojen osto-ohjelma sek yritysrahoituksen vahvistamiseksi tarkoitetut kohdennetut luotot. Lisksi ilmoitettiin valmiudesta aloittaa tarvittaessa massiiviset arvopaperiostot deflaatiouhan torjumiseksi. Tammikuussa neuvosto sitten ilmoitti laajennetun osto-ohjelman aloittamisesta. Maaliskuun alussa EKP ja eurojrjestelmn keskuspankit alkavat ostaa jlkimarkkinoilta euroalueen valtioiden, valtiosidonnaisten laitosten ja yleiseurooppalaisten laitosten arvopapereita. Ohjelman mukaiset ostot tulevat olemaan yhteens 60 miljardia euroa kuukaudessa, mik sislt katettujen joukkolainojen ja omaisuusvakuudellisten arvopaperien ostot. Ohjelmaa jatketaan ainakin vuoden 2016 syyskuun loppuun saakka ja tarvittaessa kauemminkin, kunnes EKP:n neuvosto arvioi euroalueen inflaatiovauhdin olevan kestvsti palautumassa tavoitteen mukaiselle hieman alle kahden prosentin inflaatiovauhdin tasolle. Mrllinen keventminen on viimeisin rahapoliittinen keino, joka pitkittyneen kriisin aikana on otettu kyttn. Aluksi taantumaan reagoitiin alentamalla rahapoliittiset korot lyhyess ajassa lhelle nollaa. Pankkien likviditeetti on turvattu luotto-operaatioilla. Joidenkin rahoitusmarkkinasegmenttien toimimattomuuteen reagoitiin osto.ohjelmilla (katetut joukkovelkakirjat, joidenkin maiden valtionpaperimarkkinat). Kaikilla nill toimenpiteill on ollut tavoiteltuja vaikutuksia. Ne ovat mys elvyttneet, mutta totta kai ne ovat olleet riittmttmi nostamaan Eurooppaa kasvu-uralle. Realisesti ajatellen kukaan sit tuskin odottikaan tilanteessa jossa velkaantumisen purkaminen on viel kesken ja jossa eri valtiot tunnetusti krsivt erilaisista jykkyyksist tymarkkinoilla ja tuotemarkkinoilla. Mrllisen keventmisen vaikutuksista on jo ehditty esitt epilyj. Tutkimusten mukaan Yhdysvalloissa ja Englannissa mrllisen keventminen varsinkin alkuvaiheessa vaikutti sek bruttokansantuotteeseen ett inflaatioon positiivisesti. Kukaan ei ole laskenut sit, kuinka paljon bruttokansantuote olisi laskenut ja hintataso alentunut, jos poikkeuksellisiin toimiin ei olisi lainkaan ryhdytty. Se, mik varmuudella voidaan sanoa, ett nopealla korkojen laskulla ja poikkeuksellisilla toimilla on estetty se, ett maailmantalous olisi ajautunut 1930-luvun kaltaiseen lamaan. Rahapolitiikkaa on usein syytetty siit, ett se ei ole onnistunut estmn kriisien syntymist. Sitten sit syytetn siit, ett se ei pysty nopeasti nostamaan maata taantuman ikeest. Tllaisessa kritiikiss oletetaan ainakin rivien vliss, ett keskuspankki on kaikkivoipa, ett se pystyy mandaattinsa puitteissa tekemn miltei mit tahansa. Unohdetaan, ett on muitakin talouspolitiikan lohkoja, kuten finanssipolitiikka ja rakennepolitiikka. Jos nit ei ole viritetty siten, ett ne tukevat vakaata ja kestv talouskasvua, rahapolitiikka ei voi sit yksinn taata. [Kuva 15] Rahapolitiikka ei ole kaikkivoipa eik yleislke talouden ongelmiin. Pitkn aikavlin kasvu syntyy tuottavuudesta. Kiitos! Hakkarainen (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tag=Hakkarainen)

Title: The Monetary Authority and the authority that manages the state treasury
text: Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen: The monetary authority and the authority responsible for the state treasury. Helsinki, 8.5.2015. Speeches andinterviews(/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and-interviews/) . Speech . Friday8 May 2015, 12:00 PM Pentti Hakkarainen Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors Investor event of the State Treasury and the Bank of Finland Bank of Finland Monetary Museum, 8.5.2015 THE MONETARY AUTHORITY AND THE AUTHORITY RESPONSIBLE FOR THE TREASURY Checkagainst delivery Each country needs an organisation or organisations whose job it is to manage national wealth. In Finland, the managers of national financial assets are the State Treasury and the Bank of Finland. Both organizations also have other roles. The Bank of Finland has two roles. It is the monetary authority of Finland and at the same time the European Central Bank system and the euro system. As the monetary authority, the Bank of Finland is responsible for the money supply and issue of banknotes, the holding and management of foreign exchange reserves and the reliability and efficiency of payment and other financing systems. In addition, the Bank of Finland is responsible for compiling and publishing the statistics necessary for its activities. As the monetary authority, the Bank of Finland also manages part of the national financial assets. The Bank of Finland has a moderate size of its own financial assets independent of monetary policy. It consists of gold and foreign currencies, as well as investments in the euro. At the end of April, the amount of the sMN pot was about 15 billion euros. 1 The primary objective of the Eurojs system and the Bank of Finland is to maintain price stability in the long term. The Bank must support the achievement of other economic policy objectives without jeopardising the priority. The Head of the Governing Council of the Bank of Finland is involved in all matters falling within the council's powers. The most important of these is monetary policy. Under normal circumstances, monetary policy is primarily interest rate policy. Now that monetary interest rates are at zero, we will have to resort to the same kind of means. The most recent is the extended securities purchase programme. The Bank of Finland shall contribute to the implementation of the single monetary policy. This means that the Bank of Finland lends money to counterparties operating in Finland and accepts deposits. The Bank of Finland has a long-standing system of banks' reserves, which provides banks with a flexible liquidity buffer. The payment system is a key element of the financial market infrastructure. The Bank of Finland will ensure that the core of the payment system, the real-time wholesale payment system operates in all circumstances. The wholesale payment system guarantees the finality of the payments. The amount of margin transfers made by the Bank of Finland's wholesale payment counterparties is considerable, recently amounting to around EUR 60 billion, of which the average payments of domestic operators cover approximately EUR 20 billion. The State Treasury is one of our wholesale payment customers. In addition to the Bank of Finland, the State Treasury is another key state actor in Finland that deals with money. The State Treasury's area of responsibility is extensive. We are interested in the State Treasury's financial sector, which is responsible for, among other things, government borrowing, debt and cash management and related risk management. In this area, the State Treasury and the Bank of Finland have a common interest in both professionally and at the level of the bank. The State Treasury is a central agency under the Minister of Finance, while the Bank of Finland is accountable to Parliament. In this context, it is interesting to create an eye on history. The State Treasury was established by the Imperial Declaration of 26 July 1875 for the management of the state's financial resources. It is therefore the 140th anniversary of its founding in Heinsku. Congratulations. Before Heinsku in 1875, the Bank of Finland had been responsible for managing the state's financial resources. A key reason for the establishment of the State Treasury was that in 1868 the Bank of Finland had been transferred from the Treasury of the Senate Finance Department to the State Council. The Senate, on the other hand, was subordinate to the emperor. It was considered that the management of the finances of the Senate was under the control of the Senate and the State Parliament, which is independent of the Emperor. In many countries, central banks manage the treasury and debt management policies. In other words, central banks act as fiscal agents of the government. Czech countries include the United States, The United Kingdom, Germany, Italy and Denmark. The reasons for such arrangements are historical, as many central banks were originally created to finance the state. The independence of central banks from governments has been strengthened in all developed countries over the last couple of decades, but it has done little to change the role of central banks as fiscal agents of the state. However, srkess is a longstanding monetary policy and the management of the state's finances in strict isolation. In monetary policy, the Central Bank acts independently, but as a fiscal agent it carries out the mandates of the Finance Minister.2 Our operations have been separate for 140 years. That's good. The Bank of Finland does not want to renew its tasks. The Bank of Finland relies on the expertise of the State Treasury. With its expertise, the State Treasury has already managed to acquire sssssjs for the state in the form of reduced interest costs. The central bank's role as a fiscal agent brings with it technical problems. When government payments pass through accounts with the central bank, large fluctuations arise in the liquidity of the banking system due to the fact that government payments are large and sometimes difficult to predict. In the 1990s, there were no problems with our own money. The Central Bank or the State Treasury does not measure the pace of indebtedness of central government debt. That's why the government and the parliament. The pace of indebtedness is so rapid that it raises concerns at the Bank of Finland and, I would assume, also at the State Treasury. As citizens, it is a concern for all of us, because it is our common debt. There are currently no problems with debt management or access to debt. However, they may arise if the trend of indebtedness is not reversed in the next few years. There has been a lot of encouraging news about the euro area economy in recent weeks. With the exception of Greece, europe's crisis countries are also promisingly recovering. Spain and Ireland seem to have seen the fastest economic growth in the euro area at the moment. In Finland, it is the slowest in the euro area. There are many authors behind the mysterious news. Growth is supported by the weakening of the euro and the fall in the price of the euro. Contrary to what might be said in the public debate, fiscal policy in the euro area is now more neutral than tightening. The ECB's monetary policy is functioning as expected. The extended purchase programme has addressed inflation expectations and deflationary fears. It is also one of the factors behind the depreciation of the euro. There is always another side to the coin. There are, of course, unwanted effects and risks associated with this. It has to be said that the undesirable effects and risks would also have been associated with the second option, that it would not have been done. The greatest risk would have been to drift into a deflationary balance, from which it could have taken a very long time to break away. Japan gives a cautionary example.3 The ECB's extended purchase programme, or "steering", is the theme of the morning presidency. Tuomas Vslimski, Head of the Monetary Policy and Research Department of the Bank of Finland, will begin by explaining the ECB's purchase programmes and their implementation. After that, Teppo Koivisto, Head of Finance at the State Treasury, explains why the purchase programme is about the issuer of government bonds. Finally, Mika Arola, Deputy Director of the State Treasury, will present at the Money Museum the idea of Our Common Debt, which has been opened for consideration and which deals with Finland's national debt. Viimeisin niist on laajennettu arvopapereiden osto-ohjelma. Suomen Pankki osallistuu yhteisen rahapolitiikan toteuttamiseen. Kytnnss tm tarkoittaa sit, ett Suomen Pankki lainaa rahaa Suomessa toimiville vastapuolille ja ottaa niilt vastaan talletuksia. Suomen Pankki pit yll pankkien vhimmisvarantojrjestelm, joka tarjoaa pankeille joustavan likviditeettipuskurin. Maksujrjestelm on keskeinen osa rahoitusmarkkinoiden infrastruktuuria. Suomen Pankki pit huolta siit, ett maksujrjestelm ydin, reaaliaikainen tukkumaksujrjestelm toimii kaikissa olosuhteissa. Tukkumaksujrjestelm takaa maksujen lopullisuuden. Suomen Pankin tukkumaksuvastapuolten tekemt pivittiset katesiirrot ovat huomattavan suuria, viime aikoina noin 60 miljardia euroa pivss, mist summasta kotimaisten toimijoiden keskiniset maksut kattavat noin 20 miljardia euroa. Valtiokonttori on yksi tukkumaksuasiakkaamme. Valtiokonttori on Suomen Pankin ohella toinen keskeinen rahan kanssa pivittin tekemisiss oleva valtiollinen toimija Suomessa. Valtiokonttorin tehtvalue on laaja. Meit tll tnn kiinnostaa Valtiokonttorin rahoitustoimiala, joka vastaa muun muassa valtion lainanotosta sek velan-ja kassanhallinnasta ja siihen liittyvst riskienhallinnasta. Tll alueella Valtiokonttorilla ja Suomen Pankilla on yhteisi intressej sek professionaalisesti ett kytnnn tasolla. Valtiokonttori on valtiovarainministerin alainen keskusvirasto, kun taas Suomen Pankki on tilivelvollinen eduskunnalle. Tss yhteydess on kiinnostavaa luoda silmys historiaan. Valtiokonttori perustettiin 26. heinkuuta 1875 annetulla keisarillisella julistuksella valtion rahavarain hoitoa varten. Perustamisesta tulee siis heinkuussa kuluneeksi 140 vuotta. Onneksi olkoon. Ennen heinkuuta 1875 valtion rahavarain hoitamisesta oli vastannut Suomen Pankki. Keskeinen syy Valtiokonttorin perustamiselle oli se, ett Suomen Pankki oli vuonna 1868 siirretty pois senaatin talousosaston valtiovaraintoimituskunnan alaisuudesta valtiopivien alaisuuteen. Senaatti taas oli keisarin alainen. Katsottiin, ett senaatille kuuluvien raha-asioiden hoito tytyy pit senaatin eik keisarista riippumattoman valtiopivlaitoksen valvonnassa. Monissa maissakeskuspankit hoitavat valtion kassaa ja velanhoitopolitiikkaa (debt management). Keskuspankit toisin sanoen toimivat valtiovallan fiskaalisina agentteina (fiscal agent). Tllaisia maita ovat muun muassa Yhdysvallat, Britannia, Saksa, Italia ja Tanska. Syyt tllaisiin jrjestelyihin ovat posin historiallisia, luotiinhan monet keskuspankit alun perin rahoittamaan valtiota. Keskuspankkien riippumattomuutta hallituksista on vahvistettu kaikissa kehittyneiss maissa parin viime vuosikymmenen aikana, mutta se ei ole juurikaan muuttanut keskuspankkien roolia valtion fiskaalisena agenttina. Trke on kuitenkin pit rahapolitiikka ja valtion raha-asiain hoito tiukasti erilln. Rahapolitiikassa keskuspankki toimii riippumattomasti, mutta fiskaalisena agenttina se toteuttaa valtiovarainministerin toimeksiantoja.2 Meill nm toiminnot ovat olleet erillisi jo 140 vuotta. Hyv niin. Suomen Pankissa ei haluta uusia tehtvi. Suomen Pankissa luotetaan Valtiokonttorin asiantuntemukseen. Asiantuntemuksellaan Valtiokonttori on jo thn menness onnistunut hankkimaan valtiolle sstj alentuneiden korkokustannusten muodossa. Keskuspankin toiminta fiskaalisena agenttina tuo mukanaan teknisi ongelmia. Kun valtion maksut kulkevat keskuspankissa olevien tilien kautta, pankkijrjestelmn likviditeettiin syntyy suuria vaihteluita sen takia, ett valtion maksut ovat suuria ja joskus vaikeasti ennustettavia. Meill nit ongelmia ei oman rahan aikana 1990.luvulla ollut. Keskuspankki taiValtiokonttori eivt pt valtionvelan mrst eik velkaantumisen vauhdista. Siit pttvt hallitus ja eduskunta. Velkaantumisen vauhti on tnn niin nopeaa, ett se hertt huolta Suomen Pankissa ja, nin olettaisin, mys Valtiokonttorissa. Kansalaisina se hertt huolta meiss kaikissa, onhan kyseess yhteinen velkamme. Tll hetkell velanhoidossa tai velan saatavuudessa ei ole ongelmia. Niit voi kuitenkin synty, mikli velkaantumisen trendi ei muutaman seuraavan vuoden aikana saada knnetyksi. Euroalueen taloudesta on viime viikkojen aikana tullut paljonkin rohkaisevia uutisia. Kreikkaa lukuun ottamatta mys Euroopan kriisimaat ovat lupaavasti elpymss. Euroalueen talouskasvu taitaa tll hetkell olla nopeinta Espanjassa ja Irlannissa. Suomessa se on euroalueen hitainta. Mynteisten uutisten takana on monia tekijit. Kasvua tukevat sek euron heikkeneminen ett ljyn hinnan lasku. Toisin kuin julkisesta keskustelusta voisi ptell, euroalueen finanssipolitiikka on nyt pikemminkin neutraalia kuin kiristv. EKP:n rahapolitiikka nytt toimivan odotetulla tavalla. Laajennettu osto-ohjelma on kntnyt inflaatio-odotukset ylspin ja vhentnyt deflaatiopelkoja. Se on mys yksi tekij euron heikkenemisen taustalla. Kolikolla on aina toinenkin puolensa. Mrlliseen keventmiseen liittyy, totta kai, mys ei-toivottuja vaikutuksia ja riskej. Thn on todettava, ett ei-toivotavia vaikutuksia ja riskej olisi liittynyt mys toiseen vaihtoehtoon, siihen, ett ei olisi tehty mitn. Suurin riski olisi ollut ajautuminen deflatoriseen tasapainoon, josta irtautuminen olisi voinut vied hyvin pitkn ajan. Japani antaa tst varoittavan esimerkin.3 EKP:n laajennettu osto-ohjelma eli mrllinen keventminen on tmn aamupivn teema. Suomen Pankin rahapolitiikka-ja tutkimusosaston osastopllikk Tuomas Vlimki kertoo aluksi EKP:n osto-ohjelmista ja niiden toteuttamisesta. Sen jlkeen Valtiokonttorin rahoitustoimialan toimialajohtaja Teppo Koivisto kertoo siit, milt osto-ohjelma nytt valtionobligaatioiden liikkeeseenlaskijan nkkulmasta. Lopuksi Valtiokonttorin apulaisjohtaja Mika Arola esittelee Rahamuseossa vastikn avatun, Suomen valtionvelkaa ksittelevn nyttelyn Yhteinen velkamme. Title: The international economy is strengthening, the domestic outlook is poor
text: Vice Chairman of the Board Pentti Hakkarainen: Kansainv?line's economy is strengthening, the domestic economy is bad. Vantaa 6.8.2015. . Speech . Thursday6August 2015, 1:15PM Pentti Hakkarainen Vice Chairman of the Board of Directors Event of the Economic and Financial Management of Large Cities Vantaa 6.8.2015 Esityskalvot (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and-interviews/documents/06082015-pentti. . hakkarainen.pdf) (PDF) INTERNATIONAL ECONOMY STRENGTHENS, DOMESTIC NdbTENdbT BAD Check against delivery FINNISH ECONOMYdbKYMdbT WEAKENED International economic growth has strengthened on a more broad scale. Despite country-specific differences, developments nHyt? to be on a solid footing in the euro area as well (Chart 2). The euro area's monetary policy stance, with its low interest rates, is also being improved by the depreciation of the external value of the euro and the fall in the price of the euro. In addition, fiscal consolidation measures have been taken in several euro area countries and structural reforms have already been carried out in many countries. Once these measures have been taken, they will not act as a brake on future growth. As part of the monetary policy stance, large-scale bond purchases were initiated with the aim of developing a deflationary development that is dangerous for the economy. As a result, the deflationary risk in the euro area has eased since the start of the purchase programme (See Graph 3). Of course, inflation remains generally low, influenced by the sharp fall in energy prices in the early part of the year (Chart 4). Although the global economy and Europe have improved, the Finnish economy is projected to increase the pace of international development (Graph 5). Compensating for production losses caused by the restructuring of production with new products will be slow. Structural change has led to a slowdown in productivity growth, which dampens growth in the formerly medium term. A lot of high-productivity jobs have been lost in Finnish industry. Economic growth continues to be weighed down by the structural structure, the weakened cost level and the economic difficulties in Ven?j?. Finland's GDP has declined in three years and in 2014 production was 2.9% lower than in 2011. There has been little sign of growth. 1st quarter of the current year the level of production was at the level of the previous quarter, and the statistics obtained since then were not clear. On the other hand, recent (April-May) data continue to point to declining production developments (Figure 6). According to data from Hein?ku, household confidence had also fallen sharply. The prolonged slow growth has weakened the situation in the labour market particularly strongly during the current year. Employment has been associated with a rapid rise (Figure 7). Until then, the effects of the recession and structural changes on the economy have been mitigated by the relatively strong development of private and public consumption (See Graph 8). Export growth has been very subdued and investment has plummeted. Finland is in an exceptionally difficult situation in terms of future economic growth and balanced development. DANGERS OF DEBT-DRIVEN GROWTH These developments have resulted in a deterioration in the external balance and in the continuation of government and household indebtedness (Graphs 9?10). In this situation, the options for economic policy are v?hiss?. The problems are structural and the potential and effectiveness of cyclical policies are limited. Growth based solely on consumption cannot continue on a permanent basis. Household indebtedness cannot be used to finance domestic demand, as the potential for income growth is somewhat weak due to the structure, for example. From the point of view of risks in the financial markets, an increase in debt levels is also undesirable. In Finland, households' debt burden has grown steadily in recent years and has accumulated on the shoulders of a few. Debtors are vulnerable both in terms of the development of their own economy and the sensitivity of interest rates (See Graph 11). Although the prolonged rise in house prices has stalled, the housing market is highly segregated at regional level (Graphs 12?14). Even small financial market crises and uncertainties in the housing market have an impact on household consumption patterns and thus on the real economy, even if they do not cause problems for banks. Government indebtedness has also risen to the level where the limits have been reached (Figures 15?16). The accumulation of debts for both the public and the household will put them in a difficult position in the future, especially if the conditions for economic growth do not improve soon. Indebtedness can also lead to cost-level fluctuations. In addition to debt, in a situation where money is spent not on improving production conditions but on consumption, raises prices in many sectors. The rise in prices in the service sector in recent years is a clear manifestation of this. Prices, through production, also weigh on the competitiveness of all industries, and in particular of our export sector. In Finland, prices and costs in the service sector have risen faster than in the euro area. Sustained growth in the economy can only be achieved through measures that improve the competitiveness of the export sector and the conditions for investment in enterprises. Re-increasing productivity is key to the future. FINANCIAL MARKETS ARE WORKING - DESPITE GREECE'S PROBLEMS The ability of international financial markets to function has gradually recovered, not since the end of the financial crisis. However, the expectation that the Federal Reserve will start to raise interest rates, the stability of the Chinese financial markets and the situation in Greece are creating confidence in the financial markets. The ample liquidity in the international financial system has been channelled into long-term financial investments (See Graph 17). There have been widespread warnings about overvaluations of asset prices. Low interest rates are good for the European economy in terms of recovery, but low interest rates can encourage investors to increase returns and increase risk-taking, both in existing operations and through new products and activities. Weakened market liquidity may contribute to strengthening price corrections. The simultaneous strong growth in asset prices and indebtedness is a development familiar from economic history against the background of many crises that should not be forgotten. Greece's problems in the market are being assessed as specific cases, and there has been no infection with the financial conditions of other European countries. However, under the eps security, the direct effects could be strong. The orderly management of Greece's problems is in the common interest of both creditors and debtors. Greece still needs structural measures to promote productivity and debt sustainability. Despite the current state of the Finnish economy, the availability and conditions of financing for the state, municipalities and Finnish companies have remained good. However, fluctuations in international investment flows and prices can also affect the Finnish economy. There are reasons to take care of the diversity of financial instruments and to promote competition in the provision of financial services (Graphs 18?19). The European Commission's initiative on a domestic market union is welcome. The development of the local market will improve the opportunities for business financing and create the conditions for economic growth. In Finland, the banking system is profitable and solvent, but structurally vulnerable (Figures 20? 21). It is exceptionally concentrated and dependent on foreign market financing. Four financial institutions hold a significant proportion of deposits, lending and payment services. In order to ensure the functioning of the financial markets, the Board of the Financial Supervisory Authority imposed additional requirements on banks. ECONOMY VdbLTTdbMdbTT... MdbT REFORM EFFORTS The government's economic policy programme, which, if implemented, will contribute to the consolidation of public finances, the improvement of competitiveness and structural reforms will contribute to the conditions for sustainable development (Graphs 22? 23). The increase in public debt is to be halted and structural reforms extended then through the 2014 structural policy programme. The coverage of structural reforms is considerable; reform, reform of social and health services and improvement of the conditions for housing supply. In overcoming the problems of the economy, curbing domestic cost developments is one of the crucial goals of the Czech Republic. The need to improve cost competitiveness is now 10 % or more when comparing the evolution of individual costs with the average of competitor countries. TdbYTdbNT...... NPANO NO LYKdbTT,VISSdb The problems in our economy are great, and there is hardly any sign of recovery (Graph 24). The good thing is that the seriousness of the problems is better understood. There is generally no reliance on improving the economic situation or on taking on additional debt. Now comes the long-term goals clear and moving on to solutions. What is needed is the speedy implementation of the programme. Improving cost competitiveness will play a key role. It is clear that without a sufficient strong export sector, Finland will not be able to stabilise its economy.

Thursday6August 2015, 1:15PM Pentti Hakkarainen Johtokunnan varapuheenjohtaja Suurten kaupunkien talous-ja rahoitusjohdon tilaisuus Vantaa 6.8.2015 Esityskalvot (/globalassets/en/media-and-publications/speeches-and-interviews/documents/06082015-pentti. . hakkarainen.pdf) (PDF) KANSAINVLINEN TALOUS VAHVISTUU, KOTIMAAN NKYMT HUONOT Check against delivery SUOMEN TALOUSNKYMT HEIKENTYNEET Kansainvlinen talouskasvu on vahvistunut yh laaja-alaisemmin. Maakohtaisista eroista huolimatta kehitys nytt olevan vakaalla pohjalla mys euroalueella (kuvio 2). Euroalueen nkymi kohentavat kevyt rahapolitiikka mataline korkoineen ja osaltaan mys euron ulkoisen arvon heikentyminen sek ljyn hinnan aleneminen. Niden lisksi useissa euromaissa on julkisen talouden tasapainottamistoimet ja monissa maissa mys rakenneuudistukset jo tehty. Kun toimet on saatu tehty, ne eivt jarruta tulevaisuudessa kasvua. Eurojrjestelmss osana rahapolitiikan virityst kynnistettiin laajat joukkovelkakirjojen ostot tavoitteena ehkist talouden kannalta vaarallista deflatorista kehityst. Euroalueen deflaatioriski onkin vhentynyt kevll alkaneen osto-ohjelman jlkeen (kuvio 3). Toki inflaatio on yleisesti edelleen matala, mihin vaikuttaa energian hintojen voimakas aleneminen alkuvuodesta (kuvio 4). Vaikka maailmantaloudessa ja Euroopassakin nkymt ovat parantuneet, Suomen talouden ennustetaan jvn enenevsti kansainvlisen kehityksen vauhdista (kuvio 5). Tuotannon rakennemuutoksen aiheuttamien tuotantomenetysten korvaaminen uusilla tuotteilla tulee olemaan hidasta. Rakennemuutos on johtanut tuottavuuden kasvun hidastumiseen, mik vaimentaa kasvunkymi entisestn mys keskipitkll aikavlill. Suomen teollisuudessa on menetetty paljon korkean tuottavuuden typaikkoja. Talouskasvua painavat edelleen vestn ikrakenne, heikentynyt kustannustaso ja Venjn talousvaikeudet. Suomen bruttokansantuote on pienentynyt kolmena perttisen vuonna ja vuoden 2014 tuotannon mr oli 2,9 % pienempi kuin vuonna 2011. Merkkej kasvun kynnistymisest ei ole juuri ollut. Kuluvan vuoden 1. neljnneksell tuotannon mr oli edellisen neljnneksen tasolla eivtk sen jlkeen saadut tilastot nkymi kirkasta. Pinvastoin, tuoreet (huhti-toukokuun) tiedot viittaavat edelleen pienenevn tuotantokehitykseen (kuvio 6). Kotitalouksien luottamus oli heinkuun tietojen mukaan alentunut mys selvsti. Pitkn jatkunut hidas kasvu on heikentnyt tymarkkinoilla tilannetta erityisen voimakkaasti kuluvan vuoden aikana. Tyttmyys on lhtenyt nopeaan nousuun (kuvio 7). Thn saakka taantuman ja rakennemuutosten vaikutuksia talouteen on loiventanut yksityisen ja julkisen kulutuksen suhteellisen vahvana pysynyt kehitys (kuvio 8). Viennin kasvu on ollut hyvin vaimeaa ja investoinnit ovat suorastaan romahtaneet. Suomen tilanne on poikkeuksellisen vaikea talouden tulevien kasvunkymien ja tasapainoisen kehityksen kannalta. VELKAVETOISEN KASVUN VAARAT Kehityksen seurauksena on ollut ulkoisen tasapainon heikkeneminen sek julkisen talouden ja kotitalouksien velkaantumisen jatkuminen (kuviot 910). Tss tilanteessa talouspolitiikan vaihtoehdot ovat vhiss. Ongelmat ovat rakenteellisia ja suhdannepolitiikan mahdollisuudet ja teho ovat rajallisia. Pelkstn kulutukseen perustuva kasvu ei voi jatkua pysyvsti. Kotitalouksien velkaantumisella ei voi kestvsti rahoittaa kotimaista kysynt, sill tulojen kasvumahdollisuudet ovat mm. vestn ikrakenteen takia heikot jokseenkin pysyvsti. Rahoitusmarkkinoiden riskien kannalta velka-asteiden nousu ei myskn ole toivottavaa. Suomessa kotitalouksien velkataakka on viime vuosina kasvanut tasaisesti ja on kasautunut harvojen harteille. Nm velalliset ovat haavoittuvia sek oman taloutensa kehityksen ett korkoherkkyyden suhteen (kuvio 11). Vaikka asuntojen hintojen pitkn jatkunut nousu on taittunut, asuntomarkkinat ovat alueellisesti voimakkaasti eriytyneet (kuviot 1214). Pienetkin rahoitusmarkkinoiden hirit ja epvarmuudet asuntomarkkinoilla vaikuttavat kotitalouksien kulutuskyttytymiseen ja siten reaalitalouteen, vaikka eivt aiheuttaisikaan ongelmia pankeille. Julkisen talouden velkaantuminenkin on noussut tasolle, jossa rajat ovat kytnnss tulleet vastaan (kuviot 1516). Velkamrien kasaaminen niin julkiselle kuin kotitalouksille laittaa nm tulevaisuudessa vaikeaan asemaan erityisesti jos talouskasvun edellytykset eivt pian kohene. Velkaantuminen voi osaltaan johtaa mys kustannustason vristymiin. Velan lisminen tilanteessa, jossa rahaa ei kytet tuotannollisten edellytysten parantamiseen vaan kulutukseen, nostaa monien alojen hintoja. Palvelualoilla viime vuosina tapahtunut hintojen nousu on tmn selke ilmentym. Nm hinnat uivat vlituotannon kautta mys kaikkien elinkeinojen ja erityisesti vientisektorimme kilpailukyky rasittamaan. Suomessa palvelualojen hinnat ja kustannukset ovatkin nousseet euroaluetta nopeammin. Kestv kasvua talouteen voidaan saada ainoastaan toimilla, jotka kohentavat vientisektorin kilpailukyky ja yritysten investointiedellytyksi. Tuottavuuden saaminen uudelleen kasvuun on avainasemassa tulevaisuuden kannalta. RAHOITUSMARKKINAT TOIMIVAT -HUOLIMATTA KREIKAN ONGELMISTA Kansainvlisten rahoitusmarkkinoiden toimintakyky on asteittain palautunut eik finanssikriisin jlki juuri ny. Epvarmuutta rahoitusmarkkinoiden nkymiin luovat kuitenkin odotukset Yhdysvaltain keskuspankin korkojen noston aloituksesta, Kiinan rahoitusmarkkinoiden epvakaus sek Kreikan tilanne. Kansainvlisen rahoitusjrjestelmn runsas likviditeetti on ohjautunut pitklti finanssisijoituksiin (kuvio 17). Varallisuushintojen yliarvostuksista onkin laajasti varoiteltu. Korkojen mataluus on hyv Euroopan talouden toipumisen kannalta, mutta matalat korot voivat kannustaa sijoittajia tuoton metsstykseen ja riskinoton kasvuun sek nykyisiss toiminnoissa ett uusien tuotteiden ja toimintojen kautta. Heikentynyt markkinalikviditeetti voi osaltaan voimistaa hintojen korjausliikkeit. Varallisuushintojen ja velkaantuneisuuden samanaikainen voimakas kasvu on taloushistoriasta tuttu kehityskulku monen kriisin taustalla, jota ei tule unohtaa. Kreikan ongelmat nyttisivt markkinoilla arvioitavan erityistapauksina, eik tartuntaa muiden Euroopan maiden rahoituksen ehtoihin ole tapahtunut. Epvarmuuden vallitessa epsuorat vaikutukset voisivat kuitenkin olla voimakkaita. Kreikan ongelmien hallittu hoitaminen on sek velkojien ett velallisen yhteinen etu. Kreikka tarvitsee edelleen rakenteellisia toimia, joilla edistetn tuottavuutta ja velkakestvyytt. Huolimatta Suomen talouden nkymist, ovat valtion, kuntien ja suomalaisten yritysten rahoituksen saatavuus ja ehdot pysyneet hyvin. Kansainvlisten sijoitusvirtojen ja hintojen vaihtelut voivat kuitenkin vlitty mys Suomen talouteen. Rahoituslhteiden monipuolisuudesta on syyt huolehtia sek edist kilpailua rahoituspalveluiden tarjonnassa(kuviot 1819). Euroopan Komission aloite pomamarkkinaunionista on tervetullut. Pomamarkkinoiden kehittmisell parannetaan yritysrahoituksen mahdollisuuksia ja luodaan edellytyksi talouskasvulle. Suomessa pankkijrjestelm on kannattava ja vakavarainen mutta rakenteellisesti haavoittuva (kuviot 2021). Se on poikkeuksellisen keskittynyt ja riippuvainen ulkomaisesta markkinarahoituksesta. Neljll rahalaitoksella on merkittvin osa talletuksista, luotonannosta ja maksuliikennepalveluista. Rahoitusmarkkinoiden toimivuuden varmistamiseksi Finanssivalvonnan johtokunta asetti nille pankeille lispomavaatimukset. TALOUDEN VLTTMTTMT UUDISTUSTOIMET Hallituksen talouspoliittinen ohjelma, joka tht julkisen talouden sopeuttamiseen, kilpailukyvyn parantamiseen ja rakenteellisiin uudistuksiin, edist toteutuessaan kestvn kehityksen edellytyksi (kuviot 2223). Julkisen velan kasvu on tarkoitus taittaa ja rakenneuudistuksia laajentaa sitten kevn 2014 rakennepolittiisen ohjelman. Rakenneuudistusten kattavuus on melkoinen; elkeuudistus, sosiaali-ja terveyspalvelujen uudistus ja asuntotarjonnan edellytysten parantaminen. Talouden ongelmien voittamisessa kotimaisen kustannuskehityksen hillitseminen on yksi ratkaisevan trke tavoite. Kustannuskilpailukyvyn parantamisen tarve on nyt 10 % tai enemmn, kun verrataan yksikktykustannusten kehityst kilpailijamaiden keskiarvoon. TYTNTNPANO EI LYKTTVISS Taloutemme ongelmat ovat suuria, eik merkkej elpymisest juuri ole (kuvio 24). Hyv asia on, ett ongelmien vakavuus ymmrretn yh paremmin. Suhdanteiden paranemisen varaan tai lisvelan ottamiseen ei en yleisesti tukeuduta. Nyt tuleekin pit tavoitteet selken ja edet ratkaisuihin. Se mit tarvitaan, on ohjelman ripe toimeenpano. Keskeinen merkitys tulee olemaan kustannuskilpailukyvyn kohentamisella. On selv, ett ilman riittvn vahvaa vientisektoria Suomi ei voi talouttaan vakauttaa.

Title: Industry and Finland's national economy over a couple of hundred years
text: Vice Chairman of the Executive Board Pentti Hakkarainen: Industry and Finland's national economy in a couple of hundred years. Theft 4.9.2015. . Speech . INDUSTRY AND FINLAND'S NATIONAL ECONOMY IN A COUPLE OF HUNDRED YEARS Check against delivery Again, there is more talk of structural change in the economy than in the long term. The key words are digitalisation and robotisation. A dozen years ago, there was talk of globalisation and the ICT revolution. A hundred years ago there was talk of sshksization, a couple of hundred years ago there was talk of industrialization. With the exception of globalization, all nsms terms refer to technology. It reflects the fact that the technological change has always been a driver of economic growth and development. However, technological progress alone does not explain economic growth. Technology accreditation and its development, innovation, the right incentives and the right institutions. 1. TECHNOLOGY, INCENTIVES AND INSTITUTIONS Incentives exist naturally. Anders Chydenius and Adam Smith have taught us that people have a natural tendency to seek their own best. That is the kind of work that pays the most, which is the source of the greatest value to society. That's what you're looking for. The well-being of all is increased. The condition, however, is that human beings have the freedom to seek out the Ches from which the greatest value is created. In the time of Chydenius and Smith, nsin was not. That is why both advocated the freedom to conduct a business and the right of every individual to freely sell their products and power wherever they go. The single point is that individuals can use the value they have created for their own good. The freedom to conduct a business accelerated the division of labour, which increased productivity and, through it, prosperity. The deepening of the division of labour complicated economic relations, as the number of economic players increased. For this reason, new institutions were needed, for example, to strengthen the validity of the agreements. With the development of Tysnjao, the monetary economy expanded. A financial system emerged, which in turn required its own institutions aimed at the stability of the financial markets. Nsms may sound like obvious things in itself. It is worth remembering, however, that in many countries the freedom to conduct a business is limited in many ways, and that the individual's ability to use the results of his or her activities for his or her own good is limited. American scholars Daron Acemoglu and James A. Robinson, in their fairly new book Why Nations Fail, divide institutions into inclusive and extractive. Inclusive, i.e. permissive and nondiscriminatory institutions enable all individuals to participate in society, encouraging self-help and success. Extrusive institutions, on the other hand, make it possible for rulers, oligarchs or some other privileged few to be able to transfer a large part of the results of the work into their own pockets. Economic development is stifled by such institutions. Everyone will be reminded of examples of both types of institutions. We Europeans, and especially we Finns, think our society is inclusive. It certainly is. But it is a good thing that you can slide in an extravagant direction. If the tax burden rises to a sufficient level, the tax burden is not considered fair. Acemoglu and Robinson themselves are concerned that the United States is moving in a more exclusive direction because of the fact that political power is more divided because it depends on more money. 2. EARLY INDUSTRIALIZATION In Finland, early industrialization had begun in the 1600s, when a large number of ironworks were born in the country. However, the actual industrialization did not take place until the mid-1800s. It was boosted by the harnessing of rapids, the construction of canals and railways, as well as foreign pssoma and foreign-imported know-how. The association of the markka with the gold standard in 1878 integrated the Finnish financial markets into the international financial system. Only then did it make it possible, on a larger scale, for private operators to enter the loan market and to invest in buildings, machinery and equipment with the help of borrowed money. It was also significant that the largest investments were made in sectors such as the forest industry, the production of which was intended for export. Initially, foreign ownership, then foreign borrowing money and export orientation were the factors that industrialized Finland. But even that condition was the lifting of the restrictions on business, which began in the early 1860s. Freedom to conduct a business in the Grand Duchy in 1879, the year after the transition to the gold standard. The Tys market was also liberalised at the beginning of the next decade, when the free migration of tysvoima was allowed. It is good to remember that exports to Russia were foreign trade for Finland. This was of great importance especially for Its-Suomi and its industrial locations, such as Varkaus, which by the late 1800s had become one of the most industrialized localities in Finland. In the 1880s, the locality had at least a pipe and rolling plant, a sawmill, a machine shop, a boiler shop and two shipyards. Many of them were transferred to the ownership of Ahlstrsm Oy at some point. Of great significance for the development of North Savo was the Savo Railway, which was extended from Kouvola to Kuopio in 1899 and on to Iisalmi in 1902. 3. STATE-FUNDED AND MANAGED INDUSTRIALIZATION Finnish industry in 1890 d1930 was marked by the vss of the private psoma and nsin, therefore, the largest projects had to receive pssom from the state. Examples include the presence of Europe's richest copper deposits. and the establishment of Outokumpu and the construction of the Imatra power plant. The operating conditions of the economy improved when, thanks to the new crushers, exports by ship were made possible for an environmental year. In the forest industry, paper production was introduced alongside the sawmill industry. Paradoxically, during the period when there was a nslsnhs in the country and people lived in the land pits of the Northeast, a period of economic growth took place. Economic history speaks of otake offo, or lentoonlshch, in which the economy itself is associated with a strengthening growth. Indeed, economic growth in Finland was continuous and strong up to the point of nsihin psiv. However, we adapted to it quite quickly. Ahlstrsm Osakeyhtis expanded its engineering operations in Varkaus throughout the 1930s. The market for the forest industry is lsytyivst lsnnests. After the Second World War, Finland began to be industrialised on a state-led basis. The development was influenced by war reparations and construction, which partly explained the central role of the state. It was not just a question of funding, but also of what is produced. War reparations had been paid by 1952. In the same year, Urho Kekkonen published a pamphlet entitled Does our country have the patience to prosper. The country's state-run industrial policy, based on heavy and socially intensive industry and with a strong emphasis on regional policy, was thus outlined. A similar industrial policy focused on heavy industry was also implemented by Stalin in the Soviet Union. After the war, the financial markets and the pssoma movements were severely sssnnsstels. Sssnnsstelys was carried out on behalf of the State by the Bank of Finland, which became responsible for directing funding towards investments considered to be a priority in terms of industrial policy. The financial markets, which continued until the 1980s, favoured and supported industrial investment in particular. Investment was supported by both taxation and inflation. The state-led industrial policy was also underpinned by state-run foreign trade, in particular bilateral trade with the Soviet Union, which was hardly familiar with the market economy. This state-led policy may well have been justified in the post-war years. But all choices have their alternative costs. What did you not get when choosing a strategy focused on investment and heavy industry? When scarce pssoms were diverted into industry, they were enough for other purposes. Consumption compared to the other Nordic countries to the status of the stepchild. The household's level of credit was considered to be high by limiting the maturity of their credit to the credit market and, for example, the maturity of mortgage loans, for example, very short from an international point of view to those who, under the conditions of credit, had managed to obtain credit. Inflation and tax subsidies (through depreciation) made almost any investment profitable, which is why it just managed to get credit. The increase in liquidity through investment boosted productivity, while real wages grew at a reasonably fast pace in the autumn. At the same time, however, the productivity of solid pssoma decreased. This was becoming inefficient, and the problem became a problem at the final stage, when the financial markets began to leak and the financial markets began to affect the investment market. It is generally thought that, in a market economy, sssnnssing, if it has to be resorted to, is a spatial system from which one breaks away as soon as the exceptional situation is over. On the other hand, if the sssnnsstelys continues to be sufficient for a long period of time, it will be difficult to break away because of the fact that the ssssnnssing will give rise to its own rslssinss, sssnnnsstelyss hystyvsnss. The liberalisation of the financial markets in the 1980s has been much criticised, often unjustifiably and with poor information. Among other things, the dismantling of the Sssnnsstely has been attributed to the recession of the 1990s. It is certainly the case that the liberalisation of the financial markets intensified the overheating and over-indebtedness of the late 1980s, which was also the cause of the banking crisis. A better question is why the sssnnsstelys did not begin to be dismantled earlier. The reason for this is the aforementioned rslssi. There was not a single influential entity in the country whose interest was served by the dismantling of the sssnnssing. The shunning began to unravel due to the fact that the internationalization of business and banking constantly created new opportunities for the spiralling of ssnnsssing. This, in turn, made it possible to make risky profits. miks encouraged the search for new loopholes. 4. GLOBALISATION AND THE ICT BOOM The share of industry in GDP has declined in all developed countries since the 1960s. In Finland, the share of industry in GDP rose rapidly until the 1950s, when it stabilised at around 30 per cent of GDP. The ratio remained at the same level until the mid-1980s, when it began to decline. During the recession of the 1990s, it began to rise, initially because of the decline in gdp. After that, the ratio rose until the end of the decade. In comparison, finland's reindustrialisation was a freak. The reason was the rapid recovery of industry and exports from the recession and, after that, the rise of the ICT sector. Figure 1: Share of industry in GDP Finland very quickly became involved in the suction of globalisation. Finnish companies expanded their operations internationally, and value chains became global. Thanks to the Nokia sector, Finland was interesting for a while. Finland's reputation as an ICT hub also brought foreign investment. Foreigners bought Finnish companies and in many cases continued manufacturing operations in Finland. Globalization also came to Varkaus. Ahlstrsm's energy technology was transferred to the American Foster Wheeler, Ahlstrsm's lumber industry technology to andritz from Itsva, The Ahlstrsm's screen plate production to the Canadian CAE (later AFT), Ahlstrsm's automation business to the American Honeywell, etc. A study has also been conducted on ss (Jari Jssskelsinen and Raimo Lovio, ETLA 2003). The ICT boom and the rise of Nokia is quite an exceptional event in the history of any country. Nokia's share of Finland's gross national product alone rose to four per cent and exports to 25 per cent at best. The impact of one industry was so great that, in many minds, it gave an overly positive picture of the development of the entire national economy. Productivity figures are high, but that did not mean that it could have been foreclosed on everyone. Outside the ICT sector, the productivity development of manufacturing and thus the growth in the ability to pay wages was much slower than the figures for manufacturing as a whole indicated. In addition, the rapid productivity growth in the ICT sector largely went to falling prices. In other words, the productivity hysty was transferred to foreign customers, not to Finnish wage earners or the tax authorities. 5. THE GREAT RECESSION TURNED INTO A LONG ONE In the long run, it was a long thought that Finland would have been more shy about globalisation than many other countries. Nsin certainly was. Let's not forget that the ICT boom brought prosperity, as Finns sold their Nokia shares to foreigners at a high price, when the proceeds of the joint tax brought money to the municipalities, and the option million-dollar dollars also paid tax to Finland according to the strictest. The financial crisis changed the situation. The collapse of foreign trade and the halting of investment activity after the bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers hit Finland, which is dependent on foreign trade and specialises in the production of capital goods, particularly hard. The drying up of international funding channels at the turn of 2008 and 2009 brought large companies back to become loan customers of Finnish banks, making it more difficult for the SME sector to access finance. The biggest drawer around the same time, Nokia had to recognize hsvisnss in the shill phone market. The share of the Nokia sector in terms of employment and value added decreased significantly. It also meant that, at the level of the economy as a whole, productivity fell as the share of the largest productivity industry contracted. Finland's GDP is still six per cent below the 2008 level. The Bank of Finland has calculated that the contraction of the ICT sector in 2008 and 2011 is explained by the drop in the ICT sector by about four per cent. Figure 2: Change in value ratio since 2007 The backward steps of globalization are nshty myss in Varkaus. However, the reason is not foreign-owned. The reasons are more common and apply to the whole of Finland. Finland has lost its comparative advantage in paper production, while the demand for paper in developed countries is declining. The mechanical engineering industry is challenged by investment in the world. A case study has also been carried out (Raimo Lovio, Jari Jssskelsinen, Juhan Laurila and Kari Lilja, ETLA 2006). Fortunately, recently, some positive signs have begun in Varkaus, the so-called "green belt". green shoots. Yle News reported in Heinsku (22.7.2015) that Stora Enso's paper machine is being converted to produce raw material for corrugated board and that there will also be a line to produce wooden LVL elements. Battery production is restarting. Andritz and Foster Wheeler have received new orders. 6. TST ETEENPIN Finland's economic situation is currently dire. Gross domestic product is still six per cent below the 2008 level. The latest statistics show that growth has not yet reached the point. Finland is even one of europe's crisis countries. There is no reason for us to get bogged down in the current situation when we are looking at economic development over the last couple of hundred years. Despite the occasional difficulties, Finland's economic development is very comparable over a long period of time with that of other countries with a similar level of development. So there are reasons to believe that this will continue to be the case for decades to come. But it doesn't happen in itself. There is work to be done for it. There are many difficulties that need to be overcome. Some of them are country-specific, many challenges we share with other countries. Our own challenge is demography. The finnish tysiksinen vsests is vshenemsss. This means that, without strong immigration, the labour force will be reduced. A country where the power is expected to fall cannot be an attractive destination for new investment. In Finland, it has gone unnoticed that a debate has begun in Germany on how the decline in the labour market is already affecting the investment plans of German industrial companies. Figure 3: Finnish tysiksinen vsests Another challenge posed by demography is that the demand for care services is increasing at the same time as a large part of the current social and health care sector is being transferred to the labour market. The third challenge, of course, is to finance the growing income and care expenditure, in other words, to close the so-called sustainability gap. As I said at the beginning, technological progress has taken the world economy forward and will continue to do so. However, development is not steady and continuous. Technological innovation takes place in abundance. Their influence spans a long period of time, often in completely different industries, for which they were originally created and developed. Adaptation to technological progress never occurs painlessly for tsys. It scythes at the same time as it is born elsewhere. Adapting to change requires flexibility and speed. This applies in particular to the all-embracing digitalisation that is currently under way. Now there is already quite a lot of experience, researched information on the use of ICT technology and digitalization, not only in the demand for highly qualified people, but also in the demand for low-productivity jobs. Jslkimmsinen is monitoring the growth in demand for services. There are a large number of highly skilled workers whose jobs are in demand. Much of the routine-based professional work can be transferred to machine and robot work. This means that the position of the middle class is weakening in relative terms. ICT technology and digitalisation are changing and have already dramatically changed the nature of the workplace. Permanent job descriptions begin with the transition to history. The meaning of tyspaikka and tyspiste changes when you can do whatever you want. This means that the game and the system are going to change. Based on permanent employment relationships and permanent job descriptions, it simply does not work when companies have to react more quickly to changes in their operations. The fact, if any, is that the salary and the remuneration can be agreed locally. If speed and flexibility lead to improved productivity in a company, then then the company must also be able to enjoy the fruits of the company. There is a lot of talk around the world about how the growth rate of developed countries will be clearly slower in the coming decades than what we were used to in the past decades. An annual growth rate of three per cent doubles the size of gdp in 23 years. If the increase in the pound is one per cent, it will take 70 years for the cake to double. This is one of the reasons for the long-term slowdown in growth. Government and household indebtedness will continue to slow down growth for a long time to come. vThe strain of debt rises if growth remains sluggish. The level of education in the developed countries cannot rise at the same rate as in the past. In addition, the increase in the distribution of income, which has increased, particularly in the United States, has been cited as a brake on growth. The long-term slowdown in the pace of global economic growth is bad news for Finland, whose growth in prosperity has always been based on expanding foreign trade. If demand growth is slower than usual, foreign trade growth will also slow down. There is no point in imagining that an increase in domestic demand can compensate for the loss. If global output growth slows down over a long period of time, then investment growth is also likely to slow down more. This is bad news for a country specialising in the production of capital goods, such as Finland. Finland is a small economy dependent on foreign trade. As a small country, we need production that is of great value and that we can do for a small number of people, which is especially industry. As a small country, Finland is vulnerable to fluctuations in the global economy. However, there is no need to mourn the smallness that we cannot mourn. Although the global economy is growing at a slower pace than in the past, there are always enough markets and niches for good products. In order to be able to do so, flexibility, speed and cost-effectiveness are required. The state must create the conditions for all this. The success story of our national economy - and as a key part of it - has been marked by the last 150 years of technological know-how and innovation, the right incentives for enterprise and enterprise, and good institutions such as a functioning public administration. If we take care of everyone's competitiveness, we will have success for the next five decades and a longer future, not only in Finland but also in Varkaus.

Title: Economy and Security
text: Vice Chairman of the Board pentti Hakkarainen: Economy and security. Helsinki, 9.11.2015. . Speech . Monday9 November 2015,12:05 PM Presentation by Pentti Hakkarainen, Vice Chairman of the Executive Board, Helsinki 9.11.2015 Presentation body d the presentation held may differ ECONOMIC STABILITY IS A KEY ELEMENT OF NATIONAL SECURITY Economic stability is a key element of national security. Economic stability includes issues such as sound public finances, price stability and reliable and secure financial markets. Of course, there is much more to it than that, such as a high level of employment and adequate social safety nets. Maintaining economic stability requires confidence, predictability and political stability. Economic stability can be lost in many autumns. The cause may be external or sissy-born. The external cause may be an international financial crisis, a change in the price of sljy, a contraction in world trade, geopolitics or a major natural disaster. These are factors over which the economic or other policies (at least of a small country) cannot be influenced. Commonly, if not more often, the reasons for the lack of financial stability in the country of origin. There can be many reasons, such as mismanagement, strong advocacy of special interests, or a lack of long-term tension in policy-making. In many countries, we have seen excessive government indebtedness, high inflation or, through the banking crisis, the collapse of the real economy. Conflicts of interest or weakened trust in political institutions and in the institutions of society have exacerbated the situation. A loss of economic stability, especially if it occurs for reasons of guerrilla origin, can lead to political stability. The erosion of political stability undermines security in many ways. The national capacity to make decisions is weakening and international influence is crumbling. In the worst-case scenario, the country loses its creditworthiness, which limits economic policy sovereignty. FINANCIAL MARKET STABILITY IS A KEY, IF NOT THE MOST ESSENTIAL, PART OF FINANCIAL STABILITY Financial market stability is a key, if not the most essential, part of financial stability. The reason is that, in a modern economy, all economic activity is based on the activity of the financial markets. From the czech angle, the financial markets are an integral part of the economic infrastructure. The vulnerability of financial markets has also increased. Not only have the banks become big in oliia to fail, but also the centrally dependents of oliia to fail. Central dependence arises from the increasing debt and receivables of banks and other financial actors. A significant part of the increase in private indebtedness over the last couple of decades is due to the increase in the average debt of persis' financial industry. When we talk about infrastructure, we are also talking about network effects. The network effects of financial markets are significant, both in good and bad. Today's network of financial markets covers the whole world. Globally integrated financial markets promote efficiency and, in many cases, stability. But globally integrated financial markets are also effective. Due to central dependence, the solvency of one large bank spreads at lightning speed to other banks, including across borders. The paralysis of payment transactions and short-term financing is beginning to wreak havoc on the real economy and from the first minute. Efficient and reliable operation of the financial system is a key basis for the functioning of society. It is the bloodstream of society and if there are minor blockages or problems, then the lifeblood of society can be seriously affected. Financial markets must be able to function in all circumstances. Historical experience shows that the recession that gave rise to the financial crisis is deeper and longer lasting than recessions of other causes. During the financial crisis, asset prices are falling, which is why consumption and investment are falling. The availability of credit is tightening, making it more difficult to carry out normal business and postpone investment projects for a longer period of time. An increase in the security of credit will reduce the demand for credit. Ssssssmming becomes more important when we start to prepare for worse times. DUE TO THE FINANCIAL SYSTEM,N TRa, THE FINANCIAL MARKETS MUST BE PREPARED FOR ALL POSSIBLE RISKS... IHIN Due to the financial system, the financial markets must be prepared for all possible scenarios. It is a key area of national security of supply. In cooperation with the National Emergency Supply Agency, the Bank of Finland is currently conducting crisis exercises in the financial sector for approximately five years. The previous financial sector exercise oFATO 2009o was organised in autumn 2009. More than 70 organizations and more than a thousand people took part in it. The next financial sector exercise oFATO 2015o is currently underway. The exercise is divided into three parts: pre-assignments, actual action and action-based small group activities. During it, the experiences and results of the exercise are analyzed from the systemic angle. The exercise will take place at the end of November. The aim of the exercise is to test the continuity of financial sector operators' systems and preparedness for serious hsiris situations. A key role in the preliminary work of the FATO exercise was played by the escalation of the international geopolitical situation, combined with the indebtedness of states, the refugee problem, the growth of employment, terrorist acts and cyber-hyphens. Thanks to strong international liquidity, interest rates continued to fall until shock and serious geopolitical events brought the pssoma market and the psrss rates into sync. In the case of banks, the solvency impact is relatively small due to the high entry level. The respondents were confident that their own measures were sufficient to stabilise the situation for their own bank or insurance company. However, from a macro level, the situation is more difficult. If everyone acts according to their preliminary plans, then not all company-specific measures can be implemented. In the operational scenario of the FATO exercise, emphasis was placed on the different aspects of infrastructure and cyber ireland. In order to safeguard financial services, ensuring access to, international telecommunications and communications is a priority. The exercise showed that there was already a one-day interruption in international telecommunications links, as well as key services in the financial sector: card payments, payment transactions, securities settlement and trading, as well as the distribution of money in Finland. The operational scenario also tested the preparedness of financial actors for various cyber and hybrid threats, such as denial-of-service threats, data breaches and the spread of information and panic in the market. In such situations, smooth cooperation between operators and authorities is tsrkess. In order to form a correct and comprehensive picture of the situation, there must be roles and responsibilities, as well as agreed procedures, in advance. The role of timely and carefully thought-out communication is emphasised. Many financial market participants have a reasonably high level of preparedness for cyber threats, and in hsiris situations, cooperation with the National Cyber Security Centre has experience. In the exercise, the general situational picture was shared through a training simulator. In a real situation, there are no such tys tools for building and sharing a situational picture. There would be a question between the authorities, who coordinates the situation and compiles and shares the situational picture between the authorities and the actors involved. The FATO exercise has been coordinated in time with the state administration preparedness exercise (VALHA), which will also begin, which will make the results of the FATO exercise possible. The training period for the exercise, which takes place in approximately five years, is long. An increase in the training frequency should be considered. It would also be a good idea to consider involving actors outside Finland's borders in the exercise. Such entities could include, for example, the ECB and EBA Clearing. The ECB operates a real-time payment system for large payments to the euro (Target 2). EBA Clearing, which is owned by banks, provides a range of solutions related to the European payment infrastructure. AN ECONOMIC POLICY THAT STRENGTHENS SECURITY IS ONLY POSSIBLE WITH INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION... N In March 2010, I attended a seminar on security policy held in Kajaani, where I had been invited to speak on the topic oEconomy as part of national securityo1. At the end of my presentation, I summarised my topic in a few key points. They were: -Good economic management is a prerequisite for national security d and self-efficacy d vsltsmsss. -An economic policy that strengthens security is only possible through international cooperation. -In the current economic climate, the priorities for economic security are to put public finances back on a long-term basis and to strengthen international cooperation structures in economic policy in general and in the field of financial supervision in particular. I can sign the nsms shsks, five and a half years later. The Finnish economy is now in a worse state than it was five and a half years ago. This direction must be reversed for our own safety (and for our own sake). In a world of central dependencies, we have a situation where other countries are in good economic shape. The crisis in the euro area shows that this is not always the case. In response to the crisis, the European Union has introduced a series of reforms aimed at promoting good economic management. Examples include the strengthening of fiscal policies, procedures for limiting macroeconomic balances, the establishment of macroprudential policies and the establishment of a banking union. In March 2010, I would not have guessed that five years later, the euro area had moved to single banking supervision and created a bank resolution mechanism. The banking union is now being finalised, which in some time will also include the maintenance of a common deposit insurance scheme. RECESSIONS CAUSED BY FINANCIAL CRISES INCREASE PARTY POLITICAL DIVISIONS AND POLITICAL EPCERTAINTY In Europe, the series of economic and financial crises has been followed by a refugee crisis with security policy but also economic implications. Now, more than ever, there is a need for a full-blown and political unity, which is not the case at the moment. Until then, we have talked about the currency failures of EMU and warned against the development of a federal state. There has been talk of currency failures in the Schengen Agreement. If, when the Schengen Agreement was being drawn up, there had been a serious threat of large influxes of refugees, I believe that there would then have been a willingness to create common border controls and a common refugee policy. It would also have enjoyed the support of the people and, through it, its willingness to pay, despite the fact that it would have brought with it a federal element at the eu level as a whole. Now there is a lack of political unity, which makes it difficult to solve the problem. There is a link between financial crises and political developments. German economists Manuel Funke, Moritz Scularik and Christoph Trebesch have published a study showing that recessions caused by financial crises increase party political disintegration and political certainty.2 This is reflected in an increase in support for right-wing populist and nationalist parties. Regressions caused by other causes do not have such an effect. The study is based on datasets summarising data on the results of elections (800) held during the recession in 20 developed countries over a period of 140 years. As a result of party-political disintegration and the growth of political uncertainty, the ability to make political balances is weakened. The uncertainty about the future is blurring, which is driving away investment. In addition to the euro area, this also applies to other EU countries and to a number of countries outside the EU. There are three alternative paths from the EU's corner: the path of deeper integration, the path of muddling through and the path of disintegration. Everyone can think about the threats to security associated with each path. According to Janis Emmanoulidis, director of the European Policy Centre, a Brussels think tank, muddling through is the most verifiable, though not the most desirable.3 Finally, a large part of the issues affecting national security are due to external factors and factors over which we have no direct influence. I would therefore stress that an economic policy that strengthens security requires international cooperation. Finland's attitude to the development of Economic and Monetary Union was assessed in response to a group of experts. The etels ostrobothnian proverb of the opening film of the presentation of the report is well suited to the place of the shsn: the bird of the oPahan air says that the wind is blowing from the direction. Good faith expects that the direction will change. Let the sails fall into place, and let them go. o Dr Antti Suvanto, adviser to the Board of Governors of the Bank of Finland, who in the autumn of 2015 also chaired the above-mentioned group of experts appointed by the Minister of Finance to assess the needs for the development of economic and monetary union. Taloudellinen vakaus sislt sellaisia asioita kuin terve julkinen talous, vakaa hintataso sek luotettavat ja turvalliset rahoitusmarkkinat. Nin monissa maissa on ajauduttu valtion liialliseen velkaantumiseen, korkeaan inflaatioon tai pankkikriisin kautta reaalitalouden romahtamiseen. Krjistyneet eturistiriidat tai heikentynyt luottamus poliittisiin pttjiin ja yhteiskunnan instituutioihin ovat pahentaneet tilannetta. RAHOITUSMARKKINOIDEN VAKAUS ON KESKEINEN, ELLEI KESKEISIN, OSA TALOUDELLISTA VAKAUTTA Rahoitusmarkkinoiden vakaus on keskeinen, ellei keskeisin, osa taloudellista vakautta. Pankit ovat tulleet paitsi liian suuriksi kaatumaan mys liian keskinisriippuvaisiksi kaatumaan. Keskinisriippuvuus syntyy pankkien ja muiden rahoitusalan toimijoiden vlisist kertautuvista velka-ja saatavasuhteista. Merkittv osa yksityisen velkaantumisen kasvusta parin viime vuosikymmenen aikana on perisin rahoitustoimialan keskinisten velkojen kasvusta. Kun puhutaan infrastruktuurista, puhutaan mys verkostovaikutuksista. Rahoitus-markkinoiden verkostovaikutukset ovat merkittvt, niin hyvss kuin pahassa. Mutta globaalisesti integroituneet rahoitusmarkkinat ovat mys tehokkaita vlittmn hiriit. In relation to ?ss?, the picture is somewhere m??rin contradictory. The easiest thing to measure in financial terms is interest rates. It is known to be very low in the euro area as a whole, and in Finland it is also particularly low compared to other euro area countries. Interest rates on small business loans have hovered around 2%. Another thing that is easy to see is the increase in the loan portfolio. On the Sill?k side, Finland is different from the other euro countries. It is only in the year that there is n?hty k??nnet? in a positive direction. In Finland, the situation has been different. For several years, the growth in the volume of loans taken out by companies has been quite brisk, especially in comparison with the otherwise weak growth of the economy (the annual growth rate of loans to non-financial corporations has hovered around five per cent). By metrics, the problem isn't going to be in funding. On the other hand, there is a strong message from science, especially from smaller companies: access to business finance is a problem. When that message isn't the reason for this, what's the question? The explanation is that the terms of bank loans other than interest rates have apparently tightened sharply in Finland in recent years. This applies in particular to collateral requirements, but also to the payment periods of loans and the commission costs incurred at the end of the interest rate. One of the factors contributing to the financial problems of companies is that the size of the banks and the banking sector has deteriorated and, as a result, competition in banking has deteriorated, particularly in the provinces and more, as a result, in the smaller localities.
