Tllaisesta menestyksest saatiin Suomessa esimakua jo 1600-ja 1700-luvuilla, kun Suomi oli maailman suurin tervantuottaja. Varsinaisen teollisen massatuotannon aikana metsteollisuuden menestyksess on ollut osin samoja piirteit. Tllainen suurtuotannon etuihin pohjautuva teollisen tuotannon kasvu ei kuitenkaan yksin selit Suomen menestyst. Maailman vauraimmilla talouksilla oli tuottavuudessa merkittv etumatka Suomeen paitsi teollisuudessa mys monilla palvelualoilla. Tmkin etumatka on vuosikymmenten saatossa kaventunut tai poistunut. Kansainvliset yhteydet liittyvt Suomen teollistumiseen ja tuottavuuden nopeaan kasvuun monin tavoin. Kauppayhteydet ovat mahdollistaneet viennin kasvun ja teollisuuden tarvitsemien raaka-aineiden ja puolivalmisteiden tuonnin. Lisksi poman ja ihmisten liikkuminen yli maiden rajojen on edesauttanut uusien teknologioiden kyttnottoa ja osaamisen kehittymist. Vuosikymmenten saatossa Suomeen tehtiin lukematon mr ulkomaisia suoria sijoituksia  etenkin meit kehittyneemmist talouksista. Niiden myt maahamme tuli ulkomailta investointeihin tarvittavaa rahoitusta. Usein tllaisiin investointeihin liittyi mys kansainvlisess eturintamassa olevien tuotantomenetelmien omaksumista. Nm edistysaskeleet edellyttivt monessa tapauksessa henkilkunnan osaamisen kehittmist. Nin syntyi kysynt aiempaa korkeammalle koulutukselle. Kun sit saatiin, kasvoi osaajien joukko ja sen myt valmius ottaa entist enemmn kyttn uusia teknologioita. Hyv kehitys ruokki itsen. Vhitellen kasvoi mys suomalaisten oma kyky investoida, rahoittaa investointeja ja kehitt tuotantomenetelmi. Yrittminen ja riskinotto veivt eteenpin. Monien nykyisin Suomessa toimivien yritysten tausta on tss, todenteolla 1800-luvun jlkipuoliskolla alkaneessa kehityksess. Yksi esimerkki on Stora Enso. Sen Suomen toimintojen juuret ovat Norjan Fredrikstadiin vuonna 1860 perustetussa Wilh. Gutzeit & Co -niminess hyrysahassa. Sahan perinyt Hans Gutzeit alkoi hakea sille uutta paikkaa Suomesta, miss oli paremmin saatavissa tukkeja kuin Norjassa. Vuonna 1872 hn rakennutti sahan silloiseen Kymiin, nykyisen Kotkan kaupungin alueelle. Siit tuli Suomen suurin ja nykyaikaisin, ja sen voimalhteen oli sadan hevosvoiman tehoinen hyrykone. Sahaa hoitivat Norjasta tulleet ammattimiehet joita muutti lhes sata perheineen Hans Gutzeitin mukana Kymiin. Sahaa alettiin kutsua Norjan sahaksi, jolla nimell se tunnettiin vuosikymmenien ajan. Tst alkoi monivaiheinen kehitys, joka on johtanut siihen, ett tn pivn Stora Enso on yksi maailman suurimmista metsteollisuusyhtiist. Toisena esimerkkin voidaan mainita Outokumpu Oyj. Sen lhtkohta oli vuonna 1910 Kuusjrven pitjss Outkummun kaupungin lhell tehty kuparimalmilyt. Teknologia eli kuparin erottamisessa kytetty elektrolyyttinen menetelm saatiin aluksi Norjasta. Kaivoksen toiminta ei ollut tysin ongelmatonta, ja 1910-luvun lopulla yhti vuokrattiin kolmeksi vuodeksi norjalaiselle Hybinette-yhtille. 1920-luvulla kaivoksen omistajaksi tuli Suomen valtio. Kupari tuotettiin Imatrankosken voimalaitoksen energialla. Kes-heinkuussa 1944 sotilaallinen tilanne Kannaksen rintamalla muodostui vaikeaksi. Sotataloudelle trken kuparisulaton siirto Imatralta Harjavaltaan tuli nyt vlttmttmksi. Shkn saannin vaikeutuminen ja hinnan kohoaminen sodan jlkeen vauhditti energiaa sstvn sulatusmenetelmn eli liekkisulatuksen kehittmist. Kyseess on sanottu olleen 1900.luvun huomattavimpia keksintj kuparimetallurgian alalla. Liekkisulatusmenetelm tuotteistettiin  ensin omaan Harjavallan sulattoon v. 1949 ja sitten myytiin laajemmin maailmalle, joista ensimminen Furukawalle v. 1956. Menetelm osoittautui jttimenestykseksi; koko maailman nykyisest kuparituotannosta yli puolet tuotetaan Outokummun kehittmll liekkisulattomenetelmll. Liekkisulattotekniikan pohjalta kehittyi erilliseksi prssiyhtiksi Outotec, joka on metalliteknologian eturivin osaaja tnnkin. Nykyinen Outokumpu Oyj tuottaa ruostumatonta terst ja on omalla alallaan suurin yritys Euroopassa, ellei koko maailmassa. Kolmas esimerkki on Neste Oyj. Sen edeltj perustettiin vuonna 1948 valtionyhtiksi alalle, joka oli suomalaisille tuolloin pitklti uusi. Yrityksen tarkoituksena oli turvata Suomen ljynhuoltoa. Neste sai huomattavaa kilpailuetua kilpailijoihin nhden teknisesti edistyneell prosessillaan, jossa hyvin rikkipitoisesta venlisest raakaljyst jalostetaan rikitnt polttoainetta. Neste on oman tutkimustyns tuloksena kehittnyt teknologian, jolla kasviljyist ja jtteist, kuten elintarviketeollisuuden rasvajtteest, voidaan valmistaa uusiutuvaa dieseli. Helmikuussa 2014 Talouselm-lehti valitsi keksinnn mullistavimmaksi suomalaiseksi bisnesinnovaatioksi. Nykyisin Neste on suuryritys, joka tuottaa raakaljyst ja muista syttaineista lukuisia erilaisia jalosteita. Tlt Savosta lyt samanlaisia globaalissa kilpailussa prjvi yrityksi kuten Olvi, Ponsse, Normet, Genelec jne. joiden taustalla on oman toimialan ja teknologian maailmanluokan osaaminen. Kun taloustieteilijt ovat pyrkineet selvittmn, miksi jotkin maat ovat pitkll aikavlill menestyneet taloudellisesti paremmin kuin toiset ja joissa vire elinkeinotoiminta luo kasvua, ei yksinkertaisia selityksi ole ollut tarjolla. Esimerkiksi runsaat luonnonvarat selittvt vhn ja voivat pahimmassa tapauksessa jopa knty yhteiskunnan kehityst ja talouskasvua hidastavaksi tekijksi. Erilaisista helposti mitattavissa olevista suureista ole ei tahtonut lyty selittvi tekijit. Huolelliset tarkastelut ovat ptyneet korostamaan yhteiskunnan ja talouden instituutioita. Tt kuvataan hyvin kahden professorin Daron Acemoglun ja James Robinsonin kirjassa Why Nations Fail. Mys Suomen menestyst voitaneen selitt paitsi kansainvlisten yhteyksien olemassaololla mys muilla institutionaalisilla tekijill. [Kuva 8] Talouden kannalta keskeisin Suomen institutionaalisia vahvuuksina pidetn luotettavaa oikeuslaitosta, tehokasta julkista hallintoa, korruption vhisyytt, peruskoulutuksen hyv tasoa, infrastruktuuria ja naisten laajaa osallistumista tyelmn. Vaikka parantamisen varaa on aina, Suomen vertautuu moniin muihin maihin nhden mynteisesti niden instituutioiden kohdalla. Ainakin osa niist lienee lukeutunut Suomen vahvuuksiin jo pidemmn aikaa, joten niit voi pit Suomen pitkn aikavlin menestyksen trkein taustatekijin. Edell mainitut institutionaaliset vahvuudet luovat mahdollisuuksia talouden suotuisalle kehitykselle. Esimerkiksi kun oikeuslaitoksen toiminta on ollut luotettavaa, ulkomaiset yritykset ovat uskaltaneet tehd suoria sijoituksia Suomeen. Samalla tavalla suomalaiset yrittjt ovat uskaltaneet ottaa toiminnassaan taloudellisia riskej, kun he ovat voineet luottaa psevns itse nauttimaan hedelmist projektin onnistuessa. Kaikissa muissa maissa tilanne ei ole ollut yht hyv. Mys julkisen talouden ja rahaolojen vakaus antaa mahdollisuuksia talouskasvulle. Kun julkinen talous on kestvll pohjalla, yritysten ei tarvitse pelt verotuksen yllttv kiristymist tulevaisuudessa. Kun rahaolot ovat vakaat, yritysten ei tarvitse pelt hintojen tai rahoituskulujen kkinisi liikkeit tulevaisuudessa. Suomen rahaolojen vakauden kannalta keskeisi tapahtumia olivat Suomen markan synty 1860-luvulla, sen arvon irtautuminen epvakaan Venjn ruplan kehityksest ja markan arvon sitominen hopeaan ja sittemmin kultaan. Kansainvliseen kultakantaan siirtyminen helpotti mys rahoituksen hankkimista kaukana Euroopan rahakeskuksista sijainneeseen Suomeen. *** Palatkaamme nykypivn ja Suomen talouden ajankohtaisiin haasteisiin. Kuten totesin aiemmin, kasvunkymien kannalta keskeist on nyt kustannuskilpailukyvyn palauttaminen ja kasvumahdollisuuksia tukevat rakenteelliset uudistukset. Thn viittaavat tutkimustieto sek kokemukset Suomesta ja muista maista. [Kuva 9] Voiko mys pidempi historiallinen perspektiivi voi opettaa meille jotain Suomen talouden nykyisten vaikeuksien voittamisesta? Ainakin se viittaa kansainvlisten yhteyksien trken rooliin. Lisksi se viittaa yleisemmin instituutioiden merkitykseen. Suomen talouden institutionaalisista vahvuuksista kiinnipitminen on oleellista nykyisesskin tilanteessa. Tarvitsemme tulevaisuudessakin luotettavasti ja tehokkaasti toimivaa julkista hallintoa ja oikeuslaitosta, hyv perusopetusta ja infrastruktuuria, vhist korruptiota ja naisten laajaa osallistumista tyelmn. *** Kansainvlinen keskustelu tuottavuuden kasvun tulevasta kehityksest koskee pitklti teknologista kehityst ja sen seurauksia. Historialliset tarkastelut ovat korostaneet eriden suurten teknologisten edistysaskeleiden merkityst pitkn aikavlin tuottavuuskehityksen kannalta. 1800-luvulla hyryvoiman ja rautateiden kehitys oli mullistavaa. 1900-luvun alussa laajakantoisia vaikutuksia oli shkn valjastamisella ja polttomoottorilla. Viime vuosikymmenin informaatioteknologialla on nhty samanlainen rooli. Epvarmuus koskee pitklti sit, kuinka paljon voimme odottaa informaatioteknologialta tulevina vuosina. Onko siin tehtyjen edistysaskeleiden suurimmat vaikutukset tuottavuuteen ja hyvinvointiin jo koettu, vai onko thnastinen kehitys vasta esimakua tulevasta? Onko digitalisaatio vaikutuksiltaan aiempien teknologisten vallankumousten veroinen? Nihin kysymyksiin saadaan vastauksia vasta ajan myt. [Kuva 10] Se on joka tapauksessa selv, ett digitalisaatio tulee muuttamaan yhteiskuntia tulevaisuudessakin. Tietokoneet ja robotit ovat tuhonneet monia typaikkoja ja luoneet paljon uusia, ja tm trendi tulee jatkumaan. On esitetty mys arvioita, joiden mukaan teknologinen kehitys voisi aiheuttaa tyttmyyden pysyvkin lisntymist. Historia ja taloustiede eivt kuitenkaan varauksettomasti tue tllaista nkemyst. Aiemmatkin teknologiset vallankumoukset ovat tuhonneet typaikkoja, mutta ihmisty on silti silyttnyt arvonsa. Teknologian kehitykseen liittyv huoli eriarvoisuuden kasvusta on kuitenkin syyt ottaa vakavasti. Viime vuosikymmenin digitalisaatio on yhdess globalisaation kanssa hvittnyt etenkin keskituloisia typaikkoja kehittyneiss talouksissa. Talouspolitiikassa nm trendit on tarpeen ottaa huomioon. Typaikkansa menettvien on pystyttv pivittmn osaamistaan. Syrjytyminen tymarkkinoiden ulkopuolelle ja nkalattomuus on estettv. Se on keskeist sek yhteiskuntaa koossa pitvn liiman ett talouskasvun edellytysten kannalta. [Kuva 11] Talouspolitiikan keinoin ei sen sijaan tule pyrki pysyttmn teknologian kehityst ja globalisaatiota valtakunnan rajalle. Olosuhteiden pit olla kunnossa sille, ett innovaatiot voidaan ottaa kyttn meillkin, ja meill on mahdollisuudet olla teknologian eturintamassa. Title: How are European banks?
text: Deputy Governor Pentti Hakkarainen, Studia Monetaria 8.11.2016, Helsinki: What does European banks do? . Speech . Tuesday8 November 2016, 11:00 AM Vice Chairman of the Board Pentti Hakkarainen, Studia monetaria 8.11.2016, Helsinki Slides (/globalassets/en/suomen_pankki/current affairs/speeches/Documents/161108_Mits_eurooppalaisille_pankeille_kuuluu_Studia_Moneta What is up with the European banks? The European banking sector has been the focus of attention in the financial markets and the media, particularly in the autumn, due to the weak performance of bank share prices. Ksyn tssss presentationss the state of the European banking sector and the future of the nskymis, which I hope shed light on the reasons behind investors' concerns and will also eliminate some of the certainty about the state of the banks. What is up with the European banks? In short, european banks are doing both good and bad. The good thing is that, as a result of a wide-ranging export of international reforms, banks are more stable than the time of negative shocks from the real economy and the financial markets. It has also been shown that the market turbulences caused by the shocks experienced during the current year, such as the uk people's vote in favour of leaving the EU, have not caused banks to have long-lasting or spread to the level of the system. On the other hand, the post-crisis period has been challenging for banks. Banks have been able to continue operating in many respects in a more difficult way, characterised by prolonged weak growth in the real economy and low interest rates, tightening and competition. The viability of many banks is also hampered by the fallout from the previous crisis, which is still partially unpaid. The banking sector has already been struggling with low profitability for a long time, which has negative effects both in the short and long term. In the short term, low profitability reduces banks' ability to act in the financing sector and also exposes banks to various market turbulences. Prolonged low profitability will affect banks' solvency and may ultimately jeopardise their ability to function. The post-crisis period has been an opportune breeding ground for competition, which is accelerated by the rapid technological development of financial innovation. The development of fintechnology and increased competition are good for consumers and good for financial stability, but they can also be good for banks. The future of the banks will depend on their ability to reform for a long time. When we talk about the state of European banks and the future, we should remember that there are about 5500 credit institutions in the euro area alone. Banks differ in size and operating models d as well as in their strengths and challenges. Some banks are therefore better off than others. However, I will discuss the banking sector as a whole and the themes of the pssos as a whole, which are general either for the whole sector or for significant parts of it. Banks' solvency has steadily improved As a measure of a bank's solvency, it is most commonly used to use different solvency ratios, which indicate how much a bank has in relation to its risk-weighted exposures. The Czech Republic is the core solvency ratio, which is used as a measure of a bank's solvency in solvency. However, if you want to look at the evolution of banks' solvency over a longer period of time, you will have to use the solvency indicator of the broader issue: Tier 1 d solvency ratio, as the core solvency ratio has only been in use for two years. The solvency of European banks has been steadily improving since 2008 lshtien and is lshes doubled since the crisis. The median Tier 1 d solvency ratio for euro area banks was 15.5% at the end of 2015. There are differences in the solvency of banks, but the solvency of the weakest banks has also improved significantly in recent years. All banks are currently well above the minimum solvency requirements of 8%. The share of banks' more stable financing has increased steadily While banks' solvency has improved, the share of more stable financing has also steadily increased. One of the lessons of the financial crisis was that the high share of short-term market financing in bank financing makes banks vulnerable to various market mice. The share of more stable financial assets, such as deposits, in bank financing has steadily increased since the crisis, while the share of market financing has declined. At the same time, market financing has focused more on short-term to long-term financing, which also contributes to the stability of banks' own financing. Banks' profitability has been relatively low The profitability of banks can be measured, for example, by the rate of return (ROE) of their own pssoma. According to this indicator, the profitability of European banks has been low in the post-crisis years. The average yield of the large banks in the euro area has remained around or below five per cent in recent years, while in pre-crisis years it could be as high as 10-15%. There are also large country-specific differences in the profitability of banks. The problem for system risk is that the banks with the lowest profitability often come from large European countries. Low profitability affects banks in several ways. The bank's losses undermine the bank's solvency and low rates of return, and the banks' ability to pay dividends, which reduces their attractiveness as an investment. This can reduce the scope for banks to operate if they need additional financing. The European Central Bank has estimated that the return on banks' own pssoma has been lower during the financial crisis than the cost of its own pssoma, which has been estimated at between 8% and 10%. There are several reasons for the low profitability of banks, which vary from one bank to another and from one country to another. Some of the causes are cyclical and some are more structural. Ksyn's next step was to make a significant contribution to the low profitability. Debt crisis debt collection puts a strain on profitability, especially in banks in crisis countries The financial crisis and the euro area debt crisis led to a recession in which some banks have had a large number of unmanaged loans on their balance sheets. At the end of 2015, banks in the euro area had a combined balance of 950 billion. euro value of outstanding loans, which accounts for about 9% of gdp in the euro area. The amount of non-performing loans varies considerably from country to country and is particularly high in the euro area debt crisis in the countries: Greece, Cyprus, Italy, Spain and Ireland. Non-performing loans reduce the bank's profitability in many different autumns. They are considered to be more profitable purposes than psssoma when the bank has to tie the bank to reserves for possible future credit losses. The maintenance of non-performing loans also ties up resources and increases the administrative costs of banks. The high negative spiral of non-performing loans in the bank and the real economy: a recovery in the real economy would help to unwind the problem of unmanaged loans, but the high level of non-performing loans makes it difficult for the bank to support the recovery of the real economy through financing. Although the crisis is almost ten years away, the solution to the problem of non-performing loans has progressed slowly. There are a number of reasons, including the incomplete resources or capabilities of banks to manage unmanaged loans, as well as the various factors related to bankruptcy laws. The biggest factor is money. Bad debts and their settlement are part of normal banking, but when non-performing loans account for more than a third of a bank's total loan portfolio and are repeated in several banks and in several countries, this is a problem at the level of the system. The European Central Bank, in its capacity as banking supervisor, has made a conscious effort to find a solution to the problem of non-performing loans. The first step was to clarify the extent of the problem and the next step is to provide guidance to the banks on how to solve the problem. It is clear that the problem of unmanaged loans will not be solved in one fell swoop. The problem of unmanaged loans is a good example of how expensive financial crises resulting from over-indebtedness can be and how long it can take to recover. The low growth and interest rate operating environment weakens the profitability of traditional banking Another factor that is undermining the profitability of banks, affecting banks across Europe, is the operating model of low real economy growth and interest rates. The uncertainty about the future development of the real economy will weaken the demand for credit and other banking services and will not bring income to banks in the form of increasing loan volumes and commission income. Low interest rates, on the other hand, reduce banks' interest income and narrow loan margins, as banks' ability to adopt the maturity transformation typical of banking weakens when yields are low and low. In the short term, banks can agree on falling interest rates. They may increase the value of bank-owned bonds. They may also increase net interest income because the bank's own financing costs fall faster than the interest income they receive on loans. In the end, however, the impact becomes negative. High-yielding loans will be replaced by new loans at lower interest rates, which will reduce banks' net interest income. At the same time, the positive effect of the decrease in banks' own interest costs will subside, as they will not be able to set negative interest rates on deposits. In the past, the fall in the cost of borrowing has compensated for the decrease in interest income, but in the first two quarters of 2016, a decrease in banks' net interest income has already begun to signal. The negative impact of low growth and interest rates on banks' profitability is therefore likely to increase in the future. The impact of low interest rates on banks is particularly high in Europe, as net interest income accounts for more than half of the profits of large European banks. Indeed, at the bank level, low interest rates have the greatest negative impact on those banks whose operating model is based on traditional banking and which have other forms of income. The prolonged period of low growth and interest rates has been a challenge for all developed economies since the financial crisis. The low interest rate and growth are driven by a number of structural factors, such as the ageing rate, the share of the stature rate and the slowdown in productivity developments, which are lowering the so-called natural interest rate. As a result, the period of low growth and interest rates may turn out to be a long-term scenario to which banks will have to adapt by changing their operating models. Structural problems against the background of low profitability The low profitability of banks is also due to structural factors. The European banking sector is inefficient in terms of cost structure: banks' costs in relation to revenues are high. The median cost-return ratio in the euro area was 58% in 2015 and is weak, especially in the larger euro area countries such as Germany, France and Italy. The size of the European banking sector is very large for the economy and there are a large number of banks. The network of branches of banks is extensive. In addition, the banking sector is partly fragmented by country and region. Overcapacity and fragmentation reduce the profitability of banks through low cost-effectiveness and, at the same time, may hinder the expansion of good practices and operating models from one country to another. Fines and legal fees are a burden for some banks Bank fines for breaches of general good business practice and the associated legal costs have increased significantly in the years since the financial crisis. The costs associated with bad practices have been significant for some banks. In addition to the actual costs incurred, banks' profitability is burdened by provisions for potential future costs that are excluded from the bank's productive forms of pssomanksych. In addition to the profitability of banks, violations of the policy also have a negative impact on the reputation of banks. Increased sshining creates stability at the expense of profits The 2007-08 financial crisis showed that crises can be very costly. That is why the supervisors have sought to make a financial system through a variety of financial reforms. The reforms have focused on the banks, and they have succeeded in making the banking system more stable. Risks and returns often pass through the kssi ksdesss, and vsjsjsmststs also means lower returns. It is therefore true that the restructuring of banks may have had a negative impact on the profitability of banks. They have also been able to deprive banks of some of the activities considered to be profitable but risky. An increase in stability at the expense of a certain reduction in yields is justified. It is regrettable, however, that this comes at a time when there are other challenges in creating bank returns. That is why the reform of the Sssntely must also take into account the state of the banks as a whole and give the banks enough time to adapt to the new tightening of operations. Stress tests measure banks' resilience to losses The European Banking Authority (EBA) tests banks' loss-absorbing capacity every two years in europe-wide stress tests carried out in cooperation with the ECB and the European System Risk Board. The purpose of the stress tests is to assess the loss-bearing capacity of banks in a hypothetical situation where banks' performance deteriorates significantly as a result of serious and large-scale real economy and financial market failures. The outcome of the stress test is the impact of the favourable scenario on the bank's credit losses and core solvency ratio (CET1), which is a key measure of a bank's loss-bearing capacity. The results of the stress tests confirm the picture of the state of banks The 2016 stress test involved 51 banks and their assets account for around 70% of the total assets of the European banking system. According to the results of the stress tests, the loss-bearing capacity of European banks has improved over the past two years. The average core solvency ratio of banks was better than that of the 2014 stress test, both in each case and after the favourable scenario. Despite the fact that the impact of the adverse scenario on solvency was greater than that of the 2014 stress test. Part of the reason for this was a stricter test procedure and a more severe scenario. Although there were significant differences between banks, with one exception, the core solvency ratio of all banks was well above the reference value of 5.5 % in the adverse scenario of the 2014 stress test. The stress test results thus confirm the fact that solvency is not the main problem facing banks at the moment. Stress tests are often criticised in public. The annual stress tests have been criticised because they do not highlight the problem of banks' profitability. However, it is understood that the stress test examines the carrying capacity of banks in the short term of various shocks to the real economy and the financial markets. Low profitability is a problem for a longer period of time. The stress tests do not look at banks' business strategies and long-term plans to address, for example, the NPL problem. It is good to remember that the stress test is one of the supervisor's jobs among others. The stress test gives an overview of the state of the banks from one corner, but not the overall picture. The fact that the problem of low profitability is not ostressitestatao does not mean that the supervisor does not look at it otherwise. That does not mean that the supervisor is not concerned about the profitability of the banks. Only profitable banks can remain solvent for a long period of time. The problem of banks' profitability will not be alleviated in the short term Bank share prices reflect market expectations regarding banks' future dividend-paying capacity and thus future profitability. The market's perception of the future profitability of banks has been rather pessimistic, especially during the current year, and banks' share prices have fallen. The stronger declines have occurred during events d such as the uk's withdrawal from the EU - but the share price performance has also been weak compared to international standards. It is certain that any economic growth and an increase in interest rates would not solve the problems of all banks. Banks cannot therefore expect a better state of the real economy, but their return to the level of profitability depends on their ability to reform. The importance of the banking sector in the financing system has declined since the crisis The size of the European banking system grew steadily in the years leading up to the crisis. Banks increased their lending and the supply of various financial products. Since the onset of the crisis and the reduction in risk appetite for these products, there has been no demand for these products, and the old heavy cost structures of the banks have become a burden on the banks. To the current volume of activity, the personnel and branch networks of the banks are oversized, despite the fact that they have been cut back in the years since the crisis. A crisis is always the beginning of something new. The post-crisis response has been conducive to an increase in market-based financing and an increase in the share of non-bank financial sector services. The diversification of financial resources is good for consumers. It can also be a good thing for banks, so that they do not have to be responsible for all the tasks related to the operation of the financing system. Since the years of the crisis, the role of banks in financing has increased in Europe, which means that, among other things, banks' balance sheets have remained more or less stable after the crisis, while the balance sheets of other financial players have grown. Digitalisation is more of an opportunity for banks than a threat In addition to the weak real economy and the tightening of the situation, the post-crisis response has been affected by the technological transformation of the mssr. Digitalisation and related innovations have shaped many industries and its impact has also extended to the financial sector. Technology, in particular information technology, used to provide banking insurance, financial, investment or payment services, is referred to as FinTech, financial techonoly, i.e. fintech. Over the past couple of years, numerous growth companies have emerged which effectively embrace the opportunities created by digitalisation and offer some services previously exclusively provided by banks, such as payment services. In addition, the market is currently home to a wide range of crowdfunding services, peer-to-peer lending, as well as debt funds and wealth management services. Although the number of companies is numerous, on the whole it is still marginal compared to traditional forms of financial services. In addition, competition can deprive banks of market share in some high-risk or narrow-margin segments, which means that they are not able to renew themselves and accept the potential of technology. This is the most important part of the past in terms of payment services. The ability of banks to face competition is often slowed down by the fact that many of them have outdated IT systems that can be expensive to renew. Large organizations are also often slower than small growth companies to react to rapid development, which creates a competitive advantage for newcomers. On the other hand, the diversification of financial systems and technological advances may allow banks to concentrate on their core activities, allowing some activities to be transferred to other actors. They can also try to build a new kind of financing system together with new players. This can significantly reduce the cost level of banks. A significant advantage of banks in the competition is that their customer base is already ready. Indeed, several banks have been in the past in the new technology system. The future of banks depends on their ability to reform The financial industry is in the midst of a significant transformation. The future of the banks depends on their ability to reform into a new operating environment characterised by a long period of weak growth and low interest rates, intensified sshining and increased competition. Some banks have stepped up since the crisis, but there is still room for improvement. Fintechnology is key to improving operational efficiency. Hysdynchmslls technology banks can secure their own market share and at the same time create new revenues, as well as cut fixed infrastructure costs. Do banks have a future? The operation of the funding system is based on trust. The funding will direct the funding to productive investment targets. The back of the Sssschjis is guarded by a supervisor. The banking system, which is well supervised and guaranteed by the central bank, will therefore also be in demand in the future. Banks also play an important role in society in the context of monetary policy. The financial crisis and breaches of the way banks operate have damaged confidence in the financial system. In the new financing system, modern banks will become clear, which will be able to create a profitable business model by eliminating unnecessary parts of their operations and focus on their best area of expertise, and which will operate in a way that corresponds to the reliable and responsible social actor that a bank should be. 161108 Mits European Banks kuuluu_Studia Monetaria_clear.pdf 161108 Mits European Banks kuuluu_Studia Monetaria_clear.pdf (/globalassets/en/suomen_pankki/current affairs/speeches/Documents/161108_Mits_eurooppalaisille_pankeille_kuuluu_Studia_Moneta banking (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tagbanking) nancial markets (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tagnancial markets)

Tmn on osoittanut mys se, ett kuluvan vuoden aikana koettujen sokkien -kuten Iso-Britannian kansannestystuloksen EU:sta eroamisen puolesta -aiheuttamat markkinaturbulenssit eivt ole aiheuttaneet pankeille pitkkestoisia tai jrjestelmn tasolle levinneit merkittvi hiriit. Toisaalta, kriisin jlkeinen aika on ollut pankeille haastavaa. Pankkien on tytynyt pysty jatkamaan toimintaansa monelta osin vaikeammassa toimintaympristss, jota leimaavat pitkn jatkunut heikko reaalitalouden kasvu ja matala korkotaso, kiristyv sntely ja lisntyv kilpailu. Useiden pankkien toimintakyky vaikeuttaa mys edellisen kriisin lasku, joka on viel osittain maksamatta. Pankkisektori on jo pitkn krsinyt heikosta kannattavuudesta, jolla on negatiivisia vaikutuksia sek lyhyell ett pitkll aikavlill. Lyhyell aikavlill heikko kannattavuus heikent pankkien kyky toimia rahoituksen vlittjn taloudessa ja se mys altistaa pankit haavoittuvaisiksi erilaisille markkinaturbulensseille. Pitkn jatkuessaan heikko kannattavuus sy pankkien vakavaraisuutta ja voi lopulta vaarantaa niiden toimintakyvyn. Kriisin jlkeinen aika on ollut otollinen kasvualusta kilpailulle, jota kiihdytt rahoitusinnovaatioihin liittyvn teknologian nopea kehitys. Rahoitusteknologian kehittyminen ja kilpailun lisntyminen on hyv asia kuluttajille ja rahoitusvakaudelle, mutta se voi olla hyv asia mys pankeille. Pankkien tulevaisuus riippuukin pitklti niiden kyvyst uudistua. Kun puhutaan eurooppalaisten pankkien tilasta ja tulevaisuuden nkymist, niin tytyy muistaa ett jo pelkstn euroalueella on noin 5500 luottolaitosta. Pankit ovat erilaisia niin kooltaan kuin toimintamalleiltaankin  samoin vahvuuksiltaan ja haasteiltaan. Osalle pankeista kuuluu siten parempaa kuin toisille. Ksittelen pankkisektoria tss esityksess kuitenkin posin kokonaisuutena ja kyn lpi teemoja, jotka ovat yleistettviss joko koko sektoriin tai sen merkittviin osiin. Pankkien vakavaraisuus on parantunut tasaisesti Pankin vakavaraisuuden mittarina kytetn yleisimmin erilaisia vakavaraisuussuhdelukuja, jotka kertovat kuinka paljon pankilla on pomaa suhteessa sen riskipainotettuihin saamisiin. Trkein nist on ydinvakavaraisuusuhde, jota kytetn pankin vakavaraisuuden mittarina vakavaraisuussntelyss. Jos halutaan tarkastella pankkien vakavaraisuuden kehityst pitemmll aikavlill, tytyy kuitenkin kytt laajemman poman mritelmn vakavaraisuusmittaria: Tier 1 vakavaraisuussuhdetta, koska ydinvakavaraisuussuhde on ollut kytss vasta kaksi vuotta. Eurooppalaisten pankkien vakavaraisuus on parantunut tasaisesti vuodesta 2008 lhtien ja se on lhes kaksinkertaistunut kriisin jlkeen. Euroalueen pankkien mediaani Tier 1 vakavaraisuussuhde oli vuoden 2015 lopussa 15,5 %. Pankkien vlill on eroja vakavaraisuudessa, mutta mys heikoimpien pankkien vakavaraisuus on parantunut merkittvsti viime vuosien aikana. Kaikki pankit ylittvt tll hetkell reilusti vakavaraisuussntelyn minimivaatimustason, joka on 8 %. Pankkien vakaamman rahoituksen osuus on kasvanuttasaisesti Samalla kun pankkien vakavaraisuus on parantunut, mys sen vakaamman rahoituksen osuus on kasvanut tasaisesti. Yksi finanssikriisin opetuksista oli, ett suuri lyhytaikaisen markkinarahoituksen osuus pankkien rahoituksessa tekee pankeista haavoittuvan erilaisille markkinahiriille. Vakaampien rahoituslhteiden, kuten talletuksien, osuus pankkien rahoituksesta on kasvanut tasaisesti kriisin jlkeen samalla kun markkinarahoituksen osuus on laskenut. Samalla markkinarahoitus on painottunut enemmn lyhytaikaisesta pitkaikaiseen rahoitukseen, mik mys edesauttaa pankkien oman rahoituksen vakautta. Pankkien kannattavuus on ollutpitkn heikkoa Pankkien kannattavuutta voidaan mitata esimerkiksi oman poman tuottoasteella (ROE). Tmn mittarin mukaan eurooppalaisten pankkien kannattavuus on ollut kriisin jlkeisin vuosina heikkoa. Euroalueiden suurten pankkien keskimrinen oman poman tuotto on pysytellyt viime vuosina viiden prosentin tuntumassa tai sen alle, kun se saattoi kriisi edeltvin vuosina olla jopa 10-15 %:n luokkaa. Pankkien kannattavuudessa on mys suuria maakohtaisia eroja. Jrjestelmriskin kannalta ongelmallista on se, ett heikoimman kannattavuuden pankit tulevat usein suurista Euroopan maista. Heikko kannattavuus vaikuttaa pankkeihin useilla tavoilla. Pankin tappiot heikentvt pankin vakavaraisuutta ja matalat tuottotasot vhentvt pankkien osingonjakomahdollisuuksia, mik heikent niiden kiinnostavuutta sijoituskohteena. Tm voi kaventaa pankkien toimintamahdollisuuksia jos ne tarvitsevat lisrahoitusta. Euroopan keskuspankki on arvioinut, ett pankkien oman poman tuotto on ollut finanssikriisist lhtien matalampi kuin oman poman kustannus, jonka on arvioitu olevan 8-10 %. Syit pankkien heikon kannattavuuden taustalla on useita, ja ne vaihtelevat sek pankeittain ett maittain. Osa syist on suhdanteista riippuvaisia ja osa enemmn rakenteellisia. Kyn seuraavaksi lpi merkittvimpi tekijit heikon kannattavuuden taustalla. Velkakriisin perint rasittaa kannattavuutta etenkin kriisimaiden pankeissa Finanssikriisi ja euroalueen velkakriisi johtivat taantumaan, jonka jljilt joidenkin pankkien taseisiin on jnyt paljon hoitamattomia lainoja. Euroalueen pankeilla oli vuoden 2015 lopussa yhteens lhes 950 mrd. euron arvosta hoitamattomia lainoja, mik on noin 9 % euroalueen BKT:sta. Hoitamattomien lainojen mr vaihtelee huomattavasti maittain ja on erityisen korkea euroalueen velkakriisist krsineiss maissa: Kreikassa, Kyproksella, Italiassa, Espanjassa ja Irlannissa. Hoitamattomat lainat heikentvt pankin kannattavuutta monesta eri syyst. Ne pidttvt pomaa tuottavammista kytttarkoituksista, kun pankin tytyy sitoa pomaa varauksiin mahdollisia tulevia luottotappioita varten. Hoitamattomien lainojen yllpito sitoo mys resursseja ja lis pankkien hallinnollisia kustannuksia. Korkea hoitamattomien lainojen mr yllpit mys negatiivista kierrett pankin tilan ja reaalitalouden tilan vlill: reaalitalouden toipuminen edesauttaisi hoitamattomien lainojen ongelman purkautumista, mutta hoitamattomien lainojen korkea mr vaikeuttaa pankin kyky tukea reaalitalouden toipumista rahoituksen vlityksen kautta. Vaikka kriisist on jo kohta kymmenen vuotta, hoitamattomien lainojen ongelman ratkaisu on edennyt hitaasti. Syit on useita, ja niihin lukeutuvat pankkien vaillinaiset resurssit tai kyvyt ksitell hoitamattomia lainoja sek erilaiset konkurssilainsdntn liittyvt tekijt. Suurin tekij on raha. Luottotappiot ja niiden ksittely kuuluvat normaaliin pankkitoimintaan, mutta silloin kun hoitamattomia lainoja onkin yhtkki yli kolmannes pankin koko luottokannasta ja tm toistuu useassa pankissa ja useassa maassa, kyseess on jrjestelmtason ongelma. Euroopan keskuspankki on pankkivalvojan ominaisuudessaan pyrkinyt mrtietoisesti lytmn ratkaisua hoitamattomien lainojen ongelmaan. Ensimminen askel oli selvitt ongelman laajuus ja seuraava askel on tehd ohjeistus pankeille ongelman ratkaisemiseksi. On selv, ett hyvllkn suunnitelmalla hoitamattomien lainojen ongelmaa ei tulla ratkaisemaan yhdess yss. Hoitamattomien lainojen ongelma onkin hyv esimerkki siit kuinka kalliita ylivelkaantumisesta syntyvt finanssikriisit voivat olla ja kuinka kauan niist toipuminen voi vied. Matalan kasvun ja koron toimintaymprist heikent perinteisen pankkitoiminnan kannattavuutta Toinen pankkien kannattavuutta heikentv tekij, joka vaikuttaa pankkeihin koko Euroopassa, on matalan reaalitalouden kasvun ja korkotason toimintaymprist. Epvarmuus reaalitalouden tulevasta kehityksest heikent luottojen ja muiden pankkipalveluiden kysynt eik tuo pankeille tuloa kasvavien lainavolyymien ja palkkiotuottojen muodossa. Matala korkotaso taas laskee pankkien korkotuottoja ja kaventaa lainamarginaaleja, sill pankkien kyky hydynt pankkitoiminnalle tyypillist maturiteettitransformaatiota heikkenee tuottokyrn ollessa matala ja loiva. Lyhyell aikavlill pankit voivat hyty laskevista koroista. Ne saattavat nostaa pankkien omistamien velkakirjalainojen arvoa. Ne saattavat mys nostaa korkokatetta, koska pankin omat rahoituskustannukset laskevat nopeammin kuin niiden lainoista saamat korkotuotot. Lopulta vaikutus kuitenkin kntyy negatiiviseksi. Korkeasti tuottavat lainat pttyvt ja niiden tilalle tulee uusia lainoja matalammalla korolla, joka laskee pankkien korkokatetta. Samalla pankkien omien korkokustannusten laskun positiivinen vaikutus laantuu, sill ne eivt voi asettaa negatiivisia korkoja talletuksille. Thn menness varainhankinnan kustannusten lasku on kompensoinut korkotuottojen pienentymist, mutta vuoden 2016 kahden ensimmisen neljnneksen aikana on alkanut tulla jo merkkej pankkien korkokatteen laskemisesta. Matalan kasvun ja koron negatiiviset vaikutukset pankkien kannattavuuteen todennkisesti siten kasvavat jatkossa. Matalan koron vaikutus pankkeihin on erityisen suuri Euroopassa, koska korkokate kattaa suurten eurooppalaisten pankkien tuotoista yli puolet. Pankkitasolla matala korkotaso vaikuttaakin eniten negatiivisesti juuri niihin pankkeihin, joiden toimintamalli perustuu perinteiseen pankkitoimintaan ja joilla on vhemmn muita tulomuotoja. Pitkn jatkunut matalan kasvun ja koron toimintaymprist on ollut haasteena kaikissa kehittyneiss talouksissa finanssikriisin jlkeen. Matalan koron ja kasvun taustalla on useita rakenteellisia tekijit, kuten vanhentuva vest, vhentyv tyikisten osuus ja hidastunut tuottavuuskehitys, jotka laskevat niin sanotun luonnollisen koron tasoa. Tmn vuoksi matalan kasvun ja koron aika voi osoittautua pitkkestoiseksi ilmiksi, johon pankkien on sopeuduttava toimintamallejaan muuttamalla. Rakenteelliset ongelmat heikon kannattavuuden taustalla Pankkien heikon kannattavuuden taustalla on mys rakenteellisia tekijit. Euroopan pankkisektori on kustannusrakenteeltaan tehoton: pankkien kustannukset suhteessa tuottoihin ovat korkeat. Kustannustuottosuhteen mediaani oli euroalueella vuonna 2015 58 % ja se on heikko erityisesti eriss suurissa euromaissa, kuten Saksassa, Ranskassa ja Italiassa. Euroopan pankkisektorin koko on talouteen nhden suuri ja pankkeja on lukumrltn paljon. Pankkien konttoriverkosto on laaja. Lisksi pankkisektori on osittain sek maittain ett alueittain fragmentoitunut. Ylikapasiteetti ja fragmentaatio heikentvt pankkien kannattavuutta heikon kustannustehokkuuden kautta ja samalla saattaa est hyvien kytntjen ja toimintamallien laajentumista maasta toiseen. Sakkomaksut ja oikeudenkyntikulut ovat rasite osalle pankeista Yleisten hyvien liiketoimintatapojen rikkomisesta johtuvat pankkien sakkomaksut ja niihin liittyvt oikeudenkyntikulut ovat kasvaneet merkittvsti finanssikriisin jlkeisin vuosina. Huonoihin toimintatapoihin liittyvt kustannukset ovat olleet joidenkin pankkien osalta merkittvi. Toteutuneiden kustannusten lisksi pankkien kannattavuutta rasittaa mahdollisia tulevia kustannuksia varten yllpidetyt varaukset, jotka ovat pois pankin tuottavista pomankyttmuodoista. Toimintataparikkomukset vaikuttavat pankkien kannattavuuden lisksi negatiivisesti mys pankkien maineeseen. Lisntynyt sntely luo vakautta tuottojen kustannuksella 2007-08 finanssikriisi osoitti, ett kriisit voivat olla erittin kalliita. Siksi valvojat ovat pyrkineet tekemn rahoitusjrjestelmst vhempiriskisen erilaisten sntelyuudistusten kautta. Uudistukset ovat posin kohdistuneet pankkeihin, ja ovat siin mieless onnistuneet, ett pankkijrjestelm on nyt aiempaa vakaampi. Riskit ja tuotot kulkevat usein ksi kdess, ja vhempi riskillisyys tarkoittaa vjmtt mys pienempi tuottoja. On siis totta, ett sntelyuudistukset ovat voineet vaikuttaa pankkien kannattavuuteen negatiivisesti. Ne ovat mys voineet vied pankeilta joitakin tuottaviksi katsottuja, mutta riskillisi toimintamuotoja. Vakauden lisntyminen tuottojen jonkin asteisen vhenemisen kustannuksella on perusteltua. On kuitenkin valitettavaa, ett tm osuu aikaan, jolloin pankkien tuottojen luomiseen kohdistuu mys muita haasteita. Siksi mys sntelyn uudistamisessa tytyy huomioida pankkien tila kokonaisuudessaan ja antaa pankeille tarpeeksi aikaa sopeutua uuteen sntelyltn kiristyneeseen toimintaympristn. Stressitesteill mitataan pankkien tappionsietokyky Euroopan pankkiviranomainen (EPV) testaavat pankkien tappionsietokyky joka toinen vuosi Euroopan laajuisissa stressitesteiss, jotka toteutetaan yhteistyss EKP:n ja Euroopan jrjestelmriskikomitean kanssa. Stressitestien tarkoituksena on arvioida pankkien tappionkantokyky hypoteettisessa tilanteessa, jossa pankkien toimintaympristn tila heikkenee merkittvsti vakavien ja laaja-alaisten reaalitalouden ja rahoitusmarkkinoiden hiriiden seurauksena. Stressitestin tuloksena saadaan epsuotuisan skenaarion vaikutus pankin luottotappioihin ja ydinvakavaraisuussuhteeseen (CET1), joka on keskeinen pankin tappionkantokyvyn mittari. Stressitestien tulokset vahvistavat kuvaa pankkien tilasta Vuoden 2016 stressitestiss oli mukana 51 pankkia, ja niiden varojen osuus Euroopan pankkijrjestelmn kokonaisvaroista on noin 70 %. Stressitestien tulosten mukaan Euroopan pankkien tappionkantokyky on parantunut viimeisen kahden vuoden aikana. Pankkien keskimrinen ydinvakavaraisuussuhde oli sek lhtkohtaisesti ett epsuotuisan skenaarion jlkeen parempi kuin vuoden 2014 stressitesteiss. Tm siit huolimatta, ett epsuotuisan skenaarion vaikutus vakavaraisuuteen oli suurempi kuin vuoden 2014 stressitesteiss. Osasyyn thn oli aiempaa tiukempi testimenetelm ja ankarampi epsuotuisa skenaario. Vaikka pankkien vlill oli merkittvikin eroja, yht poikkeusta lukuun ottamatta kaikkien pankkien ydinvakavaraisuussuhde ylitti selvsti vuoden 2014 stressitestin epsuotuisassa skenaariossa kytetyn 5,5 prosentin viitearvon. Stressitestitulokset vahvistavat siten sit tietoa, ett vakavaraisuus ei ole pankkien tmnhetkinen suurin ongelma. Stressitestej arvostellaan usein julkisuudessa. Tmn vuotisiin stressitesteihin on kohdistunut kritiikki siit, ett testit eivt tuo esille pankkien kannattavuusongelmaa. Tytyy kuitenkin ymmrt, ett stressitesteiss tarkastellaan pankkien kantokyky erilaisia reaalitalouden ja rahoitusmarkkinoiden shokkeja lyhyell aikavlill. Heikko kannattavuus on pitemmn ajan ongelma. Stressitestit eivt myskn tarkastele pankkien liiketoimintastrategioita ja pitkn aikavlin suunnitelmia esimerkiksi NPL-ongelman ratkaisemiseksi. On hyv muistaa, ett stressitesti on yksi valvojan tykalu muiden joukossa. Stressitesti antaa kuvan pankkien tilasta yhdest nkkulmasta, mutta ei kokonaiskuvaa. Se, ett heikon kannattavuuden ongelmaa ei stressitestata, ei tarkoita sit ettei valvoja sit tarkastelisi muuten. Se ei tarkoita sit etteik valvoja olisi huolissaan pankkien kannattavuudesta. Vain kannattavat pankit voivat pitkll aikavlill pysy vakavaraisena. Pankkien kannattavuusongelmalle ei ny helpotusta lyhyell aikavlill Pankkiosakkeiden hinnat heijastavat markkinoiden odotuksia pankkien tulevasta osingonjakokyvyst ja siten tulevasta kannattavuudesta. Markkinoiden nkemys pankkien tulevasta kannattavuudesta on ollut etenkin kuluvan vuoden ajan varsin pessimistinen ja pankkien osakekurssit ovat laskeneet. Voimakkaammat laskut ovat ajoittuneet eriden tapahtumien  kuten Iso-Britannian EU-eronestystuloksen -jlkeiseen aikaan, mutta osakekurssien kehitys on ollut heikkoa mys kansainvlisesti verrattuna. On todennkist, ett mahdollinen talouskasvu ja korkojen nousu ei sekn ratkaisisi kaikkien pankkien ongelmia. Pankit eivt siten voi jd odottamaan parempaa reaalitalouden tilaa, vaan pankkien paluu kestvn kannattavuuden tasoon riippuu pankkien kyvyst uudistua. Pankkisektorin merkitys rahoitusjrjestelmss on pienentynyt kriisin jlkeen Euroopan pankkijrjestelmn koko kasvoi tasaisesti kriisi edeltvin vuosina. Pankit kasvattivat lainanantoaan ja erilaisten rahoitustuotteiden tarjontaa. Kriisin tultua ja riskinottohalukkuuden vhennytty nille tuotteille ei olekaan ollut en kysynt, ja tuottojen vhetess pankkien vanhat raskaat kustannusrakenteet ovat muodostuneet pankeille taakaksi. Nykyiseen toiminnan volyymiin nhden pankkien henkilstmrt ja konttoriverkostot ovat ylimitoitettuja siit huolimatta, ett niit on karsittu kriisin jlkeisin vuosina. Kriisi on aina mys uuden alku. Kriisinjlkeinen toimintaymprist on ollut otollinen markkinaperusteisen rahoituksen kasvulle ja muiden kuin pankkien tarjoamien rahoitussektorin palveluiden osuuden kasvulle. Rahoituslhteiden monipuolistuminen on kuluttajille hyv asia. Se voi olla hyv asia mys pankeille, jotta niiden ei tarvitse vastata kaikista rahoitusjrjestelmn toimintaan liittyvist tehtvist. Kriisivuosien jlkeen pankkien merkitys rahoituksen vlittjn onkin vhentynyt Euroopassa, mik nkyy mm. siin ett pankkien tase on pysynyt kriisin jlkeen kutakuinkin vakaana samalla kun muiden rahoitustoimijoiden taseet ovat kasvaneet. Digitaalisaatio on pankeille enemmn mahdollisuus kuin uhka Heikon reaalitalouden ja kiristyneen sntelyn lisksi kriisin jlkeiseen toimintaympristn on vaikuttanut merkittviss mrin teknologinen murros. Digitalisaatio ja siihen liittyvt innovaatiot ovat muokanneet useita toimialoja, ja sen vaikutus on ulottunut mys rahoitussektorille. Teknologiaa, erityisesti tietotekniikkaa, jota kytetn pankki-vakuutus-, rahoitus-, sijoitus-tai maksupalvelujen tuottamiseen kutsutaan sanalla FinTech, financial techonoly, eli finanssiteknologia. Parin viime vuoden aikana on syntynyt lukuisia kasvuyrityksi, jotka hydyntvt tehokkaasti digitalisaation luomia mahdollisuuksia ja tarjoavat joitakin aikaisemmin yksinomaan pankkien tarjoamia palveluja, kuten maksupalveluja. Lisksi markkinoilla toimii nykyn erilaisia joukkorahoituspalveluja, vertaislainoja myntvi yrityksi sek velkarahastoja ja varallisuuden hallintapalveluja tarjoavia yhtiit. Vaikka yrityksi on lukuisia, kokonaisuutena ilmi on kuitenkin viel perinteisiin rahoituspalvelumuotoihin verrattuna marginaalinen. Lisntyv kilpailu voi vied pankeilta markkinaosuuksia joillakin korkean riskin tai kapeiden marginaalien segmenteill, mikli ne eivt pysty itse uudistumaan ja hydyntmn teknologian tuomia mahdollisuuksia. Thn menness tst on eniten nytt maksupalveluiden osalta. Pankkien kyky vastata kilpailuun hidastaa usein se, ett useilla niist on kytssn vanhentuneet IT-jrjestelmt joiden uusiminen voi olla kallista. Isot organisaatiot ovat usein mys pieni kasvuyrityksi hitaampia reagoimaan nopeaan kehitykseen, mik luo kilpailuetua uusille tulokkaille. Toisaalta rahoitusjrjestelmn monipuolistuminen ja teknologian kehittyminen voi luoda pankeille mahdollisuuden keskitty omiin ydintoimintoihin antaen joidenkin toimintojen siirty muille toimijoille. Ne voivat mys pyrki rakentamaan uudenlaista rahoitusjrjestelm yhdess uusien toimijoiden kanssa. Tm voi laskea pankkien kustannustasoa huomattavasti. Pankkien merkittvn etuna kilpailussa on se, ett asiakaskunta on niill jo valmiina. Useat pankit ovatkin olleet edellkvijit uuden teknologian hydyntmisess. Pankkien tulevaisuus riippuu niiden kyvyst uudistua Rahoitustoimiala on keskell merkittv murrosta. Pankkien tulevaisuus riippuu niiden kyvyst uudistua uuteen toimintaympristn, jota leimaavat pitk heikon kasvun ja matalan koron toimintaymprist, kiristynyt sntely ja lisntyv kilpailu. Osa pankeista on tehostanut toimintaansa kriisin jlkeen, mutta tehostamisen varaa on edelleen. Finanssiteknologian hydyntminen on avainasemassa toiminnan tehostamiseen. Hydyntmll teknologiaa pankit voivat turvata omat markkinaosuutensa ja samalla luoda uusia tulolhteit, sek leikata kiinteit kustannuksia infrastruktuurista. Onko pankeilla tulevaisuutta? Rahoitusjrjestelmn toiminta perustuu luottamukseen. Rahoituksen vlittj ohjaa sstt tuottaviin investointikohteisiin. Sstjien selustaa vartioi valvoja. Pankkijrjestelmlle, joka on hyvin valvottu ja jonka toimivuuden takaa keskuspankki, on siten kysynt mys jatkossa. Pankeilla on merkittv rooli yhteiskunnassa mys rahapolitiikan vlittjn. Finanssikriisi ja pankkien toimintataparikkomukset ovat vahingoittaneet luottamusta rahoitusjrjestelmn. Uudessa rahoitusjrjestelmss tulevat selvimn nykyaikaiset pankit, jotka pystyvt luomaan kannattavan liiketoimintamallin karsimalla toiminnastaan turhat osat ja keskittymll parhaaseen osaamisalueeseensa, ja jotka toimintatavoiltaan vastaavat sit luotettavaa ja vastuullista yhteiskunnan toimijaa joka pankin kuuluu olla. 161108 Mit eurooppalaisille pankeille kuuluu_Studia Monetaria_clear.pdf 161108 Mit eurooppalaisille pankeille kuuluu_Studia Monetaria_clear.pdf (/globalassets/en/suomen_pankki/ajankohtaista/puheet/Documents/161108_Mit_eurooppalaisille_pankeille_kuuluu_Studia_Moneta banking (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tag=banking) nancial markets (/en/other-pages/tag-search/?tag=nancial markets)

At the same time, there has been an international debate among economists as to whether, after the financial crisis, the slowdown in economic growth is turning into a permanent manifest, so-called secular stagnation. The idea has both authoritative defenders and more optimistic opponents. The current historically pre-existently low interest rates suggest that at least the markets are not confident in the rapid and strong acceleration of economic growth at global level. In my speech, I will discuss the economic factors and the factors that determine the conditions for future development. *** Let's start with the current niggles of the world economy. [Figure 3] Over the past few years, the pull in the global economy has changed. During the years when the international financial crisis hit Europe, the United States and other developed economies hard, growth in the emerging economies was much stronger. Overall, the financial systems of the emerging countries did not respond to the crisis much as in the old industrialised countries, and their domestic demand held up. China, in particular, was the driving force behind global demand in its own category. This changed when China's economic growth began to slow down in turn and the prices of other raw materials fell sharply a few years ago. Many emerging economies depend on export earnings from raw materials. Development weakened in countries that had previously grown rapidly, such as Brazil, South Africa and Russia. The effects of the contraction of the Russian economy have also been strongly felt in Finland. At the same time, developed economies, on the other hand, have now survived the worst stages and effects of the international financial crisis. One of the key factors for Europe's economic development is the UK's EU solution, which threatens to cancel a piece of the already established regional integration process. *** The development of the Finnish economy has been known to be weak for several years. The level of GDP is still significantly lower than in 2008, just before the start of the international financial crisis. [Figure 4] Finland's national economy has suffered several powerful blows in a short period of time. In addition to the general downturn in the international economy, the Finnish economy has been weighed down by sectoral problems in the electronics and forestry industries, the excessively rapid rise in the domestic cost level, the contraction that has begun to contract in the czech economy, and, more recently, the weakness of the Ven?j? economy. The headwinds have been particularly strong on exports. Since 2008, Finnish exports have contracted more than those of other developed economies. In fact, there has not been a single large and long-term contraction in exports for decades in another developed economy. The development of business investment has also been exceptionally weak in Finland. Household demand has remained much stronger. There is an um?rrett?v? explanation. So, since the crisis, we have not experienced the same need to reduce household debts, nor the kind of fall in house prices that we have experienced in many other countries. In Finland, the ability of the financial system to function has remained very good ? at least from the point of view of the banks themselves. On the other hand, Finnish SMEs have often pointed out that banks are not very interested in corporate finance today, and the favourable effect of low interest rates is being held back by tightened bank collateral requirements. At the moment, Finland is experiencing an incipient economic recovery. Last year, the downturn in the Finnish economy was prolonged, and the economy grew slightly. The employment situation has also improved somewhat. However, exports and productive investment by enterprises have remained at a low level. Although GDP growth has been stunted, it has not strengthened in the same way as in previous cyclical upturns, and has so far remained subdued and stable. The engine of growth in Finland is currently domestic demand, supported by low interest rates. Household consumer demand has continued to grow, and construction in particular has increased. The importance of monetary policy in the recovery shows that economic activity is being boosted by the construction activities most strongly influenced by monetary policy stimulus. All in all, Finland's economic development has been strongly ambivalent since 2008. While exports, manufacturing and business investment have contracted, private consumption and service production have increased. The decline in export earnings has meant that consumption growth has been strongly debt-driven. The expenditure of both households and the public sectors has been higher than their income for years. The latest forecasts estimate that economic growth in Finland will continue, although not very fast. However, it is certain how long such growth can continue in Finland unless exports and business investment recover. The so far weak growth in exports is a cause for concern, as a balanced and sustained economic recovery would also require a pullback for exports. If it does not, the growth at some point ? sooner or more recently - will come from the growth of foreign trade deficits and household indebtedness. Continued strong debt-driven growth would not be at the bottom of the year. *** One of the most important factors in the current economic cycles is whether the trend of long-term economic growth is slowing down. If you want to understand the broad lines of the Finnish economy from the 1800s to the present day, productivity growth plays a key role. Production per capita in Finland grew exceptionally fast compared to most other countries for most of the 1900s. Productivity growth was so rapid that it was enough to produce fruit and rapid economic growth and a reduction in the time per capita. How has Finland, the absolute periphery of Europe, become one of the most developed economies in the world? One explanation is the so-called "per?ss?hiiht?j?n advantage", i.e. it was possible to take into account the production methods and technology that had already been established elsewhere and found to be good, not just the rise. China is, of course, a huge recent example. In other words, in order to grow faster than other countries, we need conditions for a long period of time other than individual growth! One of the key factors behind Finland's success was, and may continue to be, international integration, an increase in the level of competence in the labour force and, in many respects, strong institutions. Industrialisation, which is linked to international trade, is without a doubt the most important factor in the success of the Finnish economy. The economy of a small country can prosper among the larger ones by specialising in export industries where economies of scale can be achieved. This can be successful, for example, in sectors where raw materials are abundantly extracted from the home country. ? International links are linked to Finland's industrialisation and rapid productivity growth in many ways. Trade links have made it possible to increase exports and import raw materials and semi-finished products needed by industry. In addition, the cross-border mobility of people and people has contributed to the introduction of new technologies and the development of skills. Over the decades, Finland has seen countless inflows of foreign direct investment ? especially from the most developed economies. Their country also received the necessary financing for investments from abroad. This type of investment was often accompanied by the adoption of frontier production methods. One of the advantages of direct investment is precisely the transfer of know-how from the best companies to new markets. Jukka Jalava of Statistics Finland and Matti Pohjola of Aalto University calculated some time ago that before the great financial crisis of the 2000s, the real income of Finns had risen about 12-fold in just over a hundred years, even though the amount of work done per person had decreased. [Figure 5] Over the decades, our productivity grew by 3-5% per annum. Now, however, the situation has changed. Last year, employment productivity in Finland was at the same level as in 2006. In Finland, at least for a hundred years, there has not been a decade in which productivity growth has stagnated. The situation is new. The growth rate of finland's national economy, the trend of productivity is reversed. It is also very special from a historical point of view. If the obvious slowdown in productivity growth, and even its stagnation, were to prove to be permanent, the social and economic consequences would be revolutionary. They wouldn't be easy or pleasant. One of the things that underlines the importance of productivity growth is that people have learned to trust it. For decades, in economic policy and in the labour market, we have become accustomed to relying on the fact that there will be more and more to be distributed every year. Real wages for the long term will rise and the tax base of the state will increase. Long-term calculations, for example, are based on the assumption of an increase in productivity. There are setbacks and cyclical fluctuations, but our society is built on the assumption that productivity will increase. Productivity growth comes from a few components. First of all, it is the investments that add to the independence of production. The second factor is the technological advances which add to the production of the production that can be achieved with the inputs provided. The third is structural change, in which power and production are shifted from sectors with lower productivity to those with higher productivity. In addition, there are four cases of human development, i.e. the growth of know-how, which improves the quality of work input. As in other developed countries, the reasons for the slowdown in productivity growth can be found in all sectors. The picture is well-known: Productive investment in Finland has been at a long low ebb; The structural change in the sectors of the economy does not increase productivity as in the past decades, but now works in such a way that a larger proportion of the workforce is employed in occupations in the health and care sector, where productivity is lower than, for example, in industry; and, even in terms of the rise in the level of education, the years of rapid growth are probably behind us. *** [Figure 6] It is natural in these circumstances that when examining the conditions for future productivity growth, attention is focused on technology and its impact. The question is how much productivity gains can be expected from information technology in the coming years. What is the impact of eedigiloikanee on productivity and the real income generated by the economy? The great technological revolutions in history are all the way to productivity. Of course, the requirements for skills in the labour market have always changed, and in relation to it, the change seems to be accelerating. In economic policy, it is necessary to take into account trends. The people who lose their jobs must be able to use their skills. The exclusion of the labour market and the lack of transparency is an obstacle. It is at the heart of society in terms of long-standing ties and the conditions for economic growth. Although the consequences of technological development are unpredictable in many ways, political means would not, of course, be able to slow down the introduction of new technologies. The conditions must be in place for Finland to continue to be a country in the use of new technologies. Attempts to slow down would only lead to missed opportunities in a country like Finland and to Finland's relative association with its peer countries. It is clear that the slowdown in productivity growth that has now taken place cannot be a natural expression independent of human activity. Productivity growth is the result of human activity in laboratories, companies and markets. Furthermore, the slowdown in productivity growth and the possible rebirth depend on what is done. This also applies to Finland as a national economy. In concrete terms, what can be done to relaunch productivity growth? The growth of wealth is generated by enterprise in new sectors and regions. In a country that has developed for a long time, it cannot be just a question of development and adaptation. It may be possible to catch up with the lack of productivity in some sectors of the economy, but in a country like Finland it is not enough. With productivity growth on the rise again, it is a question of proactive, innovative enterprise. This requires investment, innovation and international specialisation. In recent years, there has been a better understanding of the role of entrepreneurship, especially growth companies and venture capitalists, in economic renewal. It is considered to be very central to the present day, both among experts and in the public eye. This change in attitudes towards entrepreneurship and success is very welcome. Title: Speech at the farewell reception
text: Deputy Governor Pentti Hakkarainen: speech at the farewell reception. Helsinki, 16.1.2017. . Speech . Monday16 January 2017,6:00 PM Deputy Governor Pentti Hakkarainen Bank of Finland Helsinki, 16.1.2017. Hyvst naiset ja herrat, hyvst ystsvst/Your Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen, Dear friends Let me first thank Governor Liikanen for his kind words and also for arranging this farewell reception. I met Erkki for the first time in 1984 during my diplomat training. He was lecturing us and I remember posing him a question, to which he answered "I see that the course has not been going on for a long time yet". Here in the Bank we have worked together for more than 12 years now. It has been rewarding time. A lot of speed and a lot of dangerous curves! Not only fun but also instructive time. I have learned from him a lot. Let me take only three issues which are intertwined; empowerment, communication and breadth. -how to set goals and get things done; it's important to empower and commit other people in order to make progress. Well planned and prepared is half done, without good preparations your goal may never be achieved -relating to communication, it's not only what you say but you have to get the message across too, so that the recipient understands, or even better, internalizes the issue -explore and inspire, not only narrowly in your business matters but also more broadly in other areas of life Second, let me thank the speakers at today's seminar. It is a great honor for the Bank of Finland, and to me personally, that we had you Governor Knot, Executive Board Member Gonzales-Parmo and ECB Board Member Mersch providing your insights about the current developments in banking in general, and central banking in particular. Klaas, Josz Manuel and Yves, I really appreciate that you have taken the time. Thirdly, I would like to thank all of you here attending the reception. This is a group close to my heart. Each of you have played an important role d some very important role indeed d in my life and my working career. Thank you very much I can continue. There is a Savonian proverb that says that "it is the fault of the nuapur if the flower is not praised". Now they are praised: it has been rewarding and even challenging to work with the Bankers of Finland. I would like to express my sincerest thanks to them. To my partners from outside the bank, I am also grateful. The past few years have been a great time. The Bank of Finland's image of the financial world was nicely reproduced. At the head of finance for a large company, I was a major consumer of banking services, then a leading manager of banks, I was responsible for banking services for customers. Now nsin how the authorities operate in the financial markets, not only in Finland, but also in other parts of the world. In addition, I got to know and appreciate politicians who deal with difficult social issues. In the forthcoming European banking supervision, I will not shake off the dust of the past, but as a continuation of my previous tasks. Finland stands by the fact that there are four financial institutions operating in Finland under the direct supervision of the ECB. There will be other connections as well. The cooperation with many of them will certainly continue and I am delighted. That's why I'm not going to say good, but just thank you for the shsnastic. Ladies and Gentlemen, I am leaving the Bank but I should not say farewell. I will not disappear in any black hole. It's likely that our good cooperation continues with many of you even when I'm moving to the new position at the ECB. Thus let me only thank you for the past years and say that I'm looking forward to meeting you often in other contexts. Thank you! Thank you!

Title: Comments on "Financial sector integration  its role as a facilitator of the catching up process"
text: Deputy Governor Pentti Hakkarainen, Bank of Finland High-level Conference "Convergence in the Baltics" organised by IMF and Eesti Pank in Brussels, 1  2 February 2008 Comments on "Financial sector integration  its role as a facilitator of the catching up process". Text is not identical with the comments presented at the panel, should be deemed as a background non-paper. First, it is clear that financial sector integration plays an important role in the catching-up process of the Baltic states. Financial integration has brought about significant benefits. Entry of foreign banks has brought both improved risk management techniques as well as increased access to funding from parent banks. Without this activity of foreign banks, lending growth and hence the catching-up process would have been slower, as such growth could not have been financed domestically as the cost of capital would have been higher for smaller local banks. Integration has created a more competitive banking sector environment (with declining interest rates), improvements in the institutional environment, and increased creditworthiness of borrowers on the back of improved economic prospects. Banking sector reform also represents a key development in the transition countries. Banking sector reform has led to the emergence of new market segments and increased the range of products available to bank customers, and at the same time reduced costs. More efficient allocation of capital, reduced cost of borrowing as well as increased availability of funding contribute positively to economic development via lowering investment costs and accelerating productivity growth. Deep and liquid financial markets also strengthen the resilience of the European economy by sharing risks between regions through diversification of ownership. Hence, it can be argued that financial integration is overwhelmingly positive for the catching- up process of CEE countries. However, extensive foreign ownership in the banking sector makes financial sector stability and hence entire economic stability dependent on the continued commitment and stability of 1 (3) 1 February 2008 the foreign Hence, there is a strong need to have a regulatory / supervisory framework in the EU that is compatible with the integrated markets. The framework should be efficient and have well-coordinated supervision by the home authority and it should respect the legitimate concerns of the host authorities to be involved in the supervisory process of the major cross-border banks. Smooth cooperation amongst supervisors is needed to allow concerns regarding local economic developments to be taken into account in the supervision of the cross-border banking groups (e.g. concerns of too high credit growth or too lax lending standards). Banking supervision in the EU has been based since 1989 on the principle of home country control. Based on this principle, the supervisor in the EU country that has given authorisation to a bank supervises the entire banking group including any branches operating abroad. n In the three Baltic countries, the market share of the 3 largest foreign-owned banks (mostly subsidiaries but also branches) is 75% in LIT, 55% in LAT, and 86% in EST; and foreign ownership in general is very high and close to 100% . In Finland, we are facing a similar situation with two major foreign owned banks controlling over 50% of the loan and deposit markets. banks. b 2 (3) 1 February 2008 As a consequence of the integration and internationalisation of financial markets, the responsibilities and competences of authorities in different countries are no longer entirely aligned. This is the case particularly for systemically significant branches of cross-border banks. In terms of risks to the entire banking group and to the host financial sector, it is of secondary importance whether the bank has organised its operations through subsidiaries or branches, but in terms of legal responsibilities, there is a stark difference in the EU framework. This distinction should be milder to allow more cost-effective coordination in case of subsidiaries (reduce the overlap of many national supervisions) and to allow adequate host country involvement in case of significant branches. Bank of Finland has proposed four enhancements to the current EU financial stability framework which would go to this direction. At the moment, these issues are being evaluated as changes to the Capital Requirements Directive to be concluded on this year. This action by the Commission is very welcome, in particular as it considers establishing a legal role for supervisory colleges and clarifying the role of host supervisors of systemic branches. These enhancements are: A mandatory requirement for the exchange of information between the home and host country supervisors in case of systemically important branches. o This seems to be one of the objectives of the current Directive reform. The information exchange framework set out in MoUs should be strengthened by legal, compelling rules for information exchange both in normal and crisis times. A mandatory requirement for the delegation of ongoing supervisory tasks to host supervisors of systemically important branches. o o There does not seem to be appetite at the moment to make delegation nothing but voluntary. Supervisors seem to agree that specific supervisory duties should be carried out by those that are best placed for conducting them. But there are seem to be legal obstacles at the national level and supervisors are vary of delegating duties on which they can be held liable at a later stage should problems emerge. Hence, strong obligations seem to be needed in EU legislation in order to safeguard the interests of host countries and increase the cost- efficiency of supervision (and optimise the use of expertise of home and host authorities). Also the delegation of responsibilities should be considered, not only the delegation of tasks. A mandatory requirement for the establishment of supervisory colleges and involvement of host country authorities in case of systemically important branches. o The composition of the college should not be the unilateral decision of home supervisors, but also involve the host supervisors in a joint decision. (When there is no agreement, mediation mechanism at the Level 3 Committee could be used). o The legally-defined duties of the college should involve ongoing supervision as well as crisis management. Some recent suggestions have dealt with improving only crisis management procedures. However, it will be impossible to manage crises effectively if cooperation is activated only when a crisis is already in hand. The EU legislation is also most underdeveloped where ongoing cooperation between supervisors is concerned. 3 (3) 1 February 2008 Involvement of host country authorities in crisis management and resolution of cross-border banks with systemically important branches. o This should involve an obligation that home supervisor consult the college (including host branch supervisors) on major supervisory decisions concerning the banking group. These four enhancements in the EU financial stability framework would be necessary to facilitate effective ongoing supervision. They would improve the possibilities of maintaining stability at the national level and lead to more coordinated and efficient crisis management solutions at the EU level. They could also remove obstacles to further integration and branching by cross-border banks, by alleviating the concerns of predominantly host countries. To conclude, I would like to emphasise that these issues are relevant for the whole EU, not just for the Baltic states or in the CEEC. The integration process continues and an increasing number of large and complex banking groups will be created. Therefore, we must have a well-functioning EU level framework in place to manage potential problem / crisis situations. As we learned from the Northern Rock case in the UK, a crisis situation can take place very suddenly even in an environment with well-developed institutions.
