In the early 2000s, it was widely expected that the euro area would be capable of reasonably rapid economic growth even if growth in the US and Japanese economies slowed down. After all, the euro area, as the core area of Europe, which used to consist of small open economies, is now as autonomous in terms of foreign trade as the United States and Japan ? a large closed economy. Now we know that the n?in did not work, but at least somewhere the m??rin is ep?selv??, mist?? in september. The debate has offered a number of different explanations, including at least the following: The foundations of Europe were not as good as they thought they were. The improvement in the public finances of the large countries during the boom was only due to cyclical automation, which was not immediately understood. The tax cuts intensified the economic upturn and, through this, improved the budgetary situation on a temporary basis. However, over a longer period of time, the deficit in public finances increased as countries failed to implement the corresponding expenditure cuts. In a downturn, the public finances of the large countries fell within three per cent of total production and even exceeded the limit. There was therefore no room for stimulus for fiscal policy. Of course, there are exceptions ? e.g. Finland, where the strict fiscal policy of the 1990s gave room for manoeuvre for fiscal policy. The growth potential of the EU countries is weak. The previous "bottom growth" of output growth, which has come from the growth of the v?est?n ik?n?n, has completely ceased to exist; The EU countries are more like Japan than The United States, where power continues to grow at an annual rate of about one percent. Longterm weak growth has led to a long-term reluctance on the part of companies to invest in the euro area. Eu countries' labour markets operate inefficiently. Growth in the euro area will reach a ceiling right from the start of growth and the cost of labour will start to rise, despite the high employment rates. The euro area has fallen into a crisis of confidence. Consumer confidence is at its lowest level in six years. And the confidence of the industry is also at a low level. There is talk of a crisis of confidence, which would only improve with the US confidence indicators! However, Europeans continue to be consumers and investors themselves as citizens of small or medium-sized open economies whose economies get sick as soon as the United States sneezes! How else would the correlation be explained? Of course, the lack of confidence in the large Member States may be due to ? and probably is also due to political factors. For example, in Germany, which is the EU's largest economy, its key driver, there is no political vision on the political front that would strengthen consumer confidence. The helplessness of the P??t?jis reflects the wishes of the ??nest?js, but on the other hand, it clearly reflects the general pessimism of consumers. Summing up: Hopes that the EU will be the engine of global economic growth in a recession. China and, more generally, Asian countries other than Japan have seen their growth at an annual rate of ? China's GDP is growing at an annual rate of 8% according to official statistics - but in general, global economic growth is not really re-emerging until the rise of the US economy. According to the general forecast of the Bank of Finland and the Bank of Finland, global economic growth will be modest in the past, but if confidence is restored, economic growth will recover on a broad front towards the end of 2003. This will boost Finnish exports and investment will also recover in 2004. It should be noted that throughout the economic downturn in Finland, private consumption and investment in housing have been prolonged, largely due to the fact that, under EMU conditions, households have been able to rely on the fact that interest rates have not been able to jump to excesses. In fact, since the days of the gold standard, Finland has not enjoyed ever-low interest rates, which has not been able to fail to influence economic developments during the global economic downturn. The fact that we are part of a European currency area means that Finland's exceptionally high dependence on the telecommunications sector, which has suffered setbacks, was not passed on through exchange rate fluctuations or interest rate reactions as a stabilisation of the rest of the economy. Indeed, in the current downturn, macroeconomic policy has historically been exceptionally strong in support of demand. In addition to low interest rates, demand has also been supported by fiscal policy, where automatic stabilisers have been allowed to operate freely in the face of aggregate demand weakening ? thanks to the steady state achieved in Finland's public finances. *** Integration of financial markets ? part of the Lisbon strategy The slow pace of growth in the EU and the euro area has long been recognised as a structural problem. In Lisbon in 2000, EU leaders agreed on an ambitious strategy, which was encapsulated in the demand that, over the course of a decade, Europe should become the most competitive and dynamic knowledge-based economy in the world, capable of sustainable economic growth, creating new and better jobs and increasing social cohesion. The strategy pays particular attention to the financial markets. This is due to the fact that, in a market economy, it is the long-term functioning of the financial markets that determines the level and orientation of new investment and thus the long-term growth of productivity. The strategy states that efficient and efficient financial markets will support growth by improving the allocation of ??oms and lowering the cost of transactions. It therefore plays a key role in the development of new ideas and in the development of new ideas and in the promotion of enterprise in Europe. In particular, the development of the risk finance market is a prerequisite for innovative SMEs, and thus also for the emergence of new jobs. That is why the strategy places the emphasis on the implementation of a truly integrated siphon market in the financial services sector. There is a great deal to be gained from those companies, which are in principle large enough to attract the interest of foreign investors, but still so small that the marketing of shares abroad has been too expensive until the scale of their activities. An EU group of experts chaired by Pehr Gyllenhammar has estimated that by simply improving the functioning of financial markets, economic growth in the EU countries could be accelerated by half a per cent per annum, and by some extent more than that. Similar effects have also been obtained in other studies, e.g. Giannetti-Guiso-Jappelli-Padula-Pagano (2002) have an additional effect on growth depending on the country (e.g. for Finland) of up to about one percent per year. There is certainly a great deal of room for interpretation and uncertainties in relation to such estimates, but the impact on growth of this kind would, of course, be of great importance for europe's rigour, competitiveness and also for the budgetary finances of European countries. On the other hand, the stability of the financial markets, if badly k?y, could cause not only economic damage, but also setbacks and ep? stability in the political development of Europe. Financial and banking crises tend to destroy not only the economic p??oma and jobs, but also the political and social p??oma, and therefore the stable functioning of the market is a broad social issue. A longer and more integrated European financial market, which facilitates the decomposition and management of risks, is also desirable. The Lisbon strategy has also already produced significant results. In addition to short-term bank deposits, the common financial markets, or at least common financial markets, have also been filled with government bonds, the spreads of which have narrowed to zero interest rates. With regard to the legal procedure, a significant step forward has been the adoption of the procedure recommended by the Lamfalussy Committee. Thanks to the new procedure, the securities market legislation, including the necessary harmonisation, can be implemented much more quickly than in the past and, at the same time, the quality of the securities market can be improved. What, then, are the most important development needs of the market? Despite the conditions for improvement referred to above, the main problem with the european financial markets is considered to be the fragmentation that still afflicts them. The situation on the financial services market is still more favourable than on the stock market, and national borders have a major impact on trade in financial services, even within the euro area. The European system of payments is also very fragmented as far as payments are concerned. Although a different standardisation process has been carried out for a long time, paying from one EU country to another is much more difficult, slower and more expensive than paying in one country, especially for households and small businesses. The EU has intervened in this matter by means of a directive on the pricing of payment services, which restricts the right of banks to charge higher fees for cross-border credit transfers than for domestic payments. This alone will not eliminate the root cause of the problems, i.e. the poor compatibility of national payment systems. There are therefore reasons why the fragmentation of the payment system is detrimental to the real common market, not only in financial services, but also in many other products. The payment system is the infrastructure for the functioning of all markets. Another problem with the financial markets in the euro area, along with their fragmentation, is the lack of efficiency. As well as the cost structure of banks and securities securities, the cost structure in many European countries is quite heavy. There is a fairly broad consensus that there is potential for considerable costs in the production of financial services. In part, this inefficiency is linked to market fragmentation, which has restricted competition and made an expensive cost structure possible. The question of costs is also a question of stability, because only a profitable and cost-effective banking sector can generate sufficient income financing and ensure that its solvency is sufficient for a long period of time. The third problem facing European financial markets is that, as markets develop and integrate, financial supervision threatens to develop and develop afterwards. This is accentuated in a context of slow economic growth, when risks in the financial markets increase, as European financial supervision is based on the so-called 'green light'. the principle of the home country, so that a greater proportion of the international activities of the financial industry are controlled by an authority in a country other than the one in which the service is sold. In more cases, deposit insurance may also be the responsibility of a country other than the one in which the risks that led to the problems were taken or where the eligible depositors reside. At the same time, the decline of banking-securities and insurance activities poses new challenges for supervisory organisations. The multiplicity of authorities places great demands on their flow of information and operational cooperation. These requirements will increase as the integration of financial markets in Europe progresses in line with the objectives. Progress in the region is probably justifiable to be expected as to why the proposal for a so-called 'green card' will be made. The application of the Lamfalussy principle to the management and supervision of the entire financial market sector in the EU is realised. *** Ladies and gentlemen, Whereas the monetary system established on the basis of the Maastricht Treaty, which includes the independence of the central bank, the designation of price stability as an objective of monetary policy, and the support of the budgetary policies of the Member States, has proved its worth ? the latter not as well as had been thought for all countries (the world is not a reality!), but nevertheless the functioning of monetary union has shown that the European Union is capable of creating institutions; who are capable of pursuing a credible and long-term policy. Why is it that I do not understand how to scrap the Stability and Growth Pact, for example? It can already be said that one of the countries in the euro area, the EU, is stronger economically in a globalising economy with high certainty. Monetary union has already proved to be an important stabiliser of economic development in the euro area. Hy?tyjin? has been particularly the countries whose monetary policy before monetary union lacked credibility. Even in Finland, we have not been able to enjoy such a balanced money market for decades as in recent years. It can also be estimated that the consequences of events such as those of 11.9.2001 on the European and world financial markets would have been rather turbulent under the conditions of separate currencies, when now the situation on the financial markets was constantly under control. Of course, the same observation is also made in the current political situation: it is worth pointing out that the situation of the war in Iraq is different in terms of financial conditions in Europe from the state of the war in Kuwait with its EMS crises. In economic and political conditions, it is necessary to strengthen those factors that promote trust and vision. For this reason, it is necessary to consciously implement the agreed strategies and programmes.

Tm johtuu siit, ett markkinataloudessa juuri rahoitusmarkkinoiden toiminta pitklti ratkaisee uusien investointien mrn ja suuntautumisen ja siten mys tuottavuuden pitkn aikavlin kasvun. Erityisen paljon voitettavaa on niill yhtiill, jotka ovat periaatteessa kyllin suuria herttkseen ulkomaisten sijoittajien kiinnostusta, mutta kuitenkin sen verran pieni, ett osakkeiden markkinointi ulkomaille on thn asti ollut niiden toiminnan laajuuteen nhden liian kallista. Suomelle) jopa noin prosenttiyksikn per vuosi. Tllaisiin arvioihin liittyvt tulkinnanvaraisuudet ja epvarmuudet ovat varmasti suuria, mutta tt luokkaa olevalla kasvuvaikutuksella olisi tietenkin erittin suuri mynteinen merkitys Euroopan tyllisyyden, kilpailukyvyn ja mys Euroopan valtioiden budjettitalouden kannalta. Toisaalta rahoitusmarkkinoiden hirit ja epvakaus, jos huonosti ky, voisivat aiheuttaa paitsi taloudellista vahinkoa, mys takaiskuja ja epvakautta Euroopan poliittisessa kehityksess. Rahoitus-ja pankkikriiseiss tapaa tuhoutua paitsi taloudellista pomaa ja typaikkoja, mys poliittista ja sosiaalista pomaa, ja siksi markkinoiden vakaa toiminta on laaja yhteiskunnallinen kysymys. Tltkin osin syvemmt ja integroituneemmat eurooppalaiset rahoitusmarkkinat, jotka helpottavat riskien hajoittamista ja hallintaa ovat tavoiteltavia. Tm Lissabonin strategia on mys jo tuottanut merkittvi tuloksia. Yhteisiin tai ainakin lhes yhteisiin rahoitusmarkkinoihin on psty lyhyiden pankkien vlisten talletusten lisksi mys valtioiden joukkovelkakirjoissa, joiden korkoerot ovat kaventuneet lhes olemattomiksi. Mitk sitten ovat markkinoiden trkeimmt kehittmistarpeet? Edell viitatuista parannusedellytyksist huolimatta Euroopan rahoitusmarkkinoiden ehk suurimpana ongelmana on pidettv niit edelleenkin vaivaavaa pirstoutuneisuutta. Rahoituspalvelujen vhittismarkkinoilla tilanne on viel eptyydyttvmpi kuin osakemarkkinoilla ja kansalliset rajat vaikuttavat kytnnss erittin paljon rahoituspalvelujen vhittiskauppaan jopa euroalueen sisll. Mys Euroopan maksujrjestelm on vhittismaksujen osalta erittin pirstaleinen. Vaikka erilaista standardointityt on tehty jo pitkn, kytnnss maksaminen EU-maasta toiseen on paljon hankalampaa, hitaampaa ja kalliimpaa kuin maksaminen yhden maan sisll, varsinkin kotitalouksien ja pienyritysten maksuissa. Thn asiaan EU on skettin puuttunut maksupalvelujen hinnoittelua koskevalla direktiivill, joka rajoittaa pankkien oikeutta peri rajat ylittvist tilisiirroista korkeampia palkkioita kuin kotimaisista maksuista. Tm ei yksin poista ongelmien perussyyt eli kansallisten maksujrjestelmien heikkoa yhteensopivuutta. Siksi on syyt pelt, ett maksujrjestelmn pirstoutuneisuus haittaa psemist todellisiin yhtenismarkkinoihin ei vain rahoituspalvelujen, vaan monien muidenkin tuotteiden markkinoilla. Maksujrjestelmthn ovat kaikkien markkinoiden toiminnan kannalta vlttmtn infrastruktuuri. Toinen euroalueen rahoitusmarkkinoiden ongelma, niiden pirstoutuneisuuden ohella siis, on puutteellinen tehokkuus. Sek pankkien ett arvopaperiprssien kustannusrakenne on monissa Euroopan maissa varsin raskas. Melko laajasti ollaan yht mielt siit, ett rahoituspalvelujen tuotannossa on mahdollisuuksia huomattaviin kustannussstihin. Osittain tm tehottomuus liittyy markkinoiden pirstoutuneisuuteen, joka on rajoittanut kilpailua ja tehnyt kalliin kustannusrakenteen mahdolliseksi. Kustannuskysymys on mys vakauskysymys, koska vain kannattava ja kustannustehokas pankkisektori voi generoida riittvsti tulorahoitusta ja nin huolehtia vakavaraisuutensa riittvyydest pitkll aikavlill. Kolmas Euroopan rahoitusmarkkinoiden ongelma on, ett kun markkinat kehittyvt ja yhdentyvt, rahoitusvalvonta uhkaa jd tss kehityksess jlkeen. Tm korostuu hitaan talouskasvun oloissa, jolloin riskit rahoitusmarkkinoilla kasvavat, Euroopan rahoitusvalvontahan perustuu ns. kotivaltioperiaatteeseen, joten rahoitustoimialan kansainvlistyess yh suurempaa osaa toiminnasta valvoo jonkin muun maan viranomainen kuin sen, jossa palvelu myydn. Mys talletusvakuutus saattaa yh useammassa tapauksessa olla jonkin muun maan vastuulla kuin sen, jossa ongelmiin johtaneet riskit on otettu tai jossa korvauksiin oikeutetut tallettajat asuvat. Samalla pankki-arvopaperi-ja vakuutustoiminnan lhentyminen aiheuttaa uusia haasteita valvontaorganisaatioille. Viranomaisten monilukuisuus asettaa suuria vaatimuksia niiden vliselle tiedonkululle ja operatiiviselle yhteistylle. Nm vaatimukset kasvavat sit mukaa kun rahoitusmarkkinoiden yhdentyminen Euroopassa tavoitteiden mukaisesti etenee. Edistyst tll alueella lienee perusteltua odottaa, mikli ehdotus ns. Lamfalussy.periaatteen soveltamisesta koko EU n rahoitusmarkkinasektorin stelyyn ja valvontaan toteutuu. *** Arvoisat kuulijat, Maastrichtin sopimuksen pohjalle luotu rahapoliittinen jrjestelm, johon kuuluu keskuspankin itsenisyys, hintavakauden mrittely rahapolitiikan tavoitteeksi, ja jsenmaiden budjettipolitiikan kestvyytt tukevat snnt, on osoittanut toimivuutensa  viimeksi mainitut eivt ehk kaikkien maiden osalta niin hyvin kuin oli ajateltu (maailma ei ole tydellinen!), mutta kuitenkin ptyisin vittmn ett rahaliiton toiminta on osoittanut, ett Euroopan unioni kykenee luomaan instituutioita, jotka pystyvt harjoittamaan uskottavaa ja pitkjnteist politiikkaa. Mikn taho ei ymmrtkseni ole heittmss esimerkiksi vakaus-ja kasvusopimusta romukoppaan. Voidaan mielestni jo nyt sanoa ett yhdess euroalueen maat, EU, on taloudellisesti vahvempi globaalistuvassa taloudessa epvarmuuksien ollessa suuria. Rahaliitto on jo nyt osoittautunut merkittvksi taloudellisen kehityksen vakauttajaksi euroalueella. Hytyjin ovat olleet varsinkin ne maat, joiden rahapolitiikka ennen rahaliittoa krsi heikosta uskottavuudesta. Suomessakaan ei ole vuosikymmeniin saatu nauttia niin tasapainoisista rahamarkkinoista kuin viime vuosina. Voi mys arvioida, ett 11.9.2001 kaltaisten tapahtumien seuraukset eurooppalaisilla ja koko maailman rahamarkkinoilla olisivat olleet erillisten valuuttojen oloissa varsin turbulentit, kun nyt tilanne rahamarkkinoilla oli koko ajan hallinnassa. Tm sama havainto ptee luonnollisesti mys nykyisess poliittisessa tilanteessa: on syyt korostaa, ett Irakin sodan tilanne on Euroopan rahoitusolojen osalta erilainen kuin Kuwaitin sodan jlkitila EMS-kriiseineen. Epvarmoissa taloudellisissa ja poliittisissa oloissa on trke vahvistaa niit tekijit jotka edistvt luottamusta ja visiota. text: Bank Manager Sinikka Salo's speech at the Oiva Ketonen seminar in Lappaj?rvell? . Speech . Thursday24 April 2003,12:00 AM Suomiglobalisaation valtavirrassa Ladies and gentlemen, first of all, my sincerest thanks for the invitation to the ceremony. It is a great honour and pleasure for me to attend an authoritative seminary in my childhood home next door. My topic eeFinland in the mainstream of globalisation Is fascinating and leads me to life-long questions about the challenges facing Finland and how we are able to cope with it. At the same time, my topic is also quite broad. I can't possibly hope that I'll be able to offer even the most exhaustive presentation. On the other hand, I hope that I will be able to give some impetus to think about the position of Finland and the Finns in the ongoing globalisation process. When I look at globalisation and Finland's coping strategies, I pay constant attention to the importance of knowledge and education. One of the most important advocates of information and education and, at the same time, the implementers of education policy in Finland has certainly been Oiva Ketonen. In relation to ?ss?, I hope that my presentation will pay homage to his ideas and will fit in well with the programme of the seminar named after him. I have broken down my presentation as follows. Let me first look at globalisation a little more generally ? above all, I mean what I mean. After that, I reflect on Finland's position in the mainstream of globalisation, in which case eu integration and the significance of Finland's eu membership should be examined. Finally, I will try to outline the main challenges of Finland's survival strategy, especially for rural areas. Globalization is the "world village" Markets are becoming more and more international. In addition to various industrial products and other hy?dys, the mobility of technology and power is increasing worldwide. Indeed, the opening up of various markets is the most important part of globalisation, and at least in a short period of time for businesses and the economy. However, globalisation is more about opening up markets. It means that the importance of geography as a political and cultural factor has diminished. The characterization of "world village" ? ?m? illustrates well that globalisation is not just an economic manifestation, but is driven by the general expansion of the people's circle. El?m? is basically globalized by two interdependent autumns of the m??r. First of all, the new technology has in many respects attributed to the importance of the ethnicity of countries and peoples in the middle of the world. New products are typically lighter than old products and are therefore easier to transport over long distances. Through this, new technology has effectively shrunk the market to ethos. The shrinkage of knowledge or information has been particularly evident in the production and transfer of knowledge or information. Telecommunications are the dynamic core of the new technology. Thanks to new technologies, influences and knowledge spread faster everywhere in streams and reach a larger proportion of the world's people. It's easier to find out from around the world the things we're interested in, whether commercial, entertaining, or cultural. Thanks to the interactive information provided by the Internet, the comparison eeworldly Village is more relevant than before. It is precisely the same technological advances that make us speak of a 'new economy' that are globalising the whole of people's circles. And since technological progress is irreversible - once invented, it is not easy to invent the development of globalisation can be expected to be "one-way". Along with technology, another reason for globalization is the political changes that have occurred in recent years. Since the fall of communism and many right-wing dictatorships, governments today do not restrict people's contacts with the people in the world much more than in the past. The political changes that have led to the expansion of democracy and civil liberties have not been technologically independent. Rather, new technologies and the consequent reduction in barriers to the flow of information have played an essential role in the spread of democracy in Central and Eastern Europe as elsewhere. The development of technology has not led to a society controlled by the 'big brother' as George Orwell once did, but rather to the centralised control of access and information. The globalisation of the economy is more or more a consequence of the emergence of the world cold and the spread of the associated democratic and free model of society, and it is not really indistinguishable from the general cultural change that exists. The market is formed by how modern people el?v?t: consume, work, s???v?v?t and move, whatever entertainment or culture they follow, and so on. I think it is more right to think that the transformation of people into world-colders will globalise their economic relations at the same time as the globalisation of economic relations and that the globalisation of economic relations will globalise all other relations. In spite of this, economic relations have been in some respects in the context of globalisation. In addition to technological progress and political changes, the importance of geographical location has therefore diminished and continues to do so. At the same time, the hy?ty given by the large size of land is also diminished as more countries open up their trade and economies. Against the backdrop of globalisation in Finland, globalisation is promisingly good times. After all, we have traditionally become accustomed to the international trade, from which we have unquestionably become wealthy. Finland is a good example of globalisation at an early stage of the economy. Without the export of wood and paper products, and then many other industrial products, we would not have been able to build the welfare society in which we now live. Until then, our international trade has been largely material, export and import of goods. Now the trade should expand beyond more goods to services. At the same time, we should learn about culture in internationalisation. More than that, our success depends on people's know-how and experience and our material resources. On the challenges of EU integration Regional integration is an essential part of the globalisation process. Although the European Union may well have been rooted in the post-war effort to ensure that peace is maintained in Europe, the EU has evolved more clearly over time as a response to the challenges of globalisation for European countries. Throughout its history, EU integration has ? despite occasional difficulties ? and deepened and expanded, and the development continues to be strong. The EU's istern markets and the monetary and economic policy system created on the basis of the Maastricht Treaty, which includes the central bank's self-determination, the designation of price stability as an objective of monetary policy and the supportive aspects of the member states' budgetary policies, have proved their worth. They show that the European Union is capable of creating institutions with credible and long-term policies. The EU's competition and notable achievements are not always the same. In the press debate, attention is easily drawn to current points of contention, which, from the point of view of the whole, are often Cherys' ep?olee. It is fair to say that, in a globalising and rapidly developing world economy, the euro area and other EU countries are now significantly stronger economically than they were before economic and monetary union. Economic and monetary union has proved to be an important stabiliser of economic development in the euro area. In particular, the countries in the euro area whose monetary policy before monetary union was weak in terms of credibility have been particularly hy?tyjin?. Even in Finland, we have not been able to enjoy such a balanced money market for decades as in recent years. It is also possible to judge that the consequences of events such as those of 11.9.2001 or the war in Iraq on the European and world financial markets would have been rather turbulent under the conditions of separate currencies. Now the situation on the money markets has remained well under control all the time. Furthermore, enlargement ? except that it is politically and morally v?lt?m??n - will also economically strengthen the EU over time by bringing dynamism and new potential, new markets. Of course, the EU faces major challenges. The slow pace of growth in the EU, and especially in the euro area, has long been recognised as a structural problem. In Lisbon in 2000, EU leaders agreed on a strategy, which was encapsulated in the demand that, over the course of a decade, Europe should become the most competitive and dynamic knowledge-based economy in the world, capable of maximising economic growth, creating new and better jobs and increasing social cohesion. The Lisbon Strategy was designed to enable the EU to meet the challenges of global competition and the development of information technology. There is a general consensus that the European structures, which were good when mechanical engineering production prevailed, are not competitive in the production structure of information technology. The Lisbon Strategy, however, is not only about economics and technology, but also about highlighting the social dimension of the structural change sought. While the strategy aims at a dynamic, knowledge- and technology-based economy, the desired structural change is to be integrated into a European model of society with an emphasis on social cohesion. There is a desire for a single information society and a welfare society. At the heart of the strategy, as well as economic dynamism and social cohesion, is the improvement of employment and the integration of cohesion. In the Lisbon strategy, the development of the pan-European market, i.e. the completion of the single market, plays a leading role. Particular attention has been paid to financial markets in the strategy. This is due, among other things, to the fact that, in a market economy, it is the long-term functioning of the financial markets that determines the long-term growth of new investment and, through this, to a large extent, the long-term growth of productivity. The strategy states that efficient and efficient financial markets will support growth by improving the allocation of ??oms and lowering the cost of transactions. It therefore plays a key role in the development of new ideas and in the development of new ideas and in the promotion of enterprise in Europe. In particular, the development of the risk finance market is a prerequisite for innovative SMEs and thus also for the creation of new jobs. That is why the strategy places the emphasis on the implementation of a truly integrated siphon market in the financial services sector. There is a great deal to be gained from those companies, which are in principle large enough to attract the interest of foreign investors, but still so small that the marketing of shares abroad has been too expensive until the scale of their activities. An EU group of experts chaired by Pehr Gyllenhammar has estimated that by simply improving the functioning of financial markets, economic growth in the EU countries could be accelerated by half a per cent per annum, and by some extent more than that. Similar effects have also been obtained in recent estimates by academic researchers. There is certainly a great deal of room for interpretation and uncertainties in relation to such estimates, but the impact on growth of this kind would, of course, be of great importance for europe's rigour, competitiveness and also for the budgetary finances of European countries. In order to create a common financial market, conscious programmes are needed so that national borders do not imply additional costs for the financing and payment of households and businesses. Barriers to a single financial market are largely based on conflicts of interest between the various financial market participants. We are still halfway there, but efforts to ensure that by 2005 we could already talk about a pan-European financial market. In economic and political conditions, it is necessary to strengthen those factors that promote trust and vision. In fact, there is no other way than to implement commonly agreed strategies and programmes ? hence the Lisbon strategy ? and then consciously forward the Lisbon strategy. Europe's difficulties have not been due to the fact that there is not really a long-term effort to accelerate economic growth. The objectives are set out quite clearly in various quarters, most comprehensively in the Lisbon Strategy. The difficulty has been the ability to implement reforms to achieve the objectives. Mit tulevaisuudessa tarvitaan? Suomi on viime vuosina tullut varsin tunnetuksi "omasta tiestn" etenkin tietotekniikan alueella, mutta mys muilla elmnalueilla mallimme on saanut huomiota. Haasteena monikulttuurisen dialogin oppiminen, globalisaation ymmrtminen Keskeist Suomen selviytymisstrategiassa on mys osata toimia "maailmankylss". Suomalaisten on oltava hyvi ei vain taloudessa ja teknologiassa ja sen soveltamisessa, vaan mys kulttuurisessa, sosiaalisessa ja poliittisessa toiminnassa ja kanssakymisess. Suomi on ollut homogeeninen ja verrattain eriytynyt maa nihin aikoihin asti. Uudessa globaalissa verkottuneessa taloudessa eletn monietnisess ympristss, jossa on kyettv kulttuurien vliseen dialogiin. Suomalaisten on kehitettv kulttuurisia valmiuksia  opittava elmn ja toimimaan monikulttuurisessa ympristss  opittava mys vastaanottamaan siirtolaisia muualta. Meille suomalaisille tm on suuri asenteellinen muutos. Meidn on opittava elmn "maailmankylss". Erityisen keskeinen on koulutus. Pelkk vlineellinen koulutus ei riit, vaan mukaan on saatava voimakas sivistyksellinen, humanistinen elementti. Pohjolasta ja Euroopasta ksin suomalaisten on kyettv selviytymn hyvin erilaisissa kulttuureissa. On paitsi osattava kyd kauppaa mys annettava oma panos globaalien ongelmien ratkaisemisessa. Mielenkiintoinen piirre globalisaatiosta kydyss keskustelussa on ollut se, ett kehitysmaihin periaatteessa hyvin mynteisesti suhtautuvat ja varsin kansainvlisesti ajattelevat nuoret ovat joukolla asettuneet vastustamaan yritystoiminnan maapalloistumista ja kansainvlisen kaupan esteiden poistamista. Tt ajattelua minun on ollut hyvin vaikea ymmrt. Selvitykset osoittavat varsin yksiksitteisesti, ett kyhyydest ovat psseet eroon ne maat, jotka ovat avautuneet kansainvliselle kaupalle ja sijoituksille. Kansainvliselt kaupalta ja investoinneilta sulkeutuneiden maiden taloudellinen kohtalo on ollut ankea. Kyhien maiden nkkulmasta tulee olla huolestunut ulkomaankaupan jljell olevien esteiden silymisest, ei niiden poistamisesta. Vhiten kehittyneiden talouksien kasvun nopeutumisen este ei suinkaan ole teollisuusmaiden tuonnin tunkeutuminen niden maiden markkinoille vaan pikemminkin kehittyneiden maiden yllpitmt esteet vhn kehittyneiden maiden tuotteiden viennille. Erityisesti haitallisia tst nkkulmasta ovat maataloustuotteiden kaupan esteet. Vapaakaupan vastustaminen saattaa olla lyhytnkisesti kannattavaa niille ahtaita kansallisia ja ryhmetuja puolustaville, jotka tuontikiintiiden tai tullimuurien ansiosta hytyvt kaupan esteist. Kaupan vapauttaminen ei kuitenkaan ole nollasummapeli. Vhnkin pitemmll aikavlill kaupan vapauttamisesta hytyvt kaikki. Tst onkin selke siirty esitykseni loppuosaan, jossa lupasin ksitell Suomen haasteita erityisesti maaseudun kannalta. Maaseudun haasteet Taloudellisen integraation myt valtiot joutuvat tinkimn kansallisesta omavaraisuudestaan. Tm on tavallaan se hinta, jonka olemme joutuneet ja joudumme maksamaan korkeasta elintasosta. Moni aikanaan trkekin teollisuudenala on kansainvlisen tynjaon kehityksen myt kutistunut Suomessa lhes olemattomiin. Nin tulee ollakin. Muuten emme olisi kyenneet keskittymn korkean teknologian tuotteisiin, joihin nykyinen elintasomme kokonaan nojaa. Teollisuustuotteiden osalta maailmantalous on jo pitklle integroitunut. Mys monien palvelusten osalta maailman keskeiset markkinat ovat pitklle toisistaan riippuvia. Joillakin aloilla globalisaatio on edennyt hitaammin joko alan itsens ominaisuuksien tai kansainvliselle kaupalle asetettujen esteiden takia. Yksi tllaisista aloista on maatalous, jossa markkinoiden itsenisyytt on puolustettu vientituilla ja tuotteiden tuonnille asetetuilla rajoituksilla. Maaseudun kannalta kipe kysymys on, olemmeko seuraavaksi valmiita astumaan merkittvn askeleen globaalin talouden suuntaan maataloustuotteiden osalta. Asiasta keskustellaan parhaillaan monenkeskisiss neuvotteluissa ns. Dohan kierroksella maailman kauppajrjestss WTO:ssa. EU:n maatalouspolitiikka on yhteist. EU:n yhteinen maatalouspolitiikka lienee maailmalaajuisesti suurin yksittinen este maataloustuotteiden kaupan vapauttamiselle. Muistettakoon, ett EU:ssa maataloustukeen kytetty rahamr suunnilleen vastaa koko Saharan etelpuolisen Afrikan yhteenlaskettua bruttokansantuotetta. (Nit taustoja ajatellen on outoa, ett WTO:n toimintaa vastaan ovat viime vuosina hyknneet juuri ne ihmisryhmt, jotka kokevat olevansa kehitysmaiden asialla!) Paineet yhteisen maatalouspolitiikan uudistamiseksi kasvavat jatkuvasti monenkeskisiss kauppaneuvotteluissa. Jos suuntaus kohti vapaakauppaa jatkuu nykyiselln  mik olisi toivottavaa -EU tuskin voi jatkaa kovin pitkn nykyisen kaltaista, voimakkaaseen tuontisuojaan perustuvaa maatalouspolitiikkaansa. Paineet yhteisen maatalouspolitiikan uudistamiseksi kasvavat mys siksi, ett EU:n nykyisill jsenmailla on tuskin edellytyksi tai halukkuutta pit yll nykyist tukitasoa mys laajentuneessa EU:ssa. Suomen maaseudulle sopeutuminen EU:n maatalouspolitiikan muutoksiin ja mahdolliseen maataloustuotteiden maailmanlaajuiseen vapaakaupan avautumiseen on suuri haaste. Ehk tss yhteydess voidaan ottaa jotain oppia rahoitusmarkkinoiden vapauttamisen yhteydess meill ja muualla saaduista kokemuksista. (Nykyisin maatalouden kokonaistaloudellinen merkitys on tosin rahoitusmarkkinoihin verrattuna vhinen, joten maataloussektorin suuretkaan muutokset eivt vaikuta kokonaistaloudelliseen kehitykseen samalla tavalla kuin rahoitusmarkkinoiden muutokset. Mutta toki ne ovat keskeisesti vaikuttamassa maaseudulla.) Yksi opetus rahoitusmarkkinoiden vapauttamisessa nytt olleen se, ett uudistukset kannattaa toteuttaa vhitellen ja pmrn suhteen avoimesti. Tllin yksittiset toimijat voivat sopeutua parhaalla mahdollisella tavalla vistmttmiin muutoksiin. Aina ei kuitenkaan osattu nin menetell, vaan monissa maissa rahoitusmarkkinoiden uudistuksiin mentiin koko lailla ajopuun tavalla. Tllin tulokset olivat usein huonoja. Suomen maatalous on kynyt lpi suuren ja raskaan rakennemuutoksen viime vuosien ja vuosikymmenien aikana. Vaikka muutokset ovat olleet suuria, luulen, ett edess saattaa olla viel aikaisempaakin merkittvmpi rakennemuutos, nimittin sopeutuminen maataloustuotteiden maailmanlaajuiseen vapaakauppaan. Uskon, ett maaseudulla on hyvt valmiudet selvit tst murroksesta ja knt muutos positiiviseksi. Globalisaation valtavirta, Suomen jsenyys raha-ja talousliitossa ja sen tuoma vakaus tuovat mys maaseudulle uusia mahdollisuuksia, jotka maaseudun yrittjien ja asukkaiden on luonnollisesti itse lydettv. Title: Speech at a seminar of the Council of the Association of Finnish Local and Regional Authorities
text: Bank Manager Sinikka Salo's speech at the seminar of the Council of the Association of Finnish Local and Regional Authorities . Speech . Tuesday 3June 2003,12:00AM Reform of the welfare state and the central position of the public sector ensuring Ladies and gentlemen, First of all, I would like to express my sincerest thanks for the invitation to your 10th anniversary seminar. It is a great honour for me to come and speak at an event on the reform of the welfare state, which for me is a matter for me as a representative of the Central Bank and as a citizen. The central bank's close interest in the welfare state and in the management of public finances stems from the dependence of monetary and other economic policies. Sound public finances are a key condition for the success of monetary policy. If public finances run into financial difficulties, the financial system and the functioning of the monetary system as a whole are jeopardised. As a citizen, I am naturally interested in d like other Finns d what kind of taxation is needed to finance their services, and how you can manage, for example, services that make it possible to reconcile family and work and thus increase the participation rate so that the growing elske expenses can be handled. The successes of Finnish society over the decades are measured for a very long time, by how the public sector copes with its challenges, i.e. how much the principles of the Nordic welfare model, which enjoys great support, and reasonable taxation that encourages people to work. *** Both in Finland and in other European countries, citizens are rightly concerned about how the quality and availability of welfare services can be ensured in the future. In the Ksydysss debate, the question of securing welfare services is often referred to as a purely political issue of income distribution. It is forgotten that public welfare services can only be stable if public finances are sound. If you try to provide services by paying attention to their financing, you will have to pay attention to the poor outcome before the end of the day. The best example of a poor redistributive policy is probably Argentina. In its splendor, the country was among the richest in the world, now its vsestsn the vast majority elss in misery. The reason for the backward development has been the country's fundamentally failed economic policies. srkess's contribution to economic performance has been fuelled by oversized public welfare services, which interest groups managed to arm themselves with the political machinery. European countries have been reasonably successful in their economic policies up to the point of being. In many countries, however, there have been problems with the management of public finances in recent decades, which have led to a high level of public debt. In general, European countries have become indebted in such a way that government expenditure has been increased during a boom period, when public revenues have increased on a cyclical basis. In the downturn phase of the economic cycle, expenditure on tax revenues has not been reduced. The mere stimulus of the demand for fiscal policy did not lead to an acceleration in economic growth, as its practitioners thought at the time, but to an inflated public debt. After all, the calibrated and timed recovery policy of Vssr has slowed down rather than accelerated economic growth in Europe. In some countries, such as Belgium, Italy, Ireland and Greece in particular, the debt grew out of control in the 1970s and 1980s. Of the countries, only Ireland, thanks to economic policy guidelines and favourable external factors, has managed to escape the debt trap. In other countries, debt has hardly decreased and their indebtedness has remained at a fairly high level. Italy remains the most net indebted of the world's major industrialised countries, even though Japan is well on its way to becoming perssss. In the 1990s, heavily indebted European countries were saved from bankruptcy, probably thanks to the eu's economic and monetary union and the use of the euro alone. The pursuit of monetary union forced countries to adopt strict monetary and fiscal policies. The countries themselves would not have taken up economic policies for stability, but this was also perceived as a solution to the terms of the monetary union. A credible monetary policy and its low interest rates were also on offer. The EU's policy of indebtedness was successful, so that they all became members of monetary union. Also, expectations of low interest rates have come true, probably even above all expectations. Despite the low level of interest rates, a significant part of the public expenditure of heavily indebted countries still goes to interest on debts. If debt servicing expenditure is taken away from public expenditure, public finances are clearly overspending, generally around 5 or 6% of GDP. In reality, including debt servicing costs, public finances in the countries are under rather than oversized, and in some indebted countries there is already a threshold of up to three per cent. A huge amount of taxes is accrued from common funds, i.e. 5 or 6% of GDP, i.e. not welfare services, but interest on debts. This explains the low level of welfare services in these countries, better than political preferences or historical traditions. In order to secure future welfare services, the first and most important advice is to keep Finland's public debt under control. This means a constantly strict and prudent budgetary policy. Of course, public debt can also play a role in fiscal policy. Municipalities, and especially the state, may well accumulate debt for a year or two. But it is necessary to size borrowing prudently and to take out a loan only on a farmly basis. After that, when the debt grows above a certain point, it tends to grow at its own pace. In such a situation, or when the debt has already reached a high level, it is very difficult to keep public welfare services even at a satisfactory level. Although not all countries in the EU are heavily indebted, almost all of them are indebted. Even in Finland, where public finances are on a much more stable footing than in most other EU countries, the government debt-to-GDP ratio is around 44 per cent. Because of the indebtedness, another piece of advice in order to secure the financing of welfare services is to pursue a policy that interest rates on debts remain low. From the czech angle to the current stability, there are difficult real alternatives to the economic policy line. People need to be confident that the framework for economic activity will continue to be stable, public finances will remain stable and prices will remain stable. In addition, monetary and fiscal policy must form a supportive harmonious combination of interest rates at low interest rates. Within the framework of the EU's economic policy breakdown, this means that the ECB is keen to adhere to price stability in the euro area, while the Member States keep to the budgetary policies that put pressure on interest rates to rise, i.e. excessive debt. From the point of view of small countries, as for Finland, from the point of view of longterm interest rates, the large euro countries, i.e. Germany, France and Italy, do not issue huge mssris government bonds to finance public expenditure. Euro banknotes differ from euro coins in that they are both sides the same regardless of the issuer and therefore do not have national or national symbols. Technical progress will also continue in the future. In addition, Finnish enterprises d not small and medium-sized industrial enterprises - have been given a more stable financial framework for their activities. Although the euro has only been around for a long time, we have already had some examples of a strengthening of financial stability. During the recession that hit Finland during a period of separate monetary policy in the early 1990s, interest rates initially rose to high levels, and monetary difficulties in general strengthened the overall economic impact of the end of trade and other Hsirisides that came from the real economy. In terms of scale and severity, the demand in the technology sector in recent years can be compared well with the real economic hsiris that hit Finland in the early 1990s. In fact, interest rates have been lower in the recession than they were since the gold standard. Along with the Finnish national economy, finnish cultural life has also survived the recession with relatively little damage. All the prerequisites are now well in place. *** Good listeners! In the history of the Finnish people, money has played a major, and even exceptional, role as a symbol of national feeling and national culture. In relation to this, money is an important part of our national culture. As society changes, so does the money, the sense of nationality and the national culture. In recent years, Marka did not have the same national cultural work as in the 1800s. In addition, the MFI is required to change the pace of change in social conditions. Money-creating institutions, especially central banks, are the best means of supporting economic growth and prosperity by ensuring that monetary conditions remain stable. For us, being part of the euro area means more stability and certainty in terms of price stability and, in that way, better growth opportunities. In this way, the single currency and monetary policy also underpins the national culture that flourishes best in conditions of peace and prosperity.

Ainoastaan Saarinen jtti ehdotuksensa mraikaan menness, joten seteleiden piirtminen annettiin hnen tehtvkseen. Saarisen piirtm setelisarja laskettiin liikkeeseen vuosina 1910-1913. Saarinen toi kansallisromantiikan Suomen setelitaiteeseen. Sarjan kuva-aiheet perustuvat Suomen luontoon ja elinkeinoihin. Ajan poliittisia jnnitteiden takia valtiolliset symbolit ovat tss sarjassa pienikokoiset ja muihin kuvioihin nhden toisarvoisessa asemassa, Venjn kotka etusivulla ylreunassa ja leijona takasivulla alhaalla. Nm Vaasan Osake Pankin Setelit painettiin vaasalaisessa yksityispainossa kovassa kiireess ja sota-ajan vaikeissa oloissa. Vitetn, ett seteleiden painovri jouduttiin kiireen ja hankintavaikeuksien takia jatkamaan tavallisella rautakaupasta hankitulla maalilla. Yht kaikki lopputulos oli sopusointuinen ja tasalaatuinen. Sek tyylillisesti ett aiheiltaan vuoden 1922 setelit poikkeavat huomattavasti aikaisemmasta sarjasta. Pienemmiss seteleiss etusivulla kertautui viljanthk ja mnnynoksa symboliikka, suurimmissa seteleiss henkilhahmot olivat kansan asemasta eri aikakausien johtavia poliitikkoja, nimittin Paasikivi, Sthlberg ja Snellman. Taiteilija Eeva Oivio osallistui tyhn piirtmll muotokuvia. Muotokuvien kohteet, Anders Chydenius, Elias Lnnrot, Jean Sibelius, Paavo Nurmi ja Alvar Aalto edustavat lhinn kulttuurin eri aloja. Se ett kuva-aiheiksi tss viimeiseksi jneess markkasarjaksi valittiin kulttuurin edustajia antaa ehk jotain tukea sille aikaisemmin esittmlleni vitteelle, ett kulttuurin asema yhteiskunnassa vahvistuu taloudellisen kasvun myt. Eurosetelit poikkeavat eurokolikoista siin, ett niiden molemmat puolet ovat samat liikkeeseenlaskijasta riippumatta eik niiss siis ole kansallisia tai valtiollisia tunnuksia. Tm seteleiden ja metallirahojen ero saattaa tuntua kummalliselta, mutta sille voidaan antaa hyv selitys. EU-maiden talous-ja rahaliitossa rahapolitiikasta ptetn keskitetysti. Euroalueen yhdesskn maassa voi olla toisista euroalueen maista poikkeavaa kansallista rahapolitiikkaa. Kun Euroopan keskuspankki otti kyttn yhtenisen, ilman kansallisia tunnuksia olevan setelin, viesti oli se, ett kansallista rahapolitiikkaa ei ole eik voi olla. Finanssipolitiikka sit vastoin on edelleen kansallista ja kukin euroalueen valtio vastaa omasta taloudestaan. Sit paitsi tulot metallirahojen lymisest tuloutetaan valtiolle. Metallirahojen ominaisuuksista vastaava Ecofin-neuvosto ptyi siksi metallirahojen osalta toiseen, kansallisempaan ratkaisuun kuin Euroopan keskuspankki seteleiden osalta. Vaikka seteleiss ei ole kansallisia tunnuksia, niiss on Euroopan keskuspankin nimilyhenne kaikilla EU:n virallisilla kielill, siis mys suomeksi EKP ja ruotsiksi ECB. Seteleiden kielikysymyksess olemme euron kyttnoton palanneet hieman samantapaiseen tilanteeseen kuin Ruotsin vallan aikana. Vuosina 1644-1778 Ruotsissa kytettiin pienempien rahojen ohella kookkaita kuparilevyrahoja, plootuja. Nit oli vaikea ksitell, ja kuparin hinnan vaihtelut vaikuttivat niiden saatavuuteen. Nist syist Ruotsi otti vuonna 1661 ensimmisen Euroopan maana kyttn setelit; aikaisemmin paperirahaa oli laskettu liikkeeseen Kiinassa. Paperirahan kyttnottoon liittyen perustettiin hieman myhemmin Riksbankenin edeltj, Valtakunnan styjen pankki, maailman ensimminen keskuspankki. Ruotsin seteleiden tekstit olivat alun perin vain ruotsiksi, mutta vuonna 1748 niihin listtiin arvomerkint mys suomeksi. Syyn oli se, ett suomalaiset talonpojat vierastivat ruotsalaisia seteleit. Euroseteleiss ei siis ole kansallisia tunnuksia. Kuka tahansa voi kuitenkin tunnistaa setelist sen alun perin tilanneen keskuspankin setelin tunnusnumerosta. Suomen Pankin tilaamissa seteleiss tunnus alkaa kirjaimella L. Valtaosassa Suomessa liikkeeseen lasketuista ja suurimmassa osassa mys Suomessa kiertviss seteleiss tunnusnumero alkaa tll kirjaimella. Ajan oloon eri maissa kiertvien seteleiden jakauman on arvioitu tasoittuvan liikkeeseenlaskijasta riippumatta siten ett kussakin maassa kiert yht paljon muissa maissa laskettuja seteleit. Tllin suurin osa Suomessa kiertvist seteleist olisi laskettu liikkeeseen muissa euromaissa. Jo nyt vhintn neljnnes Suomessa kierrossa olevista suurista seteleist on Saksan Bundesbankin liikkeeseen laskemia. Niiden tunnusnumero alkaa X:ll. Setelikantojen sekoittuminen on yksi osoitus siit, ett euroalueen maat ovat pitklle integroituneet taloudellisesti. Kansallisten tunnusten puuttuessa ja eri maissa liikkeeseen laskettujen seteleiden sekoittuessa eurosetelit eivt voi ilment ja vahvistaa kansallistunnettamme samalla tavalla kuin monet aikaisemmat setelimme, eivt vhiten ensimmiset markkasetelimme 1860-luvulla. Suomalaiset taiteilijat voivat tietenkin osallistua ja ovat jo osallistuneetkin euroseteleiden suunnittelukilpailuihin. Odotettavissa on, ett he joskus tulevaisuudessa psevt suunnittelemaan liikkeeseen laskettavan eurosetelisarjan. Mutta setelit on tarkoitettu yleiseurooppalaiseen kyttn eik niihin siksi voi sisllytt suomalaiskansallisia piirteit. Kansallisilla seteleill on aikaisemmin ollut suuri merkitys kulttuurillemme. Nyt kansallisten seteleiden poistumista tuskin voi kuitenkaan pit suurena kulttuurimenetyksen. Raha on menettnyt asemansa kansallishengen ja suomalaisen kulttuurin nostattajana jo kauan aikaa sitten. Se on muuttunut arkipivisemmksi. Thn on vaikuttanut merkittvsti tekninen kehitys, jonka myt seteleiden ja kolikoiden merkitys maksuvlinein on vhentynyt selvsti kaikkialla. Erityisen selvsti vaihtorahan kytt on vhentynyt Suomessa. Pankkien kehittyneiden vhittismaksujrjestelmien ansiosta suurin osa maksuista hoidetaan meill nykyisin elektronisesti ja seteleiden ja kolikoiden kokonaismr kokonaistuotantoon suhteutettuna on alhaisempi kuin missn muussa EU.maassa. Tekninen kehitys jatkuu mys tulevaisuudessa. Vaikka tll hetkell emme viel tied, millaisia maksuvlineit tulevaisuudessa kytetn, aivan mahdotonta ei liene se, ett raha muuttuisi jossain vaiheessa kokonaan elektroniseksi. Seteleiden ja metallirahan asemesta vaihdon vlineen voitaisiin kteismaksuissakin kytt pelkstn knnykn tai jonkin muun ptelaiteen avulla liikuteltavaa tilirahaa. Tuolloinkin lytisiin epilemtt kerilijit varten juhlarahoja, mutta kyttrahat, setelit ja kiertvt metallirahat, menettisivt valuutastaan riippumatta nykyisenkin, aikaisempaa vhisemmn asemansa kansalaisten kannalta trkein symboleiden esityspaikkana. Toisaalta voidaan ajatella, ett euron kyttnotto pikemminkin vahvistaa kuin heikent kansallisen kulttuurimme edellytyksi. Esteettist tai symbolista vaikutelmaa trkempi ominaisuus rahalle on sen luotettavuus. Tss suhteessa euron kyttnottoa voidaan pit edistysaskeleena. Sen myt suomalaiset yritykset  ei vhiten pienet ja keskisuuret teollisuusyritykset -ovat saaneet toiminnalleen aikaisempaa vakaammat rahataloudelliset puitteet. Vaikka euro on ollut kytss vasta vhn aikaa, olemme jo saaneet joitakin esimerkkej rahataloudellisen vakauden vahvistumisesta. Erillisen rahapolitiikan aikana 1990-luvun alussa Suomea koetelleessa taantumassa korot nousivat aluksi enntyskorkeiksi ja muutoinkin rahatalouden vaikeudet vahvistivat idnkaupan loppumisen ja muiden reaalitaloudesta tulleiden hiriiden kokonaistaloudellisia vaikutuksia. Teknologia-alan viime vuosien kysynthiriit voi mittakaavaltaan ja ankaruudeltaan hyvin verrata Suomea 1990-luvun alussa koetelleisiin reaalitaloudellisiin hiriihin. Teknologia-alan hirit ovat nyt koetelleet alan yrityksi, joitakin ankarastikin, mutta kokonaistaloudellinen kehitys on ollut huomattavasti suotuisampaa, koska rahataloudelliset puitteet ovat pysyneet vakaina. Itse asiassa korot ovat tss taantumassa olleet alhaisempia kuin sitten kultakannan aikoihin. Suomen kansantalouden mukana mys Suomen kulttuurielm on selviytynyt taantumasta suhteellisin pienin vaurioin. Sill on nyt kaikki edellytykset selviyty hyvin jatkossakin. *** Hyvt kuulijat! Markalla ei ollut en viime vuosinaan samanlaista kansallista kulttuuritehtv kuin 1800-luvulla. Mys rahalaitoksen tytyy tehtvns tyttkseen muuttua yhteiskunnallisten olojen muutoksen myt. Title: Speech at landsbanken Investment Night
text: Bank Manager Sinikka Salo's speech at landsbanken's Investment Evening . Speech . Tuesday 21 October 2003, 12:00 AM The future of the euro At this event, I have been asked to speak on the subject of the future of the euro. sms is an interesting and broad theme that can be found in very different ways. In my presentation, I will examine the future of the euro from the international angle. The euro will have to compete with other currencies for its position on the international financial markets and the question may be how it will compete. The introduction of the euro at the beginning of 1999 was the biggest change in the international monetary system since the breakaway of the Bretton Woods system, created after the Second World War, and the gradual floating exchange rates of the currency were floated following the easing of the us dollar in August 1971. However, many observers, particularly in the United States, but also in France and other European countries, have, in the case of the euro, possibly marked the point of entry in the euro. The U.S. dollar was renamed bretton woods, the leading currency, after the collapse of the Bretton Woods djs system. Some have experienced the euro's chronology at first for a change that, over time, will challenge the hegemony of the dollar as the world's leading currency. In this case, the adoption of the euro could be compared to the years after the first World War, when the dollar rose from the pound to the world's leading currency. The basis for the international success of the currency is its success in its home country and therefore the success of the currency has generally been closely linked to the stages of the state that issued it. In the Member States of the Monetary Union, the euro is legally the only legal means of payment, and that is why its status at home is well secured. Of course, a legal monopoly does not guarantee a glorious future for the international foreign exchange market. In order to survive the competition between the leading currencies, the euro is able to make good money, i.e. to act as a measure of value and the value of the currency. Success is measured in relation to other currencies. The assessment of the future of the euro by market forces is most sensitive to international foreign exchange markets. In general, it can also be said that, in the context of free currency and currency movements, the quality of any monetary system is assessed by the average of the currencies in the context of competition on the international foreign exchange market. It is not just a question of exchange rates, but of the market's willingness to use different currencies in international payments, as reserve currency and in the euro market. The euro preceded its currency as a result of political pssching, and many of its characteristics were first tested in the process of making essentially political decisions. It may therefore appear to be an exception to the fact that the fate of currencies is determined by the competition between the two currencies in the last few years. In essence, however, the history of the birth of the euro supports rather than refutes the thesis on the importance of competition between currencies. Although in the process of emergence, the pressures of competition were influenced by politics rather than by the market mechanism, the impact of currency competition on the outcome can be clearly seen. The factor that contributed to the birth of the euro was that the currencies of most EU countries turned out to be weak in conditions where not only goods but also pssomas moved across borders. The fragility of European national currencies became clear after German integration in 1991-92, when waves of speculation severely destabilized the European exchange rate system and were in fact the country to destroy it completely. Although all the currencies of the countries that have joined the monetary union have merged with the euro, it is by no means possible to extend the euro as an average. On the other hand, the euro has inherited from the strongest predecessor, the German mark, more features than from the rest of the currency. The main institutional features of economic and monetary union, and in particular the ideas of monetary stability as the primary consideration of monetary policy and the independence of monetary policy from other policies, were incorporated into the Treaty as such in the legislation of the Federal Republic of Germany. The experience of the ERM system had convinced us that there was an irrevocable contradiction between the efforts to achieve monetary stability and credibility and, on the other hand, to steer the development of the currency through political processes, and that stability and credibility should be made the primary focus of monetary policy, as had been done in Germany. So the euro was not born out of historical void. Rather, it is the last link in the long chain of development of European currencies. It is not German nationally, but in terms of its characteristics it is essentially the successor to the German mark. In order to avoid the situation, I should say two things about the German mark and the euro. First, although Germany emerged as europe's leading economic power after the war, the triumph of the German mark was not based, at least not primarily, on the country's economic or political success. Rather, the characteristics of the German mark are inherited from the law to the euro and in the implementation of monetary policy because they are generally good currency characteristics. Germany had a self-absorbed and strong central bank, whose well-known and recognised objective of monetary policy was monetary stability. The Maastricht Treaty sought to secure the conditions for the euro. On the basis of the arrangements that have been found to be acceptable, the euro should have every chance of a great future, provided that the essential framework for success is not addressed in the future. The euro is by no means the sole heir to the German mark. Commenting on the outcome of sweden's emu referendum, Lars Heikensten, head of the Swedish Central Bank, said that there was no substantial difference between the monetary policy of the euro area and the monetary policy of Sweden. Like the ECB, the primary task of the Riksbank is to preserve the stability of the value of money, and it can only succeed if it has sufficient self-efficacy and other conditions for the successful performance of its tasks. Over the past two decades, the institutional position and monetary policy of the Riksbank have changed significantly, following the example of the German Bundesbank. Similar changes have also taken place elsewhere. That is why, in Heikensten's opinion, the ECB's addition to the Riksbank, as well as many non-European central banks, are doing well as pupils of the Bundesbank. For the euro, the adoption of the ECB's role and the principles of its monetary policy in the other leading industrialised countries will mean the stabilisation of international monetary conditions. This makes it easier for the ECB to conduct monetary policy from outside the euro area. On the other hand, international competition between currencies will intensify as more countries are able to conduct monetary policy.
