Thursday27 November 2003,12:00 AM Asuntomarkkinatja talouskehitys Keskityn tss puheenvuorossa yhtlt asuntorahoituksen ja rahapolitiikan, toisaalta asuntorahoituksen ja asuntomarkkinoiden vliseen yhteyteen. Aloitan kokoamalla yhteen suomalaisen asuntosektorin ja asuntorahoituksen erit keskeisi erityispiirteit. Pienet, mutta kalliit asunnot Suomessa on EU-maista pienimmt asunnot (keskimrin 76.5 m2 vuonna 2000), vaikka korkea BKT/capita ja pieni vestntiheys antaisivat ehk odottaa muuta. Edes kotitalouden keskikoko, joka Suomessa on melko pieni, ei selit asuntojen pienuutta. Esimerkiksi Tanskassa asuntojen keskikoko on 108,9 m2 ja Hollannissa 98 m2, vaikka molemmissa kotitalouden keskikoko on suunnilleen sama kuin meill (2.2 henke). Ruotsissa, jossa asunnon keskikoko on 90 m2, kotitalouden keskikoko on vain 2 henke. Ruotsissakin siis asuntoala henke kohti on Suomeen verrattuna liki 30% suurempi. Asuntojen keskikoko on meill kieltmtt hiljalleen kasvamassa, koska uusien asuntojen keskikoko on 87 m2 (v. 2000). Vertailussa jmme kuitenkin tsskin suhteessa useimmista muista maista jlkeen. Esimerkiksi Tanskassa uusien asuntojen keskikoko on 137 m2 ja Hollannissa 115m2. Saksassakin uusien asuntojen keskikoko on 109,2 m2 (mys siell kotitalouden keskikoko on sama kuin meill). Asuntojen keskikoon kasvu on kuitenkin kovin hidasta, koska uustuotannon suhde koko asuntokantaan on pieni, nykyn vain noin 1,5 prosentin luokkaa vuodessa. Aikaisemmin Suomi oli krkimaita asuntojen rakentajana Euroopassa, mutta nykyiselln asuntoinvestointien BKT-osuus on vajonnut EU:n keskitason tuntumaan. Tm ahtaus on tosiasia vaikka asunnot on valtaosin rakennettu aikana, jolloin Suomi oli jo noussut Euroopassa kansantulovertailujen keskikastiin. Taustalla on tunnetusti suomalaisen yhteiskunnan tavattoman nopea rakennemuutos. Nykyisist EU-maista vain Irlannissa asunnot ovat yht uusia kuin meill. Suomessa yli 56 prosenttia asunnoista on rakennettu vuoden 1970 jlkeen. Ruotsissa vastaava osuus on vain 31 prosenttia. Toisaalta vanhojen asuntojen poistuma on ollut suurta. Ennen sotia rakennettuja asuntoja on meill vain 11 prosenttia, kun esimerkiksi Ruotsissa niit on 33 prosenttia ja Tanskassa noin 42 prosenttia. Suomalaiset asuvat enimmkseen kerrostaloissa. Pientaloissa asuu suomalaista vain noin 40%, kun taas esimerkiksi tihesti asutussa Tanskassa 58,5% ja Hollannissa perti 71%. Ruotsissakin pientaloasuminen on tavallisempaa kuin meill. Uusista asunnoista on meill yhden perheen taloja vain 35%, kun taas Ruotsissa 51%, Tanskassa 60% ja Hollannissa 74%. Tm siit huolimatta, ett tutkimusten mukaan valtaosa suomalaisista haluaisi asua pientaloissa . Asuntojen pienuudesta huolimatta asumismenot eivt meill ole selvsti pienemmt kuin muualla. Asunnot ovat siis varsin kalliita. Suomelle on mys tyypillist asuntohintojen jyrkk vaihtelu. EKP:n tn vuonna julkaiseman kansallisen vertailun perusteella Suomessa asuntohintojen sykliset vaihtelut ovat olleet suurimpia koko EU-alueella. Hintojen vaihtelun taustalla ei tietenkn ole vain asuntomarkkinoiden toiminta, mutta silti on huomion arvoista, ett kun meill asuntojen reaalihinnan keskipoikkeama vuosina 1980 -2001 oli 26, se oli sek Tanskassa ett Ruotsissa vain15. Vain Irlannissa pstiin lhelle Suomen lukuja (25,8). Suomalainen asuntorahoitus perustuu vaihtuvakorkoisuuteen Siirrytn seuraavaksi tarkastelemaan rahoitusta. Aikaisemmin, luotonsnnstelyn vallitessa rahoituksen saatavuus oli Suomessa asunnontarvitsijan keskeisimpi huolenaiheita. Lainat olivat mys kovin lyhyit. Rahoituskysymys ei kuitenkaan ole ollut suomalaisen asuntopolitiikan keskeisten ongelmien joukossa en sen jlkeen kun inflaatiotavoitejrjestelm, SP:n itsenisyyden vahvistaminen ja sitten Suomen liittyminen euroalueeseen vakauttivat Suomen rahamarkkinat 1990-luvun puolivlin jlkeen. Tll hetkell asuntoluottoja tarjotaan runsaasti ja asuntorahoituksen keskeinen ongelma ei ole rahoituksen saatavuus eik edes sen hinta, vaan sen arvioiminen, mik on kunkin lainanottajan tuleva maksukyky ja kuinka suuria korko-ja muita riskej voidaan ottaa. Itse asiassa voidaan sanoa, ett rahoitus ei yleisemminkn ole en asuntomarkkinoiden keskeisimpien ongelmien joukossa, vaan ongelmia on etsittv asuntomarkkinoiden muista osatekijist. Rahamarkkinoiden vapautumisen ja sitten vakaantumisen jlkeen asuntoluottojen pituus on Suomessa voimakkaasti kasvanut. Tyypillisen uuden asuntolainan maturiteetti on meill nykyisin noin 17 vuotta. Tm on eurooppalaisessa vertailussa edelleen lyhyenpuoleinen, muttei aivan poikkeuksellisen lyhyt. Asuntojen tyypillinen vakuusarvo on 75  80 %. Tm on tavallista eurooppalaista tasoa. Periaatteessa asuntohintojen mahdollisesti suurempi vuotuinen volatiilisuus edellyttisi vakuuksien konservatiivisempaa arvostusta, mutta toisaalta lyhyt maturiteetti sallii tysimittaisemman vakuusarvon. Asuntolainojen korot ovat viime vuosina laskeneet voimakkaasti. Viime kuukausina asuntolainoja on mynnetty alle 3,5 % korolla, mik on ilmeisesti kaikkien aikojen enntys. Suomessa uuden asuntolainankorko on ilmeisesti tll hetkell matalin koko EU-alueella. Yleisen korkotason laskun lisksi thn on vaikuttanut se, ett pankkien veloittama asuntolainojen korkomarginaali (suhteessa kytettyyn viitekorkoon) on laskenut voimakkaasti, alle puoleen vuoden 1995 jlkeen. Tm osoittaa, ett ainakin asuntolainamarkkinoilla pankkikilpailu toimii vahvasti vaikka Suomen pankkisektori onkin nykyisin rakenteeltaan erittin keskittynyt. Kovin pieneksi painunut korkomarginaali on johtanut siihen, ett Suomen Pankki on julkisuudessakin kiinnittnyt huomiota siihen, ett pankkien pitisi huolehtia asuntolainojen hinnoittelun terveydest. Suomalaiselle asuntorahoitukselle ominaista on lainojen vaihtuvakorkoisuus. Melkein kaikki asuntolainat on nykyisin sidottu joko lyhyisiin euribor -korkoihin tai sitten pankkien omiin viitekorkoihin, jotka nekin mytilevt lyhytaikaisten korkojen kehityst. Viime aikoina euribor -sidonnaisuus on muodostunut tysin hallitsevaksi. Thn on tietysti osasyyn ajankohtainen korkorakenne, jonka kannustaa ottamaan lyhimpiin markkinakorkoihin sidottua lainaa, koska nm viitekorot ovat nyt poikkeuksellisen alhaiset. Eurooppalaisessa vertailussa kiintekorkoisen asuntoluoton pieni osuus osoittautuu suomalaiseksi erikoispiirteeksi. EKP:n selvityksen mukaan asuntolainoista on kiintekorkoisia esimerkiksi Hollannissa 74% ja Tanskassakin 75%. Ruotsissa, jossa kiintekorkoisia asuntolainoja on vain 38%, kuitenkin perti 62% on joko kiintekorkoisia tai sidottu keskipitkiin viitekorkoihin, eik siis lyhyisiin euribor-korkoihin. Mys Saksassa lyhyiden viitekorkojen kytt on harvinaista. Mielenkiintoista on, ett Irlanti, joka on Suomen ohella toinen maa, jossa asuntohintojen vaihtelu on ollut voimakasta, on Suomen kaltainen mys siin suhteessa ett asuntolainat on tyypillisesti sidottu lyhyisiin viitekorkoihin. Kansainvlisten esikuvien mukainen asuntorahoitusjrjestelm, joka perustuu kiintekorkoisiin kiinnelainoihin, joissa asunto itsessn on ainoana vakuutena, ja jotka rahoitetaan laskelmalla liikkeeseen pitkaikaisia obligaatiolainoja, on meill suhteellisen kehittymtn. Vain valtion asuntorahasto (ARA) on harjoittanut tmntyyppist toimintaa merkittvmmss mrin arvopaperistamalla aravalainojaan ns. Fennica-ohjelman kautta. Pankkikonsernien osaksi perustetut asuntoluottopankit viettvt siis hiljaiseloa. Lainojen arvopaperistamiseen ja kiintekorkoisuuteen (jotka sopivat hyvin yhteen) tunnetun mielenkiinnon vhisyys voi olla suhdanneluontoista ja johtua lyhyiden korkojen mataluudesta ja suomalaisten pankkien oman poman mrst, joka on nihin aikoihin saakka ollut vakavaraisuusvaatimuksiin verrattuna suhteellisen runsas. On todennkist, ett kiinnostus kiintekorkorkoisiin asuntolainoihin kasvaa joskus tulevaisuudessa, kun lyhyet korot ennemmin tai myhemmin kntyvt taas nousuun, ja arvopaperistaminenkin alkaa kiinnostaa kun pankkien omat pomat muuttuvat nykyist niukemmiksi. On mielenkiintoista nhd, miten tuleva BIS II snnst vaikuttaa pankkien haluun arvopaperistaa luottojaan. Kotitalouksien asuntovelan mr ei tll hetkell ole Suomessa kovin korkea. Eurooppalaisessa vertailussa se on pikemminkin alhaisen puoleinen. Thn on osaltaan vaikuttanut muun muassa 1990-luvun laman aikainen luottojen supistuminen, sek asuntolainojen verovhennysoikeuksien kiristminen 1990-luvulla. Kokonaan riskittmksi Suomen kotitalouksien velkaantumista ei silti pid arvioida. Thn vaikuttaa kolme syyt: lainojen vaihtuvakorkoisuus, joka lis kotitalouksien korkoriskej, asuntohintojen perinteisesti korkea volatiilisuus, ja viimeksi, muttei vhimpn se, ett asuntoluottojen mr on viime vuosina ollut tavattoman nopeassa kasvussa. Tmn kasvun on joskus hidastuttava, ja jos se tapahtuu kki, sill saattaa (aikaisemman kokemuksen perusteella arvioiden) olla yllttvn suuri asuntomarkkinoiden tilaa horjuttava vaikutus. EMU -jsenyys vakauttaa asuntomarkkinoita Euroalueen yhteinen rahapolitiikka mrytyy tunnetusti koko alueen talouskehityksen ja talousnkymien perusteella. Vaikka Suomen taloustilanne saattaa ainakin joskus poiketa ehk merkittvstikin euroalueen yleisest tilanteesta, esimerkiksi asuntomarkkinoiden osalta, ei tll siis voi olla kytnnss juuri mitn merkityst rahapolitiikan mitoituksessa. Kansallista rahapolitiikkaa, jolla periaatteessa voitaisiin reagoida kansallisiin ylikuumenemis-tai deflaatio-ongelmiin, ei Suomessa en harjoiteta. Tst on joskus tehty se johtopts, ett EMU -jsenyys olisi riski Suomen talouden ja ehk erityisesti juuri asuntomarkkinoiden vakauden kannalta. Tm ajatus kuitenkin yliarvioi kansallisen rahapolitiikan merkityst asuntomarkkinoiden vakauttajana. Esimerkiksi Suomessa 1970-ja 1980-lukujen rahapolitiikka, jota sitoi pyrkimys valuuttakurssin vakauttamiseen ja maksutaseen tasapainoon joutui usein reagoimaan tavalla, joka oli ilmeisesti asuntomarkkinoiden kannalta enemmn mytsyklinen kuin vakauttava. Meill koettiin sek 1970-ett 1980-luvuilla jyrkki asuntomarkkinoiden vaihteluita, joita kansallinen rahapolitiikka ei kyennyt tasoittamaan, lhinn siksi, ett rahapolitiikkaa oli kiinten valuuttakurssin jrjestelmn oloissa harjoitettava ennen muuta maksutaseen ehdoilla. Toisaalta suurikaan rahapoliittinen kansallinen liikkumavapaus ei tee asuntomarkkinoiden vakauttamista helpoksi tai edes mahdolliseksi. Esimerkiksi Iso-Britanniassa, joka ei ole Euroopan rahaliiton jsen, ja jonka inflaatiotavoitteeseen perustuva rahapoliittinen jrjestelm nauttii laajaa kansainvlist luottamusta, ei tst huolimatta ole onnistunut estmn asuntohintojen erittin huomattavaa nousua viime vuosien aikana. Syyn on se, ett asuntomarkkinoiden heilahtelut eivt suinkaan aina tapahdu samaan tahtiin kuin yleisten inflaatiopaineiden vaihtelut, joiden torjuntaan rahapolitiikan on suuntauduttava. Nhdkseni EKP:n rahapolitiikka ja siihen liittyv yleinen vakauden ilmapiiri pikemminkin vahvistavat kuin heikentvt Suomenkin asuntomarkkinoiden hiritnt toimintaa, ei vhiten siksi ett korkoliikkeet laajalla valuutta-alueella yleens ovat maltillisempia ja helpommin ennakoitavia kuin pienell valuutta-alueella. Missn nimess rahaliittoa ei voi pit uhkana asuntomarkkinoiden vakaudelle. Tst huolimatta asuntomarkkinoiden epvakaus on kuitenkin edelleen EMU-oloissakin yksi talouspolitiikan keskeisist riskeist. Siksi rahoitusmarkkinapolitiikassa ja pankkivalvonnassa on kiinnitettv suurta huomiota asuntorahoituksen riskien hallintaan. Jos asuntorahoitukseen liittyvt riskit nousevat liian suuriksi, sek kotitalouksien ett rahoittajien saattaisi kannattaa pyrki vhentmn niit esimerkiksi kiintekorkoisuutta suosimalla ja erill muilla keinoin, jotka liittyvt sitten jo enemmn asuntopolitiikan kuin rahoitusmarkkinapolitiikan alaan. Niist lhemmin seuraavaksi. Kansainvliset arvioijat Ympristministeri teetti viime vuonna Suomen asuntopolitiikasta kansainvlisen asiantuntija-arvion, joka valmistui joulukuussa 2002. Arvioitsijoiden mukaan trkein parannusehdotuksemme on, ett valtio ei pitisi kiinni (asumisen) tuen tasapuolisuudesta silloin, kun ongelmatkaan eivt jakaudu tasapuolisesti. Heidn mukaansa siis Suomessa tuetaan liian laajan ihmisryhmn asumista, jolloin tuen teho sosiaalisten ongelmien poistamisessa heikkenee. Asiantuntijoiden mukaan yksityiselle sektorille olisi annettava enemmn tilaa asuntomarkkinoilla, ja omistusasunnon hankkimista pitisi heidn mielestn tukea paremmin vakuutus-ja takausmarkkinoita edelleen kehittmll.. Asiantuntijat kiinnittivt siis erityist huomiota siihen, ett asumisen (kysynnn) tuki ei kohdistu sinne, miss sit eniten tarvitaan. Tm ptee tietysti asuntolainojen korkovhennyksiin, mutta kritiikki kohdistuu mys arava.asumisen tukeen, jossa tulorajat ovat niin korkeat, ett suurin osa kotitalouksista on teoriassa oikeutettu tukeen, vaikka todellisuudessa arava-asuntoja on tarjolla vain pienelle osalle kotitalouksista. Arvioitsijoiden mukaan 73 % suomalaisista on tulorajojen yms. kriteerien puolesta oikeutettuja Asuntorahaston kysynt tukeviin jrjestelmiin. Nin on siit huolimatta, ett ei ole mitn mahdollisuutta eik tarvettakaan jrjest sosiaalista asuntoa nin suurelle osalle vest: asuntokannasta vain 17 % on sosiaalisia asuntoja. Seurauksena on, ett tuki ei kohdistu suurimman tarpeen mukaan ja tulee tavoitteisiin nhden kalliiksi. Asiantuntijat katsoivat, ett Suomen asuntomarkkinat ovat rakenteellisesti epvakaat ja ett tt epvakaisuutta pitisi vhent. Thn he tarjosivat keinoina asuntolainojen korkovhennysoikeuden poistamista; kannustimia kiintekorkoisten asuntolainojen kytn lismiseksi; kiinteistveron osuuden lismist kunnallisverotuksessa ja kaavoitetun rakennusmaan saatavuuden parantamista kaikissa asuntojen hallintamuodoissa. Yksi epvakaisuutta lisv tekij on nimittin se, ett institutionaaliset sijoittajat eivt ole kovin kiinnostuneita vuokra-asunnoista mm. rajoittava tonttipolitiikan vuoksi. Tavoitteet Aikaisemmin asuntokysymyst tarkasteltiin lhinn sosiaalipolitiikan tai (viel aikaisemmin) kansanterveyden nkkulmasta. Nm kysymykset ovat luonnollisesti trkeit viel nykyisinkin. Asuntopolitiikan tavoitteena on oltava vestn asunto-olojen parantaminen. Periteisten asuntopoliittisten tavoitteiden rinnalle globalisaatio on kuitenkin tuomassa kokonaan uuden nkkulman: hyv asuminen on mys kansallinen kilpailukykykysymys. Globalisaatio merkitsee seuraavan vuosikymmenen aikana ennen kaikkea kiristyv kilpailua yritysten sijoittumisesta. Kovin kilpailu kydn siit, miss maassa ja mill alueilla tehdn korkeata osaamista vaativa ty, jossa arvonlisyksen mr ja palkkataso on korkein. Kysymys on siis esimerkiksi sellaisten toimintojen suunnittelun, markkinoinnin, liikkeenjohdon ja rahoitusyksikkjen sijoittumisesta. On Suomen kannalta trke, ett suomalaiset kasvukeskukset pystyvt tarjoamaan houkuttelevat asunto-olot sille asiantuntijavelle, josta kovimmin kilpaillaan ja joka ratkaisee suomalaisen elinkeinoelmn tulevan kasvun ja sit myt mys suomalaisen hyvinvointiyhteiskunnan tulevaisuuden. Suomessa on kansainvlisesti vertailtuna kire palkkaverotus. Sen vastapainona on tietysti pohjoismaista tasoa olevat, edulliset koulutus-ja terveyspalvelut. Kuitenkin, jotta Suomi voisi olla sijaintipaikkana houkutteleva taloudellisen kasvun katalyyttin toimivalle asiantuntijakunnalle, on sen oltava kilpailukykyinen mys asunto-olojensa suhteen. Tm kaikki tarkoittaa sit, ett Suomen asuntokantaa olisi nopeasti parannettava. Ennen kaikkea tarjolla olevien asuntojen kokoa on kasvatettava ja asuntojen laadun tulisi vastata paremmin asukkaiden toiveita -tm merkitsee mm. pientalojen osuuden kasvattamista. Toinen kilpailukyvyn ja tymarkkinoiden toiminnan kannalta keskeinen tavoite on, ett yksityiset vuokra.asuntomarkkinat olisi mys saatava toimimaan nykyist paremmin. Tll on merkityst paitsi ulkomaisen, ehk tilapisen tyvoiman maassa oleskelun kannalta, mys tyvoiman kotimaisen liikkuvuuden kannalta. Sit paitsi hyvin toimivat vuokra-asuntomarkkinat auttavat vhentmn asuntohintojen vaihtelusta kotitalouksille aiheutuvia riskej. Toimivien vuokra-asuntomarkkinoiden kehittymisen kannalta oleellisen trke institutionaalisten sijoittajien mielenkiinnon turvaamisen ohella olisi verotuksen epneutraalisuuksien poistaminen. Kolmas keskeinen tavoite on, ett asuntomarkkinoilta yleiselle talouskehitykselle ja rahoitusjrjestelmn vakaudelle tulevat uhat on voitava pit hallinnassa. Tm tarkoittaa ensinnkin kotitalouksien osalta sit, ett asuntohintojen vaihtelu kysynnn ja tarjonnan mukaan ei saisi tarpeettomasti aiheuttaa kotitalouksille mikrotason riskej: kotitaloudethan joutuvat ostamaan, myymn ja vuokraamaan asuntoja muun elmntilanteensa vaatimusten mukaan ja joutuvat tllin kohtaamaan erittin suuria ja tarpeettomia riskej, jos asuntomarkkinoilla on sellaista epvakautta, mik voitaisiin talouspoliittisin tai asuntopoliittisin keinoin poistaa. Lisksi se tarkoittaa sit, ett pankkijrjestelmn ei pitisi joutua kantamaan liian suuria asuntomarkkinoilta lhtisin olevia riskej. Tt varten olisi pyrittv rakenteellisiin uudistuksiin, jotka vhentisivt asuntohintojen vaihtelua, ja kehitettv asuntorahoituksen kytnt siten, ett suurempi osa riskist voitaisiin arvopaperistaa ja diversifioida kansainvlisille markkinoille. Mit olisi tehtv kytnnss Asuntopolitiikassa huomio olisi tulevaisuudessa kiinnitettv kysynt yleisesti tukevista toimista asuntojen tarjonnan joustavoittamiseen: asuntojen kysynnn on saatava vaikuttaa nykyist enemmn rakennustoiminnan suuntautumiseen ja laatuun. Tss erityinen asema on kuntien kaavoitus-ja tonttipolitiikalla. Tonttipolitiikkansa keinoin kunnat voisivat mys list kilpailua ja tarjontaa yksityisill vapaarahoitteisilla vuokra-asuntomarkkinoilla. Tonttipolitiikan joustavoittaminen palvelee paitsi tarjonnan kasvattamisen tavoitetta, mys vakauttaa hintojen vaihteluita. Vaikka uustuotannon merkitys asuntomarkkinoilla ei ole suuri, tonttipolitiikan merkitys on kuitenkin ilmeisesti suuri siksi, ett asuntojen hinnanmuodostus on luonteeltaan odotuksiin perustuvaa kuten muidenkin varallisuusmuotojen hinnat. Asuntojen hinta riippuu siis paitsi nykyisen uudistarjonnan mrst, mys kaikesta odotetusta tulevasta rakentamisesta. Muita hintojen vaihtelua vakaannuttavia toimia olisivat kotitalouksien korkovhennysten rajaaminen ja kiinteistveron osuuden lisminen kunnallisverotuksessa, mit jo ympristministerin kyttmt kansainvliset asiantuntijatkin suosittelivat. Tuotannontekijiden lisntyvn liikkuvuuden myt julkisen sektorin  mys kuntien -verotulojen silyttminen edes nykyiselln tulee olemaan tulevaisuudessa haastava tehtv. Tstkin nkkulmasta kiinteistveron korottamiseen saattaa kohdistua tulevaisuudessa paineita, etenkin kun veroyrien nousupaine on kunnissa jo nyt suuri. Kuten aikaisemmin sanoin, asuntorahoituksessa saattaa olla syyt suosia kiintekorkoisuutta sek riskien vhentmiseksi ett arvopaperistamisen helpottamiseksi. Kiintekorkoisuutta edistvn suuntaan voitaisiin vaikuttaa esimerkiksi korkojen verovhennysoikeuden ja/tai asuntolainojen valtiontakausjrjestelmn kautta. Asuntolainojen arvopaperistaminen on tulevaisuutta ja riskien hajauttamisen kannalta varmasti kannatettava kehityssuunta. Esteit sen etenemiselt pitisi koettaa viel lyt ja raivata pois. Yksi este on tosin vaikea poistaa: Suomen markkinoiden pienuus. Arvopaperistamisen edut tulevat nimittin parhaiten esiin vasta, kun asunto.obligaatioiden emissiot saadaan hyvin suuriksi. Tm on haaste Suomen kokoisen maan kannalta. Viime aikoina on nkynyt ehdotuksia Euroopan asuntoluottopankin perustamisesta. Tllainen pankki ostaisi tavallisilta pankeilta niiden asuntolainoja ja laskisi liikkeeseen tukkumarkkinoille suuria eri asunto-obligaatioita niden lainojen jlleenrahoittamiseksi. Idea on sikli relevantti, ett nin emissioiden koko saataisiin markkinoiden kannalta riittvn suuriksi, mutta hanke tuskin toteutuu ainakaan aivan lhivuosina. LHTEET ECB (2003). text: Bank Manager Sinikka Salo's speech at the FINLAND VOLUNTEER ECONOMY seminar . Speech . Monday8 December 2003, 12:00 AM European competitiveness, the euro and the dollar When the euro was introduced five years ago, its exchange rate against other currencies was, according to most estimates, at its equilibrium level. Since then, the euro weakened and was ultimately undervalued by all or all measures, especially the US dollar. In the autumn of 2000, the weakening of the euro led the Central Banks of Europe, the United States and the Bank of Japan to jointly carry out foreign exchange interventions to support the euro. As a result, the exchange rate of the euro stabilised and subsequently rose. Over the past two years, the euro has appreciated clearly against the US dollar. The exchange rate of the euro has revalued from its lows in 2001 by more than 40% and has recently exceeded its issuance on several occasions, i.e. the level recorded in January 1999, which until then was the strongest quotation for the euro. In the face of the appreciation of the euro, the debate on exchange rate issues, which has already ceased to exist, has resumed. However, the situation is now completely different from what it used to be. The focus of the debate, rather than the euro, is the US dollar, which has fallen in value and which still seems to be under downward pressure. The current exchange rate of the euro, on the other hand, is very much in line with the so-called euro exchange rate. with the basickijside. The euro's so-called euro-denomination the real effective exchange rate and other normal indicators of competitiveness in the euro area are their averages over long term and econometric estimates of the euro's equilibrium exchange rates are current market rates. The strong appreciation of the euro has thus been a return to normality from a situation of exceptional weakness. At the same time, however, concerns have come into the debate that the appreciation of the euro will become excessive over time. In this proposal, attention will be drawn to the fundamentals of exchange rates, in particular the imbalances in the world's current account balances, which are likely to play an important role in the future exchange rate development of the euro and the dollar in the long term. In addition to economic development and economic policy in the euro area and the United States, the exchange rate development of the two currencies depends on the economic development and policies of the world, particularly in Asian countries. The liquidation of large current account balances will have a significant impact on the development of the world economy as a whole and thus also on the development of euro and dollar exchange rates. It is true that Europe will have to acquire competitiveness by means other than an undervalued currency. Competitiveness is primarily and above all a question of real competitiveness, not exchange rates. According to my opinion, economic and monetary union has significantly strengthened europe's ability to compete on an equal footing with the other currency areas. The stability of a large currency, monetary stability and the general climate of stability more broadly are likely to create favourable climates for economic activity and prosperity. What is more important is that monetary union has opened up a genuine opportunity for European countries to create a large and well-functioning common market for the various sectors of the economy, which will help to create sustainable growth and prosperity in line with the EU's Lisbon strategy. *** The basic principles underlying exchange rates The core issue is the sustainability of external and sissic balances in the US economy The exchange rate movements of the dollar, the euro and other currencies now have to be judged against the threats posed by the inflated balances of the global economy. The core issue has become the sustainability of the external and guerrilla balances of the US economy. As a result of the non-existent nature of U.S. households, other sectors of the economy - firms and the public sector d are forced to cover the financial sector with foreign financing. The need for foreign financing, the world's largest and wealthiest economy, has been steadily increasing and, as a result, the country's debts are already well above the receivables. The country's net debt in relation to total output has already risen to 25%. The level of indebtedness is not a cause for concern. What is worrying, however, is that us indebtedness continues to rise very rapidly, at the current rate of around five per cent per annum. Due to the large size of the US economy, it is a question of huge pocket flows. Until then, the United States has had no difficulty in financing the current account deficit for the following reasons, among others: (1) The country's economy is dynamic and fast-growing. Total output has been rapidly increasing and since the 1990s the development of labour productivity has been very favourable. (2) Production costs and inflationary pressures have remained well under control, largely thanks to excellent productivity developments. (3) The depreciation of the dollar has not accelerated inflation, as foreign trade plays a relatively important role in the country's economy. In addition, the increasing shift of production to China and other low-cost countries has dampened the rise in import prices caused by the depreciation of the dollar. (4) Financing the current account deficit has been advantageous for the United States. The country's debt is mostly in the dollar, so there is no exchange rate risk associated with it, and investments from the United States abroad have yielded more than investments from abroad to the United States. Due to the low cost of financing, neither the private sector nor the public sector has been under much pressure to curb foreign borrowing, not to mention that the availability of foreign financing has been called into question, as in Finland, for example, during the banking crisis. (5) The country's central bank has been pursuing a very light monetary policy even after the country's economy has clearly started to recover. Low central bank interest rates have helped to keep the cost of long-term foreign debt under control. On the other hand, financing has been made possible by the efficiency of financing in international financial markets. Investors are able to diversify their portfolios efficiently by region and industry. This has increased the willingness of non-US investors to invest in US assets. A worrying feature of recent economic developments in the United States is the shift in demand from the private to the public sector. In the past, foreign financing was used, for example, in the form of direct investments to finance productive investments. In recent years, fiscal policy has been strongly expansionary and has led to a large deficit in public finances. Now, foreign borrowing is used to finance general government expenditure. In fact, the need for public finance is more or less the same as the need for financing for the national economy as a whole, i.e. large-scale foreign borrowing will ultimately have to be used entirely to cover the public sector funding gap. Large-scale government debt financing would lead to a significant increase in interest rates in the long term, a reduction in investment and a slowdown in productivity growth. In the medium term, therefore, the need to correct the budgetary situation and the current account is a fact of the essence for the country's economy, and the country's authorities have also recently been prepared to do so. The counterpart to the US current account deficit, the current account surplus of other countries, is located in asian countries The counterpart to the US current account deficit, the surplus of the current account of other countries, is located in asian countries. Japan's current account has traditionally been oversized and has remained above and above, despite the slowdown in growth. A large part of the country has been located in the United States. Japanese takeovers were a topical theme in U.S. political discourse in the 1980s and early 1990s, until the fears of Japan's economic difficulties about the country's economic occupation disappeared. Japan has also invested heavily in US securities. The so-called "tavern" of Asia outside of Japan. the current account balances of emerging market economies have been increasing. Indeed, the counter-balance of the us current account, which has increased in recent years, has been concentrated in Asian countries outside Japan. Although the Japanese yen is basically floating, the Bank of Japan has in recent years intervened heavily against the dollar in the foreign exchange market, as a result of which the country's foreign exchange reserves have grown to a considerable extent. However, more recently, following the improvement of the economic shocks and the partial easing of deflationary pressures, the authorities have allowed the yen to strengthen. The currencies of other Asian countries are generally still under tight political control, partly thanks to the sssnnssing of the Psssoman movements. Many countries have pegged their currencies to the US dollar. The competitiveness of the countries has strengthened, including strong export growth and current account surpluses. In order to prevent the revaluation of currencies against the dollar, the central banks of the countries have required large-scale purchases of dollars, which are the rapid growth of their foreign exchange reserves. The dollar plays a key role as a reserve currency An interesting feature in terms of the financing of the US dual iliac is the special position of the dollar as the leading reserve currency in the international foreign exchange market. At the end of last year, the dollar balance of the world's foreign reserve assets amounted to about 65% of the foreign exchange assets of the world's states, while the euro-srsisis was 15% and the yenimssrsisis 15% and the yenimssrsisis. In the context of a sharp increase in their foreign exchange reserves, particularly in the last year, Asian countries have meant a large proportion of purchases of dollar-dollar securities issued by the US government. Through this, asian countries have contributed more or less directly to the financing of the US government deficit and have also contributed to the delay in the US fiscal corrections. There is a fairly broad consensus that, in order to ensure stable and sustained growth in the global economy, the large eps balances in current account balances will have to be addressed at some point. There are several ways to make a correction. It is probably best for all parties that the current account balances are adjusted calmly and in a controlled manner, i.e. without sharp changes in exchange rates or in the crisis of the international financial system. The gradual adjustment of exchange rates, i.e. a moderate depreciation of the dollar, may well be part of a successful adjustment process. However, adjustment cannot be relied on alone, or even on changes in exchange rates alone. Changes in the exchange rate as such, without changes in other variables, affect the under- and over-balances of current account balances only relatively slowly and relatively slowly, according to the model calculations. In order to correct current account balances, changes in the real economy are needed above all. Solving the us deficit problems would require a slowdown in the country's economic growth, at least in relation to other countries. The most straightforward way would be to tighten the country's fiscal policy and steer its public finances back on a sound footing. In any event, in order to maintain the sustainability of public finances, a substantial tightening of fiscal policy will be required in the future. If the U.S. presidency does not react to the inflated foreign indebtedness in a timely manner and with sufficient force, the restrictions on growth could also come from foreign investors. If investors start to demand risk from their U.S. investments. the country's interest rates are rising and economic growth is slowing down. The solution of the problems of US economic policy would be facilitated by the acceleration of economic growth outside the United States, whereby the current account balances of the change in the cyclical situation would be partly automatically corrected. The growth potential of asia's emerging economies is considerable, but the economies of many countries, especially China, are already at the limit of their growing potential. (China's real gross domestic product has been growing at a long-term rate of 8-9% per annum.) As a result, no significant acceleration in economic growth is expected in the last few years. In Europe and Japan, there has recently been a growing sign of a rise in the economic cycle and a strengthening of demand. The economies of Europe and Japan are weak in terms of poor performance. This is due to various structural problems which have not been remedied. However, reforms have now been put on the agenda of both European and Japanese politics. As I mentioned earlier, the exchange rate of the euro against other currencies is now lshes, on the basis of all calculations, lshells equilibrium. Until then, the appreciation of the euro has only meant the unwinding of the previous haircut. Will the exchange rate development of the euro remain balanced also in the future and in Europe in terms of current price competitiveness in the future? This is possible, but on the other hand, it is also possible that the dollar's weakening pressures will partly unwind into the euro. In particular, there is a high risk that the large current account balances will not be absorbed without problems, that the dollar will weaken appreciably and that the emerging Asian market economies will continue their policy of the fixed dollar exchange rate, despite the downward pressure on the dollar. The return of the euro to low levels in the early 2000s, on the other hand, will have an impact on the euro. In other words, european countries are looking for competitiveness in other countries than the weak euro. *** Europe's competitiveness and the challenges facing the EU to boost economic growth and prosperity When discussing the economic situation in Europe, the fundamental fact is often forgotten that the emergence of monetary union has considerably and permanently strengthened the financial basis of the European economies and, through that, our ability to compete with the United States and Asian countries in terms of economic growth, employment and prosperity. Europe, which is also the single currency, took a significant step towards a vast monetary area. More than 300 million people currently live in the euro area. people, when, for example, the population of the United States is less than 280 million. and Japan's only 127 million. people. Gross domestic product in the euro area is just over 16% of world GDP, i.e. about 6% of the total gdp, compared with that of the United States (22%), but clearly higher than that of Japan (7%). If all the EU countries, including the new Member States, join next year, join the euro area over time, the euro area's budget figure will increase by about half. Vis-a-vis the euro area, the euro area would clearly become a larger market than the United States. However, total output in the euro area would rise more markedly than the figure, as the total output per capita of the new Member States is still clearly lower than the average in the current EU countries. The use of money is associated with economies of scale, and money in a large currency area generally works better in terms of exchange and value than money in a small currency area. The size of the currency area therefore offers European countries a competitive advantage, possibly even in relation to the United States. Monetary policy a success in EMU The changeover to the euro meant abandoning monetary policy in favour of a single monetary policy. At the same time, fluctuations in the average exchange rates of the euro area countries and the associated risks are fully mitigated. Many people have already forgotten that the risks were significant before the changeover to the euro. Europe's previous monetary system proved to be fragile and, in the early 1990s, it was plunged into an outright crisis which not only undermined the economic development of the countries involved in the system, but also undermined the eu's economic policy credibility. The effects of the crisis were also felt outside the monetary system. In Finland, the volatility of the European currency markets accelerated the economic depression and the outbreak of the banking crisis. Although the changeover to the euro reduced the exchange rate risks of the euro area countries, it did not, of course, eliminate them completely. However, for a large currency area, the exchange rate is an essential amount than for a small currency area. the European Central Bank does not therefore need to pay as much attention to exchange rate developments as the national central bank of a small country. This means a more stable monetary policy. Another effect of monetary union was the convergence of interest rates in the euro area countries. The development of the shortest interest rates is determined by the key interest rates of the European Central Bank, in particular the interest rate on the main refinancing operations. The European Central Bank is not in a position to control the development of other interest rates with the same degree of precision, but all monetary policy developments have a significant impact on them through expectations. In its first five years, the European Central Bank's monetary policy has been more successful than hardly anyone could have anticipated or even hoped for. Despite the difficult conditions at the start of monetary union, d I am referring in particular to the strong international upturn and the rise in the price of sljy and other import hysdys - the monetary policy has been credible from the outset. This is the case with interest rates in the euro area. Although longterm interest rates have risen slightly globally as a result of the improvement in the economic cycle, they are still very low in real terms, i.e. taking inflation into account. The integration of financial markets takes place in the What is more important is that monetary union has opened up a genuine opportunity for European countries to create a large and well-functioning common market for the various sectors of the economy. The introduction of the euro has opened up the possibility of creating a truly unified financial market in Europe. Financial markets can only change in the meantime, but I believe that over time these changes are significant and will have a major impact on the economic development of European countries. I would therefore like to stress the importance of a large and well-functioning financial market as a factor that has a positive impact on economic development. The introduction of the euro gave a significant boost to the integration of European financial markets. In particular, the unsecured short-money market for banks now operates on a euro area-wide basis. The market for government bonds and other bonds has already been integrated for a fairly long period of time. Despite significant progress, the euro area's financial markets as a whole remain more fragmented than foreign exchange conditions in the past. In terms of the commonality and depth of the financial markets and thus the liquidity of the currency, the euro area is likely to remain in the remainder of the United States for a long time. On the road to the integration of the euro area's financial markets, there are various differences in legislation (such as the Bankruptcy and Taxation Act) as well as in supervisory systems and administrative authorisation procedures. Financial market infrastructures, such as securities clearing houses, are largely national and operate differently in different countries. They are technically difficult to reconcile and it seems to be more difficult to reconcile different local interests. Even in the euro area, it is much easier to buy or sell financial services within a country than from one country to another, and even something as simple as paying becomes considerably more difficult as soon as the counterparty is from another euro country. Summary : Competitive advantages of the euro area To sum up, the euro area has two significant competitive advantages over any other currency area, namely the size of the region and the stable monetary policy of the central bank. With regard to the convergent functioning of the markets and, in particular, of the financial markets, the picture is not entirely entirely positive, but there is clear potential on the other side to strengthen the competitiveness of the euro area. To realise this potential, it is necessary to make a conscious effort to achieve a coherent financial market. It is not clear at the moment, where the goal will be achieved. Despite all the frictions, I am very optimistic about the future integration process of the financial markets. The benefits of a truly Pan-European financial market are simply too great for us to be able to accept them. The main obstacles to Europe's future and competitiveness concern the joint ability to cope with major economic or political crises. Nsits epsilys is known for its lack of a strong political center. Economic and monetary union does not mean a federal state in today's traditional way. Above all, it is important that each Member State remains responsible for its own economic policies. However, the national room for manoeuvre in economic policy is limited by the economic policy cooperation of the Member States. Cooperation is based on mutual standards and coordination based on mutually agreed standards between governments. This is a special feature of Europe. The strengthening of cooperation in the EU's economic policy is often seen as a reduction in the economic policy autonomy of the nation states. In a way, the idea of sticking to the point of view that all parties are forced to make compromises that sometimes seem awkward. Similarly, it is probably a fact that the large countries have a greater say, at least on an individual basis, in eu political decision-making and, more generally, in international cooperation, than the smaller countries. However, the idea of a loss of self-efficacy is also one-sided in relation to the fact that it does not take into account the increase in influence that we gain by participating in the eu's decision-making. It is in the interest of all Europeans that the common ssnns on which the EU is founded are sufficiently strong and that the common institutions also have sufficient powers. The recent increase in budget deficits and the excessive deficits in the Council of the EU and the decision to deal with Germany and France d or rather the absence of a balance - have revived a pertinent debate on free-riders in the monetary union. If the Member States of monetary union want to continue to enjoy the stability of monetary union, they must also play their part in supporting and eroding stability. The issue of economic policy, such as budget deficits, in the EU is not an unnecessary nuisance, but part of the guarantees that safeguard the functioning of the monetary union, in addition to the fact that they are a member of the Eu ropean Union d taking into account, among other things, the rapid expansion of all the Member States - also for their own economies. The obvious need to develop a common policy concerns the supervision of financial stability and crisis management. As the integration of the financial markets continues to take place, the need for cooperation will increase. Banks and insurance companies together form larger international entities and their liabilities and risks are spread over the euro area and also globally. In the autumn, the EU countries are already in great contact with the financial markets and in the supervision of the financial markets and in crisis management. In relative terms, the concentration of power in a wider range of cases in the community institutions seems to be somewhat of a development over time.

Title: Finland, the EU and the challenges of globalisation
text: Bank Manager Sinikka Salo's speech at talousforum 2004 seminar: Finland, the EU and the challenges of globalisation . Speech . Wednesday4 February 2004, 12:00 AM Speech at talousforum 2004 d seminar 4.2.2004 I would like to begin by expressing my sincerest thanks to the members of the Annual Economic Forum for the invitation to take part in the event. My topic "Finland, the EU and the challenges of globalisation" is the most interesting. The link between China, India and other wealthy countries and international markets has already changed the world and the Finnish economy considerably. However, the biggest changes and challenges are probably still in the future. The subject matter of my presentation is broad, and I can't even superficially cover all the relevant points. In this context, I have to be content with a couple of individual themes. A more comprehensive presentation on the subject will certainly be provided by the government's report on the impact of the change in the global economy on Finland's economic and employment strategy, initiated on the initiative of the President of the Republic. Once completed, it will hopefully also offer concrete policy recommendations on how we in Finland should respond to the challenges of globalisation. At the seminar of church and social leaders, the choices of economic policy are to be judged not only by the social responsibility of the national economy, but also by the right and vssrsn nsks angle. Throughout the ages, representatives of the Church have touched on the value base of economic activity in their speeches. A particularly emphatic statement ---on the basis of the position of office already presented by the bishops,--a few years ago, was the presentation by the bishops of the speech "Towards common goodness". 1) 1) At the beginning of their speech, the bishops quoted Isaiah. In the quote, the Prophet rhetorically asks why it is true to fast: "Sitsks, lest you hang your pssch like a reed on the shore, wear a ssk garment, lie in the dust of the earth, sitsks call fasting, a psivs according to the lord's mind? I expect another kind of fast: that you free yourself from the chains, that you untie the straps of the yoke, and that you release the oppressed, that you crush all the yokes, that you break the leipsss, that you open your home to the homeless, that you clothe the naked when you hsnet nset, and that you do not shun your brother who needs help." Globalisation or its effects should not be viewed solely from the point of view of Finland, or even primarily from the point of view of Finland. If we think about the economic choices from the perspective of the right and vssrsn nsks, we have to think about the impact of our choices on the conditions of countries other than our own. Ksyhst our brothers and sisters, whom we need to help, live largely outside Finland. Simply trying to help is not enough. Pitsss also done the right thing. When we consider whether economic policy choices are good or bad, we have to take a stand not only on our ethical values, but also on how the economy works. Without sufficient knowledge of financial matters, recommendations can easily be made to become lsyh; at worst, they even become harmful. In Finland, in the debate on globalisation, we often hear the wisdom of economics. Most of all, I have been struck by the fact that global trade d i.e. globalisation d has, in many speeches, been described as harmful to the countries of the Kchyhs. Emerging economies are therefore urged to self-exclude from international trade or to make it more difficult for international markets to function with artificial barriers and restrictions. There have been particularly enthusiastic calls for the international financial markets to be ssnnsstelys either by imposing restrictions on the movement of currencies or by a tax on currency swaps. In my opinion, such recommendations can be compared to "fasting by wearing a Sshkki garment"; the recommendations may be intended to be good, but they are not hysdyllis. Lsperchichi's recommendations are also drawn from the speeches of the priests. Hardly anyone will mind if I dare say that even the bishops' speech and the quotation from Isaiah at the beginning of it is lackluster. *** All experience shows that economies that have opened up to foreign trade and are trading-friendly have a good chance of growing rapidly. The rapid prosperity of China, India and other Asian countries in recent years demonstrates the potential of foreign trade in the fight against poverty. In addition to the rapid economic growth of these countries, the distribution of world income has already levelled off significantly. On the contrary, the economic development of countries that have been excluded from globalisation has invariably been deplorable. In the early 1900s, and in some countries even in the 1970s, there were widespread fears that market economies would enter a permanent economic downturn, at least without large-scale and direct intervention by the public authorities. This growth pessimism was based, on the one hand, on the experiences of the Great Depression and the slow growth of the period of the World Wars in general, and on the rise in popularity of Marxist thought in the early decades of the century. However, the experience of different economic systems over the last two or three centuries, in which the current period of globalisation also includes, has shown fears and hopes of a self-destructive market economy to be unfounded; On the other hand, in the light of historical experience, growth and the capacity for renewal are precisely the characteristics of a market economy. The dynamic nature of the capitalist economy was probably first noticed by the so-called capitalist economy. economists of the Austrian school in the late 1800s and early 1900s; one of them, the Americanized Joseph Schumpeter, in his 1942 book "Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy", described the nature of the transformation of the capitalist economy with the term "creative destruction", which has since become famous. The strength of the market economy lies in its ability to create genuine economic growth. Economic policy issues are not entirely or even primarily issues of income distribution, i.e. a zero-sum game, as they tend to be in a static economy. Instead of a distributive policy in a growing economy, it is necessary to pursue a policy that offers as much as possible to share with all parties. It's a simple thing that's hard to understand. As for wealth, we easily imagine that it is, in one way or another, stolen from ksyhilts. Even in the debate on globalisation, the world's economic distribution of income is thus often explained by exploitation or by the imperialist past of the industrialised countries. This is a very credible explanation of the current wealth of the Ksyh countries, and a more credible explanation of the present wealth of the rich countries. The market economy, on the other hand, has the weakness of not being able to produce a general, universal and always steady increase in prosperity. On the other hand, economic development is accompanied by various spatial growing pains. In addition to cyclical fluctuations, structural changes in the economy cause growing pains. The economic resources of even the wealthiest society are limited. New industries and new jobs can therefore only be created if the old industries wither away and the old jobs die. According to Schumpeter's idea, destruction, i.e. the growing pains of the economy and the creation of new, more productive jobs, are therefore two sides of the same growth process. *** For those caught up in structural change, these changes can be painful, and it is therefore understandable that politics constantly has to consider ways of mitigating or protecting against such changes. Especially in the U.S., many people would like to protect jobs by restricting cheap employment from countries future imports. If implemented, this policy would mean a return to the high protective tariffs or other import barriers of the post-war period. Calls for restrictions on imports in the United States are generally always in the run-up to elections, and the recent intensification of the debate is partly apparent from the corner. On the other hand, there is a fundamental background to the requirements, since the current account of the United States, i.e. the difference between exports and imports, has become strongly subordinated. Chel has been particularly affected by trade with China and other emerging economies in Asia. These countries have a large share of U.S. trade. In recent years, the balance of the current account has been affected by the monetary and fiscal policies of the countries. In the United States, domestic demand has been strongly supported by monetary and fiscal policies. At the same time, Asian countries have adopted an export-led growth strategy. The countries have sought to increase their export price competitiveness in the US market and have used foreign exchange interventions to prevent their currencies from strengthening to the dollar. Another, more structural reason for the emergence of the US current account deficit is that, since the Second World War, high tariffs on trade in manufactured goods in particular - high tariffs on imports and separate taxes on imported goods - have been progressively dismantled in multilateral and bilateral trade negotiations. This trade policy was based on the bitter experiences of the first World War. At that time, the gradual increase in trade barriers led to economic and political isolation, the stagnation of economic growth, the emergence of power blocks around the large countries and, finally, the Second World War. As a result of the dismantling of trade barriers, import duties on manufactured goods in all industrialised countries have been reduced to a fairly reasonable average level. In the United States, the tariff on industrial goods is only 2.4% of the value of imports. As a result of the dismantling of import protections, Asian countries have increasingly sold their products to the prosperous American market, where demand has been growing rapidly. The establishment of import protection in order to protect workplaces in industrialised countries is more important, although morally and economically acceptable. It is clearly a question of defending private interests at the expense of the common interest. The market of industrialised countries is open, especially for the ksyh countries. The opening up of the prosperous and fast-growing markets of the industrialised countries, and in particular of the United States, has been, and continues to be, a prerequisite for the success of a growth strategy based on exports from industrialised countries. In spite of the initial difficult circumstances, I am referring in particular to the strong international upturn and the rise in the price of sljy and other import hysdys d the ECB has managed to maintain price stability in the euro area without even having to resort to a heavy grip on monetary policy. Interest rates may also rise in the future due to the change in the cyclical situation, but it is highly probable that we do not need to pay for such high interest rates as, for example, in Finland in the first half of the 1990s. In particular, a large currency area and monetary stability provide a good basis for the growth and development of small and medium-sized enterprises. In responding to the challenges of globalisation, this is a good thing. *** The introduction of the euro has given a significant boost to the integration process of European financial markets. Progress has also been made in other market segments. The benefits of a pan-European financial market are simply too great for us to be able to accept them. The integration of nationally segmented financial markets into one well-functioning and safe European financial market will significantly improve the ability of European companies to adapt their activities to the new market conditions and new production methods arising from the progress of globalisation. It is important that it has played a central role in the economic policy cooperation of the European Union during the years. *** Good listeners! Globalisation is often seen solely and simply as a threat to existing jobs and to the existence of our welfare state. The sms angle is narrow and defensive. In my presentation, I have tried to bring a slightly wider angle to the globalisation debate. The relocation of the manufacture of manufacture of industrial products and, at some point, of agricultural products to countries with low labour force, is a threat to the survival of low-productivity jobs. However, ssss is not new. In recent decades, Finland has steadily lost jobs and entire professions, as the production of some products has either ceased altogether or moved to countries with cheap labour. At the same time, however, new jobs with higher productivity have been replaced. This change has been essential to enable productivity to rise, and without it, of course, an increase in living standards would not have been possible. The current phase of globalisation, the accession of the rich and neighbouring Asian countries to the international divide is nothing more than a new, albeit significant, step in the long-standing development of Finland and other industrialised countries. The industrialization of Asian countries has brought enormous dynamism and new opportunities to the entire world economy. Of course, in addition to the opportunities, there are significant challenges. In my opinion, it would be a great mistake to respond to these challenges by trying to return to the old policy solutions. As a member of the EU, Finland does not have to face the challenges of globalisation alone. When the challenges of globalisation are the same or almost the same for all EU Member States, I would make EU policy finland's most important instrument for preparing for these challenges. This is a more important reason, given that for all the policy instruments most relevant to the globalisation process, the EU is already centralising its work at the common level. A single monetary policy, well-functioning financial markets and a dynamic economy, for their part, support not only the citizens of the EU, but also the functioning of the world economy as a whole. As a global player, the EU is also able to influence the global economic framework in the negotiations alongside the United States as an equal influencer and partly as a counterparty. In order to ensure the continued favourable development of the world and the Finnish economy, it is essential to safeguard free trade in goods and services. The challenges of globalisation must not lead to protectionist policies. Even the construction of barriers to trade can easily lead to difficult-to-manage processes that are bad for all parties involved. In particular, for the most important countries, there would be obstacles to trade, and in particular to agricultural products. In a context of strong changes in the structure of production, well-functioning and extensive financial markets are the key to the dynamics of the economy. The emergence of a common European market is also open to us Finns, for the first time in our history, to participate in large and well-functioning financial markets. Macroeconomic policies d i.e. monetary and fiscal policies d best help to prepare for the challenges of globalisation by providing a stable framework for business. The climate of stability associated with the activities of the European Central Bank has already given results in the form of historically low interest rates. As far as fiscal policy is concerned, European countries should put their public finances on a stable and reliable footing as soon as possible, not only because of the challenges posed by globalisation. Finland's public finances are in better shape than in many other EU countries. In spite of this, maintaining a reasonably good balance will be a challenge, especially in public finances. In addition to budgetary policy, the main national policy challenges are related to structural policy. In order to maintain a high level of employment and well-being in changing circumstances, well-functioning and flexible production structures are required. There must be the courage to renew and develop.
