text: Pankinjohtaja Sinikka Salo: Lecture at the Finnish-German Technology Seminar . Speech . Wednesday15 June 2005,12:00 AM Financing innovation and the further development of the EU internal market Recent events have shown once again how closely linked europe's economic and political developments are. It is evident that the rejection of integration in the referendum on the EU Constitution has to a large extent economic causes. Europe's weak competitiveness has caused economic problems and uncertainty, which have been reflected in public opinion as economic isolationism and a desire to halt the world's transformation. It is paradoxical that the EU Constitution in particular has become one of the first victims of this climate of opinion, even though one of the central motives of European integration has been expressly the improvement of our continent's economic competitiveness and performance. Those skonomene who are behind the wave of rejection of integration in Europe are easy to point out. One of them is the precarious employment situation. Jobs have been lost in a situation where the unemployment rate is already high. Added to this is the uncertainty about the state of the public budget and, in connection with this, the uncertainty about the future of social security and pension systems. In many Countries, the balance of the state budget has deteriorated significantly, in a situation where there was otherwise already a need to cut income transfers and pensions. The demands for a balanced public budget have often been presented as demands of the EUo, as if the public funds without the EU were somehow passed on. In addition to all this, the economic problems associated with the ageing of the population have become more and more topical in Europe and that these problems have become more and more aware. As the challenges facing the European economy grow and its performance wanes, public opinion has turned harshly against a change in the world. It is as if the desire expressed by Eduard Msrike to escape the world has gained the upper hand in Europe: aLa, o world, o la to be me! Do not lure with gifts of love, Lat have this heart alone, His bliss, his pain! o On the other hand, it is clear that the European integration project, which is now facing headwinds, promises the best solutions to the problems that plague our continent's economy. Europe must respond to the challenges of ageing, globalisation and unemployment by improving its economic competitiveness and boosting productivity growth and investment. There is no other way to solve the problems. That is why the objectives behind the Lisbon Strategy adopted five years ago are more relevant today than before. At the same time, it is clear that the new economic dynamism sought by the strategy is more difficult and slower to achieve than was assumed at the time. The implementation of the Lisbon Strategy so far has been assessed in the report of the High Level Expert Group chaired by Wim Kok, published last November. The presentation of the report does not sound very positive: "Now that the deadline of 2010 has passed, the overall picture is quite mixed. Much still needs to be done to prevent Lisbon from becoming synonymous with missed goals and not promises that have been fulfilled." The Kok report identifies five areas in which action is needed. The first two of them are 'Implementation of the Knowledge Society' and 'Compliance with the Commitment to the Internal Market'. For my part, I would like to deal with these two points together today, because they are very closely linked. At the same time, these issues are at the heart of europe's productivity and competitiveness. It is about innovation, its implementation in products and its financing, but I would like to emphasise that these central issues for the economic future of our continent depend precisely on the project of the common market and on the fact that we bring this project to an end. I would also like to say a few words about the case of Finland, as Finland is one of Europe's leading countries in terms of innovation and also in the growth of industrial productivity. *** The question of reviving Europe's economic growth dynamics is often viewed from the point of view of productivity. The growth of labour productivity in Europe has declined steadily, from year to year and from decade to decade. At the same time, the growth of productivity in the United States has been improving for a long time. These are facts, but the differences in the growth of productivity should not only be considered quantitatively, since the problem behind them is primarily a qualitative one. The qualitative problem is not a consequence of the fact that work in Europe is not effective enough, but of the fact that Europe does not produce sufficiently developed and unique products and services. The European economy has focused too much on areas where productivity growth is slow, and the structural change of the European economy from low productivity to areas producing and using high technology has been too slow. The vulnerability of European competitiveness in the context of the deteriorating global competition is therefore to a large extent due to the fact that in Europe the  transition from industrial production model to post-industrial production has been too slow. Much has been discussed about the technological gap that exists between Europe and the United States. But even this gap must be located correctly. At the level of basic training, Europe's competitiveness is good. More students graduate in engineering and natural sciences at European universities than at American universities. The challenges for Europe lie in the development and use of the top spot. At the level of cutting-edge research and research and development, Europe is not far behind the US. Studies show that R&D activity and innovation are central to the growth of productivity. In relation to gross domestic product, US spending on research and development is one and a half times that of the EU. In addition, American companies make a much greater contribution to investment in R&D than European companies. Finland is one of the few EU countries where spending on research and development exceeds the three per cent target. At the same time, Finland is one of the two countries where R&D spending by companies accounts for more than two percent of the value of gross domestic product. A similar picture of the differences in product development efficiency in the EU and the United States can be obtained by looking at the number of patents applied for. The Americans patent twice as many inventions in their country as the Europeans in their own EPO system (European Patent Office). In Europe, almost as many patents are filed by American companies as by European companies, but in the United States, the proportion of European inventions patented there is less than a quarter of the number of American inventions. If one follows the value chain of innovation from research to patents and from patents to the translation of ideas into products, one is confronted with the question of financing new companies (start-ups). In this area, too, the situation in Europe is worrying. A symptom of the downturn in the European innovation chain is the small size of venture capital compared to the United States. This difference has been compensated by a certain amount after the global IT bubble burst in 2001. But the difference is still significant. It is particularly evident when looking at private venture capital financing. According to a recent study (Ernst & Young LLP and VentureOne 2005), cumulative investments by European venture capital firms in 2004 accounted for only a quarter of the value of venture capital investments in the US. In reality, the difference between the EU and the United States is not quite as dramatic, because in addition to private capital investors, public funds are also involved in this activity, the importance of which is greater in Europe than in the USA. On the other hand, studies have shown that the activity of independent capital investors is generally more successful than the activity of capital funds that operate in conjunction with banks or are owned by the public. The differences between the financial markets of Europe and the USA in the financing of new entities have been investigated, among other things, in the joint research network "Capital Markets and Financial Integration in Europe" of the Eurosystem central banks. The final report, published last December, notes that the financing system for start-ups in Europe is poorly developed and poorly integrated, both for venture capital investors and for IPO markets for young companies. The characteristics of the European innovation chain, which I mentioned above, probably explain to a large extent why the growth of productivity and the structural change of the economy in Europe have been disappointing. To sum up, innovation in Europe is relatively lower than in the United States in terms of investment in research and development, but that the activity in patent applications and the growth of economic productivity have also been more modest. This indicates that an increase in investment in research and development alone is not enough to solve this problem, but that the matter must be seen in a broader context. *** My own country, in the light of statistics, is a certain exception to the general picture in Europe. In Finland, productivity growth has been faster than the European average; the volume of R&D expenditure meets the criteria of the Lisbon Strategy, and the number of patents in relation to the population is also quite high, about twice as large as the average in the EU area. Finland's success in increasing productivity and innovation may look exemplary, and there are certainly some of the ways in which it should be of interest to other countries. Very characteristic of Finnish research and technology policy is the long-term development of knowledge and skills. This has all moved from the analysis of individual cases to a broader perspective, looking at the producers of knowledge and knowledge and their users together. One speaks of an innovation system. Finland has pioneered the development of this complex, known as the National Innovation System. In the Finnish innovation system, universities are encouraged to undertake applied research at the highest level in addition to basic research. Relations between companies and universities are particularly fostered, and it has been noted that these contacts are useful for the ongoing renewal of both sides. Although the Finnish innovation system has produced good results, Finland still suffers from the same problems as the other EU countries. Finland's success in the field of ICT technology has focused on a rather narrow sector, mobile communications and, above all, the production of communication technology. Not as good progress has been made in the application of the new technology in various areas of business life as in the production of the technology. An exception to this is the banking sector, where the growth of productivity in Finland has been of the highest international quality. In other relations, Finland's situation is that of the rest of Europe: the use of new technology to improve productivity has not progressed fast enough throughout economic life. The problems therefore lie more in the application than in the production of the technology. In Finland, as in the whole of Europe, d the productivity of the service sectors needs to be improved in particular. If the Finnish example of Europe has something instructive to offer, it is, in my view, that the innovation system must be regarded as a whole d from training to basic research, from basic research to applied research, from research to the production of innovations in cooperation between research institutes and companies d especially those companies, who boldly focus on the commercial use of the innovations. Wim Kok's High Level Group also pointed to such an integrated approach when it stated in its report: "There is no magic wand that can be used to create the stronger growth and jobs that Europe so desperately needs." *** The fact that the productivity of R&D investment in Europe is weaker than in the United States suggests, in my view, that a direct increase in investment, for example from public resources, is not sufficient to solve the existing problem. Boosting innovation-driven growth appears to require changes in the innovation environment. I would like to draw attention to a few things. For the volume and efficiency of product development efficiency, the incentives that affect R&D activity are important. I want to address three interrelated conditions for effective innovation: The innovations must have an extensive and open market area in order for their commercial value to be large. It is necessary to be able to protect the innovations at a reasonable price, in such a way as to minimise the legal uncertainty associated with their protection. Innovations need to be financed in a flexible way in order to realise their commercial potential. It is of interest that all these three conditions of successful innovation are linked to the realization and perfection of the European common market. In my view, one likely reason why European innovation has not quite met the expectations placed on it is that European markets are not sufficiently uniform in terms of innovation. The fragmentation of the markets reduces the commercial value of innovations; the inconsistency of the patent system makes the protection of innovation in the EU fragile and uncertain; and the venture capital sector is too weak and too local. The EU's inability to reach an agreement in the dispute over the Community patent, which has been going on for several years, is particularly worrying. In the current system, the application for a European patent is very expensive, mainly because of the multilingual  translations required, and in addition, disputes over patents in each Member State are upheld. The consequence of this is legal uncertainty. A Community patent could solve these problems. However, as I am sure you are aware, the undertaking failed because of a conflict over languages. Irrespective of the political dimensions of the matter, it is clear that, with regard to the innovation economy, the reduction of patent costs is a key issue for Europe's competitiveness. The financing of investments is a second key issue. Europe clearly needs more investment financing. At the same time, it is clear that one should be able to make greater use of private and independent sources of risk finance. Of course, Europe will continue to need public financing for innovation in the future. But the associated efficiency and competition problems are obvious, and therefore it is essential to develop private European venture capital markets in such a way that financial markets can participate better than before in financing worthwhile innovations. It would be particularly important to get rid of the local limitations of venture capital markets. The expertise required for the investment of venture capital is not local in nature, but is most likely linked to the sector of the project to be financed or the knowledge of the technology to be used. Therefore, it seems logical to build an effective European venture capital system on the basis of industries rather than on a regional basis. It would also be important to develop The European equity markets in such a way that IPO arrangements (initial public offering) can be carried out at a lower cost than before and that new companies have the opportunity to receive capital on a larger scale from the European capital markets. This is necessary, inter alia, to ensure that venture capital investors can sell their investments more easily when the new companies they finance have matured to receive capital from the banks. Increasing the efficiency of European securities markets and, above all, reducing the costs of cross-border trading are therefore also an essential part of the development of financial markets in a more innovation- and investment-friendly direction. Ultimately, companies' investment in innovation and the volume of risk capital required to commercialise innovation depends on the commercial potential that can be offered to new innovations. From this point of view, it is clear that the unification of the European internal market and the removal of barriers to market introduction are the most important factors in promoting innovation and thus boosting the growth of new entrepreneurial activity. The more fragmented the markets are, the smaller the commercial potential of the innovations. The same effect shall be had if there are barriers to market entry in the markets established by authorities or by undertakings in a dominant market position. For these reasons, competition policy and the common market play a crucial role in solving Europe's economic problems. The Services Directive is part of this, but there is much more to be done. *** Ladies and Gentlemen, At present, Europe is in danger of falling into a vicious circle where economic disappointments are slowing down the European integration project, which in turn would further weaken Europe's economic situation. We must now try to break this vicious circle and steer development in a different direction, so that the integration measures for the economy will create a new dynamism, which would do its part to ensure broad political support for European integration. In practice, the solution is to be found in the direction indicated by the Lisbon Strategy, and central to this is the development of the Msrke in the direction that they encourage innovation and new investments based on innovation better than before. Above all, it is about the protection of innovations, their financing and ever more open and uniform markets. Accepting economic renewal and increased efficiency does not mean renouncing the European way of life, but on the contrary, it would offer the best way of preserving this way of life, even in the face of the ageing of the population and global competition. Europe's intellectual and cultural capital creates excellent conditions for participating in the global economy as a constructive rather than a defensive partner. It would be very damaging if our continent's inadequacy in reaching common decisions were to be an obstacle here.

Die bisherige Verwirklichung der Lissabon-Strategie ist in dem im letzten November erschienenen Bericht der hochrangigen Sachverstndigengruppe unter Vorsitz von Wim Kok beurteilt worden. Die Einschtzung des Berichts klingt nicht sehr positiv: "Nachdem nun die Hlfte der Frist bis zum Jahr 2010 verstrichen ist, bietet sich ein recht gemischtes Gesamtbild. Ich mchte auch einige Worte zu dem Fall Finnland sagen, da Finnland in der Innovationsttigkeit und auch im Wachstum der Produktivitt der Industrie eines der Spitzenlnder Europas ist. *** Die Frage nach der Belebung der wirtschaftlichen Wachstumsdynamik Europas wird hufig aus dem Blickwinkel der Produktivitt betrachtet. Zugleich ist Finnland eines von den zwei Lndern, in denen die F&E-Ausgaben der Unternehmen mehr als zwei Prozent vom Wert des Bruttoinlandsprodukts ausmachen. Ein hnliches Bild ber die Unterschiede in der Produktentwicklungsttigkeit in der EU und in den Vereinigten Staaten erhlt man, wenn man die Zahl der angemeldeten Patente betrachtet. Die Amerikaner lassen in ihrem Land doppelt so viel Erfindungen patentieren wie die Europer in ihrem eigenen EPO-System (European Patent Office). In Europa werden fast ebenso viele Patente von amerikanischen wie von europischen Unternehmen angemeldet, aber in den Vereinigten Staaten liegt der Anteil der europischen Erfindungen, die dort patentiert werden, bei weniger als einem Viertel von der Zahl der amerikanischen Erfindungen. Verfolgt man die Wertschpfungskette der Innovationsttigkeit von der Forschung zu den Patenten und von den Patenten zur Umsetzung der Ideen in Produkte, so wird man mit der Frage nach der Finanzierung neuer Unternehmen (Start-ups) konfrontiert. Auch in diesem Bereich ist die Situation in Europa besorgniserregend. Ein Symptom fr die Schwche der europischen Innovationskette ist die Kleinheit der Venture Capital-Mrkte im Vergleich zu den Vereinigten Staaten. Diese Differenz hat sich um ein gewisses Ma ausgeglichen, nachdem im Jahre 2001 die globale IT-Blase geplatzt war. Aber noch immer ist der Unterschied erheblich. Besonders deutlich kommt er zum Vorschein, wenn man die private Venture Capital-Finanzierung betrachtet. Einer neueren Untersuchung zufolge (Ernst & Young LLP und VentureOne 2005) haben im Jahre 2004 die kumulativen Investitionen der europischen Venture Capital-Unternehmen nur einem Viertel von dem Wert der Venture Capital-Investitionen in den USA entsprochen. In Wirklichkeit ist die Differenz zwischen der EU und den Vereinigten Staaten nicht ganz so dramatisch, denn neben privaten Kapitalinvestoren sind an dieser Ttigkeit auch ffentliche Fonds mit beteiligt, deren Bedeutung in Europa grer ist als in den USA. Auf der andere Seite haben Studien belegt, dass die Aktivitt von unabhngigen Kapitalinvestoren im Allgemeinen erfolgreicher ist als die Ttigkeit von Kapitalfonds, die in Verbindung mit Banken agieren oder im Besitz der ffentlichen Hand sind. Die Unterschiede zwischen den Finanzmrkten Europas und der USA bei der Finanzierung neuer Unternehmensttigkeit ist unter anderem in dem gemeinsamen Forschungsnetzwerk "Capital Markets and Financial Integration in Europe" der Zentralbanken des Eurosystems untersucht worden. In dem im letzten Dezember verffentlichten Schlussbericht wird festgestellt, dass das Finanzierungssystem fr Start-ups in Europa schwach entwickelt und schlecht integriert sei, und dies gilt sowohl fr die Ttigkeit der Venture Capital-Investoren als auch fr die IPO-Mrkte fr junge Unternehmen. Die Charakteristika der europischen Innovationskette, die ich oben erwhnt habe, erklren wahrscheinlich zu einem groen Teil, warum das Wachstum der Produktivitt und der Strukturwandel der Wirtschaft in Europa enttuschend gewesen sind. Zusammenfassend kann man festhalten, dass die Innovationsttigkeit in Europa, gemessen an den Investitionen in Forschung und Entwicklung, relativ kleiner ist als in den Vereinigten Staaten, dass aber dazu auch die Aktivitt bei der Anmeldung von Patenten und das Wachstum der Produktivitt der Wirtschaft bescheidener ausgefallen sind. Das weist darauf hin, dass eine Steigerung der Investitionen in Forschung und Entwicklung allein nicht ausreicht, um dieses Problem zu lsen, sondern dass die Angelegenheit in einem greren Zusammenhang zu sehen ist. *** Mein eigenes Land stellt im Licht der Statistiken eine gewisse Ausnahme von dem allgemeinen Bild in Europa dar. In Finnland ist das Wachstum der Produktivitt schneller gewesen als im europischen Durchschnitt; das Volumen der F&E-Aufwendungen erfllt die Kriterien der Lissabon-Strategie, und auch die Zahl der Patente in Relation zu der Bevlkerungszahl ist ziemlich hoch, etwa doppelt so gro wie im EU-Raum durchschnittlich. Obwohl das finnische Innovationssystem gute Ergebnisse gebracht hat, leidet Finnland dennoch unter denselben Problemen wie die brigen EU-Lnder. Der Erfolg Finnlands im Bereich der ICT-Technologie hat sich auf einen recht schmalen Sektor konzentriert, auf die mobile Kommunikation und darin vor allem auf die Produktion von Kommunikationstechnologie. Wenn das finnische Beispiel fr Europa etwas Lehrreiches zu bieten hat, so besteht dies meines Erachtens darin, dass das Innovationssystem als eine Ganzheit zu betrachten ist  von der Ausbildung zur Grundlagenforschung, von der Grundlagenforschung zur angewandten Forschung, von der Forschung zur Hervorbringung von Innovationen in Kooperation von Forschungsanstalten und Unternehmen  vor allem solchen Unternehmen, die sich mutig auf die kommerzielle Nutzung der Innovationen fokussieren. Auf einen derartigen integrierten Ansatz hat auch die High Level Group von Wim Kok hingewiesen, als sie in ihrem Bericht feststellte: "Es gibt kein Zauberstab, mit dem sich das strkere Wachstum und die Arbeitspltze herbeischaffen lassen, die Europa so dringend braucht." *** Der Umstand, dass die Produktivitt der F&E-Investitionen in Europa schwcher ist als in den Vereinigten Staaten, deutet meiner Ansicht nach darauf hin, dass eine direkte Erhhung der Investitionen zum Beispiel aus ffentlichen Mitteln nicht ausreicht, das vorhandene Problem zu lsen. Die Ankurbelung des auf Innovationen gegrndeten Wachstums erfordert offenbar Vernderungen im Umfeld der Innovationsttigkeit. Ich mchte das Augenmerk auf einige Sachen lenken. Fr das Volumen und die Effizienz der Produktentwicklungsttigkeit sind die Ansporne wichtig, die sich auf die F&E-Ttigkeit auswirken. Ich mchte drei miteinander verbundene Bedingungen fr eine effektive Innovationsttigkeit anfhren:  Die Innovationen mssen ein umfangreiches und offenes Marktgebiet haben, damit ihr kommerzieller Wert gro ist.  Man muss die Innovationen zu einem angemessenen Preis schtzen knnen, und zwar in einer Weise, dass die mit ihrem Schutz verbundene juristische Unsicherheit minimiert wird.  Fr die Innovationen muss in flexibler Weise Finanzierung zur Verfgung stehen, damit ihr kommerzielles Potenzial realisiert werden kann. Von Interesse ist, dass alle diese drei Bedingungen einer erfolgreichen Innovationsttigkeit mit der Verwirklichung und Vervollkommnung des europischen gemeinsamen Marktes verbunden sind. Meines Erachtens liegt ein wahrscheinlicher Grund dafr, dass die europische Innovationsttigkeit nicht ganz die auf sie gesetzten Erwartungen erfllt hat, darin, dass die europischen Mrkte hinsichtlich der Innovationsttigkeit nicht gengend einheitlich sind. Die Zersplittertheit der Mrkte verringert den kommerziellen Wert der Innovationen; die Uneinheitlichkeit des Patentsystems macht den Schutz von Innovationen im EU-Raum teuer und unsicher; und der Venture Capital-Sektor ist zu schwach und zu sehr lokal organisiert. Die Unfhigkeit der EU, in dem Streit ber das Gemeinschaftspatent, der bereits seit mehreren Jahren andauert, zu einer Vereinbarung zu kommen, ist besonders besorgniserregend. In dem derzeitigen System ist die Anmeldung eines europischen Patents sehr teuer, vor allem wegen der verlangten mehrsprachigen bersetzungen, und zudem wird in den Streitigkeiten ber Patente in jedem Mitgliedstaat fr sich Recht gesprochen. Die Folge hiervon ist rechtliche Unsicherheit. Ein Gemeinschaftspatent knnte diese Probleme lsen. Wie Sie sicherlich wissen, ist das Unterfangen jedoch an einem Konflikt ber die Sprachen gescheitert. Vllig unabhngig von den politischen Dimensionen der Sache ist es klar, dass bezglich der Innovationswirtschaft die Reduzierung der Patentkosten eine fr die Wettbewerbsfhigkeit Europas zentrale Frage darstellt. Die Finanzierung der Investitionen ist eine zweite zentrale Frage. Europa braucht eindeutig mehr Finanzierung von Investitionen. Zugleich ist es klar, dass man in der Lage sein sollte, private und unabhngige Quellen von Risikofinanzierung verstrkt zu nutzen. Europa bentigt natrlich auch in Zukunft ffentliche Innovationsfinanzierung. Aber die damit verbundenen Effizienz-und Konkurrenzprobleme sind offensichtlich, und darum ist es unabdingbar, private europische Venture Capital-Mrkte zu entwickeln, und zwar in der Weise, dass die Finanzmrkte besser als bisher sich an der Finanzierung von lohnenden Innovationen beteiligen knnen. Besonders wichtig wre es, von der lokalen Begrenztheit der Venture Capital-Mrkte loszukommen. Die Expertise, die fr das Investieren von Risikokapital ntig ist, ist von ihrem Charakter her nicht lokal, sondern hchstwahrscheinlich ist sie mit der Branche des zu finanzierenden Projekts oder der Kenntnis der anzuwendenden Technik verbunden. Von daher erscheint es logisch, ein effektives europisches Venture Capital-System lieber auf der Basis von Branchen als auf regionaler Basis aufzubauen. Es wre ferner wichtig, die europischen Aktienmrkte so zu entwickeln, dass IPO-Arrangements (initial public offering) zu geringeren Kosten als bisher erfolgen knnten und dass neue Untenehmen die Mglichkeit htten, Kapital in grerem Umfang von den europischen Kapitalmrkten zu erhalten. Dies ist unter anderem fr die Sicherung dessen ntig, dass die Investoren von Risikokapital ihre Investitionen leichter verkaufen knnen, wenn die von ihnen finanzierten neuen Unternehmen dazu reif geworden sind, Kapital von den Brsen zu erhalten. Die Effizienzsteigerung der europischen Wertpapiermrkte und vor allem die Reduzierung der Kosten fr den grenzberschreitenden Handel bilden daher auch einen wesentlichen Bestandteil der Entwicklung der Finanzmrkte in eine innovations-und investitionsfreundlichere Richtung. Letztendlich hngen die Investitionen der Unternehmen in die Innovationsttigkeit und das Volumen des Risikokapitals, das fr die Kommerzialisierung der Innovationen erhltlich ist, davon ab, wie gro das kommerzielle Potenzial ist, das man neuen Innovationen bieten kann. Von diesem Standpunkt aus ist es klar, dass die Vereinigung des europischen Binnenmarktes und der Abbau von Hindernissen fr die Markteinfhrung die allerwichtigsten Faktoren fr die Frderung von Innovationen und auf diesem Wege fr die Ankurbelung des Wachstums neuer unternehmerischer Ttigkeit sind. Je zersplitterter die Mrkte sind, umso kleiner gestaltet sich das kommerzielle Potenzial der Innovationen. Dieselbe Auswirkung hat es, wenn an den Mrkten Hindernisse fr eine Markteinfhrung bestehen, die von Behrden oder von in dominierender Marktposition befindlichen Unternehmen errichtet worden sind. Aus diesen Grnden spielen die Wettbewerbspolitik und der gemeinsame Markt eine entscheidende Rolle bei der Lsung der wirtschaftlichen Probleme Europas. Die Dienstleistungsrichtlinie ist ein Teil davon, aber es gibt noch viel mehr zu tun. *** Verehrte Damen und Herren, zurzeit droht Europa in einen Teufelskreis zu geraten, wo wirtschaftliche Enttuschungen zu einem Abbremsen des europischen Integrationsprojektes fhren, was wiederum die konomische Situation Europas weiter schwchen wrde. Man muss nun versuchen, diesen Teufelskreis zu durchbrechen und die Entwicklung in eine andere Richtung zu lenken, so dass man mittels der Integrationslsungen fr die Wirtschaft eine neue Dynamik erhlt, was fr seinen Teil dazu beitragen wrde, der europischen Integration auch eine breite politische Untersttzung zu gewhrleisten. In der Praxis ist die Lsung in der Richtung zu finden, die von der Lissabon-Strategie aufgezeigt worden ist, und zentral darin ist die Entwicklung der Mrke in der Richtung, dass sie besser als bisher zu Innovationen und zu neuen, auf Innovationen basierenden Investitionen anspornen. Es geht vor allem um den Schutz der Innovationen, um deren Finanzierung und um immer offenere und einheitlichere Mrkte. Die wirtschaftliche Erneuerung und Effizienzsteigerung zu akzeptieren bedeutet nicht, dass man auf die europische Lebensform verzichten wrde, sondern dies wrde im Gegenteil die beste Mglichkeit bieten, diese Lebensform zu erhalten, auch angesichts der Alterung der Bevlkerung und des globalen Wettbewerbs. Das intellektuelle und kulturelle Kapital Europas schafft ausgezeichnete Voraussetzungen dafr, an der globalen Wirtschaft als ein konstruktiver und nicht als ein defensiver Partner teilzunehmen. Es wre ein groer Schaden, wenn die Unfhigkeit unseres Kontinents, gemeinsame Beschlsse zu fassen, hier ein Hindernis bilden wrde.

Title: Bank Manager Sinikka Salo's speech at the opening of the Snellman and Markka of Finland exhibition at the Bank of Finland Money Museum
text: Speech by Bank Director Sinikka Salo at the opening ceremony of Snellman and the Finnish Markka at the Bank of Finland's Monetary Museum . Speech . Tuesday 10 January 2006,12:00 AM Good listeners! It is a great pleasure for me to welcome you to the Bank of Finland's Monetary Museum "Snellman and the Finnish Markka", with which the Bank of Finland wants to participate in the celebration of Snellman's 200th birthday. It was designed by our researchers: Licentiate Vappu Ikonen and Dr Juha Tarkka. J.V. Snellman is actually a Finnish institution whose literary output of about 15,000 pages covers all areas of elsms. Snellman was a champion of the Finnish idea, a philosopher, a journalist, a professor and a senator. Hsn was born in 1806, five years earlier than another Finnish institution, the Bank of Finland, founded in 1811. The Snellman and The Finnish Markka nsyttelysss, which is now being opened, has focused on the meeting between Lshinns Snellman and the Bank of Finland in the 1860s, when the Snellman Treasury Board's psllikksns led the Finnish markka to the silver standard. Due to his diverse merits and, above all, as a stabilizer of monetary conditions in Finland, Snellman has got his image persti on two banknotes and is also guarding his statue of the Bank of Finland. In connection with the statue, the Bank of Finland wants to honour J.V. Snellman's elsmsntysts myss by publishing a thesis on the statue and its origins by Master Mari Tossavainen, which the author will present in a moment. *** Snellman's importance in stabilising monetary conditions in Finland is a good thing to follow the development of monetary conditions in Finland since the bank of Finland was founded in 1811. In 1809, the Bank was established by the Porvoo State Council, which became the Grand Duchy of Vensjs. Even after the establishment of the Bank of Finland, the monetary conditions in Finland have been shining for a long time due to the circulation of Swedish money in the country. The symmetry of Swedish money in Finland did not succeed until monetary realization in 1840. After that, rouble banknotes and silver coins were the only legal means of payment in Finland and monetary conditions stabilised. Preparations for own mark and own mark 1860 Finland enjoyed stable monetary conditions only fifteen years after the monetary realization of 1840. Finland's monetary conditions were rebuilt by the Crimean War, which was fought between Vensjsn and Turkey in 1854d1856. Great Britain, France and Sardinia fought as Turkey's allies against Vensjss. During the Chechen War, the Anglo-French fleet ksvi destroying fortifications also off the coast of Finland in the so-called "war zone". In the Ooland War and bombed Viapori off Helsinki. Due to the war, the redemption of rubles with silver was discontinued in finland. The value of the ruble began to decline and the silver coins began to circulate. The depreciation of money and the consequent movement of silver change caused difficulties for the whole of Finnish society. In Czech Finland, the question of a return to the silver standard was raised in several quarters. Chechnya was not yet persuaded, but Alexander II issued a declaration on 4.4.1860, by which Finland received its own monetary unit. According to it, the Value of the Finnish Markka was fourth of a ruble. Since the paper money was also accepted as legal payment in Finland, the value of the markka fluctuated with the ruble. The key official in obtaining the markka was not Snellman, but the then finance committee's pssllikks Fabian Langenskisld. J.V. Snellman was on the committee. In the Senate, Langenskisld acquired his own monetary unit for Finland and worked to restore the silver standard. However, Tys was interrupted by Langenskisld's death in 1863. Under Snellman's leadership towards the Silver Mark in 1865 After Langenskisld's death, Snellman became the head of the Treasury Board. The principle of implementing the silver standard had been obtained from St. Petersburg in 1862. In order to obtain the necessary silver, Finland took out a large loan from M.A. Rothschild's brokerage firm in Frankfurt. However, the loan had to be used to finance grain imports, so the silver standard was delayed. J.V. Snellman continued his efforts in the midst of the lost to tie the mark to silver. So, on November 4, 1865, Alexander II issued a decree stating that only silver coins (mark and ruble) were legal payments in Finland. The markka could be decoupled from the epsvakaa banknote ruble. Finland had returned to the silver standard and received its own national monetary system. Two monetary reforms d the same pssmsss Snellman is therefore not the iss of the mark, but rather the merit belongs better to Fabian Langenskisld, but rather to the stabilizer of the markka. In the monetary reform of 1865, the value of the markka was stabilized by joining the international silver-headed monetary system. It is precisely this that is at the heart of Snellman's monetary policy activities. The same monetary stability and accession to the European monetary system were pursued more than 130 years later, when Finland tied the value of the markka to the euro in the 1990s and then abandoned the markka as money. The anti-Nazi event, i.e. the renunciation of the mark, was therefore carried out in the same autumn as the changeover to the mark. We can imagine that Snellman, who is flexible in economics and has a flexible and flexible approach to economics, would certainly have blessed the reform as well. *** Thank you for your interest and ask you to get acquainted with "Snellman and the Finnish markka".

Title: Speech by Bank Director Sinikka Salo at a seminar on the experience of Austria and Finland as members of the EU and monetary union
text: Speech by Bank Director Sinikka Salo at a seminar on the experiences of Austria and Finland in the eu and monetary union, Central Bank of Austria . Speech . Monday16 January 2006, 12:00 AM The EU and the euro have brought stability and flexibility to the Finnish economy (summary) Finnish-language summary of a speech by Sinikka Salo, Bank Director, at a seminar on the experiences of Itsvalla and Finland in the eu and monetary union Bank Director Sinikka Salo analysed Finland's experience of the EU and the importance of monetary union at a colloquium organised by the Central Bank of Austria. The seminar is part of the programme of the EU Presidency of the Council of the EU and the next Finnish Presidency, which has just begun. According to Bank President Salo, the experience of the past decade in the EU is very positive for Finland: all the expectations placed on it in the Union and monetary union. Finland's economic development has been favourable and fairly stable despite the large fluctuations in the global economy. The question of the so-called epssymmetric shocks, that the abandonment of the national currency deprives the possibility of a nationally calibrated monetary and exchange rate policy, spoke to economists and politicians before the end of the year, but the problem with the post-accession economic policy and economic policy debate has become a problem. In fact, during the period of prosperity, the cyclical fluctuations of the Finnish economy have clearly synchronised with the other euro area countries, although these fluctuations have been steeper than in the average in the euro area. When Finland joined the European Union, it was just recovering from the biggest economic recession in its history. For years, Finland had been struggling with inflation and, as a result, high interest rates and ever-dwindling competitiveness, which was improved by devaluations. From the beginning of the inflation-devaluation cycle, it was clear that Finland would also be among the first to seek monetary union. Salo stressed that one of the reasons for the positive development was that confidence in the value of money and monetary policy had increased in line with the ECB's self-position and the monetary stability objective assigned to it. In recent years, inflation in Finland has remained below the euro area average, at times below it. The existence of monetary union has also protected the Finnish economy during international crises, and the fiscal policy pursued by the state has not faced any problems arising from emu. In fact, Finland's public finances have strengthened and are currently among the strongest in the euro area. Another factor that has contributed to the economic recovery has been that competition in the EU has, as expected, increased, which has led to falling consumer prices in many sectors. In two areas, developments have not met expectations: at the time of the agreement, it was thought that the share of EU partners in Finland's trade would increase and that the mobility of labour in Finland and other EU countries would increase. This has not been the case, and Salo speculated that the reason was not only the recent slow growth of the euro area and the remaining obstacles to the functioning of the stra market, such as problems with payment transactions between countries. In addition, globalisation has directed Finland's trade towards countries outside the EU. Migration to Finland has been quite high, which is worrying considering that there is already a shortage of power in many sectors in Finland. Pankinjohtaja Salon mukaan kuluneen vuosikymmenen kokemukset EU:sta ovat Suomelle hyvin mynteiset: jsenyys unionissa ja rahaliitossa nyttvt lunastaneen lhes kaikki asetetut odotukset. Suomen talouskehitys on ollut suotuisaa ja varsin vakaata huolimatta maailmantalouden suurista vaihteluista. Ns. epsymmetrisiin shokkeihin liittyv kysymys, ett kansallisesta valuutasta luopuminen vie mahdollisuuden kansallisesti mitoitetulta raha-ja valuuttakurssipolitiikalta, puhutti ekonomisteja ja poliitikkoja ennen jsenyytt, mutta liittymisen jlkeisess talouspolitiikassa ja talouspoliittisessa keskustelussa ongelma on jnyt kytnnss vhiseksi. Itse asiassa nytt, ett jsenyyden aikana Suomen talouden suhdannevaihtelut ovat selvsti synkronoituneet muiden euroalueen maiden kanssa, joskin vaihtelut ovat meill olleet jyrkempi kuin euroalueella keskimrin. Kun Suomi liittyi Euroopan unioniin, se oli juuri toipumassa historiansa suurimmasta talouslamasta. Vuosikausia Suomi oli krsinyt sitkest inflaatiosta ja sen seurauksena korkeista koroista ja jatkuvasti hiipuvasta kilpailukyvyst, jota parannettiin devalvaatioilla. Pstkseen eroon inflaatio-devalvaatiosyklist oli alusta lhtien selv, ett Suomi pyrkisi mys rahaliittoon ensimmisten joukossa. Salo korosti, ett yksi syy mynteiseen kehitykseen on, ett luottamus rahan arvoon ja rahapolitiikkaan on kasvanut EKP:n itsenisen aseman ja sille annetun rahanarvon vakaustavoitteen myt. Viime vuosina Suomen inflaatio on pysynyt lhell euroalueen keskiarvoa, ajoittain alittanut sen. Rahaliiton jsenyys on mys suojannut Suomen taloutta kansainvlisien kriisien aikana, eik valtion harjoittama finanssipolitiikka ole kohdannut mitn EMU.jsenyydest johtuneita ongelmia. Itse asiassa Suomen julkinen talous on vahvistunut ja se on nykyisin euroalueen vahvimpia. Toinen taloutta tervehdyttnyt tekij on ollut, ett EU-jsenyyden myt kilpailu odotetusti lisntyi, mik on johtanut aleneviin kuluttajahintoihin monella sektorilla. Kahdella alueella kehitys ei ole vastannut odotuksia: Jsenyytt solmittaessa ajateltiin, ett EU-kumppanien osuus Suomen kaupasta kasvaisi ja tyvoiman liikkuvuus Suomen ja muiden EU-maiden vlill lisntyisi. Nin ei ole kynyt, ja Salo arveli syyn olevan paitsi euroalueen viime aikoina hitaan kasvun ja viel jljell olevat sismarkkinoiden toiminnan esteet, kuten maiden vlisen maksuliikenteen ongelmat. Lisksi globalisaatio on suunnannut Suomen kauppaa EU:n ulkopuolisiin maihin. Muuttoliike Suomeen on ollut varsin vhist, mik on huolestuttavaa ottaen huomioon ett vestltn nopeasti ikntyvss Suomessa jo nyt on pulaa tyvoimasta monilla sektoreilla. Eik tt tehd epitsekkist syist, vaan vasta-vuoroisuuden merkeiss ja yhteisten etujen vuoksi. *** Kun puhutaan talouspolitiikan kansainvlisest koordinaatiosta, ei useinkaan viitata siihen talousjrjestelmn perusrakennetta kehittvn yhteistyhn, jonka piirteit olen edell kuvannut, vaan ymmrretn talouspolitiikka paljon suppeammassa mieless, lhinn suhdannepolitiikkana. Nin ajateltuna talouspolitiikan kansainvlinen koordinaatio tarkoittaisi raha-ja finanssipolitiikan kansainvlist yhteensovittamista. Tst aiheesta on aika ajoin keskusteltu paljonkin sek tutkijoiden ett talouspolitiikan tekijiden keskuudessa, mutta kytnnn tulokset ovat olleet paljon laihempia kuin ne, mit on saatu markkinoiden toimintaa tukevalla instituutioiden rakennustyll. Raha-ja finanssipolitiikan koordinointitarve nousee kansainvlisen politiikan asialistalle ymmrrettvsti silloin, kun maailmantaloudessa nhdn uhkaavia tasapainottomuuksia, joiden korjaaminen vaatisi useamman eri osapuolen yhteisi tai samanaikaisia toimia. Tllainen tilanne syntyi mm. ensimmisen ljykriisin jlkeen 1970.luvulla. Toinen kansainvlisi koordinointipyrkimyksi herttnyt tapaus oli vuoden 1987 prssiromahdus. Kummassakaan tapauksessa kansainvlinen talouspoliittinen yhteisty ei tuottanut kovin hyvi tuloksia. Tll hetkell merkittvin tasapainottomuus on Yhdysvaltain valtiontalouden ja vaihtotaseen jttilisminen alijm, jonka vastapuolena on eriden kehittyvien maiden, ennen muuta Kiinan maksutaseen samanaikainen ylijm. Raha-ja finanssipolitiikan globaalia koordinaatiota koskevat keskustelut kydn yleens ns. G8 -ryhmien piiriss, joihin kuuluvat taloudelliselta painoarvoltaan suurimmat maat. Suurimpien demokraattisten teollisuusmaiden johtajien vuotuiset huippukokoukset aloitettiin vuonna 1975 Ranskan Rambouillet'ssa, tllin maita oli kuusi. Sittemmin mukaan tuli Kanada ja nyt uusimpana jsenen Venj, joten nykyisin puhutaan yleens G8-ryhmst. Talouspolitiikan koordinaation kannalta yht trkeit kuin huippukokoukset ovat ryhmn valtiovarainministerien ja keskuspankkien pjohtajien kokoukset, joita on jrjestetty 3-4 kertaa vuodessa, siis useammin kuin huippukokouksia. Tuorein esimerkki talouspolitiikan koordinointipyrkimyksist G7-ryhmn piiriss on tlt vuodelta. Kokoontuessaan viime huhtikuussa Washingtonissa G7-maiden valtiovarainministerit ja keskuspankkien pjohtajat hyvksyivt yhteisen yhteenvedon siit, millaista talouspolitiikkaa maailmantalouden nykyisten tasapainottomuuksien ratkaiseminen vaatii Yhdysvalloilta, Euroopan mailta, Japanilta ja kehittyvlt Aasialta, erityisesti Kiinalta. Tss yhteydess ei ole mahdollista menn yksityiskohtiin, mutta suositusten yleispiirteet on kuitenkin syyt todeta, sill ne ehk kuvaavat G7/G8 koordinaation luonnetta. Yhteisess julkilausumassaan ministerit totesivat ensinnkin, ett osapuolet vastaavat yhdess maailmantalouden tasapainottomuuksien ratkaisemisesta, ja ett kaikkien alueiden on osallistuttava siihen. He totesivat mys, ett tm vaatii sstmisen ja investointien sek niihin liittyvien pomanliikkeiden uudelleen suuntaamista maailmassa, ja ett vallitsevat tasapainottomuudet olisi paras ratkaista kestvn talouskasvun olosuhteissa, mik vaatii talouspolitiikan vahvistamista. Kytnnn toimista julkilausuman liitteess todettiin seuraavaa: Yhdysvaltojen pitisi jatkaa ponnistuksia budjettialijmns supistamiseksi ja sstmisen lismiseksi Euroopassa olisi tehtv enemmn ty-ja hydyke-ja palvelumarkkinoiden joustavuutta lisvi uudistuksia ja tuettava kotimaisen kysynnn elpymist Japanissa olisi tehtv enemmn taloudellisen elpymisen varmistamiseksi ja pitkn aikavlin kasvuedellytysten luomiseksi rakenteellisten uudistusten avulla Kehittyvss Asiassa, erityisesti Kiinassa, tarvitaan valuuttakurssien nykyist suurempaa joustavuutta, kotimaisen kysynnn lismist ja rahoitussektorin vakauden vahvistamista ljy tuottavissa maissa tarvitaan lis investointeja tuotantokapasiteettiin, talouksien monipuolistamista ja eriss tapauksissa mys valuuttakurssien suurempaa joustavuutt Nm johtoptkset ovat varmasti oikeaan osuneita ja ainakin useimmat niiden mukaiset toimenpiteet toivottavia. Samalla lausumista ky kuitenkin hyvin ilmi, kuinka tavattoman yleisluontoista G7/G8 koordinaatio kytnnss on. Vain poikkeustapauksissa maat ovat psseet tsmlliseen sopimukseen joistakin konkreettisista yhteisist toimista esimerkiksi valuuttamarkkinoilla. Kokoukset eivt tietenkn ole merkityksettmi, mutta G7/G8  ryhmn toimintaa ei kuitenkaan voi pit osoituksena mistn globaalin raha-ja finanssipolitiikan tiiviist koordinaatiosta. On vaikeata mitata sit, kuinka suuri vaikutus G7/G8 koordinaatiolla on siihen osallistuvien maiden talouspolitiikkaan. Vaikeudet ovat tietysti tmn tapaisessa tilannesidonnaisessa koordinaatiossa viel merkittvsti suuremmat kuin kansainvlisiss sopimusneuvotteluissa esimerkiksi WTO:n piiriss, jossa pyritn sopimaan kaikkia koskevasta pelisnnist tulevien tilanteiden varalle. Juoksevan talouspolitiikan koordinaatio suvereenien kumppanien kesken on hieman kuin keskusteltaisiin korttipelin snnist sen jlkeen, kun kortit on jo jaettu. Niiden tutkimusten mukaan, joita G7-kokousten vaikutuksista on tehty, kokousten ptkset ovat toteutuneet parhaiten silloin, kun ne ovat koskeneet suurvaltojen toimintaa monenkeskisiss kansainvlisiss instituutioissa, kuten WTO:ssa tai Kansainvlisess Valuuttarahastossa. Tehokkaimmin G7/G8 koordinaatio siis ehk toimii epmuodollisena valmistelukoneistona monenkeskisten instituutioiden ptksille. Sit paitsi G8:lla on luottamusta ja tiedon vaihtoa edistvn foorumina tietysti erittin suuri poliittinen merkitys. Samalla G8-instituutio tietenkin jakaa maita "sispiirilisiin" ja muihin, mik ei ole aivan ongelmatonta. Se Washingtonin kokouksen julkilausuma, johon sken viittasin, osoittaa, ett maailmantalouden tasa.painottomuudet eivt ole vain G8-maiden sisisi kysymyksi. Erityisesti Kiinan merkitys maailman-taloudessa ja mys sen nykyisten tasapanottomuuksien osapuolena on suurempi kuin monien G8-ryhmn jsenten. Se, ett taloudellisesti trkeimmt osapuolet eivt ole ryhmss mukana, tietenkin heikent G8-ryhmn asemaa koordinaatiokeskustelujen foorumina. Yh useammin koordinaatiotapaamisia jrjestetn mys laajemmassa piiriss, kuten ns. G20-kokoonpanossa. Kokoonpanon kasvulla on kuitenkin huonotkin puolensa: sit mukaa kun maiden lukumr kasvaa, epmuodollisen ryhmn kyky keskustella, sopia ja toimia heikkenee. Vaarana voi mys olla trkeiden monikansallisten instituutioiden kuten WTO:n ja Kansainvlisen Valuuttarahaston faktisen merkityksen rapautuminen. Yksi G7/G8 ryhmn toimintaan jo lhtkohtaisesti kuuluva piirre on, ett ryhmn voivat aktiivisesti osallistua vain taloudelliselta merkitykseltn suurimmat maat. Thn on ymmrrettvt perusteet. Toisaalta pienten maiden kannalta olisi trke, ett niidenkin nkkulma tulisi huomioon otetuksi globaalissa talouspoliittisessa keskustelussa. Suomen ja muidenkin EU:n pienten jsenten kannalta ongelmaa helpottaa se, ett EU:lla on (jo vuodesta 1977 alkaen) ollut edustus G7kokouksissa. Vuodesta 1999 alkaen mys Euroopan Keskuspankki on ollut mukana valtiovarainministerien ja keskus-pankkien pjohtajien kokouksissa. EU:n edustajien velvollisuutena kokouksissa on edustaa EU:n elimiss yhteisesti ptettyj linjauksia, ja nist ptettess mys pienet EU-maat kuten Suomi ovat voineet olla mukana. EU:n edustus G8 -koordinaatiossa on Suomen kannalta erittin arvokas asia, eik sit pid vheksy. Realismin vuoksi on kuitenkin todettava, ett tll edustuksella tuskin on kovin suurta G8-ptksi legitimoivaa vaikutusta pieniss EU-maissa. Miten EU kokonaisuudessaan saataisiin paremmin kytketty globaaliin talouspoliittiseen vuoropuheluun? Joskus on esitetty EU-edustuksen yhdistmist, niin ett nykyisten neljn jsenmaan ja EU:n sijasta unionilla olisi yksi yhteinen edustus G8:ssa. Tt ajatusta on esitetty varsinkin Yhdysvalloissa, koska siklisest nkkulmasta Euroopan maiden suuri osanottajamr nytt oudolta, varsinkin kun voidaan odottaa Intian ja Kiinan jsenyyden G-kerhossa tulevan jossakin vaiheessa ajankohtaiseksi. Ajatus EU:n yhteisest edustuksesta G-ryhmss on kuitenkin poliittisesti ilmeisen eprealistinen, vaikka EU-maat ovatkin jo perustamissopimuksessa sitoutuneet keskiniseen talouspoliittiseen koordinaatioon, vaikka EU:lla on yhteinen kauppapolitiikka, ja vaikka G8-maista Italia, Ranska ja Saksa kuuluvat euroalueeseen ja niill on mys yhteinen rahapolitiikka. EU ei ole liittovaltio, eik talouspolitiikka kokonaisuudessaan kuulu EU:n kompetenssiin, vaikka sopimusten mukaan jsenmaiden kuu-luukin pit talouspolitiikkaa yhteisten intressien piiriin kuuluvana asiana. Sit paitsi G8 kokouksissa keskustellaan varsinaisen talouspolitiikan lisksi monista muistakin sellaisista kysymyksist, jotka eivt ole EU:n kompetenssin piiriss. EU-maiden yhteistoiminnan ja yhteisen edustuksen ongelmat eivt koske vain G8-kokouksia, vaan mys kansainvlisi jrjestj kuten Kansainvlist Valuuttarahastoa. Tss tilanteessa pienten EU-maiden kannalta ilmeisesti paras ja realistisin ratkaisu olisikin pyrki EU:n sisisen koordinoinnin tehostamiseen ja yhteisen kannanmuodostuksen lujittamiseen mahdollisuuksien mukaan. Tm vhentisi G8-koordinoitiin pienten jsenmaiden kannalta liittyvi legitiimisyysongelmia ja ehk lisntynyt yhtenisyys mys lisisi Euroopan kannanottojen vaikuttavuutta. Tehokkaat neuvottelut edellyttvt kuitenkin mys reagointikyky. Sit tarvitaan kantojen yhteensovittamisessa ja kompromissien teossa. EU:n koordinaation tiivistmisen kytnnn ongelmana ei siis ole vain yhteisten positioiden lytminen, vaan kyky esiinty yhtenisen ja luotettavana neuvotteluosa-puolena. Tm on merkittv haaste, joka viime kdess johtuu EU-maiden haluttomuudesta list unionin kompetenssia kansainvlisess talouspoliittisessa koordinaatiossa. *** Aloitin tmn puheenvuoroni Chydeniuksella ja Snellmanilla. Olen koettanut perustella sit ajatusta, ett talouspoliittinen suvereenisuus ei ole itsetarkoitus, vaan lhtkohta globaalin kanssakymisen edellytysten rakentamiseksi. Tss hengess minun varmaan sopii lopettaa siteeraamalla Thomas Hobbesia, joka eli noin 100 vuotta ennen Chydeniusta. Hobbes pohti "Leviathanissa" suvereenisuuden luovuttamisen ongelmaa, ja ptyi kuvaamaan luonnontilaa, kaikkien sotaa kaikkia vastaan, seuraavin sanoin: "No arts; no letters; no society; and which is worst of all, continual fear and danger of violent death; and the life of man, solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short ". Tm kuvaus sopisi mys kansallisvaltioiden vlisiin suhteisiin, jos ne kaikissa olosuhteissa tinkimtt tahtoisivat varjella toiminta-vapauttaan. Globalisaatio osoittaa, onneksi, ett nin ei ole ollut.

Title: Annual Bank of Finland/CEPR Conference "Credit and the Macroeconomy"
text: Member of the Board Sinikka Salo: Annual Bank of Finland/CEPR Conference "Credit and the Macroeconomy" . Speech . Thursday2 November 2006,12:00 AM OpeningRemarks byDr Sinikka Salo,Member of the Board,in the 7thAnnual Bank of Finland/CEPR Conference: "Credit and the Macroeconomy" I am very pleased and honoured to welcome you all to Helsinki, and to this CEPR and Bank of Finland joint Conference "Credit and the Macroeconomy". This annual event takes place now for the 7th time, which may also be regarded as a proof of fruitful cooperation between our two institutions. We at the Bank of Finland appreciate highly the work of CEPR's network of researchers and its cooperation with the central banks, and I am happy to confirm that we at the Bank are committed to maintain and foster this cooperation also in the future. As many of you may know, the Bank of Finland has long traditions in research, and research plays a crucial role in our strategy according to which we aim at being oactive member of the Eurosystemo. In the newly approved strategy for next three years this is again confirmed and strengthened. We have attempted to alternate the CEPR/Bank of Finland conference themes between macro topics and financial markets topics. This year's theme is perhaps somewhere in between, but mostly, the papers which will be discussed in this year's conference are more or less linked to the paradigm of modern dynamic macroeconomics. The DSGE.models, in which optimizing agents households and firms interact in an environment of rigidities, provide laboratories in which one can address normative issues of optimal policy design. According to Professor Gali, the current generation of DSGE models have contributed to policy in several important ways: 1) They offer new insights into the transmission process of monetary policy. 2) They force model builders to think more carefully about underlying sources of economic disturbances, and this has led to a better appreciation that the simple dichotomy between demand and supply shocks is not enough for policy analysis. Instead, one must understand the nature of the disturbances and whether they lead to inefficient fluctuations. 3) These models provide model-consistent measures of the output gap relevant for policy. 4) These models provide grounds for welfare-based policy . more specifically, the design of policy rules . giving new insights into the costs of inflation and the appropriate objectives of stabilization policy. As a consequence, a veritable explosion of policy relevant research has taken place, one in which both academic economists and central bank research economists are active participants. It is no wonder that central banks in particular are interested in these models, and are trying to adopt these models for a practical use in policy evaluationas you may know here at the Bank of Finland, the focus of one of our three research programmes has already for some time been DGE models, and their use in policy. We have set the goals of this programme in a very ambitious way to work for the integration of financial markets and their imperfections into these models! This agenda is behind our specific interest in this years' topic. In all areas of research we naturally need joint efforts, in particularly in the area of DSGE development, where cooperation between academic and central bank researchers like in this conference, is crucial. This conference is also important in fostering European contribution to this work where research on the other side of the Atlantic is perhaps more advanced and has a wider base. I find it extremely valuable that we in Europe are able to work together, for example, to study the models that hopefully give us better understanding on the very topical puzzle of current rapid credit expansion. The current credit expansion in double digits . is taking place in the Euro area regardless of rising interest rates and a reasonably low level of current and expected inflation? Should we worry or not? Perhaps this question cannot be definitely answered for good in the context of this conference, but it certainly highlights the importance of this year's theme. On behalf of the whole Board of the Bank of Finland, I wish your conference the best success in your important work.

Title: Opening of the Bank of Finland Money Museum exhibition "A Century of Banking Advertising"
text: Bank Director Sinikka Salo at the opening ceremony of the Bank of Finland's Monetary Museum "A century of bank advertising" 9.1.2007 . Speech . Tuesday 9 January2007, 12:00 AM Good listeners! I would like to welcome you all to the opening ceremony of the bank's new bank advertising exhibition at the Monetary Museum of finland. Vappu Ikonen, Jaakko Koskentola, Antti Kuusters and Teemu Taskinen have been responsible for the planning and compilation of the material. Lsmmin thank you to all of them. I think they have been very successful in their work and have created an ensemble that is both fun and thought-provoking. This has been made possible by the fact that several banks have voluntarily provided the Money Museum with their own marketing material. I would particularly like to thank the representatives of the banks for their good cooperation. The main reason why this kind of advertising is interesting is that advertising is an effective reflection of the times. The nature of each period comes out in the advertisements in some way condensed, it seems that even in a caricatured form. As early as the 1960s, the media philosopher Marshall Mc Luhan speculated that the advertising of our time would in the future be the best window for historians into the way of thinking and thinking of modern man. In addition to the actual message, the advertisements also tell a lot about the values, attitudes and wishes of their time. It is precisely bank advertising that is of particular interest among the types of advertising because, as shown by this, it touches with extraordinary depth on the fundamental issues of the economy: income and economic security, on the one hand, and the hopes and objectives of the people who want to be realised or by borrowing, on the other. In banking advertising, nskyy also a change in values: advertisements have moved from appealing to a sense of duty to the realization of elsms's pleasures. In my opinion, the key word in this is change. sms change nskyy on many levels. Nsyttelysss highlights the transformation of Finnish society from an old agricultural society to a modern consumer society. The transformation of the Finnish financial markets from the period of ssnnsstely to a free market economy. And a lot has also changed about how a Finnish bank customer - a farmer, a wage earner, a student or an investor d has been interviewed and addressed at different times. As the world changes, the emphasis on ethics and the construction of security for the future in advertisements take a back seat. "First sshshshch, then a loan," it used to be said. Now, in their marketing, banks are investing more in financing consumption instead of ssssss. It can be said that, in the light of the advertisements, consumption has changed from a vice to a permitted pleasure that does not have to wait, but can be enjoyed when it suits you by borrowing money. I do not want to condemn the change or moralise. Credit d and also consumer credit d has tsrkes and hysdyllis tehsvss. And it is a good thing that a private person in need of a loan does not have to feel that he or she is in the position of an administrative subordinate when dealing with a bank or elsewhere, but that credit negotiations are a normal business matter. With a loan, households can spread the costs of large, exceptional purchases over a longer period of time. A loan can also be used to cover a loss of income known as a farm. Credit, wisely used, is therefore a good thing, and therefore I do not want to condemn the marketing of credits. In order to function well, the loan market needs healthy competition and, therefore, advertising. However, the current marketing of consumer credit is also accompanied by obvious things that may be of concern to the public. When you look at marketing, you cannot get the impression that consumer credit is currently being sold, often through very aggressive campaigns, to people who are either in financial difficulties or whose level of financial knowledge is not particularly good. Loans are marketed from a position in which the seller has an overwhelming information advantage over the often inexperienced and even the most thoughtless customer. In the context of household indebtedness, mortgages are most often referred to, but recently the growth of household consumer credit has also accelerated quite rapidly. And if you look at the conditions under which households take out loans, many consumer loans are in a league of their own. According to the data available, almost 8% of households have experienced debt servicing difficulties, and there are currently about 300,000 people in Finland whose credit history includes a payment note. In recent years, the mssrs of households marked as Maksuhsiris has remained relatively stable, despite the exceptionally low market interest rates and the employment situation has been rapidly improving. In particular, the cost of unsecured consumer loans to the borrower is very high compared to prevailing market interest rates. Sopss credit card companies market household appliances, furniture, etc. in connection with purchases, credit with a current annual percentage rate of charge often exceeds 20%. Unsecured internet credit is marketed at an APR of approx. 15%. The highest interest rates are. in the so-called ksnnykksvipeisss, which are apparently sold more in Finland than in other EU countries. According to a study carried out last summer by the Financial Supervisory Authority, the annual percentage rate of charge on such loans can be several hundred per cent. This is very expensive money, and you may ask which customer group the expensive credit is for. Creditworthy or uncreditworthy? For the wise or the thoughtless? I will answer it for your consideration. The Finnish law does not require the annual percentage rate of charge for a loan of less than 3 months or a very small amount, but last autumn's Advisory Board for Economic Management recommended that the APRC be indicated when marketing loans of this kind. The borrower should also be informed of the penalties to be imposed if he is unable to repay his loan on time. According to the old anecdote, you can get a loan from a bank if you can prove that you don't need it. Of course, things shouldn't be crazy, but it's hardly a good idea to go to a completely different ssrilait, where you can borrow money from a customer's situation. In banking and financial activities in general, I believe that responsibility for customers is of greater importance than in many other industries. I would compare banks and financial institutions in relation to, for example, the lssksre or the lssk industry. In the same way that we require that the customer act in the best interests of his patient, it would also be required of the credit provider not to seek the benefit of the customer, but to act in such a way that the customer does not have to regret the decisions made. The spirit of popular education in the oldest bank advertisements seems patronising and certainly amusing to modern people. There is no going back to that world. But it would be a good idea for citizens from a young age to learn how to correctly assess their own borrowing potential d the risks of borrowing d and the difficulties that may arise from the payment process. The school system, the central bank and other authorities have a lot to do. And even in bank advertising, one could invest a little more in the informationality of the present d not only the obligatory, small printed text? Our campaign is open until the end of September. Welcome once again!
text_original: Pankinjohtaja Sinikka Salo Suomen Pankin rahamuseon nyttelyn "Vuosisata pankkimainontaa" avajaisissa 9.1.2007 . Speech . Tuesday 9 January2007, 12:00 AM Hyvt kuulijat! Toivotan teidt kaikki tervetulleiksi Suomen Pankin Rahamuseon uuden, pankkimainontaa ksittelevn nyttelyn avajaisiin. Nyttelyn suunnittelusta ja aineiston kokoamisesta ovat vastanneet Vappu Ikonen, Jaakko Koskentola, Antti Kuuster ja Teemu Taskinen. Lmmin kiitos heille kaikille. Minusta he ovat onnistuneet erinomaisesti tehtvssn ja luoneet kokonaisuuden, joka on yht aikaa sek hauska ett ajatuksia herttv. Nyttelyn on tehnyt mahdolliseksi se, ett useat pankit ovat ystvllisesti antaneet Rahamuseon kyttn omaa markkinointiaineistoaan. Haluan erityisesti kiitt mys pankkien edustajia hyvst yhteistyst. Tllaisen nyttelyn kiinnostavuus johtuu ennen kaikkea siit, ett mainonta heijastaa tehokkaasti aikaansa. Kunkin ajanjakson luonne tulee mainoksissa esiin jollakin tavalla tiivistyneess, vlill tuntuu, ett jopa karrikoidussa muodossa. Mediafilosofi Marshall Mc Luhan arveli jo 1960-luvulla, ett aikamme mainonta muodostaa tulevaisuudessa historioitsijoille parhaan ikkunan nykyajan ihmisen elmntapaan ja ajatusmaailmaan. Mainokset kertovat varsinaisen viestins ohella paljon mys aikansa arvoista, asenteista ja toiveista. Ehk juuri pankkimainonta on mainonnan lajien joukossa erityisen kiinnostavaa, koska niin kuin tm nyttely osoittaa, se koskettelee poikkeuksellisen syvlt elmn peruskysymyksi: yhtlt toimeentuloa ja taloudellista turvallisuutta, toisaalta ihmisten toiveita ja tavoitteita, joita sstmll tai lainaamalla halutaan toteuttaa. Pankkimainonnassa nkyy mys arvomaailman muutos: mainoksissa on siirrytty velvollisuudentuntoon vetoamisesta elmn nautintojen toteuttamiseen. Minusta tmn nyttelyn avainsana onkin juuri muutos. Tm muutos nkyy monella tasolla. Nyttelyss tulee esiin suomalaisen yhteiskunnan muutos vanhasta maatalousyhteiskunnasta moderniksi kulutusyhteiskunnaksi. Siin nkyy Suomen rahoitusmarkkinoiden muutos snnstelyn kaudelta vapaaseen markkinatalouteen. Ja paljon on muuttunut mys se, kuinka suomalaista pankkiasiakasta -maanviljelij, palkansaajaa, opiskelijaa tai sijoittajaa  on eri aikoina lhestytty ja puhuteltu. Maailman muuttuessa sstmisen etiikan korostaminen ja tulevaisuuden turvan rakentaminen jvt mainoksissa vhitellen taka-alalle. "Ensin sst, sitten laina", sanottiin ennen. Nyt pankit panostavat markkinoinnissaan yh enemmn kulutuksen rahoittamiseen sstmisen asemesta. Voi sanoa, ett mainosten valossa kulutus nytt muuttuneen lhes paheesta sallituksi nautinnoksi, jota ei tarvitse odottaa, vaan josta voi rahaa lainaamalla nauttia silloin kun se itselle sopii. En halua tt muutosta tuomita enk moralisoida. Luotolla  ja mys kulutusluotolla  on trke ja hydyllinen tehtvns. Ja on hyv, ett yksityisen lainantarvitsijan ei tarvitse tuntea olevansa hallintoalamaisen asemassa pankissa tai muualla asioidessaan, vaan ett luottoneuvotteluissa on kysymys normaalista liikeasiasta. Lainalla kotitaloudet voivat jakaa isojen, poikkeuksellisten hankintojen kustannukset pitemmn ajan kuluessa maksettaviksi. Ehk lainalla voidaan mys peitt tilapisiksi tiedettyj tulonmenetyksi. Luotto, viisaasti kytettyn, on siis hyv asia, enk siksi halua tuomita myskn luottojen markkinointia. Hyvin toimiakseen lainamarkkinat tarvitsevat tervett kilpailua ja nin ollen mys mainontaa. Nykyiseen kulutusluottojen markkinointiin liittyy kuitenkin mys ilmiit, joita voi pit huolestuttavina.
