In the Czech situation, the German mark proved to be a particularly strong and stable currency d not because of the large size of the German economy, but also because of the skilfulness of German monetary policy and the position of the Bundesbank itself. As European countries gradually began to integrate their monetary policy, the German mark became the de facto anchor of the European monetary system. And when the single central bank was set up and the changeover to the single currency, the structure of the European System of Central Banks and the principles of its monetary policy reflected the German experience and efforts to transfer the confidence enjoyed by German monetary policy to the new single currency and bank. Changes in international monetary conditions usually take place over a period of decades d as was once the case with the dollar and the pound sterling. The current use of the euro is more or less proportional to the size of the euro area. Compared to other Czech currencies, the euro is used more than the Japanese yen in world trade and on the world financial markets, but more than the US dollar. The euro continues to have a stronger regional label than the US dollar, but the euro has already emerged alongside the US dollar as the second currency adopted worldwide. One of the ways in which the currency is becoming international is through the international circulation of banknotes and coins. The US dollar is known to be the world's most common international currency. According to surveys, up to 60% of the dollar bill is in circulation outside the United States. Eurochete is not exactly internationalized. The euro banknote is currently in circulation for a total of about 650 billion, and some time ago it was estimated that there would be approximately 100 billion in euro area. Although the international usage of the euro is growing, the dollar is still growing at around 3:1. Incidentally, it should be pointed out that, outside the member countries of the euro area, the euro is also a pocket currency in Montenegro and Kosovo and, of course, also in European mini-states such as Monaco, San Marino and the Vatican. The use of the euro has become more common internationally not only as banknote money, but also as an investment currency for the foreign exchange reserves of central banks. The foreign exchange reserves of the world's central banks have been growing rapidly in recent years, especially in the rapidly developing economies of Asia, but also in the countries producing sljy and other raw materials. China and Vensjs are good examples. As foreign exchange reserves have grown, there has been interest in risk diversification and diversification of assets into different currencies. However, as an international reserve currency, the euro still has a long way to go. The euro accounts for only a third of the amount of foreign exchange reserves invested in dollars. I expect the share of the euro to increase in the future. In the international foreign exchange market for banks and large companies, the euro is, of course, also one of the main currencies. It's clearly number two right after the dollar. According to a study carried out two years ago, dollars were used throughout the world to trade in foreign exchange for the average of almost 800 million psivssss. Approximately half of the euros were traded, with 420 million psivitch. The Japanese yen and the British pound were already clearly smaller in terms of exchange. In its 10 years of existence, the euro has thus established itself on the international financial markets. It is clearly the world's second Cherkes currency. A real world currency, given the requirements for such a currency, will not be a rival to the euro and the dollar for a long time yet. Many observers have speculated that in the future there will be an increase in the importance of an Asian currency. However, this would probably have more of a regional significance in the beginning. Is the internationalisation of the euro? The introduction of the euro in the world outside the euro area is not an end in itself. The use of euro banknotes outside the euro area is sufficient for euro area countries to obtain interest-free loans from euro countries. Despite this, there are no specific objectives for the international role of the euro area within the central banks of the euro area. The policy is that the ECB does not seek to promote the growth of the role of the euro as a world currency. However, the spread of the euro has the meaning that it is a symptom value. The euro will be spread internationally if the monetary policy of the euro area is sound and if the euro area economy develops favourably. As Europeans, we are primarily interested in nsist issues. It has not been possible to clear the balance of what factors determine the success of currencies in international currency. However, it is generally accepted that the success factors are the large size and prosperity of the currency area, free and stable financial markets, a successful monetary policy and the political stability of the country(s) issuing the money. In the light of the above factors, the euro, as an international currency, has two significant advantages in particular, namely the large and expanding business area and the stability and monetary policy pursued by the European Central Bank. As noted, the euro area is one of the world's largest economies with growth potential in terms of the growth rate. Total output in the euro area is almost as high as that of the United States (about 75% of total US production in PPS) and clearly more than double that of Japan. The figures reflecting the weight of the euro area in the global economy will be strengthened if and when additional EU member countries join the euro area in due course. As EU countries succeed in reforming their economies to make them more flexible, innovative and competitive, Economic growth in Europe and the economic base of the euro could be considerably strengthened. A large number of projects are so-called. On the agenda known as the Lisbon Strategy. But the euro is not a complete project. It is unfinished, at least in relation to the level of development and uniformity of the euro area's financial markets and payment systems. I will mention just two topical issues, namely banking supervision and payment transactions. As the banks and financial markets of the euro area countries become more closely interlinked, on the other hand, what is being pursued threatens banking supervision and its future development unless new cooperation structures are created to strengthen and develop cooperation between national authorities. This is necessary to ensure the stability on which confidence in the euro has been built and on which it will continue to be based in the future. Another area of development is payment. The euro area will not be a truly unified market until payments flow smoothly from one Member State to another as they now do in the estuary of each Member State. The aim is that payments from Germany to Finland (and on the other hand!) could take place using exactly the same methods and methods as domestic payments. And that's why you'll be able to keep a lot of money, rents, etc. in the hands of a very private person. as well as commercial payments by companies. This is the aim of the ongoing SEPA (Single Euro Payment Area) project, which will run in 2010. The project is a reality for the citizens of the euro area, and it will continue to be a project for each other, even if we live in different parts of Europe. If the SEPA project is successful, it will also contribute to supporting the international status of the euro as a good payment currency. Ladies and gentlemen! Like tango dancers, the d euro needs stability and flexible mobility in order to succeed. It will receive stability from a common and credible monetary policy of the ECB, flexibility and mobility must be brought to the economies of the euro area countries through a forward-looking reform policy. Although the floor of the world economy is sometimes slippery, and its rhythm changes often yllstsvis, balance and cooperation are pushed forward by d myss in monetary policy!

Onko euron kansainvlistymisell vli? Euron kytn lisminen euroalueen ulkopuolisessa maailmassa ei ole mikn itsetarkoitus. Eurosetelien kytt euroalueen ulkopuolella hydytt kyll euroalueen maita sikli, ett saamme ikn kuin korotonta lainaa euroja kyttvist maista. Euro prj ja levi kansainvlisesti, jos euroalueen rahapolitiikka on hyv ja jos euroalueen talous kehittyy suotuisasti. Eurooppalaisina me olemme kiinnostuneita ensisijaisesti nist asioista. Nm euroalueen painoarvoa maailmantaloudessa kuvastavat luvut vahvistuvat viel, jos ja kun euroalueeseen aikanaan liittyy lis EU:n jsenmaita. Se on keskenerinen ainakin siin suhteessa, mit tulee euroalueen rahoitusmarkkinoiden ja maksujrjestelmien kehitystasoon ja yhtenisyyteen. Tm on tarpeen sen vakauden varmistamiseksi, jolle euron luottamus on rakentunut ja jolle se tulevaisuudessakin perustuu. Toinen kehityskohde on maksaminen. Title: State of financial markets and development prospects
text: Bank Manager Sinikka Salo: State and development of the financial markets, Kouvola . Speech . Friday 15August 2008, 12:00 AM THE STATE OF THE FINANCIAL MARKETS AND DEVELOPMENTKYMI BANK MANAGER SINIKKA SALO'S SPEECH TOIVO-TALOUSTALKOOT . ECONOMIC SEMINAR IN KOUVOLA The point of my analysis is international and European, since the financial markets are last global. This also shows that the us subprime mortgage market started just over a year ago in the financial markets around the world. I shall therefore begin by commenting on the recent problems of the international financial markets and their ideas. The financial market is also of great importance to Finland, although fortunately Finland has been overcome by its own problems. The nature of free financial markets includes a tendency towards their occasional hsiris, even outright crises. It is obviously difficult to learn from it, but you can try to learn from it. I will also briefly discuss the role and potential of monetary policy in the conditions of the hsiristila conditions of the financial markets. Finally, I would like to mention the process of integration of the European financial markets and the opportunities it offers. *** On recent financial markets Risks and their realisation are an integral part of the functioning of financial markets. Reasonable d less severe d hsiristilas are even thought to be hysdyllis: they are considered to be healthy risk awareness. This is one of the ways in which the market mechanism corrects its own problems. The perceived and interconnected state of the financial markets cannot be considered a normal, healthy fluctuation. Its duration and depth are a matter of conjecture, but the hsiristila will calm down in time. Now is the time to analyse the causes of the crisis and discuss how to improve the resilience of the financial markets in the future. Background to the financial market hsiristila In recent years and decades, the debt ratios of households and non-financial corporations have generally increased in the global economy and also in Finland. The development is a positive development and reflects the financing of the development. Competition in financial markets has led to longer maturities, a reduction in interest margins, while advances in risk diversification and technology have enabled banks to operate profitably in conditions of reduced margins. At the same time, there have been problems with the strong growth in funding. As the credit portfolio has grown, credit risks have increased. At the same time, risk pricing has been shaky. In the middle of last year, at the threshold of financial markets, the risks in international financial markets were so low that the situation was widely regarded as untrue: pricing in financial markets could not reflect the genuine cost of risk. The relatively light financial conditions that have continued for years played a part in underestimating the risks. There were good reasons for this financing conditions: among other things, the shift of production to low-cost countries pushed world trade prices down, and in order to deflation, central banks considered interest rates to be relatively low. As the general level of interest rates declined in the financial markets, a lot of finance had to seek investment targets from one of the riskier investments in order to achieve the usual level of returns. As a result, the quality of investments and debt material deteriorated. The most obvious example is provided by the partly reckless mortgage lending in the United States, and it is the instigator of the crisis. In the problems of the US housing market, the securitisation of mortgages played a key role. The securitisation of mortgages means the aggregation, packaging and sale of individual mortgages as securities. In many cases, a multi-tiered chain was formed between the bank and the final investor, in which the value papers resulting from the packaging of mortgage loans were repackaged two or three times into more exotic securities. Risk diversification through secondary market trading and derivatives is a sinsnss mysnteists, but there are many problems associated with its uncontrolled use: 1. Incentives to monitor creditworthiness deteriorate. When a bank also credits someone else knows that the credit risk is borne by someone else, the risk assessment is not drawn up with the same care as if the risks were paid out of one's own purse. 2. The risk of risk and its use in different situations is reduced. When a security is transferred from the originator to the appraiser and the credit to the latter market investors, even in a multi-tiered transfer, the investor is in a weak position to form an informed assessment of the risk characteristics of the security resulting from the last package. Credit risk assessment relies heavily on a limited number of credit rating agencies. There was too much confidence in the risk ratings; The risk of complex securities by the rating agencies also proved to be weak. The ratings were built on the historically probable nature of households in different financial positions falling into a state of solvency under normal economic conditions. It was not possible to assess the credit risks associated with the perceived stagnation of the housing market. Even fine math doesn't help if genuine initial risk assessments are flimsy. 3. There has also been much criticism of the bonus system of MFIs. A typical feature of many investments is that the returns are front-loaded, but the risks are strongly back-loaded. If an investment person is rewarded in such a way that the premiums focus on the initial returns but not on the potential losses over the period, then the risk to the financial institutions and the economy as a whole will be substantial. That's exactly what happened last year. The bonus systems of many of the international banks facing problems are beyond reasonable limits in terms of their advantages. 4. Securitisation was used not only for risk management, but also, apparently, for circumventing the prudential requirements imposed on banks by the authorities. The solvency ratios imposed on banks set limits on the amount of risky loans that banks can hold on their balance sheets. Ersst banks are transferred to off-balance-sheet investment companies. Although the investment companies have been formally independent of the banks, the banks have had to guarantee their activities. Thus, the transfer of securities the outside world has not hedged the banks against their risks. It is not the case that strong financial growth and underpricing of risks led to market shocks. When the risk is taken, some of it will eventually be realised. On the impact of the crisis After the start of the market, the risk premiums rose sharply. In recent times, banks have paid up to 5% of their borrowing in excess of their margins. What is more remarkable is how the crisis has not exactly turned out to be in queer: the risk has risen for everyone. The risk in the interbank market, which before the crisis was a few per cent to one hundredth of a percent, has increased to one percent. There are hardly any safe havens, the perceived risky players, in the financial markets. This situation reflects the certainty of the distribution of risks, which has not materialised even after a year and which is considered to be common to both market participants and the authorities. In part, the international hsiris has also been widely reflected in the Finnish financial markets, although there have been no problems with banks. The significant increase in the risk premiums included in Euribor rates has also affected Finland as part of the euro area. This has led to an increase in the interest rates of many Finnish debtors that monetary policy has not sought. However, it appears that the overall level of financial risks in Finland and the euro area is fairly firmly under control. The world economy is growing rapidly and the profitability of productive enterprises is generally good. Although hsiris has affected all financial market players in developed countries, only a small percentage of them are struggling with serious financial problems. What lessons can be learned from the crisis in terms of the management and supervision of the financial markets? A wide range of questions have already taken shape, but the search for answers has only just begun. One obvious question concerns the future of securitisation. Although the problems associated with securitisation are the core of the securitisation process, securitisation is not categorically condemned or attempted to stop. If properly used, securitisation is an effective tool for bank funding. It enables the diversification of risks from the banking sector to funds, investment funds and others. By securitisation, e.g. the systemic risk in the housing market can be spread over more and stronger shoulders, and thus improve the financing system. Of course, this does not mean that it does not need to be done. In the future, securitisation will be able to be carried out in a way that incentives for responsible behaviour do not lead to the kind of excesses experienced in the United States. Products should be standardized in umsrrettsvssn form, the underlying debt securities should be well applied to the mssriteledjs kriteerejs. In Europe, securitisation in most countries is still in its infancy, so that systems can be built to be better on a country-by-country basis. The broader question is how to deal with innovation in the financial markets. The emergence and wild growth of securitisation in the United States is one example in a series of innovations in the financial markets that, time and time again, bring the financial markets into unexplored waters. There will also be new products in the future, the operation of which will not initially be understood by tsys. This kind of innovation cannot be attempted by means of shunting. Instead, it is necessary to ensure that the risks arising from innovation do not threaten the infrastructure of the financial markets and, in particular, to safeguard the stability of deposit banks. In relation to chechnya, financial market authorities in many countries are the subject of serious debate. Many deposit banks, including in Europe, had acquired large positions in US subprime securities without the supervisory authorities having any knowledge of this. And even if the authorities had all the necessary information, you can ask whether the supervisor would still have understood the risks associated with these investments before they began to materialise in the middle of last year. The debate will also concern the possible needs for a new situation. It will be necessary to consider ways in which deposit banks d the back of the financial markets d are able to protect themselves from the storms of the financial markets. Could it be possible to build better security barriers around deposit banks and to steer the investment activities of deposit banks in a way that would guarantee the ability of supervisors to ensure the solvency of banks? In the history of the financial markets, there have been stages in which deposit banking and investment banking have been separated by law. In this model, deposit banks are safe havens on the financial markets for the funds of ordinary depositors, while investment banks can be used to seek better returns for those who have the will and ability to bear the risk. Radical reforms are unlikely to be repeated. Nevertheless, the lessons of the past year must be carefully weighed. We are still having to think about the structures for the management and supervision of the financial markets. Banks facing solvency problems in the financial markets, such as Northern Rock in England, have been acting nationally, and in each case the national authorities have acted quickly to calm the situation. Euro area banks operating internationally have not experienced similar difficulties. There are reasons to be particularly satisfied, as the supervision of the financial markets in Europe has not become more international at the same rate as banking, but that the supervisory and crisis management structures have remained national for a long time. Cooperation with the national authorities has certainly been developed, but it is still clear that if a heavily internationalised euro area bank were to run into difficulties, there would soon be a whole range of unresolved liability issues. Hsiris has once pointed out how tsrkess is that the management and supervision of financial markets evolves with the financial markets. Role and potential of monetary policy The strength of the global economy and increased demand have increased inflationary pressures on many greeks, particularly in food. Inflation has risen everywhere, but particularly strongly in key developing countries such as China. The rise in food prices has been accentuated in relatively high-value countries, in addition to China, in Europe, where the weight of food is high in the consumer price index. Nevertheless, the rise in food prices has also provoked more reactions, especially among low-income groups. What makes this situation particularly problematic is that the rise in inflation coincides with the financial markets' hsirs. Monetary policy will have to curb inflation in a context of severe financial markets and economic growth has clearly slowed down. However, the room for manoeuvre of central banks is relatively small. In the current situation, decoupling inflation would, at most, bring about a very short-term easing of the problems of the financial markets and macroeconomics. If longer price stability is allowed to crumble, the higher costs of correcting it in due course. Thus, the monetary policy of the European Central Bank is also calibrated during the period of financial markets from the angle of price stability. At the same time, the ECB has actively used other instruments to de-escalate financial market conditions. In particular, the ECB has secured the liquidity of the financial markets and thus prevented the escalation into an acute financial market crisis. In the future, more attention will also have to be paid to the reliability of financial markets in the preparation of monetary policy. The ability of the financial system to function is obviously a condition for the sound and predictable functioning of the monetary policy framework and the mechanism of monetary policy. Financial market heirst makes it very difficult to calibrate monetary policy. There are also limits to the possibilities of central banks in dealing with financial market crises. Central banks can support the liquidity of the financial markets, but they cannot deal with the solvency problems of MFIs - that is a matter for the stability authorities and the Finance Ministers. What's changing Why, then, will change as a result of the current crisis? The activities of financial institutions have already become d at least for some time d more cautious. In terms of interest rates, risk premiums have risen and credit conditions have been tightened in many countries. This is shown, among other things, by the surveys published in the euro area on the credit conditions of MFIs. In part, this is a healthy development, but there is a risk that caution will go too far. For the time being, however, there is no obvious sign of overcautiousness. The situation of an ordinary Finnish bank customer will probably not change substantially due to the current crisis. There are no deep-seated problems with the Finnish funding system for a while. However, the important question relates to reference rates, including: Euribor rates commonly used in Finland and the euro area. I have already referred to this; In the case of EURIBOR, the risk borne by banks from each other has become prohibitively high. A similar problem has characterised the libor rates quoted in London, which are commonly used as reference rates for credit and deposits around the world. This has given rise to a wide-ranging debate on the appropriateness of such reference rates. It is difficult to say where the development will lead. Certainly not to the disappearance of euribor and libor rates, but not to the loss of their importance. The market will certainly develop some of the alternative reference rates. Central banks generally do not interfere in reference rate systems, although in the past the Bank of Finland administers helibor rates quite exceptionally. It is likely, however, that euri-bor and libor rates are gradually stabilising, presumably with a higher risk for banks. On the integration of financial markets Finally, a few words on the integration of European financial markets. One might think of a more opportune time to talk about the european integration of the financial markets. In times when international financial markets are in the throes of prolonged turbulence, the risks of integration may be lower. However, it should be noted that, even under turbulence, EMU has ensured a fairly stable operating environment for the Finnish banking sector. Although there has been a storm around the country, the ship has been so large that there has been no need to capsize it. EMU, Europe's Economic and Monetary Union, is not a complete project. Monetary policy is common in the euro area, and the interbank market for banks is fragmented. In many other respects, we are only halfway there, or even at the beginning of the journey. The single currency and the single financial market are the reasons why the EU is part of the EU's wider single market project. A single market cannot be achieved in a fragmented financial market: there will be no fair competition if national borders make payment transactions more difficult. Similarly, the fragmentation of the local market means that, for example, the availability of risk finance may vary from country to country. The US financial markets provide a good example of the financing opportunities that developed financial markets offer to companies. Enterprise-based companies and the innovations they have carried out, the commercial hysdynchy of inventions, have had a considerable impact on the country's continued strong economic competitiveness. U.S. companies have been supported by active and skilful investors who, in addition to providing funding for the start-up, also provide management support and at the same time control the companies. Indeed, there is a broad consensus among economists, business leaders and political psschists that a vibrant investment activity is one of the key factors in the country's innovation. In the same way, it is widely believed that the weakness of local investment activity is the cause of the weakness of Europe's economic dynamics. The per capita supply of at-risk alcohol in Europe has been roughly only about a fifth of that of the United States. Efforts to increase the supply of risk finance in Europe are welcome. However, it is worth noting that the financial markets form a whole and that, for example, the heyday of foreign investment in the United States is largely based on the functioning of other segments of the financial market. I will give just one example: the prospects of profitably exiting investments made have a significant impact on the willingness of investors to invest and to build new investments. The development of private investment activities will therefore also depend on how well the financing system generates exit opportunities. The exit takes place, for example, by listing on the resin. In a small number of national financial markets, the possibilities for exiting from the market are limited. This is well illustrated by a study by the Institute for Economic Development (ETLA), according to which domestic financial markets do not meet the exit needs of local investors. It is clear that the integration of European and financial markets would offer significant opportunities in this respect. The fragmentation of banking supervision, which I mentioned by Mr sske, also makes it difficult to compete in the field of banking services internationally and through the banking sector. If the progress of European integration were a direct reflection of the importance of the common interests of the Member States, common financial supervision would probably have been in place a long time ago. The period of turbulence and confidence in the financial markets experienced in recent summers is a reminder that the financial markets' ideas about national stability and national means of achieving it do not correspond to the reality of the situation. In the financial sector, a model of supervision based on the home country principle is not enough. (After all, the home country principle means that if, for example, even a large bank operating in Finland becomes a branch of a foreign bank, the financial supervisory authority of the foreign home country is responsible for its supervision, of course in cooperation with the Financial Supervisory Authority of the Foreign Home State, in cooperation with the Financial Supervisory Authority of Finland, the oissnts stateo). There is a need for integrated European financial supervision. If there are major problems and political problems, the issue will not go off the agenda until further steps are taken in the field of integration. In all the regions, integration is progressing in stages: SEPA, the single European payments area, will gradually become available, making it as easy to pay in the euro area as it is in Finland by the end of 2010. Resin activities are even integrated globally. Cross-border settlement of securities becomes cheaper when the so-called "cross-border settlement" is completed. The TARGET2S project is a reality. The structures of banking supervision and crisis management are discussed in many for a. The development and convergence of financial markets will continue to be at the heart of eu economic policy cooperation. The integration of nationally segmented financial markets into one well-functioning and secure European financial market provides a good example of economic policy cooperation within the FRAMEWORK of the EU, but which is of great importance for the future. The seamless legislation of the Commission, the Member States d and the European Parliament in the Council of the EU d and the European Parliament is a very important piece of legislation. The European Central Bank and the entire European System of Central Banks (ESCB) d and, as part of it, the Bank of Finland d are also involved in the development process. (The basic tasks of the ESCB include, for example, promoting the proper functioning of payment systems.) Of course, the key to this is the self-determination of the various parties involved in the financial markets to develop the European market. It should also be noted that the objective of financial market integration is not to approve banks or other financial markets. The aim of financial market integration is to facilitate the functioning of the EU's enrolment market, to provide EU companies with a wider domestic market and to compete. The last few years support the competitiveness of EU businesses and the purchasing power of its citizens. In conclusion, I would like to remind you of the czech and successful eu integration process as a whole and of the successes that are the result of hope and volunteerism. Last year marked the 50th anniversary of the Treaty of Rome, which marked the beginning of a historically unique process of economic and political integration on our continent. While the ultimate objectives of securing peace and prosperity in Europe have remained the same, the process has been driven by changes in the economic and political environment. Koroissa nkyvt riskilist ovat nousseet ja luotonannon ehtoja on monissa maissa selvsti kiristetty. Tt osoittavat mm. euroalueelta julkaistut, rahalaitosten luottoehtoja koskeneet kyselytutkimukset. Tavallisen suomalaisen pankkiasiakkaan tilanne ei varmaankaan nykyisen kriisin vuoksi oleellisesti muutu. Suomen rahoitusjrjestelmss ei ole syvllisi ongelmia tll hetkell. On kuitenkin syyt huomata, ett turbulenssin oloissakin EMU on turvannut Suomen pankkisektorille varsin vakaan toimintaympristn. Vaikka ymprill on myrskynnyt, on laiva ollut niin suuri, ettei ole tarvinnut pelt sen kaatumista. EMU, Euroopan talous-ja rahaliitto, ei ole projektina valmis. Rahapolitiikka on euroalueella yhteinen, ja pankkien vliset interbank-markkinat ovat posin yhdentyneet. Monelta muulta osin ollaan vasta puolitiess tai jopa matkan alussa. Yhdysvaltain rahoitusmarkkinat tarjoavat hyvn esimerkin rahoitusmahdollisuuksista, joita kehittyneet rahoitusmarkkinat tarjoavat yrityksille. Yhdysvaltojen yrittjyytt ovat tukeneet aktiiviset ja taitavat pomasijoittajat, jotka sen lisksi, ett tuovat alkavaan yritykseen rahoitusta, mys tarjoavat liikkeenjohdollista tukea ja samalla kontrolloivat yrityst. Ekonomistit, yritysjohtajat ja poliittiset ptksentekijt ovatkin varsin yksimielisi siit, ett elinvoimainen pomasijoitustoiminta on maan innovatiivisuuden trkeimpi avaintekijit. Samalla tavoin uskotaan laajalti, ett pomasijoitustoiminnan heikkous on Euroopan talous-dynamiikan heikkouden trke syy. Riskipoman tarjonta asukasta kohden on ollut Euroopassa karkeasti ottaen vain noin viidennes Yhdysvaltain tasosta. Toimet riskirahoituksen tarjonnan lismiseksi Euroopassa ovat tervetulleita. Pienill kansallisilla rahoitusmarkkinoilla irtaantumis-mahdollisuudet vistmtt ovat rajalliset. Tm kvi hyvin ilmi Elinkeinoelmn tutkimuslaitoksen (ETLA) selvityksest, jonka mukaan kotimaiset rahoitusmarkkinat eivt vastaa pomasijoittajien irtaantumistarpeisiin. Selv on, ett Euroopan poma-ja rahoitusmarkkinoiden yhdentyminen tarjoaisi merkittvi mahdollisuuksia tss suhteessa. Mys sken mainitsemani pankkivalvonnan hajanaisuus vaikeuttaa pankkisektorin kansainvlistymist ja sit kautta kilpailua pankkipalvelujen alalla. Jos Euroopan integraation eteneminen heijastelisi suoraan jsenmaiden yhteisten intressien merkitsevyysjrjestyst, yhteinen rahoitusvalvonta olisi varmaan toteutunut jo kauan sitten. Vheksymtt thn liittyvi suuria kytnnllisi ja poliittisia ongelmia, asia ei poistu agendalta ennen kuin integraatio tllkin alalla ottaa uusia askelia. Kaikilla nill alueilla integraatiokehitys on kynniss: Yhteiseurooppalainen maksualue SEPA kynnistyy vaiheittain tehden maksamisen euroalueella yht helpoksi kuin Suomen sisll vuoden 2010 loppuun menness. Rahoitusmarkkinoiden kehittmisty ja stelyn yhtenistminen on vastedeskin EU:n talouspoliittisessa yhteistyss keskeisell sijalla. Kansallisesti lohkoutuneiden rahoitusmarkkinoiden yhdis-tmisty yksiksi hyvin toimiviksi ja turvallisiksi eurooppalaisiksi rahoitusmarkkinoiksi tarjoaa hyvn esimerkin siit EU:n puitteissa tehtvst erittin trkest, mutta paljolti nkymttmiin jvst talouspoliittisesta yhteistyst, jolla on tulevaisuuden kannalta suuri merkitys. Komission, jsenvaltioiden  ei vhiten EU:n neuvostossa  ja Euroopan parlamentin saumaton lainsdntty on tss erittin trke. Mys Euroopan keskuspankki ja koko Euroopan keskuspankkijrjestelm (EKPJ)  ja sen osana Suomen Pankki  ovat mys mukana kehitystyss. (EKPJ:n perustehtviin kuuluu esimerkiksi maksujrjestelmien moitteettoman toiminnan edistminen.) Kytnnss luonnollisesti keskeisi ovat rahoitusmarkkinoiden eri osapuolten omaehtoiset toimet Euroopan markkinoiden kehittmiseksi. On mys huomattava, ett rahoitusmarkkinoiden yhdentymisen tavoitteena ei ole hydytt pankkeja tai muita rahoitusmarkkinatahoja. Rahoitusmarkkinoiden yhdentymisell pyritn edesauttamaan EU:n sismarkkinoiden toimintaa, tarjoamaan EU:n yrityksille laajemmat kotimarkkinat ja yhtliset edellytykset kilpailla. Viime kdess nin tuetaan EU:n yritysten kilpailukyky ja kansalaisten ostovoimaa. Etenkin pienten ja keskisuurten yritysten kannattaisikin mielestni list ponnistelujaan Keski-Euroopan laajojen ja vauraiden mark-kinoiden valloittamiseksi. *** Hyvt kuulijat Tmn seminaarin otsikko korostaa toivoa ja taloustalkoita. Thn teemaan liittyen haluan yhteenvetona esitykseni lopuksi muistuttaa meit koko EU:n integraatioprosessin trkeydest ja onnistumisista, jotka ovat seurausta toivosta ja talkoista. Viime vuonna tuli kuluneeksi 50 vuotta Rooman sopimuksen solmimisesta, joka kynnisti historiallisesti ainoalaatuisen taloudellisen ja poliittisen yhdentymisprosessin maanosassamme. Kuluneina vuosikymmenin integraatio on sykleittin syventynyt ja laajentunut. Tll hetkell demokraattisten valtioiden muodostamassa EU:ssa asuu 450 miljoonaa ihmist, joista 320 miljoonaa euroalueella. Vaikka perimmiset tavoitteet, rauhan ja hyvinvoinnin turvaaminen Euroopassa, ovat pysyneet samoina, prosessin kyttvoimana ovat olleet taloudellisessa ja poliittisessa ympristss tapahtuneet muutokset. Eurooppalainen agenda on heijastanut aikaansa: integraation syveneminen alkoi hiili-ja tersteollisuudesta ja eteni sitten maatalous-ja kauppapolitiikkaan. Viime aikoina huomiota on kiinnitetty esimerkiksi kor-keakoulutukseen ja tutkimukseen: Bologna-prosessi tht yhteisen Euroopan laajuisen korkeakoulutusalueen luomiseen. Mit tulee rahatalouden yhdentymiseen, se on kuulunut osana eurooppalaiseen integraatiostrategiaan jo Rooman sopimuksen alkuajoista asti, joskin konkreettisemmat asiat, kuten kaupan rajojen ja ihmisten liikkumisen esteiden poistaminen olivat alkuaikoina selkesti sit keskeisempi. Kun yhteinen raha, euro vihdoin 10 vuotta sitten otettiin kyttn  ensin tilivaluuttana ja sitten konkreettisesti setelein ja kolikkoina  takana oli paljon toivoa ja talkootyt. Tt toivoa ja talkoohenke tarvitaan edelleenkin, jotta edell esille tuomiani rahoitusmarkkinoiden kehitysnkymi ja haasteita voidaan vied eteenpin tavoitteena Euroopan laajuiset yhteniset rahoitusmarkkinat. Euroopan rahoitusmarkkinoiden integraatio on vlttmtnt tyden hydyn saamiseksi sismarkkinoista. Rahoitusmarkkinoiden integraatio on siten keskeinen rakennuskivi EU:n jsenmaiden sopimassa Lissabonin strategiassa, jossa tavoitellaan EU:n talouden dynaamisuutta, uusia ja parempia typaikkoja  vaurautta ja kansalaisten hyvinvointia  kilpailun globalisaation myt lisntyess.

text: Bank Manager Sinikka Salo Seinsjoki -Lakeuden Brussels seminar opening speech in Seinsjoki . Speech . Friday 5September 2008,12:00 AM EUROPEAN CULTURETI... N FINNISH DEPARTMENT (EKSO) JRJESTM SEMINAR SEINJOELLA 5.9.2008 Dear general! Good etels ostrobothnians, the inhabitants of the province of my birth, and also those who came from elsewhere! Welcome to our seminar! The task of the European Department of Culture and Culture Finland (EKSO) is to produce speeches for citizens' dialogue on the diversity of European culture in order to identify and strengthen the European roots of our own culture and traditions. EKSO is a citizens' forum founded in 1969, which operates with the support of community and personal contributions and seminar-specific sponsors. I would therefore like to express my sincerest thanks to all our supporters at the outset of the programme leaflet. *** In addition to technological know-how, the economic development and well-being of modern societies is also built on cultural know-how. Europe's successes are therefore also based on Europe's strengths: a rich cultural base and the stability and social cohesion of European societies d cohesiveness. Nsin myss in Finland, and tsslls in Etels-Ostrobothnia. In Ostrobothnia, for example, the company is considered to be typically Ostrobothnian: In Ostrobothnia, the company is relatively more numerous than in the rest of Finland, and at least in my childhood in Etels-Ostrobothnia, for example, the foundation of a new house or barn or other building was always made "ksksllss", only then the responsibility for the construction was transferred entirely to the owner of the building. The desire to help the neighbor d "toiskalainen" d to get started has, in my opinion, been a great ostrobothnian co-op. The programme of the seminar has also been strongly built on the connection between and noticing the strengths of enterprise and distinctive culture. This is an enterprise, so the timing of the seminar has been successful. But even the people of Etelshtes are not alone in a globalising market d neither Finland nor any other European country d why we want to stick to the best of the European economic and social model and the rich culture. Being European involves diversity d being different d but a certain commonality is needed. Indeed, the core idea of European integration has been to link the democratic states and peoples of Europe to each other on issues where there is a common policy. A vibrant EU is a globalisation strategy for Europeans and therefore needs to be taken care of. There is a need for an open public debate on the challenges facing the EU, on the ability of its administration to act after enlargement, on its competitiveness. The EU cannot go forward against the will of its citizens. The will depends on citizens being more aware of the EU's achievements and opportunities for the common good. As a matter of profession, I would like to remind you of the success of the euro. Our common currency, the euro, is a great achievement which is now celebrating its 10th anniversary. It is somewhat paradoxical that the euro is the most popular in the EU in our country, even though polls show that we are less inclined towards the EU itself. Without the EU, there would be no euro. The euro d and its common monetary policy d is unquestionably a success story and a sign of a strong will to integrate, to nurture the vitality of our continent. Even in the context of global financial turbulence, EMU has ensured a fairly stable operating environment for the Finnish banking sector. Although there has been a storm around the country, the ship has been so large that there has been no need to capsize it. EMU, Europe's Economic and Monetary Union, is not a complete project. Monetary policy is common in the euro area, but in many other respects we are only halfway or even at the beginning of the journey. But even now, the stability brought about by the euro and the integration of European financial markets will improve the functioning of the U and euro area internal markets, also providing small and medium-sized enterprises in Ostrobothnia with growth opportunities in an enlarged domestic market of more than 450 million inhabitants. Companies would do well to increase their potential. The success of the single currency proves that the will to integrate and the central confidence of the Member States are, after all, quite strong. It is good to remember the times when European integration was once again facing headwinds as a result of the Irish people's referendum. *** Ladies and gentlemen, The challenges of the EU, business and culture issues are discussed at our seminar, where we have managed to gather a fine group of not only local influencers, but also experts from Etelstrobothnia d and so as not to become too much of an Ostrobothnian sighing circle, but also outsiders. And for a good evening spirit d although in the evening d vslills will be heard as musical performances by the Ostrobothnians. Our presenter Elina Moisio will present all the performers in more detail during the event. In words, I am pleased, on behalf of EKSO, to open our seminar on the oSeinsjoki d lakes of Brusselso and to wish everyone a fruitful and open debate on Europeanism and Etelspohjanism.

Thursday2 October 2008, 12:00 AM LADIES AND GENTLEMEN OF POWER! First of all, my sincerest thanks for the invitation to come and introduce the morning coffee discussion. I was able to choose my topic oClimate change and financial markets, which I believe to be as interesting and challenging as I am, and I look forward to a lively debate. The question is, how can the financial markets contribute to the fight against climate change and to the adaptation of societies to change? Of course, looking at this issue in the current financial market turbulence makes it possible to look at the subject as a former member of the council. In my introduction, I will primarily focus on global trade in greenhouse gas and its importance in the financial markets. In addition, I am looking at the financing of environmental crises and some environmental investment activities, all of which shape the functioning of global financial markets. (Major energy projects, such as the financing of nuclear power plants, will be available to the public, as it will attract better expertise from the audience). FIRST, BACKGROUND Climate change is not a new manifestation: in the long run of history, the earth's climate has experienced cold and hot, rainy and dry periods. What makes the climate change that is going on now different, however, is that climate change is largely caused by the people themselves and that it is happening more quickly than before. While the global average over the last 100 years has risen by 0.74(C), it is estimated that it will rise over the next hundred years by 2100 by 1.1 d 6.4(c) from the mid-1980-1999 period. In the background are the so-called. greenhouses with: energy production 26%, industry 19%, forestry 17%, agriculture 14%, transport 13%. By country, the countries are divided into: USA 22%, China 18%, EU 15%, Russia 6%, India 5% (China is now estimated to be on par with the US.) If the climate is bigger, the bigger negative impact is on global GDP. In addition, the effects of climate change are estimated to be greater and more certain in emerging economies. As far as Finland is concerned, it is interesting to note that the carbon dioxide intensity of Finnish exports is very high d twice the EU average, which is also higher than in the USA, for example. CLIMATE CHANGE AFFECTS THE ECONOMY IN MANY DIFFERENT WAYS. The much-publicised Stern report (Nicholas Stern is a former World Bank economist, British economist) focuses in particular on the wealth effects of climate change, i.e. the destruction of physical wealth and productive wealth as a result of droughts, floods and storms. According to the report, uncontrollable climate change caused by greenhouse gas can even collapse the international economy. According to Stern, the economic impacts of climate change could be more severe than those of the World Wars or the Depression of the 1930s. The recommendations of the Stern report are the most natural to interpret from the insurance-theoretic angle. The effects of climate change are very certain. A strict climate policy aims to prevent devastating disasters. In other words, a significant amount of greenhouse psschje is justified if it can be verified that the worst-case scenarios will come to pass. In addition to the destruction of production capacity, climate change is undermining the viability of the economy by making it more difficult to access resources. The most obvious example is access to water, which has become a major problem in many countries due to the increasing frequency of drought and desertification. Global agricultural production can also reflect climate change if desertification and rising seawater levels limit production potential. In addition to the effects on wealth, climate change can have a significant negative impact on economic development, also through increased security and the subsequent increase in risk premia. KYOTO AGREEMENT In the early 1990s, international economic policy really woke up to environmental problems. The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) is the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). The Climate Pact was adopted in 1992. The Treaty entered into force in 1994 and was ratified by Finland in the same year. The Climate Agreement was adopted in 1997 and entered into force on 16.2.2005. It has been ratified by a total of 181 countries (Finland with the other EU countries in 2002)." The countries that have ratified the Kyoto Protocol will commit at least five per cent of the 1990 greenhouse gas balance during the 2008-2012 commitment period. In Addition, in January 2008, the EU Commission announced new, longer-term targets for policy measures to address the negative consequences of climate change: the EU Commission set a target of a 30% reduction in greenhouse gas facilities by 2020 compared to the 1990 Kyoto base year. At the same time, the Commission proposed that the EU commit itself unilaterally to the 20% reduction target to be pursued through eu trade and other environmental and energy policy measures at EU and national level. The second phase of the programme (ECCPII), which was launched in 2005, when the czech trade was also launched, is now under way. Greenhouse gas rights and trade in them play a key role in the EU's climate change programme. The European Union Emission Trading System (EU ETS) is the world's largest multinational trading system, with the ETS covering around 12,000 energy and industrial installations, which together account for half of the EU's CO2 balance and 40% of the EU's greenhouse facilities. In Finland, the psss trade concerns approximately 500 energy production and industrial plants. In the union's guerrilla burden-sharing, Finland's objective was to stabilise the PFssje at the 1990 level of around 70.5 million carbon dioxide equivalents. Finland's energy and climate strategy emphasises trade as a steering instrument. The objective of trade is to create a cost for the negative externalities of greenhouse gases. Each institution is allowed to pssssmss on the basis of certain criteria. If a production plant is able to produce the production it wants to produce, it can sell its surplus to other production plants. The aim of the system is to make it the most economically advantageous and thus to influence global production as much as possible. Another potential problem arises when psshchi rights are often allocated in relation to past psshchi. The system distributes the system as well as rewards polluting companies. Also, the incentives to take use of clean technology may be vshsisemmst. On the EU's initiative, there are now plans to trade in the rights (60% would be auctioned in 2013 and then additional.) In addition to the development of trade, the role of global financial markets in implementing economic policies to mitigate climate change has increased significantly. Over the past three years, the trade in carbon dioxide rights has become one of the fastest growing market segments in the financial markets, with large banks and a number of smaller institutions competing. According to World Bank estimates, the trade in Psshschhold (CO2) rights reached around 64 billion in 2007. By far the largest trade mechanism for both participants and trade is the trade in greenhouse gas rights in the European Union. Next, the market for pss rights is the Clean Development Mechanism under the Kyoto Protocol, in which an industrialised country can finance projects or sinks in addition to projects in a developing country and receive the psssv reductions received from the project. At the same time, the projects must contribute to the development of the project in the target country. Other trade mechanisms include, in the USA, a national market for the prevention of acid rain. It is difficult to estimate what constitutes a trade in rights in the years. DISASTER INSURANCE AND DISASTER BONDS - NEW INSTRUMENTS TO PROTECT AGAINST NATURAL DISASTERS. As I said at the beginning, I consider it verifiable (eg. Stern Review 2007, Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), that the likelihood and duration of severe floods, droughts and storms are increasing. As a result, over the last decade, the global disaster insurance market has grown in size and range of instruments d although geographical coverage has still been limited. The global disaster insurance market is a wholesale market segment of the insurance market. Typically, direct insurers (those who provide insurance to households and businesses) seek insurance against natural disasters. In addition, by securitisation (so-called securitisation). The cat-bonds market d although still relatively small d has grown rapidly in recent years. Its market value at the end of 2007 was around 15 billion. dollars. According to market estimates, the total value of disaster insurance is around 150 billion. Most cat bonds and disaster insurance contracts focus on a few bush risks (US wind, land earthquake, EU wind, Japan: earthquake, hurricane), which cover about 90% of the total market capitalisation. Insurance policies do not cover the entire damage. However, the influx of hedge funds, banks and direct investors has led to lower insurance premiums, e.g. the increase in the premium has become smaller and shorter after large insurance claims (type HTrin), with insurance premiums typically rising as insurance companies return to normal levels. INVESTMENT Climate change affects financial markets in many other ways as well. Over a long period of time, environmental risks also start more clearly in the financial markets in general, as the environment and the factors related to living conditions affect the creditworthiness of the economy and the prices of the financial markets. After all, the prices of financial assets and contracts must reflect expected economic developments and the associated risk. For example, in the pricing of insurance contracts, shares and long-term debt, the period under consideration is so long that even long-term environmental risks become very significant. The ultimate function of the financial markets is to direct financing to investors. The raising and allocation of funds on the financial markets depends on the expected returns on investments and the risk. As climate change accelerates, there is an increased need to direct energy investments towards the production of renewable energy, such as solar, bio and wind power. However, from the investor's point of view, the production of renewable energy involves considerable risks in the early stages. Renewable energy production facilities are often small compared to conventionally operated plants. Similarly, technology is often new, and although it is developing rapidly, there are no long-term experiences. Another significant risk for the investor is that the profitability of renewable energy production is highly dependent on the price level of traditional energy products, such as sljy. The reasons for this are that the public sector plays a significant role in financing renewable energy production and, in particular, product development. However, the situation is rapidly changing. In recent years, investment in renewable energy has grown rapidly and a critical mass has now been reached that private investors have also entered the olsyts sector. The fastest growing cases have been private venture capital, private equity and also cash investments. On the asset management side, the environment is also becoming a major player. This is influenced by the increased environmental awareness of investors and by the product development of banks and funds, which offers greater opportunities for taking social and environmental consideration into account in investment activities. In the United States, one-tenth of the assets under active asset management are already so-called asset management. Socially Responsible Investing (SRJ). Companies that are genuinely committed to sustainable development and corporate social responsibility are sought as investment targets. Myss in Europe incl. Investments in the Finnish sector are growing rapidly. It can be said that in recent years the investor base has become clearly aware of the importance of environmental issues and also of the opportunities offered by the rapidly developing sector. The potential for returns and the interest of investors in the sector are also in the psrsi rates of companies that invest in the development of the sector, which have risen faster than the general trend. Environmental, central values of development have also become significant in the investment philosophy of institutional investors. In Europe, especially in the most funded schemes (in the UK and the Netherlands d formerly Finland?), joint and several investment is rapidly becoming part of the mainstream of investment. In other countries, too, socially responsible investing is additional. The increase in the social awareness of investors has a significant guiding effect, forcing companies seeking financing to pay greater attention to the environmental and social dimensions of their activities. FINALLY Even from my brief overview, it is clear that the role of global financial markets in improving the environment is significant, if not central. Recent financial market crises and crises have shown that the emergence of global financial markets and their highly sophisticated instruments poses major challenges for ssstely authorities d e.g. in the financial markets. how to make the legal and financial risks associated with transactions sufficiently attractive to the parties involved in the trade so that trust in even complex instruments is maintained and how the insensitives are set so that the perceived excesses and the financial markets function stably. Globaali katastrofien jlleenvakuutusmarkkina on vakuutusmarkkinoiden tukkumarkkina-segmentti. Tyypillisesti ensivakuuttajat (ne jotka antavat vakuutuksia kotitalouksille ja yrityksille) etsivt vakuutusta luonnon katastrofeja vastaan. Lisksi arvopaperistamalla (ns. Cat bondeilla) voidaan siirt riskej pomamarkkinoille. Cat-bondin laskee tyypillisesti liikkeeseen jlleenvakuutusyhti, mutta joskus mys ensivakuuttaja tai valtio. Cat-bondien markkina  vaikka edelleen suhteellisen pieni  on kasvanut nopeasti viime vuosina. Sen markkina.arvo oli vuoden 2007 lopussa noin 15 mrd. dollaria. Markkinoiden arvion mukaan koko katastrofijlleenvakuutuksen arvo on noin 150 mrd.dollaria. Useimmat Cat-bondit ja katastrofijlleenvakuutussopimukset keskittyvt muutamiin priskeihin (US: tuuli, maanjristys, EU: tuuli, Japani: maanjristys, hirmumyrsky), jotka kattavat noin 90 % koko markkina-arvosta. Vakuutukset eivt tyypillisimmilln korvaa koko vahinkoa. Hedge-fundien, pankkien ja suorien sijoittajien lisntyv tulo sijoittajiksi on kuitenkin alentanut vakuutusten preemioita, esim. vakuutus-maksun nousu on jnyt pienemmksi ja lyhytaikaisemmaksi suurten vakuutus-korvausten (tyyppi Katrin) jlkeen, jolloin vakuutuspreemiot tyypillisesti nousevat vakuutuslaitosten palauttaessa pomiaan normaalille tasolle. SIJOITUSTOIMINTA Ilmastonmuutos koskettaa rahoitus-markkinoita monella muullakin tavalla. Pitkn ajan ympristriskit alkavat nky yh selvemmin mys yleisesti rahoitus-markkinoilla, koska ympristn ja elinoloihin liittyvt tekijt vaikuttavat taloudenpitjien luottokelpoisuuteen ja rahoitusmarkkinoiden hintoihin. Rahoitusvarallisuuden ja rahoitus-sopimusten hintojenhan tulee heijastaa odotettua talouskehityst ja siihen liittyv riski. Esimerkiksi vakuutussopimusten, osakkeiden ja pitkaikaisen velan hinnoittelussa tarkastelujakso on niin pitk, ett pitkn ajan ympristriskitkin tulevat erittin merkittvksi. Rahoitusmarkkinoiden perimminen tehtv on ohjata rahoitusta sstjilt investoijille. Varojen hankinta ja allokoituminen rahoitusmarkkinoilla riippuvat investointien odotetuista tuotoista ja riskeist. Ilmastonmuutoksen kiihtyess on korostunut tarve suunnata energia-investointeja enenevss mrin uusiutuvan energian, kuten aurinko-, bio-ja tuulivoiman, tuotantoon. Sijoittajan kannalta uusiutuvan energian tuotantoon liittyy kuitenkin alkuvaiheessa huomattavia riskej. Uusiutuvan energian tuotantolaitokset ovat usein pieni verrattuna perinteisill energialhteill toimiviin laitoksiin. Samoin teknologia on usein uutta, ja vaikka se kehittyykin nopeasti, siit ei ole viel pitkaikaisia kokemuksia. Sijoittajan kannalta merkittv riski on mys se, ett uusiutuvalla energialla toimivan tuotannon kannattavuus on hyvin riippuvainen perinteisten energialhteiden, kuten ljyn, hintatasosta. Nist syist on ymmrrettv, ett julkisen sektorin osuus on huomattava uusiutuvan energian tuotannon ja erityisesti tuotekehityksen rahoituksessa. Tilanne on kuitenkin nopeasti muuttumassa. Viime vuosina investoinnit uusiutuvaan energiaan ovat kasvaneet nopeasti ja nyt on saavutettu sellainen kriittinen massa, ett mys yksityiset investoijat ovat lytneet tmn sektorin. Nopeiten kasvavia ovat olleet yksityiset riskipomasijoitukset (venture capital), suorat osakesijoitukset (private equity) sek mys prssisijoitukset. Mys omaisuudenhoidon puolella ympristtekijist on tulossa yh merkittvmpi tekij. Thn vaikuttaa sek sijoittajien ympristtietoisuuden lisntyminen ett pankkien ja rahastojen tuotekehittely, joka tarjoaa suuremmat mahdollisuudet sosiaali-ja ympristtekijiden huomioonottamiseen sijoitusptksi tehtess. Yhdysvalloissa aktiivisen omaisuudenhoidon piiriss olevista varoista jo kymmenesosa on ns. yhteiskuntavastuullisia sijoituksia (Socially Responsible Investing, SRJ). Niiss sijoituskohteeksi haetaan yrityksi, jotka ovat aidosti sitoutuneet kestvn kehitykseen ja yritysten yhteiskuntavastuuseen. Mys Euroopassa ml. Suomi tmn sektorin sijoitukset kasvavat nopeasti. Voidaan todeta, ett sijoittajakunta on viime vuosina selvsti tiedostanut ympristasioiden merkityksen ja mys ne mahdollisuudet, joita tm nopeasti kehittyv sektori tarjoaa. Nm tuottomahdollisuudet sek sijoittajien kiinnostus thn sektoriin nkyvt mys kestvn kehitykseen panostavien yritysten prssikursseissa, jotka ovat keskimrin nousseet yleist kurssikehityst nopeammin. Ympristeettiset, kestvn kehityksen arvot ovat nousseet merkittviksi mys institutionaalisten sijoittajien sijoitusfilosofiassa. Euroopassa varsinkin eniten rahastoiduissa elkejrjestelmiss (Iso-Britanniassa ja Alankomaissa  ent Suomi?) yhteisvastuullisesta sijoittamisesta on kehittymss nopeasti osa sijoitustoiminnan valtavirtaa. Mys muissa maissa yhteiskuntavastuullinen sijoittaminen on lisntymss. Sijoittajien yhteiskuntatietoisuuden kasvulla on merkittv ohjaava vaikutus, joka pakottaa rahoitusta hakevat yritykset kiinnittmn entist suurempaa huomiota toimintansa ymprist-ja sosiaalisiin ulottuvuuksiin. LOPUKSI Jo esittmni pienenkin katsaukseni perusteella on mielestni selv, ett ympristn parantamisessa globaalien rahoitusmarkkinoiden rooli on merkittv, ellei jopa keskeinen. Miten muuten esimerkiksi globaaleilla hydykkeill (vai pitisik puhua haitakkeesta), kasvihuonepstill, voitaisiin kyd kauppaa. Kasvihuonekaasujen pstkauppa on onnistuessaan nerokas mekanismi, joka voi vhent globaaleja kasvihuonepstj kustannustehokkaasti. Viimeaikaiset rahoitusmarkkinahirit ja kriisit ovat osoittaneet, ett globaalien rahoitusmarkkinoiden ja niiden hyvin sofistikoitujen instrumenttien muodostuminen asettaa stely-viranomaisille suuria haasteita  esim. kuinka kauppoihin liittyvt juridiset ja rahoitusriskit saadaan tarpeeksi lpinkyviksi kaupankyntiosapuolille niin ett luottamus monimutkaisiinkin instrumentteihin silyy ja kuinka insentiivit asetetaan niin, ett koetun kaltaisilta ylilynneilt vltytn ja rahoitusmarkkinat toimivat vakaasti. Uskon kuitenkin, ett nykyisest kriisist opitaan ja globaalit rahoitusmarkkinat toimivat sen jlkeen entist tehokkaammin auttaen suojautumaan ilmastonmuutoksesta johtuvilta katastrofeilta ja ohjaten pomia edistmn ilmastonmuutoksen torjumista siell miss se on tehokkainta.

Title: Innovation and Intellectual property in Financial Services
text: Member of the Board Sinikka Salo, Opening Remarks in the 9th Annual Bank of Finland/CEPR Conference co-organized with the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia: "Innovation and Intellectual property in Financial Services", Helsinki 16, October 2008 . Speech . Friday 17 October 2008, 12:00 AM Member ofthe Board Sinikka Salo 9th Annual Bank ofFinland/CEPR Conference co-organized with the FederalReserve Bank of Philadelphia: "Innovation and Intellectual property in Financial Services" Helsinki16,October 2008 I am very pleased and honoured to welcome you all to Helsinki, and to this CEPR and Bank of Finland joint Conference "Innovation and Intellectual property in Financial Services". This annual event takes place now for the 9th time, which may also be regarded as a proof of fruitful cooperation between our two institutions and involving this time also the third party, Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia. We at the Bank of Finland appreciate highly the work of CEPR's network of researchers and its cooperation with the central banks, and I am happy to confirm that we at the Bank are committed to maintain and foster this cooperation also in the future. As you know we have attempted to alternate the CEPR/Bank of Finland conference themes between macro topics and financial markets topics. This time the topic indeed goes to the core of modern financial markets and due to current financial turmoil the topic is ever more exciting and challenging. For me, at least three questions from the policy perspective are relevant: The first worry relates to risk financing necessary to new innovative investments. How will it survive and develop further in current turmoil in financial markets with (too) high risk premium? What is the role of central banks and innovation policy makers? What are the tasks of central banks as they influence on the structure of the financial markets in fostering innovation friendly environment? Should government innovation policy be contingent to financial market frictions? Should for example more public funds be channelled via R&d subsidies when financial markets are distressed? The second issue relates the first one, and thus to the character/definition of financial innovation. Is it so that financial innovations so far have been too heavily focused on finding tools for short-sighted competition between financial institutions and in this way resulted in destabilizing markets rather than designing better and more appropriate financial services for e.g. to finance R&D and innovations in real economy. How to set incentives to direct financial innovations more to this direction? In particular, we do not know yet how patentability of business methods affects the incentives to innovate, not to mention how it changes the composition of R&D in financial services. Does patentability induce financial institutions do more ostabilizingo or odestabilizingo innovation? The third topic relates to incentives for R&D in payment systems. Take for example, SEPA, Single Euro Payment Area. We know that SEPA, as a common cross-border payment system is crucial for the internal market in the EU and a good start. But how to assure that there will be enough R&D to guarantee continuous improvement within the system? This issue is inherently linked to the delicate intersection of standard-setting arrangements such as SEPA and intellectual property rights. The goal of standardization is to promote the use of innovations adopted as standard whereas intellectual property aims at stimulating innovation by giving its owner a right to exclude others from using the innovation. It is not a trivial task to strike a balance between these sometimes opposing goals. Finally, last but not least, I should like to refer to various papers to be discussed in the conference, and which deal with a very important European policy issue, notably the papers dealing with the question: should business methods be patentable also in Europe and what would be the consequences for European Financial markets? For example these kind of important topics are on the current agenda of policy makers and therefore make the seminar and papers to be presented highly relevant and topical from the current policy perspective. *** I am proud and happy to declare the seminar open, and on behalf of the whole Board of the Bank of Finland, I wish your conference the best success.

Title: Opening speech at the "France Soire" event
text: Opening speech by Bank Manager Sinikka Salo at the oFrska Soirzeo event 6.11.2008 . Speech . Thursday6November 2008,12:00 AM Opening speech at the oRanska Soirzeo event of the European Department of Culture (EKSO) and the European Parliament City Region Association at Ssstytalo on 6.11. Dear general! Welcome to the French evening! Warmly welcome to you la Soirze franaise! The task of the European Department of Culture and Culture Finland (EKSO) is to produce speeches for citizens' dialogue on the diversity of European culture in order to identify and strengthen the European roots of our own culture and traditions. We have already held a seminar a few times around the eu presidency with the favourable support of d and the country's major country. The aim has been to familiarise ourselves with the culture, politics and economy of the country holding the presidency in order to better understand the diversity of the EU. The diversity inherent in this European dimension must be understood in order to build a common Europe d common institutions, which in turn we need in order to maintain a high level of European prosperity and a European form of living. Diversity and commonality are both part of europeanism. In order to remember that Europe is also multilingual, the seminar will be held in the two official EU languages d French and Finnish. The theme of the seminar will be France, the founding country of the EU. The aim of the seminar is to talk about France, Europeanism, the great culture of France and the cultural heritage of France and Finland. We will hold a seminar together with the European Local Council. Both of us associations share the same pssmssrsn d to produce civil dialogue for the sake of our Europe. Both of us d as well as the European Culturesstisn Finnish Department and the European City Region Association operate with the support of our joint and personal contributions and seminar-specific sponsors. I would therefore like to express my sincerest thanks to all our supporters at the outset of the programme leaflet. In particular, I would like to thank Madame Bourolleau, the French Grand Prix of Finland, who, from the very first moment she came to Finland, came to the idea and has been instrumental in the seminary. *** The core idea of European integration has been to link the democratic states and peoples of Europe to each other on issues where there is a common policy, since the country is not alone in a globalising world and in a globalising market. The recent crisis in the financial markets has already shown the dynamism of EU integration and has also given new impetus, among other things. The result of the Irish people's vote is also a headwind over the integration process. The EU cannot go forward against the will of its citizens. The will therefore depends on the national authorities being more aware of the EU's achievements and opportunities for the common good. In this context, I would like to remind you of the success of the euro. Our common currency, the euro, which is now celebrating its 10th anniversary, is a great achievement. The euro d and its single monetary policy - is unquestionably a success story and a sign of a strong will for integration, for nurturing the vitality of our continent. In the context of the current global financial market crisis, EMU and the single currency, the euro, have acted as a stabilising factor. One can only imagine what the situation on the foreign exchange market would have been like now, why there would have been more currencies in Europe! Under euro conditions, the Fed and the eurosystems have also been able to lead coordinated measures by central banks to improve the functioning of global financial markets as a whole. The desire to aspire to the euro area has increased in the EU. The EU, under the French Presidency, has also shown that it is after all capable of working together to prevent the deepening of the banking crisis and to work together to find solutions at global level to overcome the financial crisis. This shows that the will to integrate and the central confidence of the Member States are, after all, quite strong and that the challenges of the EU's government can also be met in order to strengthen institutions and improve the functioning of the sizzle market. By way of example, I would like to mention the challenge facing the European financial markets, which, despite the crisis, is a key one. EMU, Europe's Economic and Monetary Union, is not a complete project. Monetary policy is common in the euro area, but in many other respects we are only halfway or even at the beginning of the journey. We need a truly integrated European financial market. The current crisis has shown that the EU urgently needs common supervision of financial markets at EU level. Otherwise, there is a risk that the process of integration of the financial markets will be halted and the markets will be renationalised, which would be a real blow to the development of the estral market. Ladies and gentlemen, I referred earlier to the economy, to financial integration, to the success of the euro as the challenges of integration. As an economist, it is my duty to recall the successes and challenges facing the EU. But is it enough to get European citizens to build European solidarity? The late Academie francaise, historian Fernand Braudel (1902-1985), points to the enthusiasm of the founding fathers of the EU and writes: oHows a lack of human knowledge to provide the citizens with only calculations that pale in comparison to all the madness lshenev's enthusiasm for the rise that Europe has experienced before and now. o I have learned d even as an economist . agree: European solidarity cannot be built on numbers alone. In Braudel's words, oEurope cannot be itself unless it relies on the age-old forces from which it has drawn its civilisation and its humanism. o We will focus on this in our fine performances and in the speeches of our performers. In words, I am pleased to open our seminar and wish everyone a fruitful and open oranska d European evening.

text: Bank Manager Sinikka Salo: Kortesjsrvelsism in the world, in Europe and in Kauhava. Keynote speech at the 140th anniversary of the municipality of Kortesjsrve in Kortesjsrve on 30.11.2008. . I would therefore like to give some impetus to thinking about the challenges facing Finland and the Finns, but also the opportunities in the current process of globalisation and also in the process of European integration. These developments also have an impact on the kortesjsrvelsisten elsmssn. Firstly, globalisation. What is globalisation? Globalisation means the opening up of economies to international trade. The market is becoming more international. In addition to various industrial products and other hysdys, the mobility of technology and power is increasing worldwide. All experience shows that economies that have opened up to foreign trade and are trading-friendly have a good chance of growing rapidly. Globalisation has accelerated in recent years as countries such as China, India and other Asian countries have opened up their economies. Our standard of living is based on international trade d in a subsistence economy we could not have concentrated, for example, on highly productive information technology, since our productive resources would have been all committed to the production of food. Nokia would have been born. In the autumn, attempts to restrict international trade, protectionism d which are required from time to time d are detrimental to the long term of prosperity. Although I speak of the economic dimensions of globalisation and in market terms, globalisation is more important than the opening up of markets. Above all, it means that geography is becoming less important as a political and cultural factor. Our "world village" d chenms characterization illustrates well that globalization is not just an economic manifest, but is driven by the general expansion of the circle of people.
